In 'the recollection of those with severed rounds, etc.,' by the word 'etc.' the inclusion of uninhabited world-systems, islands, countries, cities, villages, and so forth should be understood. However, in the Gaṇṭhipada it is said: 'The supramundane virtues, etc., of those with severed rounds were not known by the Blessed One in the time of being a Bodhisatta.' By implication, it follows that the mundane ones were known. That statement seems to be consistent with the words 'revilers of the noble ones' in the section on the divine eye knowledge. Indeed, for one who does not see the noble ones, such a thing does not occur. If one were to ask: 'For what reason is recollection mentioned here? Is this not the section on knowledge?' It is stated because for a beginner practitioner, it is produced by way of mindfulness, and because it is the special domain of mindfulness regarding past phenomena. Indeed, it is said, 'I recollect.'

“Vattamānesu [V 0.0046] vijjāna-matītesvassa sarati;

Anāgatesu dhammesu, sarati vijjāna paṇidhī”ti.

In present things, there is knowing; in past things, there is recollection. In future phenomena, there is recollection and knowing; this is the distinction.

Ācariyakumāritena silokopi vutto.

A verse was also spoken by the teacher Kumārita.

Tattha [M 0.0051] rāge ussannatare tejosaṃvaṭṭo. Dose āposaṃvaṭṭo. Mohe vāyosaṃvaṭṭo. Keci “dose tejosaṃvaṭṭo, rāge āposaṃvaṭṭo, mohe vāyosaṃvaṭṭo”ti vadanti. Yasmā amutrāti cittaṃ, vacanaṃ vā bhavādiniyamena hoti, tasmā “bhave vā”tiādi. Evaṃnāmo evaṃgottoti padadvayena ajjhattabahiddhāmūlakaṃ paññattisaṅkhātaṃ gocaranivāsaṃ dīpeti. Pavattaphalabhojano sayaṃpatitaphalāhāro. Caturāsītikappasahassaparamāyupariyanto vāti paṇidhānato pubbe. Paṭinivattantassa paccavekkhaṇaṃ pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇaṃ na hoti. “Pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇalābhīnaṃ panetaṃ ānubhāvaparidīpana”nti gaṇṭhipade vuttaṃ. Amutrāti ettha paṭhamayojanāyaṃ sīhokkantavasena anussaraṇaṃ vuttaṃ, tañca kho anulomavasena. “Paṭilomavasenā”tipi likhanti, taṃ duviññeyyaṃ. Sīhokkantaṃ dassetuṃ “anekāsu kappakoṭīsū”tiādi vuttaṃ. Yathā tanti nidassanena paṭipattisādhāraṇena phalasādhāraṇataṃ dassento brāhmaṇassa ādaraṃ janeti, attānamevekaṃ ukkaṃsetīti vacanaṃ nivāreti. “Sādhu kho pana tathārūpānaṃ arahataṃ dassanaṃ hotī”ti tassa pubbe uppannacitte eva niyojeti. Paṭhamā abhinibbhidāti vacanena avijjaṇḍakosassa bahupaṭalabhāvaṃ dasseti, tena aṭṭhaguṇissariyādinā anabhinibbhidaṃ dīpeti.

Therein, when greed is more prevalent, dissolution by fire occurs. When hatred is more prevalent, dissolution by water occurs. When delusion is more prevalent, dissolution by wind occurs. Some say: 'When hatred is more prevalent, dissolution by fire occurs; when greed is more prevalent, dissolution by water occurs; when delusion is more prevalent, dissolution by wind occurs.' Because the mind or speech there arises by the determination of existence and so on, therefore it is said, 'or in existence,' etc. By the two terms 'of such a name, of such a clan,' He indicates the dwelling place of resort, known as a concept, which is rooted in the internal and external. `Pavattaphalabhojano` means one who has for his food fruit that has fallen by itself. The phrase 'up to a maximum lifespan of eighty-four thousand aeons' refers to the time before the aspiration. For one who has regressed, the reviewing is not the knowledge of recollection of past lives. But in the Gaṇṭhipada it is said: 'This is an elucidation of the power of those who have obtained the knowledge of recollection of past lives.' Here, in the word `amutrā` ('there'), in the first construction, recollection is stated by way of the lion's leap, and that is by way of the forward order. They also write 'by way of the reverse order,' but that is difficult to understand. To show the lion's leap, it is said, 'in many crores of aeons,' etc. By the simile 'Just as that...', showing the commonality of the fruit through the commonality of the practice, He generates respect in the brahmin and prevents the saying, 'He exalts only himself.' He urges him only towards the thoughts that had previously arisen in him: 'Indeed, it is good to see such Arahants.' By the words 'the first breakthrough,' He shows the state of the eggshell of ignorance having many layers; by that, He indicates its unpenetrated state by the eightfold mastery and so on.

Pubbenivāsakathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the discourse on previous abodes is concluded.

Dibbacakkhuñāṇakathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourse on the Knowledge of the Divine Eye

13. “Cutūpapātañāṇāyā”ti phalūpacārena vuttaṃ. Idañhi dibbacakkhuñāṇaṃ rūpārammaṇattā parittapaccuppannaajjhattabahiddhārammaṇaṃ hoti. Na cutiṃ vā paṭisandhiṃ vā ārammaṇaṃ karoti. Tasmā “yathākammūpage satte pajānāmī”ti (pārā. 13) vacanaṃ viya phalūpacāreneva vuttamidanti veditabbaṃ. Dibbavihārasannissitattā kāraṇopacārena dibbaṃ. Iminā pana keci ācariyā “kusalākusalā cakkhū dibbacakkhu kāmāvacara”nti vadanti, te paṭisedhitā honti. Catutthajjhānapaññā hi ettha adhippetā. Mahājutikattā mahāgatikattāti etesu [V 0.0047] “saddasatthānusārenā”ti vuttaṃ. Ekādasannaṃ upakkilesānaṃ [M 0.0052] evaṃ uppattikkamo upakkilesabhāvo ca veditabbo, mahāsattassa ālokaṃ vaḍḍhetvā dibbacakkhunā nānāvidhāni rūpāni disvā “idaṃ nu kho ki”nti vicikicchā udapādi, so upakkileso upakkilesasutte (ma. ni. 3.236 ādayo) “vicikicchādhikaraṇañca pana me samādhimhi cavi, samādhimhi cute obhāso antaradhāyati dassanañca rūpāna”nti vacanato. Tato “rūpāni me passato vicikicchā uppajjati, idāni na kiñci manasi karissāmī”ti cintayato amanasikāro, tato kiñci amanasikarontassa thinamiddhaṃ udapādi, tato tassa pahānatthaṃ ālokaṃ vaḍḍhetvā rūpāni passato himavantādīsu dānavarakkhasādayo passantassa chambhitattaṃ udapādi, tato tassa pahānatthaṃ “mayā diṭṭhabhayaṃ pakatiyā olokiyamānaṃ natthi, adiṭṭhe kiṃ nāma bhaya”nti cintayato uppilāvitattaṃ udapādi. Gaṇṭhipade pana “uppilaṃ dibbarūpadassenenā”ti vuttaṃ, “taṃ duvuttaṃ parato abhijappāvacanena tadatthasiddhito”ti ācariyo vadati. Tato chambhitattappahānatthaṃ “mayā vīriyaṃ daḷhaṃ paggahitaṃ, tena me idaṃ uppilaṃ uppanna”nti vīriyaṃ sithilaṃ karontassa kāyaduṭṭhullaṃ kāyadaratho kāyālasiyaṃ udapādi, tato taṃ cajantassa accāraddhavīriyaṃ udapādi, tattha dosaṃ passato atilīnavīriyaṃ upadādi, tato taṃ pahāya samappavattena vīriyena chambhitattabhayā himavantādiṭṭhānaṃ pahāya devalokābhimukhaṃ ālokaṃ vaḍḍhetvā devasaṅghaṃ passato taṇhāsaṅkhātā abhijappā udapādi, tato “mayhaṃ ekajātikarūpaṃ manasi karontassa abhijappā uppannā, tasmā dāni nānāvidhaṃ rūpaṃ manasi karissāmī”ti kālena devalokābhimukhaṃ, kālena manussalokābhimukhaṃ ālokaṃ vaḍḍhetvā nānāvidhāni rūpāni manasi karoto nānattasaññā udapādi, tato “nānāvidharūpāni me manasi karontassa nānattasaññā udapādi, tasmā dāni abhijappādibhayā iṭṭhādinimittaggāhaṃ pahāya ekajātikameva rūpaṃ manasi karissāmī”ti tathā karoto abhinijjhāyitattaṃ rūpānaṃ udapādi evaṃ pahīnaupakkilesassāpi anadhiṭṭhitattā. Obhāsañhi kho jānāmi, na ca rūpāni passāmītiādi jātaṃ.

13. "For the knowledge of the passing away and reappearance of beings"—this is said by way of a fruit metaphor. For this divine eye-knowledge, because it has form as its object, takes as its object limited, present, internal, and external phenomena. It does not take passing away or rebirth-linking as its object. Therefore, it should be understood that this was spoken only by way of a fruit metaphor, like the statement, "I know beings who fare according to their kamma" (Pārā. 13). Because it is dependent on the divine abiding, it is called "divine" by way of a cause metaphor. By this, however, some teachers say, "The wholesome and unwholesome eyes are the divine eye, which is of the sense-sphere," but they are refuted. For the wisdom of the fourth jhāna is intended here. In the phrases "because of great radiance" and "because of great range," it is said, "according to the science of grammar." The order of arising and the nature as an imperfection of the eleven imperfections should be understood thus: For the Great Being, having extended the light and seen various forms with the divine eye, the doubt arose, "What, indeed, is this?" That is an imperfection, in accordance with the Upakkilesa Sutta (M.N. iii. 162): "And because of doubt, my concentration wavered; when the concentration wavered, the light disappears and the vision of forms disappears." Then, for him who was thinking, "Doubt arises in me when I see forms; now I will not attend to anything," non-attention arose. Then, for him who was not attending to anything, sloth and torpor arose. Then, to abandon that, for him who extended the light and saw forms, upon seeing dānavas, rākṣasas, and so on in the Himālaya and other places, stiffness arose. Then, to abandon that, for him who was thinking, "For me, there is no fear in what is seen when it is looked at in its natural state; what fear, then, in what is unseen?", elation arose. In the Gaṇṭhipada, however, it is said, "Elation is by the seeing of divine forms." The teacher says, "That is poorly stated, because that meaning is established by the subsequent word abhijappā." Then, to abandon the stiffness, for him who was relaxing his energy, thinking, "I have exerted strong energy, and because of that this elation has arisen in me," bodily coarseness, bodily fever, and bodily sluggishness arose. Then, for him who was abandoning that, excessively exerted energy arose. Seeing the fault in that, excessively slack energy arose. Then, abandoning that, with evenly applied energy, out of fear of stiffness, having abandoned the place of the Himālaya and so on, extending the light towards the deva-world and seeing the assembly of devas, intense longing, known as craving, arose. Then, for him who was attending to various forms, at times extending the light towards the deva-world, at times towards the human world, thinking, "For me, when attending to a form of a single kind, intense longing has arisen; therefore, I will now attend to various forms," the perception of diversity arose. Then, for him who acted thus, thinking, "For me, when attending to various forms, the perception of diversity has arisen; therefore, now, out of fear of intense longing and so on, abandoning the grasping of signs such as the desirable, I will attend only to a form of a single kind," preoccupation with forms arose. Thus, even for one whose imperfections have been abandoned, because of being unestablished, the state of "I know the light, but I do not see the forms," and so on, arose.

Tassattho – yadā parikammobhāsameva manasi karomi, tadā obhāsaṃ sañjānāmi, dibbena cakkhunā rūpāni na ca passāmi, rūpadassanakāle ca [M 0.0053] obhāsaṃ na jānāmīti. Kimatthamidaṃ vuttaṃ, na hi etaṃ upakkisesagatanti? Na kevalaṃ upakkilesappajahanamevettha kattabbaṃ, yena idaṃ visuddhaṃ hoti, aññampi taduttari kattabbaṃ atthīti dassanatthaṃ. Vicikicchā cittassa upakkilesotiādīsu “ime dhammā upakkilesāti ādīnavadassanena pajahiṃ, na mayhaṃ tadā uppannattā”ti keci vadanti. Mānusakaṃ vāti iminā sabhāvātikkamaṃ dasseti. Maṃsacakkhunā [V 0.0048] viyāti iminā pariyattiggahaṇaṃ, vaṇṇamattārammaṇatañca upameti. Vaṇṇamatte hettha satta-saddo, na “sabbe sattā āhāraṭṭhitikā”ti (a. ni. 10.27) ettha viya sabbasaṅkhatesu, hīnajātiādayo mohassa nissando vipāko. Kāyaduccaritena samannāgatā pubbe atītabhave ahesuṃ, sampati nirayaṃ upapannāti evaṃ pāṭhasesena sambandho veditabbo. “Yathākammūpagañāṇañhi ekantamatītārammaṇaṃ, dibbacakkhu paccuppannārammaṇa”nti ubhinnaṃ kiccavasena vuttaṃ. Mahallakoti samaṇānaṃ sāruppamasāruppaṃ, lokācāraṃ vā na jānātīti adhippāyena vuttattā guṇaparidhaṃsanena garahatīti veditabbaṃ. “Niyato sambodhiparāyano”ti (saṃ. ni. 2.41; 5.998, 1004) vutto ariyapuggalo maggāvaraṇaṃ kātuṃ samatthaṃ pharusavacanaṃ yadi katheyya, apāyagamanīyampi kareyya, tena so apāyupagopi bhaveyya, tasmā upaparikkhitabbanti eke. “Vāyāmaṃ mā akāsīti therena vuttattā maggāvaraṇaṃ karotī”ti vadanti. Pubbeva sotāpannena apāyadvāro pihito, tasmāssa saggāvaraṇaṃ natthi. “Pākatikanti pavattivipākaṃ ahosī”ti vadanti. “Vuddhi hesā, bhikkhave, ariyassa vinaye, yo accayaṃ accayato disvā yathādhammaṃ paṭikarotī”ti (ma. ni. 3.370; dī. ni. 1.251) vacanato pākatikaṃ ahosīti eke. Sace so na khamatīti sotāpannādīnaṃ khantiguṇassa mandatāya vā āyatiṃ tassa suṭṭhu saṃvaratthāya vā akkhamanaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Sukhānaṃ vā āyassa ārammaṇādino abhāvā kālakañcikā asurā honti. “Ito bho sugatiṃ gacchā”ti (itivu. 83) vacanato manussagatipi. Dibbacakkhuñāṇavijjāti dibbacakkhumeva dassanaṭṭhena ñāṇaṃ, tassa tassa atthassa vindanaṭṭhena vijjāti attho.

The meaning of this is: when I attend only to the preliminary-work light, then I perceive the light, but with the divine eye I do not see forms; and at the time of seeing forms, I do not know the light. For what purpose was this said? For is it not true that this is not subject to defilement? It was said to show that it is not only the abandoning of defilements that should be done here, whereby this becomes pure, but that there is something else to be done beyond that. Regarding such statements as, 'Doubt is a defilement of the mind,' some say: 'I abandoned them by seeing their danger thus, "These states are defilements," not because they had arisen in me at that time.' By 'or human,' it shows the transcending of one's natural state. By 'like the fleshly eye,' it makes a comparison to the grasping of what is learned and to having mere color as an object. Here, the word 'being' is used in the sense of mere color, not as in 'all beings are sustained by food' (AN 10.27), where it applies to all conditioned things. Inferior birth and so on are the outflow and result of delusion. The connection should be understood with the remainder of the text thus: 'Those endowed with bodily misconduct were so in a past existence, and now they have been reborn in hell.' For it is said in terms of the function of the two knowledges: 'The knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings according to their kamma has an exclusively past object, while the divine eye has a present object.' By `Mahallaka` is meant one who does not know what is proper or improper for ascetics, or worldly custom; because it is said with this intention, it should be understood as a criticism that denigrates his virtues. Some say: 'If a noble person, who is said to be "fixed in destiny, with enlightenment as his destination" (SN 2.41; 5.998, 1004), were to speak harsh words capable of creating an obstruction to the path, he might also commit an act leading to the plane of deprivation, and thereby he might also go to a plane of deprivation; therefore, this should be investigated.' Others say: 'Because it was said by the elder, "Do not make an effort," he creates an obstruction to the path.' The door to the planes of deprivation was already closed by him as a stream-enterer; therefore, for him, there is no obstruction to heaven. Some say: 'By "it became normal" is meant it was a result in the course of existence.' Others say that because of the statement, 'This, monks, is growth in the discipline of the noble one: that one sees a transgression as a transgression and makes amends in accordance with the Dhamma' (MN 3.370; DN 1.251), it was restored to normal. The statement, 'If he does not forgive,' was said with reference to not forgiving, either because of the weakness of the virtue of patience in stream-enterers and others, or for the sake of that person's good restraint in the future. The Kālakañjikā asuras exist due to the absence of pleasures or of a source for them, such as objects and so on. Because of the statement, 'Sirs, go from here to a good destination' (Iti 83), the human destination is also included. Regarding `dibbacakkhuñāṇavijjā` (the true knowledge that is the knowledge of the divine eye): the divine eye itself is `ñāṇa` (knowledge) in the sense of seeing, and it is `vijjā` (true knowledge) in the sense of finding the meaning of each respective thing. This is the meaning.

Dibbacakkhuñāṇakathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Elucidation of the Discourse on the Knowledge of the Divine Eye is completed.

Āsavakkhayañāṇakathāvaṇṇanā

The Elucidation of the Discourse on the Knowledge of the Destruction of the Taints

14. So [M 0.0054] evaṃ samāhite citteti kiṃ purimasmiṃyeva, udāhu aññasmiṃyeva catutthajjhānacitte. Aṭṭhakathāyampi yato vuṭṭhāya purimavijjādvayaṃ adhigataṃ, tadeva puna samāpajjanavasena abhinavaṃ abhiṇhaṃ katanti dassanatthaṃ “so evaṃ samāhite citteti idha vipassanāpādakaṃ catutthajjhānacittaṃ veditabba”nti vuttaṃ. Etthāha – yadi tadeva puna samāpajjanavasena abhinavaṃ kataṃ, atha kasmā pubbe viya “vipassanāpādakaṃ abhiññāpādakaṃ nirodhapādakaṃ sabbakiccasādhakaṃ sabbalokiyalokuttaraguṇadāyakaṃ idha catutthajjhānacittaṃ veditabba”nti avatvā “idha vipassanāpādakaṃ catutthajjhānacittaṃ veditabba”nti ettakameva vuttaṃ[V 0.0049], nanu idha tathāvacanaṭṭhānameva taṃ arahattamaggena saddhiṃ sabbaguṇanipphādanato, na paṭhamavijjādvayamattanipphādanatoti? Vuccate – ariyamaggassa bojjhaṅgamaggaṅgajhānaṅgapaṭipadāvimokkhavisesaniyamo pubbabhāgavuṭṭhānagāminīvipassanāya saṅkhārupekkhāsaṅkhātāya niyamena ahosīti dassanatthaṃ vipassanāpādakamidha vuttanti veditabbaṃ. Tattha pariyāpannattā, na tadārammaṇamattena. Pariyāyatoti aññenapi pakārena. “Ime āsavā”ti ayaṃ vāro kimatthaṃ āraddho? “Āsavānaṃ khayañāṇāyā”ti adhikārānulomanatthaṃ. Maggakkhaṇe hi cittaṃ vimuccati, phalakkhaṇe vimuttaṃ hotīti idaṃ ekattanayena vuttaṃ. Yañhi vimuccamānaṃ, tadeva aparabhāge vimuttaṃ nāma hoti. Yañca vimuttaṃ, tadeva pubbabhāge vimuccamānaṃ nāma hoti. Bhuñjamāno eva hi bhojanapariyosāne bhuttāvī nāma. “Iminā paccavekkhaṇañāṇaṃ dassetī”ti paccavekkhaṇañāṇassa ca paṭṭhāne “maggā vuṭṭhahitvā maggaṃ paccavekkhati, phalaṃ, nibbānaṃ, pahīne kilese paccavekkhatī”ti ayamuppattikkamo vutto. Pavattikkamo panettha sarūpato atthatoti dvidhā vutto. Tattha “vimuttamiti ñāṇaṃ ahosī”ti sarūpato catubbidhassapi paccavekkhaṇañāṇassa pavattikkamanidassanaṃ. “Khīṇā jātī”tiādi atthato. Teneva ante “abbhaññāsi”nti puggalādhiṭṭhānaṃ desanaṃ akāsi paccavekkhaṇañāṇassa tathā appavattito. Appaṭisandhikaṃ hotīti jānanto “khīṇā jātī”ti jānāti nāma. “Dibbacakkhunā paccuppannānāgataṃsañāṇa”nti anāgataṃsañāṇassa ca dibbacakkhusannissitattā vuttaṃ.

14. Regarding 'So, with mind thus concentrated': is this in the very same fourth jhāna consciousness as before, or in another? In the commentary, too, in order to show that since the two prior knowledges were attained upon emerging from that very jhāna, it is that same jhāna that is made new and repeated by way of re-entering it, it is said: 'Here, "So, with mind thus concentrated" should be understood as the fourth jhāna consciousness which is the basis for insight.' Here, it is asked: If it is that very jhāna that is made new by way of re-entering it, then why, unlike before, was it not said, 'Here, the fourth jhāna consciousness should be understood as the basis for insight, the basis for higher knowledge, the basis for cessation, the accomplisher of all tasks, the bestower of all mundane and supramundane qualities,' but only this much was said: 'Here, the fourth jhāna consciousness should be understood as the basis for insight'? Is it not the case that here is the very place for such a statement, because it is the accomplishment of all qualities together with the path of arahantship, not merely the accomplishment of the first two knowledges? It is answered: It should be understood that 'basis for insight' is stated here to show that the noble path's specific determination of the factors of enlightenment, path factors, jhāna factors, practice, and liberations necessarily occurred by means of the insight leading to emergence in the preceding stage, which is called equanimity toward formations. Because it is included therein, it is not merely by way of its object. 'By way of alternative' means by another manner. For what purpose was this section, 'These are the taints,' begun? For the sake of conforming to the topic, 'for the knowledge of the destruction of the taints.' For at the moment of the path, the mind is being liberated; at the moment of fruition, it is liberated. This is stated from the perspective of unity. For that which is being liberated is, in a later stage, called 'liberated.' And that which is liberated is, in an earlier stage, called 'being liberated.' Indeed, one who is eating is, at the end of the meal, called 'one who has eaten.' Regarding 'By this, he shows the reviewing knowledge': in the Paṭṭhāna, this order of arising is stated for reviewing knowledge: 'Having emerged from the path, one reviews the path, the fruition, Nibbāna, and the abandoned defilements.' Here, the order of occurrence is stated in two ways: according to its essence and according to its meaning. Therein, 'The knowledge arose, "I am liberated"' is an indication of the order of occurrence of all four kinds of reviewing knowledge according to its essence. 'Destroyed is birth,' etc., is according to its meaning. For that very reason, at the end, he gave the teaching “He directly knew” from the standpoint of the person, because reviewing knowledge does not occur in that way. Knowing, 'It is without relinking,' one is said to know, 'Destroyed is birth.' Regarding 'Knowledge of the present and future portion with the divine eye': this is stated because the knowledge of the future portion is also dependent on the divine eye.

Āsavakkhayañāṇakathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Discourse on the Knowledge of the Destruction of the Taints is concluded.

Upāsakattapaṭivedanākathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourse on the Declaration of the State of a Lay Follower

15. Kaṇṇasukhato [M 0.0055] hadayaṅgamatoti vacanameva sandhāya vuttaṃ. Anattukkaṃsanatotiādi puggalavasena, kaṇṇasukhatoti sotindriyaṃ sandhāya. Āpāthāramaṇīyatoti ñāṇāpāthāramaṇīyato. Sayameva heṭṭhāmukhajātaṃ vā, maggo pana asoko hoti. Tadā hi soko pahīyamāno. Cariyādianukūlato appaṭikūlaṃ. “Madhuramima”nti vuttattā “dhammamima”nti vacanaṃ adhikaṃ viya dissati. Tasmā “rāgavirāgamima”nti evaṃ visuṃ visuṃ yojetvā puna piṇḍetvā dhammamimaṃ upehīti yojetabbaṃ, “dhammameva saraṇatthamupehī”ti paṭhanti kirāti dīpeti. Saraṇagatānaṃ teneva saraṇagamanena bhayaṃ santāsaṃ duggatiṃ parikkilesaṃ dukkhaṃ hiṃsatīti ratanattayaṃ saraṇaṃ nāma. Tappasādataggarutādīhi vihatakileso tapparāyanatākārappavatto cittuppādo [V 0.0050] saraṇagamanaṃ. Taṃsamaṅgīsatto saraṇaṃ gacchati. Pabhedena pana duvidhaṃ saraṇagamanaṃ lokuttaraṃ lokiyanti. Tattha lokuttaraṃ diṭṭhasaccānaṃ maggakkhaṇe saraṇagamanupakkilesasamucchedena nibbānārammaṇaṃ hutvā kiccato sakalepi ratanattaye ijjhati. Lokiyaṃ puthujjanānaṃ saraṇagamanupakkilesaṃ tadaṅgavikkhambhanena ārammaṇato buddhādiguṇārammaṇaṃ hutvā ijjhati. Taṃ atthato ratanattaye saddhāpaṭilābho saddhāmūlikā ca sammādiṭṭhi. Lokuttarassa cattāri sāmaññaphalāni vipākaphalaṃ, sabbadukkhakkhayo ānisaṃsaphalaṃ. “Yo ca buddhañca dhammañca…pe… sabbadukkhā pamuccatī”ti (dha. pa. 190-192) hi vuttaṃ. Lokiyassa bhavabhogasampadā. “Ye keci buddhaṃ saraṇaṃ gatāse”ti (dī. ni. 2.332; saṃ. ni. 1.37) hi vuttaṃ. Lokiyasaraṇagamanaṃ tīsu vatthūsu aññāṇasaṃsayamicchāñāṇādīhi saṃkilissati, na mahājutikaṃ hoti, na mahāvipphāraṃ. Lokuttarassa natthi saṃkileso. Lokiyassa sāvajjo anavajjoti duvidho bhedo. Tattha aññasatthārādīsu attasanniyyātanādīhi sāvajjo hoti, so aniṭṭhaphalo. Anavajjo kālakiriyāya, so avipākattā aphalo. Lokuttarassa nevatthi bhedo. Bhavantarepi hi ariyasāvako aññaṃ satthāraṃ na uddisati. Yo koci saraṇagato gahaṭṭho upāsako. Ratanattayaupāsanato upāsako. Pañca veramaṇiyo [M 0.0056] sīlaṃ. Satthasattamaṃsamajjavisavāṇijjārahitaṃ dhammena jīvikaṃ ājīvo. Vuttasīlājīvavipatti vipatti nāma. Viparītā sampatti.

15. “Pleasing to the ear and captivating to the heart” is stated with reference to that very expression. “Not praising oneself,” etc., refers to the individual; “pleasing to the ear” refers to the sense faculty of hearing. “Delightful to encounter” means delightful because it appears within the range of wisdom. Even if it arises naturally with a downward inclination, the path is without sorrow. For indeed, at that moment of the path, sorrow is being abandoned. Because it is conducive to one's conduct, etc., it is not unfavorable. Since it is said, “This is sweet,” the phrase “This Dhamma” seems somewhat redundant. Therefore, having construed it separately thus, “This dispassion from passion,” and then having combined it again, it should be construed as: “Approach this Dhamma.” It is said that some recite it as, “Take the Dhamma alone for your refuge.” The Triple Gem is called “refuge” because for those who have gone for refuge, by that very going for refuge, it destroys fear, terror, bad destinations, affliction, and suffering. Going for refuge is the arising of a state of consciousness that, having its defilements destroyed through faith in them, reverence for them, etc., proceeds in the manner of having them as its final resort. A being endowed with that goes for refuge. By way of division, however, going for refuge is twofold: supramundane and mundane. Among these, the supramundane, for those who have seen the truths, at the moment of the path, by the complete cutting off of the corruptions of going for refuge, having Nibbāna as its object, is accomplished with respect to its function in the entire Triple Gem. The mundane, for ordinary people, by the temporary suppression of the corruptions of going for refuge, having the qualities of the Buddha, etc., as its object, is accomplished. In meaning, it is the attainment of faith in the Triple Gem and right view rooted in faith. For the supramundane, the four fruits of recluseship are the resultant fruit, and the destruction of all suffering is the benefit-fruit. For it is said: “Whoever has gone to the Buddha and the Dhamma... is freed from all suffering.” For the mundane, there is the accomplishment of good existence and wealth. For it is said: “Whatever beings have gone to the Buddha for refuge...” Mundane going for refuge becomes defiled regarding the three objects by ignorance, doubt, wrong knowledge, etc.; it is not of great power, nor of great pervasiveness. The supramundane has no defilement. The mundane has a twofold breaking: blameworthy and blameless. Among these, the blameworthy breaking occurs through dedicating oneself, etc., to other teachers, etc., and it has an undesirable result. The blameless breaking occurs through death; since it is without result, it is fruitless. The supramundane has no breaking at all. For indeed, even in another existence, a noble disciple does not designate another as teacher. Any householder who has gone for refuge is an upāsaka. Because of attending upon the Triple Gem, one is an upāsaka. The five abstinences are virtue. A livelihood in accordance with the Dhamma, free from trading in weapons, living beings, meat, intoxicants, and poison, is right livelihood. Failure in the aforementioned virtue and livelihood is called “failure.” The opposite is “accomplishment.”

16. Lacchāma nu khoti duggate sandhāya vuttaṃ. Sakkhissāma nukho noti samiddhe sandhāya. Tattha verañjāyaṃ. Paggayhatīti pattaṃ paggaho, tena paggahena pattenāti attho. Samādāyevāti nidassanaṃ. Na ca vaṭṭatīti puna pākaṃ kiñcāpi vaṭṭati, tathāpi na suṭṭhu pakkattā vuttaṃ, “uttaṇḍulabhattaṃ labhitvāpi pidhetuṃ na vaṭṭatī”ti aṭṭhakathāvacanañcettha sādhakaṃ. “Sāvakānaṃ vā sikkhāpadaṃ paññapessāmī”ti iminā vacanena ājīvapārisuddhisīlaṃ sandhāya “pacchā sīla”nti vuttaṃ. Upālittheropi taṃ taṃ vatthuṃ paṭicca bhagavatā bahūni sikkhāpadāni paññattāni atthīti dīpeti. Yadi evaṃ verañjāyaṃ “etassa bhagavā kālo”ti vacanaṃ na sametīti ce? Na, tato pubbe sikkhāpadābhāvappasaṅgato. Thero pana paññattāni ṭhapetvā idāni paññapetabbāni pātimokkhuddesappahonakāni sandhāyāha. Bhagavāpi “na tāva sāriputta satthā sāvakānaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññapetī”ti bhaddālisutte (ma. ni. 2.134; ādayo) viya ekaccesu paññattesupi tato paraṃ paññapetabbāni sandhāyāha. Idheva aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “sāmampi pacanaṃ samaṇasāruppaṃ na hoti na ca vaṭṭatī”ti vacanañca, tathā “ratticchedo vā vassacchedo vā”tiādivacanāni ca atthi. Aññathā “dvīhākārehi buddhā bhagavanto bhikkhū paṭipucchantī”ti [V 0.0051] idhevedaṃ pāḷiṭhapanaṃ virujjhatīti ācariyena vicāritaṃ, taṃ sundaraṃ pubbepi paññattasikkhāpadasambhavato. Kintu idha pāḷiṭhapanavirodhavicāraṇā pana nippayojanā viya mama dissati. Kasmā? Upālittherena saṅgītikāle vuttapāṭhattā. Ratticchedoti sattāhakiccaṃ sandhāya vutto. “Sattāhakaraṇīyena gantvā ratticchedo vā vassacchedo vā ekabhikkhunāpi na kato”ti vuttaṃ kira mahāaṭṭhakathāyaṃ, tasmā vassacchedassa kāraṇe sati sattāhakiccaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭatīti eke. Vinayadharā pana nicchanti, tasmā aṭṭhakathādhippāyo vīmaṃsitabbo, imāya verañjāyaṃ appicchatādipaṭipadāya pasannā. Sālīnaṃ vikati sālivikati.

16. The phrase “Shall we obtain?” is said in reference to those in distress. The phrase “Shall we not be able?” is said in reference to those who are prosperous. There, in Verañjā. Regarding paggayhati (is held): because a bowl is held, it is called paggaho (a held thing); the meaning is ‘by that held bowl.’ Samādāyeva is an example. Regarding Na ca vaṭṭati (it is not allowable): although re-cooking is allowable, it is said so because it is not well-cooked; the commentary’s statement, “Even having obtained undercooked rice, it is not allowable to cover it,” is evidence for this. By the statement, “I will lay down a training rule for the disciples,” referring to the virtue of purity of livelihood, it is called “later virtue.” The Elder Upāli also indicates that with regard to particular instances, many training rules were laid down by the Blessed One. If so, does the statement in Verañjā, ‘Now is the time, O Blessed One,’ not accord with this? No, because before that, there would be the undesirable consequence of no training rules existing. However, the Elder, excluding those rules already laid down, speaks referring to those that are to be laid down now—those that suffice for the recitation of the Pātimokkha. The Blessed One also, as in the Bhaddāli Sutta, “Not yet, Sāriputta, does the Teacher lay down a training rule for the disciples,” speaks referring to those to be laid down later, even though some had already been laid down. Right here in the commentary, there is the statement, “Cooking for oneself is not befitting a recluse and is not allowable,” and also statements such as “a break in the nights or a break in the rains-residence.” Otherwise, the placement of the Pāḷi text here, “The Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, question the monks in two ways,” would be contradicted—this was examined by the teacher, and that is good because of the existence of training rules laid down even previously. However, here, the examination of the contradiction in the placement of the Pāḷi seems useless to me. Why? Because it is the text spoken by the Elder Upāli at the time of the council. “Breaking the night” (ratticchedo) is spoken in reference to the seven-day duty. It is said in the Great Commentary: “Having gone on a seven-day duty, neither a break in the nights nor a break in the rains-residence was made even by a single monk.” Therefore, some say that when there is a reason to interrupt the rains-residence, it is permissible to perform the seven-day duty. But the Vinaya experts disagree; therefore, the commentary’s intention should be investigated. In Verañjā, people were pleased by this practice of having few wishes and so on. Sālivikati is a special preparation of sāli rice.

17-8. Upapannaphaloti bahuphalo. “Khuddaṃ madhu”nti pāṭho. Theraṃ sīhanādaṃ nadāpetuṃ pucchīti iminā ācariyo yaṃ pubbe āṇāya ṭhitānaṃ [M 0.0057] sāvakānaṃ mahānubhāvatādassanaṃ “verañjāyaṃ nivāsappayojana”nti amhehi vuttaṃ, taṃ sampādeti, rājagahe verañjāyañcāti ubhayattha vitakkuppāde ekato piṇḍetvā dassento “atha kho āyasmato sāriputtassā”tiādimāha. Kālaṃ sandhāya ciraṃ, ṭhitiṃ sandhāya cirāti viggaho.

17-8. `Upapannaphaloti` means `bahuphalo`: 'it has much fruit.' The reading is 'khuddaṃ madhu.' By the phrase 'he asked in order to make the Elder roar the lion's roar,' the commentator fulfills what we have previously stated—the showing of the great spiritual power of the disciples who stood by his command, as in 'the purpose of dwelling in Verañjā.' The Elder, wishing to show the arisings of thought in both places, at Rājagaha and at Verañjā, by combining them into one, stated the text beginning with, 'Then to the Venerable Sāriputta…' and so on. With reference to time (`kāla`), `ciraṃ` is used; with reference to duration (`ṭhiti`), `cirā` is used. This is the analysis.

Kāmaṃ hinoti attano phalanibbattiyā sahāyaṃ gacchatīti kattari hetu, tathāpi idha tena karaṇabhūtena tassa phalaṃ hinoti pavattatīti hetu. Tathā ghaṭanti tenāti ghaṭo. Kilāsunoti payojanābhāvena avāvaṭā. Abbokiṇṇāni visabhāgehi. Āgāminiyā anāgateti attho. Imesaṃyeva noti dassanatthaṃ “sabbabuddhānaṃ hī”ti vuttaṃ. Yāvasāsanapariyantāti yāva buddhā dharanti, tāvāti attho. Khattiyabrāhmaṇāva uccā, tatthāpi visesaṃ dassetuṃ “uccanīcauḷāruḷārabhogā”ti. “Manasi katvā”tipi pāṭho. Upasampādyaupasampādyaiccetaṃ dvayaṃ māgadhe “upasampajjā”ti vuccati. Anupādāyāti ārammaṇakaraṇavasena aggahetvā. Āsavehīti kattari tatiyāvibhatti. Cittānīti paccattabahuvacanaṃ. Vimucciṃsūti kammakārake. Vimocitānīti adhippāyoti ācariyo. Āsavehīti padañca paccatte karaṇavacanaṃ katvā gaṇṭhipade attho pakāsito. Yadi ariyamaggena niruddhānaṃ āsavānaṃ vasena anāsavatā, loke cittānipi anāsavā siyuṃ. Na hi niruddhāni cittāni ārammaṇāni karontīti tāni aniruddhāsavavasena sāsavānīti ce. Sotāpannassa maggacittaṃ uparimaggavajjhāsavavasena sāsavaṃ, avasiṭṭhāsavasamucchindanānubhāvattā phalāni sāsavāni siyunti? Na, āsavasamucchindanānubhāvāgataphalattā. Bhiṃsanassa karaṇaṃ bhiṃsanakataṃ, tasmiṃ bhiṃsanakatasmiṃ, bhiṃsanakiriyāyāti attho. Itthiliṅgaṃ vipallāsaṃ katvā napuṃsakaliṅgaṃ, purisaliṅgaṃ vā katvā. Nimittattheti ettha –

Indeed, ‘it happens, it goes as a companion for the accomplishment of its own fruit’—thus hetu (cause) is in the agent sense. Nevertheless, here, ‘by that which has become the cause, its fruit happens, it proceeds’—thus hetu. Likewise, ‘they strive by means of it,’ hence ghaṭo. Kilāsuno means ‘not engaged’ due to the absence of purpose. Abbokiṇṇāni means unmixed with dissimilar persons. Āgāminiyā means ‘in the future.’ To show that this is not so for these alone, it is said: ‘for of all Buddhas….’ Yāvasāsanapariyantā means ‘as long as the Buddhas are living.’ Only khattiyas and brahmins are high; to show a distinction even there, it is said: ‘of high and low, excellent and coarse enjoyments.’ There is also the reading manasi katvā. This pair, upasampādya-upasampādya, is called upasampajjā in the Magadhan language. Anupādāya means ‘without grasping’ by way of making it an object. Āsavehi is the third case (instrumental) in the agent sense. Cittāni is the plural in the subjective sense (nominative). Vimucciṃsu is in the passive voice. The teacher says the intention is ‘they were liberated’ (vimocitāni). And taking the word āsavehi as an instrumental in the subjective sense, the meaning is explained in the Ganthipada. If, by means of the taints destroyed by the noble path, there is freedom from taints, then minds in the world would also be without taints. For destroyed minds do not make the taints their objects. If you say that they are with taints by way of the undestroyed taints, then would the path-consciousness of a stream-enterer be with taints by way of the taints to be abandoned by the higher paths, and would the fruits be with taints because of the power to cut off the remaining taints? No, because it is a fruit that comes from the path possessing the power to cut off the taints. The doing of what is frightening is a ‘frightening deed’ (bhiṃsanakataṃ); in that frightening deed (bhiṃsanakatasmiṃ), the meaning is ‘in the action of frightening.’ Having inverted the feminine gender and made it neuter or masculine, it is said 'bhiṃsanakatasmiṃ'. Here, in the sense of a sign—

“Cammani [V 0.0052] dīpinaṃ hanti, dantesu hanti kuñjaraṃ;

Vālesu cāmariṃ hanti, siṅgesu sarabho hato”ti. –

“One kills a leopard for its skin; one kills an elephant for its tusks; one kills a yak for its tail-hairs; a sarabha is killed for its horns.”

Adhikaraṇaṃ.

The legal issue.

20-21. Naciraṭṭhitikakāraṇe [M 0.0058] kathite ciraṭṭhitikakāraṇaṃ atthato vuttapaṭipakkhavasena kiñcāpi siddhaṃ, tathāpi taṃ therassa vinayapaññattiyācanāya okāsakāraṇādhippāyato vinayapaññattiyācanokāsaṃ pāpetuṃ puna bhagavantaṃ “ko pana, bhante, hetū”ti pucchi. Bhagavāpi yācanaṃ sampaṭicchitukāmo byākāsi. “Āsavaṭṭhānīyā saṅghe pātubhavantī”ti puggalassa saṅghapariyāpannattā vuttaṃ. Ādaratthavasenevettha dvikkhattuṃ vuttanti yasmā thero pubbe rājagahe, sampati verañjāyanti dvikkhattuṃ kāci, tasmā ādarena punappunaṃ yācayamānaṃ passitvā sayampi bhagavā ādareneva “āgamehi tvaṃ sāriputtā”ti āha. Tenetaṃ dīpeti “mā tvaṃ punappunaṃ yācāhi, sampaṭicchitāva mayā te yācanā, pubbenanu tavayācanaṃ sampaṭicchatāva mayā ettake kāle ettakāni sikkhāpadāni paññattāni, na tāva me sāvakānaṃ āṇāpātimokkhuddesānujānanakālo sampatto, takkānumānavasena tayā ‘etassa bhagavā kālo’ti punappunaṃ niddisiyamānopi nesa so kālo, kintu tathāgatova tattha kālaṃ jānissatī”ti. Yasmā pana “sikkhāpadapaññattikālato pabhuti āṇāpātimokkhameva uddisiyatī”ti vuttaṃ, tasmā pātimokkhuddesappahonakasikkhāpadameva sandhāyāha. “Tatthāti sikkhāpadapaññattiyācanāpekkhaṃ bhummavacana”nti ekameva padaṃ vuttaṃ tassā siddhiyā itarassa siddhito. “Sāvakānaṃ visayabhāvanti iminā mahāpadumattheravādo paṭikkhitto”ti anugaṇṭhipade vuttaṃ, taṃ sundaraṃ viya. Sammukhe garahā. Parammukhe upavādo. “Na, bhikkhave, ūnadasavassena…pe… dukkaṭassā”ti (mahāva. 75) idaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ bhagavā buddhattena dasavassiko hutvā paññapesi ūnadasavassikassa tassa tathā sikkhāpadapaññattiyā abhāvato. Na tadā atirekadasavassikova dasavassikānaṃ rattaññumahattappattito, tasmā taṃ sikkhāpadaṃ verañjāyaṃ vassāvāsato pubbe rājagahe eva paññattanti siddhaṃ, tasmiṃ siddhe siddhameva “yāva na saṅgho rattaññumahattaṃ pattoti vacanaṃ ito pubbe paṭhamayācanāyapi vutta”nti. Aṭṭhakathāyampi rattaññumahattappattakāle “dve sikkhāpadānī”ti gaṇanaparicchedavacanaṃ paṭhamayācanāya vuttavacanaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Aññathā rattaññumahattappattakāle dve eva, na aññanti āpajjati.

20-21. Although the reason for long duration is, in meaning, established by way of being the opposite of what was said regarding the reason for not lasting long, nevertheless, due to the intention of creating a reason for the opportunity for the Elder's request for the laying down of the Vinaya, in order to bring it to the point of an opportunity to request the laying down of the Vinaya, he again asked the Blessed One: “But what, venerable sir, is the cause?” The Blessed One, wishing to accept the request, explained. “Things that are grounds for the taints arise in the Sangha” was said because the individual is included in the Sangha. Regarding the statement that this was said twice here out of respect: since the Elder requested twice—previously at Rājagaha, and now at Verañjā—therefore, seeing him requesting again and again with respect, the Blessed One himself said with respect: “Wait, Sāriputta.” By this, he indicates the following meaning: “Do not request again and again. Your request has already been accepted by me. Was not your request previously accepted by me? In this much time, this many training rules have been laid down. The time for me to authorize the recitation of the authoritative Pātimokkha for my disciples has not yet arrived. Although you repeatedly point out or request by way of reasoning and inference, ‘This is the time, Blessed One,’ that is not the time. Rather, the Tathāgata himself will know the time for that.” And since it was said, “From the time of laying down the training rules, only the authoritative Pātimokkha is recited,” therefore, he said this referring only to the training rules sufficient for the recitation of the Pātimokkha. “The word ‘therein’ (tattha) is a locative expression with reference to the request for the laying down of the training rule.” Only this one word was stated because from the establishment of the one (the laying down of the training rule), the establishment of the other (the recitation of the Pātimokkha) follows. In the Anugaṇṭhipada it is said: “By this, ‘the state of being the domain of the disciples,’ the view of the Elder Mahāpaduma is refuted.” That seems incorrect. Reproach is in one’s presence; slander is behind one’s back. “Bhikkhus, by one who is less than ten years ordained… an offense of wrong doing.” (Mahāvagga 75) The Blessed One, having been of ten years’ seniority as a Buddha, laid down this training rule, because for one of less than ten years’ seniority there was no such laying down of a training rule. At that time, there was no one with more than ten years’ seniority, because those with ten years’ seniority had attained the state of seniority and greatness. Therefore, it is established that this training rule was laid down in Rājagaha itself before the rains residence in Verañjā. When that is established, it is indeed established that the statement, “So long as the Sangha has not attained the state of seniority and greatness,” was said even before this, at the first request. In the Commentary, too, the statement specifying the number, “two training rules,” at the time of attaining the state of seniority and greatness, was said with reference to the statement made at the first request. Otherwise, it would follow that at the time of attaining the state of seniority and greatness there were only two, and no other.

“Atha [M 0.0059] kho āyasmato sāriputtassā”tiādimhi ayamādito paṭṭhāya atthavibhāvanā – ayaṃ [V 0.0053] kirāyasmā assajittherato paṭiladdhaṃ ekagāthāmattakaṃ dhammapariyāyaṃ nayasatasahassehi vivecento arahattaṃ patvā sāvakapāramīñāṇe ṭhito “aho vata mahānubhāvoyaṃ saddhammo, yo vināpi dhammasāminā parammukhato sutamattepi mayhaṃ mahantaṃ guṇavisesaṃ janesi, sādhu vatāyaṃ saddhammo ciraṃ tiṭṭheyyā”ti cintento “katamesānaṃ nu kho buddhānaṃ bhagavantānaṃ…pe… na ciraṭṭhitika”nti tamatthaṃ, kāraṇañca attano aggasāvakañāṇena paṭivijjhitvā “sāvakānaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattantiādiciraṭṭhitikāraṇa”nti niṭṭhaṃ katvā vinayapaññattiyācanokāsakaraṇatthaṃ bhagavantaṃ pucchi. Tato pañhassa vissajjane vinayapaññattiyācanokāse sampatte “etassa bhagavā kālo, etassa sugata kālo”ti vinayapaññattiṃ yāci. Tato bhagavā tassā yācanāya sampaṭicchitabhāvaṃ, “etassa bhagavā kālo”ti vuttakālassa akālataṃ, kālassa ca anaññavisayataṃ dīpento “āgamehi tva”ntiādimāha, tato bhagavā tassa yācanaṃ, sattesu kāruññatañca paṭicca “tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū anupajjhāyakā anācariyakā anovadiyamānā”tiādinā (mahāva. 64) nayena vepullamahattataṃ paṭicca satthā sāvakānaṃ upajjhāyavattādīni vinayakammāni, tadanurūpasikkhāpadāni ca paññapesi. Tato anukkamena dvādasamavassaṃ verañjāyaṃ vasi. Tadā ca āyasmā sāriputto satthārā niddiṭṭhesu ciraṭṭhitihetūsu jātesu “navaṅgasatthusāsanamahattatā ca sampati jātā, vinayapaññatti ca bahutarā jātā, pātimokkhuddeso eveko na tāva sāvakānaṃ anuññāto, so ca parisuddhena saṅghena karīyati. Saṅghopi etarahi parisuddho pacchimakassa sotāpannattā”ti cintetvā pātimokkhuddesaṃ anujānāpetukāmo yattakehi ca sikkhāpadehi pātimokkhuddeso anujānīyati, tattakānaṃ paññattiyācanapubbaṅgamaṃ pātimokkhuddesaṃ yācanto pubbuppannavitakkasūcanapucchāvissajjanakkamavasena yācanokāse sampatte “etassa bhagavā kālo”tiādimāha.

Regarding ‘Then to the Venerable Sāriputta…,’ this is the explanation of the meaning from the beginning. The detailed account is as follows: this venerable one, having received a Dhamma discourse of just a single verse from the Elder Assaji, analyzed it with a hundred thousand methods, attained Arahantship, and, established in the knowledge of a disciple’s perfections, thought: “Oh, how wonderful is this good Dhamma of great power, which, even without the Master of the Dhamma, when merely heard from another, has generated in me such a great special quality! It would be good indeed if this good Dhamma were to last for a long time!” Reflecting thus, he considered: “Of which Blessed Ones, Buddhas… does the teaching not last long?” Having penetrated that matter and its cause with his knowledge as a chief disciple, he came to the conclusion that “the laying down of the training rule for the disciples, and so on, is the cause for the long duration,” and then, to create an opportunity to request the laying down of the Vinaya, he questioned the Blessed One. Then, upon the answering of the question, when the opportunity to request the laying down of the Vinaya arose, he requested the laying down of the Vinaya, saying: “This is the time, Blessed One! This is the time, Sugata!” Then the Blessed One, showing that his request was accepted, that the time stated as ‘This is the time, Blessed One’ was not yet the time, and that the time was not the domain of anyone other than a Buddha, said: “Wait, you…” and so on. Then the Blessed One, on account of his request and his compassion for beings, and on account of the Sangha’s attainment of growth and greatness, laid down for the disciples the Vinaya acts such as the duties of a preceptor, and the training rules corresponding to them, by the method beginning: “Now at that time, the bhikkhus were without preceptors, without teachers, uninstructed…” Then, in due course, he spent the twelfth rains-residence at Verañjā. And at that time, when the causes for the long duration pointed out by the Teacher had arisen, the Venerable Sāriputta reflected: “The greatness of the nine-limbed Teacher’s Dispensation has now come about, and the Vinaya rules laid down have become very many. Only the recitation of the Pātimokkha has not yet been authorized for the disciples, and that is to be done by a pure Sangha. The Sangha, too, is now pure, since the last of them is a stream-enterer.” Wishing to have the recitation of the Pātimokkha authorized, and requesting the recitation of the Pātimokkha, which is preceded by a request for the laying down of as many training rules by which the recitation of the Pātimokkha would be authorized, the Elder, when the opportunity for the request arrived by way of the sequence of indicating the previously arisen thought, questioning, and answering, said: “This is the time, Blessed One…” and so on.

Tattha “yaṃ bhagavā sāvakānaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññapeyyā”ti pātimokkhuddesappahonakasikkhāpadaṃ sandhāyāha, ayamattho bhaddālisuttena (ma. ni. 2.134 ādayo) dīpetabbo[M 0.0060]. Tattha hi bahūsu sikkhāpadesu paññattesu, paññapiyamānesu ca “na tāva bhaddāli satthā sāvakānaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññapetī”tiādi (ma. ni. 2.145) vuttaṃ apaññattaṃ upādāya, tathā idhāpi apaññattaṃ sandhāya vuttanti veditabbaṃ. Parisuddhattā saṅghassa sampati sāvakānaṃ āṇāpātimokkhuddesaṃ nānujānāmīti dassento “nirabbudo”tiādimāha. Na hi parisuddhe saṅghe ovādapātimokkhuddesassa anuddesakāraṇaṃ atthi, tasmiṃ sati āṇāpātimokkhuddesānujānanādhippāyato. Tathā ca so tato aṭṭhannaṃvassānaṃ accayena anuññāto. Yathāha pātimokkhaṭhapanakkhandhake (cūḷava. 386) “na dānāhaṃ, bhikkhave, ito paraṃ [V 0.0054] uposathaṃ karissāmi…pe… pātimokkhaṃ uddiseyyāthā”ti. Yaṃ pana upasampadakkhandhake (mahāva. 129) “tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū aññataraṃ bhikkhuṃ upasampādetvā ekakaṃ ohāya pakkamiṃsu…pe… so tassā methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevitvā cirena agamāsī”ti vatthu āgataṃ, taṃ sudinnavatthuto parato uppannampi tattha yathādhikāraṃ samodhānetuṃ vuttaṃ. Tathā tattheva “ubhayāni kho panassa pātimokkhāni vitthārena svāgatāni hontī”tiādinā (pāci. 147; a. ni. 8.52; 10.33) aṅgānipi veditabbāni. Na hi ādito eva ubhatopātimokkhāni siddhānīti. Apica ādito paṭṭhāya ayamanukkamo veditabbo, seyyathidaṃ – rāhulakumāre uppanne bodhisatto nikkhamitvā chabbassāni dukkaraṃ katvā sattame abhisambuddho, tasmiṃ eva saṃvacchare kapilavatthuṃ gantvā rāhulakumāraṃ pabbājesi. Ambalaṭṭhikarāhulovādasuttaṭṭhakathāyaṃ (ma. ni. aṭṭha. 2.107 ādayo) “ayañhi āyasmā sattavassikakāle bhagavantaṃ cīvarakaṇṇe gahetvā ‘dāyajjaṃ me samaṇa dehi, dāyajjaṃ me samaṇa dehī’ti dāyajjaṃ yācamāno bhagavatā dhammasenāpatisāriputtattherassa niyyādetvā pabbājito”ti ca vuttaṃ, tasmā rāhulakumāraṃ ārabbha “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tīhi saraṇagamanehi sāmaṇerapabbajja”nti (mahāva. 105) vuttattā saraṇagamanūpasampadā paṭhamavassabbhantare eva paṭikkhittā, ñatticatutthakammavasena upasampadā anuññātāti paññāyati. Apica rāhulavatthumhi “na, bhikkhave, ananuññāto mātāpitūhi putto pabbājetabbo, yo pabbājeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti (mahāva. 105) sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ, tasmā ito pubbepi sikkhāpadāni paññattānīti siddhaṃ.

Here, regarding the statement, “Whatever training rule the Blessed One would lay down for the disciples,” He said this referring to a training rule sufficient for the recitation of the Pātimokkha. This meaning should be illustrated by the Bhaddāli Sutta. For there, when many training rules had been laid down and were being laid down, it was said, “Not yet, Bhaddāli, does the Teacher lay down a training rule for the disciples,” and so on, referring to what was not yet laid down. Similarly, here too, it should be understood as referring to what had not yet been laid down. To show, 'Because the Saṅgha is pure, I do not now permit the recitation of the Pātimokkha by command for the disciples,' He said the words beginning with 'nirabbudo' (without blemish). For indeed, when the Saṅgha is pure, there is no reason for not reciting the Pātimokkha of exhortation; for if there were such a reason, it would be because of the intention to permit the recitation of the Pātimokkha by command. And so, after the lapse of eight years from then, it was permitted. As stated in the chapter on the suspension of the Pātimokkha: “Monks, from now on I will not perform the Uposatha… you should recite the Pātimokkha.” However, in the chapter on full ordination, the case is mentioned: “At that time, monks, having given full ordination to a certain monk, left him alone and departed… he, having engaged in sexual intercourse with her, came after a long time.” This incident, though arising later than the Sudinna case, was stated there to be connected according to the context. Likewise, in the same place, the factors are also to be understood from the text beginning with, “Both Pātimokkhas are well-mastered by him in detail,” and so on. For indeed, both Pātimokkhas were not established from the very beginning. Moreover, this sequence should be understood from the beginning, namely: When Prince Rāhula was born, the Bodhisatta went forth, practiced austerities for six years, and attained full enlightenment in the seventh. In that same year, he went to Kapilavatthu and ordained Prince Rāhula. In the commentary to the Ambalaṭṭhikarāhulovāda Sutta, it is also said: “For this venerable one, at the age of seven, took hold of the corner of the Blessed One’s robe and, while asking for his inheritance saying, ‘Give me my inheritance, ascetic, give me my inheritance, ascetic,’ was handed over by the Blessed One to the Elder Sāriputta, the General of the Dhamma, and ordained.” Therefore, because it was said on account of Prince Rāhula, 'Monks, I allow the going forth as a novice with the three refuges,' it appears that the full ordination by taking refuge was rejected within the first year itself, and the full ordination by means of a motion and three announcements was permitted. Furthermore, in the case of Rāhula, the training rule was laid down: “Monks, a son should not be ordained without the permission of his parents. Whoever ordains him commits an offense of wrong-doing.” Therefore, it is established that training rules had been laid down even before this.

Sutvā [M 0.0061] ca yo hetunirodhamaggaṃ,

Nirodhupāyaṃ paṭivijjhi khippaṃ;

Jātovapekkhena asesametaṃ,

Lokaṃ vipassī sugataggasisso.

He who, having heard of the noble cessation of causes, quickly penetrated the means to cessation—that foremost disciple of the Sugata, seeing the world with insight, became one who, with contemplative wisdom, comprehended this entire matter without remainder.

So dhammasenāpati aggasisso,

Saddhammarājassa tathāgatassa;

Sayaṃ munindena yasassa patto,

Anekaso soḷasadhā pasattho.

That Elder, the General of the Dhamma, the foremost disciple of the Tathāgata, the King of the True Dhamma, attained to glory in the Dispensation, having been praised many times and in sixteen ways by the Lord of Sages himself.

Tasmā [V 0.0055] hi sikkhāpadabandhakālo,

Ñātumpi loke atibhāriyova;

Pageva sikkhāpadabhāvabhedo,

Pageva añño ubhayattha tattha.

Therefore indeed, even to know the time of establishing a training rule is extremely difficult in the world; how much more so the distinction in the nature of a training rule, and how much more so any other distinction concerning both of these.

Paccekabuddhā api taṃ dvayantu,

Ñātuṃ na sakkāva pageva netuṃ;

Nissaṃsayaṃ tattha tathāgatova,

Jānissaticcāha tathāgatoti.

Even Paccekabuddhas are indeed unable to know that pair; how much more so are they unable to lead others to know it. In that matter, only the Tathāgata will know without a doubt; therefore, it is said, 'Tathāgata'.

Iccetamatthaṃ idha bhikkhu ñatvā,

Sikkhāpadānaṃ kamabhāvabhedaṃ;

Ñātuṃ sayaṃ no na pare ca netuṃ,

Pariyesitabbo idha yuttimaggo.

A monk in this Dispensation, having understood this meaning—that one is not able to know for oneself the distinction in the sequence and nature of the training rules, nor to lead others to know it—should seek here the suitable method.

Tattha kamabhedo sikkhāpadānaṃ parato āvi bhavissati. Bhāvabhedo tāva ukkhittakānuvattanapaccayā bhikkhu anāpattiko, bhikkhunī pana samanubhaṭṭhā pārājikā hoti. Pārājikāpattipaṭicchādane bhikkhussa dukkaṭaṃ, bhikkhuniyā pārājikaṃ. Duṭṭhullaṃ ārocentassa, paṭicchādentassa ca pācittiyaṃ. Mahāsāvajjaṃ pārājikaṃ ārocentassa, paṭicchādentassa ca bhikkhussa dukkaṭaṃ. Iccevamādīhi abhāvabhedasikkhāpadānaṃ idha bhāvabhedena yuttipariyesanaṃ sādhayamānopi siyā anummādavighātabhāgīti. Ettāvatā sakalassapi vinayapiṭakassa vitakkayācanakālakālaññūkāraṇaphalapayojanehi sattahi aṅgehi paṭimaṇḍitaṃ nidānamāyasmatā upālittherena nidassitaṃ hoti. Tattha therassa vinayapaññattiyācanahetubhūto [M 0.0062] vitakko nāma. Tasseva “etassa bhagavā kālo”tiādinā pavattā yācanā nāma. Rattaññūvepullalābhaggabāhusaccamahattappatti kālo nāma. Sabbaññū eva kālaññū nāma. Āsavaṭṭhānīyānaṃ dhammānaṃ pātubhāvo kāraṇaṃ nāma. “Tesaṃyeva āsavaṭṭhānīyānaṃ dhammānaṃ paṭighātāyā”ti vacanato āsavaṭṭhānīyadhammapaṭighāto phalaṃ nāma. “Yathayidaṃ brahmacariyaṃ addhaniyaṃ assā”ti vacanato sāsanabrahmacariyassa ciraṭṭhiti payojananti veditabbaṃ. Hoti cettha –

Here, the distinction in the sequence of the training rules will become apparent later on. As for the distinction in nature, firstly, on account of following an expelled monk, a monk is without offense; but a nun, having been formally censured, is defeated (pārājikā). For concealing a pārājika offense, there is a wrong-doing (dukkaṭa) for a monk; for a nun, it is a pārājika offense. For one who reports or conceals a gross offense (duṭṭhulla), there is a pācittiya offense. For a monk who reports or conceals a grave pārājika offense, there is a wrong-doing (dukkaṭa). Thus, by these and other examples, even while accomplishing the search for what is suitable by means of a distinction in nature for training rules that here have no such distinction, one might be of a nature free from madness and distress. By this much, the introduction to the entire Vinaya Piṭaka, adorned with seven factors—reasoning, requesting, timing, the knower of the right time, cause, result, and purpose—has been shown by the venerable Upāli Thera. Therein, what is called 'reasoning' (vitakka) is the Thera’s thought which was the reason for requesting the formulation of the Vinaya rules. What is called 'requesting' (yācanā) is that which occurred through statements like, “Blessed One, this is the time for it.” What is called 'timing' (kāla) is the attainment of greatness in seniority, greatness in abundance, greatness in the highest of gains, and greatness in great learning. The All-knowing One alone is called 'the knower of the right time' (kālaññū). The arising of defilement-producing phenomena is called 'cause' (kāraṇa). The result (phala) is the destruction of those very defilement-producing phenomena, as stated: “for the sake of destroying those very defilement-producing phenomena.” The purpose (payojana) is the long endurance of the holy life of the Dispensation, according to the statement: “so that this holy life may endure for a long time”; thus it should be known. And here there is this:

“Vitakko [V 0.0056] yācanā kālo, kālaññū kāraṇaṃ phalaṃ;

Payojananti sattaṅgaṃ, nidānaṃ vinayassidhā”ti.

“Reflection, requesting, the time, the knower of the time, the cause, the result, and the purpose—thus the introduction to the Vinaya here has seven factors.”

22. Antimamaṇḍalanti abbhantaramaṇḍalaṃ. Tañhi itaresaṃ anto hoti, khuddakamaṇḍalaṃ vā. Anumatidānavasena tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ datvā. Tesaṃ buddhānaṃ cārikāya vinetabbā veneyyasattā. Ocinantā viyāti bahupupphaṃ gacchaṃ mālākārā ciraṃ ocinanti, evaṃ bahuveneyyesu gāmādīsu ciraṃ vasantā veneyyapuññaṃ pariharantā caranti. Santaṃ sukhaṃ, na vedanāsukhaṃ viya saparipphandaṃ. Dasasahassacakkavāḷeti devānaṃ vasena vuttaṃ. Manussā pana imasmiṃyeva cakkavāḷe bodhaneyyā uppajjanti. Mahākaruṇāya dhuvaṃ sattasamavalokanaṃ. Otiṇṇeti parisamajjhaṃ āgate, ārocite vā. Yena kāraṇena mayaṃ tumhākaṃ deyyadhammaṃ dadeyyāma, taṃ kuto sakkā laddhuṃ. Bahukiccā hi gharāvāsāti. Dutiyavikappe tanti deyyadhammaṃ. “Tumhehi taṃ kuto laddhā”ti anugaṇṭhipade vuttaṃ. Keci pana “paṭhamaṃ kiriyaṃ pekkhati, dutiyaṃ deyyadhamma”nti vadanti. Ācariyo pana “paṭhamayojanāya yaṃ dānapuññaṃ, taṃ kuto labbhā. Puññantarāyabahulā hi gharāvāsāti. Dutiyayojanāya temāsabbhantare yamahaṃ dadeyyaṃ, atikkantakālattā tamahaṃ sampati kuto dadeyyanti dassetī”ti vadati. Sīlādikusaladhammasandassanādidhammaratanavassaṃ.

22. “The outermost circle” means the innermost circle. For it is inside the others, or it is a small circle. Having given to those monks by way of granting permission. Those beings to be trained are to be disciplined by the journeying of those Buddhas. “Like those who pick flowers” means that just as garland-makers pick for a long time from a bush with many flowers, so too, dwelling for a long time in villages and other places with many to be trained, they wander, bearing the merit of those to be trained. Peaceful happiness, not like the happiness of feeling which is accompanied by agitation. “The ten-thousandfold world-system” is spoken of with reference to the devas. Humans who are to be enlightened, however, arise only in this very world-system. Through great compassion, there is constant, thorough observation of beings. “Having descended” means having come into the midst of the assembly, or having been announced. “The gift that we would give you, where could it be obtained? For household life has many duties.” In the second alternative, ‘that’ refers to the gift. “How was that obtained by you?” is said in the sub-commentary. Some, however, say: “The first refers to the action; the second, to the gift.” The teacher, however, says: “In the first interpretation: ‘Whatever merit of giving there is, where can it be obtained? For household life is full of obstacles to merit.’ In the second interpretation, he shows this meaning: ‘Whatever I would have given within the three months, since that time has passed, how could I now give that?’” The rain of the jewel of the Dhamma, which is the demonstration of skillful qualities such as virtue, and so on.

23. Pattuṇṇadese pattuṇṇaṃ paṭavaraṃ. Mahāyāganti mahādānaṃ. Paripuṇṇasaṅkappanti temāsaṃ sotabbaṃ ajja suṇinti.

23. In the Pattuṇṇa country, Pattuṇṇa cloth is the finest cloth. “A great sacrifice” means a great gift. “Fulfilled intention” means: “The teaching that should be heard for three months, I have heard today.”

Tatridanti idaṃ kāraṇaṃ.

“Therein, this” means this cause.

Upāli [M 0.0063] dāsakoti ācariyaparamparato. Bāhirabbhantaranidānaṃ, sikkhāpadānaṃ paññattiṭṭhānasaṅkhātaṃ āveṇikanidānañca sandhāyāha “nidānassa pabhedadīpanato”ti. Theravādādi vatthuppabhedo. Sakāya paṭiññāya mettiyaṃ bhikkhuniṃ nāsethātiādi parasamayavivajjanatotiādi. Vibhaṅganayabhedadassanatoti tisso itthiyo bhūmaṭṭhaṃ thalaṭṭhantiādi. Etthāha – kiṃ bhagavato mārāvaṭṭanapaṭighātāya satti natthīti? Atthi, tathāpissa pacchā upaguttakāle pasādahetuttā adhivāseti. Ettha upaguttādhiṭṭhānaṃ vattabbaṃ. Buddhānaṃ āciṇṇanti dijadassanena kiṃpayojananti ce? Mārāvaṭṭanahetu brāhmaṇassa puññantarāyoti payojanaṃ.

Beginning with Upāli and Dāsaka, by way of the succession of teachers. Referring to the external and internal introductions, and the special introduction known as the basis for the promulgation of the training rules, he said, “because of the clarification of the divisions of the introduction.” The divisions of the subject matter are the Theravāda and so on. Referring to, “Destroy the bhikkhunī Mettiyā by your own promise,” and so on, he said, “because of the rejection of other doctrines.” Referring to, “three women—ground-dwelling, land-dwelling,” and so on, he said, “because of showing the divisions of the method of analysis.” Here, one might ask: “Does the Blessed One not have the power to repel Māra’s turning?” He does. Nevertheless, later, at the time of Upagutta, because it is a cause for faith, He endures it. Here, the determination of Upagutta should be told. If it is asked, “What is the purpose of the Buddhas’ custom of seeing the brahmin?” The purpose is: there is an obstruction to the brahmin’s merit on account of Māra’s turning.

Dijopi [V 0.0057] so māramanorathassa,

Bhaṅgaṃ karonto jinapuṅgavassa;

Sassissasaṅghassa adāsi dānaṃ,

Asesakaṃ kappiyabhaṇḍabhedaṃ.

That brahmin also, frustrating Māra’s desire, gave a gift of various allowable goods without remainder to the foremost of conquerors, together with his community of disciples.

Kiṃ bhagavā sasisso tāva mahantaṃ kappiyabhaṇḍaṃ ubbhaṇḍikaṃ katvā agamāsīti? Na agamāsi, temāsibhāgiyaṃ pana puññarāsikaṃ deyyadhammaṃ appaṭikkhipanto brāhmaṇassa upāyato satthā adāsi.

Did the Blessed One, with his disciples, having made a bundle of so many allowable goods, then depart? He did not depart. However, not rejecting the offered item, which was a mass of merit for a three-month portion, the Teacher, by a skillful means, gave it back to the brahmin.

Tadaññathā māramanorathova,

Pūro siyā neva dijassa bhiyyo;

Pāpaṃ mahantaṃ api pāpuṇeyya,

Micchābhimānena tathāgate so.

Otherwise, only Māra’s wish would be fulfilled, and the brahmin’s wish would not be. Moreover, that brahmin might also incur great demerit through wrong pride towards the Tathāgata.

Tasmā bhagavā assādiyanto taṃ deyyadhammaṃ appaṭikkhipanto upāyena brāhmaṇassa puññabuddhiṃ katvā, mārassa ca manorathavighātaṃ katvā agamāsīti, “ayaṃ nayo aṭṭhakathaṃ vināpi pāḷinayānulomato siddho”ti vadanti. Kathaṃ? –

“Therefore, the Blessed One, while not delighting in it, yet not rejecting that offered item, by a skillful means caused the brahmin's merit to increase, and having frustrated Māra’s wish, departed.” They say, “This method is established even without the commentary, in accordance with the way of the Pāḷi.” How so? –

“Satthā sasisso yadi aggahesi,

Dijassa taṃ cīvaramāditova;

Nāthassa no vīsativassakāle,

Virujjhate jīvakayācanāpi;

Tathāpi sabbaṃ suvicārayitvā,

Yuttaṃ nayaṃ cintayituṃva yutta”nti.

“If the Teacher with his disciples had accepted that robe of the brahmin from the very beginning, would not Jīvaka’s request in the Lord’s twentieth year also be contradicted? Nevertheless, having considered everything well, it is proper to reflect upon a suitable method.” The story of Verañjā is finished.

Idāni [M 0.0064] āyasmā upālitthero vinayapaññattiyā sādhāraṇanidānaṃ dassetvā sikkhāpadānaṃ pāṭekkaṃ paññattiṭṭhānasaṅkhātaṃ nidānamādiṃ katvā puggalapaññattianupaññattivibhāgāpattibhedantarāpattiādikaṃ nānappakāraṃ vidhiṃ nijjaṭaṃ niggumbaṃ katvā dassetuṃ “atha kho bhagavā verañjāyaṃ yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā”tiādimāhāti. Idha ṭhatvā –

Now the Venerable Elder Upāli, having shown the common introduction to the Vinaya regulations, in order to explain—making them unentangled and clear, and beginning with the introduction for each training rule individually, known as the basis of promulgation—the various procedures such as the individual regulation, supplementary regulation, analysis of offenses, different kinds of offenses, and so on, spoke the words beginning, “Then the Blessed One, having stayed at Verañjā as long as he pleased…” Standing here—

Sikkhāpadāna [V 0.0058] sabbesaṃ, kamabhedaṃ pakāsaye;

Tasmiṃ siddhe nidānānaṃ, kamasiddhi yato bhave.

One should make clear the sequence and distinctions of all the training rules; for when that is accomplished, the accomplishment of the sequence of the introductions comes to be.

Tattha sabbasikkhāpadānaṃ yathāsambhavaṃ desanākkamo pahānakkamo paṭipattikkamo uppattikkamoti catubbidho kamo labbhati. Tattha bhagavatā rājagahe bhikkhūnaṃ pātimokkhuddesaṃ anujānantena pātimokkhuddesassa yo desanākkamo anuññāto, taṃ desanākkamamanulomento āyasmā mahākassapo paṭhamaṃ pārājikuddesaṃ pucchi, tadanantaraṃ saṅghādisesuddesaṃ, tato aniyatuddesaṃ vitthāruddesañca pucchitvā tadanantaraṃ bhikkhunīvibhaṅgañca teneva anukkamena pucchi, nidānuddesantogadhānañca sarūpena anuddiṭṭhānaṃ pucchanatthaṃ khandhakepi pucchi. Etena ca khandhake paññattā thullaccayā saṅgahitā honti. Pucchitānukkameneva upālitthero taṃ sabbaṃ sāpattibhedādikaṃ desento thullaccayadubbhāsitaāpattisamuṭṭhānādidīpakaṃ antokatvā desesi, ayamettha desanākkamo. Ubhatovibhaṅgakhandhakato pana uccinitvā tadā parivārapāḷi visuṃ katā. Imameva nayaṃ sandhāya aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttaṃ “eteneva upāyena khandhakaparivārepi āropesu”ntiādi (pārā. aṭṭha. 1.paṭhamamahāsaṅgītikathā). Apica pāḷiyā “etenevupāyena ubhatovinaye pucchi. Puṭṭho puṭṭho āyasmā upāli vissajjesī”ti ettakameva vuttaṃ, tasmā mahākassapo ubhatovibhaṅge eva pucchi. Vissajjento pana āyasmā upāli nivarasesaṃ desento khandhakaparivāre antokatvā desesi. Tadā ca khandhakaparivārapāḷi visuṃ katāti ayaṃ desanākkamo. Yadi evaṃ nidānuddeso paṭhamaṃ desetabboti ce? Na, tadasambhavato. So hi “yassa siyā āpattī”tiādinā (mahāva. 134) nayena pavattattā paṭhamaṃ sikkhāpadasaṅgahitāsu āpattīsu adassitāsu na sambhavati. “Yāni mayā bhikkhūnaṃ paññattāni sikkhāpadāni, tāni nesaṃ pātimokkhuddesaṃ anujāneyya”nti vacanato sikkhāpadāneva paṭhamaṃ desetabbānīti pārājikuddesakkamo sambhavati.

Here, a fourfold sequence regarding all the training rules is obtained according to what is suitable: the sequence of teaching, the sequence of abandoning, the sequence of practice, and the sequence of arising. Among these, when the Blessed One at Rājagaha, in allowing the monks the Pātimokkha recitation, permitted a sequence of teaching for it, the Venerable Mahākassapa, conforming to that sequence of teaching, first questioned about the Pārājika recitation, and after that, the Saṅghādisesa recitation. Then, having questioned about the Aniyata recitation and the detailed recitation, he thereafter questioned about the Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga in the very same order. And for the purpose of asking about those things which, though included in the Nidāna-uddesa, were not stated in their own form, he also questioned about the Khandhakas. And by this, the Thullaccaya offenses laid down in the Khandhakas are included. Following the very sequence of questioning, the Elder Upāli, while teaching all of that beginning with the classification of offenses, taught it including that which illuminates the arising of Thullaccaya and Dubbhāsita offenses, etc. This, here, is the sequence of teaching. But then, having selected from the Ubhatovibhaṅga and the Khandhakas, at that time the Parivāra text was made separate. With reference to this very method, it is said in the commentary: “By this very means, they also included it in the Khandhakas and the Parivāra,” and so on. Moreover, in the Pāḷi only this much is said: “By this very means he questioned about both Vinayas. Being questioned again and again, the Venerable Upāli answered.” Therefore, Mahākassapa questioned only about the Ubhatovibhaṅga. But the Venerable Upāli, when answering, taught without remainder, including the Khandhakas and the Parivāra. And at that time, the Khandhaka and Parivāra texts were made separate. This is the sequence of teaching. If it is said, “If so, should the Nidāna-uddesa be taught first?” No, because that is not possible. For since it proceeds by the method, “If there should be an offense for someone,” etc., it is not possible before the offenses included in the training rules have been shown. Based on the statement, “Those training rules that have been laid down by me for the monks, those he should permit them for the Pātimokkha recitation,” the training rules themselves must be taught first. Thus, the sequence of the Pārājika recitation is possible.

Pārājikuddesādisaṅgahitānaṃ [M 0.0065] āpattiakusalānaṃ yathoḷārikakkamena pahātabbattā pahānakkamopettha sambhavati. Upasampannasamanantaraṃ “tāvadeva cattāri akaraṇīyāni ācikkhitabbānī”ti (mahāva. 129) vacanato “samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesū”ti (dī. ni. 1.193) vacanato ca yathā garukaṃ ācikkhaṇaṃ sikkhanena paṭipattikkamopettha sambhavati, evamimehi tīhi kamehi desetabbānampetesaṃ sikkhāpadānaṃ yathāsambhavaṃ uppattikkamo sambhavati. Tathā hi yaṃ yaṃ sādhāraṇaṃ, taṃ taṃ bhikkhuṃ ārabbha uppanne eva vatthusmiṃ “yā pana bhikkhunī chandaso methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭiseveyyā”ti bhikkhunīnampi paññattaṃ. Aññathā taṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ [V 0.0059] anuppannapaññatti siyā. Tato “anuppannapaññatti tasmiṃ natthī”ti (pari. 247) parivāre etaṃ vacanaṃ virujjhati, ettāvatā purimena kamattayena paṭhamaṃ desetabbataṃ patte pārājikuddese paṭhamuppannattā methunadhammapārājikaṃ sabbapaṭhamaṃ desetukāmo upālitthero “tatra sudaṃ bhagavā vesāliya”nti vesālimeva pāpetvā ṭhapesi. Aññathā bārāṇasiyaṃ paññattānaṃ “na, bhikkhave, manussamaṃsaṃ paribhuñjitabba”nti (mahāva. 280) evamādīnaṃ desanādhippāye sati bārāṇasiṃ pāpetvā ṭhapeyyāti.

The sequence of abandoning also arises here, because the unwholesome states that are offenses, included in the Pārājika recitation and so on, are to be abandoned in sequence according to their grossness. Immediately after full ordination, because of the statements, “The four things not to be done should be explained at once,” and, “One trains by undertaking the training rules,” the sequence of practice also arises here through training in accordance with the declaration of the grave offenses. Thus, for these training rules that are to be taught by these three sequences, the sequence of arising is possible according to circumstance. For so it is: whichever training rule is common, when a case has arisen concerning a monk, that very rule is also laid down for nuns with the words, “Whatever nun should willingly engage in sexual intercourse…” Otherwise, that would be a rule without a precedent for the nuns. Therefore, this would contradict the statement in the Parivāra, “There is no rule without a precedent in that case.” To this extent, in the Pārājika recitation, which, by the former triad of sequences, attained the state of being what should be taught first, and because the Pārājika on sexual intercourse arose first, the Elder Upāli, wishing to teach it first of all, established the setting in Vesālī itself with the words, “There, it is said, the Blessed One was in Vesālī…” Otherwise, if there were an intention to teach the training rules laid down in Bārāṇasī, such as, “Monks, human flesh is not to be eaten,” he would have established the setting in Bārāṇasī.

Abbhantaranidānakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on the Internal Preamble is concluded.

Verañjakaṇḍavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Verañja Section is concluded.

1. Pārājikakaṇḍo

1. The Chapter on Defeat

1. Paṭhamapārājikaṃ

1. The First Offense of Defeat

Sudinnabhāṇavāravaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Recitation Section concerning Sudinna

Paṭhamassettha [M 0.0066][V 0.0060] nidāne, ṭhatvā pārājikassa viññeyyo;

Codanāparihāranayo, puggalavatthuppakāsaneyeva.

Here, standing in the prologue of the first pārājika, the method of accusation and defense should be understood precisely in the exposition of the person and the case.

Tattha bhagavā verañjāyaṃ vutthavasso anupubbena cārikaṃ caranto kattikajuṇhapakkhe eva vesāliṃ pāpuṇitvā yāva paṭhamapārājikasikkhāpadapaññāpanaṃ, tāva aṭṭha vassāni vesāliyaṃyeva viharanto viya pāḷikkamena dissati, na ca bhagavā tāvattakaṃ kālaṃ tattheva vihāsi. So hi sudinnassa sāvakānaṃ santike pabbajjaṃ upasampadañca anujānitvā yathābhirantaṃ tattha viharitvā cārikaṃ caranto bhesakaḷāvanaṃ patvā tattha terasamaṃ vassaṃ vasi, teneva anukkamena sāvatthiṃ patvā cuddasamaṃ vassaṃ vasi, pannarasamaṃ kapilavatthumhi, soḷasamaṃ āḷaviyaṃ, tato vutthavasso cārikaṃ caranto rājagahaṃ patvā sattarasamaṃ vasi, iminā anukkamena aparānipi tīṇi vassāni tattheva vasi. Ettāvatā bhagavā paripuṇṇavīsativasso rājagahato anupubbena vesāliṃ pāpuṇi, tato upasampadāya aṭṭhavassiko sudinno vesāliyaṃyeva methunaṃ dhammaṃ abhiviññāpesi, tato bhagavā tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ paṭhamaṃ pārājikaṃ paññapesīti veditabbaṃ. Tattha yasmā upālitthero ito paṭhamataraṃ tattha vesāliyañca paññattasikkhāpadāni adassetukāmo, vinayanidānānantaraṃ paṭhamapārājikameva dassetukāmo, tasmā vesāliyaṃ paṭhamaṃ nivāsaṃ, pacchā imassa sikkhāpadassa paññattikāle nivāsañca ekato katvā “tatra sudaṃ bhagavā vesāliya”ntiādimāha, tena vuttaṃ “paṭhamassettha nidāne, ṭhatvā [V 0.0061] …pe… pakāsaneyevā”ti. Tasmā imasmiṃ paṭhamapārājikassa paññattiṭṭhānasaṅkhāte nidāne ṭhatvā “tena kho pana samayena vesāliyā avidūre kalandagāmo nāma hoti…pe… aññataraṃ vajjigāmaṃ upanissāya viharatī”ti etasmiṃ imassa sikkhāpadassa puggalappakāsane, “tena kho pana samayena vajjī dubbhikkhā hoti…pe… tikkhattuṃ methunaṃ dhammaṃ abhiviññāpesī”ti (pārā. 30) imasmiṃ vatthuppakāsane ca codanānayo, parihāranayo ca veditabboti [M 0.0067] vuttaṃ hoti. Tatrāyaṃ pakāsanā – kimatthaṃ therena aññesaṃ sikkhāpadānaṃ puggalavatthūni viya saṅkhepato avatvā yattha ca so uppanno, yathā ca dhamme pasanno, yathā ca pabbajito, yathā ca imaṃ vatthuṃ uppādeti, taṃ sabbaṃ anavasesetvā puggalavatthūni vitthārato vuttānīti ce? Vuccate –

There, the Blessed One, having completed the rains-residence at Verañjā, wandering by stages, arrived at Vesālī in the bright fortnight of Kattika. Up to the laying down of the first Pārājika training rule, he appears, in the sequence of the Pāli, to have resided in Vesālī for eight years. However, the Blessed One did not stay there for that entire period. For, having granted the going forth and full ordination to Sudinna in the presence of the disciples, he stayed there as long as he pleased and then wandered on. Reaching the Bhesakaḷāvana, he spent his thirteenth rains-residence there. Following this sequence, he arrived at Sāvatthī and spent his fourteenth rains-residence there, his fifteenth at Kapilavatthu, and his sixteenth at Āḷavī. Then, having completed the rains-residence, he wandered on and reached Rājagaha, where he spent his seventeenth rains-residence. In this manner, he spent three more years there. By this time, the Blessed One had completed twenty years and gradually arrived at Vesālī from Rājagaha. Then, Sudinna, who had been ordained for eight years, engaged in sexual intercourse there in Vesālī. Then, regarding this matter, the Blessed One laid down the first Pārājika rule—this is to be understood. Here, because the Elder Upāli did not wish to show the training rules laid down prior to this one, both there and in Vesālī, but wished to show only the first Pārājika immediately after the origin of the Vinaya, he therefore combined the first residence in Vesālī and the later residence at the time of the laying down of this training rule and said, 'At that time, the Blessed One was dwelling at Vesālī…' Therefore, it is said, 'In this origin of the first… it should be explained.' Thus, standing in this origin of the first Pārājika, which is designated as the place of its establishment, it is said that in the exposition of the individual related to this training rule—namely, 'At that time, not far from Vesālī, there was a village named Kalandagāma… dwelling near a certain Vajjian village'—and in the exposition of the matter—'At that time, the Vajjis were suffering from famine… he engaged in sexual intercourse three times'—the method of accusation and the method of resolution should be understood. Herein, this exposition: If it is asked, 'Why did the Elder not state the individuals and matters related to other training rules briefly, as with other training rules, but instead described in detail, without omitting anything, where he arose, how he gained faith in the Dhamma, how he went forth, and how he caused this matter to arise?' It is said—

Evaṃ saddhāya kicchena, mahante bhogañātake;

Hitvā pabbajitānampi, pesalānampi sabbaso.

Thus, with great faith, having abandoned great possessions and relatives, even for those who have gone forth with difficulty, and for those who are altogether virtuous,

Sabbalāmakadhammāyaṃ, methuno yadi sambhave;

Na dhammadesanāyeva, siddhā virati sabbaso.

If this act of sexual intercourse, the lowest of all things, should occur, then complete abstinence is in no way accomplished by the teaching of the Dhamma alone.

Tasmā navaṅgasaddhamme, satthārā desitepi ca;

Vinayo paññapetabbo, tato dhammavisuddhihi.

Therefore, even though the nine-factored Good Dhamma has been taught by the Teacher, the Vinaya should be laid down. From that, indeed, comes the special purity of the Dhamma.

Vinayābhāvato evaṃ, ajjhācāro bhavissati;

Tasmā vinayapaññatti, sātthikā pesalassapi.

Thus, due to the absence of the Vinaya, transgression will occur. Therefore, the laying down of the Vinaya is beneficial even for the virtuous.

Anādīnavadassāvī, yasmā yaṃ pāpamācari;

Vinayoyeva saddhānaṃ, ādīnavavibhāvino.

Because one who does not see the danger commits an evil act, it is only the Vinaya that makes the danger clear to the faithful.

Tasmā saddhānusārīnaṃ, vinayo sātthakova yaṃ;

Dhammo dhammānusārīnaṃ, tato ubhayadesanā.

Therefore, this Vinaya is indeed beneficial for the faith-followers, and this Dhamma is indeed beneficial for the Dhamma-followers. Therefore, there is the teaching of both.

Api ca yadi paṇṇattivītikkamaṃ akarontassāpi yāva brahmalokā ayaso patthaṭo, pagevaññesanti dassanatthaṃ ajjhācārassa pākaṭabhāvadīpanaṃ. Kathaṃ? –

Furthermore, if ill repute spread as far as the Brahma world even for one not transgressing the rule, what then to say of others? This is to show the manifest nature of the transgression. How?

Abhabbo [V 0.0062] arahattassa, sudinno puttamātaro;

Bhabbānuppannapaññatti, tadatthaṃ na katā ayaṃ.

Sudinna is incapable of Arahantship; the son and mother are capable. This rule concerning what had not yet arisen was not made for their sake.

Nanu māgaṇḍikaṃ ajjhupekkhitvā mātāpitūnamassā hitatthaṃ dhammaṃ desetīti imamatthaṃ dassetuṃ bījakabījakamātūnaṃ arahattuppatti therena dīpitā. “Tena kho pana samayena vesāliyā avidūre kalandagāmo nāma hoti, yena samayena sudinno purāṇadutiyikāya methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevī”ti vā “yena samayena bhagavā paṭhamapārājikaṃ paññapesī”ti vā vacanaṃ idha na yujjati. Kasmā? “Idha pana hetuattho karaṇattho ca sambhavatī”ti vuttaṃ aṭṭhakathāvacanañhi idha na labbhati. Ciraniviṭṭho hi so gāmo[M 0.0068], na tasmiṃyeva samayeti. Yasmā pana so ciraniviṭṭhopi ca gāmo attano niviṭṭhakālato paṭṭhāya sabbakālamatthīti vattabbataṃ arahati, tena pariyāyena “tena kho pana samayena vesāliyā avidūre kalandagāmo nāma hotī”ti vuttaṃ.
