And just as one who undertakes a training rule is said to undertake virtue, so it is fitting to say that one who rejects a training rule rejects the training designated as virtue. Therefore, it is stated there: 'Whatever training he has undertaken, without having rejected that.' In permitting higher ordination for one who, having rejected the training, has engaged in sexual intercourse, one does not, in fact, abolish the rule. For that person did not engage in it while being a bhikkhu, and the rule is laid down as, 'Whatever bhikkhu...' Thus far, in brief, what should be said regarding 'one who has undertaken the training and livelihood' has been said.

Kiṃ iminā visesavacanena payojanaṃ, nanu “yo pana bhikkhu sikkhaṃ appaccakkhāya dubbalyaṃ anāvikatvā…pe… asaṃvāso”ti ettakameva vattabbanti ce[M 0.0084]? Na vattabbaṃ aniṭṭhappasaṅgato. Yo pana sikkhāsājīvasamāpanno theyyasaṃvāsādiko kevalena samaññāmattena, paṭiññāmattena vā bhikkhu, tassāpi sikkhāpaccakkhānaṃ atthi. Sikkhaṃ appaccakkhāya ca methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevantassa pārājikāpatti. Yo vā pacchā pārājikaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitvā na sikkhāsājīvasamāpanno tassa ca, yo vā pakkhapaṇḍakattā paṇḍakabhāvūpagamanena na sikkhāsājīvasamāpanno tassa ca tadubhayaṃ atthīti āpajjati. “Paṇḍakabhāvapakkhe ca pakkhapaṇḍako upasampadāya na vatthū”ti vuttaṃ, tasmā itarasmiṃ pakkhe vatthūti siddhaṃ, tasmiṃ pakkhe upasampanno paṇḍakabhāvapakkhe paṇḍakattā na sikkhāsājīvasamāpanno, so pariccajitabbasikkhāya abhāvena sikkhaṃ appaccakkhāya mukhena parassa aṅgajātaggahaṇādayo methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭiseveyya, tassa kuto pārājikāpattīti adhippāyo. Ayaṃ nayo apaṇḍakapakkhaṃ alabhamānasseva parato yujjati, labhantassa pana arūpasattānaṃ kusalānaṃ samāpattikkhaṇe bhavaṅgavicchede satipi amaraṇaṃ viya paṇḍakabhāvapakkhepi bhikkhubhāvo atthi. Saṃvāsaṃ vā sādiyantassa na theyyasaṃvāsakabhāvo atthi antimavatthuṃ ajjhāpannassa viya. Na ca sahaseyyādikaṃ janeti. Gaṇapūrako pana na hoti antimavatthuṃ ajjhāpanno viya, na so sikkhāsājīvasamāpanno, itarasmiṃ pana pakkhe hoti, ayaṃ imassa tato viseso. Kimayaṃ sahetuko, udāhu ahetukoti? Na ahetuko. Yato upasampadā tassa apaṇḍakapakkhe anuññātā sahetukapaṭisandhikattā. Paṇḍakabhāvapakkhepi kissa nānuññātāti ce? Paṇḍakabhūtattā opakkamikapaṇḍakassa viya.

What is the purpose of this special statement? If one were to ask, "Should one not just say this much: 'Whatever bhikkhu, without renouncing the training and without revealing his weakness... is not in communion'?" It should not be said, because of the consequence of an undesirable meaning. For whoever is not one who has entered upon the training and livelihood—such as a thief-in-communion—or is a bhikkhu by mere designation or by mere claim, even for such a one there is the renunciation of the training. And for one who engages in the sexual act without renouncing the training, there is a pārājika offense. Or for whoever, having later fallen into a pārājika offense, is not one who has entered upon the training and livelihood; and for whoever, due to being a fortnightly paṇḍaka, by reaching the state of a paṇḍaka, is not one who has entered upon the training and livelihood—for both of them, it follows that those two factors exist. It has been said, "In the phase of being a paṇḍaka, a fortnightly paṇḍaka is not a basis for ordination." Therefore, it is established that in the other phase, he is a basis. One ordained in that phase, when in the paṇḍaka phase, due to being a paṇḍaka, is not one who has entered upon the training and livelihood. He, due to the absence of a training that ought to be abandoned, if he were to engage in the sexual act—such as grasping another's genitals with the mouth and so on—without renouncing the training, whence could there be a pārājika offense for him? This is the intention. This method is applicable only for one who does not subsequently obtain the non-paṇḍaka phase. For one who does obtain it, however, just as for formless beings at the moment of attaining wholesome states, even though there is an interruption of the life-continuum, it is like not dying; so too, even in the paṇḍaka phase, the bhikkhu-state exists. Or for one who consents to communion, there is no state of being a thief-in-communion, just as for one who has committed a final offense. And it does not generate the offenses of sleeping together, etc. However, he is not one who completes a quorum, just like one who has committed a final offense. He is not one who has entered upon the training and livelihood, but in the other phase, he is. This is the difference of this one from that one. Is this one with root-conditions, or without root-conditions? Not without root-conditions. Because ordination is permitted for him in the non-paṇḍaka phase, due to his having a rebirth-linking with root-conditions. If one asks, "Why is it not permitted even in the paṇḍaka phase?" Because of being a paṇḍaka, just as for an opakkamikapaṇḍaka.

Apica [V 0.0077] sikkhāsājīvasamāpannoti iminā tassa sikkhāsamādānaṃ dīpetvā taṃ samādinnasikkhaṃ appaccakkhāya tattha ca dubbalyaṃ anāvikatvāti vattuṃ yujjati, na aññathāti iminā kāraṇena yathāvuttāniṭṭhappasaṅgato “yo pana bhikkhu bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāsājīvasamāpanno sikkhaṃ appaccakkhāyā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Yathā cettha, tathā “yo pana bhikkhu bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāsājīvasamāpanno sikkhaṃ appaccakkhāya dubbalyaṃ anāvikatvā gāmā vā araññā vā adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyeyya (pārā. 89), sugatacīvarappamāṇaṃ cīvaraṃ kārāpeyya atirekaṃ vā, chedanakaṃ pācittiya”ntiādinā (pāci. 548) nayena sabbattha yojetabbaṃ[M 0.0085]. Antamaso tiracchānagatāyapīti manussitthiṃ upādāya vuttaṃ. Na hi “pageva paṇḍake purise vā”ti vattuṃ yujjati. Sesaṃ tattha tattha vuttanayameva.

Furthermore, by the phrase 'one who has undertaken the training and livelihood,' having explained that person's undertaking of the training, it is appropriate to say 'without renouncing that undertaken training and without revealing weakness therein'—not otherwise. For this reason, to avoid the consequence of the previously mentioned undesirable meaning, it is stated: 'Whatever bhikkhu, having undertaken the training and livelihood of bhikkhus, without renouncing the training...' and so on. As it is here, so too should it be applied everywhere by the method of such passages as: 'Whatever bhikkhu, having undertaken the training and livelihood of bhikkhus, without renouncing the training and without revealing weakness, should take from a village or a forest what is not given, which is considered theft; or should have a robe made of the Sugata-measure or in excess, it is an offense requiring cutting,' and so on. The phrase 'even with a female animal' is stated with reference to a human woman. For it is not appropriate to say, 'how much more so a paṇḍaka or a man.' The remainder is just as has been explained in each respective case.

Ayaṃ paṭhamapārājikassa mātikāya tāva vinicchayo.

This, for now, is the analysis in the matrix of the first Pārājika.

Catubbidhavinayakathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Discourse on the Fourfold Vinaya

45. Nīharitvāti ettha sāsanato nīharitvāti attho. “Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā nānuyuñjitabbaṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Suttaṃ na jānāti, suttānulomaṃ na jānātī”ti (pari. 442) evamādito hi pariyattisāsanato suttaṃ, suttānulomañca nīharitvā pakāsesuṃ. “Anāpatti evaṃ amhākaṃ ācariyānaṃ uggaho paripucchāti bhaṇatī”ti evamādito pariyattisāsanato ācariyavādaṃ nīharitvā pakāsesuṃ. Bhārukacchakavatthusmiṃ “āyasmā upāli evamāha – anāpatti, āvuso, supinantenā”ti (pārā. 78) evamādito pariyattisāsanato eva attanomatiṃ nīharitvā pakāsesuṃ. Tāya hi attanomatiyā thero etadaggaṭṭhānaṃ labhi. Api ca vuttañhetaṃ bhagavatā “anupasampannena paññattena vā apaññattena vā vuccamāno…pe… anādariyaṃ karoti, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti (pāci. 343). Tattha hi paññattaṃ nāma suttaṃ. Sesattayaṃ apaññattaṃ nāma. Tenāyaṃ “catubbidhañhi vinayaṃ, mahātherā”ti gāthā suvuttā. Yaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ nāgasenattherena. Āhaccapadenāti aṭṭha vaṇṇaṭṭhānāni āhacca vuttena padanikāyenāti attho, udāhaṭena kaṇṭhokkantena padasamūhenāti adhippāyo. Rasenāti tassa āhaccabhāsitassa rasena, tato uddhaṭena vinicchayenāti attho. Suttacchāyā viya hi suttānulomaṃ. Ācariyavādo “ācariyavaṃso”ti vutto pāḷiyaṃ vuttānaṃ ācariyānaṃ paramparāya ābhatova pamāṇanti dassanatthaṃ. Adhippāyoti kāraṇopapattisiddho uhāpohanayappavatto [V 0.0078] paccakkhādipamāṇapatirūpako. Adhippāyoti ettha “attanomatī”ti keci atthaṃ vadanti.

45. Herein, 'having extracted' means having extracted from the Teaching of the scriptures. Indeed, beginning with 'Upāli, a monk endowed with five qualities should not be questioned. What five? He does not know the Sutta, he does not know what accords with the Sutta,' they extracted the Sutta and what accords with the Sutta from the Teaching of the scriptures and proclaimed it. Beginning with '“There is no offense,” thus is the learning and inquiry of our teachers, he says,' they extracted the teachers' doctrine from the Teaching of the scriptures and proclaimed it. In the case of the Bhārukacchaka, beginning with 'The Venerable Upāli said thus: “Friends, there is no offense in a dream,”' they extracted their own opinion from the Teaching of the scriptures itself and proclaimed it. Indeed, by that very own opinion, the Elder attained the foremost position. Moreover, this was said by the Blessed One: 'Being told by one who is not fully ordained about what is prescribed or not prescribed... if he shows disrespect, there is an offense of wrong-doing.' Therein, what is called 'prescribed' is the Sutta. The remaining three are called 'not prescribed.' Therefore, this verse is well-spoken: 'For the Vinaya is fourfold, O great elders.' In reference to which it was said by the Elder Nāgasena. 'By a direct word' (āhaccapadena) means by a collection of words spoken by touching upon the eight places of articulation; the intention is by a group of words uttered, produced from the throat. 'By the essence' (rasena) means by the judgment of that which is spoken directly; the meaning is by the judgment extracted from that. Indeed, what accords with the Sutta is like the shadow of the Sutta. The teachers' doctrine is called the 'lineage of teachers' in order to show that only what is brought down through the succession of teachers mentioned in the Pāli is authoritative. 'Intention' (adhippāyo) is that which is established by reason and grounds, which proceeds by the method of induction and deduction, and which resembles the standards of direct perception and so on. Herein, regarding 'intention,' some state the meaning is 'one's own opinion.'

Parivāraṭṭhakathāyaṃ[M 0.0086], idha ca kiñcāpi “suttānulomaṃ nāma cattāro mahāpadesā”ti vuttaṃ, atha kho mahāpadesanayasiddhaṃ paṭikkhittāpaṭikkhittaṃ anuññātānanuññātaṃ kappiyākappiyanti atthato vuttaṃ hoti. Tattha yasmā ṭhānaṃ okāso padesoti kāraṇavevacanāni “aṭṭhānametaṃ, ānanda, anavakāso”tiādi (pārā. 43) sāsanato, “niggahaṭṭhāna”nti ca “asandiṭṭhiṭṭhāna”nti ca “asandiṭṭhi ca pana padeso”ti ca lokato, tasmā mahāpadesāti mahākāraṇānīti attho. Kāraṇaṃ nāma ñāpako hetu idhādhippetaṃ. Mahantabhāvo pana tesaṃ mahāvisayattā mahābhūtānaṃ viya. Te duvidhā vinayamahāpadesā suttantikamahāpadesā cāti. Tattha vinayamahāpadesā vinaye payogaṃ gacchanti, itare ubhayatthāpi, teneva parivāre anuyogavatte “dhammaṃ na jānāti, dhammānulomaṃ na jānātī”ti (pari. 442) vuttaṃ. Tattha dhammanti ṭhapetvā vinayapiṭakaṃ avasesapiṭakadvayaṃ. Dhammānulomanti suttantike cattāro mahāpadese. Tattha yo dhammaṃ dhammānulomañceva jānāti, na vinayaṃ vinayānulomañca, so “dhammaṃ rakkhāmī”ti vinayaṃ ubbinayaṃ karoti, itaro “vinayaṃ rakkhāmī”ti dhammaṃ uddhammaṃ karoti, ubhayaṃ jānanto ubhayampi sampādeti.

In the commentary on the Parivāra, and also here in this commentary on the Pārājika section, although it is said, “The four great authorities are what is called ‘conformity with the Suttas’,” nevertheless, what is established by the method of the great authorities—what is rejected and not rejected, what is permitted and not permitted, what is allowable and not allowable—is what is meant. Therein, because the words ‘ṭhāna’ (place), ‘okāsa’ (opportunity), and ‘padesa’ (region) are synonyms for ‘kāraṇa’ (reason)—according to the Teaching, as in, “This is impossible, Ānanda, there is no opportunity,” etc., and according to worldly usage, as in “a place of censure,” “a position not seen,” and “a region not seen”—therefore, ‘mahāpadesā’ means ‘great reasons.’ Here, by ‘reason’ is intended a cause that makes known. Their greatness, however, is due to their vast scope, like that of the great elements. They are of two kinds: the Vinaya great authorities and the Suttantika great authorities. Among these, the Vinaya great authorities are applied only in the Vinaya, while the others are applied in both. For that very reason, in the Parivāra, in the section on the practice of inquiry, it is said, “He does not know the Dhamma; he does not know what conforms to the Dhamma.” Therein, by ‘Dhamma’ is intended the remaining two Piṭakas, having excluded the Vinaya Piṭaka. By ‘what conforms to the Dhamma’ is intended the four great authorities in the Suttanta. Therein, one who knows the Dhamma and what conforms to the Dhamma, but does not know the Vinaya and what conforms to the Vinaya, thinking, “I will protect the Dhamma,” makes the Vinaya into non-Vinaya. The other, thinking, “I will protect the Vinaya,” makes the Dhamma into non-Dhamma. One who knows both accomplishes both.

Tatridaṃ mukhamattaṃ – tattha paṭhamo “so ce pavesanaṃ sādiyati, paviṭṭhaṃ, ṭhitaṃ, uddharaṇaṃ sādiyati āpatti, na sādiyati anāpattī”ti ettha vippaṭipajjati. So hāyasmā sukhavedanīyassa upādinnaphoṭṭhabbassa, kāyindriyassa ca samāyoge sati paṭivijānanto kāyikasukhavedanuppattimattena sādiyati nāmāti paricchinditvā tassa āpatti pārājikassāti asevanādhippāyassapi āpattippasaṅgaṃ karoti, tathā yassa santhatattā vā yonidosavasena vā dukkhā asātā vedanā, vātopahaṭagattatāya vā neva kāyikavedanā, tassa jānato ajānatopi “anāpatti asādiyantassā”ti (pārā. 76) suttantaṃ dassetvā sevanādhippāyassāpi anāpattippasaṅgaṃ karoti, tathā yadi mocanarāgena upakkamato mutte saṅghādiseso, pageva methunarāgenāti dukkaṭaṭṭhānaṃ gahetvā saṅghādisesaṭṭhānaṃ karoti, evaṃ vinayaṃ ubbinayaṃ karoti nāma. Itaro “anāpatti ajānantassāti vuttattā jānato jānaneneva [M 0.0087] sukhavedanā hotu vā mā vā sādiyanā hotī”ti vatvā asevanādhippāyassapi jānato anāpattiṭṭhāne āpattiṃ karoti, anavajjaṃ sāvajjaṃ karotīti evaṃ dhammaṃ uddhammaṃ karoti. Ubhayaṃ pana jānanto “bhikkhussa sevanacittaṃ upaṭṭhiteti (pārā. 57) vacanato sevanacittamevettha [V 0.0079] pamāṇaṃ, tassa bhāvena āpatti pārājikassa, abhāvena anāpattī”ti vatvā ubhayampi rakkhati sampādeti. Iminā nayena sabbasikkhāpadesu yathāsambhavaṃ sappayojanā kātabbā.

Here is a mere introduction: Among them, the first, the Suttantika, errs in this matter: ‘If he consents to the entry, to its remaining once entered, and to its withdrawal, there is an offense; if he does not consent, there is no offense.’ That venerable one, determining that ‘consenting’ is so called merely by the arising of pleasant bodily feeling while knowing the contact that occurs when there is a coming together of a tangible object to be felt as pleasant, which is derived, and the body-faculty, thus makes the contingency of a Pārājika offense even for one who has no intention to indulge. Furthermore, for one who has a painful, unpleasant feeling either due to being covered by a cloth or due to a defect in the female organ, or for whom there is no bodily feeling at all due to the body being afflicted by wind, by showing the Sutta passage, ‘There is no offense for one not consenting,’ he makes the contingency of no offense for that person, whether knowing or not knowing, even for one with the intention to indulge. Furthermore, if there is a Saṅghādisesa offense for one who strives with the lust for emission and emits, what more is to be said of one who strives with the lust for sexual intercourse? Taking a case that is a Dukkaṭa offense, he makes it a case of a Saṅghādisesa offense. In this way, he is said to make the Vinaya into non-Vinaya. The other, the Vinayadhara, having said, ‘Because it is stated, “There is no offense for one who does not know,” for one who knows, by the very fact of knowing—whether a pleasant feeling arises or not—it is consenting,’ makes an offense in a case of no offense even for one with no intention to indulge, simply because that person knows. He makes the blameless blameworthy; in this way, he makes the Dhamma into non-Dhamma. But one who knows both, having said, ‘Because of the statement, “When a bhikkhu’s intention to indulge has arisen,” the intention to indulge itself is the standard here. By its presence, there is the falling into a Pārājika offense; by its absence, there is no offense,’ protects and fulfills both. In this way, the application with its purpose should be made in all training rules as is appropriate.

Saṅgītiṃ āropetvā ṭhapitapāḷito vinimuttaṃ katvā ṭhapitattā pāḷivinimuttā atthato, nayato, anulomato ca pāḷiokkantavinicchayappavattā anupaviṭṭhavinicchayavasena pavattāti attho. “Na samūhanissatī”ti jānantopi bhagavā kevalaṃ “tesaṃ mataṃ pacchimā janatā mama vacanaṃ viya pamāṇaṃ karotū”ti dassanatthañca parinibbānakāle evamāha “ākaṅkhamāno, ānanda, saṅgho mamaccayena khuddānukhuddakāni sikkhāpadāni samūhanatū”ti (dī. ni. 2.216), tenetaṃ siddhaṃ “paññattampi ce sikkhāpadaṃ samūhanituṃ yassa saṅghassa anuññātaṃ bhagavatā, tassa paññattānulomaṃ atirekatthadīpanaṃ, pagevānuññātaṃ bhagavatā”ti. Kiñca bhiyyo ūnātirittasikkhāpadesu ācariyakulesu vivādo aññamaññaṃ na kātabboti dassanatthañca. Kasmā saṅgho na samūhanīti? Aññamaññaṃ vivādappasaṅgadassanato. Bhagavatā ca “sabbeheva samaggehi sammodamānehi avivadamānehi sikkhitabba”nti vuttaṃ. Tattha ca ekacce therā evamāhaṃsūti ca aññavādadassanato vivadamānehi sikkhitabbaṃ jātaṃ, tadabhāvattampi ñattidutiyakammavācaṃ sāvetvā avivadamāneheva sikkhitabbaṃ akāsi.

The meaning is this: The tradition of the Aṭṭhakathā, being free from the Pāḷi because it was established after having been submitted to the Council and made separate from the established Pāḷi, proceeds in terms of meaning, method, and conformity by way of decisions that have entered into the Pāḷi and by the power of decisions that have been successively entered. Though the Blessed One knew, 'They will not abolish it,' He spoke thus at the time of His Parinibbāna merely for the purpose of showing, 'Let the later generation take their opinion as authoritative, like my own word': 'Ānanda, if the Saṅgha wishes, after my passing, let it abolish the minor and lesser training rules.' Therefore, this is established: 'If it has been permitted by the Blessed One for a certain Saṅgha to abolish even a training rule that has been laid down, for that Saṅgha, the clarification of an additional meaning is in conformity with the enactment. How much more so in the case of practicing a training rule permitted by the Blessed One?' Furthermore, it is also to show that in regard to deficient or excessive training rules, a dispute should not be made among one another in the lineages of teachers. Why did the Saṅgha not abolish them? Because of the prospect of mutual disputes. And by the Blessed One it was said, 'It should be trained by all in unity, in harmony, and without dispute.' And in that regard, because some elders spoke thus, and because of seeing other doctrines, it came to be that training had to be done while disputing. And for the sake of the absence of that, having had the motion as the second formal act announced, he made it so that training should be undertaken only by those not disputing.

Apicāti attano matiyā pākaṭakaraṇatthaṃ ārambho. Tattha “suttantābhidhammavinayaṭṭhakathāsū”ti vacanato piṭakattayassapi sādhāraṇā esā kathāti veditabbā, “atha panāyaṃ kappiya”ntiādi vinayasseva. Kārakasaṅghasadisanti saṅgītikārakasaṅghasadisaṃ. “Suttādicatukkaṃ appaccakkhāya tena aviruddhassa kammassa kārakasaṅghasadisa”nti dhammasirittherassa gaṇṭhipade vuttaṃ, taṃ ayuttaṃ, “suttameva balavataraṃ. Suttañhi appaṭivattiyaṃ kārakasaṅghasadisa”nti etehi padehi ayuttattā. Pākatike [M 0.0088] pana gaṇṭhipade “tamatthaṃ vinicchinitvā tassa kārakasaṅghasadisa”nti vuttaṃ. Paravādīti amhākaṃ samayavijānanako aññanikāyikoti vuttaṃ. Paravādī suttānulomanti kathaṃ? “Aññatra udakadantaponā”ti (pāci. 266) suttaṃ sakavādissa, tadanulomato nāḷikeraphalassa udakampi udakameva hotīti paravādī ca.

Moreover, the undertaking is to make one's own opinion evident. Therein, it should be understood that this discussion is common to the three Piṭakas, according to the saying 'in the Suttanta, Abhidhamma, and Vinaya commentaries,' while the words beginning with 'but this is allowable' pertain only to the Vinaya. 'Like the assembly of doers' means like the Saṅgha that performed the recitation. In the Gaṇṭhipada of the Elder Dhammasiri, it is said: 'Without rejecting the fourfold collection beginning with the Sutta, it is like the assembly of doers for an act that is not in conflict with it.' That is incorrect, because it is incompatible with these words: 'The Sutta alone is more authoritative. For the Sutta, being unalterable, is like the assembly of doers.' However, in the Pākatika Gaṇṭhipada, it is stated: 'Having determined that meaning, it is like the assembly of doers for that decision.' An opponent is said to be a member of another school. How is it that the opponent is in accordance with the Sutta? The Sutta, 'Except for water and a tooth-stick,' belongs to the proponent; in accordance with that, the opponent also holds that the water of a coconut is indeed just water.

“Nāḷikerassa yaṃ toyaṃ, purāṇaṃ pittabandhanaṃ;

Tameva taruṇaṃ toyaṃ, pittaghaṃ balabandhana”nti. –

The water of a coconut, when old, binds the bile; that same water, when young, destroys bile and promotes strength.

Evaṃ [V 0.0080] paravādinā vutte sakavādī dhaññaphalassa gatikattā, āhāratthassa ca pharaṇato “yāvakālikameva ta”nti vadanto paṭikkhipati. Paro ācariyavādanti “suṅkaṃ pariharatīti ettha upacāraṃ okkamitvā kiñcāpi pariharati, avahāro evā”ti aṭṭhakathāvacanato “tathā karonto pārājikamāpajjatī”ti paravādinā vutte sakavādī “suṅkaṃ pariharati, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti suttaṃ tattheva āgatamahāaṭṭhakathāvacanena saddhiṃ dassetvā paṭisedheti, tathā karontassa dukkaṭamevāti. Paro attanomatīti ettha “purebhattaṃ parasantakaṃ avaharāti purebhattameva harissāmīti vāyamantassa pacchābhattaṃ hoti, purebhattapayogova so, tasmā mūlaṭṭho na muccatīti tumhākaṃ theravādattā mūlaṭṭhassa pārājikamevā”ti paravādinā vutte sakavādī “taṃ saṅketaṃ pure vā pacchā vā taṃ bhaṇḍaṃ avaharati, mūlaṭṭhassa anāpattī”ti (pārā. 119) suttaṃ dassetvā paṭikkhipati.

When this is said by the opponent, the proponent rejects it, saying, 'Because it is in the category of grain-fruit and because it fulfills the purpose of food, it is indeed a yāvakālika.' In the section where the opponent cites the teachers' view, when the opponent says, 'Because of the commentary statement, "In the phrase ‘evades a tax,’ although one evades it by entering the vicinity, it is indeed theft," one who does so commits a pārājika offense,' the proponent objects by showing the Sutta passage, 'Evading a tax is an offense of dukkaṭa,' together with the statement from the Great Commentary found in that very place, saying, 'For one who does so, it is only a dukkaṭa offense.' In the section where the opponent cites his own opinion, when the opponent says, 'Because it is your Theravāda view that for one who was commanded, "Steal another's property in the forenoon," while he is striving, thinking, "I will steal it only in the forenoon," it becomes the afternoon, that effort is indeed an effort of the forenoon; therefore, the original instigator is not absolved, and for the original instigator, it is indeed a pārājika offense,' the proponent rejects it by showing the Sutta passage, 'He steals that item before or after that appointed time; there is no offense for the original instigator.'

Paro suttanti “aniyatahetudhammo sammattaniyatahetudhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo”ti suttaṃ paṭṭhāne likhitaṃ dassetvā “ariyamaggassa na nibbānamevārammaṇa”nti paravādinā vutte sakavādī “ārammaṇattikādisuttānulome na otaratī”ti paṭikkhipati. Suttānulome otarantaṃyeva hi suttaṃ nāma, netaraṃ. Tena vuttaṃ pāḷiāgataṃ paññāyatīti ettakenapi siddhe tisso saṅgītiyo āruḷhapāḷiāgataṃ paññāyatī”tiādi. Tādisañhi pamādalekhanti ācariyo. “Appamādo amataṃ padaṃ, pamādo maccuno pada”nti (dha. pa. 21; netti. 26) vacanato dinnabhojane bhuñjitvā parissayāni parivajjitvā satiṃ paccupaṭṭhapetvā viharanto nicco hotīti. Evarūpassa [M 0.0089] atthassa vasena āruḷhampi suttaṃ na gahetabbaṃ, tena vuttaṃ no ce tathā paññāyatīti siddhepi “no ce tathā paññāyati, na otarati na sametī”ti. “Bāhirakasuttaṃ vā”ti vuttattā attano suttampi atthena asamentaṃ na gahetabbaṃ. Paro ācariyavādantiādīsu dvīsu nayesu pamādalekhavasena tattha tattha āgataṭṭhakathāvacanaṃ theravādehi saddhiṃ yojetvā veditabbaṃ.

Regarding the opponent's sutta: having shown this sutta written in the Paṭṭhāna—‘An indeterminate root-condition is a condition for a rightness-fixed root-condition by way of object-condition’—when the opponent says, ‘The noble path does not have Nibbāna alone as its object,’ the proponent refutes this, saying, ‘It does not accord with the Suttānuloma of the Ārammaṇattika, etc.’ Indeed, only that which accords with the Suttānuloma is called a sutta; the other is not. Therefore, although it would be sufficient to say, 'what has come down in the Pāḷi is known,' it is said, ‘what has come down in the Pāḷi that was established in the three councils is known,’ and so on. Indeed, such a text is a careless writing, says the teacher. For example, from the verse ‘Heedfulness is the path to the deathless, heedlessness the path to death,’ one might wrongly infer that one who dwells having eaten offered food, having avoided dangers, and having established mindfulness, becomes permanent. By means of a meaning of this kind, even a sutta that has been established in the councils should not be accepted. Therefore, although it would be sufficient to say, ‘if it is not known to be so,’ it is said more fully, ‘if it is not known to be so, it does not accord, it does not agree.’ Because it is said, ‘or an external sutta,’ even one’s own sutta, if it does not agree with the meaning, should not be accepted. In the two methods, such as ‘the doctrine of another teacher,’ etc., a statement from the commentary that has appeared here and there by means of careless writing should be understood by reconciling it with the doctrines of the Theras.

Atha panāyaṃ ācariyavādaṃ. Paro suttanti paravādinā “mūlabījaṃ nāma haliddi siṅgiveraṃ vacā…pe… bīje bījasaññī chindati vā chedāpeti vā bhindati vā…pe… āpatti pācittiyassāti (pāci. 91) tumhākaṃ pāṭhattā haliddigaṇṭhiṃ chindantassa pācittiya”nti vutte sakavādī “yāni vā panaññāni atthi mūle sañjāyantī”tiādiṃ dassetvā tassa aṭṭhakathāsaṅkhātena ācariyavādena paṭikkhipati. Na hi gaṇṭhimhi gaṇṭhi jāyatīti. Paro suttānulomanti paravādinā “anāpatti evaṃ amhākaṃ ācariyānaṃ uggahoti vacanassānulomato ‘amhākaṃ [V 0.0081] porāṇabhikkhū ekapāsāde gabbhaṃ thaketvā anupasampannena sayituṃ vaṭṭatīti tathā katvā āgatā, tasmā amhākaṃ vaṭṭatī’ti tumhesu eva ekaccesu vadantesu tumhākaṃ na kiñci vattuṃ sakkā”ti vutte sakavādī “suttaṃ suttānulomañca uggahitakānaṃyeva ācariyānaṃ uggaho pamāṇa”ntiādiaṭṭhakathāvacanaṃ dassetvā paṭisedheti. Paro attanomatinti “dvāraṃ vivaritvā anāpucchā sayitesu ke muccantī”ti ettha pana dvepi janā muccanti yo ca yakkhagahitako, yo ca bandhitvā nipajjāpitoti tumhākaṃ theravādattā aññe sabbepi yathā tathā vā nipannādayopi muccantīti paṭisedheti.

Now, this is the teachers' doctrine. The opponent's Sutta: when the opponent says: 'Root-seed, namely, turmeric, ginger, sweet flag… if one, perceiving it as a seed, cuts, causes it to be cut, or breaks it… there is an offense of expiation (Pācittiya 91). According to your text, for a monk who cuts a turmeric rhizome, there is a pācittiya,' the proponent of one's own view refutes this by presenting the passage beginning, 'Or whatever other things there are that grow from a root,' by means of the teachers' doctrine, which is the commentary on that text. For a rhizome does not grow from a rhizome. The opponent's conformity with the Sutta: when the opponent says: 'There is no offense. In accordance with the statement, "This is the learning of our teachers," our ancient bhikkhus, having closed off a chamber in a single mansion, held that it is allowable to sleep with an unordained person. Having acted thus, they came to this conclusion. Therefore, it is allowable for us. When some among you yourselves say this, nothing can be said to you,' the proponent of one's own view rejects this, presenting the commentary's statement beginning: 'The learning of only those teachers who have mastered the Sutta and the conformity with the Sutta is the authority.' The opponent's own opinion: regarding the question, 'Among those who sleep without asking permission after opening the door, who are exempted?', the proponent refutes the opponent's claim that, because it is your Theravāda view that two persons are exempted—the one possessed by a yakkha and the one who has been bound and made to lie down—all other monks are also exempted, however they may be lying down, and so on.

Atha panāyaṃ attanomatiṃ. Paro suttanti “āpattiṃ āpajjantī”ti paravādinā gutte sakavādī “divā kilantarūpo mañce nisinno pāde bhūmito amocetvāva niddāvasena nipajjati, tassa anāpattī”tiādiaṭṭhakathāvacanaṃ (pārā. aṭṭha. 1.77) dassetvā ekabhaṅgena nipannādayopi muccantīti paṭisedheti. Athāyaṃ attanomatiṃ. Paro suttānulomanti “domanassaṃ pāhaṃ, devānaminda, duvidhena vadāmi sevitabbampi asevitabbampītiādivacanehi (dī. ni. 2.360) saṃsandanato sadārapose doso tumhākaṃ natthi, tena [M 0.0090] vuttaṃ ‘puttadārassa saṅgaho’”ti (khu. pā. 5.6; su. ni. 265) paravādinā vutte kiñcāpi sakavādī bahussuto na hoti, atha kho rāgasahiteneva akusalena bhavitabbanti paṭikkhipati. Sesesupi iminā nayena aññathāpi anurūpato yojetabbaṃ. Idaṃ sabbaṃ upatissattherādayo āhu. Dhammasiritthero pana “ettha paroti vutto aññanikāyiko, so pana attano suttādīniyeva āharati. Tāni sakavādī attano suttādimhi otāretvā sace sameti gaṇhāti, no ce paṭikkhipatī”ti vadati.

Now, this is one's own opinion. The opponent's Sutta: when the opponent says, 'They incur an offense,' the proponent of one's own view cites the commentary passage beginning: 'A person who is weary during the day, sitting on a bed, lies down through sleepiness without having lifted his feet from the ground; for him there is no offense,' and refutes the opponent's claim by stating that those lying down in a single posture, etc., are also exempted. Now, this is one's own opinion. The opponent's conformity with the Sutta: when the opponent says, 'By comparing this with the statements beginning, "I say, O lord of the devas, that displeasure is twofold: to be cultivated and not to be cultivated," there is no fault for you in supporting one's wife and children; therefore it is said, "the support of wife and children",' the proponent of one's own view, although not very learned, rejects this, saying that it must be unwholesome since it is accompanied by lust. In the remaining cases too, this method should be applied, differently or as is suitable. All this was said by the elders such as the Thera Upatissa. The Thera Dhammasiri, however, says: 'Here, "opponent" refers to one of another school, and he brings forward only his own suttas and so on. The proponent of one's own view, having compared them with his own suttas, etc., accepts them if they agree, but if not, he rejects them.'

Catubbidhavinayakathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Fourfold Discourse on the Vinaya is finished.

Padabhājanīyavaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Word-by-word Analysis

Sikkhāpadavibhaṅge pana kiñcāpi yo panāti anavasesapariyādānapadaṃ, tathāpi bhikkhūti iminā parapadena samānādhikaraṇattā tadanurūpānevassa vibhaṅgapadāni vuttāni. Bhikkhunibbacanapadāni tīṇi kiñcāpi sabhikkhubhāvassa, abhikkhubhāvassa cāti yassa kassaci pabbajitassa sādhāraṇāni, tathāpi “asuddho hoti puggalo aññataraṃ pārājikaṃ dhammaṃ ajjhāpanno, tañce suddhadiṭṭhi samāno anokāsaṃ kārāpetvā cāvanādhippāyo vadeti, āpatti saṅghādisesena dukkaṭassā”ti evamādisuttaṃ nibbacanatthayuttova puggalo “āpatti saṅghādisesena [V 0.0082] dukkaṭassā”ti (pārā. 389) ettha vatthu, na itaro gihibhūtoti dassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Sabbassapi vinayapiṭakassa sādhāraṇaṃ bhikkhulakkhaṇaṃ vatthuñhi bhagavā ārabhi. Yo pana suddho eva samāno kenaci kāraṇena gihiliṅge ṭhito, so attano sabhikkhubhāvattā eva vatthu hoti, asuddhopi bhikkhuliṅge ṭhitattāti ayamattho dassito hoti. Asuddhopi ñātakehi, paccatthikehi vā rājabhayādikāraṇena vā kāsāvesu saussāhova apanītakāsāvo vatthu eva puna kāsāvaggahaṇena theyyasaṃvāsakabhāvānupagamanato, bhikkhunibbacanatthe anikkhittadhurattāti vuttaṃ hoti. Yo pana liṅgatthenako bhikkhunibbacanatthaṃ sayañca ajjhupagato, saṃvāsaṃ thenento, tañce suddhadiṭṭhi samāno anokāsaṃ kārāpetvā cāvanādhippāyo vadeti, āpatti [M 0.0091] saṅghādisesena dukkaṭassāti ayampi attho dassito hoti.

In the Sikkhāpadavibhaṅga, although the phrase ‘yo pana’ is an all-inclusive term, nevertheless, because it is in apposition with the subsequent word ‘bhikkhu,’ its analytical terms are stated in a manner suitable to it. Although the three terms defining a bhikkhu are common to any renunciant—whether possessing the nature of a bhikkhu or not—it is nevertheless stated to show that only the person connected with the meaning of the definition in the Sutta beginning, ‘An impure person, having committed one of the pārājika offenses, if one with a pure view, intending his fall, speaks without having obtained permission, there is an offense of Saṅghādisesa or Dukkaṭa,’ is the subject here in the phrase ‘there is an offense of Saṅghādisesa or Dukkaṭa’ (Pārā. 389), and not the other who has become a layman. Indeed, the Blessed One began with the subject that has the characteristic of a bhikkhu, which is common to the entire Vinaya Piṭaka. However, one who, while being pure, for some reason adopts the appearance of a layman, is the subject precisely because of his own bhikkhu-status. This also shows that even an impure person is the subject if he maintains the appearance of a bhikkhu. Even an impure person, whose robes have been removed due to relatives, enemies, or reasons such as fear of the king, but who is still eager for the saffron robes, is indeed the subject. This is because, by taking up the saffron robes again, he does not fall into the state of a thief-in-communion, and because, in the context of the definition of a bhikkhu, he has not abandoned his duty. This is what is said. Furthermore, regarding one who is a thief of the outward sign, who has himself undertaken the purpose of the definition of a bhikkhu, and who steals the communion—if one with a pure view, intending his fall, speaks to him without having obtained permission, there is an offense of Saṅghādisesa or Dukkaṭa. This meaning is also shown.

“Samaññāya bhikkhu paṭiññāya bhikkhū”ti vacanadvayaṃ yathāvuttañca atthaṃ upabrūheti, antarā uppannāya niyatāya micchādiṭṭhiyā upacchinnakusalamūlo kevalāya samaññāya, paṭiññāya ca “bhikkhū”ti vuccati, na paramatthatoti imaṃ atirekatthaṃ dīpeti. Kiṃ vuttaṃ hoti? “Nāhaṃ, bhikkhave, aññaṃ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi, yaṃ evaṃ mahāsāvajjaṃ yathayidaṃ, bhikkhave, micchādiṭṭhi. Micchādiṭṭhiparamāni, bhikkhave, mahāvajjānī”ti āhaccabhāsitaṃ saṅgītittayāruḷhaṃ suttaṃ, aṭṭhakathāyampissa “micchādiṭṭhiparamā etesanti micchādiṭṭhiparamānī”ti (a. ni. 1.310) vuttaṃ. Pañca ānantariyakammāni mahāsāvajjāni, micchādiṭṭhi pana mahāsāvajjatarāti adhippāyoti. Kasmā? Tesañhi paricchedo atthi, sabbabalavampi kappaṭṭhitikameva hoti, niyatamicchādiṭṭhiyā pana paricchedo natthi, tāya samannāgatassa bhavato vuṭṭhānaṃ natthi, tasmā “imassa bhikkhukaraṇā kusalā dhammā saṃvijjantī”ti vā “suddhovāya”nti vā na sakkā vattuṃ. “Diṭṭhivipattipaccayā dve āpattiyo āpajjatī”ti vuttattā na sakkā “asuddho”ti vā “aññataraṃ pārājikaṃ dhammaṃ ajjhāpanno”ti vā vattuṃ. Esa hi ubhopi pakkhe na bhajati, tena vuttaṃ “samaññāya, paṭiññāya ca bhikkhu, na paramatthato”ti.

The twofold statement, 'A bhikkhu by designation, a bhikkhu by acknowledgment,' both elaborates upon the meaning as stated and reveals this additional meaning: one whose wholesome roots have been cut off by a fixed wrong view that has arisen within is called a 'bhikkhu' merely by designation and by acknowledgment, not in the ultimate sense. What is meant by this? 'Monks, I do not see even a single other thing so greatly blameworthy as this, monks: wrong view. Monks, wrong view is the paramount of great faults.' Regarding this Sutta, which was spoken directly and included in the three recitations, it is also stated in its commentary: '“Those which have wrong view as their paramount” (micchādiṭṭhiparamāni) means that wrong view is the paramount among them.' The five deeds of immediate retribution are greatly blameworthy, but the intended meaning is that fixed wrong view is even more blameworthy. Why? Because for those deeds there is a limit; even the most powerful lasts for only one eon. But for fixed wrong view, there is no limit; for one endowed with it, there is no rising from existence. Therefore, it cannot be said of this person, 'Wholesome states exist because of his becoming a bhikkhu,' or 'He is indeed pure.' Because it is stated, 'On account of the corruption of view, one incurs two offenses,' it cannot be said, 'He is impure,' or 'He has committed a certain pārājika offense.' For indeed, such a person belongs to neither side. Therefore it was said: 'A bhikkhu by designation and by acknowledgment, but not in the ultimate sense.'

Kimatthaṃ panevaṃ mahāsāvajjāya niyatamicchādiṭṭhiyā pārājikaṃ bhagavā na paññapesīti? Dubbijānattā. Pakatiyāpesā diṭṭhi nāma “sammā”ti vā “micchā”ti vā duviññeyyā, pageva “niyatā”ti vā “aniyatā”ti vāti. Tattha pārājikāpattiyā paññattāya bhikkhū aññamaññaṃ asamadiṭṭhikaṃ pārājikaṃ maññamānā uposathādīni akatvā acireneva [V 0.0083] sāsanaṃ vināseyyuṃ, sayañca apuññaṃ pasaveyyuṃ suddhesupi bhikkhūsu vippaṭipattiyā paṭipajjanena. Tasmā upāyakusalatāya pārājikaṃ apaññāpetvā tassa ukkhepanīyakammaṃ, sammāvattañca paññāpetvā taṃ saṅghena asambhogaṃ, asaṃvāsañca akāsi. Bhagavā hi tassa ce esā diṭṭhi aniyatā, sammāvattaṃ pūretvā osāraṇaṃ labhitvā pakatatto bhaveyya. Niyatā ce, aṭṭhānametaṃ anavakāso, yaṃ so niyatamicchādiṭṭhiko sammāvattaṃ pūretvā osāraṇaṃ labhitvā pakatatto bhaveyya. Kevalaṃ “samaññāyabhikkhu [M 0.0092] paṭiññāyabhikkhū”ti nāmamattadhārako hutvā paraṃ maraṇā ariṭṭho viya saṃsārakhāṇukova bhavissatīti imaṃ nayaṃ addasa.

Why then did the Blessed One not lay down a pārājika offense for such a greatly blameworthy fixed wrong view? Because it is difficult to discern. By its very nature, this thing called 'view' is difficult to know as either 'right' or 'wrong,' let alone as 'fixed' or 'not fixed.' If a pārājika offense were laid down for this, bhikkhus, considering a fellow bhikkhu with a different view to have committed a pārājika offense, might not perform the Uposatha and other duties, and would quickly destroy the Dispensation; and they themselves would generate demerit by acting wrongly towards even pure bhikkhus. Therefore, out of skill in means, without laying down a pārājika offense, the Blessed One laid down the act of suspension and proper conduct for that person, and made him to be without communion and without association with the Saṅgha. For the Blessed One saw this line of reasoning: if that view of his is not fixed, he might fulfill the proper conduct, obtain reinstatement, and return to his original state. But if it is fixed, it is impossible, there is no opportunity, for one with a fixed wrong view to fulfill the proper conduct, obtain reinstatement, and return to his original state. He would merely become one who bears the name 'a bhikkhu by designation, a bhikkhu by acknowledgment,' and after death, like Ariṭṭha, he would become a stump in the cycle of existence.

Aṭṭhasu upasampadāsu tissovettha vuttā, na itarā pāṭipuggalattā, bhikkhūnaṃ asantakattā ca. Tattha hi ovādapaṭiggahaṇapañhabyākaraṇūpasampadā dvinnaṃ therānaṃ eva, sesā tisso bhikkhunīnaṃ santakāti idha nādhippetā, tissannampi upasampadānaṃ majjhe “bhadro bhikkhū”tiādīni cattāri padāni vuttāni tissannaṃ sādhāraṇattā. Ehibhikkhubhāvena vā saraṇagamanañatticatutthena vā upasampanno hi bhadro ca sāro ca sekkho ca asekkho ca hoti, upasampadavacanaṃ pana nesaṃ sāvakabhāvadīpanatthaṃ. Ime eva hi āpattiṃ āpajjanti, na sammāsambuddhā, paccekabuddhā ca.

Among the eight kinds of higher ordination, only three are mentioned here; the others are not, because they are specific to individuals and do not belong to the bhikkhus in general. For among them, the ordination by acceptance of an exhortation and the ordination by answering questions apply only to two elders; the remaining three belong to the bhikkhunīs and so are not intended here. Within the section on these three kinds of ordination, the four terms—'a good bhikkhu,' and so on—are mentioned because they are common to all three. Indeed, one ordained by the 'Come, bhikkhu' method, or by the going for refuge, or by the formal act with a motion as the fourth, becomes good, substantial, a trainee, and a non-trainee. The term 'ordination,' however, is stated in reference to them to show their good state. For only these incur offenses, not the Perfectly Self-Enlightened Ones or the Paccekabuddhas.

Ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetoti ettha ca āpattiṃ āpajjituṃ bhabbā ñatticatuttheneva kammena upasampannā. Na hi aññe ehibhikkhusaraṇagamanaovādapaṭiggahaṇapañhabyākaraṇāhi upasampannā āpattiṃ āpajjituṃ bhabbā, tenete paṭikkhipitvā “ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhū”ti antimova vuttoti kira dhammasiritthero, taṃ ayuttaṃ. “Dve puggalā abhabbā āpattiṃ āpajjituṃ buddhā ca paccekabuddhā cā”ti (pari. 322) ettakameva vuttanti. Aññathā ehibhikkhuādayopi vattabbā siyuṃ. Kiñca bhiyyo “dve puggalā bhabbā āpattiṃ āpajjituṃ bhikkhū ca bhikkhuniyo cā”ti sāmaññena vuttattā ca, apica āpattibhayaṭṭhānadassanato ca. Kathaṃ? Āyasmā sāriputto āvasathapiṇḍaṃ kukkuccāyanto na paṭiggahesi, cīvaravippavāsabhayā ca sabbaṃ ticīvaraṃ gahetvā nadiṃ taranto manaṃ vuḷho ahosi mahākassapo. Kiñca saraṇagamanūpasampadāya upasampanne ārabbha saddhivihārikavattādīni asammāvattantānaṃ nesaṃ dukkaṭāni ca paññattāni dissanti, tasmā dubbicāritametaṃ. Ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti paṭikkhittāya saraṇagamanūpasampadāya anuññātappasaṅgabhayāti upatissatthero, āpattiyā bhabbataṃ sandhāya tasmimpi vutte pubbe paṭikkhittāpi sā puna evaṃ vadantena anuññātāti bhikkhūnaṃ micchāgāho vā vimati vā uppajjati[V 0.0084], tasmā na vuttāti vuttaṃ hoti, taṃ “bhikkhunī nāma ubhatosaṅghe upasampannā”ti (pāci. 161) iminā sameti. Idañhi sākiyādīnaṃ anuññātaupasampadāya anuppabandhabhayā vuttaṃ.

And here, the bhikkhu intended in this context is one who is capable of incurring an offense, having been ordained by the formal act with the motion as fourth. For others ordained by 'Come, bhikkhu,' by the going for refuge, by the acceptance of exhortation, or by the answering of questions, are not capable of incurring an offense. Therefore, rejecting these, the Elder Dhammasiri is said to have stated that only the final one is meant by 'This is the bhikkhu intended in this context.' But that is incorrect. For it is only stated, 'Two persons are incapable of incurring an offense: Buddhas and Paccekabuddhas.' Otherwise, those ordained by 'Come, bhikkhu,' and so on, would also have to be mentioned. Moreover, it is incorrect because it is generally stated, 'Two persons are capable of incurring an offense: bhikkhus and bhikkhunīs,' and also because a reason for fear of an offense is seen. How so? The Venerable Sāriputta, feeling scrupulous, did not accept almsfood at a guesthouse. And the Venerable Mahākassapa, out of fear of being separated from his robes, was slightly carried away by the current while crossing a river, taking all three robes with him. Furthermore, with regard to those ordained by the going for refuge, it is seen that offenses of wrong-doing were laid down for them when they did not properly observe the duties toward a co-resident and so on. Therefore, this is poorly reasoned. The Elder Upatissa says that the statement, 'This is the bhikkhu intended in this context,' was made out of fear that the rejected ordination by going for refuge might be implicitly approved. For if it were stated with reference to the capability for an offense in that case as well, a wrong view or doubt might arise for the bhikkhus that this ordination, although previously rejected, is again approved by one speaking thus. Therefore, it was not stated—this is what is meant. This is consistent with: 'A bhikkhunī is one ordained in both Saṅghas.' For this was stated out of fear of the continuation of the ordination that was permitted for the Sākiyan ladies and others.

Ayaṃ [M 0.0093] panettha amhākaṃ khanti – bhikkhu-padaniddesattā yattakāni tena padena saṅgahaṃ gacchanti, ye ca vinayapiṭake tattha tattha sandissanti sayaṃ āpattāpajjanaṭṭhena vā duṭṭhullārocanapaṭicchādanādīsu paresaṃ āpattikaraṇaṭṭhena vā, te sabbepi dassetvā idāni yadidaṃ tassa bhikkhu-padassa visesanatthaṃ vuttaṃ parapadaṃ “sikkhāsājīvasamāpanno”ti, tassa vasena idaṃ vuttaṃ “ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhū”ti. So eva hi kammavācānantarameva sikkhāsājīvasamāpanno hoti tato paṭṭhāya sauddesasikkhāpadānaṃ uppattidassanato, tasseva ca sikkhāpaccakkhānaṃ dissati, netarassa. Tasseva ca sikkhāpaccakkhānaṃ sambhavati “ullumpatu maṃ, bhante, saṅgho anukampaṃ upādāyā”ti (mahāva. 71, 126) vatvā samādinnattā, tasseva ca upasampannasamanantarameva akaraṇīyanissayācikkhanadassanato, vinayaṃ pātimokkhaṃ uddesaṃ paccakkhāmītiādisikkhāpaccakkhānalakkhaṇapāripūrito cāti sikkhāpaccakkhānaṃ upādāya so eva idhādhippetoti vuttaṃ hoti.

Herein, this is our preference: Because this is the explanation of the term 'bhikkhu,' having shown all those meanings—whatever meanings are included by that term, and whichever ones are seen here and there in the Vinaya Piṭaka, either by way of oneself incurring an offense or by way of causing others to incur an offense in matters such as informing about or concealing a grave offense—now, by means of the subsequent term, ‘one who has undertaken the training and livelihood,’ which was stated for the purpose of qualifying that term ‘bhikkhu,’ this was said: ‘This is the bhikkhu intended in this context.’ Indeed, it is that very one who becomes ‘one who has undertaken the training and livelihood’ immediately after the kammavācā, because from that point on, the arising of the training rules with their expositions is shown. And it is of that very one that the renunciation of the training is seen, not of another. And for that very one, the renunciation of the training is possible because it has been undertaken after saying, ‘Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha, out of compassion, raise me up.’ Furthermore, for that very one, immediately after having been fully ordained, the instruction on things not to be done and on the supports is shown. And because he is fulfilled with the characteristic of renouncing the training, such as [saying], ‘I renounce the Vinaya, the Pātimokkha, the recitation,’ therefore, on account of the renunciation of the training, it is said that that very one is intended here.

Yasmā panassa sikkhāpaccakkhānaṃ sabbathā yujjati, tasmā “sikkhaṃ paccakkhāya taṃ taṃ vatthuṃ vītikkamantassa tato tato āpattito anāpatti, itarassa āpattī”ti vattuṃ yujjati, tasmā “yattha yattha sāvajjapaññatti, anavajjapaññatti vā, ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti vuccati, tattha tattha tadajjhācāratthenāyameva ñatticatutthena upasampanno adhippeto nāmā”ti vattuṃ yujjatīti veditabbaṃ. Evaṃ sante yaṃ vuttaṃ “yāya kāyaci upasampadāya ayaṃ imasmiṃ ‘methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevitvā pārājiko hotī’ti atthe bhikkhūti adhippeto”ti, tampi na vattabbameva. Kathaṃ hoti? Virodhadosopi parihato hoti. Kathaṃ? Sace ñatticatutthena upasampanno eva idhādhippeto “bhikkhū”ti ca “upasampanno”ti ca, tena na upasampanno anupasampanno nāmāti katvā ñatticatutthakammato aññathā upasampannā nāma mahākassapattherādayo itaresaṃ anupasampannaṭṭhāne ṭhatvā sahaseyyapadasodhammāpattiṃ janeyyuṃ, omasanādikāle ca dukkaṭameva janeyyunti evamādiko virodhadoso parihato hotīti sabbaṃ ācariyo vadati. Maṅguracchavi nāma sāmo.

However, since for that monk the renunciation of the training is in every way proper, it is therefore proper to say: 'For one who, having renounced the training, transgresses this or that rule, there is no offense from that particular transgression; for the other, there is an offense.' Therefore, it should be known that it is proper to say: 'Wherever there is a regulation concerning what is faulty or a regulation concerning what is faultless, this one is called the 'bhikkhu' intended in this context. In each of those cases, by reason of transgressing that regulation, it is only this one ordained by the act of motion and three announcements who is indeed intended.' This being so, that which was said—'By whatever kind of ordination one is ordained, in this context of "having engaged in sexual intercourse, one is defeated," this one is intended as 'bhikkhu''—even that should not be said at all. How is this so? The fault of contradiction is also avoided. How? If, here, only one ordained by the act of motion and three announcements is intended by the terms 'bhikkhu' and 'ordained one', then, having considered that one not ordained by that act is called 'unordained', those named 'ordained' by other means—such as the Elder Mahākassapa and others—standing in the position of the unordained, would incur the offense of lying down together and the offense of teaching the Dhamma word by word. And at the time of insulting and so on, they would incur only a dukkaṭa offense. In this way, such a fault of contradiction is avoided. So says the teacher. Maṅguracchavi means of a golden color.

Yasmā [M 0.0094] te atimahanto jātimado cittaṃ pariyuṭṭhāti, tasmā tumhehi mama sāsane evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ[V 0.0085]. “Sātasahagatā paṭhamajjhānasukhasahagatā asubhe ca ānāpāne cā”ti gaṇṭhipade vuttaṃ. Uddhumātakasaññāti uddhumātakanimitte paṭiladdhapaṭhamajjhānasaññā. Rūpasaññāti pathavīkasiṇādirūpāvacarajjhānasaññā. So taṃ byākāsi “avibhūtā, bhante, uddhumātakasaññā avaḍḍhitabbattā asubhānaṃ, vibhūtā, bhante, rūpasaññā vaḍḍhitabbattā kasiṇāna”nti. Pañcaupasampadakkamo mahāvaggā gahito. Ñatticatutthenāti ettha kiñcāpi ñatti sabbapaṭhamaṃ vuccati, tissannaṃ pana anussāvanānaṃ atthabyañjanabhedābhāvato atthabyañjanabhinnā ñattitāsaṃ catutthāti katvā “ñatticatuttha”nti vuccati. Byañjanānurūpameva aṭṭhakathāya “tīhi anussāvanāhi ekāya ca ñattiyā”ti vuttaṃ, atthapavattikkamena padena pana “ekāya ñattiyā tīhi anussāvanāhī”ti vattabbaṃ. Yasmā panettha “cattārimāni, bhikkhave, kammāni (mahāva. 384), cha imāni, bhikkhave, kammāni adhammakammaṃ vaggakamma”nti (mahāva. 387) vacanato kuppakammampi katthaci “kamma”nti vuccati tasmā “akuppenā”ti vuttaṃ.

Because the very great pride of birth afflicts the mind, therefore, you should train thus in my Dispensation: 'Accompanied by delight, accompanied by the happiness of the first jhāna, in the foul and in in-and-out breathing'—this is stated in the Gaṇṭhipada. The perception of a bloated corpse refers to the perception of the first jhāna attained through the sign of a bloated corpse. The perception of form refers to the perception of form-sphere jhānas, such as the earth kasiṇa and others. He explained it thus: 'Venerable sir, the perception of a bloated corpse is not manifest because the foul objects are not to be developed; venerable sir, the perception of form is manifest because the kasiṇas are to be developed.' The fivefold procedure for higher ordination is taken from the Mahāvagga. Regarding the term ñatticatuttha (motion-fourth), although the motion (ñatti) is stated first, because there is no difference in meaning and phrasing among the three proclamations (anussāvana), the motion—which is distinct in meaning and phrasing—is considered the fourth in relation to them; therefore, it is called 'motion-fourth.' In accordance with the wording, the commentary states: 'With three proclamations and one motion.' However, in terms of the sequence of meaning, it should be said: 'With one motion and three proclamations.' Because here, according to the statement, 'Monks, there are these four formal acts (Mahāvagga 9.3.5); monks, these six formal acts are an unlawful act, an act done by an incomplete assembly...' (Mahāvagga 9.3.9), even a formal act liable to be overturned is sometimes called a 'formal act,' therefore the qualification 'by an unshakeable one' is stated.

Yasmā akuppampi ekaccaṃ na ṭhānārahaṃ, yena appatto osāraṇaṃ “sosārito”ti campeyyakkhandhake (mahāva. 395 ādayo) vuccati, tasmā “ṭhānārahenā”ti vuttaṃ. Yadi evaṃ “ṭhānārahenā”ti idameva padaṃ vattabbaṃ, na pubbapadaṃ iminā akuppasiddhitoti ce? Taṃ na, aṭṭhānārahena akuppena upasampanno imasmiṃ atthe anadhippetoti aniṭṭhappasaṅgato. Dvīhi panetehi ekato vuttehi ayamattho paññāyati “kevalaṃ tena akuppena upasampanno ayampi imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto ‘bhikkhū’ti, ṭhānārahena ca upasampanno ayampi imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto ‘bhikkhū’ti, kuppena upasampanno nādhippeto”ti. Tenāyampi attho sādhito hoti “yo pana, bhikkhu, jānaṃ ūnavīsativassaṃ puggalaṃ upasampādeyya, so ca puggalo anupasampanno”ti (pāci. 403) vacanato yāva na ñāyati, tāva samaññāyabhikkhupaṭiññāyabhikkhubhāvaṃ upagatopi na pubbe dassitasamaññāyabhikkhupaṭiññāyabhikkhu viya aññesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ upasampannaṭṭhāne ṭhatvā omasanapācittiyādivatthu hoti, kevalaṃ anupasampannaṭṭhāne ṭhatvā “anupasampanne upasampannasaññī [M 0.0095] padaso dhammaṃ vāceti, āpatti pācittiyassā”tiādi (pāci. 47) āpattivatthumeva hutvā tiṭṭhati. Akuppena upasampanno pana pacchā pārājikopi jātito upasampannaṭṭhāne tiṭṭhatīti “paṇḍako, bhikkhave, anupasampanno na upasampādetabbo, upasampanno nāsetabbo”tiādinā (mahāva. 109) nayena vuttesu pana vajjanīyapuggalesu koci puggalo “upasampanno”ti vuccati, nopi upasampannaṭṭhāne tiṭṭhati, koci tiṭṭhatīti veditabbaṃ.

Since even an unoverturnable procedure is sometimes not valid—as in the Campeyya section where one who has not attained reinstatement is called 'well reinstated' (Mahāvagga 9.4.8)—therefore, 'by a valid one' is stated. If so, should only this term 'by a valid one' be stated, and not the preceding term, on the grounds that the unoverturnable nature is established by this? That is not so, for it would lead to the undesired consequence that one ordained by an unoverturnable but invalid procedure is not intended in this meaning. However, when these two are stated together, this meaning is understood: 'One ordained merely by that unoverturnable procedure is also intended in this meaning as 'a bhikkhu,' and one ordained by a valid procedure is also intended in this meaning as 'a bhikkhu,' but one ordained by an overturnable procedure is not intended.' By this, the following meaning is also established: According to the rule, 'If a bhikkhu knowingly ordains a person under twenty years of age, that person is not ordained' (Pācittiya 65), as long as this is not known, even if one has attained the state of a bhikkhu by designation and by acknowledgement, he is not, like the previously mentioned bhikkhu by designation and by acknowledgement, a basis for an offense of insult, a pācittiya, etc., by standing in the place of an ordained bhikkhu for other bhikkhus. Merely by standing in the place of an unordained person, he remains only as the basis for an offense, such as in 'If, perceiving an unordained person as ordained, one teaches the Dhamma word by word, it is a pācittiya offense' (Pācittiya 4). However, one ordained by an unoverturnable procedure, even if later having committed a pārājika, still stands in the place of an ordained one by his nature as a bhikkhu. But among the persons to be avoided stated by the method of 'A eunuch, bhikkhus, being unordained, should not be ordained; if ordained, he should be expelled' (Mahāvagga 1.61), etc., it should be understood that some individuals are called 'ordained' but do not stand in the place of ordained ones, while some do stand in that place.

Ettha [V 0.0086] pana atthi kammaṃ akuppaṃ ṭhānārahaṃ, atthi ṭhānārahaṃ nākuppaṃ, atthi akuppañceva na ṭhānārahañca, atthi nākuppaṃ na ca ṭhānārahanti idaṃ catukkaṃ veditabbaṃ. Tattha paṭhamaṃ tāva vuttaṃ, tatiyacatutthāni pākaṭāni. Dutiyaṃ pariyāyena bhikkhunisaṅghato ekatoupasampannāya liṅgaparivatte sati labbhati. Tassa hi puggalassa pubbe sikkhamānakāle laddhaṃ ñatticatutthaupasampadākammaṃ kiñcāpi akuppañceva ṭhānārahañca, purisaliṅge pana pātubhūte “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, taṃyeva upajjhaṃ tameva upasampada”nti (pārā. 69) ettha apariyāpannattā tassa puggalassa kevalaṃ sāmaṇerabhāvāpattito kammaṃ dāni kuppaṃ jātanti vuccati. Liṅgaparivattena cīvarassa adhiṭṭhānavijahanaṃ viya tassa puggalassa bhikkhunisaṅghena katāya upasampadāya vijahanaṃ hotīti veditabbaṃ, aññathā so puggalo upasampanno bhikkhūti āpajjati. Atha vā liṅgaparivatte asatipitaṃ ekatoupasampadākammaṃ kuppati, yathāṭhāne na tiṭṭhati. Tasmā na tāva sā “bhikkhunī”ti saṅkhyaṃ gacchati. Yasmā aññataraṃ pārājikaṃ dhammaṃ āpajjitvāpi anāpajjitvāpi uppabbajitukāmatāya gihiliṅgaṃ sādiyantiyā punapi upasampadā ubhatosaṅghe labbhati, tasmā tena pariyāyena “kuppatīti kuppa”nti vuccati, yathāvuttakammadosābhāvato pana “ṭhānāraha”nti. Bhikkhunī pana gihiliṅgaṃ sādiyantikāle na purisaliṅgapātubhāve sati bhikkhūsu upasampadaṃ labbhatīti sādhakaṃ kāraṇaṃ na dissati, sikkhaṃ paccakkhāya uppabbajitā ce, labhatīti eke, taṃ panāyuttaṃ bhikkhuniyā sikkhāpaccakkhanābhāvatoti amhākaṃ khantīti ācariyo. “Yathā ‘kattabba’nti vuttaṃ, tathā akate kuppatīti katvā karaṇaṃ satthusāsana”nti gaṇṭhipade vuttaṃ. Yattha yattha “gaṇṭhipade”ti vuccati, tattha tattha “dhammasirittherassa gaṇṭhipade”ti gahetabbaṃ.

Here, it should be understood that there is this tetrad: (1) there is an act that is unalterable and valid; (2) there is an act that is valid but not unalterable; (3) there is an act that is unalterable but not valid; and (4) there is an act that is neither unalterable nor valid. Among these, the first has already been stated; the third and fourth are evident. The second is found by way of a particular case: when a person who has received one-sided ordination from the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha undergoes a change of sex. For such a person, although the act of ordination by motion and three announcements, obtained during their time as a trainee, is both unalterable and valid, when male characteristics manifest, it is said that the act has now become alterable. This is because that person is not included in the passage, “I allow, monks, that same preceptor and that same ordination,” and because that person merely attains the state of a novice. It should be understood that the ordination performed by the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha for that person is abandoned, just as the determination of a robe is relinquished by a change of sex; otherwise, it would follow that that person is an ordained bhikkhu. Alternatively, even without a change of sex, that one-sided ordination is alterable; it does not stand in its proper place. Therefore, she does not yet attain the designation of ‘bhikkhunī.’ Because, whether or not she has committed any pārājika offense, if, with a desire to disrobe, she adopts the characteristics of a layperson, she can receive ordination again in both Saṅghas. Therefore, by that reasoning, because it is alterable, it is called ‘alterable’; but because of the absence of the aforementioned faults in the act, it is called ‘valid.’ However, for a bhikkhunī at the time of adopting the characteristics of a layperson, should male characteristics manifest, no supporting reason is seen for the view that she does not obtain ordination among the bhikkhus. Some say that if she disrobes by renouncing the training, she obtains it. But that is inappropriate, because there is no renunciation of the training for a bhikkhunī—this is our view, says the teacher. In the Gaṇṭhipada it is said: 'Because it is alterable when not performed as it was said it "should be done," the performance is the Teacher's instruction.' Wherever ‘Gaṇṭhipada’ is mentioned, it should be understood as ‘the Gaṇṭhipada of Dhammasiri Thera.’

Sājīvapadabhājanīyavaṇṇanā

The Exposition on the Analysis of the Terms of the Sājīva

“Mahābodhisattā [M 0.0096] niyatā”ti vuttaṃ anugaṇṭhipade. Yattha “anugaṇṭhipade”ti, tattha “vajirabuddhittherassā”ti gahetabbaṃ. Sāvakabodhipaccekabodhisammāsambodhīti vā tīsu bodhīsu sammāsambodhiyaṃ sattā bodhisattā mahābodhisattā nāma. Pātimokkhasīlabahukattā, bhikkhusīlattā, kilesapidahanavasena vattanato, uttamena bhagavatā paññattattā ca adhikaṃ, buddhuppādeyeva pavattanato uttamanti aññatarasmiṃ gaṇṭhipade. Kiñcāpi paccekabuddhāpi dhammatāvasena pātimokkhasaṃvarasīlena samannāgatāva honti, tathāpi “buddhuppādeyeva pavattatī”ti niyamitaṃ tena pariyāyenāti. Tenāha “na hi [V 0.0087] taṃ paññattiṃ uddharitvā”tiādi. Pātimokkhasaṃvaratopi ca maggaphalasampayuttameva sīlaṃ adhisīlaṃ, taṃ pana idha anadhippetaṃ. Na hi taṃ pātimokkhuddesena saṅgahitanti. Samantabhadrakaṃ kāraṇavacanaṃ sabbasikkhāpadānaṃ sādhāraṇalakkhaṇattā imissā anupaññattiyā ariyapuggalā ca ekaccaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjantīti sādhitametaṃ, tasmā “na hi taṃ samāpanno methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevatī”ti aṭṭhakathāvacanaṃ asamatthaṃ viya dissatīti? Nāsamatthaṃ, samatthameva yasmiṃ yasmiṃ sikkhāpade sāsā vicāraṇā, tassa tasseva vasena aṭṭhakathāya pavattito. Tathā hi kaṅkhāvitaraṇiyaṃ (kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. nidānavaṇṇanā) udakukkhepasīmādhikāre “timaṇḍalaṃ paṭicchādetvā antaravāsakaṃ anukkhipitvā uttarantiyā bhikkhuniyā”ti vuttaṃ bhikkhunivibhaṅge āgatattā. Eseva nayo aññepi evarūpesu. Kimatthanti ce taṃ? Pāḷikkamānuvattanena pāḷikkamadassanatthaṃ. Tatridaṃ samāsato adhippāyadīpanaṃ – padasodhammasikkhāpadassa tikaparicchede upasampanne upasampannasaññī, anāpatti, akaṭānudhammasikkhāpadavasena upasampanne ukkhittake siyā āpatti, tathā sahaseyyasikkhāpadeti evamādi. Attho panettha parato āvi bhavissati.

“Great Bodhisattas are determined for Buddhahood,” it is said in the Anugaṇṭhipada. Wherever “Anugaṇṭhipada” is mentioned, it should be understood as “that of the Venerable Vajirabuddhi.” Or, among the three enlightenments—the enlightenment of a disciple, the enlightenment of a Paccekabuddha, and perfect self-enlightenment—those Bodhisattas who are devoted to perfect self-enlightenment are called Great Bodhisattas. Because of the abundance of the Pātimokkha virtue, because it is the virtue of monks, because it functions by way of covering defilements, and because it was laid down by the supreme Blessed One, it is superior; and because it exists only at the time of a Buddha’s arising, it is supreme—thus it is said in a certain Gaṇṭhipada. Although Paccekabuddhas are also indeed endowed with the virtue of the Pātimokkha restraint by way of their nature, nevertheless, it is determined by that reason that “it exists only at the time of a Buddha's arising.” Therefore, he said, “For one does not, having set aside that regulation...” and so on. And the virtue associated with the path and fruit itself is higher virtue than the virtue of the Pātimokkha restraint, but that is not intended here, for it is not included in the recitation of the Pātimokkha. The statement of reason is good in every way; because it is a common characteristic of all training rules, it is established by this supplementary regulation that even noble individuals commit a certain offense. Therefore, does the statement of the commentary, “For one who has attained that does not engage in sexual intercourse,” seem as if it is ineffective? It is not ineffective; it is indeed effective, for the commentary proceeds by way of whichever training rule is under that particular investigation. For so it is: in the Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī, in the section on the water-throwing boundary, it is said, “of a bhikkhunī who, having covered the three circles and having lifted up her under-robe, is crossing over,” because this comes in the Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga. This is the same method in other such cases as well. If one should ask, “For what purpose is this statement?” It is for the purpose of showing the sequence of the Pāḷi by following the sequence of the Pāḷi. Therein, this is a brief clarification of the intention: In the threefold section of the Padasodhamma training rule, for one who is ordained and perceives the other as ordained, there is no offense. By way of the Akaṭānudhamma training rule, for one who is ordained but suspended, there would be an offense; likewise in the Sahaseyya training rule, and so on. The meaning here will become clear later on.

Yaṃ vuttaṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “tatopi ca maggaphalacittameva adhicittaṃ, taṃ pana idha anadhippeta”nti ca, “tatopi ca maggaphalapaññāva adhipaññā, sā pana idha anadhippetā. Na hi taṃsamāpanno bhikkhu methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevatī”ti. “Tatra yāyaṃ adhisīlasikkhā, ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā sikkhā”ti imāya pāḷiyā virujjhati. Ayañhi pāḷi adhisīlasikkhāva idha adhippetā, na [M 0.0097] itarāti dīpeti. Aṭṭhakathāvacanaṃ tāsampi tiṇṇaṃ lokiyānaṃ adhippetataṃ dīpeti. Ayaṃ panettha aṭṭhakathādhippāyo – tissopi lokiyā sikkhā imasmiṃ paṭhamapārājike sambhavanti, kālenāpi adhicittapaññālābhī bhikkhu tathārūpaṃ asappāyaṃ paccayaṃ paṭicca tato tato adhicittato, adhipaññāto ca āvattitvā sīlabhedaṃ pāpuṇeyyāti ṭhānametaṃ vijjati, na lokuttaracittapaññālābhī, ayaṃ nayo itaresupi sabbesu adinnādānādīsu sacittakesu labbhati, acittakesu pana itaropi. Tathāpi kevalaṃ vinayapiṭakassa, pātimokkhasīlassa ca saṅgāhakattā “sikkhaṃ appaccakkhāyā”ti imasmiṃ uttarapade paccakkhānārahā adhisīlasikkhāva lokiyāti dassanatthaṃ pāḷiyaṃ “tatra yāyaṃ adhisīlasikkhā, ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā sikkhā”ti vuttanti veditabbaṃ.

What was stated in the commentary—'Furthermore, the path-and-fruition consciousness is the higher mind, but that is not intended here,' and 'Furthermore, the path-and-fruition wisdom is the higher wisdom, but that is not intended here. For a monk who has attained that does not engage in sexual intercourse'—contradicts this Pāli passage: 'Therein, this higher training in virtue is the training intended in this context.' For this Pāli passage indicates that only the higher training in virtue is intended here, not the others. The commentary’s statement indicates that even those three mundane trainings are intended. This is the commentary’s intention here: all three mundane trainings are possible in this first pārājika offense. The possibility exists that a monk who has attained the higher mind and higher wisdom might, in time, due to an unsuitable condition, turn away from that higher mind and higher wisdom and commit a breach of virtue; this possibility, however, does not exist for one who has attained supramundane consciousness and wisdom. This method is found in all other cases involving intention, such as taking what is not given, etc.; but in those without intention, another method is also found. Nevertheless, because it is a compilation pertaining to the Vinaya Piṭaka and the Pātimokkha virtue, in order to show that in this subsequent phrase, 'without having renounced the training,' only the mundane higher training in virtue is fit for renunciation, it was said in the Pāli, 'Therein, this higher training in virtue is the training intended in this context.' Thus it should be understood.

Ettha sikkhāti kāyavacīduccaritato viratī ca cetanā ca, aññatra cetanāyeva veditabbā. Sikkhāpadanti sauddesasikkhāpadaṃ, ekaccaṃ anuddesasikkhāpadañca labbhati. Cittassa adhikaraṇaṃ katvāti tasmiṃ sikkhatīti adhikaraṇatthe bhummanti dassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Yathāsikkhāpadanti paccavekkhaṇavasena vuttaṃ. Sīlapaccavekkhaṇāpi hi sīlameva, tasmā suppaṭicchannādicārittesu [V 0.0088] virativippayuttacetanaṃ pavattentopi sikkhaṃ paripūrentotveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati. “Sampajānamusāvāde pācittiya”nti (pāci. 2) vuttamariyādaṃ avītikkamanto “tasmiñca sikkhāpade sikkhatī”ti vuccati. Aññatarasmiṃ pana gaṇṭhipade vuttaṃ “sikkhāti taṃ sikkhāpadaṃ sikkhanabhāvena pavattacittuppādo. Sājīvanti paññatti. Tadatthadassanatthaṃ pubbe methunasaṃvarassetaṃ adhivacana”nti. Yasmā sikkhāya guṇasammatāya puññasammatāya tantiyā abhāvato lokassa dubbalyāvikammaṃ tattha na sambhavati. Patthanīyā hi sā, tasmā “yañca sājīvaṃ samāpanno, tattha dubbalyaṃ anāvikatvā”ti vuttaṃ. Āṇāya hi dubbalyaṃ sambhavatīti āyasmā upatisso.

Here, 'training' should be understood as abstinence from misconduct of body and speech, and also volition; elsewhere, it should be understood as volition alone. The 'training rule' refers to the formulated training rule, and sometimes an unformulated training rule is also obtained. The phrase 'having made the mind the location' was stated to show that in 'one trains in that,' the locative case is used in the sense of location. The phrase 'as per the training rule' is stated in the sense of reflection. For reflection on virtue is indeed virtue itself. Therefore, even when one generates a volition disconnected from restraint in conduct such as being well-covered, one is still reckoned as fulfilling the training. One who does not transgress the limit stated as, 'In intentional false speech, there is an offense entailing expiation,' is said to 'train in that training rule.' However, in a certain gloss it is stated: ''Training' is the arising of a state of mind that proceeds by way of practicing that training rule. 'Good livelihood' is a designation. To show its meaning, it was formerly a term for restraint regarding sexual intercourse.' Because, due to the absence of a tradition of training esteemed as a quality and as merit, the manifestation of the world's weakness is not possible there. For that is desirable; therefore it is said, 'And having undertaken that good livelihood, without manifesting weakness there.' For weakness is possible through a command—thus says the Venerable Upatissa.

Sikkhāpaccakkhānakathāvaṇṇanā

An Exposition of the Discussion on the Renunciation of the Training

Ettha [M 0.0098] yāmīti amukasmiṃ titthāyatane, gharādimhi vā. Bhāvavikappākārenāti “ahaṃ assa”nti āgatattā yaṃ yaṃ bhavitukāmo, tassa tassa bhāvassa vikappākārena, bhikkhubhāvato aññabhāvavikappākārenāti adhippāyo.

Here, 'I go' (yāmi) means to a certain sectarian center, or to a house and so on. 'By way of a conceptual mode of becoming' means: because it is stated as 'I would be,' whatever state one wishes to become, it is by a conceptual mode of that very state; the meaning is, by a conceptual mode of another state than the state of a bhikkhu.

46. Handāti vacasāyeva. Gihibhāvaṃ patthayamānotiādipadehi cittaniyamaṃ dasseti. Ekeneva cittena sikkhāpaccakkhānaṃ hoti, na tadabhāvenāti.

46. 'Handa' is by speech alone. With phrases such as 'desiring the state of a householder,' he shows the determination of the mind. The renunciation of the training occurs with a single mind-moment alone, not by its absence.

51. Buddhaṃ dhammantiādipadehi khettaniyamaṃ dasseti. Tattha ādito cuddasahi padehi sabhāvapariccāgo, pacchimehi aṭṭhahi bhāvantarādānañca dassitaṃ hoti. Paccakkhāmi dhārehīti etehi kālaniyamaṃ dasseti. Vadatīti iminā padena payoganiyamaṃ dasseti. Viññāpetīti iminā vijānananiyamaṃ dasseti. Ummattako sikkhaṃ paccakkhāti, ummattakassa santike sikkhaṃ paccakkhātītiādīhi puggalaniyamaṃ dasseti. Ariyakena milakkhassa santike sikkhaṃ paccakkhātītiādīhi pana puggalādiniyamepi sati vijānananiyamāsambhavaṃ dasseti. Tattha “yāya milakkhabhāsāya kālaniyamo natthi, tāyapi bhāsāya kālaniyamatthadīpane sati sikkhāpaccakkhānaṃ ruhatīti no matī”ti ācariyo. Davāyātiādīhi khettādiniyame satipi cittaniyamābhāvena na ruhatīti dasseti. Sāvetukāmo na sāvetīti cittaniyamepi sati payoganiyamābhāvena na ruhatīti dasseti. Aviññussasāveti, viññussa na sāvetīti cittakhettakālapayogapuggalavijānananiyamepi sati yaṃ puggalaṃ uddissa sāveti, tasseva savane na ruhati, na aññassāti dassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ, tena vuttaṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “yadi ayameva jānātūti ekaṃ [V 0.0089] niyametvā āroceti, tañce so eva jānāti, paccakkhātā hoti sikkhā. Atha so na jānāti…pe… appaccakkhātā hoti sikkhā”ti. Sabbaso vā pana na sāveti, appaccakkhā hoti sikkhāti cittādiniyameneva sikkhā paccakkhātā hoti, na aññathāti dassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Ettāvatā “sikkhā…pe… dubbalyaṃ anāvikatvā”ti padassa padabhājanaṃ tīhi ākārehi dassitaṃ [M 0.0099] hoti. Tattha dve amissā, pacchimo eko missoti veditabbo. Teneva vacībhedenāti tadatthadīpanamattaṃ vacanaṃ sutvāva teneva vacībhedena jānāpetīti attho. Cittasampayuttanti paccakkhātukāmatācittasampayuttaṃ. Samayaññū nāma tadadhippāyajānanamattena hoti.

51. He shows the determination of the field with phrases such as 'Buddhaṃ, Dhammaṃ,' etc. Therein, with the first fourteen words, the relinquishment of one's state is shown, and with the last eight, the assumption of another state is also shown. With 'Paccakkhāmi, dhārehi,' he shows the determination of time. With the word 'vadati,' he shows the determination of application. With 'viññāpeti,' he shows the determination of cognition. With such phrases as 'An insane person renounces the training,' and 'one renounces the training in the presence of an insane person,' he shows the determination of person. But with such phrases as 'A noble one renounces the training in the presence of a barbarian,' he shows the impossibility of the determination of cognition even when there is determination of person and so forth. Therein, the teacher states: 'In whatever barbarian language there is no determination of time, if the meaning of the determination of time is indicated even by that language, the renunciation of the training is valid—this is our view.' With such phrases as 'In jest,' he shows that it is not valid due to the absence of the determination of mind, even when there are determinations of field and so forth. With 'Wishing to announce, he does not announce,' he shows that it is not valid due to the absence of the determination of application, even when there is determination of mind. The phrase 'He announces to one who does not understand, but does not announce to one who understands' is stated to show the following: even when there are determinations of mind, field, time, application, person, and cognition, it is valid only by the hearing of that very person for whom it is intended and announced, but not by the hearing of another. Therefore, it is said in the commentary: 'If, having determined, "Let only this one know," he announces it to one person, and if that very person knows it, the training is renounced. But if that person does not know… the training is not renounced.' The phrase 'Or if he does not announce at all, the training is not renounced' is stated to show that the training is renounced only by the determination of mind and so forth, and not otherwise. To this extent, the word analysis of the phrase 'sikkhaṃ…pe… dubbalyaṃ anāvikatvā' is shown in three ways. Therein, two are unmixed, and the last one is mixed—this should be understood. Regarding 'by that very verbal expression,' the meaning is: having heard a statement that merely indicates that meaning, he makes it known by that very verbal expression. 'Associated with mind' means associated with the mind possessing the wish to renounce. 'One who knows the occasion' is so-called merely by knowing the intention of that statement.

53. Vaṇṇapaṭṭhānaṃ buddhaguṇadīpakaṃ suttaṃ. Upāligahapatinā vuttā kira upāligāthā. Paññāṇaṃ saññāṇanti atthato ekaṃ, tasmā bodhipaññāṇanti bodhisaññāṇaṃ, bodhibījanti vuttaṃ hoti.

53. The Vaṇṇapaṭṭhāna is a Sutta that illuminates the virtues of the Buddha. The verses spoken by the householder Upāli are indeed the Upāligāthā. The words 'paññāṇa' and 'saññāṇa' are one in meaning; therefore, 'bodhipaññāṇa' (enlightenment-knowledge) is said to be 'bodhisaññāṇa' (enlightenment-knowing), that is, 'bodhibīja' (the seed of enlightenment).

Dvinnampi niyametvāti ettha “dvīsupi jānantesu eva paccakkhāmīti adhippāyena vutte tesu eko ce jānāti, na paccakkhātā hotī”ti aññatarasmimpi gaṇṭhipade vuttaṃ, taṃ aṭṭhakathāya na sameti. “Gihī homī”ti vā “gihimhī”ti vā vutte kiñcāpi vattamānavacanaṃ hoti. “Dhārehī”ti atthābhāvā ca “dhārehī”ti vutte ca parassupari gacchati, tasmā na hoti. Sandiṭṭhikaṃ dhammanti sabbattha dhammavacanaṃ vuttaṃ yaṃ sandhāya “sandiṭṭhika”nti vadati, taṃ pakāsetuṃ. Aññathā “vijitavijayaṃ paccakkhāmī”ti vutte cakkavattiādīsupi tappasaṅgato buddhasaddopi avasāne vattabbo bhaveyya. Ācariyavevacanesu pana yo maṃ pabbājesītiādi upajjhaṃ aggahetvā, paraṃ vā uddissa pabbajitaṃ sandhāya vuttanti. Okallakoti kapaṇādhivacanaṃ. Moḷibaddhoti sikhābaddho, omukkamakuṭo vā. Cellako athero. Ceṭako majjhimo. Moḷigallo mahāsāmaṇero. Manussaviggahanāgādīnaṃ nāgarūpādīnaṃ vā santike, bhāsājānanakinnarādīnaṃ vā. “Devatā nāma mahāpaññā”ti kira pāṭho. Davāyāti sahasā. Ravābhaññenāti khalitabhaññena. Akkharasamayānañhi nābhiññātāya vā karaṇānaṃ avisadatāya vā hoti ravābhaññaṃ. Avidheyyindriyatāya “potthakarūpasadisassā”ti vuttaṃ, garumedhassa mandapaññassa. Kittāvatā pana garumedho hotīti ce? Samaye akovidatāya.

Here, in the text 'dvinnampi niyametvā', it is said in a certain knotty passage: 'When it is said with the intention, "I renounce," while both are knowing, if among them only one knows, it is not renounced.' That does not agree with the commentary. When 'Gihī homi' (I am a householder) or 'Gihimhi' (I am a householder) is said, although it is a present tense expression, it is not effective, both because the word 'dhārehi' has no meaning here, and because when 'dhārehi' is said it passes over to another. The phrase 'sandiṭṭhikaṃ dhammaṃ' is said to explain that word 'dhamma'—which is used everywhere—in reference to which one says 'sandiṭṭhika'. Otherwise, if one were to say, 'I renounce the conquered conquest,' then due to its relevance even in the case of a wheel-turning monarch and so on, the word 'Buddha' would also have to be designated at the end. But in the teacher's alternative phrasing, the statement such as 'he who ordained me,' is said in reference to one who has gone forth without taking a preceptor, or with reference to another. 'Okallaka' is a term for a wretched person. 'Moḷibaddha' is one with a topknot, or one wearing a crown. A 'cellaka' is a non-elder novice. A 'ceṭaka' is a medium novice. A 'moḷigalla' is a great novice. In the presence of nāgas with human form, or those with the mere form of a nāga, or in the presence of kinnaras who know human speech, and so on, the training is not renounced. It is said the reading is: 'Deities, indeed, are of great wisdom.' 'Davāya' means hastily. 'Ravābhaññena' means with faulty speech. Faulty speech occurs due to not knowing the convention of letters or due to a lack of clarity in the organs of articulation. Due to unruly faculties, it is said of one with dull wisdom, of slow intelligence, that he is 'like a blank book.' If it is asked, 'To what extent is one of dull wisdom?' It is due to a lack of skill in the convention.

Sikkhāpaccakkhānakathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Discourse on the Renunciation of the Training is finished.

Mūlapaññattikathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourse on the Root Designation

55. “Paṭisevatināmā”ti [M 0.0100][V 0.0090] padaṃ mātikāyaṃ natthi, tasmā “paṭiseveyyāti etthā”tiādimāha. “Eso methunadhammo nāmā”ti sabbapāḷipotthakesu, aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “eso vuccati methunadhammo nāmā”ti uddhaṭā. Itthiyā nimittena attano nimittanti duviññeyyametaṃ dassitaṃ. Attano nimittena itthiyā nimittaṃ suviññeyyattā na dassitaṃ. Cattāri ṭhānāni muñcitvāti ettha abbhantaratalaṃ chupantaṃyeva sandhāya vuttaṃ, acchupantaṃ nīharantassa anāpatti. Majjhanti aggappadesaṃ. Uparibhāgamajjhanti uparibhāgassa aggappadesaṃ.
