The state of being related or unrelated is applicable only to a conditioned phenomenon, not to a designation, because it is the object of a legal issue, and it occurs in a legal issue; thus, it is a legal issue, just as there is the metaphorical usage of ‘couch’ for one who is on the couch. It is also written: ‘By way of convention, a rootless name-designation does not exist. It is merely conventional; it does not exist by its own nature. It is merely a term; there is no referent.’ ‘Here’ (idheva) means in this very training rule. ‘Not everywhere’ means not in disputes, legal issues, and so on. Why? Because of the passage beginning with `Na hi`. For a rootless legal issue does not exist in the way that disputes, legal issues, and so on, exist. ‘By the previously mentioned settlements’ means by the settlements stated as ‘those settlements that proceed regarding a legal issue’—this is the intended meaning. Furthermore, it is said they have no intrinsic nature because no intrinsic nature is acquired, like unarisen consciousness, etc. For designation is not the basis of legal issues like disputes, etc.; settlements do not proceed based on designation; therefore, it is not the subject of a legal issue. The intended meaning is that designation is not the basis of legal issues like disputes, etc. And here it is said:

“Pārājikāpatti amūlikā ce,

Paṇṇattimattā phalamaggadhammā;

Catutthapārājikavatthubhūtā,

Paṇṇattimattāva siyuṃ tatheva.

If a pārājika offense were rootless and merely a designation, then the path and fruit states, which are the basis of the fourth pārājika, would likewise be merely designations.

“Tato dvidhā maggaphalādidhammā,

Siyuṃ tathātītamanāgatañca;

Paṇṇattichakkaṃ na siyā tato vā,

Pariyāyato sammutivādamāhā”ti.

Therefore, the states beginning with path and fruit, and likewise the past and the future, would be twofold. The sixfold designation would not exist. Or, for that reason, by way of an alternative explanation, he stated the discourse on convention.

Anuvadantīti akkosanti. Kiccayatāti karaṇīyatā. Taṃ katamanti ce? Apalokanakammantiādi. Kiccanti viññattisamuṭṭhāpakacittaṃ kira adhippetaṃ.

`Anuvadanti` means they revile. `Kiccayatā` means that which ought to be done. If it is asked, “What is that?” It is the act of announcement, and so on. By `kicca`, it is said, the mind that gives rise to intimation is intended.

387. Sutādīnaṃ abhāvena amūlakattanti ettha yo disvāpi “diṭṭhosi mayā”ti vattuṃ asakkonto attano diṭṭhaniyāmeneva “sutosi mayā”ti vadati. Tassa tasmiṃ asuddhadiṭṭhittā āpatti, idha pana yo pubbe sutvā anāpatti, pacchā taṃ vissaritvā suddhadiṭṭhi eva samāno vadati, taṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. “Esa nayo sabbatthāti apare”ti vuttaṃ. Jeṭṭhabbatiko kākekappaṭivattā[V 0.0178]. Yadaggenāti yāvatā, yadā vā. No kappetītiādi vematikābhāvadīpanatthameva vuttanti dasseti. Tena vematikova nassarati [M 0.0200] sammuṭṭho nāmāti āpajjati, taṃ na yuttaṃ tadanantarabhāvato, tasmā dutiyattheravādo pacchā vutto.

387. Regarding 'being baseless due to the absence of hearing, etc.': here, one who, even having seen, is unable to say, 'You were seen by me,' and says, 'You were heard by me,' merely by his own fixed perception of having seen—for him, there is an offense because of his impure view regarding that person. But here, this was said in reference to one who, having heard previously (for whom there is no offense), later forgets it and speaks while being of pure view. It is said, 'Others say, "This is the method in all cases."' Jeṭṭhabbatika has conduct similar to that of Kāka. `Yadaggena` means 'to what extent' or 'when'. It shows that 'he does not allow,' etc., was said merely for the purpose of indicating the absence of doubt. By this, it would follow that only one who is doubtful forgets and is called 'confused'. That is not correct, because of its being immediately subsequent. Therefore, the view of the second elder was stated afterwards.

389. Sabbatthāti sabbaaṭṭhakathāsu. Okāsakammanti okāsakaraṇaṃ. “Okāsena kammaṃ okāsakamma”nti likhitaṃ. Asūriyaṃ passati kaññāti ettha yathā kaññā sūriyaṃ na passatīti bhavati, evaṃ “anokāsaṃ kāretvā”ti vutte okāsaṃ na kāretvāti hoti.

389. `Sabbatthāti` means in all the commentaries. `Okāsakamma` means the making of an opportunity. It is written: “An act by means of an opportunity is `okāsakamma`.” Here, in the phrase `asūriyaṃ passati kaññā` (a maiden sees a non-sun), just as the meaning is 'the maiden does not see the sun', so too, when `anokāsaṃ kāretvā` (having caused a non-opportunity) is said, the meaning is 'not having caused an opportunity'.

Paṭhamaduṭṭhadosasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the first training rule concerning a corrupt-minded fault is concluded.

9. Dutiyaduṭṭhadosasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

9. The Commentary on the Second Training Rule Concerning a Corrupt-Minded Fault

391. Veḷuvaneyevāti idaṃ tehi vuttavelaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. “Pubbe mayaṃ āvuso sutena avocumhā”ti “amhehi sā ussāhitā kupitehi anattamanehī”tiādivacanaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ, aññabhāgassa idanti manussabhikkhubhāvato aññabhāgassa tiracchānachagalakabhāgassa idaṃ chagalakajātaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ. Aññabhāgo vā assa atthīti so tiracchānachagalakabhāvasaṅkhāto aññabhāgo assa chagalakassa atthīti svāyaṃ chagalako aññabhāgiyaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ nāma.

391. “In the Bamboo Grove” — this was said with reference to the time they spoke. The statement, “Previously, friends, we spoke by hearsay,” refers to such statements as, “She was instigated by us, who were angry and displeased.” “This belongs to another party” — from the standpoint of a human monk, this legal issue, which is of the nature of a goat, belongs to another party, that of an animal-goat. Or, “he has another party” means that this other party, designated as the state of an animal-goat, belongs to this goat. Therefore, this very goat is called a legal issue belonging to another party.

Tattha paṭimāya sarīraṃ, silāputtakassa sarīranti nidassanaṃ, paṭhamaṃ panettha nibbacanaṃ jātipadatthotivādīnaṃ matena vuttaṃ. Sā hi sāmibhāvena, niccabhāvena ca padhānattā sattisabhāve ṭhitā. Tabbiparītakattā byattākati jātiyo tu padattho iti imassa suttassa vasena dutiyaṃ nibbacanaṃ vuttanti veditabbaṃ. Nāmakaraṇasaññāya ādhāroti ettha nāmameva nāmakaraṇaṃ. Nāmaṃ karontānaṃ saññā nāmakaraṇasaññā, tassā. Manussajātiko chagalakajātiādhāro nāma. Na hi taṃ nāmaṃ kacchapalomaṃ viya anādhāranti adhippāyo. Taṃ pana chagalakassa dabboti dinnanāmaṃ “deso”ti vuccati. Tasmā theraṃ amūlakenātiādinā aññampi vatthuṃ therassa lissati silissati vohāramatteneva, na atthato, īsakaṃ allīyatīti lesoti adhippāyo. Yasmā desalesā atthato ninnānākaraṇā, tasmā “kañcidesaṃ lesamattaṃ upādāyā”ti uddharitvā “dasa lesā jātileso”tiādi vuttanti veditabbaṃ. Yathā nidāne[M 0.0201], evaṃ sikkhāpadapaññattiyampi mātikāyampi ayamevattho. Yasmā aññabhāgiyassa adhikaraṇassāti chagalakassa. Kañcidesaṃ lesamattaṃ upādāyāti dabboti nāmaṃ upādāyāti ayamattho [V 0.0179] aṭṭhuppattivaseneva āvibhūto, tasmā na vibhatto. Kiñca bhiyyo aniyamattā. Na hi mettiyabhūmajakānaṃ viya sabbesampi chagalakameva aññabhāgiyaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ hoti. Aññaṃ gomahiṃ sādikampi hoti, na ca mettiyabhūmajakā viya sabbepi nāmalesamattameva upādiyanti. Aññampi jātilesādiṃ upādiyanti, tasmā aniyamattā ca yathāvuttanayena na vibhattaṃ. Kiñca bhiyyo tathā vutte chagalakasseva aññabhāgiyatā sambhavati, na aññassa, yena sova dassito. Leso ca nāma lesova, na jātiādi, yena sova dassitoti evaṃ micchāgāhappasaṅgato ca tathā na vibhatto.

Herein, the body of an image and the body of a stone doll are examples. The first etymology here is stated according to the view of those who hold that 'species is the meaning of the word'. For that species, due to being primary through its nature as owner and its nature as permanent, is established in the state of potentiality. It should be known that the second etymology is stated by means of this discourse which says, "The individual, the form, and the species are the meaning of the word," because it is contrary to that. In the phrase 'a basis for the perception of naming,' the name itself is the naming. The perception of those who make a name is the perception of naming; of that. One of the human species is called the basis for the goat species. Indeed, that name is not without a basis, like the hair of a tortoise—this is the meaning. But that name given to the goat, "Dabba," is called 'desa' (a part). Therefore, regarding the Elder, by the phrase 'groundlessly,' etc., another matter clings to the Elder by way of conventional speech only; in terms of meaning, it does not adhere even slightly. Therefore, it is called 'lesa' (a trace)—this is the meaning. Since 'desa' and 'lesa' are not different in meaning, it should be known that having extracted the phrase "taking up some part as a mere trace," it is said, "desalesa (part-trace), jātilesa (species-trace)," and so on. Just as in the origin story, so too in the laying down of the training rule and in the matrix, this is the very same meaning. Because 'of a legal issue belonging to another category' refers to the goat. The meaning "taking up the name 'Dabba'" for "taking up some part as a mere trace" became manifest only by way of the arising of the case; therefore, it was not analyzed. Furthermore, it was not analyzed due to its indeterminacy. For not for everyone is the aññabhāgiya legal issue only about a goat, as it was for the Mettiyā and Bhūmajaka monks. Other animals, such as a cow or a buffalo, can also be involved. And not all monks, like the Mettiyā and Bhūmajaka, take up merely a trace of a name. They take up other things, such as a trace of species, etc. Therefore, also due to this indeterminacy, it was not analyzed in the aforementioned manner. Furthermore, if it were stated in such a way that only the goat is indicated, then the state of being aññabhāgiya would be possible only for the goat, not for another. And if it were stated in such a way that only it is indicated, it would imply that a trace is only a trace, not species, etc. Thus, also to avoid the consequence of wrong grasping, it was not analyzed in that way.

393. Aññabhāgiyassāti cuditakato aññassa. Adhikaraṇassāti manussassa vā amanussassa vā tiracchānagatassa vāti evaṃ vattabbaṃ. Evañhi vutte manussādīnaṃyeva jātilesādayo vuttā honti, aññathā catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ te āpajjanti “adhikaraṇassa kañci desaṃ lesamatta”nti sāmivacanaṃ pubbaṅgamaṃ uddiṭṭhattāti ce? Na, nāmassa viya jātiādīnaṃ manussādīnaṃ ādhārabhāvaniyamasambhavato, adhikaraṇabhāvāniyamatoti vuttaṃ hoti. Niyame ca sati jātiyā ādhāro jāti, liṅgassa ca liṅgaṃ, āpattiyā ca āpanno ādhāro, viruddhānampi asamādinnānampi pattacīvarānaṃ sāmiko ādhāro, yena adhikaraṇasaṅkhyaṃ gaccheyyāti āpajjatīti adhikaraṇassāti padaṃ abhājetabbameva bhaveyyāti na uddharitabbaṃ siyā, uddharitabbaṃ. Tasmā “adhikaraṇanti vacanasāmaññato”tiādi sabbaṃ vattabbaṃ. Apākaṭā ito aññatra dassitaṭṭhānābhāvato. Jānitabbā ca vinayadharehi yasmā aññathā parivāre “vivādādhikaraṇaṃ catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ vivādādhikaraṇaṃ bhajatī”tiādinā nayena anāgataṭṭhāne “kasmā”ti vutte kāraṇaṃ na paññāyeyya, tasmā tesaṃ tabbhāgiyatā ca aññabhāgiyatā ca jānitabbā vinayadharehi. Tāsu hi viññātāsu vivādādhikaraṇaṃ vivādādhikaraṇaṃ bhajati. Kasmā? Tabbhāgiyattā. Itaraṃ na bhajati aññabhāgiyattāti sukhakāraṇato paññāyanti, tasmā vacanasāmaññato laddhaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ nissāyātiādi. Tattha [M 0.0202] yasmā āpattaññabhāgiyaṃ mahāvisayaṃ, itarehi asadisaniddesañca, tasmā taṃ adhikaraṇapariyāpannampi samānaṃ visuṃ vuttaṃ “āpattaññabhāgiyaṃ vā hotī”ti. Adhikaraṇapariyāpannattā ca “adhikaraṇaññabhāgiyaṃ vā”ti ettha vuttanti veditabbaṃ. Tatthāpi mahāvisayattā, mātikāyaṃ āgatattā ca paṭhamaṃ aññabhāgiyatā vuttā, pacchā tabbhāgiyatāti veditabbā. Tattha yasmā adhikaraṇaññabhāgiyavacanena atthāpattinayena siddhaṃ. Adhikaraṇaṃ tabbhāgiyaṃ, tasmā “adhikaraṇaṃ tabbhāgiyaṃ hotī”ti evaṃ uddesaṃ akatvā “kathaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ adhikaraṇassa tabbhāgiyaṃ hotī”ti pucchāpubbaṅgamaniddeso kato. Tatthāpi āpattādhikaraṇassa aññabhāgiyatā kiñcāpi pārājikena [V 0.0180] anuddhaṃsibhādhikārattā pārājikānaṃyeva vasena vuttā, atha kho sesāpattikkhandhavasenāpi veditabbā. Yā ca sā codanā “asuko nāma bhikkhu saṅghādisesaṃ ajjhāpajjanto diṭṭho hotī”tiādikā, tattha “saṅghādisese thullaccayadiṭṭhi hoti, dubbhāsite saṅghādisesadiṭṭhi hotī”ti evamādikā vinaye apakataññutāya, taṃtaṃvatthusarikkhatāya vā vuttāti veditabbā. Sabbatthāpi “pārājikadiṭṭhi hotī”ti na vuttaṃ. Tathāsaññino anāpattito. “Tabbhāgiyavicāraṇāya”nti tabbhāgiyapadaniddese aññabhāgiyatāyapi niddiṭṭhattā vuttaṃ.

393. Herein, 'belonging to another party' means of someone other than the accused. 'Of a legal issue' should be stated as pertaining to a human, a non-human, or an animal. For if stated this way, species, traces, and so on, are mentioned only in relation to humans and others; otherwise, they would apply to all four types of legal issues. If one were to say: 'Is it because the genitive case—"of a legal issue, some part, a mere trace"—is stated first?' No. This is because, just as for a name, it is possible to determine the state of being a basis for species and so on in relation to humans and others, and also because the state of being a legal issue is to be determined, it is said. And when there is determination, the basis of species is species, the basis of gender is gender, the basis of an offense is the one who has committed the offense, and the owner is the basis even for conflicting or unaccepted bowls and robes. It would follow that it would be counted as a legal issue on that basis. Therefore, the term 'of a legal issue' should indeed not be analyzed and should not be extracted. However, it should be extracted. Therefore, all such as '"a legal issue", by the generality of the term' should be stated. They are not clear, because there is no place shown other than this. And they should be known by the experts in Vinaya. Because otherwise, in the Parivāra, according to the method beginning 'A dispute-legal-issue, among the four legal issues, is classified as a dispute-legal-issue,' when 'Why?' is asked in a future context, the reason would not be apparent. Therefore, their 'belonging to that category' and 'belonging to another category' should be known by the experts in Vinaya. Indeed, when these are known, a dispute-legal-issue is classified as a dispute-legal-issue. Why? Because it belongs to that category. The other kind is not so classified because it belongs to another category. This is understood for a simple reason. Therefore, it should be known that it is based on the legal issue obtained by the generality of the term, and so on. Among these, because an offense belonging to another category has a wide scope and its explanation is dissimilar to the others, therefore, even though it is included under legal issues, it is stated separately as 'or it is an offense belonging to another category.' And because it is included under legal issues, it should be understood that it is stated here as 'or a legal issue belonging to another category.' Even among these two, it should be known that due to its wide scope and its appearance in the matrix, 'belonging to another category' is stated first, and 'belonging to that category' is stated afterward. Here, because a legal issue belonging to that category is established by the method of implication through the statement 'a legal issue belonging to another category,' therefore, instead of making the statement 'a legal issue belongs to that category' as an introduction, the exposition is made with a preceding question: 'How is a legal issue one belonging to that category of a legal issue?' Even there, the 'belonging to another category' of an offense-legal-issue, although stated in terms of pārājika offenses because it is the section on non-destruction by a pārājika, should also be understood in terms of the remaining classes of offenses. And that accusation, such as, 'A certain monk was seen committing a saṅghādisesa offense,' and so on—here, statements like 'in a saṅghādisesa, there is the view of a thullaccaya; in a wrongly spoken word, there is the view of a saṅghādisesa,' and so on, should be understood as stated in the Vinaya due to being unskilled or due to similarity in the respective cases. In all cases, it is not said, 'there is the view of a pārājika.' This is because for one with such a perception, there is no offense. The phrase 'For the investigation of that which belongs to that category' is stated because in the exposition of the term 'belonging to that category', 'belonging to another category' is also indicated.

Vatthusabhāgatāyāti anuvādavatthusabhāgatāyāti attho. Aññathā “catasso vipattiyo”ti vacanaṃ virujjheyya. Sabhāvasarikkhāsarikkhato cāti sabhāvena sadisāsadisato. Tattha jhānādivatthuvisabhāgatāyapi sabhāvasarikkhatāya uttarimanussadhammapārājikāpatti tasseva tabbhāgiyāva hoti. Tathā vatthuvasena anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ, kiccādhikaraṇañca pāṭekkaṃ catubbidhampi vuttaññabhāgiyaṃ na jātaṃ, tasmā tadaññabhāgiyatāya viditāya tabbhāgiyatā pāriyesayuttiyā avuttāpi sijjhatīti katvā “aññabhāgiyameva paṭhamaṃ niddiṭṭha”ntipi vattuṃ yujjati. Ekaṃsena tabbhāgiyaṃ na hotīti sarikkhavasena arahattaṃ āpatti anāpattīti vivādasabbhāvato abyākatabhāvena vivādādhikaraṇassapi aññabhāgiyaṃ siyā, pāḷiyaṃ āpattādhikaraṇassa vuttattā evaṃ vuttaṃ, ādito paṭṭhāyāti “aññabhāgiyassa adhikaraṇassā”ti ito paṭṭhāya. “Methunarāgena manussaviggaho dosenātiādinā [M 0.0203] sarikkhato cā”ti likhitaṃ. Taṃ vatthuvisabhāgatāya eva siddhaṃ. Ayaṃ pana vatthusabhāgatāyapi sati āpattisabhāgatā sarikkhatoti no takkoti ca, ekasmimpi hi vatthusmiṃ āpattibhedo hotīti ācariyo. Parato vuttanayena veditabbanti sambandho.

By 'due to similarity of the subject matter' is meant due to similarity of the subject matter of the accusation. Otherwise, the statement 'four failures' would be contradicted. And 'due to similarity and dissimilarity in nature' means because of being similar or dissimilar in nature. Therein, even with the dissimilarity of the subject matter, such as jhāna, etc., due to the similarity of nature, the pārājika offense of claiming a superior human state belongs to that very same category. Similarly, by way of the subject matter, neither a legal issue based on accusation nor a legal issue based on procedure, each being fourfold, has become what is called 'belonging to another category'. Therefore, since its nature of belonging to another category is known, its nature of belonging to its own category, even though unstated, is established by the logic of searching. For this reason, it is also proper to say, 'Only that which belongs to another category was pointed out first.' Regarding 'it is not exclusively of that category': because of the possibility of a dispute—'is it an offense or not an offense?'—concerning Arahantship, by way of similarity, a legal issue based on dispute could also belong to another category due to its indeterminate nature. Because the legal issue based on an offense is stated in the Pāḷi, it is stated thus. 'Starting from the beginning' means starting from this phrase, 'of the legal issue belonging to another category.' It is written: 'Sexual intercourse is due to lust; killing a human is due to hatred,' and so on, and 'due to similarity.' That is established precisely by the dissimilarity of the subject matter. But this is our reasoning: even when there is similarity of subject matter, there is similarity by way of the offense's nature. Indeed, even in a single subject matter, there is a difference in offenses, so says the teacher. The connection should be made thus: 'It should be understood according to the method to be stated hereafter.'

“Kiccameva kiccādhikaraṇa”nti vuttattā saṅghakammānametaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Kammalakkhaṇanti kammānaṃ sabhāvaṃ. Taṃ nissāyāti pubbeva hi saṃvidhāya saṅgho kammaṃ karoti. Atha vā purimaṃ purimanti parivāsaukkhepaniyādīni saṅghakammāni nissāya abbhānaosāraṇādi uppannanti katvā vuttaṃ. Tasmā kiñcāpi saṅghakammameva kiccādhikaraṇaṃ, tathāpi sesaviseso labbhatīti dasseti.

Because it is said, 'The procedure itself is a legal issue based on procedure,' this is a designation for the formal acts of the Saṅgha. 'The characteristic of an act' means the inherent nature of acts. Regarding 'relying on that': for, having arranged it beforehand, the Saṅgha performs the formal act. Or alternatively, regarding 'the preceding, the preceding': it is said having considered that, relying on preceding formal acts of the Saṅgha, such as probation (parivāsa), suspension (ukkhepaniya), and so forth, subsequent acts such as rehabilitation (abbhāna), reinstatement (osāraṇa), etc., have arisen. Therefore, it shows that although a formal act of the Saṅgha is itself a legal issue based on procedure, nevertheless, a further distinction is obtained.

394. Atthato ekaṃ, tasmā desassa atthamavatvā “leso”tiādi vuttaṃ kira.

394. In meaning, it is the same. Therefore, it is said that 'a pretext,' and so forth, was stated without explaining the meaning of the passage.

395. Savatthukaṃ katvāti puggalassa upari āropetvā khattiyādibhāvena ekajātikopi dīgharassakāḷakodātādīnaṃ [V 0.0181] diṭṭhasutaparisaṅkitānaṃ vasena aññabhāgiyatā, dīghaṃ khattiyaṃ ajjhācarantaṃ disvā rassādikhattiyapaññattiyā ādhārabhāvato jātilesena codeti, ekaṃ vā khattiyaṃ ajjhācarantaṃ disvā tato visiṭṭhaññabhāgabhūtaṃ khattiyaṃ jātilesaṃ gahetvā “khattiyo diṭṭho tvaṃ khattiyosī”ti codeti diṭṭhādiaññabhāgena. Ettha ca “dīghādayo, diṭṭhādayo ca jātināmādīnaṃ vatthubhūtattā adhikaraṇa”nti likhitaṃ. Taṃ “adhikaraṇabhāvāniyamato”ti vuttadosaṃ nātikkamati, aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “khattiyajātipaññattiyā ādhāravasena adhikaraṇatā ca veditabbā”ti vuttaṃ. Tampi nāmagottato aññissā nāmagottapaññattiyā nāma kassaci abhāvato na sabbasādhāraṇaṃ, tasmā “adhikaraṇassā”ti paduddhāraṇaṃ adhikaraṇacatukkadassanatthaṃ, taṃ samānavacanadassanatthanti no takkoti. Tattha dīghādino vā diṭṭhādino vāti ettha dīghāditā, diṭṭhāditā ca aññabhāgo, yo cuditako itarassa viseso yato aññoti vuccati.

395. Regarding 'having made it have a basis,' this refers to the state of being a different aspect, which comes about by attributing to a person—even if of the same caste—characteristics such as being tall, short, dark, or fair, which are seen, heard, or suspected, by way of being a Khattiya, and so forth. For instance, having seen a tall Khattiya transgressing, one accuses him by way of a caste-pretext, because the designation 'Khattiya' (which also includes short, etc.) serves as the basis. Or, having seen one Khattiya transgressing, one takes the caste-pretext related to another Khattiya who is a distinguished and different part from that one, and accuses him by way of a different aspect of what is seen, etc., saying, 'A Khattiya was seen; you are a Khattiya.' And here it is written: 'Tallness, etc., and what is seen, etc., are a legal issue because they are the basis for caste, name, and so forth.' This does not overcome the fault stated as 'due to the non-invariability of being a legal issue.' In the commentary, it is said: 'And the state of being a legal issue should be understood by way of being the basis for the designation of the Khattiya caste.' Even that is not universally applicable, because for anyone there is no designation of name and clan other than by name and clan. Therefore, the extraction of the word 'of the legal issue' is for the purpose of showing the four legal issues; it is not our reasoning that it is for the purpose of showing a synonymous word. Therein, regarding 'of tallness, etc., or of what is seen, etc.,' here, the state of being tall, etc., and the state of being seen, etc., are a different aspect. This different aspect is a distinction of the accused from the other, from which it is called 'different.'

399. Lahukaṃ āpattinti pārājikato lahukāpatti saṅghādisesādi. Teneva ante taṃ dassentena “bhikkhu saṅghādisesaṃ ajjhāpajjanto [M 0.0204] diṭṭho hotī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Āpattilesopi kimatthaṃ jātilesādayo viya na vitthāritoti ce? Tathā asambhavatoti veditabbaṃ.

399. A minor offense means an offense lighter than a pārājika, such as a saṅghādisesa, and so forth. For that very reason, at the end, by way of demonstrating this, it is said: 'A bhikkhu is seen incurring a saṅghādisesa offense,' and so forth. If it is asked why the offense-pretext is not elaborated upon like the caste-pretext, and so forth, it should be understood that this is because it is not possible in that way.

400. Sāṭakapatto sarīraṭṭhapatto. Āpattiyāti pārājikāpattiyā aññabhāgiyaṃ saṅghādisesādi, adhikaraṇañca āpattipaññattiyā. “Leso nāma āpattibhāgo”ti vuttattā āpattibhāvaleso vuttoti veditabbo, tasmā pārājikāpattito aññabhāgiyassa āpattipaññattiyā ādhāraṇaṭṭhena “adhikaraṇa”nti saṅkhyaṃ gatassa saṅghādisesādino āpattinikāyassa āpattibhāvalesaṃ gahetvā codanā āpattilesacodanāti veditabbā.

400. Sāṭakapatto means sarīraṭṭhapatto (a bowl related to the body). (There is also a reading pariyaṭṭhapattaṃ, meaning an earthen bowl). In this context, āpattiyā refers to that which is a different part from a Pārājika offense, such as a Saṅghādisesa offense, etc., and it is also a legal question concerning the designation of an offense. Because it is said, "A 'pretext' (lesa) is a part of an offense (āpattibhāga)," it should be understood that the pretext which is the state of being an offense is spoken of. Therefore, an accusation made by taking the pretext which is the state of being an offense of the group of offenses such as Saṅghādisesa, etc.—which, being a different part from a Pārājika offense, has come to be called a 'legal question' (adhikaraṇa) by way of being the basis for the designation of an offense—should be known as an 'offense-pretext accusation' (āpattilesacodanā).

408. Anāpatti tathāsaññī codeti vā codāpeti vāti āpattaññabhāgiyacodanāyameva, na aññattha. Ettāvatā paṭhamaduṭṭhadose vuttavicaraṇāya saṃsanditaṃ hoti, taṃ idha kathaṃ paññāyatīti ce? Kaṅkhāvitaraṇiyā vacanato. Vuttañhi “tattha idha ca āpattaññabhāgiyacodanāya tathāsaññinopi anāpattī”ti.

408. In the phrase, "There is no offense for one who, perceiving it as such, accuses or causes another to accuse," this applies only to an accusation concerning a different part of an offense, not to another accusation. By this much, it is connected with the discussion stated in the first training rule on malicious intent. If one were to ask, "How is that apparent here?" It is apparent from the Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī. For indeed, it was said: "There and here, in the case of an accusation concerning a different part of an offense, there is no offense even for one perceiving it as such."

Aññābhāgiyasikkhaṃ yo, neva sikkhati yuttito. Gacche vinayaviññūhi, aññabhāgiyatañca

Whatever monk does not properly practice the training that has the fruit of Arahantship as its part, that monk should, in the view of those skilled in the Vinaya, reach the state of being one of another faction.

Soti.

Thus.

Dutiyaduṭṭhadosasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the second training rule concerning malicious intent is concluded.

10. Paṭhamasaṅghabhedasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

10. The commentary on the first training rule concerning schism in the Saṅgha.

409. “Vajjaṃ [V 0.0182] na phuseyyā”ti ca pāṭho.

409. There is also the reading: "He should not encounter a fault."

410. Tesaṃ anurūpājānanato asabbaññū assa. “Na, bhikkhave, asenāsanikena vassaṃ upagantabba”nti (mahāva. 204) vuttattā paṭikkhittameva. Tikoṭiparisuddhanti parassa pāpapasaṅganivāraṇatthaṃ vuttaṃ, na paṭiccakammanivāraṇatthaṃ koṭīhīti ākārehi. Parisuddhanti vimuttaṃ. Dasahi lesehi uddissa kataṃ samaṇā paribhuñjanti, assamaṇā imeti sāsanassa garahabhāvo āgaccheyya[M 0.0205], garahapaccayā loko vā apuññaṃ ariyūpavādaṃ pasaveyya, tehi vimuttanti attho. Vāguranti migajālaṃ. Attano atthāya vātiādinā paresaṃ atthāya kate kappiyabhāvaṃ dassetvā bhikkhūnañca aññesañca atthāya kate taṃ dassetuṃ “matānaṃ petakiccatthāyā”tiādimāha.

410. Because of not knowing what is suitable for them, he would not be omniscient. Because it is said, "Monks, one without a lodging should not enter upon the rains residence" (Mahāvagga 204), it is indeed prohibited. The phrase "pure in three aspects" (tikoṭiparisuddhaṃ) is said to prevent another's doubt that it might be an occasion for demerit; it is not said to prevent an action that arises from a cause. Here, `koṭīhi` means by aspects. `Parisuddhaṃ` means freed. If ascetics consume meat that was prepared having been specified with the ten traces, a state of being blamed would come to the Dispensation, with the thought, "These are not true ascetics." Or, on account of that blame, the world might generate demerit, the slandering of noble ones. The meaning of "freed from them" (tehi vimuttaṃ) is being free from those causes for generating demerit. `Vāgura` means a deer-net. By the phrase beginning "for one's own benefit," having shown the permissibility of what is prepared for the benefit of others, in order to show that same permissibility for what is prepared for the benefit of monks and others, he stated the phrase beginning "for the sake of funeral rites for the dead."

Yaṃ yaṃ hītiādi tassa kāraṇassa dassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Puna pañcannaṃ sahadhammikānaṃ atthāya kataṃ na kappatīti vuttanti kira dhammasiritthero. Gaṇṭhipade “bhikkhūnameva suddhānaṃ atthāya kataṃ na vaṭṭatī”ti likhitaṃ. Aparehi pana “matānaṃ petakiccatthāyātiādinā vuttepi kappati, bhikkhūnaṃyeva atthāyāti iminā ‘bhikkhūnampi datvā mayaṃ bhuñjissāmā’ti katampi vuttaṃ. Puna ‘pañcasu ekaṃ uddissakataṃ itaresaṃ na kappatī’ti dassanatthaṃ ‘pañcasu hi sahadhammikesūtiādi vutta’nti vadantī”ti vuttaṃ. Aññatarasmiṃ pana gaṇṭhipade “amhākanti ca rājayuttādīnanti ca vutte vaṭṭatīti vatvā ‘tumhāka’nti avatvā ‘petakiccatthāyāti vuttepi vaṭṭatī’ti ca dassetvā sabbattha vuttānaṃ, ādisaddena saṅgahitānañca lakkhaṇaṃ ṭhapentena ‘bhikkhūnaṃyevā’tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha ‘bhikkhūnaṃ uddiṭṭhe evāti adhippāyenā’ti vuttaṃ. Na ‘tumhākaṃ, amhākañcāti vutte anāpattī’ti dassanatthaṃ. Kasmā? Missakavārassa abhāvā. Lakkhaṇaṃ nāma vuttānaṃ, vuttasadisānañca hoti. ‘Sace petakiccatthāyāti vuttaṭṭhāne bhikkhūnaṃ bhojanaṃ sandhāya karontī’ti vadanti mahāaṭṭhakathāyañca ‘tasmiṃ vāre ca na tumhākanti vutte vaṭṭatī’ti vuttattā. Teneva idhāpi ‘petakiccatthāya, maṅgalādīnaṃ vā atthāya katepi eseva nayo’ti pubbe vuttatthavasena vuttaṃ. ‘Avadhāraṇatthena missake vaṭṭatī’ti ce? ‘Kappiyamaṃsassa hi paṭiggahaṇe āpatti natthī’ti vacanena akappiyapaṭiggahaṇe āpattīti āpannaṃ, ‘tañca gahetabbaṃ siyā’ti paṭikkhipitabbā”ti vuttaṃ, taṃ sundaraṃ viya dissati, vicāretvā gahetabbaṃ. Yattha cāti bhikkhūnaṃ atthāya katepi. Tamatthaṃ āvi kātuṃ “sace panā”tiādi vuttaṃ[V 0.0183]. Ettha pana “bhikkhunīnaṃ dukkaṭaṃ, itaresaṃ daṇḍakammavatthū”ti vadanti. Kappaṃ nirayamhīti asaṅkhyeyyakappaṃ. Vivaṭṭaṭṭhāyikāleyeva saṅghabhedo hotīti. Kappanti āyukappaṃ.

The phrase `yaṃ yaṃ hi`, and so forth, is stated for the purpose of showing that reason. Furthermore, the Elder Dhammasiri reportedly said: 'Meat prepared for the sake of five fellow practitioners is not allowable.' In the Gaṇṭhipada, it is written: 'Meat prepared for the sake of only pure monks (i.e., unmixed with novices) is not allowable.' Others, however, say: 'Even when it is said, “for the sake of the dead, for funeral rites,” and so on, it is allowable. By this phrase, “for the sake of monks only,” it is also stated regarding meat prepared with the thought, “Having given to the monks, we shall eat.”' Furthermore, it is said that they say: 'To show this meaning—“Meat prepared having specified one among five fellow practitioners is not allowable for the others”—the passage beginning with `pañcasu hi sahadhammikesu` is stated.' In another Gaṇṭhipada, however, it is stated: 'Having stated, “When it is said, ‘for us,’ and ‘for royal officials and so on,’ it is allowable,” and having shown, “Without saying, ‘for you (venerable sirs),’ even when it is said, ‘for the sake of funeral rites,’ it is allowable,” the Commentator, establishing the characteristic of those who are mentioned everywhere and those included by the word `ādi` (etc.), stated the passage beginning with `bhikkhūnaṃyeva`.' Therein, it is stated that this was said with the intention: 'only in the case of meat specified for monks.' It was not stated to show that 'there is no offense when it is said, “for you” or “for us.”' Why? Because of the absence of a mixed case. A characteristic, indeed, applies to those who are mentioned and to those who are similar to what is mentioned. They say, 'If, in a situation where it is said, “for the sake of funeral rites,” they prepare it intending it as a meal for the monks,' because it is stated in the Mahā-aṭṭhakathā, 'And in that case, when it is said, “Not for you,” it is allowable.' For that very reason, here also it is stated according to the meaning previously given: 'Even when meat is prepared for the sake of funeral rites, or for the sake of auspicious ceremonies and so on, this same principle applies.' If one should say, 'Because of the emphatic meaning, it is allowable in a mixed case,' [that view] should be rejected. For it is said: 'By the statement, “Indeed, in receiving allowable meat there is no offense,” the meaning is arrived at that in receiving unallowable meat there is an offense, and that [meaning] should be accepted.' That appears sound, but it should be accepted only after investigation. Regarding the phrase `yattha ca`, this means: even when meat is prepared for the sake of monks. To make that meaning clear, the passage beginning with `sace pana` is stated. Here, however, they say: 'For nuns, it is a dukkaṭa offense; for others, it is a matter for disciplinary action.' 'A kappa in hell' means an incalculable kappa. Schism in the Saṅgha occurs only during the period of thriving. 'Kappa' here means a lifespan-eon.

411. Kusalanti khemaṃ. Āpattibhayā katā lajjīhīti ettha āpattibhayena avassaṃ ārocentīti dassanatthaṃ “lajjī rakkhissatī”ti (visuddhi. 1.42; pārā. aṭṭha. 1.45) porāṇavacanassānurūpato [M 0.0206] “aññehi lajjīhī”ti vuttaṃ. Alajjissapi anārocentassa āpattiyeva “ye passanti ye suṇantī”ti vacanato.

411. "Kusalaṃ" means safety. Here, in the phrase "by the scrupulous who are motivated by fear of an offense," in order to show that "they certainly inform out of fear of an offense," and in accordance with the ancient saying, "The scrupulous one will guard," it is said, "by other scrupulous ones." For one who does not inform, even about a shameless person, there is an offense indeed, because of the statement, "those who see, those who hear."

416. Asamanubhāsantassāti kammakārake kattuniddeso, samanubhāsanakammaṃ akariyamānassāti attho. Odissa anuññāto nāma ummattakakhittacittavedanaṭṭādiko “anāpatti ādikammikassā”ti ariṭṭhasikkhāpade āgatattā atthīti ce? Yampītiādi. Sā panesā anāpatti. So vuccatīti tattha āgatopi sakammabyāvaṭopi evaṃ vuccati. Etenupāyenāti asamanubhāsantassa ca ādikammikassa ca vuttatthavasena. Ṭhapetvā ariṭṭhasikkhāpadanti tattha ādikammikapadābhāvā.

416. Regarding "asamanubhāsantassa," it is an indication of the agent in the objective case; the meaning is "for one to whom the act of admonition is not being performed." If one should say, "Is there not one who is specifically permitted—namely one who is insane, mentally deranged, afflicted by pain, and so on—since it is stated in the Ariṭṭha training rule, 'There is no offense for the initial perpetrator'?" The reply is "Yampi...", etc. But that is a non-offense. Regarding "so vuccati" (he is so called): even one who has arrived there and one who is occupied with their own affairs is spoken of thus. "By this method" means: by the power of the stated meaning for both one who is not being admonished and for the initial perpetrator. The phrase "excepting the Ariṭṭha training rule" is stated because the term "initial perpetrator" is absent there.

Tivaṅgikanti ettha vācāya eva paṭinissajjantassa oṭṭhacalanādikāyaviññatti hoti, tasmā duvidhampi viññattiṃ kathentassa hoti. Vacībhedaṃ kātuṃ asakkontassa kāyavikāraṃ karontassa anāpattiyā bhavitabbaṃ. Kasmā? Tivaṅgesu ekassa parihīnattā, tasmā tivaṅgabhāvo āpattiyā, aṅgahānibhāvo anāpattiyāti gahetabbaṃ. Ettha siyā – yadi aṅgahānibhāvena anāpatti, evaṃ santepi vikāraṃ akatvā citteneva vissajjentassa anāpattiyā bhavitabbanti? Taṃ na, kasmā? Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “kāyavikāraṃ vā vacībhedaṃ vā akarontasseva pana āpajjanato akiriya”nti hi vuttaṃ, “cittaṃ vā anuppādentassa vā”ti na vuttaṃ, tasmā cittañca nāma viññattipaṭibaddhaṃ evāti visuṃ aṅgabhāveneva vuttattā jānitabbanti ce? Taṃ na, dvinnaṃyeva akiriyāti, tasmā cittena vissajjentassāpi āpatti viya dissati, upaparikkhitvā gahetabbaṃ. Tattha “akusalacitta”nti vuttanti ce? “Cittabāhullato vutta”nti vadanti. Tepi kira bāhullato vadanti.

Here, regarding the term `tivaṅgika`, for a monk who renounces by speech alone, there is bodily intimation, such as the movement of the lips; therefore, it is the case for one who makes both kinds of intimation. For one who is unable to make a verbal utterance but makes a bodily gesture, there should be no offense. Why? Because of the deficiency of one of the three factors. Therefore, it should be understood that the state of having three factors pertains to an offense, and the state of a deficient factor pertains to no offense. Here, an objection might be raised: 'If there is no offense due to the deficiency of a factor, then for one who renounces by mind alone without making a gesture, there should also be no offense.' That is not so. Why? Because in the commentary it is said, 'For one who does not make a bodily gesture or a verbal utterance, there is non-action with respect to incurring an offense'; but it is not said, 'or for one who does not arouse the mind.' If one were to argue, 'Therefore, it should be known that what is called “mind” is indeed connected to intimation, because it is spoken of as a separate factor,' that is also not so. The non-action pertains to only two factors. Therefore, for one who renounces by mind alone, it appears as if there is an offense; this should be accepted after examination. Therein, if one should say, 'It is said “unwholesome mind,”' they say, 'It is said due to the abundance of mind-states.' Indeed, those teachers too speak from the perspective of abundance.

Paṭhamasaṅghabhedasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the first training rule concerning schism in the Saṅgha is concluded.

11. Dutiyasaṅghabhedasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

11. Commentary on the Second Training Rule concerning Schism in the Saṅgha

422. Saññīti [V 0.0184] saññino.

422. Saññīti means saññino (those who are percipient).

Dutiyasaṅghabhedasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the second training rule concerning schism in the Saṅgha is concluded.

12. Dubbacasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

12. Commentary on the Training Rule concerning Being Difficult to Admonish

424. Pataṃ [M 0.0207] patitaṃ vivari vivaṭṭayi. Ekato ussāreti ca giḷitato ṭhapeti ca. Ekapaṃsuthupakanadīsaṅkhaṃ dīghamūlakapaṇṇasevālaṃ sevālaṃ daṇḍisipippariṃ paṇakaṃ pesiṭṭhiṃ nissāreti. Tilabījakanti sukhumamūlapaṇṇakaṃ hutvā udakapiṭṭhe pattharikaṃ udakapappaṭakaṃ nissāreti.

424. One uncovers and turns over every fallen thing. One also gathers them together and also places them together. One removes a single heap of dust mixed with a little mud, moss with long roots and full of leaves, the red-colored stalked plant, the water-plant called 'narapasī', moss, and moss with a small base. Here, in the word tilabījaka, it means one removes a thin film on the water that, having fine roots and fine leaves, is spread on the surface of the water.

425-6. “Dubbaccajātiko”tipi paṭhanti. Apadānenāti purāṇakammena. “Kiṃ pubbepi mayaṃ evarūpaṃ karomātiādinā ekūnavīsatī”ti mahāpaccariyaṃ kira vuttaṃ. Mahāaṭṭhakathāyañca anumānasuttaṭṭhakathāyañca “soḷasavatthukā”ti vuttaṃ, taṃ sameti.

Some also read 'of a nature difficult to admonish' (dubbaccajātiko). Here, 'by a past deed' (apadānena) means by a past action. It is said that in the Mahāpaccariya it is stated, 'Did we also in the past do such a thing?' and so on, for nineteen topics. And in the Mahā-aṭṭhakathā and the Anumānasutta commentary, 'sixteen grounds' is stated; that agrees.

Dubbacasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the training rule concerning being difficult to admonish is concluded.

13. Kuladūsakasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

13. The Commentary on the Training Rule concerning Corrupting Families

431. Na kevalaṃ vihāro eva kīṭāgiri, sopi gāmo “kīṭāgiri”cceva vuccati. Gāmañhi sandhāya parato “na assajipunabbasukehi bhikkhūhi kīṭāgirismiṃ vatthabba”nti vuttaṃ. Ekasaṃvacchare dvikkhattuṃ vassati kira, taṃ sandhāya “dvīhi meghehī”ti vuttaṃ. Samadhikanti cha jane sandhāya. Akatavatthunti navaṃ aṭṭhuppattiṃ. “Jābhisumanādigacchaṃ allānaṃ haritānaṃ evā”ti likhitaṃ. Bhūtagāmabījagāmabhedato panesa bhedo. Vatatthāyāti vatiatthāya. Yaṃkiñcīti sodakaṃ vā nirudakaṃ vā. Ārāmādiatthāyāti vanarājikādiatthāya. Mālāvaccharopanaṃ kuladūsakaṃyeva sandhāya, ganthanādisabbaṃ na sandhāya vuttanti. Kathaṃ paññāyatīti ce? Taṃ dassetuṃ “buddhena dhammo”tiādi. “Āveḷaṃ ābiḷa”ntipi pāṭho.

431. Not only the monastery is Kīṭāgiri; that village is also called 'Kīṭāgiri'. Indeed, referring to the village, it is stated later: 'The monks Assaji and Punabbasuka should not dwell in Kīṭāgiri.' It is said that it rains twice in one year; referring to this, 'by two clouds' is stated. 'More than that' (samadhikaṃ) is said referring to six people. 'Unmade ground' (akatavatthu) means a new occasion for an offense. It is written: 'A bush of jasmine and so on, moist and green indeed.' This distinction, however, is from the division of living plants and seed plants. 'For the sake of the fence' (vatatthāya) means for the purpose of a fence. Here, 'whatever' (yaṃkiñci) refers to a water-course, whether with or without water. 'For the sake of a park, etc.' (ārāmādiatthāya) means for the sake of a forest-line, etc. The planting of small flowering plants is said with reference only to the act of corrupting families; it should be understood that this is not said with reference to all such acts, such as stringing flowers. If it is asked, 'How is this known?'—to show this, 'the Dhamma by the Buddha,' etc., is stated. There is also the reading 'āveḷaṃ ābiḷaṃ'.

Gopphananti ganthanaṃ. Veṭhimanti taggatikameva. Vedhimaṃ aññena kenaci pupphaṃ vedhetvā kataṃ[V 0.0185]. Kaṇṭakampi bandhitunti ettha “sayaṃ vijjhanatthaṃ na vaṭṭati. Aññassatthāya vaṭṭatī”ti vadanti. Jālamayaṃ vitānaṃ jālavitānaṃ. Pupphapaṭicchakaṃ gavakkhaṃ viya sachiddaṃ karonti. Tālapaṇṇaguḷakanti tālapaṇṇamayaṃ puna katampi paṭichijjakameva. Dhammarajju cetiyaṃ vā bodhiṃ vā pupphappavesanatthaṃ āvijjhitvā [M 0.0208] baddharajju. “Kāsāvena baddhampi suttavākādīhi baddhaṃ bhaṇḍitasadisa”nti likhitaṃ. Aṃsabhaṇḍikaṃ pasibbake pakkhittasadisattā vedhimaṃ na jātaṃ, tasmā “sithilabaddhassa antarantarā pakkhipituṃ na vaṭṭatī”ti vadanti. “Aññamaññaṃ aphusāpetvā anekakkhattumpi parikkhipituṃ vaṭṭatī”ti vadanti. Pūritanti dīghato pasāretvā pūritaṃ. Ghaṭikadāmaolambakoti “yamakadāmaolambako”ti likhitaṃ. “Geṇḍukharapattadāmānaṃ paṭikkhittattā celādīhi katadāmampi na vaṭṭati akappiyānulomattā”ti vadanti.

'Gopphana' means tying or stringing. 'Veṭhima' means something of that same nature. A 'vedhima' is made by piercing a flower with some other thing. Here, concerning 'even a thorn may be tied,' they say: "It is not suitable for piercing by oneself; it is suitable for the purpose of another." A canopy made of a net is a 'jālavitāna'. They make a flower-receptacle with holes, like a latticed window. Here, regarding 'tālapaṇṇaguḷaka', a cluster made of palm leaves, even if made again, is simply to be cut again. A 'dhammarajju' is a rope tied to a cetiya or a Bodhi tree, having been pierced for inserting flowers. It is written: "Even if tied with a kāsāva robe, or tied with thread, fiber, and so on, it is similar to being strung into a garland." An 'aṃsabandhika' (shoulder-strap), because it is similar to being placed in a bag, does not become a 'vedhima'; therefore, they say: "For a loosely tied one, it is suitable to insert [flowers] in the spaces in between." They say: "Without causing them to touch one another, it is suitable to encircle [it] even many times." 'Pūrita' means filled by being spread out lengthwise. Regarding 'ghaṭikadāmaolambaka', it is written as 'yamakadāmaolambaka' (a hanging pair of garlands). They say: "Because garlands of 'geṇḍuka' and 'kharapatta' are prohibited, even a garland made of cloth and so on is not suitable, because it conforms to what is unallowable."

“Recakaṃ nāma tathālāsiyanāṭanaṭānaṃ nacca”nti likhitaṃ. Taṃ “parivattantī”ti vuttaṃ. “Sāriyo nāma rutasunakhā siṅgālakammakuruṅgakeḷipane ṭhitā”ti kira pāṭho. “Nibujjhantī”ti pāḷi.

It is written: "'Recaka' is the dance of those who perform swaying, causing to dance, and dancing." That is said to be 'parivattanti' (they turn around). It is said that there is this reading: "'Sāriyo' are howling dogs, standing amidst the actions of jackals and the play of deer." There is the Pāḷi text 'nibujjhanti'.

432. Abalabalādi-padānaṃ uppaṭipāṭiyā. Yathā pāmokkhānaṃ vasena sabbepi “assajipunabbasukā”ti vuttā, tathā pāmokkhappattasāvakassa vasena tadāyattavuttine sabbepi “sāriputtā”ti. Tena vuttaṃ “gacchatha tumhe sāriputtā”ti.

432. The words 'abalabala,' etc., are stated out of their proper order. Just as, by way of the chiefs, all are called 'Assaji and Punabbasu,' so too, by way of the disciple who has attained the foremost position, all those whose living is dependent on him are called 'Sāriputtas'. Therefore, it was said: "Go, you Sāriputtas."

433. “Gāme vā na vasitabba”nti imināva tasmiṃ gāme aññattha na vasitabbanti siddhaṃ. “Tasmiṃ vihāre vā”ti kasmā vuttanti ce? Atthasabbhāvato. Yasmiñhi gāme kuladūsakakammaṃ kataṃ, tasmiṃ gāme, yasmiṃ vihāre vasantena kuladūsanaṃ kataṃ, taṃ vihāraṃ ṭhapetvā aññasmiṃ vasituṃ na vaṭṭatīti dassanatthaṃ. Taṃ kathanti ce? “Gāme vā na vasitabba”nti vacanena yasmiṃ gāme kuladūsanakammaṃ kataṃ, tasmiṃ vihārepi vasituṃ na labbhatīti āpannaṃ, taṃ disvā “tasmiṃ vihāre”ti vuttaṃ, tena tasmiṃ gāme aññasmiṃ vasituṃ labbhatīti siddhaṃ. “Tasmiṃ vihāre vasantenā”ti iminā tasmiṃ gāme aññattha vasantena sāmantagāme piṇḍāya carituṃ vaṭṭatīti dīpitaṃ hoti. Sāmantavihārepīti sāmantavihāro nāma tasmiṃyeva gāme tassa vihārassa sāmantavihāro ca tassa gāmassa sāmantavihāro cāti ubhayaṃ vuccati, etena tasmiṃ gāme aññattha vasantena tasmiṃ gāme piṇḍāya na caritabbaṃ. Sāmantagāmepi piṇḍāya carituṃ vaṭṭati, puna yasmiṃ gāme kuladūsanakammaṃ kataṃ, tassa sāmantagāme kuladūsakavihārassa sāmantavatthuvihāre vasantena tasmiṃ gāmepi carituṃ vaṭṭati. Yasmiṃ [V 0.0186] sāmantagāme kuladūsakaṃ na kataṃ, tasmimpi carituṃ vaṭṭati, neva vihāreti adhippāyo. “Na [M 0.0209] nagare caritu”nti vuttattā aññasmiṃ vihāre tasmiṃ gāme vasituṃ vaṭṭatīti dīpitaṃ hotīti eke. Gaṇṭhipadesu pana vicāraṇā eva natthi, tasmā suṭṭhu vicāretvā kathetabbaṃ.

433. By this very statement, 'One should not dwell in the village,' it is established that one should not dwell elsewhere in that village. If it is asked, 'Why was it said, "or in that monastery"?', it is because of the possibility of a certain meaning. Indeed, it was said for the purpose of showing that in whichever village an act of corrupting families has been committed, and while dwelling in whichever monastery in that village the corruption of families was done, it is not proper to dwell in another monastery, having set aside that monastery. If it is asked, 'How is this so?', by the statement, 'One should not dwell in the village,' the meaning is arrived at that if an act of corrupting families has been committed in a village, it is not permissible to dwell even in a monastery in that village. Seeing this, it was said, 'in that monastery.' By that, it is established that it is permissible to dwell elsewhere in that village. By this phrase, 'while dwelling in that monastery,' it is clarified that while dwelling elsewhere in that village, it is not proper to go for alms in a neighboring village. Here, in the phrase 'Even in a neighboring monastery,' a 'neighboring monastery' means both a monastery that is near to that monastery in that very village, and a monastery that is near to that village; in this manner, both are meant. By this, while dwelling in another place in that village, one should not go for alms in that village. It is proper to go for alms also in a neighboring village. Furthermore, if in a certain village an act of corrupting families was done, while dwelling in a neighboring village in a monastery on grounds adjacent to the family-corrupting monastery, it is proper to go for alms even in that neighboring village. In whichever neighboring village the corruption of families was not done, it is proper to go for alms in that village as well; the intention, however, is not in the monastery where the offense was committed. Some say that because it was said, 'One should not go about in the city,' it is clarified that it is proper to dwell in another monastery in that village. But in the Gaṇṭhipadas, there is no investigation at all; therefore, this should be stated only after having investigated it well.

436-7. Dāpetuṃ na labhanti, pupphadānañhi siyā. Tasseva na kappatīti ettha yāguādīni ānetvā “dadantū”ti icchāvasena vadati ce, sabbesaṃ na kappati, kevalaṃ pana suddhacittena attānaṃ vā paresaṃ vā anuddisitvā “ime manussā dānaṃ datvā puññaṃ pasavantū”ti vadantassa tasseva na kappati yāguādīnaṃ paccayapaṭisaṃyuttakathāya uppannattā. Mahāaṭṭhakathāyampi “pañcannampi sahadhammikāna”nti visesetvā avuttattā atthato sayamevāti apare. Ācariyā pana “yathā mahāpaccariyaṃ, kurundiyañca ‘tassevā’ti visesetvā vuttaṃ, evaṃ mahāaṭṭhakathāyaṃ visesetvā na vuttaṃ, tasmā sabbesaṃ na kappatī”ti vadanti.

436-7. They are not allowed to cause others to give, for it would be an offering of flowers. Herein, regarding the phrase 'it is not allowable for him alone': if one, having brought rice-gruel and so forth, says, 'Let them give,' through the power of desire, it is not allowable for all. However, for one who, with a pure mind and without specifying oneself or others, says, 'May these people, having given a gift, generate merit,' it is not allowable for that one alone, because of the arising of talk connected with requisites such as rice-gruel. Others say that in the Mahāaṭṭhakathā, because it is not specified by saying 'for the five co-religionists,' the meaning is 'by oneself alone.' But the teachers say: 'Just as in the Mahāpaccarī and the Kurundī it is specified as "for him alone," so in the Mahāaṭṭhakathā it is not specified; therefore, it is not allowable for all.'

Kuladūsakasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the training rule concerning corrupting families is concluded.

Terasakakaṇḍavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Terasakakaṇḍa is concluded.

3. Aniyatakaṇḍo

3. The Chapter on the Indeterminate

1. Paṭhamaaniyatasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

1. Commentary on the First Indeterminate Training Rule

444-5. Uddesanti [V 0.0187][M 0.0210] uddisanaṃ, āsāḷhinakkhattaṃ nāma vassūpagamapūjā. Sotassa rahoti ettha raho-vacanasāmaññato vuttaṃ duṭṭhullasāmaññato duṭṭhullārocanappaṭicchādanasikkhāpadesu pārājikavacanaṃ viya. Tasmā “cakkhussa raheneva pana paricchedo kātabbo”ti vuttaṃ. Kathaṃ paññāyatīti ce? “Mātugāmo nāma tadahujātāpi dārikā”ti vacanato, “alaṃkammaniyeti sakkā hoti methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevitu”nti vacanato ca rahonisajjassādo cettha methunasannissitakileso, na dutiye viya duṭṭhullavācassādakileso, tasmā ca paññāyati “sotassa raho nādhippeto”ti. Keci pana “tañca labbhatīti vacanassa dassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ, tena dutiye vuttā viññū paṭibalā gahitā hotī”ti vadanti. Yena vā sāti ettha vā-saddo “tena so bhikkhu kāretabbo vā”ti yojetabbo, so ca vikappattho, tasmā kāretabbo vā paṭijānamāno, na vā kāretabbo appaṭijānamānoti attho. Tena vuttaṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “paṭijānamānova tena so bhikkhu kāretabbo…pe… na kāretabbo”ti. Tasmā eva pāḷiyaṃ tadatthadvayadassanatthaṃ “sā ce evaṃ vadeyyā”tiādi vuttaṃ. “Saddheyyavacasā”ti iminā sotāpannā atthabhañjanakaṃ na bhaṇanti, sesaṃ bhaṇantīti vādīnaṃ vādo paṭisedhito hoti. “Diṭṭha”nti vuttattā “olokesī”ti sundaraṃ. Rakkheyyāsīti mama visesaṃ kassaci nāroceyyāsīti adhippāyo.

444-5. 'They point out' means a declaration; the Āsāḷhī constellation means a festival of offering upon entering the Rains-residence. Herein, 'seclusion of the ear' is stated due to the general nature of the word 'seclusion', just as the word 'pārājika' is stated in the training rules on announcing and on concealing a grave offense due to the general nature of 'grave offense'. Therefore, it was said, 'but the determination should be made only by seclusion of the eye.' If it is asked, 'How is this understood?' It is understood from the passage, 'A woman means even a girl born on that very day,' and from the passage, '“Suitable for the act” means she is able to engage in sexual intercourse.' And herein, the pleasure in sitting in seclusion is a defilement associated with sexual intercourse; it is not, as in the second case, the defilement of pleasure in lewd speech. And for that reason, it is understood that 'seclusion of the ear' is not intended. But some say: 'This is stated to show the statement, "And that is also obtained." By this, the intelligent and capable woman mentioned in the second case is included.' Herein, in 'yena vā sā', the word 'vā' should be construed as 'by that, that monk should be dealt with'. And that word 'vā' has the meaning of an alternative. Therefore, the meaning is: if he confesses, he should be dealt with; if he does not confess, he should not be dealt with. For that reason, it is said in the Commentary: 'Only if he confesses should that monk be dealt with... he should not be dealt with.' For this very reason, in the Pāḷi text, in order to show these two meanings, 'If she should speak thus,' etc., is stated. By this, 'of trustworthy speech', the view of those who hold that stream-enterers do not speak falsehood that destroys the benefit, but do speak other falsehoods, is refuted. Because it was said, 'was seen', the word 'you looked' is appropriate. Regarding 'You should guard', the intention is, 'You should not announce my special attainment to anyone.'

446. “Sā ce evaṃ vadeyya ‘ayyassa mayā sutaṃ nisinnassa mātugāmaṃ duṭṭhullāhi vācāhi obhāsentassā’”ti, idaṃ kimatthamettha vuttaṃ, na adhippetañhetaṃ idha sotassa raho nādhippetoti katvāti ce? Alaṃkammaniyaṭṭhāne duṭṭhullavācāpi labbhati, na pana nālaṃkammaniyaṭṭhāne methunanti dassanatthaṃ vuttanti veditabbanti. Yathā etaṃ, tathā “sā ce evaṃ vadeyya [V 0.0188] ‘ayyassa mayā sutaṃ mātugāmassa santike attakāmapāricariyāya vaṇṇaṃ bhāsantassā’”ti etampi idha labbhati, na dutiye nālaṃkammaniyaṭṭhānattāti eke. Kaṅkhāvitaraṇiyaṃ (kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. dutiyāniyatasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā) idhāpi dutiyāniyatādhikāre pārājikāpattiñca [M 0.0211] parihāpetvā duṭṭhullavācāpattiyā vuttattā paṭhamāniyate duṭṭhullavācāpatti na vuttāti ce? “Sā ce”ti tassā pāḷiyā potthakā sodhetabbā. Gaṇṭhipade ca “idha sikkhāpade methunakāyasaṃsaggarahonisajjānamevāgatattā cakkhussarahova pamāṇa”nti likhitaṃ, dutiyāniyatādhikāre ca “anandho kāyasaṃsaggaṃ passati, abadhiro duṭṭhullaṃ suṇāti, kāyacittato kāyasaṃsaggo, vācācittato duṭṭhullaṃ, ubhayehi ubhaya”nti ca likhitaṃ. Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “samuṭṭhānādīni paṭhamapārājikasadisānevā”ti vuttattāpi duṭṭhullavādo na sundaro “tadahujātā”ti vuttattāti.

446. If one were to ask: Regarding the text, 'If she were to say, "I heard from the venerable one who, while seated, was addressing a woman with lewd words,"' for what purpose is this stated here, given that seclusion of the ear is not intended in this case? It should be understood that it is stated to show this meaning: in a place suitable for sexual intercourse, lewd speech is also possible, but in a place not suitable for sexual intercourse, sexual intercourse is not. Just as this is stated, so too, some say that this statement, 'If she were to say, "I heard from the venerable one who was praising the service of his own sensual desires in the presence of a woman,"' is also possible here, but not in the second Aniyata rule because it is a place not suitable for sexual intercourse. If it is argued that in the Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī, in the section on the second Aniyata, the offense of lewd speech is stated—having excluded the Pārājika offense—whereas in the first Aniyata, the offense of lewd speech is not stated, then the manuscripts of that Pali text beginning with 'Sā ce' should be corrected. And in the Gaṇṭhipada it is written: 'Here in this training rule, because only sexual intercourse, bodily contact, and sitting in seclusion have come down, seclusion of the eye is the standard.' And in the section on the second Aniyata it is also written: 'One who is not blind sees bodily contact; one who is not deaf hears lewd speech. Bodily contact is from body and mind; lewd speech is from speech and mind; from both, both occur.' Also, because it is stated in the Aṭṭhakathā, 'The origins and so forth are just like those of the first Pārājika,' the argument for lewd speech is not sound, on account of it being stated 'even a girl born on that very day'.

Paṭhamaaniyatasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the first indeterminate training rule is concluded.

2. Dutiyaaniyatasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

2. Commentary on the Second Indeterminate Training Rule

453. Dutiye kesuci potthakesu “na heva kho pana paṭicchannaṃ āsanaṃ hoti āsana”nti likhitaṃ. “Āsananti adhikaṃ, uddharitānurūpa”nti likhitaṃ. Dvepi rahā idha adhippetā kāyasaṃsaggaduṭṭhullavācārahonisajjaggahaṇato. Yadi evaṃ “mātugāmo nāma viññū paṭibalā”ti kimatthaṃ vuttanti? Ayameva hi mātugāmo dvinnampi kāyasaṃsaggaduṭṭhullavācānaṃ ekato vatthubhūto, tasmā vuttaṃ. Kāyasaṃsaggassa vatthubhūto dassito, na itarassāti katvā duṭṭhullavācameva sandhāya tassā vatthuṃ dassento evamāha.

453. In some manuscripts of the second rule, it is written: “Indeed, a concealed seat is not a seat seat.” It is also written: “The word ‘seat’ is excessive and suitable for removal.” Both kinds of seclusion are intended here, because of the inclusion of bodily contact, lewd speech, and secluded sitting. If this is so, why is it said: “A woman is one who is intelligent and capable”? For this very woman is the basis for both bodily contact and lewd speech together; therefore, it is stated. The basis for bodily contact is shown, but not for the other. Considering this, referring only to lewd speech and showing its basis, it is said thus.

Etthāha – yathā paṭhame anadhippetāpi duṭṭhullavācā sambhavavisesadassanatthaṃ vuttā, idhāpi kāyasaṃsaggo, kasmā na tassa vasena cakkhussa raho gahetabboti? Āma na gahetabbo, na ca gahito, gahito eva pana nisajjavasena, na hi aṅgassa nisajjā visesoti. Appaṭicchanne sati kathaṃ cakkhussa rahoti ce? Dūrattā. Paṭhame kasmā itthisatampi anāpattiṃ na karoti, idha kasmā ekāpi karotīti ce? No vuccati siddhattā. Siddhaṃ hoti, yadidaṃ aññataro bhikkhu vesāliyaṃ mahāvane…pe… dvāraṃ vivaritvā nipanno hoti…pe… sambahulā itthiyo yāvadatthaṃ [M 0.0212] katvā pakkamiṃsūti (pārā. 77). Tasmā na methunassa mātugāmo dutiyo hoti. Itthiyo hi aññamaññissā vajjaṃ paṭicchādenti, teneva bhikkhunīnaṃ [V 0.0189] vajjapaṭicchādane pārājikaṃ paññattaṃ. Tathā “āyasmā udāyī tā itthiyo vihāraṃ pekkhāpetvā tāsaṃ itthīnaṃ vaccamagga”nti (pārā. 283) ettha “yā pana tā itthiyo hirimanā, tā nikkhamitvā bhikkhū ujjhāpentī”ti (pārā. 283) vacanato duṭṭhullassa mātugāmo dutiyo hotīti siddhanti adhippāyo. Ubhayatthāpi ummattakādikammikānaṃ anāpattīti tesaṃ pāṭekkaṃ nidāne āgataṃ, ādikammikānaṃ anāpattīti attho. Anugaṇṭhipade pana “acelakavagge rahopaṭicchannāsanasikkhāpade ‘viññū puriso dutiyo hotī’ti (pāci. 288) imassa anurūpato ‘itthīnaṃ satampi anāpattiṃ na karotī’ti vutta”nti ca, “dutiyāniyate ‘itthīpi purisopī’ti idaṃ bhikkhunīvagge osānasikkhāpadassa, acelakavagge appaṭicchannāsanasikkhāpadassa ca anāpattivāre ‘yo koci viññū puriso dutiyo’ti vuttaṃ. Imesaṃ anurūpato vuttanti veditabba”nti ca vuttaṃ.

Here it is said: Just as in the first [Pārājika], even though not intended, lewd speech was mentioned to show a possible special case, so too here bodily contact was mentioned. Why, then, is 'seclusion from the eye' not to be taken by means of that? Yes, it should not be taken, and it is not taken. However, it is indeed taken by means of sitting, for sitting is not a special feature of the limb. If [one asks]: 'When it is unconcealed, how can there be seclusion from the eye?' [The answer is:] Due to distance. If [one asks]: 'In the first [Pārājika], why do even a hundred women not constitute grounds for an offense, whereas here, why does even one?' [The answer is:] It is not stated, because it is established. It is established by this story: a certain monk in the Great Wood at Vesālī... having opened the door, was lying down... many women did as they wished and then departed. Therefore, a woman is not a second party for [an accusation of] sexual intercourse. For women conceal one another's faults; for that very reason, a pārājika offense was laid down for bhikkhunīs for concealing a fault. Likewise, in the text, 'Venerable Udāyī, having had those women inspect the monastery, [showed] them his private parts,' because it is said, 'But those women who were modest, having left, complained to the monks,' it is established that for lewd speech, a woman is a second party. This is the meaning. The statement 'In both cases, there is no offense for the insane, the first offender, etc.' is stated in the origin story of each of those rules; the meaning is that there is no offense for the first offenders. But in the Anugaṇṭhipada it is said: 'In the Acelakavagga, in the training rule on a secluded and concealed seat, in accordance with this text, "a discerning man is the second party," it is said, "even a hundred women do not bring about a non-offense."' And it is also said: 'In the second Aniyata rule, regarding the phrase "either a woman or a man," in the non-offense section of the final training rule in the Bhikkhunīvagga and of the training rule on an unconcealed seat in the Acelakavagga, it is said: "any discerning man is the second party." It should be understood that this is said in accordance with these rules.'

Dutiyaaniyatasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the second indeterminate training rule is concluded.

Pakiṇṇakavaṇṇanā

The Miscellaneous Commentary

Apicettha idaṃ pakiṇṇakaṃ, seyyathidaṃ – idaṃ aniyatakaṇḍaṃ nippayojanaṃ apubbābhāvatoti ce? Na, garukalahukabhedabhinnāpattiropanāropanakkamalakkhaṇadīpanappayojanato. Ettha hi “sā ce evaṃ vadeyya ‘ayyo mayā diṭṭho nisinno mātugāmassa methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevanto’ti, so ca taṃ paṭijānāti, āpattiyā kāretabbo…pe… nisajjāya kāretabbo”tiādinā (pārā. 446) āpattiyā garukāya lahukāya ca ropanakkamalakkhaṇaṃ, kāretabboti iminā anāropanakkamalakkhaṇañca dassitaṃ. Lakkhaṇadīpanato ādimhi, ante vā uddisitabbanti ce? Na, asambhavato. Kathaṃ? Na tāva ādimhi sambhavati, yesamidaṃ lakkhaṇaṃ, tesaṃ sikkhāpadānaṃ adassitattā. Na ante, garukamissakattā, tasmā garukalahukānaṃ majjhe eva uddisitabbanti arahati ubhayāmissakattā. Yā tattha lahukāpatti dassitā[M 0.0213], sāpi garukādikā. Tenevāha “methunadhammasannissitakilesasaṅkhātena rahassādenā”tiādi, tasmā garukānaṃ eva anantaraṃ uddiṭṭhātipi eke. Evaṃ sante paṭhamamevālaṃ tāvatā lakkhaṇadīpanasiddhito, kiṃ dutiyenāti ce? Na, okāsaniyamapaccayamicchāgāhanivāraṇappayojanato. “Paṭicchanne āsane alaṃkammaniye”ti okāsaniyamato hi tabbiparīte okāse idaṃ lakkhaṇaṃ na vikappitanti micchāgāho hoti, tannivāraṇato dutiyampi sātthakamevāti adhippāyo. Kasmā? Okāsabhedato, rahobhedadīpanato, rahonisajjassādabhedadīpanato[V 0.0190]. Okāsaniyamabhāve ca rahonisajjassādabhedo jāto. Dvinnaṃ rahonisajjasikkhāpadānaṃ nānatājānanañca siyā, tathā kāyasaṃsaggabhedadīpanato. Nālaṃkammaniyepi hi okāse appaṭicchanne, paṭicchannepi vā nisinnāya vātapānakavāṭachiddādīhi nikkhantakesādiggahaṇena kāyasaṃsaggo labbhatīti evamādayopi nayā vitthārato veditabbā. “Bhikkhupātimokkhe āgatanayattā bhikkhunīpātimokkhe idaṃ kaṇḍaṃ parihīnanti veditabba”nti vadanti. Atthuppattiyā tattha anupannattāti eke. Taṃ anekatthabhāvadīpanato ayuttaṃ. Sabbabuddhakāle hi bhikkhūnaṃ pañcannaṃ, bhikkhunīnaṃ cattāro ca uddesā santi. Pātimokkhuddesapaññattiyā asādhāraṇattā tattha niddiṭṭhasaṅghādisesapācittiyānanti eke. Tāsaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ ubbhajāṇumaṇḍalikaaṭṭhavatthukavasena kāyasaṃsaggaviseso pārājikavatthu, “hatthaggahaṇaṃ vā sādiyeyya, kāyaṃ vā tadatthāya upasaṃhareyyā”ti (pāci. 674-675) vacanato sādiyanampi, “santiṭṭheyya vā”ti (pāci. 675) vacanato ṭhānampi, “saṅketaṃ vā gaccheyyā”ti (pāci. 675) vacanato gamanampi, “channaṃ vā anupaviseyyā”ti (pāci. 675) vacanato paṭicchannaṭṭhānapavesopi, tathā “rattandhakāre appadīpe paṭicchanne okāse ekenekā santiṭṭheyya vā sallapeyya vā”ti (pāci. 838) vacanato duṭṭhullavācāpi pācittiyavatthukanti katvā tāsaṃ aññathā aniyatakaṇḍassa avattabbatāpattitopi na vuttanti tesaṃ adhippāyo.

Furthermore, in this matter, this is a miscellaneous point. If it were to be asked: 'Is this Aniyata section without purpose because it is not new?' No, because its purpose is to clarify the characteristics of the procedure for imposing and not imposing offenses, which are distinguished as grave and light. For here, by such passages as, 'If she were to say thus: "Venerable sir, I saw you sitting and engaging in sexual intercourse with a woman," and he confesses it, he should be dealt with according to the offense... he should be dealt with for sitting,' the characteristic of the procedure for imposing both a grave and a light offense is shown; and by the words 'he is not to be dealt with,' the characteristic of the procedure for not imposing is also shown. If it is said, 'Since it clarifies the characteristics, should it be stated at the beginning or at the end?' No, because it is impossible. How so? It is not possible at the beginning, because the training rules whose characteristics these are have not yet been shown. Nor at the end, because it is mixed with grave offenses. Therefore, it is proper that it should be stated in the middle, between grave and light offenses, as it is mixed with both. The light offense shown there also has a grave offense as its origin. Hence, it is said, “by way of the enjoyment of seclusion, which is reckoned as a defilement connected with sexual intercourse,” and so on. Therefore, some say it is stated immediately after the grave offenses. If this is so, then the first training rule alone would be sufficient, since the clarification of the characteristic is accomplished by that much. What is the purpose of the second? No, its purpose is to prevent the wrong assumption arising from the condition of the restriction of place. For from the restriction of place, “on a concealed seat, suitable for intimacy,” a wrong assumption arises that this characteristic is not construed in a place contrary to that. To prevent that, the second training rule is also meaningful—this is the intention. Why? Due to the distinction of place, the clarification of the distinction of seclusion, and the clarification of the distinction of the enjoyment of sitting in seclusion. And in the absence of the restriction of place, a distinction in the enjoyment of secluded sitting arises. There would also be the knowing of the difference between the two training rules on secluded sitting, and likewise due to the clarification of the distinction of bodily contact. For even in an unconcealed location unsuitable for intimacy, or even in a concealed one, bodily contact can be obtained by grasping the hair, etc., of a sitting woman, which has come out through openings such as windows or door-holes. Such methods and others should be understood in detail. Some say, “Because the method is given in the Bhikkhu Pātimokkha, this section is to be understood as omitted in the Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha.” Others say it is because the occasion for it did not arise there. That is incorrect because it clarifies the state of having many meanings. For in all eras of the Buddhas, there are five recitations for bhikkhus and four for bhikkhunīs. Some say that because the formulation of the Pātimokkha recitation is not shared, the Saṅghādisesa and Pācittiya offenses specified there are not common. For those bhikkhunīs, a specific kind of bodily contact, by way of the Ubbhajāṇumaṇḍalika and Aṭṭhavatthuka training rules, is a matter for a pārājika offense. And by the statement, “she might consent to the grasping of her hand, or she might bring her body near for that purpose,” consenting is also a matter for a pārājika offense. By the statement, “or she might stand,” standing is also a matter for a pārājika offense. By the statement, “or she might go to an appointed place,” going is also a matter for a pārājika offense. By the statement, “or she might follow him into a hidden place,” entering a hidden place is also a matter for a pārājika offense. Likewise, by the statement, “in the dark of night, without a lamp, in a concealed place, a bhikkhunī alone with a man might stand or converse,” even coarse speech is a matter for a pācittiya offense. Therefore, their intention is that the Aniyata section is not stated for them because its offenses are covered for them in other ways, and thus it is something that need not be stated.

Pakiṇṇakavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Miscellaneous is concluded.

Aniyatakaṇḍaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Section on the Indefinite is concluded.

4. Nissaggiyakaṇḍo

4. 4. The Nissaggiya Chapter

1. Cīvaravaggo

1. 1. The Chapter on Robes

1. Paṭhamakathinasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

1. 1. Commentary on the First Training Rule concerning the Kaṭhina

459. Samitāvināti [M 0.0214][V 0.0191] samitā’nena kilesāti samitāvī, tena samitāvinā. “Tīṇi cīvarānī”ti vattabbe “ticīvara”nti vuttaṃ. Saṅkhyāpubbo digunekavacananti ettha lakkhaṇaṃ veditabbaṃ. Taṃ pana adhiṭṭhitassapi anadhiṭṭhitassapi nāmaṃ “ekarattampi ce bhikkhu ticīvarena vippavaseyyā”tiādīsu ticīvarādhiṭṭhānena adhiṭṭhitassa nāmaṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ticīvaraṃ adhiṭṭhātu”nti (mahāva. 358) ettha anadhiṭṭhitassa nāmaṃ, idha tadubhayampi sambhavati. “Bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ ticīvaraṃ anuññātaṃ hotī”ti ettha adhiṭṭhitameva. “Aññeneva ticīvarena gāmaṃ pavisantī”ti ettha anadhiṭṭhitameva. Ekasmiṃyeva hi cīvare ticīvarādhiṭṭhānaṃ ruhati, na itarasmiṃ pattādhiṭṭhānaṃ viya, tasmā itaraṃ atirekaṭṭhāne tiṭṭhati. Tena vuttaṃ “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū atirekacīvaraṃ dhāressantī”tiādi.

459. Regarding `samitāvinā`: one is a `samitāvī` (one who has quelled) because 'the defilements have been quelled by this Blessed One'. `Tena samitāvinā` means 'by that one who has quelled'. When it should be said ‘tīṇi cīvarāni’ (three robes), it is said ‘ticīvaraṃ’. Here, the grammatical characteristic should be understood: a `digu` compound with a numerical prefix is in the singular. That name, however, applies both to what is determined and what is not determined. In passages such as “if a bhikkhu should be separated from his three robes even for a single night,” it is the name for that which is determined by the determination of the three robes. In “I allow, bhikkhus, to determine the three robes,” it is the name for that which is not determined. Here, both are possible. In “the three robes are allowed to the bhikkhus by the Blessed One,” it refers only to what is determined. In “they enter the village with another set of three robes,” it refers only to what is not determined. For the determination of the three robes is valid for only one set of three robes, not for another, just like the determination of a bowl. Therefore, the other stands in the position of an extra. Hence it is said, “How indeed could the group-of-six bhikkhus wear an extra robe?” and so on.

460-1. Paṭhamapaññattiyā panettha ekarattampi atirekacīvaraṃ dhāreyya, nissaggiyaṃ vuttaṃ hoti, tato paraṃ “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, dasāhaparamaṃ atirekacīvaraṃ dhāretuṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha ‘dasāhaparamaṃ atirekacīvaraṃ dhāretabbaṃ, taṃ atikkāmayato nissaggiyaṃ pācittiya’”nti evaṃ bhagavā paripuṇṇaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññāpesi. Atha pacchimabodhiyaṃ ajātasattukāle kathinaṃ anuññātaṃ, tato paṭṭhāya bhikkhū idaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ “niṭṭhitacīvarasmiṃ bhikkhunā ubbhatasmiṃ kathine dasāha…pe… pācittiya”nti uddisanti, esa nayo dutiyatatiyakathinesupi. Tathāpi kaṅkhāvitaraṇiyaṃ (kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. kathinasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā) “dasāhaparamanti [V 0.0192] ayamettha anupaññattī”ti ettakaṃyeva vuttaṃ, tasmā “niṭṭhitacīvarasmiṃ bhikkhunā ubbhatasmiṃ kathine”ti vacanaṃ na paññatti, na ca anupaññattīti siddhaṃ. Na hi paññattivatthusmiṃ, anupaññattivatthumhi vā kathinādhikāro dissatīti yathāvuttanayova sāroti niṭṭhamettha gantabbaṃ. Athāpi siyā “kathinassuppattikālato paṭṭhāya bhagavato vacanaṃ anupaññattibhāvena vutta”nti. Yadi evaṃ dve anupaññattiyo siyuṃ, tato parivāre (pari. 24) “ekā [M 0.0215] anupaññattī”tivacanavirodho. Apica yathāvuttanayadīpanatthaṃ idha taṃ vacanaṃ paṭhamapaññattikāle avatvā pacchā vuttaṃ. Ettha sādhitattā dutiyatatiyesu pacchā vuttapaṭhamapaññattīsu evaṃ vuttaṃ. Aññathā tatthapi taṃ vacanaṃ pacchā vattabbaṃ siyā. Anugaṇṭhipade pana “pacchā vuttabhāvaṃ sandhāya niṭṭhitacīvarasmintiādīsu anupaññattī”ti vuttaṃ. Sekkhaputhujjanānaṃ pemaṃ, arahantānaṃ gāravo. Dasamaṃ vā navamaṃ vāti ettha bhummatthe upayogavacanaṃ.

460-1. In the first promulgation, if one were to keep an extra robe even for a single night, it is said to be forfeitable. Thereafter, the Blessed One laid down the training rule in full thus: “I allow, bhikkhus, to keep an extra robe for a maximum of ten days. And thus, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule: ‘An extra robe may be kept for a maximum of ten days. For one who exceeds that, it is forfeitable and an offense of expiation.’” Then, at Pacchimabodhi, during the time of King Ajātasattu, the Kaṭhina was allowed. From then on, bhikkhus recite this training rule as: “When a bhikkhu has finished making his robe and the Kaṭhina has been lifted, for a maximum of ten days… an offense of expiation.” This is the method for the second and third Kaṭhina rules as well. Nevertheless, in the Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī, only this much is stated: “Here, ‘for a maximum of ten days’ is a subsequent promulgation.” Therefore, it is established that the statement “When a bhikkhu has finished making his robe and the Kaṭhina has been lifted” is neither an original promulgation nor a subsequent promulgation. For the matter of the Kaṭhina is not seen in the subject-matter of the original promulgation or in the subject-matter of the subsequent promulgation. Thus, it should be concluded here that the method as stated is the essence. Alternatively, there might be this view: “From the time of the origin of the Kaṭhina, the Blessed One’s statement was made as a subsequent promulgation.” If so, there would be two subsequent promulgations, which would contradict the statement in the Parivāra: “There is one subsequent promulgation.” Moreover, to clarify the method as stated, that statement was not made here at the time of the first promulgation but was stated later. Because it has been established here, it is stated thus in the second and third rules, which are original promulgations stated later. Otherwise, that statement would have to be stated later there as well. However, in the Anugaṇṭhipada, it is said: “With reference to its having been stated later, the phrase beginning with niṭṭhitacīvarasmiṃ is a subsequent promulgation.” The affection of trainees and worldlings is called ‘cherishing’; the reverence of Arahants is called ‘cherishing’. Here, in the phrase ‘the tenth or the ninth,’ the accusative case is used in the sense of the locative.

462-3. Niṭṭhitacīvarasminti idaṃ kevalaṃ cīvarapalibodhābhāvamattadīpanatthaṃ vuttaṃ, tasmā “naṭṭhaṃ vā vinaṭṭhaṃ vā daḍḍhaṃ vā cīvarāsā vā upacchinnā”ti vuttaṃ. Yadi dasāhaparamaṃ dhāretabbacīvaradassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ siyā, naṭṭhādikaṃ so dhāreyya. Dhāraṇañcettha ṭhapanaṃ, paribhogo vā. Taṃ dvayaṃ katepi yujjati, akatepi yujjati, tasmā “kataṃ vā hotī”tipi na vattabbaṃ. Na hi katameva atikkāmayato nissaggiyanti, tasmā yaṃ cīvaraṃ upādāya “niṭṭhitacīvarasmi”nti vuttaṃ. Tampi ubbhatasmiṃ kathine dasāhaparamaṃ kālaṃ dhāretabbanti attho na gahetabbo. Tañhi cīvaraṃ santañce, ubbhatasmiṃ kathine ekadivasampi parihāraṃ na labbhati. Apica “cīvaraṃ nāma vikappanupagaṃ pacchima”nti vuttaṃ. Tattha ca kataṃ nāma hoti, tasmāpi na taṃ sandhāya dhāretabbanti vuttanti veditabbaṃ asambhavato.

462-3. The phrase “the robe is finished” is said merely for the purpose of clarifying the absence of any impediment concerning the robe. Therefore, it is said, “it is lost, or destroyed, or burnt, or the hope for a robe is cut off.” If it were said for the purpose of showing the robe that should be kept for a maximum of ten days, one could keep what is lost, etc. Here, “keeping” refers to storing or using. Both are applicable to a robe that is made and also to one that is not made; therefore, it should not be said, “or it is made.” For it is not that only a made robe becomes subject to forfeiture for one who exceeds the time limit. Therefore, the meaning that the robe, with reference to which “the robe is finished” is said, should also be kept for a maximum of ten days when the Kaṭhina is lifted, should not be understood. For if that robe exists, when the Kaṭhina is lifted, not even a single day’s allowance is obtained. Moreover, it is said, “A robe, namely the last one, is one suitable for determination.” And in that case, it is called ‘made.’ Therefore also, it should be understood that it is not said with reference to that robe that ‘it should be kept,’ because of the impossibility.

Anugaṇṭhipade panetaṃ vuttaṃ “tattha siyā – tassa bhikkhuno cīvaraṃ naṭṭhādīsu aññataraṃ yadi bhaveyya, katamaṃ cīvaraṃ dasāhaparamaṃ dhāreyya. Yasmā dhāretabbacīvaraṃ natthi, tasmā atthuddhāravasena karaṇapalibodhadassanatthaṃ ‘naṭṭhaṃ vā’tiādipadāni vuttāni. Ayaṃ panattho ‘naṭṭhaṃ vā’tiādinā nayena vuttacīvarānaṃ aññatarasmiṃ cīvare asati gahetabbo, sati taṃ dasāhaparamaṃ atikkāmayato nissaggiyaṃ. Esa nayo sabbattha. ‘Kataṃ vā hotī’ti vuttacīvaramevādhippetaṃ. Kasmā pana katacīvaraṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetanti na vuttanti ce? Pākaṭattā. Kathaṃ? Naṭṭhavinaṭṭhacīvarādīnaṃ dhāraṇassa abhāvato katacīvarameva idhādhippetanti pākaṭaṃ. Yathā kiṃ? Yathā paṭhamāniyate methunakāyasaṃsaggarahonisajjānamevāgatattā sotassa raho atthuddhāravasena [V 0.0193] vuttoti pākaṭo, tasmā ‘cakkhussa raho itarasmiṃ atthe adhippeto’ti na vutto. Evaṃsampadamidanti veditabbaṃ. ‘Kataṃ vā hotī’ti idaṃ na vattabbaṃ, kasmā? Akataṃ atikkāmayatopi nissaggiyattā, kiñcāpi nissaggiyaṃ hoti[M 0.0216], idha pana ticīvarādhiṭṭhānamadhippetaṃ. Tasmiṃ ticīvarādhiṭṭhāne akataṃ, arajitaṃ, akappiyakatañca ‘imaṃ saṅghāṭiṃ adhiṭṭhāmī’tiādinā nayena adhiṭṭhātuṃ na vaṭṭati, tadatthadīpanatthaṃ ‘kataṃ vā hotī’ti vuttaṃ. Itarathā ‘niṭṭhitacīvarasmiṃ paṭiladdhe’ti vadeyya, evaṃ sante ticīvaraṃ dasāhaṃ atikkāmayato nissaggiyanti kathaṃ paññāyatīti ce? Vacanappamāṇato. ‘Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ticīvaraṃ adhiṭṭhātuṃ na vikappetu’nti vuttattā idhāpi ‘atirekacīvaraṃ nāma anadhiṭṭhita’nti ettakameva vattabbaṃ siyā. Yasmā ‘kataṃ vā hotī’ti vacanena idhādhippetacīvarena saddhiṃ sesampi dasāhaparamato uttari dhāretuṃ na labbhatīti anujānanto ‘atirekacīvaraṃ nāma anadhiṭṭhitaṃ avikappita’nti āha. Tattha siyā – yathā ‘avikappita’nti atthuddhāravasena vuttaṃ, tathā ‘vikappanupagaṃ pacchima’ntipi. Kasmā? Yasmā ticīvarameva dasāhaparamaṃ dhāretabbaṃ ‘niṭṭhitacīvarasmi’ntiādianupaññattivasena. Itarathā ekāhātikkamepi nissaggiyaṃ hoti ‘yo pana, bhikkhu, atirekacīvaraṃ dhāreyya, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiya’nti vacanato. Na ticīvarato aññampi cīvaraṃ dasāhaparamaṃ dhāretabbaṃ, tato paraṃ nissaggiyaṃ ‘antodasāha’nti vuttattā.
