Yathāha ‘anāpatti antodasāhaṃ adhiṭṭheti, vikappetī’ti, itarathā ‘antodasāhaṃ adhiṭṭhetī’ti vacanamattameva bhaveyya, tasmā aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttanayeneva attho gahetabbo. Idaṃ sabbaṃ apare vadantī”ti. Ettha antokathine uppannacīvaraṃ katameva santañce, dasāhaparamaṃ dhāretabbanti idañcimassa sādhanatthaṃ vuttavacanañca parato idheva vuttavicāraṇāya yathāvuttayuttiyā ca virujjhatīti na gahetabbaṃ.

Moreover, in the Anugaṇṭhipada it is said: “Herein, there might be this objection: If a robe of that bhikkhu were to be one among those that are lost and so forth, which robe should he keep for a maximum of ten days? Because there is no robe to be kept, the words ‘lost or’ and so forth are stated for the purpose of showing the impediment to making (a robe) by way of extracting the meaning. This meaning, however, should be understood thus: when a robe is not in one of the states mentioned in the manner of ‘lost or’ and so forth, but is present, for the bhikkhu who lets it exceed the maximum of ten days, it becomes an item to be relinquished. This is the method in all cases. In the phrase ‘or if it is made,’ only the aforementioned robe is intended. If one should ask, ‘But why is it not stated that a made robe is intended in this context?’ Because it is obvious. How is it obvious? Because of the impossibility of wearing lost, destroyed robes, and so forth, it is obvious that only a made robe is intended here. Like what? Just as in the first Aniyata rule, because only sexual intercourse, bodily contact, and sitting in a secluded place are mentioned, it is obvious that ‘seclusion of the ear’ is stated by way of extracting the meaning; therefore, it is not stated that ‘seclusion of the eye’ is intended in another sense. This should be understood as a comparable case. This phrase ‘or if it is made’ should not be stated. Why? Because even for one who lets an unmade robe exceed the time limit, it becomes an item to be relinquished. Although it does become an item to be relinquished, here the determination of the three robes is intended. In that determination of the three robes, it is not allowable to determine an unmade, undyed, and improperly made robe in the manner of ‘I determine this outer robe,’ and so forth. To clarify that meaning, ‘or if it is made’ is stated. Otherwise, He would have said, ‘when a completed robe is obtained.’ If it were so, how would it be known that for a bhikkhu who lets the three robes exceed ten days, they become items to be relinquished? It is known from the authority of the text. Since it is said, ‘I allow, O bhikkhus, the determination of the three robes, not their assignment to others,’ here too, it would only be necessary to say, ‘an extra robe is that which is undetermined.’ Because, by the phrase ‘or if it is made,’ while allowing that along with the robe intended here, the remaining robes also may not be kept beyond the maximum of ten days, He said, ‘An extra robe is that which is undetermined and unassigned.’ Herein, there might be this objection: Just as ‘unassigned’ is stated by way of extracting the meaning, so too should ‘liable to be assigned later’ also be stated by way of extracting the meaning. Why was it not stated? Because it is laid down by way of a supplementary regulation, such as ‘when the robe is completed,’ that only the three robes are to be kept for a maximum of ten days. Otherwise, it would become an item to be relinquished even by exceeding one day, according to the text: ‘Whatever bhikkhu should keep an extra robe, it is to be relinquished and entails a pācittiya offense.’ Another robe, apart from the three robes, may also be kept for a maximum of ten days; beyond that, it is to be relinquished, because it is said, ‘within ten days.’ As He said: ‘There is no offense if one determines or assigns it within ten days.’ Otherwise, there would only be the mere statement, ‘one determines within ten days.’ Therefore, the meaning should be understood only according to the method stated in the commentary. All this, others say.” Herein, the view that ‘if a robe that has arisen within the Kathina period is already made, it may be kept for a maximum of ten days,’ and the statement cited to establish this, are contradicted by the investigation stated later in this very text and by the aforementioned reasoning; therefore, it should not be accepted.

Idheva vuttavicāraṇā nāma – “sve kathinuddhāro bhavissatī”ti ajja uppannacīvaraṃ tadaheva anadhiṭṭhahantassa aruṇuggamane nissaggiyaṃ. Kasmā? “Niṭṭhitacīvarasmi”ntiādinā sikkhāpadassa vuttattā. Antokathine atirekadasāhampi parihāraṃ labhati, kathinato uddhaṃ ekadivasampi na labhati. Yathā kiṃ? Yathā atthatakathino saṅgho atthatadivasato paṭṭhāya yāva ubbhārā ekadivasāvasesepi kathinubbhāre ānisaṃsaṃ labhati, punadivase na labhati. Sace satisammosā bhājanīyacīvaraṃ na bhājitaṃ, punadivase anatthatakathinānampi sādhāraṇaṃ hoti. Divasā ce sāvasesā, atthatakathinasseva saṅghassa pāpuṇāti, evameva atthatadivasato paṭṭhāya yāva ubbhārā anadhiṭṭhitaṃ avikappitaṃ vaṭṭati anuññātadivasabbhantarattā. Kathinadivaso [M 0.0217] gaṇanupago hoti, ubbhatadivasato paṭṭhāya dasāhaparamaṃ kālaṃ uppannacīvaraṃ parihāraṃ labhati, tato [V 0.0194] paraṃ na labhati. Kasmā? “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, dasāhaparamaṃ atirekacīvaraṃ dhāretu”nti vacanato. Antokathinepi ekādase aruṇuggamane nissaggiyappasaṅgaṃ “niṭṭhitacīvarasmiṃ ubbhatasmiṃ kathine”ti ayaṃ anupaññatti vāretvā ṭhitā, na ca te divase adivase akāsīti. Tathā tatiyakathine ca vicāritaṃ “niṭṭhitacīvarasmiṃ bhikkhunā ubbhatasmiṃ kathine bhikkhuno paneva akālacīvaraṃ uppajjeyyā’ti vadantena bhagavatā yaṃ mayā heṭṭhā paṭhamasikkhāpade ‘dasāhaparamaṃ atirekacīvaraṃ dhāretabba’nti anuññātaṃ, tampi kathinamāsato bahi uppannameva, na antoti dīpitaṃ hotī”ti ca, “‘kālepi ādissa dinnaṃ etaṃ akālacīvara’nti (pārā. 500) vacanato kathinubbhārato uddhaṃ dasāhaparihāraṃ na labhatīti dīpitaṃ hoti, tehi saddhiṃ puna kathinubbhārato uddhaṃ pañca divasāni labhatīti pasaṅgopi ‘niṭṭhitacīvara…pe… khippameva kāretabba’nti akālacīvarassa uppattikālaṃ niyametvā vuttattā vārito hoti. Tadubhayena kathinabbhantare uppannacīvaraṃ kathinubbhārato uddhaṃ ekadivasampi parihāraṃ na labhatīti siddhaṃ hotī”ti ca. Tasmā duvidhampetaṃ vicāraṇaṃ sandhāya amhehi “idheva vuttavicāraṇāya yathāvuttayuttiyā ca virujjhatīti na gahetabba”nti vuttanti veditabbaṃ.

Here, what is called the stated investigation is as follows: If, thinking, ‘Tomorrow the withdrawal of the Kathina will occur,’ a robe arises today, and one does not determine it on that very day, it becomes subject to relinquishment at the rising of the dawn. Why? Because the training rule is stated by way of ‘When the robe-work is finished,’ and so forth. Within the Kathina period, one obtains a concession even beyond ten days, but after the Kathina, one does not obtain it even for a single day. Like what? Just as a Sangha that has spread the Kathina obtains the benefits from the day it was spread until its withdrawal, even if only one day remains until the Kathina withdrawal, but does not obtain them on the following day. If, due to a lapse of memory, a robe meant for distribution is not distributed, on the next day it becomes common property even for those who have not spread the Kathina. If days remain, it belongs only to the Sangha that has spread the Kathina. In the same way, from the day it was spread until its withdrawal, an undetermined and unshared robe is allowable because it is within the permitted days. The Kathina day is included in the count. From the day of withdrawal onward, a robe that has arisen obtains a concession for a period of at most ten days, but not beyond that. Why? Because of the statement: ‘I allow, O bhikkhus, to keep an extra robe for at most ten days.’ Even within the Kathina period, the contingency of an offense requiring relinquishment at the rising of the dawn on the eleventh day is prevented by this supplementary regulation, ‘When the robe-work is finished, when the Kathina is withdrawn’; and it did not render those days invalid. Likewise, in the third Kathina section it is investigated: By saying, ‘When the robe-work is finished, when the Kathina is withdrawn by a bhikkhu, if an out-of-season robe should arise for that bhikkhu,’ the Blessed One has shown that what was allowed by me below in the first training rule—‘An extra robe may be kept for at most ten days’—that too applies only to a robe that has arisen outside the Kathina month, not within. And also, it is shown that because of the statement, ‘Even if given designated for the season, this is an out-of-season robe,’ one does not obtain the ten-day concession after the withdrawal of the Kathina. The implication that one again obtains five days after the withdrawal of the Kathina, along with those, is also prevented because it was stated, having limited the time of arising for an out-of-season robe, ‘When the robe-work is finished… it should be made quickly.’ By both of these reasons, it is established that a robe that has arisen within the Kathina period does not obtain the concession even for a single day after the withdrawal of the Kathina. Therefore, it should be understood that it was said by us, with reference to both these kinds of investigation, that ‘It is not to be accepted because it contradicts the investigation stated herein and the reasoning stated as above.’

Etthāha – “niṭṭhitacīvarasmiṃ ubbhatasmiṃ kathine”ti idaṃ bhummaṃ kiṃ cīvarassa uppatti niyameti, udāhu dhāraṇaṃ, udāhu ubhayanti, kiñcettha, yadi uppattiṃ niyameti, pacchimakattikamāse eva ubbhatasmiṃ kathine uppannacīvaraṃ tato paṭṭhāya dasāhaṃ dhāretabbaṃ aniṭṭhitepi tasmiṃ māseti āpajjati. Atha dhāraṇaṃ niyameti, antokathine uppannacīvaraṃ ubbhatepi dasāhaparamaṃ dhāretabbanti āpajjati. Atha ubhayaṃ niyameti, tatiyakathine viya visesetvā vattabbanti? Vuccate – kāmaṃ ubhayaṃ niyameti, na pana visesane payojanaṃ atthi. Yaṃ antokathine uppannacīvaraṃ sandhāya “niṭṭhitacīvarasmi”nti vuttaṃ, na taṃ sandhāya “dhāretabba”nti vuttaṃ, sādhitañhetaṃ. “Kataṃ vā hotī”tiādivacanato tadatthasiddhi, tena puna visesane payojanaṃ natthi, na hi katameva nissaggiyaṃ karoti, na ca naṭṭhādikaṃ dhāretuṃ sakkāti. Yena vā adhippāyena bhagavatā idaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ, so [M 0.0218] adhippāyo tatiyakathine pakāsitoti veditabbo. Kasmā tattha pakāsitoti ce? Visesavidhānadassanādhippāyato. Visesavidhānañhi “no cassa pāripūrī”tiādi. Tatthāpi “cīvaraṃ uppajjeyyā”ti avatvā “akālacīvaraṃ uppajjeyyā”ti visesanena ubbhatepi kathine kālacīvaraṃ atthīti dīpeti. Kiñcetaṃ? Pacchimakattikamāse uppannacīvaraṃ, teneva tattha “anatthate kathine ekādasamāse uppanna”nti vuttaṃ, tasmā uppattiniyame vuttadosābhāvasiddhi. Yañca [V 0.0195] tattha “kālepi ādissa dinnaṃ etaṃ akālacīvaraṃ nāmā”ti vuttaṃ, tassa dve atthavikappā. Ādesavasena “akālacīvara”nti laddhasaṅkhyampi kāle uppannattā kālaparihāraṃ labhati, pagevānādesanti ayaṃ paṭhamo vikappo uppattiniyame vuttadosābhāvameva upatthambheti. Tathā ādesavasena akālacīvarasaṅkhyaṃ gataṃ cīvarakāle uppannattā cīvarakālato paraṃ dasāhaparihāraṃ na labhati, pagevānādesanti ayaṃ dutiyo dhāraṇaniyame vuttadosābhāvameva upatthambheti. Yadi evaṃ ādesavasena akālacīvarassa akālacīvaratā kimatthikāti ce? Saṅghuddesikassa tassa atthatakathinassapi bhikkhusaṅghassa sādhāraṇabhāvatthikāti veditabbā.

Here it is asked: “When the robe-work is finished, when the kaṭhina is withdrawn”—does this locative phrase determine the arising of the robe, or its keeping, or both? And what is the case here? If it determines the arising, then when the kaṭhina has been withdrawn in the last month of Kattika, it would follow that a robe that has arisen must be kept for ten days from then onwards, even if that month has not ended. If it determines the keeping, then it would follow that a robe that has arisen within the kaṭhina period must be kept for at most ten days even when the kaṭhina has been withdrawn. If it determines both, then should it be specified with a distinction, as in the case of the third kaṭhina? It is said: It may well determine both, but there is no purpose in making a distinction. The phrase “when the robe-work is finished” is stated with reference to a robe that has arisen within the kaṭhina period; the phrase “it should be kept” is not stated with reference to that—and this has been established. The meaning is established by the statement “or it is made,” and so forth; therefore, there is no purpose in a further distinction. For it does not make a robe that is merely made subject to relinquishment, nor is it possible to keep a lost or damaged robe. Alternatively, the intention with which the Blessed One laid down this training rule should be understood as having been clarified in the case of the third kaṭhina. If it is asked, 'Why is it clarified there?' Because of the intention to show a special regulation. The special regulation is “if there is no completion for him,” and so forth. There, too, by not saying “a robe may arise” but using the qualifier “an out-of-season robe may arise,” it indicates that even when the kaṭhina is withdrawn, a seasonal robe exists. What is this? A robe that has arisen in the last month of Kattika. For that very reason, it is said there: “arisen in the eleven months when the kaṭhina is not spread.” Therefore, the absence of the stated flaw is established when the arising is the determining factor. And as for the statement made there: “Even if given by designation in the season, this is called an out-of-season robe,” it has two alternative meanings. First alternative: Even if it has acquired the designation “out-of-season robe” by way of designation, because it has arisen in season, it obtains the seasonal allowance—how much more so if not designated. This first alternative supports the absence of the stated flaw when the arising is the determining factor. Likewise, a robe that has acquired the designation “out-of-season robe” by way of designation, because it has arisen during the robe season, does not obtain the ten-day allowance beyond the robe season—how much more so if not designated. This second alternative supports the absence of the stated flaw when the keeping is the determining factor. If so, what is the purpose of an out-of-season robe's state of being an out-of-season robe by way of designation? It should be understood that its purpose is for that robe, designated for the Sangha, to be common property for the community of monks, including those who have spread the kaṭhina.

Apica puggalassa kathinadivasāpi divasāva. Evaṃ gaṇanupagattā akālacīvarasaṅkhayāpaṭilābhānubhāvena “ubbhatasmiṃ kathine”ti vacanāpekkhassa anissaggiyattā tadanulomattā “kālacīvarassapī”ti evaṃ sabbathā catubbidhaṃ ettha vacananti veditabbaṃ. Apica atthi ekaccena kathinuddhārena ubbhate kathine uppannaṃ ekaccassa bhikkhuno kālacīvaraṃ hoti, ekaccassa akālacīvaraṃ, taṃ sīmātikkantassa, no ubbhāragataṃ. Taṃ dvinnaṃ vasena ubbhate uppannaṃ ṭhapetvā itaresaṃ aññatarena ubbhate uppannanti veditabbaṃ. Tañhi yassa ubbhataṃ, tassa akālacīvaraṃ, itarassa kālacīvaraṃ. Tathā atthi ekaccena kathinuddhārena ubbhate kathine uppannaṃ sabbassapi akālacīvarameva hoti. Taṃ yathāṭhapitaṃ veditabbaṃ. Tathā atthi ubbhatasmiṃ kathine uppannaṃ ṭhapetvā vassānassa pacchime māse uppannaṃ. Tathā atthi ubbhatasmiṃ kathine uppannaṃ akālacīvaraṃ, taṃ hemante, gimhe vā uppannanti veditabbaṃ. Evaṃ puggalakālabhedato bahuvidhattā uppannassa “ubbhatasmiṃ kathine uppanna”nti na vuttanti veditabbaṃ. Anekaṃsikattā imampi atthavikappaṃ [M 0.0219] dassetuṃ “ubbhatasmiṃ kathineti bhikkhuno kathinaṃ ubbhataṃ hotī”ti. Ettāvatā siddhepi “aṭṭhannaṃ mātikānaṃ aññatarāyā”tiādi vuttaṃ. “Dhārayāmī”ti bhikkhunīvibhaṅge āgatoti vattabbo. “Eva”nti vacanena vacanabhedo tattha natthīti vuttaṃ hoti.

Moreover, for an individual, the kaṭhina days are also just days. Thus, it should be understood that the statement here is in every respect fourfold: because it is subject to counting; by the power of obtaining the designation 'out-of-season robe'; because, with reference to the phrase 'when the kaṭhina is removed', it is not subject to forfeiture; and because of its conformity thereto for a seasonal robe as well. Furthermore, there is a case where, when the kaṭhina is removed by a certain type of kaṭhina-removal, a robe that has arisen is a seasonal robe for one monk, and an out-of-season robe for another; this applies to one who has transgressed the boundary, not to one whose kaṭhina has been formally removed. It should be understood that, excluding that which has arisen when the kaṭhina has been removed on account of two grounds, it has arisen when removed by any of the others. For the one for whom it has been removed, it is an out-of-season robe; for the other, it is a seasonal robe. Similarly, there is a case where, when the kaṭhina has been removed by a certain type of kaṭhina-removal, whatever has arisen is an out-of-season robe for everyone. This should be understood as it was established. Likewise, there is that which has arisen in the last month of the rains retreat, apart from that which has arisen when the kaṭhina has been removed. Also, there is an out-of-season robe that has arisen when the kaṭhina has been removed; it should be understood that this has arisen in winter or summer. Thus, it should be understood that because of the manifold nature of what has arisen due to distinctions of person and time, it is not stated as 'what has arisen when the kaṭhina has been removed'. Because of this ambiguity, to show this alternative meaning, it is said: 'When the kaṭhina is removed' means 'the kaṭhina is removed for that monk'. Even though this is established by just that, it is also said: 'by any one of the eight matrices', and so forth. It should be understood that 'Dhārayāmi' comes from the Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga. By the word 'eva', it is said that there is no difference in the wording there.

“Vikappanupagaṃ pacchima”nti idaṃ sabbasaṅgāhikattā vuttaṃ. “Adhiṭṭhānupagaṃ pacchima”nti asabbasaṅgāhikaṃ. Na hi yattakaṃ saṅghāṭi adhiṭṭhānupagaṃ pacchimaṃ, tattakaṃ antaravāsakādi adhiṭṭhānupagaṃ pacchimaṃ hoti adhiṭṭhānassa bahuvidhattā. Na evaṃ vikappanāya bhedo tassā ekavidhattāti veditabbaṃ. “Ekādase aruṇuggamane nissaggiya”nti antimaṃ ṭhapetvā tato purimatarasminti attho veditabbo. Antimaṃ nāma aparakattikāya paṭhamāruṇuggamanaṃ. Tañhi kālattā nissaggiyaṃ na karoti, tenevāha accekacīvarasikkhāpadaṭṭhakathāyaṃ “chaṭṭhito paṭṭhāya pana uppannaṃ anaccekacīvarampi paccuddharitvā ṭhapitacīvarampi etaṃ parihāraṃ labhatiyevā”ti (pārā. aṭṭha. 2.646-9). Imaṃyeva [V 0.0196] nayaṃ sandhāya “accekacīvarassa anatthate kathine ekādasadivasādhiko māso, atthate kathine ekādasadivasādhikā pañca māsā, tato paraṃ ekadivasampi parihāro natthī”ti tatthevāha. Imasmiṃ naye siddhe anaccekacīvaraṃ dvādasāhe na labhatīti siddhameva hoti. Tato “anaccekacīvare anaccekacīvarasaññī, anāpattī”ti (pārā. 650) ettha accekacīvarasadise aññasmiṃ anadhiṭṭhiteti siddhaṃ hoti. Tattha pana “pañca māsā”ti ukkaṭṭhaparicchedavacanaṃ. Vassikasāṭikañca avassikasāṭikabhāvaṃ patvā ekādasamāse parihāraṃ labhatīti veditabbaṃ.

“The last one suitable for vikappanā” is stated because it is all-inclusive. “The last one suitable for determination” is not all-inclusive. For whatever is the last robe suitable for determination as an outer robe, that same is not the last robe suitable for determination as an undergarment and so forth, because determination is of many kinds. It should be understood that there is no such distinction for vikappanā, as it is of a single kind. “On the eleventh dawn, it is to be forfeited”—the meaning should be understood as referring to what is earlier than the very last, excluding the very last. The very last, namely, is the first dawn of the later Kattika month. For that day does not cause forfeiture, because it is the robe season. Therefore, it is said in the commentary on the training rule concerning urgent robes: “From the sixth day onwards, however, even a non-urgent robe that has arisen, and even a robe that has been set aside after being withdrawn, certainly obtains this allowance.” With reference to this very method, it is said in that same place: “For an urgent robe, when the kaṭhina is not spread, the allowance is for a month plus eleven days; when the kaṭhina is spread, it is for five months plus eleven days; beyond that, there is no allowance even for a single day.” When this method is established, it is indeed established that a non-urgent robe is not allowable for twelve days. Therefore, in the statement “Regarding a non-urgent robe, being aware of it as a non-urgent robe, there is no offense,” it is established that this refers to another robe similar to an urgent robe that has not been determined. There, however, “five months” is a statement defining the maximum limit. And it should be understood that a rains-cloth, having reached the state of being a non-rains-cloth, obtains the allowance for eleven months.

Dasāhātikkantaṃ nissaggiyanti ettha āpattivuṭṭhāne “dasāhappaṭicchannaṃ pakkhaatirekapakkhamāsaatirekamāsapaṭicchanna”ntiādivacanabhedo viya, na idha vacanabhedo, tasmā saṃvaccharātikkantampi dasāhātikkantameva nāma, tathā dutiyakathinepi saṃvaccharavippavutthampi rattivippavutthameva. Tatiye saṃvaccharātikkantampi māsātikkantameva nāmāti veditabbaṃ. “Anadhiṭṭhite adhiṭṭhitasaññī nissaggiyaṃ pācittiya”nti idamekassa tikapācittiyassa ādipadadīpanaṃ. Esa nayo avikappitetiādīsupi, tasmā ettha aṭṭhasu tikacchedesu ekaṃ vitthāretvā itaresaṃ ekekamādipadaṃ vitthārehvā dve dve bhagavatāva [M 0.0220] saṅkhittattāti bahūsupi tikacchedesu sambhavantesu eko eva vuccati, “ayaṃ vinayassa dhammatā”ti vadanti. Dukkaṭavāresu pana ekaṃ dukkaṭaṃ vitthāretvā sesāni satta tatheva saṅkhittāni. Tathā antimantimo ekeko anāpattikoṭṭhāsoti veditabbaṃ.

“Passed beyond ten days, it is to be forfeited.” Here, in the matter of rising from an offense, unlike the distinctions in wording such as ‘concealed for ten days, concealed for more than a fortnight, concealed for more than a month,’ there is no distinction in wording here. Therefore, even if it has passed beyond a year, it is still called ‘passed beyond ten days.’ Similarly, in the second kaṭhina training rule, even if one has been separated from it for a year, it is still called ‘separated for a night.’ In the third, even if it has passed beyond a year, it is still called ‘passed beyond a month’—this should be understood. “Perceiving what is not determined as determined, it is a nissaggiya pācittiya offense”—this is the explanation of the first phrase of one of the threefold pācittiya offenses. This same method applies to the cases beginning with ‘not shared’ and so on. Therefore, here, among the eight threefold sections, after elaborating on one, for the others, two phrases each have been condensed by the Blessed One himself. Thus, even though many threefold sections are possible, only one is stated, for they say, “This is the nature of the Vinaya.” In the sections on the dukkaṭa offense, however, one dukkaṭa is elaborated upon, while the remaining seven are similarly condensed. Likewise, each very last section is a case of non-offense—this should be understood.

Anāpatti antodasāhanti ayaṃ saṅkhepattho – taṃ dasāhaparamaṃ dhāretabbaṃ. Taṃ atirekacīvaraṃ yathāsakaṃ adhiṭṭhānaṃ antodasāhaṃ adhiṭṭheti vā vikappeti vā vissajjeti vā attano dhammatāya nassati vā vinassati vā ḍayhati vā añño vā taṃ acchinditvā gaṇhāti vissāsanto vā gaṇhāti pācittiyato anāpatti. Dukkaṭato pana siyā āpatti siyā anāpatti saññābhedena. Antimānaṃ panettha dvinnaṃ padānaṃ vasena anacchinne acchinnasaññī nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ. Avissāsaggāhe vissāsaggāhasaññī nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyantiādikā dve tikapācittiyā, dve ca dukkaṭā saṅkhittāti veditabbā. Ettha hi yadi antodasāhaṃ adhiṭṭheti, dasāhaparamaṃ aruṇaṃ atikkamitvā tassa divasabhāge adhiṭṭhahatīti veditabbaṃ. Ayaṃ tāva pāḷivinicchayo.

“No offense within ten days”—this is the summary meaning: it should be kept for a maximum of ten days. Regarding that extra robe, if within ten days one determines it, places it under shared ownership, or relinquishes it; or if it is lost by its own nature, is destroyed, or is burned; or if another takes it by force or with trust—there is no offense requiring expiation. From the perspective of an offense of wrong-doing, however, there may be an offense or no offense, depending on the distinction in perception. Herein, by means of the last two phrases—‘When it has not been taken away, perceiving it as taken away, it is an offense of relinquishment and expiation,’ and ‘When it is not taken with trust, perceiving it as taken with trust, it is an offense of relinquishment and expiation’—it should be understood that two threefold offenses of expiation and two offenses of wrong-doing are summarized. Herein, should one determine it within ten days, it should be understood that one determines it during the daytime after the dawn of the tenth day at the latest has passed. This, for now, is the ruling of the Pāli text.

Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana ito garukatarānītiādimhi ayaṃ codanāpubbaṅgamo vinicchayo – gaṇṭhipade [V 0.0197] panassa ito nissaṭṭhacīvaradānato garukampi ñattidutiyakammaṃ yathā apalokanena karonti, evamidaṃ ñattiyā kattabbampi pakativacanena vaṭṭatīti. Yadi evaṃ parivāre kammavaggassa aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “ñattikammampi ekaṃ ñattiṃ ṭhapetvāva kātabbaṃ, apalokanakammādivasena na kātabba”nti (pari. aṭṭha. 482) yaṃ vuttaṃ, tena virujjheyya. Tenetaṃ vuccati “tesaṃ etaṃ anuloma”nti, tasmā anulomanayeneva taṃ vuttaṃ. Niyamaṃ pana yathā dvinnaṃ pārisuddhiuposatho vinā ñattiyā hoti, evaṃ dvinnaṃ nissaṭṭhacīvaradānampīti vadāma, tasmā “āyasmato demā”ti vattuṃ vaṭṭati. Kathaṃ panetaṃ ñātabbanti? Tadanulomattāti. Ekadevedaṃ ñattikammaṃ apalokanenāpi kātuṃ vaṭṭatīti sādhananti veditabbanti ācariyo. Anugaṇṭhipade panettha codanaṃ katvā “etaṃ sādhitaṃ. Ñattikammaṃ ekaṃ ñattiṃ ṭhapetvāva kātabba”nti pāḷiyā āgataṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ, idaṃ pana pāḷiyaṃ nāgataṃ, lesato āharitvā vuttanti katvā etaṃ apalokanenāpi vaṭṭatīti.

In the Commentary, however, in the passage beginning ‘more serious than this,’ this decision is preceded by a challenge. But in the Gaṇṭhipada, it is argued that just as a formal act with a motion and one announcement—which is more serious than this giving of a relinquished robe—is performed by an act of informing, so too this act, which should be done by a motion, is permissible by an ordinary statement. If so, it would contradict what is stated in the Commentary on the Kammavagga in the Parivāra: ‘A formal act with a motion should be done only by positing one motion; it should not be done by way of an act of informing, etc.’ (Pari. Aṭṭha. 482). Because of that, it is said, ‘This is in conformity with them,’ and thus it is stated only by way of conformity. As a rule, however, we say that just as the Uposatha of purity for two monks occurs without a motion, so too does the giving of a relinquished robe for two. Therefore, it is permissible to say, ‘We give to the venerable one.’ But how is this to be known? Because of its conformity. The teacher states that it should be known that the proof is this statement: ‘This one formal act with a motion is also permitted to be done by an act of informing.’ In the Anugaṇṭhipada, however, having raised a challenge, it is stated with reference to what has come in the Pāli: ‘This is proven. A formal act with a motion should be done only by positing one motion.’ But this has not come in the Pāli; it is stated having been brought by way of a hint, and for that reason, it is said that this is also permissible by an act of informing.

468. Esa [M 0.0221] nayoti aññesaṃ cīvaresu upacikādīhi khāyitesu mamapi khāyitānītiādi. “Aññena kataṃ…pe… sādhaka”nti vacanato samānajātikaṃ, ekatthajātikañca tatiyakathinaṃ paṭhamasamānamevāti siddhaṃ hoti.

468. ‘This is the method’ means: when the robes of others are eaten by termites and so forth, one thinks, ‘My robes are also eaten,’ and so on. Because of the text, ‘What is done by another… is effective,’ it is thereby established that the third kathina, being of the same kind and of a single purpose, is indeed the same as the first.

469. Ticīvaraṃ adhiṭṭhātunti ettha ticīvaraṃ ticīvarādhiṭṭhānena adhiṭṭhātabbayuttakaṃ, yaṃ vā ticīvarādhiṭṭhānena adhiṭṭhātuṃ avikappetuṃ anujānāmi, tassa adhiṭṭhānakālaparicchedābhāvato sabbakālaṃ icchantassa adhiṭṭhātuṃyeva anujānāmi, taṃ kālaparicchedaṃ katvā vikappetuṃ nānujānāmi. Sati pana paccaye yadā tadā vā paccuddharitvā vikappetuṃ vaṭṭatīti “anāpatti antodasāhaṃ adhiṭṭheti, vikappetī”ti vacanato siddhaṃ hotīti vuttametaṃ. Vassikasāṭikaṃ tato paraṃ vikappetuṃyeva nādhiṭṭhātuṃ. Vatthañhi katapariyositaṃ antocatumāse vassānadivasaṃ ādiṃ katvā antodasāhe adhiṭṭhātuṃ anujānāmi, catumāsato uddhaṃ attano santakaṃ katvā ṭhapitukāmena vikappetuṃ anujānāmīti attho. Sugatacīvarato ūnakanti tiṇṇampi cīvarānaṃ ukkaṭṭhaparicchedo. “Ticīvaraṃ pana parikkhāracoḷaṃ adhiṭṭhātuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti vāde pana sati tathārūpapaccaye vaṭṭati. Yathā sati paccaye vikappetuṃ vaṭṭatīti sādhitametaṃ, pageva aññena adhiṭṭhānena adhiṭṭhātuṃ. “Antodasāhaṃ adhiṭṭheti, vikappetī”ti aniyamato vuttanti saṅghāṭi, uttarāsaṅgo, antaravāsakanti adhiṭṭhitānadhiṭṭhitānaṃ samānameva nāmaṃ. “Ayaṃ saṅghāṭī”tiādīsu (mahāva. 126) hi anadhiṭṭhitā vuttā. “Ticīvarena vippavaseyyā”ti ettha adhiṭṭhitā vuttā. Sāmantavihāre vāti gocaragāmato vihāreti dhammasiritthero. Dūratarepi labbhatevāti [V 0.0198] ācariyo. Anugaṇṭhipadepi “sāmantavihāre vāti desanāsīsamattaṃ, tasmā ṭhapitaṭṭhānaṃ sallakkhetvā dūre ṭhitampi adhiṭṭhātabba”nti vuttaṃ. Sāmantavihāro nāma yattha tadaheva gantvā nivattituṃ sakkā. Rattivippavāsaṃ rakkhantena tato dūre ṭhitaṃ adhiṭṭhātuṃ na vaṭṭati, evaṃ kira mahāaṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttanti. Keci “cīvaravaṃse ṭhapitaṃ añño parivattitvā nāgadante ṭhapeti, taṃ ajānitvā adhiṭṭhahantassapi ruhati cīvarassa sallakkhitattā”ti vadanti. Adhiṭṭhahitvāti parikkhāracoḷādivasena. Mahantataramevātiādi sabbādhiṭṭhānasādhāraṇalakkhaṇaṃ[M 0.0222]. Tattha puna adhiṭṭhātabbamevāti adhiṭṭhitacīvarassa ekadesabhūtattā. Anadhiṭṭhitañce, adhiṭṭhitassa appabhāvena ekadesabhūtaṃ adhiṭṭhitasaṅkhyameva gacchati. Tathā adhiṭṭhitañce, anadhiṭṭhitassa ekadesabhūtaṃ anadhiṭṭhitasaṅkhyaṃ gacchatīti hi lakkhaṇaṃ, na kevalañcettha dutiyapaṭṭameva, tatiyapaṭṭādikampi. Yathāha “anujānāmi…pe… utuddhaṭānaṃ dussānaṃ catugguṇaṃ saṅghāṭiṃ…pe… paṃsukūle yāvadattha”nti (mahāva. 348).

469. “To determine the three robes”: here, the three robes are suitable to be determined by the determination of the three robes; or it is a robe which I allow to be determined, and not made subject to `vikappana`, by means of the determination of the three robes. Since there is no time limit for its determination, I allow one who wishes to determine it at any time; I do not allow making it subject to `vikappana` after setting a time limit. However, when there is a reason, it is allowable to withdraw the determination and make it subject to `vikappana` at any time. This is established by the passage: “There is no offense if one determines it or makes it subject to `vikappana` within ten days.” This has been stated. The rains-bathing cloth, however, should only be made subject to `vikappana` after that period, not determined. For a cloth that has been finished, I allow it to be determined within ten days, starting from the first day of the rains within the four months. But after the four months, for one who wishes to keep it as their own possession, I allow it to be made subject to `vikappana`—this is the meaning. “Less than the Sugata's robe” is the maximum limit for all three robes. However, in the view that “it is allowable to determine the three robes as an accessory cloth,” it is allowable when there is such a suitable reason. Just as it is established that it is allowable to make it subject to `vikappana` when there is a reason, how much more so to determine it with another determination. The statement, “One determines it or makes it subject to `vikappana` within ten days,” is said without restriction. Thus, the names “outer robe,” “upper robe,” and “inner robe” are the very same for those that are determined and those that are not determined. Indeed, in phrases like “This is the outer robe,” an undetermined one is spoken of. In the phrase, “One might be separated from the three robes,” a determined one is spoken of. “Or in a neighboring monastery” means in a monastery near the alms-resort village, according to the Elder Dhammasiri. The Teacher says it is allowable even at a greater distance. In the Anugaṇṭhipada too, it is said: “‘In a neighboring monastery’ is merely the heading of the teaching. Therefore, having mentally marked the place where it is kept, one should determine it even if it is far away.” A neighboring monastery is a place to which one can go and return on the very same day. For one who is guarding against separation at night, it is not allowable to determine a robe that is further than that; so it is said in the Great Commentary. Some say: “If a robe placed on a robe-bamboo is moved by another and placed on an elephant-tusk peg, even for one who determines it without knowing this, the determination is valid because the robe has been mentally marked.” “Having determined it” is by way of an accessory cloth and so forth. “Even larger,” and so on, is a characteristic common to all determinations. Therein, the statement “it must be determined again” is because of it becoming a part of a determined robe. If an undetermined piece of cloth, being a small part of a determined robe, is added, it goes into the category of ‘determined’. Similarly, if a determined piece of cloth, being a part of an undetermined robe, is added, it goes into the category of ‘undetermined’. For this is the characteristic. And here it is not only a second layer, but also a third layer and so on. As it is said: “I allow… a four-fold outer robe of new cloth… as much as is needed for a rag-robe.”

Avasesā bhikkhūti vakkhamānakāle nisinnā bhikkhū. Tasmā vaṭṭatīti yathā “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ticīvaraṃ adhiṭṭhātuṃ na vikappetu”nti vuttaṃ, evaṃ parikkhāracoḷampi vuttaṃ, na tassa ukkaṭṭhaparicchedo vutto, na ca saṅkhyāparicchedo, tasmā tīṇipi cīvarāni paccuddharitvā “imāni cīvarāni parikkhāracoḷāni adhiṭṭhāmī”ti adhiṭṭhahitvā paribhuñjituṃ vaṭṭatīti attho. “Nidhānamukhameta”nti kathaṃ paññāyatīti ce? “Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhūnaṃ paripuṇṇaṃ hoti ticīvaraṃ, attho ca hoti parissāvanehipi thavikāhipī”ti etasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, parikkhāracoḷa”nti (mahāva. 358) anuññātattā. Bhikkhūnañca ekameva parissāvanaṃ, thavikā vā vaṭṭati, na dve vā tīṇi vāti paṭikkhepābhāvato vikappanupagapacchimappamāṇāni, atirekappamāṇāni vā parissāvanādīni parikkhārāni kappantīti siddhaṃ. Yadi evaṃ “yaṃnūnāhaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ cīvare sīmaṃ bandheyyaṃ mariyādaṃ ṭhapeyya”nti (mahāva. 346) vacanavirodhoti ce? Na, anusandhiyā ajānanato, virodhato ca. Kiṃ vuttaṃ hoti? Cīvarakkhandhake (mahāva. 326 ādayo) paṭhamaṃ gahapaticīvaraṃ anuññātaṃ, tato pāvārakosiyakojavakambalādi. Tato “tena kho pana samayena saṅghassa uccāvacāni cīvarāni uppannāni honti. Atha kho bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi ‘kiṃ nu kho bhagavatā cīvaraṃ anuññātaṃ, kiṃ ananuññāta’”nti etasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, cha cīvarāni khoma”ntiādinā (mahāva. 339) kappiyacīvarajāti anuññātā, na pana saṅkhyāpamāṇaṃ. Tato “addasa bhagavā…pe… sambahule bhikkhū cīvarehi ubbhaṇḍite sīsepi cīvarabhisiṃ karitvā khandhepi cīvarabhisiṃ karitvā [V 0.0199] kaṭiyāpi cīvarabhisiṃ karitvā āgacchante, disvāna bhagavato etadahosi…pe… yepi kho te kulaputtā imasmiṃ dhammavinaye sītālukā sītabhīrukā, tepi sakkonti [M 0.0223] ticīvarena yāpetuṃ, yaṃnūnāhaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ cīvare sīmaṃ bandheyyaṃ mariyādaṃ ṭhapeyyaṃ ticīvaraṃ anujāneyya”nti (mahāva. 346) cīvaraṃ anuññātaṃ, tañca kho ekameva. Chabbaggiyā pana micchā gahetvā bahūni parihariṃsu. Tāni nesaṃ atirekaṭṭhāne ṭhitāni honti. Tato “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, dasāhaparamaṃ atirekacīvaraṃ dhāretu”nti (mahāva. 347) anuññātaṃ, tenetaṃ paññāyati. Atirekāni bahūni cīvarāni te parihariṃsu, “tāni dasāhaparamameva dhāretuṃ anujānāmi, na tameveka”nti vadantena yā pubbe ticīvarādhiṭṭhānasaṅkhātā cīvare sīmābaddhā, mariyādā ca ṭhapitā, tāya satipi ticīvarabāhullapariharaṇakkamo dassito divasaparicchedavasena. Tato paraṃ “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, atirekacīvaraṃ vikappetu”nti (mahāva. 347) anujānantena vināpi divasaparicchedena atirekacīvarapariharaṇakkamo dassitoti dvepi tāni nidhānamukhānīti siddhaṃ. Tathā parikkhāracoḷādhiṭṭhānampi siyā, aññathā itaracīvarādhiṭṭhānānujānanavirodho siyā sīmāmariyādaṭṭhapanavirodhato. Ticīvarādhiṭṭhānapaññattiyeva ticīvaramariyādā hoti. Tena vuttaṃ “pāṭekkaṃ nidhānamukhameta”nti. “Paṭhamaṃ ticīvaraṃ ticīvarādhiṭṭhānena adhiṭṭhātabbaṃ, puna pariharituṃ asakkontena paccuddharitvā parikkhāracoḷaṃ adhiṭṭhātabbaṃ, na tveva āditova idaṃ vutta”nti vuttaṃ. “Yathā ticīvaraṃ pariharituṃ asakkontassa gilānassa vippavāsasammuti anuññātā, agilānassapi sāsaṅkasikkhāpade (pārā. 652) tassa antaraghare nikkhepo ca, tatopi sati paccaye chārattavippavāso, tatopi asakkontassa paccuddhāro, paccuddhaṭampi antodasāhe adhiṭṭhātuṃ, asakkontassa vikappanā ca anuññātā. Tatheva dvinnampi sammukhāparammukhāvikappanānaṃ parasantakattā vikappanapaccaye asati ‘parikkhāracoḷa’nti adhiṭṭhahitvā paribhuñjituṃ bhagavatā anuññātaṃ siyā, yato tadadhippāyaññū evaṃ vadantī”ti mahāpaccariyampi vuttaṃ. Pubbetiādi “pāṭekkaṃ nidhānamukha”nti vuttassa payogadassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Abaddhasīmāyaṃ dupparihāranti vikappanādiatthāya upacāraṃ atikkamitvāpi gamanasambhavato.

“The remaining bhikkhus” means the bhikkhus who were seated at the time of speaking. Therefore, it is permissible. Just as it was said, “I allow, bhikkhus, to determine the triple robe, not to share it,” so too was the accessory cloth spoken of. Its maximum limit was not stated, nor was a numerical limit. Therefore, having withdrawn even the three robes, it is permissible to determine, “I determine these robes as accessory cloths,” and then use them; this is the meaning. If it is asked, “How is this known as an opening for storage?” Because in the case where “at that time the bhikkhus’ triple robe was complete, and there was a need for water strainers and bags,” it was allowed, saying, “I allow, bhikkhus, an accessory cloth” (Mahāvagga 358). And because there is no prohibition stating, ‘Only one water strainer or bag is permissible for a bhikkhu, not two or three,’ it is established that requisites such as water strainers, whether of the minimum size for sharing or of an extra size, are allowable. If it is said, “If so, this would contradict the statement, ‘Suppose I were to set a boundary for the bhikkhus’ robes, establish a limit’?” (Mahāvagga 346), the answer is no, due to not knowing the connection and due to the apparent contradiction. What was said? In the Chapter on Robes (Mahāvagga 326 ff.), first, the householder's robe was allowed, then robes of Pāvāra silk, Kosiya silk, Kojavaka felt, blankets, etc. Then, in the case where “at that time, various robes had arisen for the Sangha. Then it occurred to the bhikkhus, ‘What kind of robe has been allowed by the Blessed One, and what has not been allowed?’” the types of allowable robes were permitted by the text beginning, “I allow, bhikkhus, six kinds of robes: linen...” (Mahāvagga 339), but not a numerical limit. Then, “the Blessed One saw... many bhikkhus coming, burdened with robes, having made a bundle of robes on their heads, on their shoulders, and on their waists. Having seen them, it occurred to the Blessed One... ‘Even those clansmen in this Dhamma and Vinaya who are sensitive to cold and fear the cold are able to manage with a triple robe. Suppose I were to set a boundary for the bhikkhus’ robes, establish a limit, and allow the triple robe’” (Mahāvagga 346). Thus the triple robe was allowed, and that was just one set. But the Group-of-six bhikkhus, having misunderstood, used many. Those stood in the category of ‘extra’ for them. Then it was allowed, “I allow, bhikkhus, to keep an extra robe for a maximum of ten days” (Mahāvagga 347); by this it is known. They used many extra robes, and by his saying, “I allow those to be kept for a maximum of ten days, not that one only,” a method for managing an abundance of robes was shown by way of a limitation of days, even while the boundary and limit previously established for robes, known as the determination of the triple robe, existed. After that, by allowing, “I allow, bhikkhus, to share an extra robe” (Mahāvagga 347), a method for managing an extra robe even without a limitation of days was shown. Thus it is established that both of these are openings for storage. Similarly, the determination of an accessory cloth would be possible; otherwise, there would be a contradiction with the allowance for the other determination of robes, due to the contradiction with establishing a boundary and limit. The regulation for the determination of the triple robe itself is the limit for the triple robe. Therefore it was said, “Each is an opening for storage.” It was said: “First, the triple robe should be determined by the determination of the triple robe. Then, by one who is unable to maintain it, having withdrawn it, the accessory cloth should be determined. This was not, however, stated from the very beginning.” It is also said in the Mahāpaccarī: “Just as for a sick person unable to maintain the triple robe, permission to be away from it was allowed; and for one not sick, in the training rule concerning a dangerous situation (Pārājika 652), the placing of it inside a house was also allowed; and further, if there is a reason, being away for six nights; and further, for one unable, withdrawal; and to determine the withdrawn robe within ten days; and for one unable, sharing was also allowed. Just so, since both kinds of sharing—in person and in absence—make it the property of another, when there is no condition for sharing, it may be that it was allowed by the Blessed One to determine it as an ‘accessory cloth’ and use it, since those who know his intention speak thus.” The preceding passage (beginning with `pubbe`, 'formerly') was stated to show the application of the saying, “Each is an opening for storage.” The statement “In an area with an unbound boundary, it is difficult to maintain” is made because, for the purpose of sharing, etc., it is possible to go even beyond the vicinity.

Vassikasāṭikā anatirittappamāṇāti tassā ukkaṭṭhaparicchedassa vuttattā vuttaṃ. Paccattharaṇampi adhiṭṭhātabbamevāti “idaṃ, bhante, amhākaṃ senāsanassa upari attharitabba”ntiādinā dinnaṃ nādhiṭṭhātabbaṃ, “idaṃ tumhāka”nti [M 0.0224] dinnaṃ sayaṃ adhippetaṃva adhiṭṭhātabbanti adhippāyo. “Sakiṃ adhiṭṭhitaṃ adhiṭṭhitameva hoti, na puna paccuddharīyati kālaparicchedābhāvato”ti likhitaṃ. “Ekavacanenapi vaṭṭatīti apare”ti vuttaṃ. Bhesajjanavakammamātāpituādīnaṃ [V 0.0200] atthāyāti ettha “iminā bhesajjaṃ cetāpessāmi, idaṃ mātuyā dassāmī”ti ṭhapentena adhiṭṭhātabbaṃ. “‘Idaṃ bhesajjassa, imaṃ mātuyā’ti vibhajantena adhiṭṭhānakiccaṃ natthīti apare”ti vuttaṃ. “Sakabhāvaṃ mocetvā ṭhapanaṃ sandhāyāhā”ti likhitaṃ.

It is said that the rainy-season robe should not exceed the prescribed measurement, because its maximum limit has been stated. Regarding the statement, 'An underlay is also to be determined': the intention is that what is given with words such as, 'Venerable sir, this is to be spread over our dwelling,' should not be determined. But what is given with the words, 'This is for you,' should be determined by oneself as intended. It is written: 'Once determined, it remains determined and is not to be withdrawn again, as there is no time limit.' It is said: 'Others say, "It is allowable even with a single utterance."' Regarding what is for the purpose of medicine, new work, mother, father, and so on: here, it should be determined by one setting it aside thinking, 'With this, I will have medicine procured,' or, 'I will give this to my mother.' It is said: 'Others say, "For one who specifies, ‘This is for medicine, this is for my mother,’ there is no need for determination."' It is written: 'This was stated with reference to setting something aside after relinquishing one's ownership of it.'

“Puna adhiṭṭhātabbanti ayaṃ saṅgītito paṭṭhāya āgataaṭṭhakathāvādo. Tato paraṃ ācariyānaṃ tattha tattha yuttivicāraṇā”ti vuttaṃ. Pamāṇacīvarassāti pacchimappamāṇassa. Dve cīvarānīti saha uttarāsaṅgena. Esa nayoti pamāṇayuttesu yattha katthacītiādinayova. “Taṃ atikkāmayato chedanaka”nti (pāci. 533) vacanato uttari paṭisiddhaṃ, tato heṭṭhā appaṭisiddhattā vaṭṭati. Tattha siyā – ticīvarassa pacchimappamāṇaṃ visuṃ sutte natthīti, na vattabbaṃ, sikkhākaraṇīyehi siddhattā. Kiṃ vuttaṃ hoti? “‘Parimaṇḍalaṃ nivāsessāmi, pārupissāmi, suppaṭicchanno antaraghare gamissāmī’ti (pāci. 576-579) vacanato yattakena pamāṇena parimaṇḍalatā, suppaṭicchannatā ca aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttakkamena sampajjatī”ti vattabbaṃ. Tesaṃ vasena pacchimappamāṇanti siddhaṃ, tañca kho muṭṭhipañcakādi yathāvuttameva vuccate. Tenevāha lesaṃ ṭhapetvā “visuṃ sutte natthī”ti.

It was said: 'Regarding “It should be determined again,” this is the commentarial tradition that has come down since the Council. Beyond that is the teachers' investigation of what is proper in various instances.' 'Of the standard-sized robe' means of the minimum standard size. 'Two robes' means together with the upper robe. 'This is the method' means it is the method beginning with 'in any standard-sized [robe] whatsoever.' According to the passage, 'For one who exceeds it, there is an offense of cutting,' what is beyond is prohibited; what is below that is permissible, since it is not prohibited. Here, an objection might be raised: 'The minimum standard size for the triple robe is not separately stated in the Sutta.' This should not be said, because it is established by the training rules. What is meant? It should be said that, 'According to the passage, “I will wear the lower robe evenly all around; I will wear the upper robe evenly all around; I will go into inhabited areas well-covered,” by whatever standard size evenness and being well-covered are accomplished according to the method stated in the commentary.' By means of these rules, the term 'minimum standard size' is established. And that, indeed, is said to be five fists and so on, just as has been stated. Therefore, having provided a hint, he said, 'It is not separately in the Sutta.'

Apicettha adhippetaṃ, tathāpi na sametiyevāti attho, tasmā “yadī”tiādisambandho addhā vutto. Yasmā paricchinno sameti ca. Itaresu pana ekaccasmiṃ ācariyavāde neva paricchedo atthi. Ekaccasmiṃ na pubbāparaṃ sametīti sambandho. Adhiṭṭhānaṃ adhiṭṭhānameva, paribhogakāle pana arajitaṃ na vaṭṭati. Idaṃ sabbaṃ ticīvare eva. Imassa pana sikkhāpadassa ayaṃ saṅkhepavinicchayo – anatthate kathine hemantānaṃ paṭhamadivasato paṭṭhāya atthate kathine gimhānaṃ paṭhamadivasato paṭṭhāya uppannacīvaraṃ sandhāya “niṭṭhitacīvarasmi”ntiādi vuttanti.

Moreover, although this is intended here, the meaning is that it still does not quite agree; therefore, the connection beginning with 'if' is certainly stated. Because it is defined, it also agrees. However, in some other doctrines of the teachers, there is no definition at all. In some, the preceding and succeeding parts do not agree—this is the connection. A determination is just a determination, but at the time of use, an undyed robe is not allowable. All this pertains only to the triple robe. For this training rule, however, this is the concise analysis: with reference to a robe that has arisen when the Kathina is not spread, from the first day of the winter months onward, and when the Kathina is spread, from the first day of the summer months onward, the passage beginning with 'when the robe is finished' is stated.

Etthāha – “rajakehi dhovāpetvā setaṃ kārāpentassāpi adhiṭṭhānaṃ adhiṭṭhānamevā”ti vacanato arajitepi adhiṭṭhānaṃ ruhati, tena sūcikammaṃ [M 0.0225] katvā rajitvā kappabinduṃ datvā adhiṭṭhātabbanti niyamo na kātabboti? Vuccate, kātabbova patto viya adhiṭṭhito. Yathā puna setabhāvaṃ, tambabhāvaṃ vā patto adhiṭṭhānaṃ na vijahati, na ca pana tādiso adhiṭṭhānaṃ upagacchati, evametaṃ daṭṭhabbanti. “Yato paṭṭhāya paribhogādayo vaṭṭanti, tato paṭṭhāya antodasāhe adhiṭṭhātabba”nti vadanti.

Here a questioner says: 'According to the statement, “Even for one who has a robe washed by a launderer and made white, the determination is still a determination,” a determination takes effect even on an undyed robe. Therefore, should the rule not be made that it must be determined only after doing the needlework, dyeing it, and applying the marking-spot (kappabindu)?' The reply is: It must indeed be made, just like a determined bowl. Just as a bowl that has become white or reddish does not lose its determination, yet such a bowl is not in a state to be determined anew, so should this be understood. They say: 'From the time that usage and so forth are allowable, from then on it must be determined within ten days.'

Avisesena [V 0.0201] vuttavacananti adhiṭṭhātabbaṃ adhiṭṭheti, vikappetabbaṃ vikappetīti evaṃ savisesaṃ katvā avacanaṃ “na vikappetu”nti (mahāva. 358) iminā viruddhaṃ viya dissati. Idāni idaṃ adhiṭṭhānavikappananayapaṭibaddhaṃ khandhakaṃ, parivārañca missetvā pakiṇṇakaṃ vuccati – khandhake tāva “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ticīvaraṃ adhiṭṭhātuṃ na vikappetuṃ, vassikasāṭikaṃ vassānaṃ cātumāsaṃ adhiṭṭhātuṃ, tato paraṃ vikappetu”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Parivāre “na nava cīvarāni adhiṭṭhātabbāni, na nava cīvarāni vikappetabbānī”ti (pari. 329), “dasake dasa, ekādasake ekādasa cīvarāni adhiṭṭhātabbāni, na vikappetabbānī”ti (pari. 331) ca anekakkhattuṃ vacanena suṭṭhu daḷhaṃ katvā “sabbāni cīvarāni adhiṭṭhātabbāni, na vikappetabbānī”ti vuttaṃ, tasmā ubhopi te viruddhā viya dissanti, khandhake eva ca “vassikasāṭikaṃ vassānaṃ cātumāsaṃ adhiṭṭhātuṃ tato paraṃ vikappetu”nti (mahāva. 358) vuttaṃ. Tadaṭṭhakathāyaṃ “vassikasāṭikā anatirittappamāṇā nāmaṃ gahetvā vuttanayeneva cattāro vassike māse adhiṭṭhātabbā, tato paraṃ paccuddharitvā vikappetabbā”ti vuttaṃ. Idañca viruddhaṃ viya dissati aññamaññaṃ hemante paccuddhārasambhavato, vassāne vikappanāsambhavato ca. Tathā idha “anāpatti antodasāhaṃ adhiṭṭheti vikappetī”ti vacanappamāṇato sabbattha vikappanāya appaṭisiddhabhāvo veditabboti (pārā. aṭṭha. 2.469) aṭṭhakathāvacanaṃ parivāravacanena viruddhaṃ viya dissati, na hi viruddhaṃ tathāgatā bhāsanti, tasmā aṭṭhakathānayovettha paṭisaraṇaṃ, yena sabbampi taṃ ekarasaṃ hoti. Parivāraṭṭhakathāyañca vuttaṃ “na vikappetabbānīti adhiṭṭhitakālato paṭṭhāya na vikappetabbānī”ti (pari. aṭṭha. 329). Ticīvarāni adhiṭṭhitakālato paṭṭhāya, vassikasāṭikādīni ca attano attano adhiṭṭhānakhette na akāmā vikappetabbānīti attho, avasesapāḷi, attho ca idha aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vutto, tasmā sabbampetaṃ ekarasanti.

The statement spoken without distinction means: what is to be determined, one determines; what is to be shared, one shares. Thus, the statement made with a distinction, namely, 'one should not share it,' appears contradictory. Now, this miscellaneous teaching, which is connected with the method of determination and sharing, is presented by combining the Khandhaka and the Parivāra. Firstly, in the Khandhaka, it is said: 'I allow, O bhikkhus, the determination of the three robes, not their sharing; the determination of the rains-cloth for the four months of the rains, and after that, its sharing,' and so on. In the Parivāra, it is said: 'Nine robes are not to be determined, nine robes are not to be shared'; and, made very firm by a statement repeated many times, 'In the section of ten, ten robes, and in the section of eleven, eleven robes are to be determined, not to be shared,' and 'All robes are to be determined, not to be shared.' Therefore, both of these texts appear contradictory. And in the Khandhaka itself it is said: 'to determine the rains-cloth for the four months of the rains, and after that, to share it.' In its commentary, it is said: 'The rains-cloth, of a size not exceeding the limit, is to be determined by name for the four rainy months according to the method already stated. After that, having been withdrawn, it is to be shared.' This also appears mutually contradictory, because of the possibility of withdrawal in the winter season and the impossibility of sharing in the rainy season. Likewise, here, the commentary's statement—that from the authority of the text 'There is no offense if one determines or shares within ten days,' it should be understood that sharing is not prohibited in all cases—appears contradictory to the text of the Parivāra. For the Tathāgatas do not speak what is contradictory. Therefore, in this matter, the method of the commentary is the refuge, by which all of this has a single, consistent meaning. And in the Parivāra commentary it is said: 'The words "are not to be shared" mean they are not to be shared from the time of determination onwards.' The meaning is this: the three robes are not to be shared from the time of determination onwards, and the rains-cloth and so on are not to be shared unwillingly within their own respective periods of determination. The remaining Pāḷi and its meaning are stated here in the commentary; therefore, all of this has a single, consistent meaning.

Etthāha [M 0.0226] – yadi evaṃ “nava cīvarāni nādhiṭṭhātabbānī”ti ca vattabbaṃ. Vikappitakālato paṭṭhāya hi nādhiṭṭhātabbānīti? Ettha vuccate – “ticīvaraṃ adhiṭṭhātuṃ na vikappetuṃ…pe… parikkhāracoḷaṃ adhiṭṭhātuṃ na vikappetu”nti ettha sabbattha adhiṭṭhāne paṭisedhādassanato, vikappanāya adassanato ca “tato para”nti dvīsveva paricchedadassanato ca “nava cīvarāni adhiṭṭhātabbāni, na vikappetabbāni ceva vuttanti veditabbaṃ. Aparo nayo – anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ticīvaraṃ adhiṭṭhātuṃ akāmā. Kasmā? Kāle uppannaṃ anadhiṭṭhahantassa kālātikkame āpattisambhavato, akāle uppannaṃ anadhiṭṭhahantassa dasāhātikkame āpattisambhavato ca. Tattha yaṃ kāle uppannaṃ appahontepi dasāhe kālātikkame āpattikaraṃ, taṃ [V 0.0202] nissajjanakāle “idaṃ me, bhante, atirekacīvaraṃ dhāritaṃ nissaggiyaṃ, imāhaṃ saṅghassā”tiādinā nissajjitabbaṃ, itaraṃ yathāpāḷimeva. Tattha paṭhamanayo “yo pana, bhikkhu, atirekacīvaraṃ dhāreyya nissaggiya”nti imāya paṭhamapaññattiyā vasena vutto, dutiyo anupaññattiyā vasena vutto.

Here, one objects: If so, then it should also be stated, 'The nine robes are not to be determined.' Is it that from the time of sharing, they are not to be determined? To this, it is replied: In the text, 'One should determine the three robes, not share them… one should determine the accessory cloth, not share it,' it should be understood that it is said, 'The nine robes are to be determined, and not to be shared.' This is because no prohibition against determination is shown in all cases, because a prohibition against sharing is shown, and because a limit, 'beyond that,' is shown for only two robes. Another method: I allow, O bhikkhus, the determination of the three robes by one who is unwilling. Why? Because for one who does not determine a robe that has arisen in season, an offense can occur by exceeding the season; and for one who does not determine a robe that has arisen out of season, an offense can occur by exceeding ten days. Of these, the robe that has arisen in season, even if ten days are not sufficient, causes an offense when the season is exceeded. That robe must be relinquished at the time of relinquishment with the words, 'Venerable sir, this extra robe has been kept by me; it is to be relinquished. I relinquish this to the Saṅgha,' and so on. The other robe should be relinquished exactly according to the Pāḷi. Of these, the first method is stated by means of this first regulation: 'Whatever bhikkhu should keep an extra robe, it is to be relinquished.' The second is stated by means of the secondary regulation.

Yathā ca nissajjitabbavatthumhi asati yathāpāḷiṃ avatvā kevalaṃ āpatti eva desetabbā, yathā ca vassikasāṭikanissajjane kevalaṃ pariyiṭṭhamatte yathāpāḷiṃ avatvā yathāsambhavaṃ nissajjitabbaṃ, tathā idampīti veditabbaṃ. Yathā saṃvaccharātikkantaṃ atirekacīvaraṃ “dasāhātikkanta”micceva vuccati. Saṃvaccharavippavutthaticīvaraṃ, māsātikkantañca “rattivippavuttha”nti ca “chārattavippavuttha”nti ca vuccati, tathā idampi “dasāhātikkanta”micceva vuccatīti eke, tasmā siddhamidaṃ “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ticīvaraṃ adhiṭṭhātuṃ akāmā”ti, tathā akāmā na vikappetunti attho. Icchāya hi sati “paccuddharitvā vippavāsasukhatthaṃ vikappanāya okāso dinno hoti, dasāhātikkame ca anāpattī”ti vacanato vikappetuṃ anujānāmīti vuttaṃ hoti. Tathā vassikasāṭikā akāmā adhiṭṭhātuṃ dasāhātikkame āpattisambhavato. Kittakaṃ kālanti ce? Vassānaṃ cātumāsaṃ, icchāya pana sati uddhaṃyeva vikappetabbaṃ. “Sabbattha vikappanāya appaṭisiddhabhāvo veditabbo”ti hi vuttaṃ. “Atthāpatti hemante āpajjati, no gimhe, no vasse”ti (pari. 323) ca vuttaṃ, tena vuttaṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “tato paraṃ paccuddharitvā vikappetabbā”ti.

It should be understood that this case is similar to others: just as when there is no object to be relinquished, one should simply confess the offense without reciting the Pāḷi formula; and just as when relinquishing the rains-cloth, one should relinquish it according to the circumstances after merely searching for it, without reciting the Pāḷi formula. Just as an extra robe kept beyond a year is still called 'one that has exceeded ten days'; and just as a triple robe from which one has been separated for a year, or for more than a month, is called 'separated for a night' or 'separated for six nights' respectively; so too, some say, this is also simply called 'one that has exceeded ten days.' Therefore, this statement is established: 'I allow, O bhikkhus, the determination of the three robes by one who is unwilling.' The meaning is that one who is unwilling should not share it. For when there is willingness, because of the passage stating, 'Having withdrawn it, the opportunity for sharing is given for the sake of the comfort of living apart, and there is no offense in exceeding ten days,' it is said that one is permitted to share. Similarly, the rains-cloth is to be determined by one who is unwilling, because an offense can occur when ten days are exceeded. If one asks, 'For how long?' For the four months of the rains. But if there is willingness, it should be shared after that period. For it is said, 'It should be understood that sharing is not prohibited in all cases.' And it is also said, 'An offense occurs in the winter, not in the hot season, not in the rainy season.' Therefore, it is stated in the commentary, 'After that, one should withdraw it and share it.'

Tatrāyaṃ [M 0.0227] vicāraṇā – kadā paccuddharitabbā, kadā vikappetabbā, kiñcettha yasmā “tato para”nti vuttaṃ. Hemantañca pattamatte sā adhiṭṭhānaṃ vijahati, tasmā “paccuddharitvā”ti na vattabbaṃ adhiṭṭhānassa natthitāya, atha “antocātumāse vikappetabbā”ti na vattabbaṃ. “Tato paraṃ vikappetu”nti hi vuttanti? Ettha ekacce vadanti “vattabbameta”nti. Yathā parivutthaparivāso, ciṇṇamānatto ca santo niṭṭhitesupi parivāsamānattadivasesu, tathā niṭṭhitesupi adhiṭṭhānadivasesu sādhiṭṭhānametanti eke. Aṭṭhakathācariyānaṃ idaṃ sanniṭṭhānaṃ “kattikapuṇṇamadivase paccuddharitvā pāṭipadadivase vikappetabbā”ti. Vuttañhetaṃ parivāraṭṭhakathāyaṃ “kattikapuṇṇamāsiyā pacchime pāṭipadadivase vikappetvā ṭhapitaṃ vassikasāṭikaṃ nivāsento hemante āpajjati. Kurundiyaṃ pana ‘kattikapuṇṇamadivase apaccuddharitvā hemante āpajjatī’ti vuttaṃ, tampi suvuttaṃ. ‘Cātumāsaṃ adhiṭṭhātuṃ, tato paraṃ vikappetu’nti hi vutta”nti (pari. aṭṭha. 323). Tattha kurundinayo pacchā vuttattā sārato daṭṭhabbo[V 0.0203], na purimo. Nivāsento hi gimhepi orenaddhamāsaṃ āpajjati eva. Idha ca “atthāpatti hemante āpajjati, no gimheti vutta”nti kurundivacanassāyamattho dissati.

Here is the investigation: When should it be withdrawn, when should it be assigned, and what is meant here by 'after that'? The determination ceases as soon as the winter season arrives. Therefore, it should not be said, 'having withdrawn it,' because the determination no longer exists; nor should it be said, 'it should be assigned within the four months,' because it was stated, 'after that, one should assign it.' Here, some say, 'This can be said.' Just as one who has completed probation and one who has undergone penance are considered as such even after the days of probation and penance are finished, so too, even after the days of determination are finished, this is considered a determined item—so say some. The commentary teachers have concluded thus: 'On the full-moon day of Kattika, it should be withdrawn, and on the first day of the dark fortnight following, it should be assigned.' For it is said in the Parivāra commentary: 'A monk wearing a rains-cloth that was assigned and set aside on the first day following the full moon of Kattika incurs an offense in the winter season.' But in the Kurundī, it is said, 'If one does not withdraw it on the full-moon day of Kattika, one commits an offense in the winter season.' That too is well said. For it was stated, 'One should determine it for the four months, and after that, one should assign it.' Therein, the Kurundī method, being stated later, should be regarded as the authoritative one, not the former one. For one who wears it incurs an offense within half a month, even in the hot season. And here, the meaning of the Kurundī statement is seen to be: 'an offense is incurred in the winter, not in the hot season.'

“Kattikapuṇṇamadivase apaccuddharitvā tasmiṃyeva divase avikappento pacchimapāṭipadadivase apaccuddhārapaccayā dukkaṭaṃ āpajjati, na, avikappanapaccayā dasāhaparihārasambhavato”ti kāraṇameke vadanti. Evaṃ sati hemante pattamatte adhiṭṭhānaṃ vijahatīti āpajjati, tañca ayuttaṃ. Adhiṭṭhānañhi “aññassa dānena…pe… chiddabhāvenāti imehi navahi kāraṇehi vijahatī”ti (pārā. aṭṭha. 2.469) vuttaṃ, na “adhiṭṭhānakhettātikkamena vā”ti. Asādhāraṇattā na vuttanti ce? Na, “chiddabhāvenā”ti na vattabbappasaṅgato, chiddabhāvena pana ticīvarasseva sabbaṭṭhakathāsu adhiṭṭhānavijahanassa vuttattā. Tasmā hemantassa paṭhamadivase apaccuddhārapaccayā dukkaṭaṃ āpajjati, na paccuddharitvā avikappanapaccayā. “Vikappetu”nti vacanato tato adhiṭṭhānaṃ na vijahatīti paññāyati. Na hi kattikapuṇṇamāsiyā pacchime pāṭipadadivase avikappetvā hemante āpajjatīti vuttanti adhippāyo, yasmā taṃ apaccuddhārapaccayā dukkaṭaṃ hemantassa paṭhamaaruṇakkhaṇe eva āpajjati, tasmā “kattikapuṇṇamadivase apaccuddharitvā”ti vuttaṃ. Paccuddhaṭaṃ pana hemante dasāhaparihāraṃ [M 0.0228] labhati. “Dasāhe appahonte cīvarakālaṃ nātikkāmetabbā”ti (pārā. aṭṭha. 2.630) hi vuttaṃ, tañca kho samaye uppannaṃ ce, nāsamaye. Tathā ca sādhitaṃ apaccuddhaṭaṃ na nissaggiyaṃ hoti, no ca taṃ paridahitaṃ, tasmā kattikapuṇṇamadivase eva paccuddharaṇañca vikappanañca kattabbanti siddhaṃ, ettha ca yathā atirekacīvaraṃ dasame divase vikappentena dasāhaparamaṃ dhāritaṃ hoti, antodasāhe ca vikappitaṃ hoti, tathā kattikapuṇṇamāya vikappentena vassānaṃ cātumāsaṃ adhiṭṭhitañca hoti, tato paraṃ anāpattikhette eva vikappanā ca hotīti veditabbaṃ. Ettāvatā atthi vikappanākhette adhiṭṭhānaṃ, adhiṭṭhānakhette ca vikappanāti dīpitaṃ hoti. Aññathā “atthāpatti adhiṭṭhānena āpajjati, anadhiṭṭhānena āpajjati. Atthāpatti vikappanāya āpajjati, avikappanāya āpajjatī”ti dukesu dve dukāni vattabbāni siyuṃ. Tattha paṭhamaduke paṭhamapadaṃ sambhavati. Vikappanakhette hi vassikasāṭikādīnaṃ adhiṭṭhānena vinayātisāradukkaṭaṃ āpajjati. Eteneva dutiyadukkaṭassa dutiyapadaṃ vuttaṃ hoti. Anadhiṭṭhānena āpajjatīti natthi. Antodasāhe anāpajjanato, vikappanādisambhavato ca vikappanāya āpajjatīti natthi sabbattha vikappanāya appaṭisiddhattā, tasmā tāni dukāni “na labbhantī”ti na vuttāni. Etthāha – yā sā “atthāpatti hemante āpajjatī”ti (pari. 323) vacanappamāṇato dukkaṭāpatti sādhitā, sā [V 0.0204] sañcicca apaccuddharantassa yujjati, asatiyā ce, kañci, anāpatti. Kattikapuṇṇamāya paccuddhaṭaṃ sañcicca avikappayato dukkaṭena saha punadivase nissaggiyaṃ, asatiyā avikappayato nissaggiyameva idha paṭhamapaññattiyā. Yaṃ pana vuttaṃ mātikāṭṭhakathāyaṃ (kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. kathinasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā) “vassikasāṭikā vassānamāsātikkamenāpi, kaṇḍupaṭicchādi ābādhavūpasamenāpi adhiṭṭhānaṃ vijahati, tasmā sā tato paraṃ vikappetabbā”ti, tenetaṃ virujjhati, na kevalaṃ idameva, “tato paraṃ paccuddharitvā vikappetabbā”ti aṭṭhakathāvacanañca virujjhati. Tato paraṃ nāma hi hemantaṃ, tattha ce paccuddhāro, “vassikasāṭikā vassānamāsātikkamenāpī”tiādi na yuttaṃ adhiṭṭhānābhāvena paccuddhārābhāvato. Avirodho ca icchitabbo, tasmā “paccuddharaṇaṃ vattamatta”ntivādo etthāpi sambhavatīti ce? Na, kurundi vacanavirodhato. Tattha hi kattikapuṇṇamāya paccuddhāro vutto, tasmā [M 0.0229] vassānadivasattā sādhiṭṭhānāvasā paccuddharīyatīti na paccuddhāro vattamattaṃ, tasmā “tato para”nti yāva puṇṇamā adhippetā siyā. Yathā cāyaṃ vikappo, tathā “vassānamāsātikkamenāpi ābādhavūpasamenāpī”ti idampi avassaṃ paccuddharitabbatāya vuttaṃ siyā. Evañca sati idha samantapāsādikāya tadavacanena sameti. Aññathā idhapi taṃ vattabbaṃ siyāti yathāvuttova vidhi ettha sambhavati, kiñcāpi sambhavati, duviññāpayassa pana lokassa suviññāpanatthaṃ vuttā. Yasmā pana sā vassānātikkamena adhiṭṭhānaṃ vijahati, hemantapaṭhamāruṇe ca apaccuddhārapaccayā dukkaṭā sādhitā, tasmā kattikapuṇṇamāyameva paccuddharitvā vikappetabbā, avikappitāya “nissaggiyāpajjanamevā”ti vattabbaṃ. Ettāvatāpi santosaṃ akatvā vinicchayo pariyesitabbo. Hoti cettha –

Some say that if, on the full-moon day of Kattika, one does not revoke the determination and does not make a formal declaration on that very day, one incurs a dukkaṭa offense on the following first day of the waning moon due to not revoking, not due to not making a formal declaration, because a ten-day allowance is possible. If this is so, it would follow that the determination is abandoned as soon as winter arrives, which is not proper. For it is said that the determination is abandoned for these nine reasons: 'by giving to another... by being torn,' but it is not said, 'or by transgressing the period of determination.' If it is said that it is not mentioned because it is uncommon? No, because it would follow that 'by being torn' should not be said; however, in all the commentaries, the abandoning of the determination by being torn is mentioned only for the three robes. Therefore, on the first day of winter, one incurs a dukkaṭa offense due to not revoking, not due to not making a formal declaration after having revoked. From the statement, 'Let him make a formal declaration,' it is understood that the determination is not abandoned by that transgression of the period. For it is not said that one incurs an offense in winter by not making a formal declaration on the first day of the waning moon following the Kattika full moon—this is the intention. Because that dukkaṭa offense, due to not revoking, is incurred at the very moment of the first dawn of winter, it is therefore said, 'not having revoked on the full-moon day of Kattika.' But a revoked robe obtains a ten-day allowance in winter. For it is said, 'If ten days are not sufficient, the robe-season should not be transgressed.' And that is if the robe has arisen in season, not out of season. And so, a completed robe, even if unrevoked, is not subject to forfeiture, nor is it to be worn. Therefore, it is established that on the full-moon day of Kattika itself, both revocation and formal declaration should be done. And here, just as an extra robe, for which a formal declaration is made on the tenth day, is kept for a maximum of ten days and has a formal declaration made for it within ten days, so too, for one making a formal declaration on the Kattika full moon, it has been determined for the four months of the rains, and after that, the formal declaration occurs only in the period where there is no offense. This should be understood. By this much, it is shown that there is determination in the period of formal declaration, and formal declaration in the period of determination. Otherwise, in the couplets, two couplets would have to be stated: 'There is an offense that is incurred through determination, and that is incurred through non-determination. There is an offense that is incurred through formal declaration, and that is incurred through non-formal declaration.' There, in the first couplet, the first phrase is possible. For in the period of formal declaration, by determining the rains-cloth, etc., one incurs a dukkaṭa offense of transgressing the Vinaya. By this very reasoning, the second phrase of the second couplet is stated. The case 'one incurs an offense through non-determination' does not exist, because no offense is incurred within ten days and because formal declaration, etc., are possible. The case 'one incurs an offense through formal declaration' does not exist, because formal declaration is not forbidden anywhere. Therefore, those couplets are not stated, the reason being that 'they are not found.' Here, an objector says: That dukkaṭa offense which is established by the authority of the statement, 'There is an offense; one incurs it in winter,' applies to one who intentionally does not revoke. If he does not revoke through mindlessness, what offense is there? No offense. For one who intentionally does not make a formal declaration for what was revoked on the Kattika full moon, on the next day it becomes subject to forfeiture along with a dukkaṭa offense. For one who does not make a formal declaration through mindlessness, it is only subject to forfeiture, here by the first ruling. But as for what is said in the Mātikā Commentary: 'The rains-cloth abandons its determination also by the passing of the rains-months, and the itch-covering cloth also by the subsiding of the illness; therefore, after that, a formal declaration should be made for it'—this is contradicted by that. Not only this, but the commentary statement 'after that, having revoked it, a formal declaration should be made for it' is also contradicted. For 'after that' means winter, and if revocation occurs there, the statement 'the rains-cloth, also by the passing of the rains-months,' etc., would not be proper, due to the absence of determination and thus the absence of revocation. And non-contradiction should be desired. Therefore, if it is said that the view 'revocation is a mere formality' is also possible here? No, because of contradiction with the word of the Kurundī. For there in the Kurundī, revocation on the Kattika full moon is mentioned. Therefore, because it is a day of the rains-season, it is revoked while it still has its determination. Thus, revocation is not a mere formality. Therefore, in the phrase 'after that,' 'up to the full moon' may be intended. And just as this is an alternative explanation, so too this statement, 'also by the passing of the rains-months, also by the subsiding of the illness,' may have been said because the robe must necessarily be revoked. This being so, it agrees with the Samantapāsādikā here in its silence on that statement. Otherwise, that would have to be said here also. Thus, the procedure as stated is possible here. Although it is possible, it was said for the sake of making it easy to understand for the world which is difficult to make understand. But because that rains-cloth abandons its determination by the passing of the rains-season, and a dukkaṭa offense is established due to not revoking at the first dawn of winter, therefore, on the Kattika full moon itself, it should be revoked and have a formal declaration made for it. For that which has not had a formal declaration made, it should be said that 'only the incurring of a forfeiture offense occurs.' Even with this much, not being satisfied, a decision should be sought. And here there is:

“Evaṃ abhāvaṃ vinayassa pāḷi,

Bhinnaṃ abhinnañca tadatthayuttiṃ;

Viññātukāmena tadatthaviññū,

Pariyesitabbā vinaye viññāyā”ti.

Thus, a monk who desires to know the Pāḷi of the Vinaya, its non-existence, what is divided and undivided, and the logical connection of its meaning, should seek out those who know that Vinaya Pāḷi and commentary in order to understand the Vinaya.

“Tuyhaṃ gaṇhāhī”ti vutte vināpi “mayhaṃ gaṇhāmī”ti vacanena sudinnaṃ hoti. Itaro ce adhivāseti, tenāpi suggahitaṃ hoti, no ce adhivāseti, dentena sudinnaṃ. Taṃ pana vatthu na kassaci hoti. Tathā “mayhaṃ gaṇhāmī”ti vadati, sāmiko ce adhivāseti, vināpi “gaṇhāhī”ti vacanena suggahitaṃ. No ce adhivāseti, sāmikasseva taṃ, na hi tassetaṃ vinayakammanti ettha vinayakammassatthāya ce gaṇhāti, na vaṭṭati. Na kevalaṃ attano atthāya gahitaṃ[V 0.0205], puna tassapi deti, vaṭṭatīti ca. Tathā anapekkho hutvā parassa vissajjetvā puna tena dinnaṃ vā tassa vissāsanto vā paribhuñjati, vaṭṭati. Tatthāpi vinayakammavasena na vaṭṭatīti eke. Te eva “mahantaṃ vā khuddakaṃ karotī”ti ettha “ticīvare dīghato vidatthi anatikkamitvā chinditvā karoti, evaṃ sesesupī”ti vadanti. Evarūpesu ṭhānesu porāṇācariyānaṃ kathāmaggaṃ suṭṭhu ācariyakulasevanāya sañjānitvā tena saṃsanditvā sato sampajāno hutvā sotūnañca cittaṃ avimohetvā kathetabbaṃ. Esā amhākaṃ āyācanā.

When it is said, 'Take it for yourself,' even without the words 'I take it for myself,' it is well-given. If the other person consents, it is also well-received; if he does not consent, it is well-given by the giver. But that item belongs to no one. Similarly, if one says, 'I take it for myself,' and the owner consents, it is well-received even without the words, 'Take it.' If the owner does not consent, it belongs to the owner himself, for this is not a Vinaya transaction for him. Herein, if one receives it for the purpose of a Vinaya transaction, it is not allowable. It is not taken for one's own purpose only; if one gives it back to him, it is allowable. This too should be known. Likewise, having become unconcerned and having relinquished it to another, if one again enjoys what is given by that person, or enjoys it while trusting that person, it is allowable. Some say that even in that case, it is not allowable by way of a Vinaya transaction. They themselves, regarding 'whether making it large or small,' say, 'In the case of the triple robe, one makes it by cutting it lengthwise without exceeding a span, and so it is also in the case of the remaining robes.' In such cases, one should, having known well the path of speech of the ancient teachers by frequenting the lineage of teachers and having compared it with that, become mindful and fully aware, and speak without confusing the minds of the listeners. This is our request.

Paṭhamakathinasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the first Kathina training rule is concluded.

2. Udositasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

2. Explanation of the Udosita Training Rule

471. Santaruttarena [M 0.0230] janapadacārikaṃ pakkamanti. Kasmā? Kiñcāpi “na, bhikkhave, santaruttarena gāmo pavisitabbo, yo paviseyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti (mahāva. 362) paṭhamaṃ vuttaṃ. Pacchā pana “pañcime, bhikkhave, paccayā saṅghāṭiyā nikkhepāya, uttarāsaṅgassa, antaravāsakassa nikkhepāya gilāno vā hoti, vassikasaṅketaṃ vā, nadīpāraṃ gantuṃ vā, aggaḷaguttivihāro vā, atthatakathinaṃ vā hotī”ti vuttattā, aṭṭhakathāyampissa “pañcasu petesu aggaḷagutti eva pamāṇaṃ. Gutte eva hi vihāre nikkhipitvā bahi gantuṃ vaṭṭati, nāgutte”ti vuttattā apaññattepi kathine “te bhikkhū aggaḷaguttivihāre ṭhapethā”ti vatvā sabhāgānaṃ hatthe cīvaraṃ nikkhipitvā santaruttarena gāmappavese laddhakappiyā janapadacārikaṃ pakkāmiṃsūti veditabbaṃ.

471. They set out on a journey through the countryside with their inner and upper robes. Why? Although it was first said, “Monks, a village is not to be entered with only the inner and upper robes; whoever should enter commits an offense of wrong-doing,” it was later said, “Monks, there are these five reasons for setting aside the outer robe, the upper robe, and the inner robe: one is sick, or there is a sign of rain, or one is going to the other side of a river, or the monastery is secured with a bolt, or the Kaṭhina has been spread.” And because it is also said in its commentary, “Among these five, a monastery secured with a bolt is the standard. For it is allowable to go outside after leaving the robe in a secured monastery, but not in an unsecured one.” Therefore, it should be understood that even when the Kaṭhina was not in effect, those monks, having said, “Place the robes in the monastery secured with a bolt,” and having placed the robe in the hands of their companions, set out on their journey through the countryside with their inner and upper robes, having obtained what is allowable for entering a village.

473. Avippavāsasammutinti avippavāsatthaṃ, vippavāsapaccayā yā āpatti, tadabhāvatthaṃ vā sammutiṃ dātunti attho. Tato paṭṭhāya vaṭṭati. Kittakaṃ kālaṃ vaṭṭatīti? Māsaṃ vā atirekaṃ vā yāva gamane saussāho, tāva vaṭṭati. Tena vuttaṃ “dhuranikkhepaṃ karontena paccuddharitabba”nti. Puna sammutidānakiccaṃ natthīti sace dvādasannaṃ vassānaṃ accayena añño rogo hoti, vaṭṭati, upasampadakammaṃ viya yāvajīvaṃ ekāsammuti vaṭṭatīti ca.

473. The phrase 'authorization for non-separation' means to grant an authorization for the purpose of non-separation, or for the purpose of preventing the offense that arises from separation. From that point onward, it is allowable. For how long is it allowable? For a month or more; for as long as one is keen on the journey, for that long it is allowable. Therefore it was said: “It should be rescinded by the one who lays down the burden.” As to there being no need for a renewed act of granting authorization: if, after the passing of twelve years, another illness arises, it is allowable. And it should be understood that, like the act of higher ordination, a single authorization is allowable for life.

“Kataṃ vā hotī”tiādi imasmiṃ sikkhāpade na vattabbaṃ, kasmā? Karaṇapalibodhe upacchinnepi anadhiṭṭhitacīvarato vippavāsapaccayā āpattiyā asambhavato, tasmā “niṭṭhitacīvarasminti bhikkhuno cīvaraṃ adhiṭṭhitaṃ hotī”ti ettakameva vattabbanti ce? Na, tadāyattattā[V 0.0206]. Adhiṭṭhānañhi karaṇapalibodhassa niṭṭhāpanāyattaṃ, tasmā “kataṃ vātiādi vutta”nti ca vuttaṃ. Tattha katanti pubbe vuttameva.

The phrase 'or if it is completed,' etc., should not be stated in this training rule. Why? Because even when the obstacle to the making has ceased, since the robe has not been determined, there is no possibility of an offense arising from the factor of separation. Therefore, if it is asked, 'Should it only be said, "When the robe is finished, the monk's robe is determined"?' No, because of its dependence on that. For the determination is indeed dependent on the completion of the making that was subject to an obstacle; therefore, 'or if it is completed,' etc., is stated. Therein, 'completed' is as has been stated previously.

477-8. Avippavāsalakkhaṇavavatthāpanatthanti ettha “antogāme cīvaraṃ nikkhipitvā antogāme vatthabba”ntiādivacanato avippavāsalakkhaṇaṃ vavatthāpitaṃ, tabbiparītanayena vippavāsalakkhaṇaṃ veditabbaṃ. Gāmo ekūpacārotiādimhi pana ṭhapetvā satthaṃ, rukkhamūlaṃ, ajjhokāsañca sesesu parikkhepāparikkhepavasena ekūpacāranānūpacāratā veditabbā. Yasmā pana [M 0.0231] satthaṃ duvidhaṃ niviṭṭhaṃ, aniviṭṭhañca, tesu aniviṭṭhaṃ ekakulassa vā nānākulassa vā aparikkhittameva hoti, niviṭṭhaṃ siyā parikkhittaṃ, siyā aparikkhittaṃ, tasmā tattha parikkhepādivasena adassetvā abbhantaravasena vutto. Tathā abbhokāse. Rukkhamūle chāyāvasena. Aññathā “sattho ekūpacāro nānūpacāro”tiādi uddesavirodho siyā vibhaṅge adassitattā, tasmā satthassa purato ca pacchato ca sattabbhantarā, passato ca ekabbhantaranti ayamekūpacāro, tato paraṃ nānūpacāro. Tathā rukkhamūlassa yattha majjhanhike kāle chāyā pharati, ayaṃ ekūpacāro. Itaro nānūpacāro. Kasmā? Tattha hi parikkhepo appamāṇaṃ. Chāyāva pamāṇaṃ. Ajjhokāsassa pāḷiyaṃ vuttova. “Satthādīnaṃ ekakulasantakavasena ekūpacāratā”ti likhitaṃ, tasmā nivesane, udosite ca vuttaparicchedova aṭṭādīsūti katvā saṃkhittaṃ.
