Now, if those donors do not come and take it, having asked the donors, if it is relinquished for his own benefit, having forfeited it to the Saṅgha, the offense should be confessed. If not, only the offense should be confessed. This was stated. That statement is self-contradictory. For when the offense is confessed, it is established that money was received. When that is established, this statement, 'What is produced from that is allowable for him also,' is not correct. If one should say, 'It is indeed allowable'? No. It is not correct that the offense should be confessed without having forfeited the article. If one should say, 'It is correct because the training rule is for an unintentional act'? No, because of the phrase 'one receives money' is used everywhere. For it is said, 'one receives money'; otherwise, the word 'money' everywhere would be meaningless, since even without it, that meaning would be established. And by this bhikkhu, an article was received, and by the donor, only an article was given. One who takes the money that is on the article with a thieving mind should be dealt with according to the step-by-step valuation for theft. And in the Commentary, it is said, '“Perceiving what is money as not money” means having the perception of rough leaves, etc., with regard to gold, etc.,' by way of the statement, 'one receives money.'

“Apica puññakāmā”tiādi pana vidhānantaradassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ, teneva hi “imasmiṃ gehe idaṃ laddhanti sallakkhetabba”nti vuttaṃ. Aññathā sallakkhaṇe vimativasena, vimatiyā ca sati nissaggiyameva “rūpiye vematiko”tiādi vacanatoti. Idaṃ vidhānaṃ niratthakameva āpajjati, na ca niratthakaṃ. Kasmā? Dussante baddhakahāpaṇādi assatiyā dinnaṃ vatthasaññāya paṭiggahitañca, tato na rūpiyaṃ dinnañca hoti paṭiggahitañcāti. Ettha āpattidesanākiccaṃ natthi, taṃ pana dāyakānameva paṭidātabbaṃ. Tato uppannaṃ kappiyabhaṇḍañca sabbesaṃ kappatīti imassa vidhānantaradassanatthaṃ “apica puññakāmā”tiādīti no takkoti ācariyo.

Moreover, the passage beginning with 'those who desire merit' is stated to show another method. For that very reason, it is said, 'In this house, this has been received—thus it should be noted.' Otherwise, in the matter of noting, there is doubt; and when there is doubt, it is indeed a matter for relinquishment, because of the saying, 'one who is uncertain about money,' and so forth. This method would become entirely meaningless, but it does not become meaningless. Why? Because a kahāpaṇa, etc., tied in the hem of a cloth is given through mindlessness and is received with the perception of it being an article; therefore, it is not that money is given and received. Here, there is no duty of confessing an offense; however, that should be returned to the donors themselves. To show another method for this statement, 'And the allowable goods that arise from that are permissible for all,' the passage beginning with 'Moreover, those who desire merit' is stated. The teacher says, 'This is our reasoning.'

Rūpiyasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rule on Money is concluded.

9. Rūpiyasaṃvohārasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

9. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Transactions involving Money

587. “Jātarūparajataparivattana”nti [M 0.0264] ukkaṭṭhaparicchedena vuttaṃ, tathā “rūpiyaṃ nāma satthuvaṇṇo kahāpaṇo”tiādi pāḷivacanañca. “Arūpiye rūpiyasaññī rūpiyaṃ cetāpetī”tiādi tikavacanato, “dukkaṭavatthunā pana nissaggiyavatthuṃ cetāpentassa…pe… nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ garukassa cetāpitattā”ti aṭṭhakathāvacanato ca pana anukkaṭṭhaparicchedopettha labbhatīti siddhaṃ. Satthuvaṇṇo ca kahāpaṇo ca tato ye caññe vohāraṃ gacchantīti evamettha samuccayo veditabbo. Imasmiṃ pana sikkhāpade “nānappakārakaṃ nāma katampi akatampi katākatampī”ti ettha vibhattānaṃ tiṇṇaṃ rūpiyārūpiyānañca dvinnaṃ vasena pañca tikā vuttā, aṭṭhakathācariyehi tadanulomato eko tiko dassitoti sabbe cha honti.

587. The phrase 'exchange of gold and silver' is stated according to the highest standard; similarly, the Pāḷi saying beginning with 'money means gold, the kahāpaṇa' is also stated according to the highest standard. However, from the statement of the triad beginning with 'perceiving what is not money as money, one causes an exchange of money,' and from the commentary's statement, 'for one who causes a forfeitable object to be exchanged with an object involving a dukkaṭa offense... it is a nissaggiya pācittiya because a serious object was caused to be exchanged,' it is established that a non-highest standard is also obtained here. Gold and the kahāpaṇa, and whatever other things apart from these are used in transactions—thus the collection should be understood here. In this training rule, however, in the phrase 'various kinds, namely, wrought, unwrought, and both wrought and unwrought,' five triads are stated by way of the three divided types and the two types of money and non-money. Since the commentary teachers, in accordance with these, have shown one triad, all together there are six.

Etthāha – aññasmiṃ sikkhāpade ekasmiṃ tikacchede dassite satipi sambhave itare na dassīyanti[V 0.0236], idheva kasmā dassitoti? “Nānappakāraka”nti mātikāyaṃ vuttattā idheva nānappakārabhāvadassanatthanti. Na kayavikkayasikkhāpadepi vattabbappasaṅgatoti ce? Na, idha dassitanayattā. Atha ca rūpiyassa vibhaṅge “ye vohāraṃ gacchantī”ti ante vuttattā satthuvaṇṇādayo vaḷañjanupagā evāti siddhaṃ. Tato avaḷañjanupagehi jātarūparajatehi vohārena na nissaggiyanti āpajjati, tasmā taṃ āpajjanatthanti dassentena “katena kataṃ cetāpetī”tiādayo tikā vuttāti, evaṃ sante rūpiyavibhaṅge “ye ca vohāraṃ gacchantī”ti na vattabbaṃ, tasmiṃ pade avutte avaḷañjanupagāpi saṅgahaṃ gatāva hontīti katādīhi tikattayassa vattabbapayojanaṃ na bhavissatīti ce? Na, kappiyabhaṇḍena kappiyabhaṇḍapaavattanassāpi rūpiyasaṃvohārabhāvappasaṅgato. “Ye vohāraṃ gacchantī”ti vacanenapi kamuka kathala kaṃsabhājana sāṭakādiparivattanassapi rūpiyasaṃvohārabhāvappasaṅgo evāti ce? Na, katādivacanena jātarūpādiakappiyavatthūnaññeva adhippetabhāvadīpanato, tasmā ubhayenapi yadetaṃ katākatādibhedaṃ pākatikarūpiyaṃ yañca kahāpaṇamāsakasaṅkhepaṃ, yañca kahāpaṇādivohārūpagaṃ, ubhayampetaṃ idha ca anantarātītasikkhāpade ca rūpiyaṃ nāmāti adhippetatthasiddhi hoti, na taṇḍulādīni, tattha katādivohārāsambhavato. Ettāvatā katāditikattayappayojanaṃ vuttaṃ.

Here it is said: In another training rule, although it is possible, when one triad-division is shown, the others are not. So why is it shown only here? Because it is stated in the matrix, “of various kinds,” it is shown only here in order to demonstrate its various kinds. If it is objected that this should also be stated in the training rule on buying and selling, this is not so, because the method has been shown here. Furthermore, because in the analysis of rūpiya, it is stated at the end, “those that are used in trade,” it is established that gold and so on are only those things used in transactions. From that, it would follow that trading with gold and silver not used in transactions would not be an offense entailing forfeiture. Therefore, to show that such an offense is incurred, the triads such as “one causes to be obtained what is made with what is made” are stated. If this is so, one might object that in the analysis of rūpiya, the phrase “and those that are used in trade” should not be stated, for if that phrase were omitted, even items not used in transactions would be included, and thus there would be no purpose in stating the three triads beginning with “what is made.” This is not so, because it would lead to the consequence that even the exchange of an allowable item for an allowable item would be considered a transaction with rūpiya. One might further object that even with the statement “those that are used in trade,” the exchange of items like areca nuts, earthenware, bronze bowls, or cloth would still be considered a transaction with rūpiya. This is not so, because the statement beginning with “what is made” clarifies that only unallowable items such as gold and silver are intended; therefore, the aforementioned consequence does not arise. Therefore, by both these statements, the intended meaning is established of what is called 'rūpiya'—both here and in the immediately preceding training rule: it is both the natural rūpiya which is distinguished as made, unmade, and so on, and that which is designated as kahāpaṇa and māsaka and is used in trade as kahāpaṇas and the like. Rice and the like are not included, because for them, a transaction involving “what is made” is not possible. Thus, the purpose of the three triads beginning with “what is made” has been stated.

Idāni [M 0.0265] sesattikāni vuccati – ettha hi yathāvuttappabhedaṃ nissaggiyavatthu rūpiyaṃ nāma, sesaṃ dukkaṭavatthupi kappiyavatthupi na rūpiyanti arūpiyaṃ nāma hotīti katvā “arūpiye arūpiyasaññī pañcannaṃ sahadhammikānaṃ anāpattī”ti idaṃ na ekaṃsikaṃ āpajjati dukkaṭavatthumhi dukkaṭāpajjanato. Idha vacanappamāṇato nissaggiyavatthuto aññaṃ antamaso muttādipi arūpiyameva nāma. Tattha pañcannaṃ sahadhammikānaṃ anāpattīti ce? Na, rājasikkhāpadavirodhato. Tattha hi “muttā vā maṇi vā”ti vuttaṃ, tasmā muttādi akappiyaṃ dukkaṭavatthūti ca siddhaṃ nissaggiyavatthūsu abhāvā. Evaṃ sante “arūpiye arūpiyasaññī pañcannaṃ sahadhammikānaṃ anāpattī”ti suddhakappiyabhaṇḍaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ, na sabbaṃ arūpiyaṃ. Tato aññattha pana “arūpiye rūpiyasaññī”tiāditikadukkaṭe ca aṭṭhakathāyaṃ dassitatike ca sabbaṃ arūpiyaṃ nāmāti veditabbaṃ, tasmā arūpiyabhāvadīpanatthaṃ dutiyo tiko vutto. Tadatthameva aṭṭhakathāyaṃ dassito eko tiko. Kasmā na pāḷiyaṃ so vuttoti ce? Tattha cetāpitaarūpiye rūpiyachaḍḍanakasammutikiccābhāvato. Tasmiñhi tike vutte kappiyavatthunopi arūpiyachaḍḍanakasammuti dātabbāti āpajjati, tassa vasena rūpiyachaḍḍanakasammuti eva na vattabbāti? Na, rūpiyassapi sammutikiccābhāvappasaṅgato, tasmā rūpiye rūpiyasaññī kappiyavatthuṃ cetāpeti pattacatukke tatiyapattaṃ viya, taṃ saṅghādīnaṃ nissajjitabbaṃ, nissaṭṭhaṃ pana [V 0.0237] aññesaṃ kappati tatiyapatto viya. Atha sampaṭicchitarūpiyena cetāpitaṃ hoti dutiyapatto viya, taṃ vināpi sammutiyā yo koci bhikkhu chaḍḍeti, vaṭṭati. Tato paraṃ “sace tattha āgacchati ārāmiko vā”tiādinā vuttanayeneva paṭipajjitabbaṃ. Tattha “rūpiye”ti vā “arūpiye”ti vā sabbattha bhummappatte attano santakaṃ, upayogappatte parasantakanti veditabbaṃ. Etthāha – upatissatthero purimasikkhāpadena rūpiyapaṭiggahaṇaṃ vāritaṃ, iminā suddhāgamena kappiyakārakassa hatthe kappiyaṃ nissāya ṭhitena saṃvohāro vāritoti.

Now, the remaining triads are spoken of. Here, as previously classified, the object entailing forfeiture is called 'rūpiya'; the remainder—whether an object of wrong-doing or an allowable object—is not rūpiya, and so is called 'arūpiya'. Therefore, the statement, 'In the case of non-rūpiya, perceiving it as non-rūpiya, there is no offense for the five co-religionists,' does not apply invariably, because of the incurring of an offense of wrong-doing in the case of an object of wrong-doing. Here, by the authority of the text, anything other than an object entailing forfeiture—even pearls and the like—is indeed called 'arūpiya'. If it is said, 'In that case, there is no offense for the five co-religionists,' this is not so, because of the contradiction with the Rāja training rule. For there it is said, 'a pearl or a gem'; therefore, it is established that pearls and the like are unallowable, an object of wrong-doing, due to their absence among objects entailing forfeiture. This being so, the statement, 'In the case of non-rūpiya, perceiving it as non-rūpiya, there is no offense for the five co-religionists,' is said with reference to purely allowable goods, not all non-rūpiya. However, in other cases, such as in the triad of offenses of wrong-doing beginning with 'perceiving rūpiya in non-rūpiya' and in the triad shown in the commentary, it should be understood that all is called 'arūpiya'. Therefore, the second triad is stated for the purpose of clarifying the state of being non-rūpiya. For that very purpose, one triad is shown in the commentary. If it is asked, 'Why is it not stated in the Pāḷi?', it is because, in that case, for non-rūpiya that has been caused to be acquired, there is no procedure of formal designation for discarding rūpiya. For if that triad were stated, it would follow that even for an allowable object, a formal designation for discarding non-rūpiya would have to be given. And on account of that, should the formal designation for discarding rūpiya itself not be spoken of? No, because it would lead to the consequence of there being no procedure of formal designation even for rūpiya. Therefore, when one, perceiving rūpiya as rūpiya, causes an allowable object to be acquired, it is like the third bowl in the tetrad of bowls; that object must be relinquished to the Sangha and others. Once relinquished, it becomes allowable for others, like the third bowl. But if it has been caused to be acquired with received rūpiya, it is like the second bowl; any monk whatsoever may discard that object even without a formal designation, and it is proper to do so. Thereafter, one should proceed according to the method stated in the passage beginning, “If a monastery attendant or…” In all these cases, whether it is said 'in rūpiya' or 'in arūpiya', it should be understood that when the locative case is used, it refers to one's own property, and when the accusative case is used, it refers to another's property. Here, the Elder Upatissa said: By the previous training rule, the acceptance of rūpiya is prohibited; by this one, a transaction is prohibited for one who relies on an allowable item in the hands of a steward, when it is a simple acquisition.

589. Nissaggiyavatthunā nissaggiyavatthuṃ…pe… aparāparaparivattane imināti ettha ekasmiṃ eva vatthusmiṃ dvinnaṃ sikkhāpadānaṃ vasena ekato āpatti vuttā, taṃ pana pacchimassa vasena nissajjitabbaṃ. Etena nissaggiyaṃ āpannampi āpajjatīti eke. Parassa rūpiyaggahaṇaṃ parivattananti rūpiye aggahite tassa abhāvato imināva āpatti, na purimena omasavādo viya. Musāvādena [M 0.0266] musā vadantassāpi hi omasavādeneva āpatti. Nissaggiyavatthunā dukkaṭa…pe… eseva nayoti etassa yuttiṃ dassento “yo hi aya”nti āha.

589. Regarding 'an object entailing forfeiture by means of an object entailing forfeiture... and so on... in the case of repeated exchanges, by this': here, in a single item, an offense is stated as occurring simultaneously by means of two training rules. However, that object should be forfeited according to the latter rule. Some say that by this, one who has already incurred an offense entailing forfeiture incurs yet another. Regarding 'taking another's rūpiya is an exchange': since the rūpiya was not accepted, due to the absence of that offense, the offense is incurred by this rule alone, not by the former, just as in the case of slanderous speech. For indeed, even for one who speaks falsely by means of lying, the offense is incurred under the rule for slanderous speech alone. Regarding 'an offense of wrong-doing by means of an object entailing forfeiture... and so on... this is the method': showing the appropriateness of this text, he said, 'For indeed this...'

Vaḍḍhiṃ payojentassāti ettha idaṃ gahetvā sati māse, sati saṃvacchare “ettakaṃ dehī”ti ce vadati. Rūpiyasaṃvohāro hoti. Vinā kappiyakārakena “ettakā vuḍḍhi hotu, ettakaṃ gaṇhā”ti vadato dukkaṭaṃ kayavikkayalakkhaṇābhāvato. “Mūle mūlasāmikāna”ntiādi kappiyakaraṇūpāyadassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ, na kevalaṃ nissaṭṭhaṃ aparibhogaṃ hoti, puna evaṃ kate paribhuñjituṃ vaṭṭati. Tassapi paribhoge mūlassa kappiyakaraṇūpāyo ce na hoti, kappiyaṃ ācikkhitabbanti yathā pāḷiyā cettha kappiyakaraṇūpāyo, so ca tatiyapattepi, “yathā ca attano atthāya gahite evarūpupāyo, tathā saṅghādiatthāya gahitepi eso vā”ti vuttaṃ. Ime kira paṭhamadutiyapatte yāva gahaṭṭhena parivatteti, tāva na kappiyakaraṇūpāyo, anekapurisayugampi “akappiyā evā”ti aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttaṃ. Anugaṇṭhipade pana “saṅghasantakaṃ kappiyabhaṇḍaṃ vikkiṇitvā āgatakahāpaṇānipi paṭiggahaṇaṃ mocetvāva sampaṭicchitabbāni, tasmā kappiyakārako ce imāni tāni kahāpaṇānīti vadati, na vaṭṭatiyeva, paṭikkhipitabbaṃ, na vicāretabbaṃ, vicāreti ce? Sabbesaṃ na kappati. Paṭiggahaṇaṃ mocetvā sampaṭicchitāni ce vicāreti, tasseva na vaṭṭatī”ti abhikkhaṇaṃ vuttaṃ.

Here, regarding one who applies interest: having taken this, if after a month or a year one says, 'Give this much,' it is a monetary transaction. For a monk who, without a steward, says, 'Let the increase be this much; take this much,' there is a dukkaṭa offense, because of the absence of the characteristic of buying and selling. The passage beginning with 'The principal belongs to the owners of the principal' is stated to show the method of making something allowable. It is not merely that the relinquished item is unusable; rather, when this is done, it is permissible to use it. Even in the use of that, if there is no method for making the principal allowable, one must declare what is allowable. For this reason, here the method of making it allowable is just as in the Pāḷi, and that method also exists in the case of the third bowl. 'Just as there is such a method for what is received for one's own benefit, so too for what is received for the benefit of the Sangha, etc., this is the very method,' it is said. It is said that regarding these first and second bowls, as long as a layperson exchanges them, there is no method of making them allowable. It is stated in the commentary that even after many pairs of men, 'they are indeed unallowable.' However, in the Anugaṇṭhipada, it is frequently stated: 'Having sold allowable goods belonging to the Sangha, even the kahāpaṇas that have come must be accepted only after having relinquished the act of receiving. Therefore, if the steward says, "These are those kahāpaṇas," it is not permissible at all. It must be rejected; it must not be managed. If one does manage it? It is not allowable for all. If one manages things that were accepted after relinquishing the act of receiving, it is not permissible only for that person.'

Rūpiyasaṃvohārasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the training rule on monetary transactions is finished.

10. Kayavikkayasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

10. Commentary on the Training Rule on Buying and Selling

593. Paṭapilotikānanti [V 0.0238] paṭapilotikehi. “Ajjhācarati, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti idaṃ purimasikkhāpadepi veditabbaṃ. “Kayitañca hoti vikkayitañcā”ti etesaṃ padānaṃ viparītato “attano bhaṇḍa”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Kasmā? “Iminā ima”nti vacanānurūpato. Saddhādeyyavinipātanaṃ panettha aṭṭhānapadānaṃ vasena veditabbaṃ.

593. “Paṭapilotikānaṃ” means “with coarse cloths.” The phrase, “one transgresses, it is a dukkaṭa offense,” should also be understood in the previous training rule. In the opposite sense of the words, “it is bought and it is sold,” the passage beginning with “one's own goods” is stated. Why? Because of its conformity to the expression “this with this.” Here, the squandering of faith-offerings should be understood by way of inappropriate grounds.

Kayavikkayasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the training rule on buying and selling is concluded.

Niṭṭhito kosiyavaggo dutiyo.

The second chapter, the Kosiyavagga, is concluded.

3. Pattavaggo

3. The Chapter on Bowls

1. Pattasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

1. Commentary on the Training Rule on Bowls

598. Bahū [M 0.0267] patte sannicayanti ettha sannicayanti bhāvanapuṃsakaṃ, bahū patte vā gahetvā sannicayaṃ karissantīti attho. “Aḍḍhaterasapalamāsānaṃ gāhikā”ti likhitaṃ. Ettha –

598. In the phrase 'they accumulate many bowls,' the word 'accumulate' (`sannicayanti`) is a verbal neuter. Or, the meaning is: 'Having taken many bowls, they will make an accumulation.' 'They hold thirteen and a half palas and māsas' is written. Herein—

“Kuḍuvo catupaleyyo, kuḍuvānaṃ catugguṇaṃ;

Patthaṃ catugguṇo māsā-ti kamāhu catugguṇa”nti. –

“A kuḍuva is four palas; four kuḍuvas make a pattha; four patthas make a māsā—thus they say, fourfold in succession.”

Ādiṃ lokavohāraṃ dassetvāva keci papañcenti.

Some elaborate only after showing such worldly conventions from the beginning.

602. Khādananti khādanīyaṃ sūpādi. “Byañjanassa mattā nāma odanato catuttho bhāgo”ti (ma. ni. aṭṭha. 2.387) brahmāyusuttaṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttattā ālopassa catutthabhāgaṃ byañjanaṃ anurūpanti gahetabbaṃ. “Bhikkhuniyā pattasannicayassa vāritattā tadanulomato bhikkhūnampi dutiyo vārito”ti vuttaṃ, taṃ na yuttaṃ, pāḷiyañhi “sannicayaṃ kareyyāti anadhiṭṭhito avikappito”ti (pāci. 735) vuttaṃ. So hi kathinakkhandhake (mahāva. 306 ādayo) nicayasannidhi [V 0.0239] viya ekopi punadivase “sannicayo”ti vuccati. Anantarasikkhāpade pana “dutiyo vāritoti adhiṭṭhānaṃ niyataṃ, tasmā dve patte adhiṭṭhātuṃ na labhati. Sace ekato adhiṭṭhāti, dvepi na adhiṭṭhitā honti. Visuṃ visuṃ adhiṭṭhāti, dutiyo anadhiṭṭhito”ti vadanti. Vikappetuṃ pana bahūpi labhati. Idāni vattabbaṃ sandhāya “nāmamatte viseso”ti vuttaṃ. Tattha nāmanti majjhimo majjhimomako majjhimukkaṭṭhotiādi.

602. 'Food' means edible items such as bean-curry and so on. Because it is stated in the Commentary to the Brahmāyusutta, 'The measure of curry, it is said, is a fourth part of the rice,' it should be understood that a suitable amount of curry is a fourth part of a morsel. It is said, 'Because the accumulation of bowls is forbidden for a bhikkhunī, in accordance with that, a second bowl is also forbidden for bhikkhus.' That is not correct, for in the Pāḷi it is said, 'He would make an accumulation'—meaning a bowl that is not determined, not shared. For in the Kathinakkhandhaka, like a stored-up hoard, even a single bowl on the next day is called an 'accumulation.' However, in the immediately following training rule, they say: 'Because a second bowl is forbidden, the determination is fixed. Therefore, one does not get to determine two bowls. If one determines them together, both are not determined. If one determines them separately, the second is undetermined.' But one is allowed to share even many. Now, with reference to what is to be said, it was stated, 'The difference is in name only.' Therein, 'name' refers to medium, medium-small, medium-large, and so on.

608. “Pākassa hi ūnattā pattasaṅkhyaṃ na gacchatī”ti vacanato adhiṭṭhitapattopi kharapākena setattā adhiṭṭhānaṃ vijahatīti ce? Na, adhiṭṭhānavijahanesu navasu anāgatattā, tasmā paṭhamapākānaṃ eva ūnattā pattasaṅkhyaṃ na gacchati, tasmiṃ sati aññaṃ viññāpetuṃ na vaṭṭati. “Ūnapañcabandhanenā”ti hi vuttaṃ. Chidde, rājiyā vā hi sati tehi adhiṭṭhānaṃ vijahatīti vijahite nāyaṃ paṭisedho, tasmā paccuddharitvā, vikappetvāpi aññaṃ viññāpetuṃ na labhati.

608. If one were to say: 'In accordance with the statement, “Due to a deficiency in the firing, it does not attain the designation of a bowl,” does even a determined bowl abandon its determination due to a rough firing and becoming white?' No, because it is not included among the nine grounds for abandoning a determination. Therefore, it is only due to the deficiency of the first firings that it does not attain the designation of a bowl; while that is the case, it is not allowable to request another. For it is said, 'With less than five bindings.' For only when there is a hole or a crack does it abandon the determination on account of them. When it is abandoned, this prohibition does not apply. Therefore, having withdrawn the determination and having made a formal disposal, one is allowed to request another.

Evaṃ pattakārako mūlaṃ labhitvāti ettha pacitvā ṭhapitadivasato paṭṭhāya. Dātukāmo hutvāti ettha dinnadivasato, sutadivasato vā [M 0.0268] paṭṭhāya dasāhaṃ veditabbaṃ. Liṅgaparivattena pana dasāhātikkame pattasāmikassa bhikkhussa, bhikkhuniyā pana rattātikkame nissaggiyaṃ.

Thus, in the phrase 'the bowl-maker, having received the price,' the period begins from the day it was fired and set aside. In the phrase 'wishing to give,' ten days should be understood beginning from the day it was given or from the day it was heard of. However, by a change of gender, upon exceeding ten days, it becomes an item to be forfeited for the bhikkhu who is the owner of the bowl; but for a bhikkhunī, upon exceeding one night, it becomes an item to be forfeited.

Pattasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the training rule concerning the bowl is finished.

2. Ūnapañcabandhanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

2. Commentary on the Training Rule Concerning a Bowl with Fewer than Five Bindings

612-3. Bahū patte viññāpentīti ekamekaṃ viññāpentā bahū bhikkhū bahū patte viññāpenti, bahū vā bhikkhū patte viññāpentīti attho. “Na, bhikkhave, patto viññāpetabbo, yo viññāpeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti idaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ ūnapañcabandhanena samūhataṃ hoti na hotīti? Na hoti tameva gahetvā “viññāpeti, payoge dukkaṭa”nti vuttattāti eke. Paṭilābhampi pariyādiyitvā taṃ dukkaṭaṃ vuttaṃ, tasmā taṃ “paṭilābhena nissaggiyo hotī”ti iminā samūhataṃ hoti. Aññathā sadukkaṭaṃ nissaggiyaṃ āpajjati anāpattivāravirodho ca. Yā kāci pana akataviññatti ananuññātakāle dukkaṭameva. Bhinnenāti itthambhūtalakkhaṇe, bhedenāti vā attho, hetvatthe karaṇavacanaṃ.

612-3. In 'requesting many bowls,' the meaning is that many bhikkhus, requesting one by one, request many bowls, or that many bhikkhus request bowls. Is this training rule—'Bhikkhus, a bowl is not to be requested; whoever should request one, there is an offense of wrong-doing'—abolished by the rule concerning a bowl with fewer than five bindings, or not? Some say it is not, because, taking that very rule, it is stated: 'He requests; in the effort, there is a dukkaṭa.' That dukkaṭa was stated encompassing even the acquisition; therefore, that rule is abolished by this one: 'With the acquisition, it becomes an item to be forfeited.' Otherwise, one would incur a nissaggiya offense together with a dukkaṭa, and there would be a contradiction with the section on non-offenses. However, any unmade request at an unallowed time is simply a dukkaṭa. In 'bhinnena' (by a broken one), the instrumental case is in the sense of indicating a state. Or the meaning is 'by means of a break' or 'because of a break'; the instrumental case is in the sense of cause.

Ūnapañcabandhanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the training rule concerning a bowl with fewer than five bindings is finished.

3. Bhesajjasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

3. The Commentary on the Training Rule Concerning Medicine

620. “Sā [V 0.0240] ahosi suvaṇṇamālā”ti vacanato ṭhapetvā sahadhammike aññesaṃ yathāsukhaṃ rūpiyaṃ dātuṃ vaṭṭati uggaṇhāpetuṃ, sabyohārāpebhuñcāti ācariyo, vīmaṃsitabbaṃ iddhimassa iddhivisayattā.

620. Because of the phrase 'She became a golden garland,' the teacher said that, setting aside co-religionists, it is allowable for others to give silver as they wish, to have it accepted, and to have it used in trade. This should be investigated, as it is within the sphere of power of one with psychic power.

622. “Yesaṃ maṃsaṃ kappatī”ti vacanena yesaṃ maṃsaṃ na kappati, tesaṃ sappiādi kiñcāpi na kappati, na pana nissaggiyavatthūti veditabbaṃ. Tathā na paṇītabhojanavatthūti. Uggahitakaṃ katvā nikkhittanti ajjhoharaṇatthaṃ nikkhittaṃ. Itarañhi paṭiggahetvā ajjhoharituṃ vaṭṭati. Ubhayesampīti pacchābhattaṃ paṭiggahitehi, purebhattaṃ paṭiggahitehi ca katānaṃ. “Maṃsassa akappiyattā”ti kāraṇapatirūpakaṃ vatvā. Khādiṃsūti “vikāle [M 0.0269] kevalaṃ navanītameva khāditukāmena dadhitakkagatāni apanetabbāni, pacitukāmassa sāmaṃpākaṃ na hotīti therassa adhippāyo”ti vuttaṃ. “Khayaṃ gamissatī”ti vacanato khīraṃ pakkhipitvā pakkasappi vikāle kappatīti siddhaṃ. Bhesajjehīti yāvajīvikabhesajjehi. Katatelaṃ purebhattanti apacitvā kataṃ eva. Uṇhodakenāti tāpanabhāvaṃ dīpetīti keci, taṃ na sundaraṃ. Nibbaṭṭitattāti piññākādito. “Telatthāya paṭiggahita…pe… dukkaṭamevā”ti vacanato atelatthāya paṭiggahitehi, sattāhātikkantehipi katatelaṃ katadivasato paṭṭhāya sattāhaṃ vaṭṭatīti chāyā dissati, karamandaṃ rukkhasāroti keci.

622. By the statement, 'for whom meat is allowable,' it should be known that for those beings for whom meat is not allowable, although ghee and so forth derived from them are not allowable, they are not items to be forfeited (nissaggiya). Likewise, it should be known that they are not items of fine food (paṇītabhojana). 'Having taken it up and set it down' means set down for the purpose of consumption. As for the other kind, it is indeed allowable to receive and consume it. 'For both' refers to that made from items received after the meal and from items received before the meal. Having stated, 'Because of the unallowability of the meat,' as a semblance of a reason. Regarding 'They ate,' it is said: 'By one who wishes to eat only fresh butter at an improper time, the particles of curd and buttermilk should be removed; for one who wishes to cook, there is no self-cooking. This is the Elder's intention.' From the statement, 'It will spoil,' it is established that cooked ghee with milk added is allowable at an improper time. 'With medicines' means with lifelong medicines. 'Oil made before the meal' means simply that which is made without being cooked. Regarding 'with hot water,' some say it indicates a state of being hot, but that is not fitting. 'Because it is produced' means from oil-cake and so forth. From the statement, 'Received for the purpose of oil... it is only a dukkaṭa offense,' an implication is seen that oil made from items received for a purpose other than oil, even those that have passed seven days, is allowable for seven days starting from the day it was made. Some say that karamanda is tree pith.

623. Avasakasaṭe yasmā khīrādīni pakkhipitvā telaṃ pacanti, tasmā kasaṭaṃ na vaṭṭati, telameva vaṭṭati, tena vuttaṃ “pakkatelakasaṭe viya kukkuccāyatī”ti. Vasāya saddhiṃ pakkattā na vaṭṭatīti ce? Vadatha, bhante, navanīte dadhiguḷikātiādisambandho. Madhumhi cattāro kālikā yathāsambhavaṃ yojetabbā, ucchumhi ca, kathaṃ? Samakkhikaṃ seḷakaṃ madhu yāvakālikaṃ. Anelakaṃ udakasambhinnaṃ yāmakālikaṃ, asambhinnaṃ sattāhakālikaṃ, madhusiṭṭhaṃ parisuddhaṃ yāvajīvikaṃ. Tathā ucchu vā raso vā sakasaṭo yāvakāliko, nikkasaṭo udakasambhinno yāmakāliko, asambhinno sattāhakāliko, sukkhakasaṭaṃ yāvajīvikanti veditabbaṃ. Kasmā? Udakasambhedavisesato.

623. Because they cook oil by adding milk and other things into fat-less dregs, the dregs are not allowable; only the oil is allowable. Therefore, it is said: 'He has scruples as with cooked oil dregs.' If it is said that it is not allowable because of being cooked together with animal fat, one should state the connection, venerable sir, with the case of things like curd-lumps in fresh butter. In honey, the four time-limited allowances should be applied as is suitable, and in sugarcane as well. How? Honey containing bees and bee larvae is allowable for the morning. Honey without bee larvae, when mixed with water, is allowable for one watch; when unmixed, it is allowable for seven days. Pure beeswax is allowable for a lifetime. Similarly, sugarcane or its juice with dregs is allowable for the morning; without dregs and mixed with water, it is allowable for one watch; when unmixed, it is allowable for seven days. Dried dregs are allowable for a lifetime. Thus it should be known. Why? Because of the distinction of being mixed with water.

Kiṃ vuttaṃ hoti? Catūsu kālikesu pubbaṃ pubbaṃ garukaṃ, aparaṃ aparaṃ lahukaṃ. Tesu cāyaṃ udakasambhedo garukaṃ lahukaṃ karoti, lahukañca garukaṃ. Ambarasādīni hi yāvakālikattā [V 0.0241] garukāni, udakasambhedo pana tāni ambapānādisamaññaṃ datvā lahukāni yāmakālikāni karoti. “Phāṇitaṃ nāma ucchumhā nibbattanti ucchurasaṃ upādāyā”ti aṭṭhakathāvacanato ucchuraso sattāhakālikoti siddhaṃ. Tattha “udakasambhedo taṃ yāmakālikaṃ karotī”tiādiṃ bahuṃ vatvā yojitā.

What is said? Among the four time-limited allowances, the former are stricter and the latter are more lenient. Among them, this mixing with water makes the strict lenient, and the lenient strict. Indeed, things like mango juice are strict because they are allowable for the morning, but mixing with water, by giving them the designation of 'mango drink' and so on, makes them lenient and allowable for one watch. From the commentary's statement, 'Molasses is produced from sugarcane, taking sugarcane juice as its source,' it is established that sugarcane juice is allowable for seven days. There, the application is made after saying much, such as, 'mixing with water makes it allowable for one watch,' and so on.

Apicettha ucchuraso “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ucchurasa”nti (mahāva. 300) anuññātattā guḷodakaṃ viya ucchurasasāmaññato udakena asambhinnopi agilānassa [M 0.0270] vaṭṭati, tenevāha aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “ucchuraso nikasaṭo pacchābhattaṃ vaṭṭatī”ti (mahā. aṭṭha. 300). Ayaṃ sabbo no takkoti ācariyo. Keci panāhu “phāṇitaṃ nāma ucchumhā nibbatta’nti vacanato, ‘ucchurasaṃ upādāyā’ti aṭṭhakathāvacanato ca ucchuraso phāṇitameva, tasmā guḷe viya paṭipajjitabba”nti. Keci “vuttanayena sattāhakālikova samāno ‘anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ucchurasa’nti visuṃ anuññātattā asambhinnopi agilānassa vaṭṭatī”ti vadanti. Keci “vuttanayena visuṃ anuññātattā eva sambhinno vā asambhinno vā yāmakālikova, guḷodakaṃ pana sattāhakālikamevā”ti vadanti. Keci “guḷodakaṃ viya so duvidhopi sattāhakālikoyevā”ti vadanti.

Moreover, herein, sugarcane juice, because it was allowed by the words, “I allow, O monks, sugarcane juice,” is, like jaggery water, by virtue of being generally sugarcane juice, allowable for one who is not ill even if unmixed with water. For that very reason, it is said in the Commentary: “Sugarcane juice, if without dregs, is allowable after the meal.” This entire decision is our reasoning, thus says the teacher. Some, however, say: “Because of the Pali text which says, ‘Molasses is produced from sugarcane,’ and because of the word of the Commentary, ‘based on sugarcane juice,’ sugarcane juice is indeed molasses. Therefore, it should be treated like jaggery.” Some say: “By the aforesaid method, although it is a seven-day provision, because it is separately allowed with the words, ‘I allow, O monks, sugarcane juice,’ it is allowable for one who is not ill even if unmixed.” Some say: “By the aforesaid method, precisely because it is separately allowed, whether mixed or unmixed, it is indeed a one-watch provision; jaggery water, however, is indeed a seven-day provision.” Some say: “Like jaggery water, that sugarcane juice of both kinds is indeed a seven-day provision.”

Tatthāyaṃ paṭhamācariyavāde vicāraṇā – phāṇitānumatiyāyeva ucchurasānumatiyā siddhito visuṃ “ucchurasa”nti uddharitvā anumati niratthikāti āpajjati, tathā “ucchuraso nikasaṭo pacchābhattaṃ vaṭṭatī”ti aṭṭhakathāpi niratthikā. “Sattāhaṃ vaṭṭatī”ti vattabbaṃ siyāti, na ca tathā sakkā vattuṃ. Pacchābhattaṃ vaṭṭanakarasādhikārattāti ce? Na, tasmiṃ adhikāre sattāhakālikassa avattabbappasaṅgato. Kālabhedaṃ anapekkhitvā rasādhikāre otiṇṇattā vuttoti ce? Na sakkā “nikasaṭo sattāhaṃ vaṭṭatī”ti vattuṃ. Pacchābhattaṃ vaṭṭanakarasādhikārattā na vattabbanti ce? Na, evañhi vutte tadaññaraso viya ayampi pacchābhattameva vaṭṭati, na tato paranti āpajjati. Tato paraṃ aparibhogattā “pacchābhattaṃ vaṭṭatī”ti vuttanti ce? Na, yāvakālikabhāvappasaṅgato. Na so pasaṅgo ābhidosikassāpi ucchurasassa pākena phāṇitādibhāvappasaṅgato. Ayameva tatiyacatutthācariyavādesu vicāraṇā. Dutiyavāde vicāraṇā vuttā, vimaddo panettha bhesajjakkhandhake (mahāva. 300) āvi bhavissati. Phāṇitaṃ nāma ucchumhā nibbattanti madhukatālanāḷikeraphāṇitādito ukkaṭavatthuto nissaggiyavatthuphāṇitassa visesavacanaṃ, tenetaṃ paññāyati “nissaggiyavatthubhūtaṃ idha phāṇitaṃ nāma ucchumhā nibbattameva, na madhukādito nibbatta”nti. Ettāvatā yaṃkiñci ucchumhā nibbattaṃ[V 0.0242], na taṃ sabbaṃ phāṇitameva nāmāti sādhitaṃ hoti. Teneva khandhake phāṇitaṃ paṭhamaṃ anujānitvāva pacchā ucchuraso anuññāto, tathā tattheva guḷaṃ, guḷodakañca.

Herein is the examination of the first teacher's view: by the permission for molasses alone, since the permission for sugarcane juice is accomplished, it follows that a separate permission, having extracted the term 'sugarcane juice,' is pointless. Likewise, the commentary stating, 'Unstrained sugarcane juice is allowable after the meal,' would also be pointless. It should be said, 'It is allowable for seven days,' but it cannot be said so. If it is said that this is because it falls under the category of juices allowable after the meal? No, because in that category, it would follow that a seven-day allowable is not to be mentioned. If it is said that it is stated thus because it is included in the category of juices without regard to the difference in time-period? It cannot be said, 'Unstrained sugarcane juice is allowable for seven days.' If it is said that it is not stated thus because it falls under the category of juices allowable after the meal? No, for if it were said so, it would follow that this juice, like other juices, is allowable only after the meal, and not beyond that. If it is said, 'It is allowable after the meal' because it is not consumed beyond that? No, because this would lead to the consequence of it being a yāvakālika item. That consequence would not arise, because even for sugarcane juice that is left overnight, through cooking, it would follow that it attains the state of molasses and so on. This very same is the examination in the views of the third and fourth teachers. The examination of the second view has been stated; the detailed analysis of this will become clear in the Chapter on Medicines (Mahāvagga 300). The phrase, 'Molasses is what is produced from sugarcane,' is a specific statement distinguishing the molasses that is a Nissaggiya item from items of wrong-doing (dukkata) such as molasses from the madhuka tree, palmyra, coconut, and so on. By this it is understood: 'Here, what is called molasses that has become a Nissaggiya item is only that produced from sugarcane, not that produced from madhuka, etc.' By this much, it is established that not everything produced from sugarcane is called 'molasses'. For that very reason, in the Khandhaka, having first allowed molasses, sugarcane juice was allowed afterwards; similarly, in that same place, jaggery and jaggery-water were also allowed.

Ucchurasaṃ [M 0.0271] upādāya apakkā vātiādimhi pana yesaṃ laddhi “ucchuraso yāmakāliko”ti. “Te apakkā vāti sāmaṃ bhikkhunā apakkā vā. Avatthukapakkā vāti vinā vatthunā pakkā vā”ti atthaṃ vaṇṇayanti, taṃ na yuttaṃ “ucchurasaṃ upādāyā”ti imassa vacanassa payojanābhāvappasaṅgato, bhikkhuno pacanādhikārābhāvā. Sāmapāko idhādhippetoti ce? Sāmaṃ apakkassa ucchurasassa tesaṃ attanomatiyā phāṇitabhāvasiddhito ca parato “purebhattaṃ paṭiggahitena aparissāvitaucchurasena kataphāṇita”ntiādinayadassanato ca taṃ ayuttaṃ, tattha “aparissāvitaucchurasena sayaṃkataṃ nirāmisameva vaṭṭatī”ti vacanaṃ yaṃ tattha kasaṭaṃ sāmapākaṃ na janeti, savatthukapaṭiggahitakataṃyeva taṃ karotīti dīpeti, tasmā paṭiggahetuṃ na vaṭṭati vikāleti porāṇā. “Koṭṭitaucchuphāṇitaṃ ‘rajanapākaṃ viya oḷārikaṃ savatthukapakkaṃ nāma hotī’ti saññāya purebhattameva vaṭṭatī”ti vuttaṃ. Mahāaṭṭhakathācariyā “evaṃ phāṇitaggahaṇaṃ amadhuraṃ, tasmā pacchābhattaṃ na vaṭṭatī”ti vadiṃsu. Kiṃ madhuratāya, amadhuratāya vāti? Atthameva dassetuṃ mahāpaccariyaṃ tathā vuttanti upatissatthero āha kira. Taṃ yuttanti ucchuto nibbattattā vuttaṃ, tenevāha “khaṇḍasakkharaṃ pana…pe… vaṭṭatī”ti. “Taṃ khīraghaṭe pakkhipitvā pacantī”ti likhitaṃ. Jallikā nāma pheṇādi.

Regarding the phrase '`ucchurasaṃ upādāya apakkā vā`' and so on, there are those whose view is that 'sugarcane juice is a `yāmakālika`.' They explain '`apakkā vā`' as 'uncooked by the monk himself,' or '`avatthukapakkā vā`' as 'cooked without a substance.' This is not suitable, as it would follow that the phrase '`ucchurasaṃ upādāya`' has no purpose, and that a monk has no authority to cook. If it is said that self-cooking is intended here, that is unsuitable, both because, by their own opinion, uncooked sugarcane juice is established as being molasses, and because of the method shown later, such as 'molasses made from unstrained sugarcane juice received before the meal,' and so on. Therein, the statement 'what is made by oneself from unstrained sugarcane juice is allowable only when unmixed with other provisions' indicates that the dregs therein do not constitute an act of self-cooking; rather, it renders it as something made after having been received together with its substance. Therefore, the ancients say it is not allowable to receive it at an improper time. It is said: 'Molasses from pounded sugarcane is allowable only before the meal, with the perception that "like the cooking of dye, it is coarse and is called 'cooked with substance'"'. The teachers of the Mahā-aṭṭhakathā said, 'Thus, the acceptance of molasses that is not sweet is not allowable after the meal.' What does it matter whether it is sweet or not sweet? The Elder Upatissa reportedly said that it was stated thus in the Mahāpaccarī just to show the meaning. That is suitable; it is said because it is produced from sugarcane. For that very reason, he said, 'But sugar candy... is allowable.' It is written, 'They cook it by putting it in a pot of milk.' `Jallikā` means foam and so on.

Bhesajjodisaṃ vadantena itare atthuddhāravasena vuttā. “Āhāratthaṃ pharituṃ samatthānī”ti khandhake (mahāva. 260) “yaṃ bhesajjañceva assa bhesajjasammatañca lokassa, āhāratthañca phareyyā”ti vuttattā vuttaṃ. Ettha vicāraṇā bhesajjakkhandhake āvi bhavissati.

By the one who spoke the designation of medicine, the other designations are stated by way of extracting their meaning. The phrase 'capable of serving the purpose of nourishment' is stated because it is said in the Khandhaka (Mahāvagga 260): 'Whatever is both a medicine and is considered a medicine by the world, and would also serve the purpose of nourishment.' Herein, the detailed investigation will become manifest in the Bhesajjakkhandhaka (Chapter on Medicine).

624. Dvāravātapānakavāṭānīti dvārassa ca vātapānānañca kavāṭāni. Kasāvapakkhepamattena hi tāni attano sabhāvaṃ pariccajitāni honti, tasmā “makkhetabbānī”ti vuttaṃ. “Kasāvo nāma kanakalambādīnipī”ti vadanti. Adhiṭṭhetīti “idāni ajjhoharaṇīyaṃ na bhavissati, bāhiraparibhogo bhavissatī”ti cittaṃ uppādeti. Idha “vikappetī”ti padaṃ natthi. Adhiṭṭhānampi mukhāruḷhiyā vuttaṃ “imaṃ navanītaṃ adhiṭṭhāmī”ti avattabbato.

624. `Dvāravātapānakavāṭāni` means the shutters of the door and of the windows. For, by the mere application of an astringent dye, they abandon their own nature; therefore, it is said, 'they should be smeared.' They say, 'An astringent dye also includes things like golden-colored liquid extracts and so on.' 'He determines' means he gives rise to the thought, 'Now this will not be for consumption; it will be for external use.' Here, the word 'vikappeti' is not found. The determination is also stated by way of common parlance, because 'I determine this fresh butter' should not be said.

625. Paribhuñjituṃ [M 0.0272] pana na vaṭṭatīti vissāsābhāvaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Sace savissāso, vaṭṭatīti [V 0.0243] “paribhuñja tva”nti ettāvatā vissajjitaṃ hoti, tasmā ubhinnaṃ anāpattīti sambandho. Sace na vissajjitaṃ, āpatti hotīti siddhaṃ. Tasmā ubhinnaṃ santakaṃ cīvaraṃ aññatarena sammukhībhūtena adhiṭṭhātabbaṃ. No ce adhiṭṭhāti, nissaggiyaṃ hotītipi yujjati. Kākanikamattañce mūlaṃ adinnaṃ, “na adhiṭṭhānupagaṃ…pe… sakabhāvaṃ na upetī”ti iminā etaṃ sadisaṃ na hoti, ābhidhammikagaṇānaṃ dinnaṃ viya ca na hoti. Kasmā? Ābhidhammikā hi anupasampannāpi honti, pacchā ābhidhammikabhūtānampi taṃ sādhāraṇaṃ hotīti. Ettha dvepi upasampannā eva, dvinnampi tattha yathākāmakaraṇīyatā atthi mamattañca, na evaṃ tadaññesaṃ sādhāraṇaṃ, na ca dve tayo bhikkhū “ekato vassissāmā”ti karonti, rakkhati tāva. “Avibhattattā anāpattī”ti iminā ca idaṃ sadisaṃ, yena mūlena paṭiggahitaṃ, tassa sace itaro deti, so vā taṃ itarassa deti, sati paṭiggahaṇe sattāhātikkame nissaggiyattā, tasmā taṃ cīvaraṃ dvīsu sammukhībhūtena ekena adhiṭṭhātabbaṃ. Kiñcāpi ettha payogo na dissati samānaparikkhārānaṃ dvinnaṃ adhiṭṭhānapayogābhāvato, tathāpi samānasabbabhaṇḍakānaṃ dvinnaṃ telādi yena paṭiggahitaṃ, tassa kālātikkame āpattisambhavato, anadhiṭṭhāne dullabhavisesahetuttā ca “adhiṭṭhātabba”nti vuttaṃ. Taṃ ayuttaṃ pattacīvarasattāhakālikānaṃ asadisavidhānattā. Ettha pattacīvarañhi attano santakabhāvaṃ upagatameva anadhiṭṭhahantassa kālātikkame āpatti, sattāhakālikaṃ pana parasantakasādhāraṇampi paṭiggahitaṃ paṭiggāhakassa kālātikkame āpattikaraṃ. Paṭiggahaṇañcettha pamāṇaṃ, na tattha sakasantakatā, sattāhakālikañca nissaggiyaṃ, sabbesampi anajjhoharaṇīyaṃ. Pattacīvaraṃ aññassa paribhuñjato anāpatti. Idañca kālātikkantampi nissajjitvā pacchā laddhaṃ kappati. Pattacīvaraṃ pana taṃ tassa vinayakammanti kappatīti. Avibhattassapi imassa dānaṃ ruhati, na pattacīvarassa. Vuttañhetaṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “dvinnaṃ santakaṃ hoti…pe… sacepi avibhajitvā saddhivihārikādīnaṃ denti, adinnameva hotī”ti. Yassa dānameva na ruhati, tassa kuto adhiṭṭhānaṃ. Eko ce pattacīvaraṃ dasame divase itarassa deti. Tato paṭṭhāya so dasa divase pariharituṃ labhati[M 0.0273], na tathā sattāhakālikanti sabbathā upaparikkhiyamānaṃ sarikkhaṃ nakkhamatīti na taṃ sārato daṭṭhabbanti ācariyassa takko. “Vinayakammavasena pana anissajjitvā sahasā virujjhitvā kassaci pariccattampi puna paṭilabhitvā paribhuñjituṃ na vaṭṭatī”ti vuttaṃ, sace desantaritaṃ, samuddantaritaṃ vā cīvaraṃ nissaggiyaṃ jātaṃ, taṃ idha ṭhitena bhikkhunā ekassa vantena cittena cattaṃ katvā anapekkhitvā āpattiṃ desetvā tassa vissāsena puna gahetvā adhiṭṭhātabbaṃ, “pattādīsu ca ayameva nayo”ti ca vuttaṃ, “tālanāḷikeraphāṇitampi sattāhakālikaṃ evā”ti ca. “Dvinnaṃ santakaṃ ekena paṭiggahitaṃ sattāhakālikaṃ sattāhātikkame āpattiṃ na karoti[V 0.0244], paribhuñjituṃ pana dvinnampi na vaṭṭatī”ti ca “parasantakaṃ paṭiggahetvā ṭhapitepi eseva nayo”ti ca keci vadanti. Dukkaṭavatthubhūtaṃ sappiādi nissajjitabbaṃ puna paribhuñjituṃ vaṭṭatīti vidhānaṃ na dissatīti.

625. “However, it is not permissible to use it”—this was stated with reference to the absence of familiarity. If there is familiarity, it is permissible. Thus, by saying, “You may use it,” it is considered relinquished, and so there is no offense for either. If it is not relinquished, an offense occurs—this is established. Therefore, a robe belonging to both should be formally determined by one who is present. If one does not determine it, it becomes forfeitable—this is also reasonable. If even a capital share the size of a kākaṇika has not been given, this case is not similar to the statement, “It is not subject to determination… it does not attain the state of being one's own,” nor is it like something given to groups of Abhidhamma scholars. Why? Because Abhidhamma scholars can even be unordained, and later, that item remains common property even for those who become Abhidhamma scholars. Here, both are ordained monks, and both have the right to act as they wish concerning it, and a sense of ownership; it is not in this way common property for others, nor do two or three monks make an agreement, saying, “We will spend the rains retreat together”; for the time being, it is protected. And this case is similar to the statement, “Because it is undivided, there is no offense.” By whichever person it was received with the capital, if the other gives his share to him, or if that person gives it to the other, upon this receiving, it becomes forfeitable with the passing of seven days. Therefore, that robe should be determined by one of the two who is present. Although in this case a procedure is not seen—due to the absence of the procedure of determination for the shared requisites of two monks—nevertheless, it is said, “It should be determined,” because for two who share all items, if oil and so on are received by one, an offense can occur for him when the time passes, and because not determining it is a cause for a rare, special case. That is unsuitable, because the regulations for bowls and robes, and for seven-day medicaments, are not similar. Here, a bowl or robe that has indeed attained the state of being one's own property incurs an offense for the one who does not determine it when the time passes. A seven-day medicament, however, even if it is common property with another, when received, causes an offense for the receiver when the time passes. And in this case, the act of receiving is the standard, not personal ownership. And a seven-day medicament is forfeitable; it is not to be consumed by any monk. There is no offense for someone who uses another's bowl or robe. And this item, even if the time has passed, is allowable if it is received again after having been forfeited. A bowl or robe, however, is allowable for that person as a formal act of discipline. The giving of this seven-day medicament is valid even if it is undivided, but not so for a bowl or robe. For this is stated in the commentary: “It is the property of two… if they give it to co-residents and others without dividing it, it is as if not given.” For one whose very act of giving is not valid, how can there be determination? If one monk gives a bowl or robe to another on the tenth day, from that day onward, that monk may keep it for ten days; it is not so for a seven-day medicament. Thus, when thoroughly examined in every way, the comparison is not tenable. Therefore, that should not be regarded as the essential point—this is the teacher’s reasoning. But it has been said: “Even if given up to someone after hastily quarreling, without having forfeited it by means of a formal act of discipline, it is not allowable to get it back and use it.” If a robe has become forfeitable because it is in another region or across an ocean, a monk who is here should, with a mind that has relinquished it, having made it abandoned and without regard for it, confess the offense, and then, through familiarity with him, take it back again and determine it. And it has been said: “This same method applies to bowls and so on,” and, “Even palmyra and coconut molasses are indeed seven-day medicaments.” And some say: “A seven-day medicament belonging to two, received by one, does not create an offense when seven days pass, but it is not allowable for either to use it,” and, “This same method applies even when another's property is received and stored.” A regulation stating that ghee and so on, which has become the basis for a dukkaṭa offense, should be forfeited and is then allowable to be used again, is not seen.

Bhesajjasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule concerning medicines is concluded.

4. Vassikasāṭikasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

4. The Explanation of the Training Rule Concerning the Rainy-Season Robe

627. “Ekameva katvā”ti vacanena vassikasāṭikalakkhaṇena ñātakānampi satuppādaṃ karontena ekameva gahetabbanti dhammasiritthero. Catubbidhaṃ khettanti ettha kiñcāpi tividhaṃ dissati, taṃ pana evaṃ gahetabbaṃ, yasmiṃ khette pariyesituṃ labhati, taṃ pariyesanakhettaṃ nāma, “evaṃ karaṇanivāsanādhiṭṭhānakhettānipī”ti vuttaṃ. Ettha pacchimena purimaggāho veditabbo, na purimena pacchimaggāho, yathālābhanti ācariyo. Tassattho – adhiṭṭhānakhettena pacchimena purimānaṃ tiṇṇaṃ gāho hoti, tathā nivāsanakhettena dvinnaṃ purimānaṃ. Karaṇakhettena pana ekasseva purimassa gāho hotīti. Ettha pana kiñcāpi karaṇakhettanivāsanakhettānaṃ kālato nānattaṃ natthi, kiriyato pana “aṭṭhiṃ katvā nivāsetabba”nti pāḷivacanato, tasmā dvidhā katvā vuttaṃ aññatarābhāvena, tadatthasiddhito ca, kathaṃ panettha nānattaṃ natthīti paññāyatīti ce? Pāḷito, “aḍḍhamāso seso gimhānanti katvā nivāsetabba”nti hi pāḷi, tathā mātikāṭṭhakathāto (kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. vassikasāṭikasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā) ca.

627. The Elder Dhammasiri says that by the phrase 'Only one having been made,' and by the characteristic of a rainy-season robe, a monk who causes mindfulness to arise even for his relatives should accept only one. Regarding 'the fourfold field,' although a threefold one appears here, it should be understood thus: the field in which one is able to search is called the searching field. It is said, 'Likewise are the making, wearing, and determination fields.' Here, the inclusion of the former by the latter should be understood, not the inclusion of the latter by the former; it is 'according to what is obtained,' says the teacher. Its meaning is this: by the determination field, which is the last, there is the inclusion of the three former fields. Likewise, by the wearing field, there is the inclusion of the two former fields. But by the making field, there is the inclusion of only the one former field. Here, although there is no difference in terms of time between the making field and the wearing field, there is a difference in terms of action, due to the Pāli statement, 'Having made it firm, it should be worn.' Therefore, it is spoken of as twofold. And due to the absence of one or the other, and because the purpose of that is established, if it is asked, 'How is it known that there is no difference here?' It is known from the Pāli. Indeed, there is the Pāli text: 'Thinking, “Half a month of the hot season remains,” it should be worn,' and likewise from the Mātikāṭṭhakathā.

Tathāha [M 0.0274] “pacchimo aḍḍhamāso karaṇanivāsanakhettampī”ti, iminā nayena tividhameva khettantipi siddhaṃ. Samantapāsādikāyaṃ pana katthaci potthake “jeṭṭhamūlapuṇṇamāsiyā pacchimapāṭipadadivasato paṭṭhāya yāva kāḷapakkhuposatho, ayameko addhamāso pariyesanakhettañceva karaṇakhettañca. Etasmiñhi antare vassikasāṭikaṃ aladdhaṃ pariyesituṃ, laddhaṃ kātuñca vaṭṭati, nivāsetuṃ, adhiṭṭhātuñca na vaṭṭatī”ti pāṭho dissati, so apāṭho yathāvuttapāḷimātikāṭṭhakathāvirodhato, tasmā tattha “aladdhaṃ pariyesituṃ vaṭṭati, kātuṃ, nivāsetuṃ, adhiṭṭhātuñca na vaṭṭatī”ti pāṭho veditabbo. Evaṃ tāva pacchimena purimaggāhasiddhi veditabbā, na purimena karaṇakhettādīnaṃ gāho sambhavati. “Māso seso gimhānanti vassikasāṭikacīvaraṃ pariyesitabba”nti ettakameva hi vuttaṃ, na, aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “ayameko addhamāso pariyesanakhettañceva karaṇakhettañcā”ti vuttattāti ce? Na, tassa lekhanadosattā[V 0.0245], tathā sādhitaṃ. Karaṇakhettena pana nivāsanakhettaggāho atthi kālanānattābhāvato, teneva pubbe yathālābhaggahaṇaṃ kataṃ, tathā ca sādhitameva, na bhedo panatthi, payojanaṃ vuttameva. Nivāsanakkhettena adhiṭṭhānakkhettaggāho natthi eva, na hi purimena pacchimaggāho veditabbo. Na pāḷivirodhatoti ce? Na, tadatthājānanato. “Māso seso gimhānanti addhamāso seso gimhāna”nti ettha iti-saddassa hi ito paṭṭhāyāti attho. Parato āpattikhettadassanato itarassa anāpattikhettabhāvo dassitova hoti. Dinnapubbatopi ñātakapavāritaṭṭhānato nipphādentassa nissaggiyaṃ piṭṭhisamayattā, pakatiyā vassikasāṭikadāyakā nāma saṅghassa vā puggalassa vā apavāretvā anusaṃvaccharaṃ dentā, tattha satuppādova vaṭṭati. Vattabhede dukkaṭanti tadaññesu.

For thus it is said: 'The latter half-month is also the field for making and wearing,' and by this method, the threefold field is also established. However, in some manuscripts of the Samantapāsādikā, this reading is seen: 'From the day after the full moon of Jeṭṭhamūla until the Uposatha of the dark fortnight, this one half-month is both the field for searching and the field for making. During this interval, it is permissible to search for the rainy-season robe if not yet obtained and to make it if obtained, but it is not permissible to wear it or to determine it.' That is an incorrect reading because it contradicts the aforesaid Pāli, Mātikā, and Commentary. Therefore, the reading there should be understood as: 'It is permissible to search for it if not obtained, but it is not permissible to make it, wear it, or determine it.' Thus, firstly, it should be understood that the inclusion of the earlier periods by the latter period is established; the inclusion of the field for making and so on by the earlier period is not possible. For it is only said, 'When a month of the hot season remains, the rainy-season robe is to be sought.' If one were to say this is not so because it is stated in the commentary, 'This one half-month is both the field for searching and the field for making,' the reply is: No, because that is a scribal error; it has been established thus. However, by the field for making, the inclusion of the field for wearing exists, due to the absence of a difference in time. For that very reason, the phrase 'according to what is received' was used previously, and thus it has been established. There is no difference, and the purpose has already been stated. By the field for wearing, the inclusion of the field for determination does not exist at all, for indeed, the inclusion of the latter by the former is not to be understood. If one were to say, 'Is it not due to contradiction with the Pāli?' The reply is: No, it is due to not knowing its meaning. Here, regarding the phrase 'When a month of the hot season remains,' the word 'iti' has the meaning 'from this point onward,' thus implying 'when a half-month of the hot season remains.' Because the field of offense is shown later, the state of the other as a field of non-offense is thereby shown. Even if previously given, for one who has it made from a place of relatives or an invited place, it is a nissaggiya offense, due to it being the piṭṭhisamaya (post-period). By nature, those called 'donors of the rainy-season robe' are those who give annually to the Sangha or to an individual without being invited. In that case, only causing mindfulness to arise is proper. In case of a breach of practice, there is a dukkaṭa offense; this applies in the case of others.

“Sace kata…pe… vassūpanāyikadivase adhiṭṭhātabbā…pe… cha māse parihāraṃ labhatī”ti vacanato antovassepi yāva vassānassa pacchimadivasā akatā parihāraṃ labhatīti dīpitaṃ hoti. Kasmā na vicāritanti ce? Atthāpattisiddhattā. “Cha māse parihāraṃ labhatī”ti vacanena akatā labhatīti siddhameva, taṃ kiñcāpi siddhaṃ, sarūpena pana anāgatattā sarūpena dassetuṃ, dussaddhāpayattā upapattito dassetuñca idamāraddhaṃ [M 0.0275] ācariyena, “yathā cettha, evaṃ kathinabbhantare uppannacīvarampi heṭṭhā vuttanayeneva paṭipajjitabba”nti anugaṇṭhipade vuttaṃ, taṃ duvuttaṃ tattheva pubbāparavirodhato. Yañcettha aṭṭhakathāvacanaṃ sādhakattena vuttaṃ, taṃ tamatthaṃ na sādheti. “Yadi nappahoti yāva kattikapuṇṇamā parihāraṃ labhatī”ti vacanaṃ appahontassa yāva kattikapuṇṇamā tāva parihārakhettaṃ, tato paraṃ ekadivasopi na hotīti dīpeti, tasmā appahonakabhāvena akatāva yāva kattikapuṇṇamā parihāraṃ labhati, tato paraṃ na labhatīti siddhaṃ. Tathā tadeva vacanaṃ kataparihāraṃ na labhatīti dīpeti, tasmā kattikapuṇṇamadivaseyeva adhiṭṭhātabbā. “Appahonte dasāhe antovasse karaṇapariyosānaṃyeva pamāṇa”nti likhitaṃ.

Because of the statement, 'If made… on the day of entering the rains-residence, it should be determined… one obtains the privilege for six months,' it is thereby shown that even within the rains-residence, if it is not made by the last day of the rains-residence, one obtains the privilege. If it is asked, 'Why is this not investigated?' Because it is established by implication. By the statement, 'one obtains the privilege for six months,' it is indeed established that if it is not made, one obtains it. Although that is established, this was undertaken by the teacher in order to state it explicitly, since it had not been stated explicitly, and to demonstrate it through reasoning, because it is difficult to inspire belief. What was said in the Anugaṇṭhipada, 'Just as here, so too, a robe that has arisen within the kathina period should be dealt with only by the method stated below,' is poorly stated because of the contradiction between the earlier and later parts in that very text. And the statement from the commentary cited here as proof does not accomplish that purpose. The statement, 'If it is not sufficient, one obtains the privilege until the full moon of Kattika,' indicates that for one for whom it is not sufficient, the period of privilege lasts until the full moon of Kattika, and not even a single day beyond. Therefore, it is established that due to the state of insufficiency, if it is not made, one obtains the privilege until the full moon of Kattika, but not beyond. Likewise, that very statement indicates that the privilege is not obtained if it has been made use of; therefore, it should be determined only on the day of the full moon of Kattika. It is written, 'When there is insufficiency, within ten days during the rains-residence, the completion of the making itself is the measure.'

Etthāha – “ekāhadvīhādivasenā”tiādi na vattabbaṃ. Kasmā? Gimhadivasānaṃ anadhiṭṭhānakālattā, tasmā eva “antodasāhe vā tadaheyeva vā adhiṭṭhātabbā’ti ca sāmaññato na vattabbaṃ gimhadivasānaṃ adhiṭṭhānakhettabhāvappasaṅgato”ti. Ettha vuccati – na, tadatthājānanato. Dasāhānāgatāya vassūpanāyikāya gimhadivasā dasāhā honti, paṭhamadivase ca laddhā niṭṭhitā vassikasāṭikā dasāhātikkantāpi vassūpanāyikadivasaṃ adhiṭṭhānakhettaṃ appattattā [V 0.0246] na ca tāva nissaggiyaṃ hoti, vuttañcetaṃ “vassūpanāyikato pubbe dasāhātikkamepi anāpattī”ti.

Here, an objector says: '“By way of one day, two days, etc.” and so on should not be said. Why? Because the days of the hot season are not a time for determination. Therefore, the general statement “it should be determined within ten days or on that very day” should not be said, because it would follow that the days of the hot season are a period for determination.' Here, the reply is given: No, this is due to not understanding its meaning. For the commencement of the rains-residence that has not yet arrived within ten days, the hot-season days are those ten days. And if a rains-cloth is obtained and completed on the first day, even if ten days have passed, since the period for determination—the day of commencing the rains-residence—has not been reached, it is not yet subject to forfeiture. And this has been said: “Even if ten days are exceeded before commencing the rains-residence, there is no offense.”

Antodasāhe adhiṭṭhātabbāti idaṃ na avisesena etasmiṃ antare gimhadivasepi adhiṭṭhātabbanti imamatthaṃ dīpetuṃ vuttaṃ, kintu gimhadivase ce uppannā, adhiṭṭhānakhette ca antodasāhaṃ hoti, antodasāhe khetteyeva adhiṭṭhātabbā, na khettanti katvā dasāhaṃ atikkamitabbanti dīpetuṃ vuttaṃ. Kasmā? Gimhadivasānampi gaṇanūpagattā, tasmā akhettadivasepi gaṇetvā khette eva “antodasāhe adhiṭṭhātabbā”ti vuttaṃ hotīti.

The statement, “It should be determined within ten days,” was not said to indicate this meaning without distinction: that it should be determined even on a hot-season day within this interval. But rather, it was said to indicate this: if a rains-cloth arises on a hot-season day, and the period for determination is within ten days, it should be determined only within that ten-day period; one should not exceed the ten days by considering it not to be the period. Why? Because even the hot-season days are included in the count. Therefore, having counted even the days that are not the period, it is said, “It should be determined within the ten days only within the period.” Thus it should be understood.

Vassikasāṭikasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the training rule concerning the rains-cloth is finished.

5. Cīvaraacchindanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

5. The Commentary on the Training Rule on Snatching a Robe

632. Sāmanti [M 0.0276] sakasaññitāniyamanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Sakasaññitāyeva hi acchindāpanaacchindanesu nissaggiyaṃ, tasmā nissaggiyamūlaṅganidassanametaṃ. “Cīvara”nti vuttattā “acīvaraṃ acchindantassa na nissaggiya”nti vuttameva hoti. “Datvāti datvā vā dāpetvā vā”ti kiñcāpi padabhājanaṃ yujjati, aññassa pana santakaṃ aññassa bhikkhuno dāpetvā taṃ sayaṃ vā acchindeyya, teneva vā acchindāpeyyāti aniṭṭhappasaṅgabhayā na vuttaṃ, atthato pana attano santakaṃ aññena saddhivihārikādinā dāpetvā, aññassa santakaṃ vā tassa vissāsā dāpetvā taṃ acchindeyya vā acchindāpeyya vā nissaggiyanti veditabbaṃ, tañca kho anapekkho datvā. Yadi evaṃ “cajitvā dinnaṃ acchinditvā gaṇhanto bhaṇḍagghena kāretabbo”ti idaṃ kinti ce? Sakasaññāya aggahetvā aññāya theyyāya gaṇhantaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ, teneva vuttaṃ “sakasaññāya gahitattā panassa pārājikaṃ natthī”ti, apica “anāpatti so vā deti, tassa vā vissasanto gaṇhātī”ti vacanatopi taṃ siddhameva. Ettāvatā tāvakālikaṃ katvā dinnaṃ acchindantassa anāpatti sādhitā hoti. “Amhākaṃ santike upajjhaṃ gaṇhissatī”tiādivacanaṃ sāmaṇerassa dānaṃ dīpeti, tañca idha nādhippetaṃ. Pāḷiyaṃ (pārā. 633-634) upasampanne tikapācittiyaṃ viya anupasampanne tikadukkaṭampi āgatanti ce? Na, tadadhippāyājānanato. Anupasampannakāle evaṃ datvā aññassa santike upasampannaṃ disvā kupito ce acchindati, upasampannasseva vā “sikkhaṃ paccakkhāya tumhākaṃ santike [V 0.0247] upasampajjissāmī”ti vadantassa datvā puna acchindati ce, nissaggiyanti ayamettha adhippāyo.

632. The word `sāmaṃ` (oneself) is stated for the purpose of defining the perception of it as one's own property. For it is only with the perception of it as one's own property that in cases of causing to snatch back or snatching back, it is an offense of relinquishment. Therefore, this is an illustration of the root-factor of the offense of relinquishment. Since 'robe' is stated, it is indeed stated that 'for one who snatches back what is not a robe, there is no offense of relinquishment'. Although the word-analysis '`datvā` means having given oneself or having caused another to give' is suitable, it was not stated due to the fear of the undesirable implication that one might cause another's property to be given to another bhikkhu and then snatch it back oneself, or cause it to be snatched back by that very one. In terms of meaning, however, it should be known that if one causes one's own property to be given by another, such as a co-resident, or causes another's property to be given through trust in that person, and then snatches it back or causes it to be snatched back, it is an offense of relinquishment; and this is when it was given without expectation of return. If so, what then is this statement: 'One who, having relinquished it, snatches back what was given, should be dealt with according to the value of the goods'? It was said in reference to one who takes it not with the perception of it as one's own, but with a different perception, that of theft. For that very reason it was said: 'But because it was taken with the perception of it as one's own, there is no pārājika offense for him.' Furthermore, from the statement, 'There is no offense if he gives it, or if one takes it trusting him,' this is indeed established. By this much, the absence of an offense is established for one who snatches back what was given on a temporary basis. The statement 'He will take a preceptor in our presence,' and so forth, indicates a gift to a novice, and that is not intended here. If one should say: 'Just as in the Pāḷi for an ordained person there is a `tikapācittiya`, for an unordained person a `tikadukkaṭa` also is found,' the answer is no, because of not knowing the meaning of that Pāḷi. If, having given thus while he was unordained, one sees him become ordained in the presence of another and, being angry, snatches it back; or if, having given to an ordained person himself who says, 'Having renounced the training, I will become ordained in your presence,' one then snatches it back, it is an offense of relinquishment. This is the meaning here.

633. Sakiṃ āṇatto bahukampi acchindati, nissaggiyanti ekabaddhattā ekaṃ pācittiyaṃ, taṃ sandhāyetaṃ vuttaṃ “āṇatto bahūni gaṇhāti, ekaṃ pācittiya”nti. Mātikāṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana “vatthugaṇanāya āpattiyo”ti vuttaṃ, taṃ āṇattiyā bahuttā “sabbāni gaṇhā”ti vadantassa gāhaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ, teneva tattha vuttaṃ “ekavācāya sambahulā āpattiyo”ti. Evaṃ sante pāḷivacanaṃ, aṭṭhakathāvacanadvayañca aññamaññaṃ sameti, parasantakampi nissaggiyaṃ hoti paṃsukūlañca, tena “dussante baddharūpiyaṃ viyā”ti vuttaṃ, taṃ [M 0.0277] tadatthaniyamadassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ, yathāvachāditaṃ acchindanacittena sacittakaṃ, vacīkammaṃ pana kevalaṃ acchindāpentasseva “dehī”ti balakkārena gaṇhatopi veditabbaṃ, taṃ na yuttaṃ “anāpatti so vā detī”ti vacanato. “Tuṭṭho vā duṭṭho vā deti, anāpattiyevā”ti mātikāṭṭhakathāvacanato vāti ce? Na, ubhayattha attano ruciyā dānaṃ sandhāya vuttattā, pasayhāvahāre anāpattippasaṅgato ca. “Bhikkhussa sāmaṃ cīvaraṃ datvā’ti pāḷivacanato ca mātikāṭṭhakathāya aṅgavavatthāne ‘upasampannatā’ti vuttattā ca ubhayattha dānaharaṇesu bhikkhubhāvo icchitabboti dīpetī”ti vadanti, idamayuttanti no takkoti ācariyo. Kasmā? Anupasampannassa cīvaraṃ datvā taṃ upasampannakāle acchindantassa anāpattippasaṅgato. “Anupasampannassa cīvaraṃ vā aññaṃ vā parikkhāraṃ datvā…pe… āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti vacanato dukkaṭaṃ tattha hotīti ce? Nāsiddhattā, dānakāle eva upasampannatā pamāṇanti asiddhametaṃ aṭṭhakathāya vā pāḷiyā vā yuttito vā, tasmā taṃ na yuttanti attho. Anupasampannassa cīvaraṃ datvā tasseva anupasampannakāleyeva cīvaraṃ acchindantassa dukkaṭaṃ, upasampannakāle vā datvā anupasampannakāle acchindantassa dukkaṭanti tassa vacanassa idaṃ vikappantarañca sambhavati, tasmā (pārā. 631 ādayo) vikappantarassa sambhavato ca na yuttaṃ, yasmā anupasampannakāle datvā upasampannakāle acchindantassa visuṃ dukkaṭaṃ na paññattaṃ, tasmā purāṇacīvaradhovāpanādisikkhāpadesu viya aparabhāge upasampannatā cettha pamāṇaṃ, tasmā “upasampannatā”ti aṅgesu vuttattā ca taṃ na yuttanti attho. Ettha “paccāsīsantasseva dānamadhippetaṃ, na nissaṭṭhadāna”nti dhammasiritthero vadati kira, vīmaṃsitabbaṃ.

633. If, having been commanded once, one snatches away even many robes, it is an offense of relinquishment. Here, because they are bound as one, it is one pācittiya offense. In reference to that, this was stated: 'Having been commanded, one takes many; it is one pācittiya offense.' In the Mātikāṭṭhakathā, however, it is stated: 'Offenses are according to the count of the objects.' That was said in reference to the taking by one who says, 'Take all,' due to the command being for many items. For that very reason, it is stated there: 'By one utterance, there are many offenses.' This being so, the statement of the Pāḷi and the two statements of the commentary are in agreement with each other. What belongs to another can become an offense of relinquishment, as can dust-heap cloth. Therefore, it was said, 'Like money bound in the corner of a cloth.' That was said for the purpose of showing the rule for that meaning. It is intentional when done with a mind to snatch away what is concealed. However, the verbal action should be understood to apply not only to one who causes another to snatch away, but also to one who takes by force, saying, 'Give!' That is not correct, on account of the text: 'There is no offense if he gives it...' If it is said that there is no offense on account of the Mātikāṭṭhakathā statement, 'Whether pleased or displeased, one gives; it is indeed no offense'? No, because in both cases, it was said in reference to giving according to one's own wish, and because of the consequence of no offense in a case of taking by force. Some say, 'From the Pāḷi statement, "Having oneself given a robe to a bhikkhu," and because "being ordained" is stated in the Mātikāṭṭhakathā in the section defining the factors, it is shown that in both cases of giving and taking, the status of a bhikkhu is required.' The teacher says, 'Our reasoning is that this is incorrect.' Why? Because of the consequence of no offense for one who gives a robe to an unordained person and then snatches it away when that person is ordained. If it is said that a dukkaṭa offense is incurred there on account of the statement, 'Having given a robe or other requisite to an unordained person... there is an offense of dukkaṭa'? No, because it is not established. That being ordained at the very time of giving is the standard—this is not established by the commentary, or by the Pāḷi, or by reasoning. Therefore, the meaning is that this is not correct. For one who, having given a robe to an unordained person, snatches away the robe while that same person is still unordained, there is a dukkaṭa offense. Or, for one who, having given it at the time of ordination, snatches it away at the time of non-ordination, there is a dukkaṭa offense. Thus, this alternative explanation of that statement is also possible. Therefore, also because of the possibility of an alternative explanation, it is not correct. Since a separate dukkaṭa offense is not prescribed for one who gives when a person is unordained and snatches it away when they are ordained, therefore, just as in the training rules concerning the washing of old robes and so forth, being ordained at a later stage is the standard here. Therefore, because 'being ordained' is stated among the factors, the meaning is that this is not correct. Here, it is said that the Elder Dhammasiri says, 'The giving intended is only that of one who expects it back, not an outright gift.' This should be investigated.

Cīvaraacchindanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on snatching a robe is concluded.

6. Suttaviññattisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

6. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Requesting Thread

637. Chaṭṭhe [V 0.0248] kiñcāpi “sāmaṃ suttaṃ viññāpetvā”ti vuttaṃ, mātikāṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana “cīvaratthāya sāmaṃ viññattaṃ sutta”nti avatvā kevalaṃ “cīvaratthāya viññāpitasutta”nti aṅgesu vuttattā aññena cīvaratthāya viññattaṃ suttampi saṅgahaṃ gacchatīti veditabbaṃ. Sāmanti cettha kassaci niyamanaṃ. “Sāmaṃ [M 0.0278] viññāpetvā”ti kiñcāpi vuttaṃ, tathāpi “sāmaṃ vāyāpeyyā”ti attano atthāya vāyāpeyyāti evaṃ sambandho, attho ca veditabbo, pāḷiyaṃ pana āsannapadena yojanā katā, tasmā sāmaṃ viññattaṃ suttanti aññaviññattaṃ kappiyaṃ āpajjati, hatthakammayācanavasena laddhatantavāyopi kappiyo. Vikappanupagapacchimappamāṇaṃ ce, tante vītaṃyeva sakiṃ adhiṭṭhātabbaṃ, puna adhiṭṭhānakiccaṃ natthi adhiṭṭhitena ekībhāvūpagamanato. “Sace pana paricchedaṃ dassetvāva cinasāṭakaṃ viya, antarantarā adhiṭṭhitaṃ hoti, puna adhiṭṭhātabba”nti vuttaṃ. “Paṭilābhenāti vacanena vāyāpetvā ṭhapessāmītiādi ekasmiṃ antogadhaṃ hotī”ti vadanti.

637. In the sixth, although it is said, “having requested thread oneself,” in the Mātikāṭṭhakathā, however, because it is said in the sections merely as “thread requested for the purpose of a robe,” without stating “thread requested by oneself for the purpose of a robe,” it should be understood that thread requested by another for the purpose of a robe is also included. And here, “oneself” does not constitute a restriction regarding anyone. Although it is said, “having requested oneself,” nevertheless, regarding the phrase “one should have it woven oneself,” the connection and the meaning should be understood as “one should have it woven for one’s own purpose.” In the Pāḷi, however, the connection is made with the adjacent word. Therefore, even with the wording “thread requested by oneself,” thread requested by another becomes allowable. Even a weaver obtained by means of requesting handiwork is allowable. If it is the final measure suitable for vikappana that is woven on the loom, it should be determined once only; there is no further task of determination, because of its having reached a state of oneness with what has been determined. It is said: “But if, however, like a Chinese cloth, showing the divisions, it is determined section by section, it must be determined again.” They say that by the phrase “upon acquisition,” such things as “having had it woven, I will set it aside” are included in a single case.

Suttaviññattisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on requesting thread is finished.

7. Mahāpesakārasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

7. Explanation of the Training Rule on Major Weavers

642. Visiṭṭhaṃ kappañca tassa vacanena visiṭṭhaṃ katañca pamāṇaṃ, na āmisadānaṃ. Kesuci potthakesu “cīvara”nti uddharitvā vibhāgo vutto, taṃ na sametīti.

642. The special arrangement and what is made special by his word is the measure, not the giving of material things. In some manuscripts, a division is spoken of, having extracted the word 'cīvara'; that does not agree.

Mahāpesakārasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on Major Weavers is finished.

8. Accekacīvarasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

8. Explanation of the Training Rule on the Emergency Robe

646. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, accekacīvaraṃ paṭiggahetvā nikkhipitu”nti, “yāva pavāraṇā pavāritā”ti ca yaṃ vuttaṃ, te pana bhikkhū tassa vacanassa atthaṃ micchā gahetvā accekacīvaraṃ nikkhipantā cīvarakālasamayaṃ atikkāmesuṃ. Kimidaṃ vibhattaṃ, udāhu avibhattanti? Vibhattaṃ, puggalikaṃ vā. Teneva parato “amhākaṃ, āvuso, accekacīvarānī”ti vuttaṃ, avibhattaṃ pana saṅghikattā na kassaci nissaggiyaṃ karoti.

646. As to what was said: 'I allow, monks, having received an emergency robe, to set it aside,' and 'until the Pavāraṇā has been performed'—those monks, however, having wrongly understood the meaning of that statement, while setting aside the emergency robe, let the robe-season pass. Was this divided, or undivided? It was divided, or belonging to individuals. For that very reason, it was later said, 'Friends, these are our emergency robes.' An undivided robe, however, being communal property, does not become subject to forfeiture for anyone.

Apica [V 0.0249] “accekacīvaraṃ paṭiggahetvā nikkhipitu”nti iminā sāmaññavacanena vassūpanāyikadivasato paṭṭhāya, piṭṭhisamayato paṭṭhāya vā yāva pavāraṇā [M 0.0279] nikkhipituṃ vaṭṭati eva saṅghikattā, puggalikampi “vassaṃvutthakāle gaṇhathā”ti dinnattā. Tādisañhi yāva vassaṃvuttho hoti, tāva na tasseva, dāyakassa santakaṃ hoti, tathā ito tatiyavasse, catutthavasse vā “pavāraṇāya gaṇhathā”tiādinā dinnampi nikkhipitvā yathādānameva gahetabbaṃ. Ayamattho aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (pārā. aṭṭha. 2.646-9 ādayo) pākaṭo. Tāni cīvarakālasamayātikkame na nissaggiyānīti ce? Na, uddissa dinnattā. Yasmā ayaṃ samayo “kālepi ādissa dinna”nti ettha “kālo”ti āgato, gaṇabhojanasikkhāpadādīsu “samayo”tveva āgato, tasmā idha tesaṃ ekatthatādassanatthaṃ ekato “cīvarakālasamayo”ti vuttanti veditabbaṃ. Mātikāyaṃ panettha tādisaṃ cīvaraṃ attano santakabhāvaṃ upagataṃ puggalikaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ, tenevāha “bhikkhuno paneva accekacīvaraṃ uppajjeyyā”ti. Attano kuṭiyā vassaṃvutthassa bhikkhuno hi dātuṃ alabhanto antovasse eva dānakiccaṃ pariniṭṭhāpetvā gacchati, tathā saṅghassa. Tasmā idaṃ accekacīvaraṃ atthi uppannakālato paṭṭhāya saṅghassa vā puggalassa vā santakabhāvaṃ upagacchantaṃ, yaṃ na vassāvāsikabhāvena dinnaṃ, atthi uppannakālato paṭṭhāya anupagantvā vassaṃvutthakāleyeva puggalassa vā saṅghassa vā upagacchantaṃ, yaṃ vassāvāsikabhāvena uppajjitvā samaye dinnaṃ, atthi samaye dinnampi puggalassa santakabhāvaṃ anupagacchantaṃ, saṅghasantakabhāvaṃ vā dāyakasantakabhāvaṃ vā upagacchantaṃ, īdisaṃ sandhāya “saññāṇaṃ katvā nikkhipitabba”nti vuttaṃ. Idaṃ atirekasaṃvaccharampi nikkhipituṃ labhati attano santakabhāvaṃ anupagatattā, tasmā “dasāhānāgata”nti ito aññaṃ sandhāya vuttanti siddhametanti. Dasāhato puretaraṃ labhitvā yāva pavāraṇā nikkhipituṃ na labhati, tasmā sakabhāvūpagatameva adhiṭṭhātabbaṃ, taṃyeva sandhāya “dasāhānāgata”nti vuttaṃ, yato “antosamaye adhiṭṭheti, vikappetī”ti anāpattivāre vuttaṃ. Saññāṇaṃ katvā nikkhipitabbakaṃ pana parassa dātabbatāya sakabhāvaṃ anupagataṃ, na hi taṃ sandhāya “adhiṭṭheti, vikappetī”ti sakkā vattuṃ, na ca taṃ imasmiṃ atthe nissaggiyaṃ hoti saṅghassa nissaggiyābhāvato, aṭṭhakathāyampi ayamattho suṭṭhu pākaṭova. Katamaṃ saññāṇaṃ katvā nikkhipitabbanti ce? Parasantakaṃ cīvaraṃ saṅghikameva [M 0.0280] hoti, tato “sallakkhetvā sukhaṃ dātuṃ bhavissatī”ti iminā hi parassa santakabhāvo dassito.

Furthermore, by this general statement, 'Having received an emergency robe, one may store it,' it is indeed permissible to store it from the day of entering the rains-residence, or from the back-cloth period, until Pavāraṇā, because it is Sangha property; and also a personal robe, because it was given with the instruction, 'Take it at the time of having completed the rains-residence.' For indeed, as long as one has not completed the rains-residence, such a robe does not belong to him; it is the property of the donor.
