1. The Commentary on the Training Rule Concerning Plants.

89. Pharasuṃ niggahetuṃ asakkontoti dassitabhāvaṃ jānāpeti. Kasmā ayaṃ pharasuṃ uggirīti ce? Manussānantiādi tassa parihāro. “Ākoṭesi chindīti ca vacanato rukkhadevatānaṃ hatthāni chijjanti, na cātumahārājikādīnaṃ viya acchejjānī”ti vadanti.

89. “Unable to restrain the axe” makes known the state that was shown. If one should ask, “Why did he raise the axe?” the answer to that is “for humans,” and so on. They say that because of the statement, “He struck and cut,” the hands of tree-deities are cut, and they are not indestructible like those of the devas of the Cātumahārājika realm and so on.

90-92. Bhavanti ahuvuñcāti dvikāliko bhūtasaddo. Yadi bījato nibbattena bījaṃ dassitaṃ, tadeva santakaṃ yadidaṃ. Sova kukkuṭo maṃsimakkhitoti ayameva hi parihāro. Aṭṭhakathāsupi hi “bīje bījasaññī”ti likhitaṃ. Yaṃ bījaṃ bhūtagāmo nāma hoti, tasmiṃ bīje bhūtagāmabījeti yojetvā. Amūlakattā kira sampuṇṇabhūtagāmo na hoti, “samūlapatto eva [V 0.0266] hi bhūtagāmo nāmā”ti kāraṇaṃ vadanti. “Abhūtagāmamūlattāti bhūtagāmato anuppannattā abhūtagāmamūlaṃ, bhūtagāmassa amūlakattā vā. Na hi tato añño bhūtagāmo uppajjatī”ti dvidhāpi likhitaṃ. Piyaṅgu asanarukkho vaḍḍhanattaco khajjaphalo, “pītasālo”tipi vuccati. Amūlakabhūtagāme saṅgahaṃ gacchatīti nāḷikerassevāyaṃ. Ghaṭapiṭṭhijātattā, bījagāmānulomattā ca dukkaṭavatthu. Na vāsetabbaṃ “durūpaciṇṇattā”ti likhitaṃ, “yesaṃ rukkhānaṃ sākhā ruhatīti vacanato yesaṃ na ruhati, tesaṃ sākhāya kappiyakaraṇakiccaṃ natthīti siddha”nti vuttaṃ. Muddatiṇanti tassa nāmaṃ. “Muñjatiṇanti pāṭho”ti likhitaṃ.

90-92. The word 'bhūta' in 'bhavanti' and 'ahuvuñca' is of two tenses. If the seed is indicated by the plant life produced from the seed, then that very seed is the possession, that is, this seed. Indeed, this is the explanation: 'Like that very rooster smeared with earth.' Indeed, in the commentaries it is written: 'perceiving a seed in a seed.' That seed which is called plant life, in that seed, it should be connected as 'in the seed which is plant life.' Because it is rootless, it is said that a complete plant life does not exist; they state the reason thus: 'Indeed, only that which has a root and leaves is called plant life.' Regarding 'because its source is not from plant life': it is a source not from plant life because it does not arise from plant life, or because the plant life itself is rootless. Indeed, no other plant life arises from it. Thus it is written in two ways. Piyaṅgu is the asana tree; it has growing bark and edible fruit. It is also called 'pītasālo' (having yellow heartwood). Regarding 'it is included in rootless plant life': this refers specifically to the coconut palm. Because it is produced on the back of a pot, and because it is in conformity with the seed-group, it is a ground for a dukkaṭa offense. It should not be used, for it is written: 'because it is improperly practiced.' It is stated: 'From the text “of which trees the branch grows,” it is established that for those whose branches do not grow, there is no task of making their branches allowable.' Its name is 'muddatiṇa.' It is written: 'The reading is muñjatiṇa.'

Samaṇakappehīti samaṇavohārehi, tasmā vattabbaṃ bhikkhunā “kappiyaṃ karohī”ti. Tassa āṇattiyā karontenāpi sāmaṇerādinā “kappiya”nti [M 0.0298] vatvāva aggiparijitaṃ kātabbanti siddhaṃ. Aggiparijitādīni viya kappiyattā abījanibbaṭṭabījānipi “pañcahi samaṇakappehī”ti (cūḷava. 250) ettha paviṭṭhāni, yathālābhato vā samaṇakappavacanaṃ gahetabbaṃ. “Kappiya’nti vattukāmo ‘kappa’nti ce vadati, ‘vaṭṭatī’ti vadantī”ti vuttaṃ. “Kappiya’nti vacanaṃ sakasakabhāsāyapi vaṭṭatī”ti vadanti. “Kappiyanti vatvā”ti vuttattā bhikkhunā ‘kappiyaṃ’icceva vattabbaṃ, “itarena pana yāya kāyaci bhāsāyā”ti vadanti, vīmaṃsitabbaṃ. “Ucchuṃ kappiyaṃ karissāmīti dāruṃ vijjhatī”ti vacanato kappiyaṃ kātabbaṃ sandhāya viraddheti vuttaṃ hoti, ācariyā pana “kappiyaṃ kāretabbaṃ sandhāya kappiyanti sitthādiṃ kāreti, vaṭṭatī”ti vadanti, tassa kāraṇaṃ vadantā kātuṃ vaṭṭanabhāveneva virajjhitvā katepi kappiyaṃ jātaṃ. Yadi na vaṭṭeyya, sitthādimhi kate na vaṭṭeyyāti, upaparikkhitabbaṃ. Uṭṭhitasevālaghaṭaṃ ātape nikkhipituṃ vaṭṭati, vikopetukāmatāya sati dukkaṭaṃ yuttaṃ viya. “Puppharajjubhājanagatikā, tasmā na vaṭṭati. Nāḷe vā baddhapupphakalāpe nāḷasmiṃ katepi vaṭṭati tasmiṃ pupphassa atthitāyā”ti vadanti. Porāṇagaṇṭhipade “bījagāmena bhūtagāmo dassito anavasesapariyādānattha”nti vuttaṃ.

“By the conventions of ascetics” means by the usages of ascetics. Therefore, a bhikkhu should say, “Make it allowable.” It is established that even when a novice or another acts under his instruction, a thing touched by fire must be made so only after saying 'kappiyaṃ'. Just as things touched by fire and so forth are allowable, so too seeds from cuttings and extracted seeds are included here under 'the five ascetic conventions' (Cūḷavagga 250) because they are allowable; or, the term 'ascetic convention' should be understood according to what is available. It is said: “If one, wishing to say 'kappiyaṃ', says 'kappa', they say 'it is allowable'.” They also say: “The word 'kappiyaṃ' is valid in one's own respective language.” Because it is stated “having said 'kappiyaṃ'”, a bhikkhu should say only 'kappiyaṃ'. They say, “But by another, it may be said in any language whatsoever”; this should be investigated. From the saying, “Thinking, 'I will make sugarcane allowable,' he pierces the wood,” it is said that one fails with regard to making it allowable. The teachers, however, say: “Intending to have something made allowable, one has a rice-ball, etc., made while saying 'kappiyaṃ'; this is allowable.” Stating the reason for this, they say that simply by virtue of its being fit to be done, even when it is done after a procedural failure, it becomes allowable. If it were not allowable, then when a rice-ball, etc., is made, it would not be allowable; this should be investigated. It is allowable to place a water pot on which moss has grown in the sun; if there is an intention to destroy it, a dukkaṭa offense seems proper. They say: “It has the nature of a container for a flower-garland, therefore it is not allowable. Or, in a bundle of flowers tied to a stalk, even if the stalk is prepared, it is allowable because of the existence of the flower on it.” In the ancient glossary, it is said: “The plant-kind is indicated by the seed-kind for the purpose of including everything without remainder.”

Bhūtagāmasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rule Concerning Plants is concluded.

2. Aññavādakasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

2. The Explanation of the Training Rule Concerning Speaking Otherwise

98-9. Aññaṃ vadatīti aññavādakaṃ, “vacanaṃ kareyyā”ti likhitaṃ. “Tuṇhībhūtassetaṃ nāma”nti pāṭho. Ugghātetukāmoti samohanitukāmo, antarāyaṃ kattukāmoti porāṇā.

98-9. He speaks otherwise, therefore he is called one who speaks otherwise. It is written: 'One should speak.' The reading is: 'This is the name of one who has become silent.' 'Desiring to refute' means desiring to confuse; according to the ancients, it means desiring to make an obstruction.

100. “Sudiṭṭho [V 0.0267] bhante, na paneso kahāpaṇotiādīsu anāropite dukkaṭena musāvādapācittiyaṃ, aropite pācittiyadvayaṃ hotī”ti vadanti, vīmaṃsitabbaṃ.

100. In cases such as 'Venerable Sir, it is clearly seen, but this is not a kahāpaṇa,' if the matter is not brought up, there is a pācittiya offense for false speech along with a dukkaṭa offense; if it is brought up, there are two pācittiya offenses,” they say. This should be investigated.

102. Adhammena vā vaggena vā na kammārahassa vāti ettha “mayi vutte maṃ vā aññaṃ vā saṅgho adhammena vā kammaṃ, vaggena vā kammaṃ karissati, na [M 0.0299] kammārahassa vā me, aññassa vā kammaṃ karissatī”ti na kathetīti yojetabbaṃ.

102. Here, concerning 'by unrighteous means or by a faction or against one not deserving of action,' it should be connected thus: Thinking, “If I speak, the Saṅgha will perform an action toward me or another by unrighteous means, or by a faction, or will perform an action toward one not deserving of it—whether toward me or another,” he does not speak.

Aññavādakasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rule Concerning Speaking Otherwise is concluded.

3. Ujjhāpanakasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

3. Explanation of the Training Rule on Fault-finding

103. “Chandāyā”ti akkharakkharāyātiādi viya liṅgavipallāsena vuttaṃ, chandatthanti vā attho. Yesaṃ senāsanāni paññapeti, tesaṃ attani chandatthanti adhippāyo.

103. The word ‘chandāyā’ is stated with a gender inversion, like ‘akkharakkharāyāti,’ etc., or its meaning is ‘for the sake of will.’ The intention is that for those for whom lodgings are assigned, it is for the sake of their own will.

106. Anupasampannantiādīsu karaṇattho gahetabbo. Aññaṃ anupasampannanti aññena anupasampannena. Tassa vāti anupasampannassa. “Sammutikāle pañcaṅgavirahādayo asammatā nāmā”ti, “upasampannena laddhasammuti sikkhāpaccakkhānena vinassatī”ti ca vuttaṃ. Saṅghenāti sabbena saṅghena kammavācāya assāvetvā “taveso bhāro”ti kevalaṃ āropitabhāro. Kevala-saddo hettha kammavācāya assāvitabhāvamattameva dīpeti. Sayamevāti itaresaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ anumatiyā. Abhūtena khīyanakassa ādikammikassa kathaṃ anāpattīti ce? Iminā sikkhāpadena. Musāvāde āpattiyeva dve pācittiyo vuttā viya dissanti pubbapayoge rukkhādichindanādīsu viya, vicāretabbaṃ.

106. In the phrases beginning with ‘anupasampanna’ (not fully ordained), the instrumental sense should be understood. ‘Another not fully ordained’ means by another who is not fully ordained. ‘Of him’ means of the one not fully ordained. It is said, ‘During the time of authorization, those lacking the five qualities, etc., are considered unauthorized,’ and ‘authorization obtained by one who is fully ordained is lost by renouncing the training.’ ‘By the Saṅgha’ means that the entire Saṅgha, without announcing it by a formal act, merely assigned the responsibility by saying, ‘This is your responsibility.’ Here the word ‘kevala’ (merely) indicates only the fact that it was not announced by a formal act. ‘By oneself’ means with the agreement of the other bhikkhus. If it is asked, ‘How is there no offense for the first offender who maliciously accuses falsely?’, the answer is: Because of this training rule. In the case of false speech, there is indeed an offense; two pācittiya offenses seem to be stated, as in the preliminary action in cases like cutting down a tree, etc. This should be investigated.

Ujjhāpanakasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on fault-finding is concluded.

4. Paṭhamasenāsanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

4. Explanation of the First Training Rule on Lodgings

110. “Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hotī”ti vacanato, parivāre “ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññattī”ti (pari. 226) vacanato ca idha atthi anupaññattīti siddhaṃ. Kiñcāpi siddhaṃ, “evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyāthā”tiādinā [V 0.0268] pana paññattiṭṭhānaṃ na paññāyati, kevalaṃ “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, aṭṭhamāse…pe… nikkhipitu”nti ettakameva vuttaṃ, taṃ kasmāti [M 0.0300] ce? Paṭhamapaññattiyaṃ vuttanayeneva vattabbato avisesattā na vuttaṃ. Yadi evaṃ kā ettha anupaññattīti? Ajjhokāseti. Ayamanupaññatti paññattiyampi atthīti ce? Atthi, taṃ pana okāsamattadīpanaṃ, dutiyaṃ cātuvassikamāsasaṅkhātakāladīpanaṃ. Yasmā ubhayampi ekaṃ kālokāsaṃ ekato katvā “ajjhokāse”ti vuttanti dīpento bhagavā “anujānāmi, bhikkhave…pe… nikkhipitu”nti āhāti veditabbaṃ. Teneva mātikāṭṭhakathāyaṃ (kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. paṭhamasenāsanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā) vuttaṃ “yattha ca yadā ca santharituṃ na vaṭṭati, taṃ sabbamidha ajjhokāsasaṅkhyameva gatanti veditabba”nti. Hemantakālassa anāpattisamayattā idaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ nidānānapekkhanti siddhaṃ, tathā hi ajjhokāsapadasāmatthiyena ayaṃ viseso – vassānakāle ovassakaṭṭhāne ajjhokāse, maṇḍapādimhi ca na vaṭṭati. Hemantakāle pakatiajjhokāse na vaṭṭati, sabbamidha ovassakepi maṇḍapādimhi vaṭṭati, tañca kho yattha himavassena senāsanaṃ na temeti, gimhakāle pakatiajjhokāsepi vaṭṭati, tañca kho akālameghādassaneyevāti ayaṃ viseso “aṭṭha māse”ti ca “avassikasaṅkete”ti ca etesaṃ dvinnaṃ padānaṃ sāmatthiyatopi siddho.

110. From the statement, ‘Thus, this training rule was laid down by the Blessed One for the bhikkhus,’ and from the statement in the Parivāra, ‘There is one enactment, one supplementary enactment,’ it is established that there is a supplementary enactment here. Although it is established, the place of the enactment is not discerned by the text beginning with, ‘And thus, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule…’; only ‘I allow, bhikkhus, for eight months…to store it away’ is stated. If it is asked why, it is because it was not stated, as it should be understood in the same way as stated in the first enactment, there being no distinction. If so, what is the supplementary enactment here? It is ‘in the open.’ If it is asked, ‘Is this supplementary enactment also in the original enactment?’ Yes, it is. However, that one is merely an indicator of place, while the second indicates the time—the period reckoned as the four months of the rainy season. Because both—time and place—are combined into one and called ‘in the open,’ it should be understood that the Blessed One, indicating this, said, ‘I allow, bhikkhus…to store it away.’ Therefore, in the Mātikāṭṭhakathā it is said: ‘Wherever and whenever it is not allowable to spread out, all of that should be understood as included here in the category of “in the open.”’ Since the winter season is a time of no offense, this training rule is established as not depending on a cause. Thus, by the force of the word ‘in the open,’ this is the distinction: during the rainy season, it is not allowable in the open in a place exposed to rain, nor in a pavilion and so forth. In the winter season, it is not allowable in a normal open place; here, it is entirely allowable even in a pavilion and so forth that is exposed to rain, provided that the lodging is not dampened by frost. In the hot season, it is allowable even in a normal open place, and that is only when an unseasonal cloud is seen. This distinction is also established by the force of these two phrases: ‘for eight months’ and ‘in a place not designated for the rains.’

Kiñca bhiyyo – aṭṭhakathāyaṃ sandassitavisesova. Cammādinā onaddhako vā navavāyimo vā na sīghaṃ vinassati. Kāyānugatikattāti kāye yattha, tattha gatattā. Saṅghikamañcādimhi kāyaṃ phusāpetvā viharituṃ na vaṭṭatīti dhammasiritthero. “Saṅghikaṃ pana ‘ajjhokāsaparibhogena paribhuñjatha, bhante, yathāsukha’nti dāyakā denti senāsanaṃ, evarūpe anāpattī”ti andhakaṭṭhakathāyaṃ vacanato, idha ca paṭikkhepābhāvato vaṭṭati. “Aññañca evarūpanti apare”ti vuttaṃ. “Pādaṭṭhānābhimukhāti nisīdantassa pādapatanaṭṭhānābhimukhā”ti likhitaṃ. Sammajjantassa pādaṭṭhānābhimukhanti ācariyassa takko.

Furthermore, in the commentary, a special case is shown. A bed covered with leather, etc., or newly woven, does not quickly perish. 'Because it accompanies the body' means because it goes wherever the body goes. Thus said Elder Dhammasiri: 'It is not proper to dwell causing the body to touch a communal bed, etc.' 'However, donors offer a communal lodging, saying, “Venerable sirs, use it as an open-air lodging, as you please.” In such a case, there is no offense'—thus it is said in the Andhakaṭṭhakathā; and because here there is no prohibition, it is permissible. It is said: 'And others say, “And another such as this.”' 'Facing the place where the feet are placed' means, for one who is sitting, facing the place where the feet will fall—thus it is written. Facing the place where the feet are placed for one who is sweeping—this is the teacher's reasoning.

111. “Pāduddhārenāti bahiupacāre ṭhitattā”ti likhitaṃ. Gacchanti, dukkaṭaṃ dhammakathikassa viya. Kasmā na pācittiyaṃ? Pacchā āgatehi vuḍḍhatarehi uṭṭhāpetvā gahetabbato. Dhammakathikassa pana anuṭṭhapetabbattā. “Anāṇattiyā paññattiyampi tassa bhāro”ti vuttaṃ.

111. It is written: 'Regarding pāduddhārena (by lifting the feet), it is because of standing outside the boundary.' When they go, it is a dukkaṭa offense, as in the case of a Dhamma teacher. Why is it not a pācittiya offense? Because it should be taken after having made the more senior monks who arrived later get up. However, for a Dhamma teacher, it is a pācittiya offense because he should not be made to get up. It is said: 'Even when spreading a seat on one's own accord, without being commanded, it is his responsibility.'

112. Pariharaṇeyevāti [V 0.0269][M 0.0301] ettha gahetvā vicāraṇeti dhammasiritthero. Attano santakakaraṇeti upatissatthero. Bījanīpattakaṃ caturassabījanī.

112. Here, regarding pariharaṇe eva (in the very act of handling), Elder Dhammasiri says it means 'in taking and arranging.' Elder Upatissa says it means 'in making it one's own property.' A bījanīpattaka is a square fan.

113. “Yo bhikkhu vā sāmaṇero vā…pe… lajjī hotī’ti vuttattā alajjiṃ āpucchitvā gantuṃ na vaṭṭatī”ti vadanti. Pāṭhe “kenaci palibuddhaṃ hotī”ti ca aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “palibuddha”nti ca senāsanaṃyeva sandhāya vuttaṃ, tasmā tathāpi atthīti gahetabbaṃ. “Anāpucchaṃ vā”ti pāṭho.

113. They say: 'Because it is said, “Whatever bhikkhu or sāmaṇera... is conscientious,” it is not proper to go after asking permission from a shameless one.' Both in the Pāḷi text, 'is obstructed by something,' and in the commentary, 'obstructed,' are said referring only to the lodging; therefore, it should be understood that this is also the case. There is the reading: 'or without asking.'

Paṭhamasenāsanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the first training rule concerning lodgings is concluded.

5. Dutiyasenāsanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

5. The commentary on the second training rule concerning lodgings.

116-7. Ettakameva vuttamaṭṭhakathāsu, tathāpi padaṭṭhādayopi labbhanti eva. Anugaṇṭhipade “aññaṃ attharaṇādi akappiyattā na vutta”nti vuttaṃ. “Mañcaṃ vā pīṭhaṃ vā vihāre vā vihārūpacāre vā’ti imināpi saṃsandanatthaṃ ‘kiñcāpi vutto, atha kho’tiādi āraddha”nti ca vuttaṃ. Upacāramattañcetaṃ “rukkhamūle”ti, tattha vattabbaṃ natthi.

In the commentaries, only this much is stated; nevertheless, patterned floor-coverings and so forth are indeed allowable. In the Anugaṇṭhipada, it is said: 'Other coverings, etc., are not mentioned because they are unsuitable.' And it is also said: 'For the purpose of connecting with this Pāḷi, “a bed or a seat... or in the vicinity of a monastery,” the passage beginning with “although it is said... now then...” is begun.' This phrase, “at the foot of a tree,” is merely a reference to the vicinity; there is nothing to be said regarding it.

118. Anāpucchitvāpi gantuṃ vaṭṭatīti asatiyā gacchatopi anāpatti, āpucchanaṃ pana vattaṃ sañcicca anāpucchato vattabhedadukkaṭattā. Puggalikasenāsane saṅghikaseyyaṃ, saṅghikasenāsane vā puggalikaseyyaṃ attharitvā gacchantassa dukkaṭaṃ yuttaṃ viya. Kasmā? “Seyyāmattameva nasseyyā”ti vuttattā. Idha pana “palibuddhaṃ palibuddho”ti duvidhampi atthi.

118. Regarding the statement, 'It is allowable to go even without asking permission,' there is no offense for one who goes unmindfully. Asking permission, however, is a duty, because for one who intentionally does not ask, there is a dukkaṭa offense for breaking a duty. For one who goes away after having spread bedding belonging to the Saṅgha in a personal lodging, or personal bedding in a lodging belonging to the Saṅgha, a dukkaṭa offense seems fitting. Why? Because it was said: 'The bedding itself should not perish.' Here, however, both Pāḷi readings, 'palibuddhaṃ' and 'palibuddho,' exist.

Dutiyasenāsanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the second training rule concerning lodgings is concluded.

6. Anupakhajjasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

6. The commentary on the training rule concerning not encroaching.

121. Chabbaggiyesuyeva therā bhikkhūti keci. Pāde dhovitvātiādimhi pavisantassa vā pādadhovanapāsāṇato yāva mañcapīṭhaṃ passāvatthāya nikkhamantassa vā yāva passāvaṭṭhānanti yojanā kātabbā. Evaṃ sante [M 0.0302] “passāvatthāya nikkhamantassa vā”ti na vattabbaṃ, “passāvaṭṭhānato nikkhamantassa vā”ti vattabbaṃ. Passāvaṭṭhānanti katthaci potthake. Tathā hi mātikāṭṭhakathāyaṃ (kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. anupakhajjasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā) [V 0.0270] “pavisantassa pādadhovanapāsāṇato yāva mañcapīṭhaṃ nikkhamantassa mañcapīṭhato yāva passāvaṭṭhānaṃ, tāva upacāro”ti vuttaṃ, tasmā “pāde dhovitvā pavisantassa, passāvatthāya nikkhamantassa ca dvāre nikkhittapādadhovanapāsāṇato, passāvaṭṭhānato ca mañcapīṭha”nti katthaci potthake pāṭho, so apāṭho. Kasmā? Mañcapīṭhānaṃ upacārassa vuttattā. Pavisantassa yāva mañcapīṭhānaṃ upacāro, nikkhamantassa tato paṭṭhāya yāva passāvaṭṭhānaṃ vaccakuṭicaṅkamaṭṭhānanti iminā atthena yathā saṃsandati, tathāvidho pāṭhoti ācariyo.

121. Some say that the senior monks are only those of the group of six. In the phrase 'having washed the feet,' and so on, for one entering, the connection should be made from the foot-washing stone up to the bed or bench; or for one exiting for the purpose of urination, up to the place for urination. This being so, it should not be said, 'or for one exiting for the purpose of urination,' but rather, 'or for one exiting from the place for urination.' The reading 'place for urination' is found in some books. Indeed, in the Mātikāṭṭhakathā, it is stated: 'For one entering, the vicinity extends from the foot-washing stone up to the bed or bench; for one exiting, it extends from the bed or bench up to the place for urination.' Therefore, in some books, the reading is: 'for one entering after washing the feet, and for one exiting for the purpose of urination, from the foot-washing stone placed at the door, and from the place for urination up to the bed or bench.' But this is a corrupt reading. Why? Because the vicinity of the beds and benches has been stated. For one entering, the vicinity extends up to the beds and benches; for one exiting, it extends from there up to the place for urination, the latrine, and the walking place. The teacher states that a reading which accords with this meaning is of the kind to be adopted.

122. Upacāraṃ ṭhapetvāti idha vuttaupacāraṃ ṭhapetvā. “Dassanasavanūpacārepi santharantassā”ti likhitaṃ.

122. In the phrase 'having set aside the vicinity,' it means having set aside the vicinity mentioned in this training rule. It is written: 'Even for one spreading within the vicinity of sight and hearing.'

Anupakhajjasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the training rule concerning encroaching is concluded.

7. Nikkaḍḍhanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

7. Commentary on the Training Rule Concerning Expulsion

126-7. Chasattakoṭṭhakāni vāti ettha dvārakoṭṭhakaṃ adhippetaṃ. “Nikkhamā”ti vacanaṃ sutvāpi attano ruciyā nikkhamati, anāpatti; idha aggisālādi eva upacāroti.

126-7. Here, in the phrase 'six or seven rooms,' the gateway is intended. Even having heard the words 'Go out,' if one leaves by one’s own preference, there is no offense. Here, it should be known that the fire-hall and so on is the vicinity.

Nikkaḍḍhanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the training rule concerning expulsion is concluded.

8. Vehāsakuṭisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

8. Commentary on the Training Rule Concerning a High Dwelling

129. “Pamāṇamajjhimassa galappamāṇe dinnatulāpi vehāsakuṭiyevā”ti likhitaṃ, “na sā idha adhippetā”ti vuttaṃ.

129. It is written: 'Even a beam given at the neck-level of a person of middle stature is a high dwelling.' It is said: 'That is not intended here.'

Vehāsakuṭisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the training rule concerning a high dwelling is concluded.

9. Mahallakavihārasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

9. Commentary on the Training Rule Concerning a Large Dwelling

135. Yāva [M 0.0303] dvārakosāti dvārasamīpā, yāva bhittīti attho, taṃ suvuttaṃ. Kavāṭavitthārappamāṇoti [V 0.0271] hatthapāsassādhippetattā, samantā kavāṭavitthārappamāṇaupacārassa gahitattā aparipūraupacārāpi hoti. Ālokaṃ karotīti ālokaṃ sandheti pidhetīti sandhi eva ālokasandhināmakā honti. Vātapānakavāṭalepakamme appaharitaṭṭhānakiccaṃ natthi.

9. 'As far as the door-post' means from near the door, that is, as far as the wall; that is well-stated. 'The extent of the door-leaf's breadth' is because a hand's reach is intended, and because the vicinity, having the measure of the door-leaf's breadth, is taken all around, it can also be an incomplete vicinity. 'It makes light' means it joins or covers the light, therefore the joints themselves are called 'light-joints'. In the work of plastering a window-shutter, there is no task for a place without greenery.

136. Iṭṭhakāti chadanakapālāsilādiiṭṭhakā. Chadanūparīti ettha paṭhamaṃ tāva ekavāraṃ aparisesaṃ chādetvā puna chādanadaṇḍake bandhitvā dutiyavāraṃ tatheva chādetabbaṃ. “Tatiyavāracatutthavāre sampatte dve magge adhiṭṭhahitvā tatiyamaggaṃ āṇāpetvā pakkamitabba”nti vuttaṃ, taṃ “punappunaṃ chādāpetī”ti iminā yujjati.

135. 'Bricks' means bricks such as roofing tiles, stone slabs, and so on. Regarding 'on top of the roofing': first, having roofed it one time without remainder, and then, having bound the roofing battens, it should be roofed a second time in the same way. It is said: 'When the third or fourth time is reached, having determined two courses, and having given the order for the third course, one should depart.' That accords with 'he has it roofed again and again'.

Porāṇā pana “paṭhamavāreyeva tayo magge adhiṭṭhātuṃ vaṭṭati, catutthato paṭṭhāya āpatti pācittiyaṃ, catutthalepato paṭṭhāya āpattī”ti vadanti. Tattha chadane vuttavidhinidānena sameti, lepe vuttavidhitikacchedena sameti. Tathāpi so na yuttova. Nidāne, aṭṭhakathāyañca siddhalepattā sabbasovāpi acchanne, channevāpi anekaso pariyāyassa tatiyasseva adhiṭṭhānanti no sametīti ācariyo. “Dve magge”ti, “dve chadane”ti ca “tatiyavārato paṭṭhāya evaṃ chādāpehī’ti āṇāpetvā pakkamitabba”nti ca upatissatthero vadati kira.

136. The ancient teachers, however, say: 'It is allowable to determine the three courses in the first instance itself; from the fourth course onwards, there is a pācittiya offense; from the fourth plastering onwards, there is an offense.' Therein, regarding the roofing, it accords with the procedure stated in the Nidāna; regarding the plastering, it accords with the detailed decision of the stated procedure. Even so, that decision is indeed not suitable. The teacher says that because in the Nidāna and in the commentary the plastering is completed, it does not accord that whether completely unroofed or roofed many times, the determination is only for the third course of the sequence. The Elder Upatissa, it is said, also states: 'Two courses,' and 'two coverings,' and 'from the third time onwards, having given the order, "Have it roofed in this way," one should depart.'

Mahallakavihārasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the training rule concerning a large dwelling is concluded.

10. Sappāṇakasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Training Rule Concerning Living Beings

140. Sappāṇakasikkhāpadaṃ uttānatthameva.

10. The training rule concerning living beings has an obvious meaning.

Samatto vaṇṇanākkamena bhūtagāmavaggo dutiyo.

140. The second chapter, the Bhūtagāmavagga, is concluded according to the sequence of the commentary.

3. Ovādavaggo

The Chapter on Exhortation

1. Ovādasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

3. Commentary on the Training Rule on Admonition

144. Kathānusārenāti [V 0.0272][M 0.0304] yo bhikkhunovādakatthiko kiṃsīlo kiṃsamācāro katarakulā pabbajitotiādi kathānusārenāti attho. Saggamaggagamanepīti api-saddena mokkhagamanepi. “Lakkhaṇappaṭivedhapaṭisaṃyutto”ti aṭṭhagarudhammānusārena vattabbaṃ dhammakathaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ.

1. 'In accordance with the talk' means: by following the line of talk concerning a monk who desires to admonish bhikkhunīs, such as, 'What is his virtue? What is his conduct? From what family did he go forth?' This is the meaning. In 'even in going on the path to heaven,' by the word 'api,' going to Nibbāna is also included. The phrase 'connected with the penetration of characteristics' was said with reference to the Dhamma talk that should be given in accordance with the eight weighty rules.

145-147. Nissīmanti vihāre baddhasīmato aññaṃ abaddhasīmaṃ, gāmasīmādinti attho. “Supinantenapī”ti na sabbesanti idha bāhullanayena vuttaṃ. Chabbaggiyā hi keci vīsativassāpi atthi atirekavīsativassāpīti iminā imaṃ majjhimabodhikāle paññattanti viññāyati. “Sīlavā hotī”ti vatvā tassa catubbidhattā idha adhippetasīlameva dassetuṃ “pātimokkhasaṃvarasaṃvuto”tiādi vuttaṃ. Gaṇṭhānugaṇṭhipadesu “satisaṃvarādayo idha nādhippetā, tena vibhaṅgapāṭhaṃ dasseti aṭṭhakathācariyo”ti vuttaṃ. Atthatoti pāḷiatthato. Kāraṇatoti kāraṇūpapattito, aṭṭhakathātoti adhippāyo. Atha vā kāraṇatoti dhammato, tena atthato dhammatoti vuttaṃ hoti. Atha vā atthatoti phalato. “Kāraṇatoti hetuto. Dhammapadampi jātakena sahā”ti likhitaṃ. Pañhaṃ kathetunti “pañhaṃ puṭṭho kathetī”ti ettha bhikkhuniyā puṭṭhena “na jānāmī”ti na sakkā kathetuṃ. “Na kho pana taṃ bhagavanta”nti pāṭho. “Na kho paneta”nti ca likhanti, taṃ na sundaraṃ. “Kāsāyavatthavasanāyā”ti vacanato pārājikāyapi na vaṭṭati. Bhikkhuniyā kāyasaṃsaggameva vuttaṃ. Methunena hi bhikkhunīdūsako hoti.

145-147. Herein, `nissīmaṃ` (outside the boundary) means another, unestablished boundary (`abaddhasīma`) apart from the established boundary (`baddhasīma`) in a monastery, such as a village boundary, etc. This is the meaning. Herein, 'even by means of a dream' is not said for all of them; here it is stated by way of generality. Indeed, some of the group-of-six monks were also of twenty years' standing, and they were also of more than twenty years' standing. For this reason, it is understood that this training rule was laid down in the middle period of the enlightenment. Having said, 'He is virtuous,' because that virtue has a fourfold nature, in order to show only the virtue intended here, 'restrained by the Pātimokkha restraint,' etc., was said. In the passages of the `gaṇṭhi` and `anugaṇṭhi`, it is said: 'Restraint by mindfulness, etc., are not intended here; therefore, the commentary master shows the text of the Vibhaṅga.' `Atthato` means from the meaning of the Pali. `Kāraṇato` means from the suitability of the reason; this is the intention from the commentary. Alternatively, `kāraṇato` means from the Dhamma; therefore, it comes to be said as 'from the meaning and from the Dhamma.' Alternatively, `atthato` means from the result. It is written: '`Kāraṇato` means from the cause. The Dhammapada also, together with the Jātaka.' Regarding `pañhaṃ kathetuṃ` (to speak on a question): Herein, in the phrase `pañhaṃ puṭṭho kathetī` (being asked a question, he speaks), it is not possible for one who has been asked by a bhikkhunī to say, 'I do not know.' There is the reading `na kho pana taṃ bhagavanta`. And they write `na kho paneta`, but that is not good. Because of the statement 'for wearing the saffron robe,' it is not allowable even for a bhikkhunī who has committed a pārājika offense. Only bodily contact with a bhikkhunī was stated. For by sexual intercourse one becomes a defiler of a bhikkhunī.

148-9. Bhikkhūnaṃ santike upasampannā nāma parivattaliṅgā, pañcasatā sākiyāniyo vā. “Dhammadesanāpattimocanatthaṃ panā”ti vacanato mātugāmaggahaṇena sabbattha bhikkhunīsaṅgahaṃ gacchatīti siddhaṃ. Bhikkhuniggahaṇena pana mātugāmo tiriyaṃ taraṇasikkhāpade (pāci. 187-190) saṅgahito, na aññattha. “Osāretabbā”ti pāḷipāṭho, pāḷi osāretabbāti attho[M 0.0305]. “Osāretabba”nti aṭṭhakathāpāḷi. Ekasmiṃ ṭhāne vandite dosābhāvato bahūsu ekāya vandite vaṭṭatīti ce? Bhikkhūhi kattabbaṃ natthi, bhikkhuniyāyeva kattabbaṃ, tasmā na vaṭṭati[V 0.0273]. “Yattha katthaci nisinnāyāti antodvādasahatthe nisinnāyā”ti vadanti. Na nimantitā hutvā gantukāmāti nimantitā hutvā gantukāmā bhikkhū idha nādhippetā, vassaṃ upagantukāmāva adhippetāti attho. Yato panāti bhikkhunīvihārato. Tatthāti bhikkhunīvihāre. Kiñcāpi “ovādadāyakā bhikkhū”ti vacanato ovādadāyakeheva sabhikkhuko āvāso hoti, na sabbehīti āpanno, tathāpi asati bhikkhunovādake ovādasaṃvāsānaṃ atthāya yācanatthāya avassaṃ gantabbattā aññehipi bhikkhūhi sabhikkhukopi sabhikkhuko evāti veditabbo. Sā rakkhitabbāti vassacchedāpatti rakkhitabbā. Kasmā? Āpadāsu hītiādi. “Ayaṃ uposatho cātuddasikoti pucchitabba”nti vuttaṃ, tampi terasiyaṃyeva, etarahi pana bhikkhuniyo cātuddasiyaṃyeva gantvā “kadā ayya uposatho”ti pucchanti. “Jāyāyo vā jāriyo vā”ti adhippāyena vuttaṃ kira. “Gaccheyya ce, āpattī”ti pāṭho. Dve tissoti dvīhi tīhi. Ekato āgatānaṃ vasena “tāhī”ti bahuvacanaṃ vuttanti adhippāyo. “Ekā bhikkhunī vā bahū bhikkhunī vā bahūhi bhikkhunupassayehi ovādatthāya pesitā”ti vacanassa vitthāro “bhikkhunisaṅgho ca ayya bhikkhuniyo cā”tiādinā vutto. “Bhikkhunisaṅgho ca ayya bhikkhuniyo cā’tiādi nānāupassayehi pesitāya vacana”nti ca “aparipuṇṇasaṅghapuggalanānāvāsadutiyavacanavasena pañcakkhattuṃ upasaṅkamanaṃ vutta”nti ca likhitaṃ. Yasmiṃ āvāse pātimokkhuddeso na pavattati, tatthāpi yācanaṃ sampaṭicchitvā punadivase yena paṭiggahitaṃ, tena “natthi koci bhikkhu bhikkhunovādako sammato”tiādi vattabbaṃ. Atthi ce sammato, niddisitabbo. “Sayameva ce sammato, aha’nti vattabba”nti vuttaṃ. Sace sammato vā ovādapaṭiggāhako vā pātimokkhaṃ uddisati, aññena ārocāpetabbanti eke, “attanāpi ārocetuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti ca vadanti. Kesuci potthakesu “ayyānaṃ pavāretī”ti likhitaṃ, evaṃ sati “ayyassa pavāremī”ti vattabbaṃ, potthake natthi.

148-9. Those ordained in the presence of bhikkhus are, namely, those who have changed gender, or the five hundred Sākyan women. Because of the statement, 'For the purpose of teaching the Dhamma and releasing from offenses,' it is established that everywhere, by the term 'mātugāma,' the inclusion of a bhikkhunī is accomplished. However, by the term 'bhikkhunī,' 'mātugāma' is included in the training rule on crossing a river, but not elsewhere. 'Osāretabbā' is the Pāḷi reading; the meaning is that the Pāḷi should be recited to the end. 'Osāretabba' is the commentary's Pāḷi reading. If one were to say: 'Since there is no fault when paying homage in one place, is it permissible for one among many bhikkhunīs to pay homage?' There is nothing to be done by the bhikkhus; it is to be done only by the bhikkhunī. Therefore, it is not permissible. Regarding 'wherever she is seated,' they say it means 'seated within twelve cubits.' The phrase `gantukāmā` (those wishing to go) does not here refer to bhikkhus wishing to go after being invited; rather, the meaning is that only those wishing to enter the rains-residence are intended. 'From where?' means from the bhikkhunī monastery. 'There?' means in the bhikkhunī monastery. Although it follows from the statement 'bhikkhus who give advice' that a monastery is 'with bhikkhus' only because of the advising bhikkhus and not because of all bhikkhus, nevertheless, in the absence of a bhikkhunī-adviser, because it is necessary to go to request for the sake of advice and communion, it should be understood that even with other bhikkhus, it is still a monastery 'with bhikkhus.' 'She should be protected' means the offense of breaking the rains-residence should be guarded against. Therefore, he said, 'in times of danger,' etc. It was said, 'It should be asked, “Is this Uposatha on the fourteenth?”' That too should be asked only on the thirteenth day. But nowadays, bhikkhunīs go on the fourteenth day itself and ask, 'Venerable sirs, when is the Uposatha?' It is said that this was spoken with the intention: 'Are they wives or mistresses?' There is a reading: 'If one should go, there is an offense.' 'Two or three' means 'by two or three.' The intention is that the plural 'tāhi' (by them) is used on account of their having come together. The elaboration of the statement, 'One bhikkhunī or many bhikkhunīs sent from many bhikkhunī residences for the purpose of advice,' is stated by 'the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs and the venerable bhikkhunīs,' etc. And it is written: '“The Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs and the venerable bhikkhunīs, etc.” is the statement of one sent from various residences,' and 'The fivefold approach is stated by way of the second statement regarding an incomplete Saṅgha, an individual, and various residences.' In a monastery where the recitation of the Pātimokkha does not occur, even there, having accepted the request, on the next day, the one by whom it was accepted should say, 'There is no bhikkhu appointed as a bhikkhunī-adviser,' etc. If there is an appointed one, he should be indicated. It is said, 'If he himself is the appointed one, he should say, “I am.”' If the appointed one or the one who accepted the request for advice recites the Pātimokkha, some say it should be announced by another, and they also say it is permissible to announce it oneself. In some books, it is written, 'She invites the venerable sirs.' This being so, it should be said, 'I invite the venerable sir'; this is not found in the book.

Ovādasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rule on Admonition is concluded.

2. Atthaṅgatasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

2. The Explanation of the Atthaṅgata Training Rule

153. Munātīti [M 0.0306] jānāti. Antaradhāyatipīti ettha taduttamaṃ ce atthi, taṃ passāmi, yaṃ vicittaṃ vā, tadatthañca. Taggha kāraṇaṃ. Saha uppādamanantarā kiriyā. Yamā ca te manasā katatra netvāti. Yathā pāto siyā pāto bhavaṃ pātova udakato uggantvā ṭhitaṃ, tathā virocamānaṃ aṅgīrasaṃ buddhaṃ passa, na kevalaṃ padumaṃ viya, virocamānaṃ tapantamādiccamivantalikkheti [V 0.0274] sambandho. Atha vā aṅgīrasaṃ buddhaṃ padumaṃva virocamānaṃ sūriyaṃva tapantaṃ passa buddhaṃ. Yathā pāto siyā phullamavītagandhaṃ kokanudasaṅkhātaṃ padumaṃ passasi, tathā virocamānaṃ aṅgīrasaṃ buddhaṃ passa. Ubhayeneva hi bhagavato kanti dīpitāti katvā dīpitaguṇasubhaṃ buddhaṃ sakkatvā taṃ kantiṃ pūjeyya. Pūjaneyyatopi vītināmeyya iti lakkhaye. “Ekato upasampannāyā”ti pāḷi.

153. 'Munāti' means 'he knows'. Herein, regarding 'antaradhāyati', if there is a psychic power superior to that, I shall see it; whatever wondrous psychic power there is, I shall also see that psychic power for the sake of its wondrousness. Thus, indeed, having made it the cause, the action occurs immediately after the arising. And having led those psychic powers with the mind to wherever one wishes to perform them, there are also the twin psychic powers, and so on. Just as a lotus that has come to be in the morning, arisen in the morning, having risen from the water in the morning and stands, so should you see the shining Buddha, the Aṅgīrasa. Not merely like a lotus, but see the Buddha, the Aṅgīrasa, shining, blazing like the sun in the sky—this connection should be made. Alternatively: see the Buddha, the Aṅgīrasa, shining like a lotus; see the Buddha, the Aṅgīrasa, blazing like the sun. Just as in the morning you see a lotus called a kokanuda, which is fully bloomed and has an unfading fragrance, so should you see the shining Buddha, the Aṅgīrasa. Indeed, by both similes, the Blessed One's pleasing quality is shown. Thinking thus, how could one honor that beautiful Buddha whose qualities have been shown? One should note that he surpasses even what is worthy of honor. There is the Pāḷi text: 'Ekato upasampannāya'.

156. “Ekato upasampannāna”nti aṭṭhakathāpāṭho. “Abhabbo tva”ntiādivacanato anukampāvasena saddhivihārikādiṃ saṅghikā vihārā nikkaḍḍhāpentassa anāpatti viya dissati. Abhabbo hi thero sañcicca taṃ kātuṃ, gavesitabbāva ettha yuttīti keci. Therena sikkhāpadapaññattito pubbe katanti mama takko.

156. The commentary reading is 'Ekato upasampannāna'. From the statement 'Abhabbo tva,' etc., it appears like there is no offense for one who, out of compassion, has a co-resident, etc., expelled from a monastery belonging to the Saṅgha. Indeed, the elder is incapable of doing that intentionally; herein, the proper reason should be sought—thus say some. My conjecture is that it was done by the elder before the laying down of the training rule.

Atthaṅgatasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Atthaṅgata Training Rule is concluded.

3. Bhikkhunupassayasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

3. The Explanation of the Bhikkhunupassaya Training Rule

162. “Ekarattampi vasantī”ti (pāci. 161) vacanato yattha rattiyaṃ na vasanti, tattha gantvā ovadituṃ vaṭṭatīti eke. Yadi evaṃ saṅketaṭṭhānaṃ gantvā ovadituṃ vaṭṭatīti siddhaṃ. “Tato addhayojaneyeva sabhikkhuko āvāso icchitabbo”ti na vattabbaṃ. Bhikkhunovādako ce addhayojanaṃ gantvā ovaditukāmo hoti, bhikkhunisaṅgho ca addhayojanaṃ gantvā sotukāmo, “vaṭṭatī”ti vattabbaṃ siyā, tañca na vuttaṃ, tasmā na vaṭṭati. Heṭṭhimaparicchedena pana “ekarattampī”ti vuttaṃ. Tato paṭṭhāya upassayaṃ hoti, na upassayasaṅkhepena katamattenāti vuttaṃ hoti. Yattha vāsūpagatā [M 0.0307] bhikkhuniyo, so upassayasaṅkhyaṃ gacchati, tattha na gantvā ovādo dātabbo. Ekāvāse divā vaṭṭatīti eke, vicāretvā yuttataraṃ gahetabbaṃ.

162. Because of the statement, 'They reside even for one night,' some say it is allowable to go and advise where they do not reside at night. If so, it is established that one may go to an appointed place to advise them. It should not be said, 'From there, a residence with monks should be sought only within half a yojana.' If an advisor of bhikkhunīs wishes to go half a yojana to advise, and the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs also wishes to go half a yojana to listen, it would have to be said, 'It is allowable'—but this was not said; therefore, it is not allowable. However, by the lower definition, 'even for one night' is stated. From that point onward, it is an upassaya; it is said that it does not become an upassaya merely by being designated as such. Where bhikkhunīs have gone to reside, that comes to be designated as an upassaya; one should not go there to give advice. Some say it is allowable during the day in the same residence—this should be investigated, and the more suitable interpretation adopted.

Bhikkhunupassayasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Bhikkhunupassaya Training Rule is concluded.

4. Āmisasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

4. The Explanation of the Āmisa Training Rule

164. “Upasampannaṃ saṅghena asammata”nti pāḷivacanato, “sammatena vā saṅghena vā bhāraṃ [V 0.0275] katvā ṭhapito”ti aṭṭhakathāvacanato ca aṭṭhahaṅgehi samannāgato sammatena vā vippavasitukāmena “yāvāhaṃ āgamissāmi, tāva te bhāro hotū”ti yācitvā ṭhapito, tassābhāvato saṅghena vā tatheva bhāraṃ katvā ṭhapito aṭṭhahi garudhammehi ovadituṃ labhati, pageva aññena dhammenāti siddhaṃ. “Yo pana bhikkhu asammato bhikkhuniyo ovadeyya, pācittiya”nti pageva bhāraṃ katvā aṭṭhapitaṃ sandhāya vuttanti veditabbaṃ. Abhayagirivāsīnampi idameva mataṃ, anugaṇṭhipade pana imaṃ nayaṃ paṭikkhipitvā “natthi kocī”tiādinā “etarahi ovādako asammato bhikkhunovādako nāmā”ti vatvā “yaṃ pana andhakaṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttaṃ ‘upasampannaṃ saṅghena kammavācāya asammataṃ, bhikkhusaṅghena pana bhikkhunisaṅghassa anuggahaṃ karotha, bhikkhuniyo ovadatha, bhikkhusaṅghassa ca karotha phāsuvihāranti evaṃ yācitvā ṭhapito bhikkhusaṅghaṃ āpucchitvā, tato so thero bhikkhuniyo ovadati, evarūpaṃ bhikkhusaṅghena asammatanti, tatra vuttanayeneva attho gahetabbo”ti vuttaṃ. Porāṇagaṇṭhipade pana “asammato gāmaṃ ovādatthāya āgatānaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ vacanaṃ sutvā paṭivacanaṃ dento saṅghānumatiyā, na ñatticatutthenā”ti vuttaṃ, taṃ anugaṇṭhipadamatena sameti, andhakaṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttavacanaṃ tena sameti, tañca pāḷivacanaṃ, na hi ovādapaṭiggāhako, pātimokkhuddesako vā “pāsādikena sampādetū”ti vacanamattena bhikkhunovādako nāma hoti. Hotīti ce, anupasampannopi tattakena vacanena “bhikkhunovādako hotū”ti vattabbo. Hotīti ce, yaṃ vuttaṃ gaṇṭhānugaṇṭhipadesu “asammato nāma asammatabhāvena ‘bahussuto tvaṃ ovadāhī’ti [M 0.0308] saṅghena bhāraṃ katvā ṭhapito”ti. Ettha bāhusaccena kiṃ payojanaṃ. Anugaṇṭhipadeyeva “abhayagirivāsī vadatīti sutvā sammatena vā āṇatto ovadituṃ labhatīti dhammasiritthero pacchā anujānātī”ti vuttaṃ. Kiṃ bahukāya. “Pāsādikena sampādetū”ti ettakamattena bhikkhunovādako hoti. Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “bhāraṃ katvā”ti iminā kiṃ payojanaṃ, tattakampi vattuṃ añño na labhati, tena ca “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ṭhapetvā bālaṃ gilānaṃ gamikaṃ avasesehi ovādaṃ gahetu”nti (cūḷava. 414) ayaṃ pāḷi virujjheyya. Kathaṃ? Tassa hi “na, bhikkhave, ovādo na paccāharitabbo”ti (cūḷava. 415) canato sammatāsammatabhāvena natthi kocīti “pāsādikena sampādetū”ti vattabbaṃ siyā, vadanto ca idha paṭhamena āpattiyā kāretabbo hotīti. Hotu asammatattā, akatabhārattā ca. Imassa ca bhikkhunovādakatte imassa khīyanena dukkaṭaṃ siyā, sabbametaṃ aniṭṭhaṃ, tasmā aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “ayamettha bhikkhunovādako nāmā”ti avuttattā tathā bhāraṃ katvā ṭhapito ovadituṃ labhatiyeva, nāññoti ācariyo.

164. From the Pāḷi statement, 'not appointed by the Saṅgha,' and from the commentary statement, 'appointed by making it a duty, either by one who is appointed or by the Saṅgha,' it is established that a bhikkhu endowed with eight qualities is permitted to admonish with the eight grave rules—when he has been appointed by one who is appointed; or by one wishing to go away, having been requested, 'For as long as I shall be gone, let the duty be yours'; or, in his absence, appointed by the Saṅgha in the same way by making it a duty—what then to speak of by another rule. This is established. The rule, 'Whatever bhikkhu, not being appointed, should admonish the bhikkhunīs, it is a pācittiya offense,' should be understood as referring to one who has not been appointed by having the duty made from the outset. The Abhayagiri residents also hold this same view. However, in the Anugaṇṭhipada, rejecting this method, it is stated, beginning with 'There is none,' and further, 'Nowadays, an admonisher who is not appointed is called a bhikkhunī-admonisher.' But what is stated in the Andhakaṭṭhakathā: 'One who is fully ordained but not appointed by the Saṅgha through a formal act, but who has been appointed after being requested by the Bhikkhu Saṅgha thus: "Please show favor to the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha, admonish the bhikkhunīs, and also provide for the comfortable abiding of the Bhikkhu Saṅgha," having consulted the Bhikkhu Saṅgha; therefore that elder admonishes the bhikkhunīs—such a one is not appointed by the Bhikkhu Saṅgha. In that case, the meaning should be taken according to the method stated there.' However, in the Porāṇagaṇṭhipada, it is stated: 'An unappointed one, hearing the words of bhikkhunīs who have come to the village for admonishment, gives a reply with the Saṅgha's consent, not by a ñatticatuttha-kamma.' That accords with the view of the Anugaṇṭhipada, and the statement in the Andhakaṭṭhakathā accords with that, and that is a Pāḷi statement. For indeed, one who receives admonishment or one who recites the Pātimokkha does not become a bhikkhunī-admonisher merely by the statement 'Let him accomplish it with grace.' If it is said that he does become one, then even an unordained person could become a 'bhikkhunī-admonisher' by such a statement. If it is said that he does become one, then regarding what was stated in the Gaṇṭhipadas and Anugaṇṭhipadas—'An unappointed one means one who has been appointed by the Saṅgha by making it a duty, saying, "You are very learned, you should admonish"'—what is the use of great learning here? In the Anugaṇṭhipada itself, it is stated: 'Hearing that the Abhayagiri residents say so, one who is appointed or ordered is permitted to admonish—thus the elder Dhammasiri later concedes.' What is the use of saying much? By merely saying, 'Let him accomplish it with grace,' one becomes a bhikkhunī-admonisher. In the commentary, what is the use of the phrase 'having made it a duty'? Even that much cannot be said by another. Moreover, the Pāḷi passage, 'I allow, O bhikkhus, having excluded the foolish, the sick, and the traveler, for the rest to receive admonishment' (Cūḷavagga 414), would be contradicted by this. How? For, from the statement, 'O bhikkhus, admonishment is not to be refused' (Cūḷavagga 415), it follows that there is no one who can refuse based on the admonisher's status as appointed or not appointed. Therefore, it should be said, 'Let him accomplish it with grace.' And one who speaks thus should be made to incur an offense under the first rule here. Let it be so—due to not being appointed and the duty not having been made. And if this one were a bhikkhunī-admonisher, by disparaging him there would be a dukkaṭa offense. All this is undesirable. Therefore, because the commentary does not say, 'Herein, this is what is called a bhikkhunī-admonisher,' only one who has been so appointed by having the duty made is indeed permitted to admonish, and no other—so says the teacher.

Āmisasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule concerning material things is finished.

5. Cīvaradānasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

5. The Explanation of the Training Rule Concerning the Giving of Robes

169. Sādiyissasīti [V 0.0276] pucchā.

169. “Will you consent?”—this is the question.

Cīvaradānasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule concerning the giving of robes is finished.

6. Cīvarasibbanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

6. The Explanation of the Training Rule Concerning the Sewing of Robes

176. Vañcetvāti “tava ñātikāyā”ti avatvā “ekissā bhikkhuniyā”ti ettakameva vatvā, te hi “ekissā”ti vacanaṃ sutvā aññātikāya santakasaññino sibbesuṃ. Imasmiṃ sikkhāpade “cīvaraṃ nāma channaṃ [M 0.0309] cīvarānaṃ aññataraṃ cīvara”nti ettakameva pāḷi, tena vuttaṃ “cīvaranti yaṃ nivāsetuṃ vā pārupituṃ vā”tiādi. “Vikappanupagaṃ pacchima”nti ca likhitaṃ, so pamādalekho.

176. Regarding 'having deceived': without saying, “for your relative,” but saying only this much, “for a certain bhikkhunī,” those pupils, having heard the words “for a certain one,” sewed it, perceiving it as belonging to a non-relative. In this training rule, only this much is the Pāḷi text: “A robe means one of the six robes.” Therefore, it is said, “A robe is that which one may wear as a lower garment or put on as an upper garment,” and so on. And, “The last is suitable for vikappana” is also written; that is a text written through negligence.

Cīvarasibbanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule concerning the sewing of robes is finished.

7. Saṃvidhānasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

7. The Explanation of the Training Rule Concerning Arrangement

181. Tā bhikkhuniyo dūsayiṃsūti vipariṇāmo kātabbo.

181. Regarding “they corrupted those bhikkhunīs,” a change of construction is to be made.

182-4. Sampadantīti padasā gacchanti. Vuttanayenevāti “sampatanti etthāti sampāto”tiādinā. Padagate upacāro na labbhati, accāsannattā missaṃ viya hotīti. Kukkuṭavassitaparicchinno mahāaṭṭhakathāyaṃ. “Tampi vohārenā”ti likhitaṃ. “Yebhuyyena tathā sanniveso hotīti katvā aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttaṃ, tasmā na pamādalekho”ti ca, “ukkaṭṭhaparicchedena vuttaṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ, tato uddhaṃ addhayojanalakkhaṇasampattaṃ nāma hotīti gahetabba”nti ca vuttaṃ. “Kappiyabhūmi kirāyaṃ…pe… na vadantī”ti vuttaṃ. Duddasañhettha kāraṇaṃ. Kataraṃ pana tanti? “Gacchāmāti saṃvidahati, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti vuttaṃ. Tattha “gacchāmā”ti vattamānavacanantañca, amagge bhikkhunupassayādimhi na sambhavatiyeva manussānaṃ antaragharādimhi maggasaṅkhepagamanato, uccāsayanādiuppattiṭṭhānattā ca. Na titthiyaseyyāya vā pabbajitāvāsattā. Dvāreti samīpatthe bhummaṃ, tasmā taṃ dassetuṃ puna “rathikāyā”ti āha. Sesaaṭṭhakathāyaṃ [V 0.0277] “etthantare saṃvidahitepi bhikkhuno dukkaṭa”nti āgatattā na sameti. “Gāmantare”ti vacanato aññagāmassa upacārokkamane eva āpatti. “Addhayojane”ti vacanato atikkamaneyeva yuttaṃ.

182-4. Sampadantīti means: they go on foot. Vuttanayenevāti means: by the method already stated, such as, "They arrive here, thus it is an arrival." In the case of going on foot, the designation 'vicinity' is not obtained; because of being too close, it is as if mixed. The area defined by a cock's crow is mentioned in the Great Commentary. It is written: "That too is by convention." And also: "It is stated in the commentary because for the most part, such is the settlement; therefore, it is not a careless writing." And it is also said: "It is stated in the commentary with the maximum definition; it should be understood that beyond that, the attainment of the characteristic of half a yojana does not occur." It is stated: "This is indeed a suitable ground... (etc.)... they do not say." For the reason here is difficult to see. What then is that principle? It is stated: "If one makes an arrangement, saying, 'Let us go,' there is an offense of wrong conduct." There, the word "gacchāma" is also a present tense ending. On a non-path, such as in a bhikkhunī's residence, it simply does not occur, both because of people going in the manner of a path within houses, etc., and because of it being a place where high seats, etc., arise. Or, it does not occur in the residence of heretics, because it is a dwelling of renunciants. The word dvāre is in the locative case with the meaning of 'nearness'; therefore, to show that meaning, he again said rathikāyā. Because it is stated in the remaining commentary, "Even if an arrangement is made in this interval, there is a wrong conduct for the bhikkhu," it does not agree. Because of the phrase "in another village," the offense is only in entering the vicinity of another village. Because of the phrase "at half a yojana," it is proper only in the case of exceeding it.

185. Raṭṭhabhedeti vilope. Porāṇagaṇṭhipade “tayopi saṅketā kāladivasamaggavasena, tattha pacchimeneva āpattī”ti vuttaṃ. “Iminā maggenā”ti vissajjetvā aññena gacchanti ce, āpattiyevāti attho.

185. Raṭṭhabhedeti means: in devastation. In the ancient gloss it is said: "There are also three kinds of appointments: by way of time, day, and path. Among them, the offense is only by the last one." If, having arranged, "By this path," they then go by another, there is an offense indeed; this is the meaning.

Saṃvidhānasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Exposition on the Training Rule Concerning Arrangements is concluded.

8. Nāvābhiruhanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

8. Exposition on the Training Rule Concerning Boarding a Boat

189. Nadiyā [M 0.0310] kuto gāmantaranti ce? “Yassā nadiyā”tiādimāha. Gāmantaragaṇanāyāti yasmiṃ gāmatitthe āruḷho, taṃ ṭhapetvā aññagāmagaṇanāya. “Mātugāmopi idha saṅgahaṃ gacchatī”ti ācariyassa takko, teneva “ubhayattha ekato upasampannāya dukkaṭaṃ, sikkhamānāya sāmaṇeriyā anāpattī”ti ca na vuttaṃ. Eseva nayo aññesupi evarūpesu.

189. If it is asked, 'How is there another village on a river?' To answer this, he said, 'By which river,' and so on. Regarding the reckoning of another village: having arrived at a certain village landing, excluding that one, it is by the count of another village. 'Even a woman is included here,' is the teacher’s reasoning; for that very reason, it was not said, 'For one fully ordained in both Sanghas together, there is a dukkaṭa offense; for a sikkhamānā or a female novice, there is no offense.' This is the same method in other such training rules.

191. “Lokassādamittasanthavavasena keḷipurekkhārā saṃvidahitvā”ti vuttattā akusalacittaṃ lokavajjanti vattabbanti? Na vattabbaṃ, “keḷipurekkhārā”ti vacanaṃ yebhuyyatāya vuttaṃ. Porāṇagaṇṭhipade ca “tīṇi cittāni tisso vedanā”ti vuttaṃ, saṃvidahanakāle vā keḷipurekkhāro bhikkhu saṃvidahati, āpatti bhikkhuno gāmantarokkamane, addhayojanātikkame vā. Kusalacitto vā hoti paccavekkhanto, cetiyādīni vā passanto, abyākatacitto vā hoti kilamathavasena niddāyantoti ticittāni gahitānīti veditabbā.

191. Should it be said that because it was stated, 'having arranged with entertainment as the precursor, due to delight in the world, friendship, and intimacy,' an unwholesome mind is blameworthy in the world? It should not be said. The statement 'with entertainment as the precursor' was said with regard to the majority of cases. And in the ancient glossary, it is said, 'three minds, three feelings.' Or, at the time of arranging, a bhikkhu arranges with entertainment as the precursor; the offense for the bhikkhu is upon entering another village or upon exceeding half a yojana. Or, while going along reflecting or seeing shrines and so on, one may have a wholesome mind. Or, falling asleep due to fatigue, one may have an indeterminate mind. Therefore, it should be understood that the three minds are taken.

Nāvābhiruhanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Exposition on the Training Rule Concerning Boarding a Boat is concluded.

9. Paripācitasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

9. Exposition on the Training Rule Concerning Causing Food to Be Prepared

192. Ceṭaketi dārake. Taruṇapotaketi porāṇā. “Pāpabhikkhūnaṃ pakkhupacchedāya idaṃ paññattaṃ, tasmā pañca bhojaneyevāpatti vuttā”ti likhitaṃ.

192. Ceṭake means young boys. The ancients say it means young, tender monks. It is written: 'This was laid down to cut off the faction of evil monks; therefore, the offense was stated only for the five kinds of staple food.'

194-7. Nipphāditanti [V 0.0278] viññattiyā na hoti, kintu parikathādīhi, tasmā iminā sikkhāpadena anāpatti, taṃ sandhāya “sabbattha anāpattī”ti vuttaṃ. “Kathānusārena tattha pasīditvā denti, idaṃ paripācitaṃ na hoti, vaṭṭantī”ti paṭhamasikkhāpade vuttattāti dhammasiritthero, upatissatthero pana “itarampi vaṭṭatiyevā”ti āha. Porāṇagaṇṭhipade pana “yasmā devadatto pakatiyā tattha bhikkhuniparipācitaṃ bhuñjati, tasmā imaṃ aṭṭhuppattiṃ nidānaṃ katvā idaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññatta”nti vuttaṃ.

194-7. Nipphāditan ti means it is not accomplished by a hint, but rather by preliminary talk and so on. Therefore, by this training rule, there is no offense. With reference to that, it was said, 'There is no offense in all cases.' The Elder Dhammasiri said: 'Because it was stated in the first training rule, "Following the sequence of the talk, having gained faith in that person, they give; this is not ‘caused to be prepared’; it is allowable."' The Elder Upatissa, however, said: 'The other kind of food is also indeed allowable.' But in the ancient glosses, it is said: 'Because Devadatta, by nature, eats food there that was caused to be prepared by a bhikkhunī, this training rule was laid down having made this origin story the cause.'

Paripācitasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Exposition on the Training Rule Concerning Causing Food to Be Prepared is concluded.

10. Rahonisajjasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

10. Exposition on the Training Rule Concerning Secluded Sitting

198. “Upanandassa [M 0.0311] catutthasikkhāpadena cā”ti pāṭho.

198. The reading is: 'And by the fourth training rule of Upananda.'

Rahonisajjasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Exposition on the Training Rule Concerning Secluded Sitting is concluded.

Samatto vaṇṇanākkamena ovādavaggo tatiyo.

The third chapter, the Admonition Chapter, is completed in the order of the commentary.

4. Bhojanavaggo

4. The Fourth Chapter: The Chapter on Food

1. Āvasathapiṇḍasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

1. Exposition on the Training Rule Concerning Alms-food in a Public Rest House

203-4. Pūgassāti pūgena. Kukkuccāyantoti nissaraṇenettha bhavitabbaṃ, taṃ mayaṃ na jānāmāti sanniṭṭhānassa karaṇavasena “kukkuccāyanto”ti vuccati. Yathā hi āyasmā upāli nayaggāhena “anāpatti āvuso supinantenā”ti (pārā. 78) āha, tathā theropi “anāpatti gilānassā”ti kasmā na paricchindatīti? Anattādhikārattā vinayapaññattiyā, “nāyaṃ attano okāso”ti paṭikkhittattā, sikkhāpadassa aparipuṇṇattā. Paṭhamapārājikasikkhāpade paripuṇṇaṃ katvā paññatteyeva hi so thero “anāpatti supinantenā”ti [V 0.0279] āha “aññatra supinantā”ti vuttapadānusārenāti. Yasmā odissa ayāvadattheva dāyakānaṃ pīḷā natthi, tasmā “anodissa yāvadattho”ti vuttaṃ.

203-4-6. Pūgassāti means 'by a group'. Regarding kukkuccāyanto: Herein, it should be understood as an absence of recollection. By way of making the conclusion, 'We do not know that point,' it is called kukkuccāyanto (being scrupulous). For, just as the Venerable Upāli, having grasped the method, said, 'Friend, there is no offense in the case of a dream,' in the same way, why does the Elder not decide, 'There is no offense for one who is sick'? Because the laying down of the Vinaya is not his own authority; because it was rejected with the thought, 'This is not my own sphere'; and because of the incompleteness of the training rule. Indeed, it was only when the first Pārājika training rule was laid down after being made complete that the Elder (Upāli) said, 'There is no offense in the case of a dream,' in accordance with the stated phrase, 'except in the case of a dream.' Because when something is designated but not for as long as one wishes, there is no affliction for the donors, therefore it was said, 'undesignated, for as long as one wishes.'

208. “Antarāmagge ekadivasa’nti ekaṃyeva sandhāya vutta”nti ca “eseva nayoti vuttanayameva dassetuṃ gantvā paccāgacchanto hītiādimāhā”ti ca “suddhacitto hutvā pakatigamaneva bhuñjituṃ labhatī”ti ca “agilānassa gilānasaññino kāyena samuṭṭhātī”ti ca likhitaṃ.

208. 208. And it is written: 'Regarding 'on the road for one day,' this was said with reference to eating only once.' And: 'Regarding 'this is the very method,' to show the very method that was stated, he said 'having gone and then returning,' and so on.' And: 'Having a pure mind, one is allowed to eat in the usual way.' And: 'For one who is not sick but has the perception of being sick, the offense arises through the body.'

Āvasathapiṇḍasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on alms-food in lodgings is concluded.

2. Gaṇabhojanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

2. Explanation of the Training Rule on Group Meals

209-218. Guḷhapaṭicchannoti apākaṭova. Eko puttenāti ekassekaṃ bhattaṃ “ahaṃ aññena nimantito”ti na vuccati. “Sace ekato gaṇhanti [M 0.0312], gaṇabhojanaṃ hotī”ti (pāci. aṭṭha. 217-218) vuttattā cattāro upāsakā cattāro bhikkhū visuṃ visuṃ nimantetvā hatthapāse ṭhitānaṃ ce denti, gaṇabhojanaṃ hoti evāti eke, taṃ na yuttaṃ viya. “Viññattito pasavane gaṇassa ekato gahaṇe iminā sikkhāpadena āpatti, visuṃ gahaṇe paṇītabhojanasūpodanaviññattīhī”ti likhitaṃ. “Viññattito pasavanaṃ aṭṭhuppattivasena aṭṭhakathāyaṃ anuññātaṃ. Sūpodanādivasena tattha āpatti evā”ti vuttaṃ, taṃ na yuttaṃ. Kasmā? Parivāre (pari. 168) eva dvinnaṃ ākārānaṃ āgatattā, tasmā aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “anuññāta”nti duvuttaṃ. Aṭṭhuppattiyaṃyeva pākaṭanti “padabhājane na vutta”nti vattabbaṃ. Ekato gaṇhantīti gahitabhattāpi aññe yāva gaṇhanti, tāva ce tiṭṭhanti, ekato gaṇhantiyeva nāma. “Gacchati ce, anāpattī”ti vadanti.

209-218. Regarding guḷhapaṭicchanna, it was simply not apparent. Regarding eko puttena, it is not said of one meal for one monk, 'I have been invited by another.' Because it is said, 'If they receive together, it is a group meal,' some say that if four lay devotees invite four monks separately and give to them while they are standing within arm's reach, it is indeed a group meal; this, however, appears to be not proper. It is written: 'In the case of causing a meal to be procured through an intimation, when it is received together by a group, there is an offense under this training rule; when it is received separately, there are offenses under the training rules on intimating for fine food, rice, and curry.' It is said: 'Causing a meal to be procured through intimation is permitted in the commentary on the basis of the occasion of the arising of the rule. There, an offense arises on account of rice, curry, and so on.' That is not proper. Why? Because in the Parivāra itself, the two modes have been mentioned. Therefore, the statement in the commentary, 'it is permitted,' is a misstatement. It is clear in the occasion of the arising of the rule itself; therefore, it should be said, 'It is not stated in the word-analysis.' Regarding 'they receive together': even having received their meal, if they wait while others receive theirs, it is indeed called 'receiving together.' They say, 'If one goes away, there is no offense.'

Etthāha – “paṭiggahaṇameva hettha pamāṇa”nti vuttaṃ, atha kasmā pāḷiyaṃ “gaṇabhojanaṃ nāma yattha cattāro…pe… bhuñjanti, etaṃ gaṇabhojanaṃ nāmā”ti (pāci. 218) vuttanti? Vuccati – yatthāti upayogatthe bhummavacanaṃ. Cattāroti gaṇassa heṭṭhimaparicchedanidassanaṃ. Pañcannaṃ bhojanānanti āpattippahonakabhojananidassanaṃ. Aññatarena bhojanena nimantitāti akappiyanimantananidassanaṃ. Nimantanavaseneva pana gaṇabhojanassa vuttattā “nimantitā bhuñjantīti vutta”nti vuttaṃ. “Aññataraṃ bhojanaṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjantī”ti [V 0.0280] pana na vuttaṃ aṭṭhuppattiyaṃyeva pākaṭattā. Yaṃ bhuñjantīti evaṃ sambandho veditabbo. Tattha bhuñjantīti paṭiggāhakaniyamavacanaṃ. Na hi appaṭiggahitakaṃ bhikkhū bhuñjanti. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti “gaṇassa yato paṭiggahitāhārabhojanahetu pācittiya”nti. Āgantukapaṭṭaṃ moghasuttena sibbitvā ṭhapenti, tattha anuvāte yathā ekatalaṃ hoti, tathā hatthehi ghaṭṭeti. Valetīti āvaṭṭeti. Parivattananti suttaṃ gaṇhantānaṃ sukhaggahaṇatthaṃ suttaparivattanaṃ karoti, paṭṭaṃ sibbantānaṃ sukhasibbanatthaṃ paṭṭaparivattanañca. Navacīvarakārako idhādhippeto, na itaroti. “Bimbisāraṃ āpucchitvā sambhāre kayiramāneyeva kālā atikkantā, pacchā gaṇabhojanasikkhāpade paññatte bhagavantaṃ upasaṅkamitvā pucchī”ti vadanti, aññathā aṭṭhakathāya virujjhanato.

Here, a questioner objects: 'It is stated in the commentary, “Receiving itself is the standard here.” If so, why is it stated in the Pāḷi text: “A group meal is where four... eat; this is called a group meal”?' The reply is given: The word `yattha` (where) is a locative case form used in the sense of 'usage' (i.e., in the accusative sense). The word `cattāro` (four) indicates the lower limit of the group. The phrase `pañcannaṃ bhojanānaṃ` (of the five foods) indicates food sufficient for an offense. The phrase `aññatarena bhojanena nimantitā` (invited with one of the foods) indicates an improper invitation. However, since the group meal is mentioned solely by way of invitation, it is stated, 'Being invited, they eat.' But 'having requested a certain food, they eat' is not stated, because it is already evident in the origin story itself. The connection should be understood thus: 'That which they eat...' Therein, the word `bhuñjanti` (they eat) is a term specifying the act of receiving. For indeed, monks do not eat what has not been received. This is what is meant: 'A Pācittiya offense is incurred because of the group's eating of received food.' They set aside the guest-patch after sewing it with a temporary thread; there, along the border, they rub it with their hands so that it becomes a single flat surface. `Valeti` means 'one rolls it up.' As for `parivattana` (turning), one does the turning of the thread for the sake of easy handling for those taking the thread, and also the turning of the cloth-patch for the sake of easy sewing for those sewing it. Here, a maker of a new robe is intended, not the other. They say: 'Having taken leave of Bimbisāra, while the materials were still being prepared, the time elapsed. Afterwards, when the training rule on group meals was laid down, they approached the Blessed One and asked.' This is said because otherwise, it would contradict the commentary.

220. “Dve [M 0.0313] tayo ekatoti yepi akappiyanimantanaṃ sādiyitvā”tiādivacanena akappiyanimantanapaccayā eva anāpatti, viññattito āpattiyevāti dīpeti. Animantito catuttho yassa tadetaṃ animantitacatutthaṃ. Esa nayo sabbattha. Pavesetvāti nisīdāpetvā. Cīvaradānasamayaladdhakacatukkaṃ cīvarakārasamayaladdhakacatukkanti evamādīni. Tāni cāti yehi bhojanehi visaṅketo natthi, tāni. Mahāthereti upasampanne. Aṭṭhatvāti ṭhitena nimittaṃ dassitaṃ hoti. Tattha tattha gantvāti rathikādīsu bhikkhusamīpe gantvā. Imasmiṃ pana sikkhāpade katthaci potthake “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, cīvaradānasamaye gaṇabhojanaṃ bhuñjituṃ. Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhūna”nti pāṭho dissati. Katthaci “bhuñjitu”nti vatvā “evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyāthā”ti pāṭho, ayaṃ sobhano.

220. By the text beginning with, “Dve tayo ekato... yepi akappiyanimantanaṃ sādiyitvā,” it shows this meaning: there is no offense merely on account of consenting to an improper invitation, but there is indeed an offense on account of an intimation. That for which the fourth is uninvited, that is 'having an uninvited fourth.' This is the method in all cases. 'Pavesetvā' means having made them sit. The group of four obtained at the time of robe-giving, the group of four obtained at the time of robe-making, and so forth. 'Tāni ca' means those foods for which there is no discrepancy. 'Aṭṭhatvā' means a sign is shown by one who is standing. 'Tattha tattha gantvā' means having gone to the vicinity of a monk in places such as main roads, etc. However, in this training rule, in a certain manuscript, the reading is seen: “I allow, O monks, to eat a group meal at the time of robe-giving. Thus this was laid down by the Blessed One for the monks.” In a certain manuscript, after saying “to eat,” there is the reading, “And so, O monks, you should recite this training rule.” This reading is good.

Gaṇabhojanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on group meals is concluded.

3. Paramparabhojanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

3. Commentary on the Training Rule Concerning Successive Eating

221. Adhiṭṭhitāti niccappavattā. Badaracuṇṇasakkarādīhi yojitaṃ badarasāḷavaṃ. Kirakammakārenāti kirassa kammakārena.

221. 'Adhiṭṭhitā' means regularly established. A jujube confection prepared with jujube powder, sugar, and so forth. 'Kirakammakārena' means by the worker of Kira.

226. “Vikappetvā gaṇhāhī”ti etthāhu porāṇattherā “bhagavato sammukhā avikappetvā gehato nikkhamitvā rathikāya aññatarassa bhikkhuno santike vikappesi, vikappentena pana ‘mayhaṃ bhattapaccāsaṃ itthannāmassa dammī’ti vattabbaṃ, itarena vattabbaṃ ‘tassa santakaṃ paribhuñja vā [V 0.0281] yathāpaccayaṃ vā karohī’”ti. Pañcasusahadhammikesūti sammukhā ṭhitassa sahadhammikassa yassa vikappetukāmo, taṃ sahadhammikaṃ adisvā gahaṭṭhassa vā santike, sayameva vā “pañcasu sahadhammikesu itthannāmassa vikappemī”ti vatvā bhuñjitabbanti eke, evaṃ sati thero tasmiṃyeva nisinnova tathā vācaṃ nicchāretvā paṭiggaṇhātīti takko dissati. Mahāpaccariyādīsu pana parammukhā vikappanāva vuttā, sā “tena hānanda, vikappetvā gaṇhāhī”ti iminā sameti, tathāpi mātikāṭṭhakathāyaṃ (kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. paramparabhojanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā) “tasmā yo bhikkhu pañcasu sahadhammikesu [M 0.0314] aññatarassa ‘mayhaṃ bhattapaccāsaṃ tuyhaṃ dammī’ti vā ‘vikappemī’ti vā evaṃ sammukhā vā ‘itthannāmassa dammī’ti vā ‘vikappemī’ti vā evaṃ parammukhā vā”ti vacanato sahadhammikassa santike eva vattabbaṃ, na sayamevāti dissati. Yasmā ayaṃ pacchimanayo porāṇagaṇṭhipadenapi sameti, tasmā idha mātikāṭṭhakathānusārena attho veditabbo. Ettha kiñcāpi “te manussā…pe… bhojanamadaṃsū”ti vacanato akappiyanimantanaṃ paññāyati, tathāpi therassa kukkuccuppattikāraṇena bhattena so nimantitoti veditabbo. Aññathā parato “dve tayo nimantane ekato bhuñjatī”ti vacanena, anāpattivārena ca virujjhati.

226. Regarding 'Having made it allowable, take it,' the ancient elders said: 'Without making it allowable in the presence of the Blessed One, having gone out from the house, he made it allowable on the street in the presence of a certain bhikkhu. Moreover, by the one making it allowable, it should be said, “I give my expectation of a meal to so-and-so,” and by the other it should be said, “Either make use of what is his, or do as is suitable.”' Regarding 'among the five co-religionists': some say that if one wishes to make it allowable to a co-religionist who is present, but without seeing that co-religionist, one may say in the presence of a householder or by oneself, 'Among the five co-religionists, I make it allowable for so-and-so,' and then it may be eaten. This being so, the reasoning appears that the elder, while sitting right there, utters such words and then accepts it. But in the Mahāpaccarī and other texts, making it allowable in absence is indeed stated. That agrees with this: 'Well then, Ānanda, having made it allowable, take it.' Nevertheless, according to the Mātikā-aṭṭhakathā, which states, 'Therefore, whichever bhikkhu says to one among the five co-religionists, either in person, “I give my expectation of a meal to you” or “I make it allowable,” or in absence, “I give it to so-and-so” or “I make it allowable,”' it appears that it must be said only in the presence of a co-religionist, and not just by oneself. Because this later method also agrees with the ancient gloss, the meaning here should be understood according to the Mātikā-aṭṭhakathā. Here, although from the statement, 'those people... gave food,' an improper invitation is apparent, nevertheless, it should be understood that he was invited with the meal that was the cause for the elder's scrupulousness to arise. Otherwise, it would be contradicted by the later statement, 'one eats from two or three invitations together,' and by the no-offense clause.

229. Etthāyaṃ vicāraṇā – “añño manusso pattaṃ gaṇhāti, na dātabba”nti vacanato aparabhāge akappiyanimantanena natthi payojanaṃ, pubbabhāgeyeva akappiyanimantanena payojananti svepi bhante āgaccheyyāthāti ettha kataraṃ akappiyanimantanaṃ, tasmā adhippāyo cettha pamāṇanti. Na, “piṇḍāya caritvā laddhabhattaṃ bhuñjati, āpattī”ti vacanatoti. Tattha “svepi bhante”ti ettha yathā vacanamattaṃ aggahetvā akappiyanimantanakkamena attho gahito, tathā “piṇḍāya caritvā”ti etthāpi antarā akappiyanimantanena laddhabhattaṃ sandhāya vuttanti attho gahetabbo. Piṇḍāya hi carantaṃ disvā “ettha, bhante, bhattaṃ gaṇhathā”ti dinnampi akappiyanimantanena laddhaṃ nāma hoti. Vohārena pana “piṇḍāya caritvā laddhabhatta”nti vuccati, evaṃsampadamidaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Aññathā mātikāṭṭhakathāyaṃ “gaṇabhojane vuttanayeneva pañcahi bhojanehi nimantitassa…pe… parassa parassa bhojane”ti vuttavacanavirodho. Idañhi vacanaṃ yena paṭhamaṃ nimantito, tato paṭhamanimantitaṃ ādāya gato parassa parassa nimantanakadāyakassa bhojaneti atthaparidīpanato nimantanato laddhabhattassa bhojaneyeva āpattīti dīpeti. “Dve tayo nimantane ekato”ti vacanenapi sameti, aññathā “yena nimantito, tassa bhojanato parassa bhojane”ti ettakaṃ vattabbaṃ siyā, pāḷiyaṃ vā “nimantanena ekatobhuñjatī”ti ettakaṃ vattabbaṃ siyā. Dutiyanimantanassa paṭhamabhojane āpattippasaṅganivāraṇatthaṃ [V 0.0282] “yena yenā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Nimantanapaṭipāṭiyā bhuñjatīti pāḷīti ce? Na, “anāpatti niccabhatte”tiādipāḷivirodhato.

229. Here is the consideration: Because of the statement, “Another person takes the bowl, it should not be given,” in the later part an improper invitation is of no use, but only in the earlier part is an improper invitation of use. Therefore, in the phrase “Venerable, may you come tomorrow as well,” what is the improper invitation? Hence, intention itself is the standard here. No, because of the statement, “Having wandered for alms-food, one eats the food obtained; there is an offense.” Therein, just as in the phrase “Venerable, may you come tomorrow as well,” the meaning is understood according to the method of an improper invitation, not taking it as mere words, so too in the phrase “having wandered for alms-food,” it should be understood that this is stated in reference to food obtained by an improper invitation in the interim. Indeed, having seen a monk wandering for alms-food, even food given with the words, “Come, venerable, take this food,” is called ‘obtained by an improper invitation’. But by convention, it is called “food obtained having wandered for alms-food”; this consistency should be seen thus. Otherwise, it would contradict the statement made in the Mātikā commentary: “As in the case of a group meal… in the meal of one after another.” Indeed, this statement, by clarifying the meaning that one who was first invited, then having taken that first invited food, while going, eats the meal of a subsequent donor who gives an invitation, shows that there is an offense only in eating the food obtained from an invitation. It also agrees with the statement, “two or three invitations at once.” Otherwise, only this much should have been said: “by whom one was invited, in the meal of another over his own,” or in the Pāḷi, only this much should have been said: “one eats from invitations together.” The phrase “by whichever, by whichever,” etc., was stated in order to prevent the contingency of an offense regarding the first meal due to a second invitation. And if it is said, “There is a Pāḷi text stating, ‘One who eats according to the order of the invitations [commits no offense],’” [the reply is:] No, because of the contradiction with the Pāḷi text beginning with, “There is no offense in the case of a permanent meal.”

Gaṇṭhipade [M 0.0315] pana “piṇḍāya caritvā laddhabhattaṃ kasmā bhuñjituṃ na labhatīti ce? ‘Paramparabhojanaṃ nāma pañcannaṃ bhojanānaṃ aññatarena bhojanena nimantito, taṃ ṭhapetvā pañcannaṃ bhojanānaṃ aññataraṃ bhojanaṃ bhuñjati, etaṃ paramparabhojanaṃ nāmā’ti vuttattā”ti likhitaṃ. Yadi evaṃ niccabhattādikampi na vaṭṭatīti āpajjatīti niccabhattādi odissakanti ce? Taṃ na, tadaññassa attano dhanena nipphannassa, saṅghato laddhassa vā pāto pacanakayāgu ce ghanā hoti, tassāpi, ekakuṭikaṃ gāmaṃ upanissāya viharato bhikkhācariyavasena labhitabbaniccabhattassa ca akappiyabhāvappasaṅgato. Tattha bhikkhācariyavasena laddhaṃ na kappati nimantanakānaṃ appasādāvahanatoti ce? Na, “pañca bhojanāni ṭhapetvā sabbattha anāpattī”ti vacanavirodhato. Khādanīyampi hi parassa khāditvā bhuttattā nimantanabhojanaṃ abhuñjanto appasādaṃ karoti eva, tasmā appasādāvahaṃ appamāṇaṃ, tasmā niccabhattādi odissakaṃ na sambhavati. Apica heṭṭhā vuttanayena saddhiṃ idha vuttanayena saṃsanditvā yaṃ yaṃ khamati, taṃ taṃ gahetabbanti sabbopi kesañci ācariyānaṃ vinicchayo. Ācariyassa pana vinicchayo ante āvi bhavissati. “Khīraṃ vā rasaṃ vā pivato amissampīti adhippāyo”ti vuttaṃ. Gaṇṭhipade “heṭṭhā odanenāmissetvā upari tiṭṭhatī”ti likhitaṃ.

In the Gaṇṭhipada, however, it is written: “If it is asked, ‘Why, after going for alms and obtaining food, is one not allowed to eat it?’ [The answer is] because it is stated: ‘Successive eating (paramparabhojana) means that having been invited with one of the five kinds of food, one sets that aside and eats another of the five kinds of food—this is called successive eating.’” If so, it would follow that even regular meals and the like are not permissible. And if it is said that regular meals and the like are odissaka (specifically designated)? That is not so, because it would lead to the consequence of being unallowable for food produced by one's own wealth other than that, or obtained from the Saṅgha, or for morning gruel if it is thick, and also for the regular meal to be obtained by means of an alms-round for a bhikkhu dwelling dependent on a village with a single hut. Among these, if it is said that food obtained by means of an alms-round is not allowable because it brings about displeasure in the inviters, that is not so, because it contradicts the statement, “Setting aside the five kinds of food, there is no offense anywhere.” For even having eaten another's hard food, by not eating the invited meal, one certainly causes displeasure. Therefore, causing displeasure is not the standard. Therefore, regular meals and the like cannot be odissaka. Moreover, having compared the method stated below with the method stated here, whatever is suitable should be accepted—this is the entire decision of some teachers. The Teacher's decision, however, will become clear at the end. It is said: “The meaning is that for one drinking milk or juice, it is also unmixed.” In the Gaṇṭhipada, it is written: “It stands above, unmixed with the rice below.”

Mahāupāsakoti gehasāmiko. Mahāaṭṭhakathāyaṃ “āpattī”ti vacanena kurundiyaṃ “vaṭṭatī”ti vacanaṃ viruddhaṃ viya dissati. “Dvinnampi adhippāyo mahāpaccariyaṃ vicārito”ti likhitaṃ. “Cārittatoti ‘santaṃ bhikkhuṃ anāpucchā’ti parato vattabbato”ti vuttaṃ. Vacīkammaṃ avikappanaṃ. Ettha “mahāupāsako bhikkhū nimanteti…pe… pacchā laddhaṃ bhattaṃ bhuñjantassa āpatti.
