Piṇḍāya caritvā laddhabhattaṃ bhuñjati, āpattī”ti aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vacanato, “kālasseva piṇḍāya caritvā bhuñjimhā”ti pāḷito, khandhake “na ca, bhikkhave, aññatra nimantane aññassa bhojjayāgu paribhuñjitabbā, yo paribhuñjeyya, yathādhammo kāretabbo”ti (mahāva. 283) vacanato ca nimantetvā vā pavedetu animantetvā vā, paṭhamagahitanimantanassa bhikkhuno paṭhamanimantanabhojanato aññaṃ yaṃ kiñci parasantakaṃ bhojanaṃ paramparabhojanāpattiṃ karoti. Attano santakaṃ, saṅghagaṇato laddhaṃ vā agahaṭṭhasantakaṃ vaṭṭati, nimantanato paṭhamaṃ nibaddhattā pana niccabhattādi parasantakampi vaṭṭati. Khandhake [M 0.0316] “na ca[V 0.0283], bhikkhave…pe… yathādhammo kāretabbo”ti (mahāva. 283) vacanaṃ parasantakabhojanavuttaniyamanaṃ. Tato hatthakova no takkoti ācariyo.

A great lay devotee means a householder. In the Mahāaṭṭhakathā, the statement “it is an offense” seems to contradict the statement “it is allowable” in the Kurundī. It is written: “The intention of both was examined in the Mahāpaccarī.” It is said that `Cārittato` refers to the Cāritta training rule, which is stated later as ‘without asking the present monk’. Verbal action is not a specific determination. Here, because of the statement in the commentary, “A great lay devotee invites monks… for one who eats food obtained afterward, it is an offense. If he eats food obtained by going on alms-round, it is an offense,” and from the Pāḷi, “We ate after going for alms at the proper time,” and because of the statement in the Khandhaka, “And, monks, one should not partake of another’s food or gruel. Whoever should do so should be dealt with according to the Dhamma” (Mahāva. 283)—whether one informs after having invited or informs without having invited, for a monk who has accepted the first invitation, any other food whatsoever belonging to another, apart from the food of the first invitation, incurs an offense of successive eating. Food that is one’s own property, or obtained from the Saṅgha or a group, or is the property of non-householders, is allowable. However, because it is established prior to the invitation, a regular meal and so forth, even if it is the property of another, is allowable. In the Khandhaka, the statement “And, monks… should be dealt with according to the Dhamma” is a regulation stated concerning the eating of food belonging to another. Therefore, the teacher states: “Our reasoning is as certain as something held in the hand.”

Paramparabhojanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Training Rule Concerning Successive Eating is concluded.

4. Kāṇamātāsikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

4. Commentary on the Kāṇamātā Training Rule

31-3. Paṭiyālokanti pacchimaṃ desaṃ. Pūvagaṇanāyāti atirittapūvagaṇanāyāti attho. Sace “apātheyyādiatthāya sajjita”nti saññāya gaṇhāti, acittakattā sikkhāpadassa āpatti eva. Atha uggahitaṃ gaṇhāti, na muccatiyeva. Asaṃvibhāge pana anāpatti akappiyattā. Acittakatā paññattijānanābhāveneva, na vatthujānanābhāvenāti eke. Na, mātikāṭṭhakathāyaṃ “pātheyyādiatthāya sajjitabhāvajānana”nti aṅgesu avuttattā. Porāṇagaṇṭhipade panevaṃ vuttaṃ “ekena vā anekehi vā dvattipattapūresu gahitesu tesaṃ anārocanena vā sayaṃ vā jānitvā yo aññaṃ gaṇhāti, tassa dukkaṭaṃ. Ekato tīsu, catūsu vā paviṭṭhesu ekena ce dvepattapūrā gahitā, dutiye dve gaṇhante paṭhamo ce na nivāreti, paṭhamassa pācittiyaṃ. Nivāreti ce, anāpatti, dutiyasseva dukkaṭa”nti. Sace sañcicca na vadati, porāṇagaṇṭhipade vuttanayena pācittiyaṃ, mātikāṭṭhakathāvasena (kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. kāṇamātāsikkhāpadavaṇṇanā) dukkaṭaṃ. “Atirekapaṭiggahaṇa”nti tattha pañcamaṃ aṅgaṃ vuttaṃ, tasmā appaṭiggahitattā na pācittiyaṃ, kattabbākaraṇato pana dukkaṭaṃ. Aññathā kiriyākiriyaṃ idaṃ āpajjati, anivāraṇaṃ, anārocanaṃ vā chaṭṭhaṅgaṃ vattabbaṃ siyā. Ekanikāyikānaṃ vāti ettha “āsannavihārabhikkhū, āsannaāsanasālāgatā vā sace visabhāgehi ānītaṃ na paṭiggaṇhanti, ‘ārāmikādīnaṃyeva vā dāpentī’ti jānāti, yattha paribhogaṃ gacchati, tattha dātuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti vuttaṃ. “Dvattipattapūrā’ti vacanato pacchiādīsu adhikampi gaṇhato anāpattī”ti keci vinayadharamānino vadanti, taṃ tesaṃyeva nisīdatu, ācariyā pana “pacchiādīsupi ukkaṭṭhapattassa pamāṇavasena dvattipattapūrā gahetabbā. Ukkaṭṭhaparicchedakathā hesā”ti vadanti.

31-3. 'Looking back' refers to the western direction. 'Counting the cakes' means counting the excess cakes. If one accepts with the perception, 'It is prepared for the purpose of provisions, etc.,' there is an offense indeed, on account of it being an unintentional act with respect to the training rule. If, then, one accepts an object whose acceptance is invalid, one is not freed indeed. In the case of not sharing, however, there is no offense, because it is unallowable. Some say that an unintentional act is due only to not knowing the regulation, not to not knowing the object. This should not be accepted, because in the Mātikā-aṭṭhakathā, 'knowing that it was prepared for the purpose of provisions, etc.' is not stated among the factors. In the Porāṇagaṇṭhipada, however, it is said thus: 'When two or three bowlfuls of cakes have been accepted by one or many, if another bhikkhu accepts more, either without informing them or knowing it himself, he commits a wrong-doing. When three or four have entered together, if one has accepted two bowlfuls of cakes, and while a second is accepting two, the first does not prevent him, the first commits an offense requiring confession. If he does prevent him, there is no offense; there is a wrong-doing for the second one only.' If one intentionally does not speak, according to the method stated in the Porāṇagaṇṭhipada, it is an offense requiring confession; according to the Mātikā-aṭṭhakathā, it is a wrong-doing. 'Accepting an excess' is stated there as the fifth factor; therefore, because of not having received, there is no offense requiring confession, but because of not doing what should be done, there is a wrong-doing. Otherwise, this training rule would become an offense of commission and omission, and 'not preventing' or 'not informing' would have to be stated as a sixth factor. Regarding 'or for those of the same group,' it is said: 'If one knows that bhikkhus in a nearby monastery, or those who have come to a nearby rest house, do not accept what is brought by those of a different group, or that they have it given only to monastery attendants and so on, it is allowable to have it given where it will be consumed.' Some who consider themselves experts in Vinaya say, 'Because of the wording "two or three bowlfuls," there is no offense for one who accepts even more from baskets, etc.' Let that remain in their minds alone. The teachers, however, say, 'Even from baskets, etc., only two or three bowlfuls should be accepted, according to the measure of a superior bowl. This is the explanation of the limit of a superior bowl.'

Kāṇamātāsikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Kāṇamātā Training Rule is concluded.

5. Paṭhamapavāraṇasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

5. The Commentary on the First Pavāraṇā Training Rule

236. Yāvadatthapavāraṇāya [V 0.0284][M 0.0317] pavāritā kiñcāpi “pavāritā”icceva adhippetā aṭṭhuppattiyāva, atha kho pacchimāva idhādhippetā.

236. Although it is only in the origin story that one is considered 'invited' by the 'invitation until satisfaction', nevertheless, here only the final invitation is intended.

237. “Alametaṃ sabba”nti vuttattā atirittaṃ nāma hoti. Bhikkhussa idampi te adhikaṃ, ito aññaṃ na lacchatīti kira attho.

237. Because it was said, 'This is enough for all,' it is called 'excess.' For a monk, 'This too is extra for you; from this you will not get other food'—this is indeed the meaning.

238-9. “Asanaṃ paññāyatī”ti eteneva “bhuttāvī”ti etassa siddhattā visuṃ atthasiddhi natthi. Yadi atthi, aṅgānaṃ chakkattadassananti. Vuttampi cetantiādi pavāraṇaṅgānaṃ pañcakattadassanaṃ. Varakoti yo koci varako. “Pavāraṇaṃ pana janetiyevāti visuṃ sitthaṃ vodakaṃ karonti, pavāraṇaṃ na janeti. Yāguṃ vā pivanto paṭhamaṃ udakaṃ pivati, vaṭṭati. Avasiṭṭhaṃ heṭṭhāsitthaṃ pavāraṇaṃ na janetī”ti likhitaṃ. Upatissatthero “janetiyevā”ti vadati, taṃ na icchanti ācariyā. Bhajjitapiṭṭhanti taṇḍulacuṇṇameva. Bhajjitasattuyo piṇḍetvā katamodako sattumodako.

By this very phrase, 'Food appears,' the meaning of 'one who has eaten' is established, so there is no separate establishment of the meaning. If there were, it being so, it would be a showing of the factors as sixfold; thus it should be known. The statement beginning 'And if it is said...' is a showing of the factors of invitation as fivefold. 'Varako' means any kind of millet. Regarding 'But it does generate the invitation': they make a lump of rice watery separately; this does not generate the invitation. Or, for one drinking gruel, if he first drinks water, it is allowable. The remaining lump of rice at the bottom does not generate the invitation,' thus it is written. The Elder Upatissa says, 'It does indeed generate it,' but the teachers do not accept this. 'Roasted flour' is only rice flour. A sweet-ball made by lumping together roasted barley-meal is a barley-meal sweet-ball.

“Yāgusitthamattāneva dve…pe… paṭikkhipati, na pavāretī”ti vuttattā paracaṅkamacchādayo pakkhipitvā pakkayāguṃ pivanto sace aññaṃ tādisaṃyeva paṭikkhipati, pavāraṇā na hotīti kira dhammasiritthero. Sace aññaṃ paṭikkhipati, na pavāreti. Kasmā? Asanasaṅkhātassa vippakatabhojanassābhāvato. Bhojanasālāyaṃ bhuñjanto ce, attano apāpuṇanakoṭṭhāsaṃ abhihaṭaṃ paṭikkhipati, na pavāreti. Kāmaṃ paṭikkhipati, patte pana ārāmiko ākirati, tato bhuñjituṃ na vaṭṭati. Idañhi buddhappaṭikuṭṭhaanesanāya uppanneyeva saṅgahaṃ gacchati. Yathā hi saṅghato uddhaṭapiṇḍaṃ dussīlo deti, taṃ paṭikkhipati, na pavāreti, evaṃsampadamidaṃ. “Visabhāgo lajjī ce deti, taṃ tena sambhogaṃ akattukāmatāya paṭikkhipati, pavāretīti apare”ti vuttaṃ. Parivesanāyāti bhattagge. “Maṃsena rasaṃ, maṃsañca rasañca maṃsarasanti āpajjanato ‘maṃsarasa’nti vutte paṭikkhepato hoti, maṃsassa rasaṃ maṃsarasanti viggaho nādhippeto”ti vuttaṃ. Maṃsakarambako nāma…pe… vaṭṭatīti suddhayāgu eva hoti. Appavāraṇamissakakarambakoyeva hoti, tasmā na pavāreti, tena vuttaṃ parato “idañca karambakena na samānetabba”ntiādi, tasmā “taṃ abhiharitvā [M 0.0318] kañjiyaṃ gaṇhathā’ti vadantaṃ paṭikkhipati, pavāraṇā na hotī”ti ca “missakayāguṃ gaṇhathā’ti avuttattā ‘sammissitaṃ visuṃ [V 0.0285] katvā detī’ti vuttattā”ti ca vuttaṃ, yasmā yāgumissakanti ettha padadvaye pavāraṇārahassa nāmaggahaṇaṃ natthi, tasmā tatra ce yāgu bahutarā vā hoti samasamā vā, na pavāreti. Kasmā? Tattha abhihārakapaṭikkhepakānaṃ yāgusaññattā. Yāgu ce mandā, bhattaṃ bahutaraṃ, pavāreti. Kasmā? Tesaṃ ubhinnampi tattha bhinnasaññattāti takko ācariyassa. Bhattamissake pavāraṇārahassa nāmassa sabbhāvato sabbadā pavāreti eva. Missake pana vuttanayena kāraṇaṃ vattabbaṃ. Visuṃ katvā detīti yathā bhattasiṭṭhaṃ na patati, tathā gāḷhaṃ hatthena pīḷetvā parissāvetvā deti.

Because it is said, “If one refuses just two… rice-grains of gruel… one does not complete the invitation,” if, while drinking gruel cooked with things like fish from another's fishing-weir put into it, one refuses another of the very same kind, the invitation is not completed—so, it is said, the Elder Dhammasiri said. If one refuses another, one does not complete the invitation. Why? Because of the absence of unfinished food which is designated as a meal. If, while eating in the dining hall, one refuses a portion that has been brought forward but has not yet reached oneself, one does not complete the invitation. Indeed, one may refuse, but if a monastery attendant then pours it into the bowl, it is not proper to eat from it. For this is included only in what has arisen from a wrongful search censured by the Buddha. Just as when an immoral monk gives almsfood set aside from the Sangha, and one refuses it, one does not complete the invitation; the accomplishment of this example should be seen in the same way. It is said: “Others say: If a conscientious person of a different communion gives, and one refuses it due to the desire not to have communion with him, one completes the invitation.” “At the time of serving” means at the meal-place. It is said: “Because it comes to mean ‘juice with meat,’ ‘meat and juice,’ and ‘meat-juice,’ when ‘meat-juice’ is said, the invitation is completed by the refusal. The analysis ‘the juice of meat is meat-juice’ is not intended.” In the passage “A meat-porridge named… is allowable,” it is only pure gruel. It is a porridge mixed with something that does not require an invitation; therefore, one does not complete the invitation. Because of that, it is said later on: “And this should not be equated with porridge,” etc. Therefore, it is also said that if one refuses someone saying, “Having brought that, take the rice-gruel,” the invitation is not completed. And it is also said that this is because “Take the mixed gruel” was not said, and because it is said, “He gives what is mixed, having separated it.” Because here in the two words “gruel-mixture,” there is no taking of the name of something suitable for invitation, therefore, in that case, if the gruel is more or is equal, one does not complete the invitation. Why? Because in that case, for both the one who brings it and the one who refuses it, there is the perception of it as gruel. If the gruel is little and the boiled rice is more, one completes the invitation. Why? Because in that case, for both of them, there is a different perception—this is the teacher's reasoning. In the case of a mixture with boiled rice, because of the presence of the name of something suitable for invitation, one always completes the invitation. But in the case of a mixture, the reason should be stated according to the method mentioned. “He gives it having separated it” means that he gives it having pressed it firmly with the hand and strained it, so that a grain of boiled rice does not fall.

Akappiyakatanti ettha “kappiyaṃ akārāpitehi kadalipphalādīhi saddhiṃ atirittaṃ kappiyaṃ kārāpetvāpi taṃ kadalipphalādiṃ ṭhapetvā avasesaṃ bhuñjituṃ vaṭṭati. Amissakarasattā puna tāni kappiyaṃ kārāpetvā aññasmiṃ bhājane ṭhapetvā atirittaṃ kāretvā bhuñjituṃ vaṭṭati. Kasmā? Pubbe tesu vinayakammassa anāruḷhattā”ti vadanti. “Bhuttāvinā ca pavāritena āsanā vuṭṭhitena kata”nti vacanato bhuttāvinā appavāritena āsanā vuṭṭhitena kattabbanti siddhaṃ, tasmā “pātova addhānaṃ gacchantesu dvīsu eko pavārito avuṭṭhito tattha nisīdati, so itarena piṇḍāya caritvā laddhaṃ bhikkhaṃ attanā abhutvāpi ‘alametaṃ sabba’nti kātuṃ labhati evā”ti vuttaṃ, taṃ sukkapakkhe “bhuttāvinā kataṃ hotī”ti imināva siddhaṃ, tasmiṃ pakkhe attano sattaṅgāni na pūrenti, kaṇhapakkhe paṭibhāgena satta vuttānīti veditabbaṃ. Bhuttāvinā appavāritena āsanā vuṭṭhitena, avuṭṭhitena vā kataṃ hoti, vaṭṭati. “Pavāritena āsanā avuṭṭhitenevā”ti imaṃ pana atthavikappaṃ dīpetuṃ “sattaṅgāni vuttānī”tipi vattuṃ vaṭṭati. So puna kātuṃ na labhati paṭhamaṃ katassa puna teneva kattabbappasaṅgato. Yañca akataṃ, taṃ kattabbanti hi vuttaṃ. Atha sova paṭhamo puna kattukāmo hoti, aññasmiṃ bhājane pubbe akataṃ kātuṃ labhati. Dutiyo paṭhamabhājanepi kātuṃ labhati. “Yena akataṃ, tena kātabba”nti hi vuttaṃ. Imamevatthaṃ sandhāya “yena yaṃ paṭhamaṃ kappiyaṃ kataṃ, tameva so puna kātuṃ na labhati, aññena kātabba”nti [M 0.0319] likhitaṃ. Tattha tanti taṃ paṭhamaṃ katanti attho. Pesetvā kāretabbanti ettha anupasampanno ce gato, tatraṭṭhena ekena bhikkhunā paṭiggāhetvā aparena kāretabbanti tattha ekova evameva kātuṃ na labhatīti. “Yaṃ kiñci gilānaṃ uddissā’tiādivacanato vihārādīsu gilānassa pāpuṇanakoṭṭhāsampi gilānātirittaṃ nāma, tasmā vaṭṭatī”ti vadanti. Āhāratthāyāti vikāle evāti eke.

Here, regarding that which has not been made allowable: 'Even after having had what is extra made allowable together with banana fruits, etc., which have not been made allowable, it is permissible to set aside those banana fruits, etc., and eat the remainder. Because of having unmixed juice, again, after having had those things made allowable, placing them in another vessel, and having had the extra made allowable, it is permissible to eat. Why? Because previously, the Vinaya-act had not been applied to them,' they say. Because of the text, 'Done by one who has eaten, has been formally satisfied, and has risen from his seat,' it is established that it should be done by one who has eaten, has not been formally satisfied, and has risen from his seat. Therefore, it is said: 'Among two monks going on a journey early in the morning, one, having been formally satisfied but not having risen, sits there. Regarding the alms-food obtained by the other who went for alms, the first monk, even without having eaten it himself, is indeed permitted to make it allowable by saying, "This is enough for all."' That is established in the white section by this very phrase, 'it is done by one who has eaten.' In that section, one's own seven factors are not fulfilled. It should be understood that in the dark section, seven are stated as a counterpart. It is permissible when done by one who has eaten and has not been formally satisfied, whether having risen from the seat or not having risen. However, to clarify this alternative meaning, 'By one who has been formally satisfied, but only without having risen from his seat,' it is also permissible to say, 'The seven factors are stated.' He is not permitted to do it again, because of the consequence that what was done the first time would have to be done again by that very same person. For it is said, 'And what has not been done, that should be done.' Now, if that very same first person wishes to do it again, he is permitted to do in another vessel what has not been done before. A second person is permitted to do it even in the first vessel. For it is said, 'By whom it has not been done, by him it should be done.' Referring to this very meaning, it is written: 'By whom a certain thing was first made allowable, that very thing he is not permitted to do again; it should be done by another.' Therein, the word `tanti` means 'that which was done first.' Here, regarding 'having sent someone to have it done': if an unordained person has gone, one monk who is present there should have him receive it, and another should have it made allowable. Therefore, in that case, a single monk is not permitted to do it in this same way. From the statement beginning, 'Whatever is for a sick person...,' they say: 'Even the share that reaches a sick person in a monastery, etc., is called 'extra for the sick'; therefore, it is permissible.' Some say that 'for the purpose of food' is stated only with reference to the wrong time.

241. Kāyakammaṃ [V 0.0286] ajjhoharaṇato. Vacīkammaṃ vācāya “atirittaṃ karotha bhante”ti akārāpanenāti veditabbaṃ.

241. Bodily action is from swallowing. Verbal action is from not causing one to say by speech, 'Make it extra, venerable sir'; thus it should be understood.

Paṭhamapavāraṇasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the first Pavāraṇā training rule is concluded.

6. Dutiyapavāraṇasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

6. The Commentary on the Second Pavāraṇā Training Rule

243. Sādhāraṇamevāti sabbapavāraṇānaṃ sādhāraṇaṃ “yāvattakaṃ icchasī”ti idaṃ.

243. Herein, in the phrase `sādhāraṇameva`, this saying, 'as much as you wish,' is common to all Pavāraṇās.

Dutiyapavāraṇasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the second Pavāraṇā training rule is concluded.

7. Vikālabhojanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

7. The Commentary on the Training Rule on Untimely Eating

247-9. Naṭānaṃ nāṭakāni naṭanāṭakāni, sītāharaṇādīni. Mūlañca taṃ khādanīyañcāti mūlakhādanīyaṃ. Esa nayo sabbattha. Piṭṭhanti cuṇṇaṃ. Khārakamūlanti yūpasamūlaṃ. Caccumūlaṃ neḷiyamūlaṃ. Tambakaṃ vacaṃ. Taṇḍuleyyakaṃ cūḷakuhu. Vatthuleyyakaṃ mahākuhu. Vajakali nikoṭṭhaṃ. Jajjharī hirato.

247-9. The dramas (`nāṭakāni`) of dancers (`naṭānaṃ`) are `naṭanāṭakāni`, such as the abduction of Sītā. It is a root (`mūlaṃ`) and it is edible (`khādanīyaṃ`), thus it is an edible root (`mūlakhādanīyaṃ`). This method applies everywhere. In the word `piṭṭha`, it means powder. `Khārakamūla` is `yūpasamūla`. `Caccumūla` is `neḷiyamūla`. `Tambaka` is `vaca`. `Taṇḍuleyyaka` is `cūḷakuhu`. `Vatthuleyyaka` is `mahākuhu`. `Vajakali` is `nikoṭṭha`. `Jajjharī` is `hirato`.

Koṭṭhaṃ jaraṭṭhaṃ vuccati. Gaṇṭhi muhukulamudu vicayattha vajamuju vaduḷavi.

`Koṭṭha` is called `jarattha`. `Gaṇḍi`, `muhukulamudu`, `vicayattha`, `vajamuju`, and `vaduḷavi` mean a lump.

Vajjayetime kiṃsukaṃ, haliddi. Kaseruko, kaṭibalavanti tassa nāmaṃ. Ambāṭakaṃ amūlakaṃ piḍhala kakkula. Masālu kinaḷa. Āluva kaḷi taḍḍhiaḷi alasa kaṭissala namedati mera. Siggu sīri koḷa kālakaṃ nekaḷavi. Khīravallikando tumūroriyo hoti. Saṅkhato dhovanameva. Ayaṃ “parisaṅkhāro”ti likhitaṃ. Khīrakākolī kirikaveḷi. Jīvikaṃ jīvihi. Usabhaka ummasuviyi.

One should avoid these: `kiṃsuka` and `haliddi`. `Kaseruko`: its name is `kaṭibalavanti`. `Ambāṭaka`, `amūlaka`, `piḍhala`, and `kakkula` are synonyms. `Masālu` is `kinaḷa`. `Āluva` is `kaḷi`, `taḍḍhiaḷi`, `alasa`, `kaṭissala`, `namedati`, and `mera`. `Siggu` is `sīri`, `koḷa`, `kālaka`, and `nekaḷavi`. The `khīravalli` tuber is `tumūroriyo`. Being prepared (`saṅkhato`) is merely washing. It is written: 'This is the preparation (`parisaṅkhāra`).' `Khīrakākolī` is `kirikaveḷi`. `Jīvikaṃ` is `jīvihi`. `Usabhaka` is `ummasuviyi`.

Hintālaṃ [M 0.0320] kitili. Kuntāla toho tilisatā padikaḷiro paṭasevalakaḷi. Karamandakaṃ karamba daṇḍokira udakajoti kaṇḍako. “Siṅghatakotipi vuccatī”ti likhitaṃ. Phaggava hakiḷi. Nattamālanti karañji.

`Hintāla` is `kitili`. `Kuntāla` is `toho`, `tilisatā`, `padikaḷiro`, and `paṭasevalakaḷi`. `Karamandaka` is `karamba`, `daṇḍokira`, `udakajoti`, and `kaṇḍako`. It is written: 'It is also called `siṅghatako`.' `Phaggava` is `hakiḷi`. `Nattamāla` is `karañji`.

Sellu [V 0.0287] loholiyaṃ. Kāsamaddaka kuduvavali anasikina. Ummādiya melelidiya. Cīnamuggo venamutti huramugga. Rājamāso māhaviliti. Aggimanto muñci. Sunipaṇṇako tipilavanināḷikā tilaka. Bhūmiyaṃ jātaloṇīti ettha loṇīnāmassa sādhāraṇattā “bhūmiya”nti visesetvā vuttaṃ. Brahmīpattaṃ demeteye paṇasā. “Dīpavāsino vadantī”ti sithilaṃ katvā kasmā vuttanti ce? “Khādanīyatthaṃ pharatīti lakkhaṇena asamānattā”ti vuttaṃ. Padeliviniteki. Sulasipaṇṇanti tasāpalikaṃ.

`Sellu` is `loholiyaṃ`. `Kāsamaddaka` is `kuduvavali`, `anasikina`. `Ummādiya` is `melelidiya`. `Cīnamuggo` is `venamutti`, `huramugga`. `Rājamāso` is `māhaviliti`. `Aggimanto` is `muñci`. `Sunipaṇṇako` is `tipilavanināḷikā`, `tilaka`. Herein, in the phrase `bhūmiyaṃ jātaloṇī`, because the name `loṇī` is common, it is specified with `bhūmiyaṃ`. `Brahmīpattaṃ` is `demeteye`, `paṇasā`. If it is asked why 'The island-dwellers say' is stated loosely, it is stated thus because it is not the same in the characteristic of being an edible item. `Sulasipaṇṇaṃ` is `tasāpalikaṃ`.

Agandhikapupphaṃ karissayeti cekavādidapupphaṃ celepatimalaṃ. Jīvantīpupphaṃ jīvitandigamala. Bakula muthuvala. Kuyyaka punapunnāmapunnarā, jātisumana. Navamālikā cehemala.

`Agandhikapupphaṃ`. `Karissayeti cekavādidapupphaṃ` is `celepatimalaṃ`. `Jīvantīpupphaṃ` is `jīvitandigamala`. `Bakula` is `muthuvala`. `Kuyyaka` is `punapunnāma`, `punnarā`. `Jātisumana`. `Navamālikā` is `cehemala`.

Tintiṇika kacinī vileyi. Mātuluṅga lavano. Pussaphala supuli. Timbarūsaka tigibberehiti susatudhuta. Tipusavātiṅgaṇa dhutatikeṇa paṭiyi. Coca variyiyeli. Moca atireli. Goṭṭhaphalaṃ pūvaphalanti eke. Koṭṭhase kira acchiva.

`Tintiṇika` is `kacinī`, `vileyi`. `Mātuluṅga` is `lavano`. `Pussaphala` is `supuli`. `Timbarūsaka` is `tigibberehiti`, `susatudhuta`. `Tipusavātiṅgaṇa` is `dhutatikeṇa`, `paṭiyi`. `Coca` is `variyiyeli`. `Moca` is `atireli`. Some say `goṭṭhaphalaṃ` is `pūvaphalaṃ`. The word `acchiva`, it is said, is in the meaning of `koṭṭhasa`.

Asamussi bimba iti keci. Kāsmarīti sepaṇṇi. Atitemeti kariyametissa. Jātiphalaṃ kataṃmeti. Kaṭukaphalaṃ tiriraka.

Some say `asamussi` is `bimba`. `Kāsmarī` is `sepaṇṇi`. `Atitema` is a synonym for `kariyametissa`. `Jātiphalaṃ` is `kataṃmeti`. `Kaṭukaphalaṃ` is `tiriraka`.

Taruṇaphalaṃ kiriupulu. Pokkharaṭṭhi kiñcakkhaṭṭhi. Siddhatthakaṃ sāsapaṃ setavaṇṇaṃ. Rājikaṃ rattaṃ hoti.

`Taruṇaphalaṃ` is `kiriupulu`. `Pokkharaṭṭhi` is `kiñcakkhaṭṭhi`. White-colored mustard is called `siddhatthakaṃ`. Red-colored mustard is called `rājikaṃ`.

Hiṅguṃ hiṅgujatunti sabbāpi hiṅguvikatiyo. Ettha hiṅgujatu nāma pattasākhā pacitvā kātabbā. Sākhā pacitvā katā sipāṭikā. Aññehi missetvā katāti keci. Takaṃ kaṭṭhajanti aggikeḷini. Nikitissākālesayo. Timera, takapatti pasākhāpatte pacitvā kātabbā. “Takapaṇṇi sāvati eva kātabbā”ti likhitaṃ.

`Hiṅgu` and `hiṅgujatu` are all varieties of asafoetida. Herein, `hiṅgujatu` is that which should be prepared by cooking the branches of that plant. That which is made by cooking the branches is called `sipāṭikā`. `Takaṃ` is `kaṭṭhajaṃ` (resin from the shoot). `Timera` (resin). `Takapatti` is `pasākhā` (resin from the leaves), which should be prepared by cooking the leaves. It is written: '`Takapaṇṇi` should be prepared from the dry leaves themselves.'

Vikālabhojanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on eating at the wrong time is concluded.

8. Sannidhikārakasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

8. Explanation of the Training Rule on Storing Food

253. Aparajju [V 0.0288][M 0.0321] sannidhi nāma hotīti attho. Ajja paṭiggahitanti na kevalaṃ paṭiggahitameva, atha kho uggahitakampi, teneva aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassāti evaṃ sannidhikataṃ yaṃ kiñci yāvakālikaṃ vā yāmakālikaṃ vā ajjhoharitukāmatāya gaṇhantassa paṭiggahaṇe tāva āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti vuttaṃ. Yadi taṃ paṭhamameva paṭiggahitaṃ, “paṭiggahaṇe tāvā”ti na vattabbaṃ, tasmā veditabbametaṃ “attano kāle gahitaṃ ajja paṭiggahita’nti vutta”nti.

253. The meaning is that it is called 'storing' with reference to the next day. In the phrase 'received today,' it is not only what has been formally received, but indeed also that for which the formal receiving has lapsed. For that very reason, it is said in the Commentary: 'For a monk who, with the desire to consume, takes anything stored thus—whether an item allowable for the morning or a limited-period-allowable—at the moment of receiving, there is the incurring of a dukkaṭa offense.' If that allowable item was received for the very first time, the phrase 'at the moment of receiving' should not be said. Therefore, this should be known: 'An allowable item taken at its proper time is said to be "received today".'

Etthāha – yathā pañca bhesajjāni uggahitakāni anadhippetāni. Sattāhātikkame anāpatti anajjhoharaṇīyattā, tathā idhāpi uggahitakaṃ nādhippetanti? Ettha vuccati – bhesajjasikkhāpade (pārā. 618 ādayo) uggahitakaṃ nādhippetanti yuttaṃ attano kālātikkamanamattena tattha āpattippasaṅgato. Ettha na yuttaṃ attano kālātikkamanamattena āpattippasaṅgābhāvato. Ajjhoharaṇeneva hi ettha āpattīti adhippāyo, tasmā anugaṇṭhipadamatena ajja uggahetvā punadivase bhuñjanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati.

Here, an objector says: Just as with the five medicines, those for which the formal receiving has lapsed are not intended for the rule. There is no offense for exceeding seven days because they are not to be consumed. Similarly, here also, is that for which the formal receiving has lapsed not intended for the rule? To this, the rebuttal is stated: In the training rule on medicines, the statement that 'that for which the formal receiving has lapsed is not intended' is fitting, because there, an offense would be entailed merely by the exceeding of its own time limit. Here, it is not fitting, because an offense is not entailed merely by the exceeding of its own time limit. Indeed, the intention here is that the offense is only through consumption. Therefore, according to the view of the Anugaṇṭhipada, a monk who, having let the formal receiving lapse today, consumes it on the next day, incurs two offenses.

Tatrāyaṃ vicāraṇā – attanā bhuñjitukāmo ajja uggahetvā punadivase bhuñjati, dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Sāmaṇerādīnaṃyeva atthāya uggahetvā gahitaṃ punadivase paṭiggahetvā bhuñjanto āpattiyā na kāretabboti. Paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassāti etthāyamadhippāyo – sace belaṭṭhasīso viya dutiyatatiyādidivasatthāya ajja paṭiggahetvā sāmaṇerādīnaṃ gopanatthāya deti, tassa punadivase ajjhoharaṇatthaṃ paṭiggahaṇe āpatti dukkaṭassāti sambhavati. Sayameva sace taṃ gopetvā ṭhapeti, punadivase patitaṃ kacavaraṃ disvā vimativasena vā paṭiggaṇhato paṭiggahaṇatova āpatti dukkaṭassāti sambhavati. No ce paṭiggaṇhāti, taṃ dukkaṭaṃ natthi. “Idañhi ‘ekaṃ pādaṃ atikkāmeti, āpatti thullaccayassā’tiādi viyā”ti vuttaṃ. Yo pana ekappahāreneva dvepi pāde atikkāmeti, tassa taṃ thullaccayaṃ natthi, evaṃsampadamidanti veditabbaṃ. Ettha paṭiggahitabhāvaṃ avijahantameva sannidhiṃ [M 0.0322] janetīti dhammasiritthero, taṃ “paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti pāḷiyā virujjhati. Kapālena pīto pana sneho abbohāriko. Kiñcāpi uṇhe otāpentassa paggharati, tathāpi “bhesajjasikkhāpade viyā”ti vuttaṃ. Itarathā kapālena pītā sappiādayopi sattāhātikkame āpattiṃ janeyyunti. Sayaṃ paṭiggahetvāti idhāpi pubbe vuttavidhiyeva. Duddhotapattakathāpi etena sameti viya[V 0.0289]. Āhāratthāyāti kālepi labbhati. Pakatiāmiseti kappiyāmise. Sāmisena mukhena ajjhoharato dveti “hiyyo paṭiggahitayāmakālikaṃ ajja purebhattaṃ sāmisena mukhena ajjhoharato dve pācittiyānī”ti likhitaṃ. Ajja paṭiggahitaṃ yāvakālikampi hi yāmātikkantapānakena saṃsaṭṭhaṃ sannidhiṃ karoti. Akappiyamaṃsesu manussamaṃse thullaccayaṃ, sesamaṃse dukkaṭañca vaḍḍhati.

Herein is the investigation: If one, desiring to eat for oneself, having let the acceptance lapse today, eats it on the next day, one incurs two offenses. If for the sake of novices and others only, one has let the acceptance lapse for what was received, a monk who eats it on the next day without receiving it again should not be charged with an offense. Regarding 'If one receives it, there is an offense of wrong-doing,' this is the intention: if, like the Elder Belaṭṭhasīsa, one receives it today for the sake of the second, third, or subsequent days and gives it to novices and others for safekeeping, for him, in the act of receiving it on the next day for the purpose of consumption, an offense of wrong-doing is possible. Or, if one stores and keeps it oneself, and on the next day, seeing fallen rubbish, for one who receives it again, perhaps due to doubt, from the very act of receiving, an offense of wrong-doing is possible. If one does not receive it, there is no such offense of wrong-doing. For it is said: 'This is like, "If one moves one foot across, there is an offense of grave transgression," and so on.' But for one who moves both feet across in a single stride, there is no such grave transgression for him; this case should be understood as being similar. Herein, the Elder Dhammasiri says that it generates storing only for one who does not abandon the state of having received it. That contradicts the Pali text: 'If one receives it, there is an offense of wrong-doing.' However, oil absorbed by a potsherd is not subject to the rule. Although it may ooze out for one who is heating it in the sun, nevertheless, it is said, 'it is like in the training rule on medicines.' Otherwise, ghee and so on, absorbed by a potsherd, would generate an offense in transgressing the seven days. Here too, regarding 'having received it oneself,' it is just the procedure stated previously. The discussion on a poorly washed bowl also seems to be in agreement with this. 'For the sake of food' is obtained even in the proper time. 'Ordinary food' means allowable food. Regarding 'for one consuming with a mouth containing food, there are two,' it is written: 'For one who, in the forenoon today, consumes with a mouth containing food a yāmakālika item that was received yesterday, there are two pācittiya offenses.' Indeed, even a yāvakālika item received today, if mixed with a drink that has passed the yāma, creates storing. Among unallowable fleshes, a grave transgression accrues for human flesh, and an offense of wrong-doing for the remaining fleshes.

255. Sattāhakālikaṃ yāvajīvikaṃ āhāratthāyāti kālepi dukkaṭameva sannidhiṃ anāpajjanatoti keci. Tadahu paṭiggahitaṃ tadahu purebhattaṃ vaṭṭatīti ce? Na, pāḷiyampi aṭṭhakathāyampi visesassa natthitāya. Bhesajjasikkhāpade purebhattaṃ yathāsukhaṃ paribhuñjanaṃ vuttanti ce? Āhāre sappiādi saṅgahaṃ yāti, tena taggatikavasena vuttaṃ, na bhesajjavasena vuttanti upatisso.

255. Some say that regarding the seven-day and lifelong allowances for the purpose of food, it is a `dukkaṭa` offense even at the proper time, because it does not amount to storing. If it is asked: 'Is what is received on that day allowable in the morning of that same day?' No, because of the non-existence of a distinction in the Pāḷi as well as in the Commentary. If it is asked: 'In the training rule on medicine, is it not said that one may consume as one pleases in the morning?' The reply is: Ghee and so on are included under food; therefore, it is spoken of by way of being in that category, not by way of being medicine. Thus says Upatissa.

Sannidhikārakasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the training rule concerning the act of storing is finished.

9. Paṇītabhojanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

9. Commentary on the Training Rule concerning Choice Food

259. Akappiyasappināti yesaṃ maṃsaṃ na kappati, tesaṃ sappinā. “Vasātelañhi ṭhapetvā akappiyasappi nāma natthī”ti likhitaṃ. Visaṅketanti ettha “sūpodanaviññattipi na hotī”ti vuttaṃ. Kāyikānīti kāyena āpajjitabbāni.

259. 'Unallowable ghee' means ghee from animals whose flesh is not allowable. It is written: 'Indeed, having set aside fat and oil, there is no such thing as unallowable ghee.' In this context, 'without a sign,' it is said: 'there is not even a request for soup and rice.' 'Bodily' means those offenses to be incurred by means of the body.

261. Mahānāmasikkhāpadena kāretabboti saṅghavasena pavārite bhesajjatthāya sappiādipañcakaṃ viññāpeti ce, tattha “na bhesajjena karaṇīyena [M 0.0323] bhesajja”nti ettha saṅgahaṃ gacchati, tasmā “tena pācittiya”nti vuttaṃ. Pāḷimuttakesu “bhikkhunīnampi dukkaṭa”nti likhitaṃ.

261. 'Should be dealt with according to the Mahānāma training rule' means: if, when one has been invited on behalf of the Saṅgha, one requests the five items beginning with ghee for the purpose of medicine, then it is included under the case of 'not medicine, but with a need for medicine.' Therefore, it is said, 'a `pācittiya` offense because of that.' In the Pāḷimuttaka texts, it is written: 'For bhikkhunīs too, it is a `dukkaṭa` offense.'

Paṇītabhojanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Training Rule concerning Choice Food is finished.

10. Dantaponasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

10. Commentary on the Training Rule concerning the Tooth-Stick

264-5. Mukhadvāranti kaṇṭhanāḷi. Uccāraṇamattanti ukkhipitabbamattakaṃ. Kasaṭaṃ chaḍḍetvāti [V 0.0290] samudācāravasena, achaḍḍitepi “vaṭṭatī”ti vuttaṃ. Hatthapāsātikkamanti dāyakassa. Bhikkhussa detīti aññassa bhikkhussa. Kañjikanti yaṃ kiñci dravaṃ. Patto paṭiggahetabboti bhūmiyaṃ ṭhapite abhihārābhāvato. “Yathā paṭhamataraṃ patitatheve doso natthi, tathā ākiritvā apanentānaṃ patitathevepi abhihaṭattā nevatthi doso”ti likhitaṃ. Carukenāti khuddakapiṇḍena. Jāgarantassapīti “api-saddena suttassapī”ti likhitaṃ. Kecīti abhayagirivāsino. Tehi kāyasaṃsagge kāyapaṭibaddhenāpi tappaṭibaddhenāpi thullaccayāpatti dassitā evāti attho. Kāyapaṭibaddhapaṭibaddhenāti vacanamattamevetaṃ. “Satthakenāti paṭiggahitakenā”ti likhitaṃ, taṃ dullikhitaṃ satipi male puna paṭiggahetabbakiccābhāvato. Kesañci atthāyāti anupasampannānaṃ atthāya. “Sāmaṇerassa hatthaṃ phuṭṭhamattameva taṃ pariccatta”nti likhitaṃ.

264-5. 'The mouth's entrance' means the throat passage. 'Just enough to lift' means just enough to be raised. 'Having discarded the refuse' refers to conventional practice; even if not discarded, it is said, 'it is valid.' 'Beyond arm's reach' refers to the donor's. 'Gives to a bhikkhu' means to another bhikkhu. 'Gruel' means any liquid. 'The bowl should be received': this is because there is no offering when it is placed on the ground. It is written: 'Just as there is no fault in the very first drop that falls, so too, for those who are carrying it away after having poured it, even in a drop that falls, there is no fault because it has been brought forward.' 'With a small lump' means with a tiny morsel. Regarding 'even of one who is awake,' it is written that the word 'api' also implies 'even of one who is asleep.' 'Some' refers to the Abhayagiri residents. By them, it is shown that for bodily contact, whether with what is connected to the body or with what is connected to that, there is a thullaccaya offense—this is the meaning. 'With what is connected to that which is connected to the body' is merely a verbal expression. It is written, ''With a knife' means with one that has been received,' but this is poorly written because even if there is dirt or rust, there is no need to receive it again. 'For the sake of some' means for the sake of those who are not fully ordained. It is written: 'That item is relinquished by the mere touching of a novice's hand.'

Paṭiggahaṇupagabhāraṃ nāma majjhimapurisena ukkhipitabbakaṃ. Mūlapaṭiggahaṇameva vaṭṭatīti ettha “macchikavāraṇatthanti vuttattā ‘abhuñjanatthāyāpi paṭiggahetvā gahite vaṭṭatī’”ti ye vadanti, te vattabbā “sīsamakkhanatelaṃ paṭiggahetvā ‘idaṃ sīsamakkhana’nti anābhogeneva sattāhaṃ atikkāmentassa kiṃ nissaggiyaṃ bhaveyyā”tiādi, suttādhippāyo pana evaṃ gahetabbo “macchikavāraṇatthaṃ bījantassa tasmiṃ laggarajādimhi patte patite sukhaṃ paribhuñjituṃ sakkā’ti saññāya pubbe paṭiggahitabba”nti vuttaṃ. Parivattanakathāyaṃ “amhākaṃ taṇḍulesu khīṇesu etehi amhākaṃ hatthagatehi sāmaṇerasantakehipi sakkā patiṭṭhapetu’nti bhikkhūnaṃ cittuppādo ce sambhavati, ‘parivattanaṃ sātthaka’nti upatissatthero”ti vuttaṃ. Yadi evaṃ suddhacittānaṃ niratthakanti āpannameva, tathā “paṇḍito esa sāmaṇero pattaparivattanaṃ katvā dassati, mayameva ca imassa vissāsena vā yācitvā [M 0.0324] vā bhuñjissāmā”ti citte sati bhuñjituṃ na vaṭṭati katepi parivattaneti ca āpannaṃ, kiṃ bahunā. Nirapekkheheva gaṇhitabbaṃ, na sāpekkhehīti dassanatthaṃ vuttanti ācariyo. Ayamevattho “sace pana sakkoti vitakkaṃ sodhetuṃ, tato laddhaṃ khāditumpi vaṭṭatī”ti vacanena siddhova. Ādhārake patto ṭhapito hoti yathāpaṭiggahitabhāve nirālayo. Samuddodakena appaṭiggahitakena. Meṇḍakassa khīraṃ khīrattāva vaṭṭati. “Attano pana khīraṃ mukheneva pivantassa anāpattīti dassetuṃ vutta”nti vuttaṃ. “Sarīranissitamahābhūtāni hi idhādhippetānī”ti likhitaṃ, tadubhayampi “kappiyamaṃsakhīraṃ vā”tiādinā nayena virujjhati.

What is called 'a load suitable for receiving' is a load that can be lifted by a man of medium strength. In this text [which states], 'Only the initial receiving is allowable,' because it is said, 'for the purpose of warding off flies,' those who say, 'Even if received for a purpose other than eating, it is allowable once taken,' should be told the following: 'If a monk receives oil for anointing the head and, merely through inattention, lets seven days pass, would it become an item for forfeiture?' and so on. However, the meaning of the Sutta should be understood thus: It is said, 'It should be received beforehand with the thought: "When dust and so forth that has stuck to the fan of one who is fanning to ward off flies falls into the bowl, it will be possible to consume [the food] with ease."' In the discussion on exchange, it is said: 'If the thought arises in the monks, "When our rice is exhausted, we can sustain ourselves with these belongings of the novices that have come into our hands," then the exchange is meaningful,' said the Elder Upatissa. If this is so, it indeed follows that for those with pure minds, it is meaningless. Likewise, it also follows that if the thought arises, 'This novice is wise; having exchanged the bowl, he will give it, and we ourselves will eat [from it] either through familiarity or by asking,' then even if the exchange is made, it is not allowable to eat. What more is there to say? It should be taken only by those without expectation, not by those with expectation—it is said to show this meaning, says the teacher. This very meaning is indeed established by the statement: 'If, however, one is able to purify one's thought, then what is obtained from that is allowable even to eat.' The bowl placed on the stand remains in the state in which it was received, without attachment. With seawater that has not been formally received. The milk of a goat is allowable simply because it is milk. It is said, 'To show that there is no offense for one who drinks his own milk directly with his mouth.' It is written, 'For the great elements dependent on the body are intended here,' but both of these are contradicted by the method beginning with 'or permissible meat and milk...'

Apica “appaṭiggahitabhājane aññabhikkhusantake attano piṇḍapātaṃ pakkhipati, ‘taṃ thoka’nti vā aññena vā kāraṇena vadati, taṃ sabbesaṃ na kappati. Kasmā? Vinayadukkaṭattā[V 0.0291]. Attanā paṭiggahetvā pakkhipitabbaṃ vinayavidhiṃ akatvā dukkaṭanti adhippāyo. Evaṃ tādisaṃ kimatthaṃ na bhuñjatīti? Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ ‘uggahitako hotī’ti vuttattā. Evañhi tattha vuttaṃ bhūmiyaṃ vā bhājane vā phalaṃ vā yaṃ kiñci āmisaṃ vā yāvajīvikampi appaṭiggahitakaṃ ajānanto āmasati, na vaṭṭati, uggahitakaṃ hotī”ti anugaṇṭhipade vuttaṃ, tasmā imassa matena bhikkhu bhikkhussa sace patte appaṭiggahite piṇḍaṃ ṭhapeti, taṃ akappiyaṃ uggahitakanti siddhaṃ. Ayamevattho “sace attano vā bhikkhūnaṃ vā yāgupacanakabhājane…pe… nirāmisaṃ katvā paribhuñjitabba”nti vacanena saṃsanditvā kathetabbo. “Kappiyamaṃsakhīraṃ vā”ti pasaṅgavasena vuttaṃ. Dadhi ce paṭiladdhaṃ, tañca adhippetanti keci.

Furthermore, if a bhikkhu places his own almsfood into the unreceived bowl belonging to another bhikkhu, saying, 'This is a little,' or for some other reason, that food is not allowable for any of them. Why? Because it is a dukkaṭa offense according to the Vinaya. The meaning is that it is a dukkaṭa offense for not having followed the Vinaya procedure of receiving it oneself before placing it. Thus, for what reason is such food not to be eaten? Because it is stated in the Commentary that it becomes 'taken up' (uggahitaka). For it is stated thus in the Anugaṇṭhipada: 'If one, not knowing, touches an unreceived item—be it on the ground or in a bowl, be it fruit or any kind of edible, even a lifelong tonic—it is not allowable; it becomes 'taken up' (uggahitaka).' Therefore, according to this opinion, if a bhikkhu places almsfood in the bowl of another bhikkhu while it is unreceived, it is established that this unallowable food is 'taken up'. This very meaning should be explained by connecting it with the statement: 'If, for oneself or for the bhikkhus, in a vessel for cooking gruel... it should be made free of the food item and then consumed.' The phrase 'allowable meat or milk' was stated by way of incidental mention. And if curd is obtained, some say that this too is intended.

Dantaponasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rule on the Tooth-Stick is concluded.

Samatto vaṇṇanākkamena bhojanavaggo catuttho.

The fourth, the Chapter on Food, is completed according to the order of the explanation.

5. Acelakavaggo

5. The Chapter on the Naked Ascetic

1. Acelakasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

1. The Explanation of the Training Rule on the Naked Ascetic

269. Vighāsādānaṃ antarā pūvalābhena aññatarā paribbājikā pavisitvā ṭhitā. Dāpetīti anupasampannena.

269. Regarding `Vighāsādānaṃ` (eating leftovers): In the midst of them, a certain female wanderer, having obtained a cake, entered and stood. The phrase 'causes to be given' means by one who is not fully ordained.

Acelakasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rule on the Naked Ascetic is concluded.

2. Uyyojanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

2. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Incitement

276. Vijahantassāti [M 0.0325] anādaratthe sāmivacanaṃ. Uyyojakassa vijahantassa sato āpatti dukkaṭassātipi attho. Idha anupasampanno nāma sāmaṇerovādhippeto.

276. The word `vijahantassa` is the genitive case used in the sense of disrespect. This is also the meaning: for the inciting bhikkhu, being aware as the other is leaving his hand's reach, there is a dukkaṭa offense. Here, by 'one who is not fully ordained', only a novice is intended.

Uyyojanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rule on Incitement is concluded.

3. Sabhojanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

3. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Eating Together

280. Sabhojaneti [V 0.0292] ettha paṭhamavikappo “itthī ca puriso cā”ti iminā tatiyapadena yujjati, dutiyavikappo paṭhamehi dvīhi. Kuleti ghare. Anupavisitvā nisīdanacittena sacittakaṃ.

280. In sabhojane, the first alternative connects with this third phrase, "a woman and a man"; the second alternative connects with the first two. In kule, it means in a house. Having entered with the intention of sitting down, it is intentional.

Sabhojanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on eating together is concluded.

4. Rahopaṭicchannasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

4. The Explanation of the Training Rule on a Concealed, Secluded Place

284. Idha pañcamaṃ upanandassa catutthaṃ hoti, tasmā bhikkhunivaggassa dasamaṭṭhakathāyaṃ upari upanandassa “tatiyasikkhāpadenā”ti na pāṭho, “catutthenā”ti pāṭhoti veditabbo.

284. Here, the fifth is the fourth for Upananda. Therefore, in the commentary on the tenth training rule of the Bhikkhunīvagga, regarding Upananda above, the reading is not "by the third training rule"; the reading should be "by the fourth." Thus it should be understood.

Rahopaṭicchannasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on a concealed, secluded place is concluded.

5. Rahonisajjasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

5. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Sitting in a Secluded Place

289. Rahonisajjasikkhāpadaṃ uttānatthameva.

289. The training rule on sitting in a secluded place has a clear meaning indeed.

6. Cārittasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

6. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Proper Conduct

294. Sabhattoti nimantanabhattoti porāṇā.

294. In sabhatto, it means a meal with a common invitation; thus say the ancients.

Purebhattañca piṇḍāya, caritvā yadi bhuñjati;

Siyā paramparāpatti, pacchābhattaṃ na sā siyā.

And if, having gone for alms before the meal, one eats, there would be a successive offense; if one eats after the meal, that offense would not be.

Pacchābhattañca [M 0.0326] gamiko, pubbagehaṃ yadi gacche;

Eke āpattiyevāti, anāpattīti ekacce.

And if a traveling monk, after the meal, should go to the previous house, some say it is an offense indeed; some others say it is not an offense.

Kulantarassokkamane[V 0.0293], āpattimatayo hi te;

Samānabhattapaccāsā, iti āhu idhāpare.

Indeed, those who are of the opinion that it is an offense say so because it occurs upon entering another family's house. Others here say it is because there is an expectation of a common meal.

Matā gaṇikabhattena, samenti naṃ nimantane;

Vissajjanaṃ samānanti, eke sammukhatāpare.

Their opinion should be reconciled by the case of a group meal.

Sanniṭṭhānatthikeheva, vicāretabbabhedato;

Viññū cārittamicceva, sikkhāpadamidaṃ vidūti.

Because of the various points to be investigated by those who seek a definite conclusion, the wise know this training rule simply as 'Proper Conduct'.

Cārittasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on proper conduct is concluded.

7. Mahānāmasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

7. The Explanation of the Training Rule Concerning Mahānāma

310. Kālanti so. Yasmā saṅghapavāraṇāyamevāyaṃ vidhi, tasmā “ñātakānaṃ pavāritāna”nti vuttaṃ. “Iminā hi tayā pavāritamha, amhākañca iminā ca iminā ca attho”ti yathābhūtaṃ ācikkhitvā viññāpetuṃ gilānova labhati. Yaṃ pana vuttaṃ paṇītabhojanasikkhāpade “mahānāmasikkhāpadena kāretabbo”ti, taṃ saṅghavasena pavāritaṃ, bhesajjatthāya sappiādibhesajjapañcakaṃ viññāpeti ce, “na bhesajjena karaṇīyena bhesajjaṃ viññāpetī’ti vacanena pācittiyanti attho”ti (pāci. 309) likhitaṃ.

310. In this context, `so` refers to that Mahānāma. Because this procedure is only for the invitation of the Sangha, therefore it is said, "of relatives who have been invited." Only a sick monk is permitted to inform by stating what is true, thus: "Indeed, by this we have been invited by you, and for us there is a need for this and this." As for what was said in the training rule on fine foods, "it should be done according to the Mahānāma training rule," that was said of an invitation by way of the Sangha. If one requests the five medicines, such as ghee, for a medicinal purpose, it is written: "By the statement, 'One requests medicine when there is no need for medicine,' a pācittiya is incurred; this is the meaning."

Mahānāmasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Mahānāma training rule is concluded.

8. Uyyuttasenāsikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

8. Commentary on the Training Rule Concerning an Army Drawn Up for Battle

311-5. Maṃ diṭṭhenāti mayā diṭṭhena, mama dassanena vā. Ekampi sarahatthaṃ purisanti aṅgapariyāpannaṃ.

`Maṃ diṭṭhena` means `mayā diṭṭhena` (by me who has seen), or `mama dassanena` (by the seeing of me). The phrase `Ekampi sarahatthaṃ purisaṃ` (even one man with an arrow in hand) is included as a component (of the army).

Uyyuttasenāsikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the training rule concerning an army drawn up for battle is concluded.

9. Senāvāsasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

9. Commentary on the Training Rule Concerning Staying with an Army

319. Navame [V 0.0294][M 0.0327] senāparikkhepena vā parikkhepārahaṭṭhānena vā sañcaraṇaṭṭhānapariyantena vā paricchinditabbā.

319. In the ninth (rule), the boundary should be defined by the army's encampment, or by a place suitable for an encampment, or by the limit of the area for moving about.

Senāvāsasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the training rule concerning staying with an army is concluded.

10. Uyyodhikasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

10. Commentary on the Training Rule Concerning a Military Display

324. Dasame ekamekaṃ dassanāya gacchati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Yattha ṭhito passati, āpatti pācittiyassātiādi. Aṭṭhame pana ekamekaṃ dassanāya gacchati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Yattha ṭhito passati, āpatti dukkaṭassāti pāḷi. Kasmā? Aṅgappamāṇābhedepi anīkavisesato. Dasame pana aṭṭhamaṅgassa dassanena dukkaṭaṃ siyāti.

324. In the tenth (rule), if one goes to see each one, there is an offense of dukkaṭa. Where one stands and sees, there is an offense of pācittiya, and so on. However, in the eighth (rule), if one goes to see each one, there is an offense of dukkaṭa. Where one stands and sees, there is an offense of dukkaṭa; this is the Pāḷi text. Why? Although there is no difference in the measure of the components, it is due to the specific nature of the military formation. However, in the tenth (rule), by seeing the eighth component, there would be a dukkaṭa offense.

Uyyodhikasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the training rule concerning a military display is concluded.

Samatto vaṇṇanākkamena acelakavaggo pañcamo.

The fifth chapter, the Acelakavagga, is completed according to the order of the commentary.

6. Surāpānavaggo

6. The Chapter on Drinking Intoxicants

1. Surāpānasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

1. Commentary on the Training Rule Concerning Drinking Intoxicants

Āyasmato yaṃ muni sāgatassa,

Mahiddhikattassa nidassanena;

Pānassa doso tassa dassanatthaṃ,

Pubbeva so bhaddavatiṃ payāto.

In order to show the fault of drinking by means of the demonstration of the great psychic power of the Venerable Sāgata, that Sage proceeded beforehand to Bhaddavatī.

Tasmā [V 0.0295] passaṃ nāgamapothayitvā,

Vinissaṭaṃ sāgataṃ iddhiyā ca;

Nato surāpānanisedhanatthaṃ,

Kosambimevajjhagamāti ñeyyaṃ.

Therefore, seeing the Elder Sāgata who, without striking the nāga, would cause its pride to be dispelled by psychic power alone, He, for the purpose of prohibiting the drinking of intoxicants, went to Kosambī itself. Thus it should be known.

326-8. Pasupālakāti [M 0.0328] ajapālakā. Yena majjati, tassa bījato paṭṭhāya. Keci “sacittakapakkhe cittaṃ akusalamevāti (kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. paṭhamapārājikavaṇṇanā) vuttattā vatthuṃ jānitvā pivato akusala”nti vadanti. Evaṃ sati “akusaleneva pātabbatāyāti na vattabba”nti vutte “sacittakapakkhameva sandhāyā”ti vadanti. Evaṃ sati “kusalākusalābyākatacittanti vattabba”nti vutte tampi “tabbahulanayena vutta”nti vadanti. Kaṅkhāvitaraṇiyampi avisesetvā “akusalacitta”nti (kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. surāpānasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā) vuttaṃ, tasmā “taṃ akusaleneva pivatī”ti vadantīti.

In `Pasupālaka`: it means goat-herds. 'By which one is intoxicated': this refers to starting from the preparation of the ingredients of that intoxicant. Some say: 'Because it is stated in the section on the intentional case that "the mind is only unwholesome," for one who drinks knowing the substance, it is unwholesome.' This being so, when it is said, 'It should not be said that it is to be drunk only with an unwholesome mind,' they say, 'It is said referring only to the intentional case.' This being so, when it is said, 'It should be said that it is drunk with wholesome, unwholesome, or indeterminate minds,' they say, 'That too is said in the sense of the predominance of the unwholesome.' In the Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī as well, without making a distinction, it is said, "unwholesome mind." Therefore, they say, 'One drinks it only with an unwholesome mind.'

Surāpānasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on drinking intoxicants is concluded.

2. Aṅgulipatodakasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

2. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Prodding with a Finger

330. Aṅgulipatodakasikkhāpadaṃ uttānatthameva.

330. The training rule on prodding with a finger is indeed clear in meaning.

3. Hasadhammasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

3. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Playful Conduct

336. Tatiye kathaṃ tivedanaṃ? Hasādhippāyeneva “parassa dukkhaṃ uppādessāmī”ti udakaṃ khipantassa dukkhavedanaṃ. Sesaṃ uttānaṃ.

336. In the third, how are the three feelings? For one who throws water with only the intention of jesting, thinking, 'I will cause suffering to another,' painful feeling arises. The rest is clear.

Idaṃ saññāvimokkhañce, tikapācittiyaṃ kathaṃ;

Kīḷitaṃva akīḷāti, micchāgāhena taṃ siyā.

If this is liberation by perception, how is it a triple pācittiya? That perception of 'not-playing' while actually playing would be through wrong grasping.

Ettāvatā kathaṃ kīḷā, iti kīḷāyaṃ evāyaṃ;

Akīḷāsaññī hotettha, vinayatthaṃ samādaye.

By this much, the playing is done. Thus, in the very act of playing, one has the perception of 'not-playing'.

Ekantākusalo [V 0.0296] yasmā, kīḷāyābhiratamano;

Tasmā akusalaṃ cittaṃ, ekamevettha labbhatīti.

Because one whose mind delights in play is entirely unwholesome, therefore only a single unwholesome mind is obtained here.

Hasadhammasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on playful conduct is concluded.

4. Anādariyasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

4. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Disrespect

344. “Lokavajjaṃ atikkamitvā ‘idaṃ amhākaṃ ācariyuggaho’ti vadantassa na vaṭṭatī”ti likhitaṃ. Yaṃ saṃkiliṭṭheneva cittena āpajjati, yaṃ vā ariyapuggalo [M 0.0329] apaññatte sikkhāpade ajjhācarati, idaṃ lokavajjanti sabbatthikavādīādīni ācariyakulāni. Tattha dutiyatatiyavikappo idha na adhippeto sekhiyānaṃ lokavajjattā.

344. It is written: 'It is not proper for one who, having transgressed a worldly fault, says, “This is the teaching method of our teachers.”' That offense which one commits with a defiled mind, or that matter which a noble person transgresses before a training rule is laid down—this is a worldly fault, according to the schools of teachers such as the Sarvāstivādins. In this training rule, the second and third alternatives are not intended, because the Sekhiya rules are worldly faults.

Gārayho ācariyuggahoti ettha “yasmā ucchuraso sattāhakāliko, tassa kasaṭo yāvajīviko, dvinnaṃyeva samavāyo ucchuyaṭṭhi, tasmā vikāle ucchuyaṭṭhiṃ khādituṃ vaṭṭati guḷaharīṭakaṃ viyā’ti evamādiko sampati nibbatto gārayhācariyavādo na gahetabbo”ti ca, paṇṇattivajje pana vaṭṭatīti “na pattahatthena kavāṭo paṇāmetabbo’ti imassa ‘yena hatthena patto gahito, tena hatthena na paṇāmetabbo, itarena paṇāmetabbo’ti atthaṃ gahetvā tathā ācaranto na āpattiyā kāretabbo. ‘Tathā buddhabodhicetiyānaṃ pupphaṃ gaṇhituṃ vaṭṭatīti tathā ācaranto”ti ca. Tathā ācarati abhayagirivāsiko. Mahāvihāravāsino ce evaṃ vadanti, “mā evaṃ vadā”ti apasādetabbo. Tena vuttaṃ “suttaṃ suttānulomañca uggahitakānaṃyevā”tiādi. “Idaṃ sabbaṃ upatissatthero āhā”ti ca vuttaṃ. “Suttānulomaṃ aṭṭhakathā”ti likhitaṃ.

Here, regarding 'A blameworthy teacher's doctrine': 'Because sugarcane juice is a seven-day allowance, and its pulp is a lifetime allowance, the combination of the two is a sugarcane stalk. Therefore, it is proper to chew a sugarcane stalk at the wrong time, like jaggery and myrobalan.' Such a blameworthy teacher's doctrine that has now arisen should not be accepted. However, in the case of a fault by prescription, it is proper. Regarding 'A door should not be pushed with the hand holding a bowl,' having taken the meaning as, 'It should not be pushed with the hand that holds the bowl; it should be pushed with the other hand or another object,' one who acts accordingly should not be charged with an offense. And also, one who acts according to the view, 'Similarly, it is proper to take flowers of the Buddha, the Bodhi tree, and a Cetiya,' should not be charged with an offense. A resident of the Abhayagiri monastery acts thus. If the residents of the Mahāvihāra say so, they should be rebuked, 'Do not speak thus.' Therefore, it is said, 'The Sutta and that which is in conformity with the Sutta should be learned only by those who have studied them,' and so on. And it is also said, 'The Elder Upatissa said all this.' It is written, 'That which is in conformity with the Sutta is the Commentary.'

Anādariyasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on disrespect is concluded.

5. Bhiṃsāpanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

5. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Intimidation

345. Bhiṃsāpanasikkhāpadaṃ uttānatthameva.

345. The training rule on intimidation is clear in meaning.

6. Jotisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

6. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Kindling a Fire

354. “Visibbanāpekkho”ti [V 0.0297] vacanato yassa apekkhā natthi, tassa anāpatti.

354. Because of the phrase 'expecting to warm oneself,' for one who has no such expectation, there is no offense.

Jotisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on kindling a fire is concluded.

7. Nahānasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

7. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Bathing

364. Nahānasikkhāpadaṃ uttānatthameva.

364. The training rule on bathing is clear in meaning.

8. Dubbaṇṇakaraṇasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

8. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Discoloring

368. Alabhīti [M 0.0330] labho. Yathā “pacatīti paco, pathatīti patho”ti vuccati, evaṃ “labhatīti labho”ti kasmā na vuttaṃ? Pariniṭṭhitalābhasseva idhādhippetattā. Maggeti sibbinimagge. Kappakatena saddhiṃ akappakataṃ sibbeti. Yāvatā adhiṭṭhānaṃ na vijahati, tāvatā pubbaṃ kappameva. Kappaṃ na vijahati ce, puna kappaṃ dātabbanti ācariyassa takko.

368. Because one has obtained (alabhi), it is called a gain (lābho). Just as it is said, 'Because one cooks (pacati), it is called a cook (paco); because one recites (pathati), it is called a reciter (pāṭho)', why is it not similarly said, 'Because one obtains (labhati), it is called a gain (lābho)'? Because here, only a gain that is fully accomplished is intended. In the phrase 'magge', it means 'in the line of sewing'. One sews a robe that has not been marked with the kappa-bindu together with one that has been marked. As long as the determination is not abandoned, it remains as the previous marking (kappa). If the marking is not abandoned, a new marking should be applied again—this is the teacher's reasoning.

Dubbaṇṇakaraṇasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the training rule concerning making a disfiguring mark is concluded.

9. Vikappanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

9. The Commentary on the Training Rule on Vikappana (Joint Ownership)

374. Paribhogo ettha kāyakammaṃ. Apaccuddhāraṇaṃ vacīkammaṃ.

374. Here, using the robe is a bodily action. Failure to revoke the joint ownership is a verbal action.

Vikappanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the training rule on Vikappana (Joint Ownership) is concluded.

10. Cīvarāpanidhānasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

10. The Commentary on the Training Rule Concerning Hiding a Robe

379. Dasame yasmā nisīdanasanthataṃ cīvaranisīdanampīti ubhayampi sadasameva, tasmā taṃ ubhayampi ekato katvā “nisīdanaṃ nāma sadasaṃ vuccatī”ti āha. Tatthāpi cīvaraggahaṇena cīvaranisīdanaṃ gahitamevāti atthato santhatanisīdanameva vuttaṃ hoti. Yadi evaṃ “nisīdanasanthataṃ [V 0.0298] nāma sadasaṃ vuccatī”ti vattabbanti? Na, itarassa anisīdanaadasabhāvappasaṅgato. Ettha nisīdanasanthatassa pācittiyavatthuttā itarampi pācittiyavatthumevāti veditabbaṃ tajjātikattā. Sassāmike sūcighare sūcigaṇanāya āpattiyoti porāṇā.

379. In the tenth rule, because both the felt sitting-cloth (nisīdana-santhata) and the robe sitting-cloth (cīvara-nisīdana) have a border, therefore, combining them both, it was said, 'A sitting-cloth is what is called bordered.' Even there, by the inclusion of the word 'robe' (cīvara), the robe sitting-cloth is already included; therefore, in meaning, only the felt sitting-cloth is being spoken of. If that is so, should it not be said, 'A felt sitting-cloth is what is called bordered'? No, because that would lead to the other one being considered not a sitting-cloth and not bordered. Here, since a pācittiya offense is stated for the felt sitting-cloth, it should be understood that the other is also a basis for a pācittiya offense, because it is of the same nature. In the case of a needle-case that has an owner, offenses are incurred according to the number of needles—so say the ancients.

Cīvarāpanidhānasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the training rule concerning hiding a robe is concluded.

Samatto vaṇṇanākkamena surāpānavaggo chaṭṭho.

The sixth chapter, the Surāpāna Vagga, is completed according to the sequence of the commentary.

7. Sappāṇakavaggo

7. The Chapter on Living Beings

1. Sañciccapāṇasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

1. The Commentary on the Training Rule on Intentionally Taking Life

382. Sañciccapāṇasikkhāpadaṃ [M 0.0331] uttānatthameva.

382. The training rule on intentionally taking life has an obvious meaning.

2. Sappāṇakasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

2. The Commentary on the Training Rule Concerning Water Containing Living Beings

387. “Pāṇo atthī”ti jānantopi “marissantī”ti avicāretvā pivatice, anāpatti.

387. Even while knowing, 'There is a living being,' if one drinks without reflecting, 'They will die,' there is no offense.

Jale pakkhipanaṃ pupphaṃ, jalappavesanaṃ idaṃ;

Evaṃ ubhinnaṃ nānattaṃ, ñeyyaṃ ñāṇavatā sadāti.

Placing a flower in water, and this entry into water—thus this distinction between the two should always be known by one who is wise.

Sappāṇakasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the training rule concerning water containing living beings is concluded.

3. Ukkoṭanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

3. The Commentary on the Training Rule on Reopening a Settled Issue

392. Tatiye dvādasa ukkoṭā veditabbā. Tattha akataṃ kammaṃ, dukkaṭaṃ kammaṃ, puna kātabbaṃ [V 0.0299] kammanti anuvādādhikaraṇe labbhanti. Anihaṭaṃ, dunnihaṭaṃ, na puna haritabbanti vivādādhikaraṇe labbhanti, avinicchitaṃ, duvinicchitaṃ, puna vinicchitabbanti āpattādhikaraṇe labbhanti. Avūpasantaṃ, duvūpasantaṃ, puna vūpasametabbanti kiccādhikaraṇe labbhantīti aṭṭhakathānayo, pāḷiyaṃ panettha mukhamattameva dassitaṃ.

392. In the third rule, twelve reopenings are to be understood. Therein, an undone act, a badly done act, an act to be done again—these are obtained in a case of accusation. Not removed, badly removed, to be removed again—these are obtained in a case of dispute. Undecided, badly decided, to be decided again—these are obtained in a case of offense. Unsettled, badly settled, to be settled again—these three are obtained in a case of business. This is the method of the commentary. In the Pāḷi, however, only a hint is shown here.

Ukkoṭanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on reopening is concluded.

4. Duṭṭhullasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

4. The Explanation of the Training Rule on a Grave Offense

399. “Pārājikānīti atthuddhāravasena dassitānī”ti kathaṃ viññāyatīti ce? Parivārapāḷito. Vuttañhi tattha “āpattādhikaraṇapaccayā kati āpattiyo āpajjati. Āpattādhikaraṇapaccayā catasso āpattiyo āpajjati. Bhikkhunī jānaṃ pārājikaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicchādeti, āpatti pārājikassa. Vematikā paṭicchādeti, āpatti thullaccayassa. Bhikkhu saṅghādisesaṃ paṭicchādeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Ācāravipattiṃ paṭicchādeti[M 0.0332], āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti (pari. 290). Pārājikaṃ paṭicchādento bhikkhu anāpatti, no āpattiṃ āpajjati avuttattāti ce? Na, saṃkiliṭṭhena cittena paṭicchādane vinā āpattiyā asambhavato. Dukkaṭavāre vattabbāpi pārājikāpattiyo paṭhamaṃ atthuddhāravasena saṅghādisesehi saha vuttattā na sakkā puna vattunti na vuttāti veditabbā.

399. If it is asked, 'How is it known that "The Pārājika offenses are shown by way of extracting the meaning"?' From the Parivāra Pāḷi. For it is stated there: 'On account of a case concerning an offense, into how many offenses does one fall? On account of a case concerning an offense, one falls into four offenses. If a bhikkhunī knowingly conceals a Pārājika matter, there is an offense of Pārājika. If, being doubtful, she conceals it, there is an offense of Thullaccaya. If a bhikkhu conceals a Saṅghādisesa, there is an offense of Pācittiya. If he conceals a breach of conduct, there is an offense of Dukkaṭa.' (Pari. 290). If one should say: 'A bhikkhu concealing a Pārājika is without offense; he does not fall into an offense because it is not stated?' No, because it is impossible for the act of concealing with a defiled mind to be without an offense. The Pārājika offenses, although they should be stated in the section on Dukkaṭa, are not stated because, having been first stated by way of extracting the meaning along with the Saṅghādisesa offenses, they cannot be stated again. Thus it should be understood.

Yāva koṭi na chijjatīti cettha yo antamaso paṭicchādanatthaṃ aññassa ārocetu vā, mā vā, paṭicchādanacitteneva āpattiṃ āpanno. Tassa puna aññassa paṭicchādanatthaṃ anārocaneneva na koṭi chinnā hoti, kiṃ puna paṭinivattitvā vacanena payojananti na antimassa anārocanena chinnā hoti, appaṭicchādanena eva chinnā hoti, tato appaṭicchādanatthaṃ apubbassa ārocetabbaṃ, tato paṭṭhāya koṭi chinnā hoti, tadabhāvo paṭinivattitvā appaṭicchādanatthaṃ ārocetabbaṃ, evampi koṭi chinnā hotīti evaṃ no paṭibhātīti ācariyo. Tatiyena dutiyassāti ettha “dutiyo nāma paṭhamo”ti vadantānaṃ “vatthu puggalo na vattabbo”ti vāritattā na sundaraṃ. Aññassa catutthassa ārocanepi na sundaraṃ. Kasmā? Pubbeva sutvā aññassa anārocitattā. “Sutena aññassa ārocetabbaṃ siyā”ti vadanti.

And here, regarding 'until the limit is not broken': whoever, at the very least, for the purpose of concealment, whether he informs another or not, having only the intention to conceal, falls into an offense. For that monk, the limit is not broken merely by not informing another for the purpose of concealment. What then is the use of turning back and speaking? Therefore, the limit is not broken by not informing the last one; it is broken only by non-concealment. Therefore, for the purpose of non-concealment, it should be told to one who has not heard before. From then on, the limit is broken. In the absence of that, one should turn back and inform for the purpose of non-concealment; even so, the limit is broken. Thus it appears to us, said the teacher. Here, regarding 'by the third to the second': for those who say, 'the second is the first,' because it is prohibited by the phrase, 'the object, the person should not be told,' it is not proper. Informing another, a fourth person, is also not proper. Why? Because having heard before, one did not inform another. They say, 'Having heard, one should inform another.'

Duṭṭhullasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the training rule concerning a grave offense is concluded.

5. Ūnavīsativassasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

5. The Explanation of the Training Rule Concerning Those Under Twenty Years of Age

404. Punappunaṃ [V 0.0300] uppajjanato bahudhā. Hāyanavaḍḍhananti mātukucchismiṃ ce dvādasannaṃ māsānaṃ ūnatāya hāyanaṃ kataṃ. Pasūtassa vaḍḍhanaṃ kātabbaṃ. Mātukucchismiṃ ce vaḍḍhanaṃ kataṃ. Pasūtassa hāyanaṃ kātabbaṃ. Nikkhamanīyapuṇṇamāsī nāma sāvaṇamāsassa puṇṇamāsī. “Pāṭipadadivaseti dutiye upagacchati divase”ti likhitaṃ. So hi pasūtadivasato paṭṭhāya paripuṇṇavīsativasso hoti. Avasesānaṃ dvinnaṃ vassānaṃ adhikadivasāni honteva, tasmā nikkaṅkhā hutvā upasampādenti. Taṃ sandhāyāti gabbhavassañca pavāretvā laddhavassañca agaṇetvā jātadivasato paṭṭhāya gaṇetvā [M 0.0333] ekūnavīsativassaṃ. Ekūnavīsativassoti “gabbhavassaṃ eva pahāyā”ti likhitaṃ, taṃ dullikhitaṃ.

404. Because it arises again and again, it is of many kinds. Regarding decreasing and increasing: if in the mother's womb a decrease is accounted for due to being less than twelve months, then after birth an increase should be accounted for. If an increase is accounted for in the mother's womb, then after birth a decrease should be accounted for. The full moon day called Nikkhamanīyapuṇṇamāsī is the full moon day of the month of Sāvaṇa. It is written: 'Regarding the first day of the fortnight, on the second day, the day of entering upon the Rains.' For from the day of birth, he is fully twenty years old. For the remaining two years, there are indeed extra days; therefore, being without doubt, they ordain him. Regarding that: excluding the year in the womb and not counting the year acquired after the Pavāraṇā, counting from the day of birth, he is nineteen years old. Regarding 'nineteen years,' it is written, 'excluding only the year in the womb,' but that is poorly written.

406. Aññaṃ upasampādetīti upajjhāyo vā ācariyo vā hutvā upasampādeti. “Opapātikassa soḷasavassuddesikabhāvato puna cattāro vasse atikkamitvā upasampadā kātabbā”ti ācariyā vadantīti keci.

406. Ordains another: one ordains having become either a preceptor or a teacher. Some say that the teachers say, 'For one of spontaneous birth, because of being sixteen years of age for instruction, ordination should be performed after another four years have passed.'

Ūnavīsativassasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule concerning one under twenty years of age is concluded.

6. Theyyasatthasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

6. Explanation of the Training Rule Concerning a Caravan of Thieves

409. Theyyasattho ce suddhamātugāmo dve āpattiyo. Atha bhikkhuniyo, samayo rakkhati. Theyyasatthabhāvassa ṭhānaṃ katvā rakkhaṇīyattā sahadhammikānaṃ rakkhatiyevāti eke. Theyyabhāve na sahadhammikatā, tasmā na rakkhati evāti eke. Apārājikatheyyabhāve sati sahadhammikabhāvoti ce? Itarasmiṃ itaranti samayo anissaṭo āpajjati. Bhikkhu theyyasattho ce, yathāvatthukameva. Theyyasatthe theyyasatthasaññī saddhiṃ saṃvidhāyāti ca. “Saddhi”nti padaṃ kesuci natthi, taṃ ananurūpaṃ. Tathā dutiyepi.

409. If it is a caravan of thieves and a mere woman, there are two offenses. But if they are bhikkhunīs, the agreement protects. Some say it certainly protects because co-religionists are to be protected, even when making the state of being a caravan of thieves the ground for it. Others say that in the state of being a thief, there is no state of being a co-religionist; therefore, it certainly does not protect. If it is said that in the case of theft not entailing a pārājika offense there is the state of being a co-religionist, then what of the other case? Therefore, the agreement not being given up, one incurs an offense. If a bhikkhu is in a caravan of thieves, the offense is simply in accordance with the case. And it should be understood as: having made an arrangement together with a caravan of thieves, while being perceptive of it as a caravan of thieves. In some texts, the word 'saddhiṃ' is not present; that is not suitable. Likewise in the second case as well.

Theyyasatthasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule concerning a caravan of thieves is concluded.

7. Saṃvidhānasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

7. Explanation of the Training Rule on Arrangements

412. “Tena [V 0.0301] kho pana samayena aññatarā itthī”ti ca pāṭho atthi, kesuci natthi. Natthibhāvo sundaro “tena kho samayenā”ti adhikārattāti keci. Idha ekatoupasampannā, sikkhamānā, sāmaṇerīti imāpi tisso saṅgahaṃ gacchanti. Imāsaṃ pana samayo rakkhati, ayamimāsaṃ, mātugāmassa ca viseso.

412. The reading 'At that time, a certain woman...' also exists; in some texts, it does not. Some say its absence is better because 'At that time...' is the governing clause. Here, a bhikkhunī ordained by one Saṅgha, a female probationer, and a female novice—these three are also included. For these, however, the agreement protects; this is the difference between them and a laywoman.

414. Apicettha “viññū paṭibalā”ti vacanato appaṭibalā anāpattivatthukāti eke, taṃ na yuttaṃ dukkaṭavatthukattā. “Bhikkhu saṃvidahati, mātugāmo [M 0.0334] na saṃvidahati, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti hi vuttaṃ. Tathā hi upaparikkhitabbaṃ.

414. Moreover, here, because of the text 'intelligent and capable,' some say that an incapable one is a case of no offense. That is not right, because it is a case for an offense of wrong-doing. For it has been said: 'A bhikkhu makes an arrangement, a woman does not make an arrangement; there is an offense of wrong-doing.' For that very reason, it should be investigated.

Saṃvidhānasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on arrangements is concluded.

8. Ariṭṭhasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

8. Explanation of the Training Rule Concerning Ariṭṭha

417. Gahaṭṭhassāpi bhikkhunīdūsakakammaṃ mokkhantarāyikameva, tasmā tassa pabbajjāpi paṭikkhittā. Vipākantarāyikā ahetukattā. Pubbe sañcicca āpannā sammuṭṭhā suddhasaññino antarāyikā eva. Sesāti jātikā. Rasenāti bhāvena. Adhikuṭṭanaṭṭhenāti adhikaraṇaṃ katvā kuṭṭanaṭṭhena chindanaṭṭhena. Asisūnūpamā kusaladhammacchedanaṭṭhena. Sattisūlūpamā cittavitudanaṭṭhenāti porāṇā. Anāpattipāḷiyaṃ “ādikammikassā”ti mukhāruḷhavasena likhitaṃ.

417. Even for a layperson, the act of violating a bhikkhunī is indeed an obstacle to liberation; therefore, for that person, ordination is also prohibited. It is an obstacle to the result of kamma because of being without root-causes at rebirth. Offenses previously committed intentionally, though forgotten, are indeed obstacles for one of pure perception. In the phrase `sesāti` (the rest), it means each one. In `rasena`, it means by nature. In `adhikuṭṭanaṭṭhena`, it means having made it a basis, by the meaning of reviling, which is the meaning of cutting off. By the meaning of cutting off wholesome qualities, it is like a razor and a knife. By the meaning of piercing the mind, it is like a dart and a spear; thus say the ancients. In the Pāḷi of the non-offense section, the phrase `ādikammikassa` is written by way of being orally transmitted.

Ariṭṭhasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Ariṭṭha training rule is concluded.

9. Ukkhittasambhogasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

9. Explanation of the Training Rule on Association with a Suspended Monk

425. “Taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissaṭṭhenāti iminā laddhinānāsaṃvāsakataṃ dīpetī”ti vuttaṃ. Ticittanti ettha vipākābyākatacittena sahavāseyyaṃ kappeyyāti evamattho daṭṭhabbo. Aññathā sacittakattā sikkhāpadassa kiriyābyākataṃ sandhāya na yujjati.

425. It is said: 'By this phrase, "by one who has not abandoned that view," it shows the state of being in different communion due to doctrine.' Herein, in `ticittam`, the meaning should be understood thus: one might arrange to lie down together with a resultant-indeterminate mind. Otherwise, because the training rule pertains to a conscious being, it is not suitable in reference to the functional-indeterminate.

Ukkhittasambhogasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on association with a suspended monk is concluded.

10. Kaṇṭakasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

10. Explanation of the Kaṇaka Training Rule

428. Yattha [V 0.0302] te na passāmāti teti taṃ. Atha vā tava rūpādiṃ na passāma. Ayaṃ samaṇuddeso pārājiko hoti. “Sace taṃ diṭṭhiṃ paṭinissajjati, saṅghassa ārocetvā saṅghānumatiyā pabbājetabbo”ti porāṇagaṇṭhipade vuttaṃ, taṃ na yuttaṃ, daṇḍakammanāsanā hi idhādhippetā. Yadi [M 0.0335] so pārājiko, liṅganāsanā nāma siyā. Te paṭisevato nālaṃ antarāyāyāti ca diṭṭhi satthari asatthādidiṭṭhi na hoti. Sace sā yassa uppajjati, so pārājiko hoti, tasmimpi evameva paṭipajjitabbaṃ saṃvare atiṭṭhanto liṅganāsanāyeva nāsetabboti ācariyassa takko.

428. In 'Where we do not see you,' in the word `te`, the meaning should be understood as `taṃ` (you). Or, 'we do not see your form, etc.' This novice incurs a Pārājika. In the ancient commentary it is said: 'If he abandons that view, having informed the Saṅgha, he should be expelled with the Saṅgha's approval.' That is not correct, for here destruction by a penal act is intended. If he is a Pārājika, it would be a case of destruction of the characteristic [disrobing]. And in the phrase 'for one who associates with them, it is not sufficient for an obstacle,' the view in question is not the view regarding the Teacher as a non-Teacher, etc. If that latter view arises for someone, they become a Pārājika. For that novice also, it should be dealt with in just this way. This is the teacher's reasoning: a novice who does not stand firm in restraint should be removed only by destruction of the characteristic.

Kaṇṭakasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Kaṇaka training rule is concluded.

Samatto vaṇṇanākkamena sappāṇakavaggo sattamo.

The seventh chapter, the Sappāṇakavagga, is concluded in accordance with the sequence of the commentary.

8. Sahadhammikavaggo

8. The Sahadhammika Chapter

1. Sahadhammikasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

1. Explanation of the Sahadhammika Training Rule

434. Sahadhammikasikkhāpadaṃ uttānatthameva.

434. The Sahadhammika training rule is of clear meaning indeed.

2. Vilekhanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

2. Explanation of the Training Rule on Disparagement

438. Āpattiñca satisammosāyāti ettha ca-saddo kattabbañca na karotīti dīpeti, na cattāri evāti vuttaṃ hoti. Raṭṭhekadeso janapado. Buddhakāle ariṭṭhakaṇṭakā sāsanapaccatthikā. “Nālaṃ antarāyāyā”ti vacanena hi te bhagavato asabbaññutaṃ dīpenti. Parinibbute bhagavati dasavatthudīpakā vajjiputtakā. Te hi vinayasāsanapaccatthikā. Parūpahārādivādā pana suttantābhidhammappaccatthikā. Ke pana te? Ekacce mahāsaṅghikādayo, na sabbeti dīpanatthaṃ “parūpahārā…pe… vādā”ti visesanavacanamāha. Tattha ye kuhakā pāpicchakā [V 0.0303] abhūtaṃ ullapitvā paṭiladdhavarabhojanāni bhuñjitvā muṭṭhassatī niddaṃ okkamitvā sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ pattā, aññehi taṃ disvā “atthi arahato sukkavissaṭṭhī”ti vutte “mārakāyikā upasaṃharantī”ti vatvā janaṃ vañcenti. Ye ca sammāpaṭipannā akuhakā, tepi taṃ vacanaṃ sutvā keci taṃdiṭṭhikā honti adhimānino ca. Attano sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ passitvāpi nādhimuccanti, anadhigate adhikatasaññinova honti. Tathā atthi arahato aññāṇakaṅkhāvitaraṇā nāmagottādīsu viya saccesu paravitaraṇā parehi paññattā nāmānīti adhippāyo yathāsambhavaṃ yojetabbo. Tattha vinayadharo “aṭṭhānametaṃ, bhikkhave, anavakāso[M 0.0336], yaṃ arahato asuci mucceyya (kathā. 313; mahāva. 353). Diṭṭhadhammā…pe… aparappaccayā satthusāsane”tiādīni (mahāva. 30) suttapadāni dassetvā te sāsanapaccatthikesu niggahitaṃ niggaṇhātīti adhippāyo. Itare “pariyatti mūla”nti vādino. “Pātimokkhe uddissamāne”ti nidānavasena vuttaṃ. Tathāgatassa vibhaṅgapadāni siddhāni. Siddheyeva kiṃ imassa aṅgāni? Garahitukāmatā upasampannassa santike sikkhāpadavivaṇṇanañcāti.
