692. “Aparikkhittassa gāmassa upacāraṃ atikkāmentiyā”ti vacanenapi evaṃ veditabbaṃ – vikālagāmappavesane dvinnaṃ leḍḍupātānaṃyeva vasena upacāro paricchinditabbo, itarathā yathā ettha parikkhepārahaṭṭhānaṃ parikkhepaṃ viya katvā “atikkāmentiyā”ti vuttaṃ, evaṃ tatthāpi “aparikkhittassa gāmassa upacāraṃ atikkamantassā”ti vadeyya. Yasmā pana tattha parikkhepārahaṭṭhānato uttari eko leḍḍupāto upacāroti adhippeto, tasmā tadatthadīpanatthaṃ “aparikkhittassa gāmassa upacāraṃ okkamantassā”ti vuttaṃ. Yaṃ pana andhakaṭṭhakathāyaṃ “parikkhepārahaṭṭhānaṃyeva ‘upacāra’nti sallakkhetvā parikkhepaparikkhepārahaṭṭhānānaṃ ninnānākāraṇadīpanatthaṃ ‘upacāraṃ okkamantassā’ti vuttaṃ pāḷivisesamasallakkhetvāva aparikkhittassa gāmassa upacāraṃ atikkamantassa idha upacāro parikkhepo yathā bhaveyya, taṃ upacāraṃ paṭhamaṃ pādaṃ atikkamantassa āpatti dukkaṭassa. Dutiyaṃ pādaṃ atikkamantassa āpatti pācittiyassā”ti vuttaṃ, taṃ na gahetabbameva pāḷiyā visesasabbhāvatoti. “Aparikkhittassa gāmassa upacāraṃ okkamantiyātipi ekaccesu dissati, taṃ na gahetabbanti apare”ti vuttaṃ. Tattha “pāḷivisesamasallakkhetvā”ti duvuttaṃ, kasmā? Vikālagāmappavesanasikkhāpadepi katthaci “upacāraṃ atikkamantassā”ti pāṭho dissatīti, so andhakaṭṭhakathāpāṭhato gahitoti ācariyo. Aparikkhittassa upacārokkamanameva pāṭho yujjati, na atikkamanaṃ. Kasmā? Bahūsu ṭhānesu pāḷiyā aṭṭhakathāhi virujjhanato, imasmiṃ vāpi sikkhāpade virujjhati. Kathaṃ? Gaṇamhā ohīyamānāya araññe āpatti hoti, na gāme. Atha ca pana nidassanampi “sikkhāpadā buddhavarenā”ti (pari. 479) gāthā dassitā, tasmā upacārokkamanapariyāpannanadiṃ atikkāmentiyā hoti. Kiñca bhiyyo “gacchantassa catasso āpattiyo, ṭhitassa cāpi tattakātiādīnaṃ (pari. 475) parivāragāthānaṃ [M 0.0359][V 0.0327] aṭṭhakathāhi upacārokkamanameva pāṭhoti niṭṭhaṃ gantabba”nti ca vuttaṃ, suṭṭhu sallakkhetvā kathetabbaṃ.

692. Regarding the phrase 'for one crossing the vicinity of an unenclosed village,' it should be understood thus: In the case of entering a village at an improper time, the vicinity should be defined by the distance of two clod-throws. Otherwise, just as here, having treated a place worthy of an enclosure like an enclosure, it is said 'for one crossing,' so there too one should say, 'for one crossing the vicinity of an enclosed village.' However, since it is intended there that the vicinity is one clod-throw beyond the place worthy of an enclosure, therefore, to clarify that meaning, it is said 'for one entering the vicinity of an enclosed village.' As for what is said in the Andhakaṭṭhakathā: 'Having considered only the place worthy of an enclosure as the "vicinity," and for the purpose of showing the non-difference between the enclosure and the place worthy of an enclosure, it is said "for one entering the vicinity." Without considering the specific Pāḷi text, for one crossing the vicinity of an unenclosed village, just as the vicinity here would be the enclosure, for one crossing that vicinity with the first footstep, there is an offense of dukkaṭa. For one crossing with the second footstep, there is an offense of pācittiya'—that should not be accepted at all, because of the specific suitability of the Pāḷi. It is said: 'Also "for one entering the vicinity of an unenclosed village" is seen in some texts; that should not be accepted, say others.' Therein, the statement 'without considering the specific Pāḷi' is wrongly stated. Why? Because also in the training rule on entering a village at an improper time, the reading 'for one crossing the vicinity' is seen in some texts; the teacher says that this is taken from the Andhakaṭṭhakathā reading. For an unenclosed village, only the reading 'entering the vicinity' is suitable, not 'crossing over.' Why? Because it contradicts the Pāḷi texts and the commentaries in many places, and it also contradicts in this very training rule. How? For one being left behind by the group, an offense occurs in the wilderness, not in the village. Moreover, the verse 'sikkhāpadā buddhavarenā' (Pari. 479) is also shown as an example; therefore, the offense occurs for one crossing a river that is included in 'entering the vicinity.' Furthermore, it is also said: 'According to the commentaries on the Parivāra verses beginning with "For one going, four offenses; for one standing, also that many" (Pari. 475), it should be concluded that the reading is only "entering the vicinity".' This should be stated after careful consideration.

“Padasā gamanameva hi idhādhippetaṃ, teneva paṭhamaṃ pādaṃ atikkāmentiyātiādimāhā”ti ettha vikālagāmappavesanasikkhāpadādīsu tadabhāvā yānena vā iddhiyā vā pavisato, addhānaṃ gacchato ca āpattīti dīpeti. Tattha asāruppattā āpattimokkho natthīti eke, vicāretvā gahetabbaṃ. Bhikkhunīvihārabhūmi “gāmantara”nti na vuccati gāmantarapariyāpannāyapi kappiyabhūmittā. “Parato ‘sace bhikkhunīsu mahābodhiyaṅgaṇaṃ pavisantīsu ekā bahi tiṭṭhati, tassā āpattī’tiādivacanato bhikkhuvihāro na kappiyabhūmīti siddhaṃ, tasmā kañcinagare khandhadhammavihāro viya, kāvīrapaṭṭane sārīdhammavihāro viya ca aññopi so vihāro, tasmā sīmabaddhasukhatthaṃ gāmantarabhāve nirantarā adhiṭṭhānatthaṃ pavisantiyā, nikkhamantiyāpi gāmantarāpatti hotīti apare”ti vuttaṃ. Catugāmasādhāraṇattāti ettha evaṃvidhe vihāre sīmaṃ bandhantehi cattāropi te gāmā sodhetabbāti veditabbā. Saṃvidahitvā bhikkhuniyā vā mātugāmena vā theyyasatthena vā saddhiṃ taṃ vihāraṃ okkamantiyā catasso āpattiyo ekatova honti. “Gāmantare gāmantare āpatti pācittiyassā”ti vuttāti eke.

In this commentary passage, where it is said, 'Indeed, only going on foot is intended here, for that reason he said, “when she oversteps with the first foot,” and so on,' it shows that in the training rules concerning entering a village at the wrong time and so on, due to the absence of that [specification of walking], an offense is incurred for one who enters by vehicle or by psychic power, and for one who goes on a long journey. Some say that in that case, due to unsuitability, there is no release from the offense. This should be accepted after investigation. The ground of a bhikkhunī monastery is not called 'another village' because it is allowable ground, even though it is included within another village. From the statement that comes later, 'If, while bhikkhunīs are entering the Mahābodhi courtyard, one stands outside, for her there is an offense,' and so on, it is established that a bhikkhunī monastery is not allowable ground. Therefore, like the Khandhadhamma monastery in Kañcinagara, and like the Sārīdhamma monastery in Kāvīrapaṭṭana, so too is any other such monastery. Others say, 'Therefore, for the ease of establishing a boundary, and for the purpose of determining it as being uninterrupted in its state as another village, for a bhikkhunī who is entering and also for one who is leaving, the offense of [crossing into] another village occurs,' it is said. Here, in the phrase 'due to being common to four villages,' it should be known that when establishing a boundary in such a monastery, those four villages must be cleared. Having made an arrangement, when entering that monastery together with a bhikkhunī, or with a woman, or with a caravan of thieves, four offenses are incurred at once. Some say this is because it is stated, 'For each and every other village, there is an offense of pācittiya.'

Dutiyapāduddhāre saṅghādisesoti ettha sace dutiyo pāduddhāro kappiyabhūmiyaṃ hoti, na saṅghādiseso, akappiyabhūmiyaṃ eva saṅghādiseso. “Ubhayatīresu vicaranti, vaṭṭatīti dassanūpacārassettha sambhavā”ti likhitaṃ, taṃ yuttaṃ. Savanūpacāro hettha nadīpāre, gāmantare vā appamāṇanti. Andhakaṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana “paratīrato nadiṃ otaritvā dassanūpacārato dārūni, paṇṇānivā maggitvā āneti, anāpatti. Ticīvarāni paratīre otāpeti, anāpattī”ti vuttaṃ. “Orimatīrameva āgacchati, āpattī”ti atikkamitukāmatāya paviṭṭhattā vuttaṃ. “Nhāyanādikiccena paviṭṭhānaṃ katthevālayasambhavā vaṭṭatī”ti vuttaṃ. Gāmantare pamāṇanti aṭṭhakathāyaṃ paratīrato nadiṃ otaritvā dassanūpacārato dārūni paṇṇāni sakagāmato thokampi taraṇavārena na vaṭṭati kira nikkhamitvā pavisituṃ.

Regarding 'a saṅghādisesa offense in the second lifting of the foot': here, if the second lifting of the foot is in an allowable area, it is not a saṅghādisesa; only in an unallowable area is it a saṅghādisesa. It is written, “‘They move about on both banks; it is allowable because of the possibility of being within the range of sight here’.” That is correct. Indeed, here the range of hearing on the other side of the river or in another village is without limit. But in the Andhaka commentary it is said: “Having descended into the river from the other bank, one seeks and brings firewood or leaves from within the range of sight; there is no offense. One dries the three robes on the other bank; there is no offense.” The statement, “‘One comes only to this bank; there is an offense’,” is said because one has entered with the desire to cross over. It is said: “For those who have entered for a purpose such as bathing, it is allowable because of the possibility of lingering right there.” In the commentary, regarding 'the measure in another village': having descended into the river from the other bank for firewood and leaves from within the range of sight, it is not allowable, it is said, to exit from one's own village even a little by means of crossing and then to enter.

Agāmake [M 0.0360] araññeti agāmalakkhaṇe araññeti attho. Iminā āpattikhettaṃ dassitaṃ. Yasmā idaṃ āpattikhettaṃ, tasmā yā bhikkhunupassayato gāmassa indakhīlaṃ atikkamati, sā asante [V 0.0328] gāme gaṇamhā ohīyanāpattiṃ āpajjati. Dassanasavanūpacārābhāvepi pageva gāme indakhīlātikkamanakkhaṇeyeva āpajjati. Sace tattha ekā bhikkhunī atthi, tassā dassanasavanūpacārātikkamanakkhaṇe āpajjati, araññamaggagamanakāle evāyaṃ vidhīti na gahetabbaṃ. Gāmato pana nikkhamantī ito paṭṭhāya āpajjatīti dassanatthaṃ “agāmakaṃ arañña”nti vuttaṃ. Vuttañhetaṃ “ārādhikā ca honti saṅgāhikā lajjiniyo, tā kopetvā aññattha na gantabbaṃ. Gacchati ce, gāmantaranadīpārarattivippavāsagaṇamhā ohīyanāpattīhi na muccatī”tiādi. Tattha “gaṇamhā ohīyanāpatti sakiṃyevāpajjati. Itarā gāme gāme pāre pāre aruṇe aruṇe cāti veditabba”nti vuttaṃ. Tattha “vuttañheta”ntiādīni asādhakāni yathāsambhavaṃ gahetabbattā. “Mahābodhiyaṅgaṇantiādi evaṃ gāmassa āsannaṭṭhānepi imaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjatīti dassanatthaṃ vutta”nti likhitaṃ.

“In a wilderness without a village” means in a wilderness characterized as being without a village. By this, the field of the offense is shown. Because this is the field of the offense, therefore, whichever bhikkhunī crosses the threshold of the village from the bhikkhunī's monastery, she, in the absence of a village, incurs the offense of being left behind by the group. Even in the absence of the range of sight and hearing, she incurs the offense already at the very moment of crossing the threshold in the village. If there is one bhikkhunī there, she incurs the offense at the moment of crossing beyond the range of sight and hearing of that bhikkhunī. It should not be understood that this rule applies only at the time of traveling on a wilderness path. However, to show that one leaving the village incurs the offense from this point onwards, the phrase “a wilderness without a village” was stated. For it is said: “They are pleasing, supportive, and conscientious bhikkhunīs. Having angered them, one should not go elsewhere. If one does go, one is not freed from the offenses of going to another village, crossing a river, spending the night separately, and being left behind by the group,” and so on. Therein, it is said: “The offense of being left behind by the group is incurred only once. The others, it should be known, are incurred in every village, on every shore, and at every dawn.” Therein, the phrases “For it is said,” and so on, are not proofs, because they are to be taken as is appropriate. It is written: “The phrase ‘the courtyard of the Mahābodhi,’ and so on, was stated to show that one incurs this offense even in a place near a village.”

Tatiyasaṅghādisesasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the third Saṅghādisesa training rule is concluded.

4. Catutthasaṅghādisesasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

4. Commentary on the Fourth Saṅghādisesa Training Rule

694. Paṭivattāti paṭivacanaṃ denti. Kammadosanti “anaññāya gaṇassa chandanti evamādī”ti likhitaṃ. Kattabbaṭṭhānadosanti porāṇā. Kārakagaṇassāti kārakasaṅghassa. “Bhikkhunisaṅghaṃ sannipātetvā’ti vuttattā kārakasaṅghopi ayamevāti ce? Paṭhamameva kārakasaṅghaṃ na āmantetvā balakkārenāyaṃ thullanandā taṃ bhikkhuniṃ osāresī”ti porāṇagaṇṭhipade vuttaṃ, tasmā kārakabhikkhūnaṃ sammukhāpi tesaṃ anumatiṃ paṭhamaṃ aggahetvā taṃ kammaṃ na paṭippassambhetabbanti siddhaṃ hoti, paṭippassaddhaṃ balakkārena na kātabbamevāti adhippāyo. “Bhikkhunīpi diṭṭhāvikammaṃ kātuṃ labhatī”ti ca tattha vuttaṃ.

694. They give a reply. Regarding `kammadosa`, it is written: 'without knowing the consent of the assembly, and so on'. The ancients say this means 'a fault in the place where it should be done'. `Kārakagaṇassa` means of the `kārakasaṅgha`. If one were to say, 'Because it is said, “having assembled the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha,” is this very assembly also the `kārakasaṅgha`?'—it is said in the ancient glossary: 'Without first inviting the `kārakasaṅgha`, this Thullanandā reinstated that bhikkhunī by force.' Therefore, it is established that even in the presence of the acting bhikkhus, that formal act should not be rescinded without first taking their consent. The intention is that the rescinding should not be done by force at all. And it is also said there: 'A bhikkhunī, too, is allowed to perform the formal act of making one's view known'.

698. Asante kammakārakasaṅghe osāreti, anāpattīti ettha kittāvatā asanto nāma hotīti? Idaṃ sabbattha na vicāritaṃ. Kārakānaṃ [M 0.0361] kālakiriyāyāti eke. Ekassapi abhāvenāti eke. Ekasmiṃ rajjeti eke. Ekaraṭṭheti eke. Ekagāmeti eke. Ekasmiṃ āvāseti eke. Yattha sakkā apaloketunti eke. Antoaddhayojaneti eke. Tattha tasmiṃ āvāse asante kārakasaṅghe osāreti, anāpattīti idaṃ pasaṃsanti ācariyā. Yattha sakkā apaloketunti sāmīci.

698. Regarding 'When one reinstates in the absence of the formal act-performing Saṅgha, there is no offense'—to what extent is it called 'absent'? This matter has not been investigated in all the glossaries. Some say: due to the death of the acting monastics. Others say: due to the absence of even one. Some say: in one kingdom. Others say: in one country. Some say: in one village. Others say: in one residence. Others say: where it is possible to make an announcement. Others say: within half a yojana. Among these, the teachers praise this decision: if one reinstates in the absence of the formal act-performing Saṅgha in that residence, there is no offense. The statement 'where it is possible to make an announcement' is the proper practice.

Catutthasaṅghādisesasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Fourth Saṅghādisesa Training Rule is concluded.

5. Pañcamasaṅghādisesasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

5. Commentary on the Fifth Saṅghādisesa Training Rule

701. Etaṃ [V 0.0329] na vuttanti bhikkhuniyā avassutabhāvo daṭṭhabboti etaṃ niyamanaṃ na vuttaṃ. Taṃ avacanaṃ pāḷiyā sameti. Katarapāḷiyāti? “Anavassutoti jānantī paṭiggaṇhātī”ti imāya. Yadi hi puggalassa avassutabhāvo na pamāṇaṃ, kiṃ imāya pāḷiyā payojanaṃ, “anāpatti ubho anavassutā honti, anavassutā paṭiggaṇhātī”ti ettakameva vattabbaṃ siyā. Attano hi anavassutabhāvoyeva pamāṇanti. Imassa pana anāpattivārassa ayamattho – ubho ce anavassutā, sabbathāpi anāpatti. Atha bhikkhunī anavassutā samānā avassutampi “anavassuto”ti saññāya tassa hatthato paṭiggaṇhāti, evampi anāpattīti. Atha sā anavassutāpi aññaṃ anavassutaṃ vā avassutaṃ vā “avassuto”ti jānāti, dukkaṭameva. Vuttañhetaṃ anantarasikkhāpade “kissa tvaṃ ayye na paṭiggaṇhāsīti. Avassuto ayyeti…pe… nāhaṃ avassutā”ti.

701. Herein, 'This was not stated' means that the stipulation, 'the bhikkhunī's uncorrupted state is to be seen,' was not stated. That non-statement accords with the Pāḷi. With which Pāḷi? With this: 'Knowing him to be uncorrupted, she receives.' For if the uncorrupted state of the person were not the standard, what would be the purpose of this Pāḷi? Only this much should have been said: 'There is no offense if both are uncorrupted; an uncorrupted one receives.' For one's own uncorrupted state is indeed the standard. However, this is the meaning of this non-offense clause: if both are uncorrupted, there is no offense in any way. Furthermore, if a bhikkhunī, being uncorrupted, receives from the hand of one who is corrupted, with the perception that 'he is uncorrupted,' even so there is no offense. But if she, though uncorrupted, knows another—whether uncorrupted or corrupted—to be 'corrupted,' it is only a dukkaṭa offense. And this was stated in the immediately preceding training rule: 'Why, venerable lady, do you not receive?' 'The venerable sir is corrupted.' ... 'I am not corrupted.'

Pañcamasaṅghādisesasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Fifth Saṅghādisesa Training Rule is concluded.

6. Chaṭṭhasaṅghādisesasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

6. Commentary on the Sixth Saṅghādisesa Training Rule

705. Tenāti tasmā. Yasmā uyyojikā na deti na paṭiggaṇhāti, tasmā paṭiggaho na vijjatīti attho. Itarissā paribhogapaccayā. “Akusalacitta”nti bāhullena vuttaṃ. “Vaṭṭatīti saññāya vadantiyāpi āpattī”ti vadanti.

705. Herein, `tena` means 'therefore.' Because the instigating bhikkhunī neither gives nor receives, therefore there is no 'receiving'; this is the meaning. For the other, the offense is conditioned by enjoyment. The phrase 'unwholesome mind' is stated by way of generalization. They say: 'There is an offense even for one who speaks with the perception that “it is allowable.”'

Chaṭṭhasaṅghādisesasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Sixth Saṅghādisesa Training Rule is concluded.

7. Sattamasaṅghādisesasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

7. Commentary on the Seventh Saṅghādisesa Training Rule

712-4. Kammavācato [M 0.0362] pubbe āpannāpattiyo na paṭippassambhanti. Ñattiyā dukkaṭathullaccayā paṭippassambhanti saṅghādisese patteti porāṇā. Taṃ “ajjhāpajjantiyā”ti pāḷiyā sameti. “Sutvā na vadantī”ti ettha sace jīvitabrahmacariyantarāyabhayā na vadanti, anāpatti[V 0.0330]. “Adhammakamme adhammakammasaññā āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti vuttattā “anāpatti asamanubhāsantiyā”ti saṅghādisesaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ.

Offenses incurred before the Kammavācā do not subside. The ancients say that when a Saṅghādisesa has been incurred, the dukkaṭa and thullaccaya offenses subside by the ñatti. This accords with the Pāḷi text 'ajjhāpajjantiyā' (while incurring). Here, in 'having heard, they do not speak,' if they do not speak due to fear of danger to life or the holy life, there is no offense. Because it is said, 'In an unlawful act, with the perception of it as an unlawful act, there is an offense of dukkaṭa,' the statement 'there is no offense for one who does not admonish' is said with reference to the Saṅghādisesa.

Sattamasaṅghādisesasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Seventh Saṅghādisesa Training Rule is concluded.

8. Aṭṭhamasaṅghādisesasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

8. Commentary on the Eighth Saṅghādisesa Training Rule

715. Paccākatāti parājitā. Kuladūsakasikkhāpadassa, imassa ca nidānamattameva nānākaraṇaṃ. Vuttañhi tattha “tassa vacanassa paṭinissaggāya eva vacanīyo, na kuladūsananivāraṇatthāyā”ti. Evaṃ sante ubhopetā āpattiyo aññamaññaṃ sabhāgatthā, tasmā idaṃ tassa anupaññattisadisaṃ āpajjati, tato idaṃ niratthakameva āpajjatīti? Na evaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Vatthuvisesato, kammavācāvisesato ca ubhinnaṃ nānākaraṇaṃ.

715. Here, 'rejected' means they have committed a pārājika offense. The difference between the training rule on corrupting families and this one is only a matter of the origin story. For it is said there: 'He should be spoken to only for the retraction of that statement, not for the purpose of preventing the corrupting of families.' This being so, are both these offenses similar in nature to each other, and therefore this one becomes like an amendment to that one, and thus becomes entirely pointless? It should not be seen thus. The difference between the two lies in the specific object and the specific formal act.

Aṭṭhamasaṅghādisesasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Eighth Saṅghādisesa Training Rule is concluded.

9. Navamasaṅghādisesasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

9. Explanation of the Ninth Saṅghādisesa Training Rule

723. “Kāyikavācasikena saṃsaggenā”ti pāṭhaseso.

723. The remainder of the text should be understood as: 'through bodily and verbal association.'

Navamasaṅghādisesasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Ninth Saṅghādisesa Training Rule is concluded.

Saṅghādisesakaṇḍavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Saṅghādisesa Section is concluded.

3. Nissaggiyakaṇḍavaṇṇanā

3. Explanation of the Nissaggiya Section

1. Paṭhamanissaggiyapācittiyasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

1. Explanation of the First Nissaggiya Pācittiya Training Rule

733. Paṭhamanissaggiyapācittiyasikkhāpadaṃ [V 0.0331][M 0.0363] uttānameva.

733. The First Nissaggiya Pācittiya Training Rule is self-explanatory.

2. Dutiyanissaggiyapācittiyasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

2. Explanation of the Second Nissaggiya Pācittiya Training Rule

740. Vatthusampattattā vā na tassā anāpannakāmatāya vā anāṇattikatāya vā akālacīvaramadaṃsu. Yathādāne eva upanetabbaṃ, na bhājetabbaṃ puggalikattāti adhippāyo. Atthato hi itarampi yathādāne eva upanetabbameva. Gaṇṭhipade pana “ayyāya dammīti evaṃ paṭiladdhanti nissaṭṭhapaṭiladdhaṃ. Yathādāneti dāyakehi pariccattavidhānena. Upanetabbanti akālacīvarabhāvena bhājetabbanti adhippāyo. Idha bhājāpitāya laddhacīvarameva nissaggiyaṃ hoti, taṃ vinayakammaṃ katvāpi attanā na labhatī”ti likhitaṃ. Yadi nissaṭṭhapaṭiladdhaṃ sandhāya idaṃ vuttaṃ siyā, “nissajjitabbaṃ saṅghassa vā gaṇassa vā puggalassa vā dadeyya, dadeyyuṃ, ayyāya dammī”ti vuttattā tīṇipetāni padāni vattabbāni siyuṃ, tasmā na kevalaṃ nissaṭṭhapaṭiladdhameva yathādāne upanetabbaṃ, aññāhi bhikkhunīhi laddhakoṭṭhāsampi yathādāneyeva upanetabbaṃ.

740. Either because the object was complete, or because of the desire for her not to incur an offense, or because it was not by command, they gave an out-of-season robe. The meaning is that it should be brought just as it was given; it should not be divided, because it is a personal gift. Indeed, in essence, even another robe should be brought just as it was given. But in the Gaṇṭhipada, it is written: 'Regarding "having been obtained thus, 'I give to the venerable lady'": this is a robe obtained through forfeiture. "As it was given" means in the manner given up by the donors. "It should be brought" means it should be divided as an out-of-season robe.' This is the meaning. Here, only a robe obtained through having it divided becomes subject to forfeiture; having performed the Vinaya act for it, one does not obtain it oneself. If this were said in reference to a robe obtained by forfeiture, because it is said, "It should be forfeited; one should give it to the Sangha, or to a group, or to an individual; they should give; 'I give to the venerable lady'," these three phrases would have to be stated. Therefore, not only a robe obtained by forfeiture should be brought as it was given, but also a share obtained by other bhikkhunīs should be brought just as it was given.

741. “Akālacīvare kālacīvarasaññāya anāpattī”ti pana bhājanapaccayā āpajjitabbāpattiṃ nāpajjatīti ettakameva dīpeti, na paṭiladdhaṃ, na yathādāne dātabbanti imamatthaṃ dīpeti. Lesena pana gaṇhāti ce, bhaṇḍagghena kāretabbā.

741. The statement, 'There is no offense regarding an out-of-season robe if one perceives it as in-season,' however, indicates only this much: that one does not incur an offense that should be incurred due to the condition of division. It does not indicate about what was obtained, nor does it indicate this meaning: that it should be given as it was originally given. But if one takes it by a hint, she should be made to pay the value of the goods.

Dutiyanissaggiyapācittiyasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Second Nissaggiya Pācittiya Training Rule is concluded.

3. Tatiyanissaggiyapācittiyasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

3. Explanation of the Third Nissaggiya Pācittiya Training Rule

744. Sakasaññāya [V 0.0332] gahitattā pācittiyaṃ, dukkaṭañca vuttaṃ. Itarathā bhaṇḍagghena kāretabbaṃ.

744. Because it is taken with the perception of it being one's own, a Pācittiya offense and a Dukkaṭa offense are stated. Otherwise, it should be made good at the value of the goods.

Tatiyanissaggiyapācittiyasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Third Nissaggiya Pācittiya Training Rule is concluded.

4. Catutthanissaggiyapācittiyasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

4. Explanation of the Fourth Nissaggiya Pācittiya Training Rule

752. Lesena [M 0.0364] gahetukāmatā, aññassa viññussa viññāpanaṃ, paṭilābhoti tīṇi aṅgāni, tasmā paṭhamaṃ viññattaṃ alabhitvā aññaṃ tato ūnatarampi labheyya, nissaggiyameva aṅgasampattito. Esa nayo aññatthāpi.

752. The desire to take by a hint, making it known to another wise person, and acquisition: these are the three factors. Therefore, if without obtaining what was first requested, one obtains another thing, even one of lesser value than that, it is indeed subject to forfeiture due to the completion of the factors. This is the principle in other cases as well.

Catutthanissaggiyapācittiyasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Fourth Nissaggiya Pācittiya Training Rule is concluded.

5. Pañcamanissaggiyapācittiyasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

5. Explanation of the Fifth Nissaggiya Pācittiya Training Rule

753. “Telaṃ gopetvā sappimpi me attano kulagharā”ti kira pāṭho.

753. It is said that the reading is: 'Having stored oil, ghee also is from my own family home.'

Pañcamanissaggiyapācittiyasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Fifth Nissaggiya Pācittiya Training Rule is concluded.

6. Chaṭṭhanissaggiyapācittiyasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

6. Explanation of the Sixth Nissaggiya Pācittiya Training Rule

758-762. Pāvārikassāti dussavāṇijakassa. Yāya cetāpitaṃ, tassā nissaggiyaṃ, nissaṭṭhapaṭilābho ca. “Itarāsaṃ pana jānitvā vassaggena pattakoṭṭhāsaṃ sādiyantīnampi na nissaggiyaṃ, kevalaṃ yathādāne eva tāhipi upanetabba”nti vadanti. “Nissaṭṭhaṃ paṭilabhitvāpi yathādāne upanetabba’nti vuttattā sesāhi gahitaṃ suggahita”nti vadanti. Ettha gilānāyapi na mokkho.

`Pāvārikassa` means 'of the cloth merchant'. For whichever bhikkhunī it was caused to be bought, for her it is to be forfeited, and there is recovery of the forfeited article. They say: 'However, for the other bhikkhunīs who, knowing, consent to the share that has arrived by seniority in the rains-residence, it is not to be forfeited; merely, it should be brought by them just as it was given.' They also say: 'Because it is said, "Even having recovered the forfeited item, it should be brought just as it was given," the item taken by the remaining bhikkhunīs is well-taken.' Here, there is no exemption even for a sick bhikkhunī.

Chaṭṭhanissaggiyapācittiyasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Sixth Nissaggiya Pācittiya Training Rule is concluded.

7. Sattamanissaggiyapācittiyasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

7. Explanation of the Seventh Nissaggiya Pācittiya Training Rule

764. Sattame [V 0.0333] “sayaṃ yācitakenā”ti kiñcāpi avisesena vuttaṃ. Tathāpi aññadatthikena attuddesikena saññācikenāti attho veditabbo. Ayamattho “bhikkhuniyo tena ca parikkhārena sayampi yācitvā [M 0.0365] bhesajjaṃ cetāpetvā paribhuñjiṃsū”ti imissā pāḷiyā atthena saṃsanditvā veditabbo. Tassāyamattho – tena parikkhārena bhesajjaṃ cetāpetvā ca-saddena saññācikena ca bhesajjaṃ cetāpetvāti imamatthaṃ dīpento “sayampi yācitvā bhesajjaṃ cetāpetvā”ti āha. Aññathā “tena parikkhārena bhesajjaṃ cetāpetvā sayampi yācitvā paribhuñjiṃsū”ti iminā anukkamena pāḷi vattabbā siyā.

764. In the seventh, although the term `sayaṃyācitakena` ('by what is requested by oneself') is stated generally, it should nevertheless be understood to mean 'by what is requested for another's purpose, for one's own sake, with enticement.' This meaning is to be understood by connecting it with the meaning of this Pali passage: 'The bhikkhunīs, with that requisite and also having requested for themselves, caused medicine to be bought and used it.' The meaning of that passage is this: to explain the meaning 'having caused medicine to be bought with that requisite, and (by the word `ca`) also with what was requested with enticement,' he said, 'having also requested for themselves and caused medicine to be bought.' Otherwise, the Pali text would have to be stated in this sequence: 'having caused medicine to be bought with that requisite, and having requested for themselves, they used it.'

Padabhājane pana “saṃyācikenāti sayaṃ yācitvā”ti tasseva padassa adhippāyamattaṃ vuttaṃ. Sā hi padabhājanadhammatā. “Saṅghikaṃ lābhaṃ pariṇata”ntiādipadānaṃ bhājane pana sā pākaṭā. Aññathā saṃyācikapadena ko añño atirekattho saṅgahito siyā, so na dissatīti tadeva padaṃ nippayojanaṃ, idañca sikkhāpadaṃ purimena ninnānākaraṇaṃ siyā. Attano hi santakaṃ yathākāmaṃ karaṇīyanti. Ettha ca saṅghassa yācanāya vasena ekato hutvā yācanāya laddhaṃ saṃyācikanti veditabbaṃ. Aññathā ito parena saṃyācika-saddena idaṃ nibbisesaṃ āpajjatīti “puggalikena saṃyācikenā”ti idañca sikkhāpadaṃ visuṃ na vattabbaṃ siyā idheva tena āpajjitabbāpattiyā saṅgahitattā, na ca saṅgahitā āpattidvayabhāvato. Missetvā cetāpitattā hi ekameva āpattīti ce? Na, saṃyācikapadassa nippayojanabhāvappasaṅgato, evaṃ saṅghikamahājanikapuggalikāni missitvā cetāpane ekāpattibhāvappasaṅgato ca.

In the word analysis, however, ‘saṃyācikena’ means ‘having requested oneself’—only the intended meaning of that very word is stated. Indeed, such is the nature of word analysis. In the analysis of terms beginning with ‘saṅghikaṃ lābhaṃ pariṇataṃ,’ however, this is evident. Otherwise, what other additional meaning would be included by the term ‘saṃyācika’? That is not seen. Therefore, that very word would be useless, and this training rule would have no difference from the previous one. For one’s own property may be dealt with as one wishes. And here, what is obtained by requesting, having come together by means of a request of the Saṅgha, should be known as ‘saṃyācika.’ Otherwise, this would become indistinct from the subsequent word ‘saṃyācika.’ Therefore, this training rule, ‘puggalikena saṃyācikena,’ should not be stated separately, because the offense that should be incurred by that other rule would be included right here. But it is not included, because there are two offenses. If one were to say: 'Because it was caused to be purchased after mixing, there is indeed only one offense'? No, because of the consequence that the word ‘saṃyācika’ would be useless, and because of the consequence that there would be only one offense when causing Saṅghika, Mahājanika, and Puggalika items to be purchased after mixing them.

Sattamanissaggiyapācittiyasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Seventh Nissaggiya Pācittiya Training Rule is concluded.

8. Aṭṭhamanissaggiyapācittiyasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

8. Explanation of the Eighth Nissaggiya Pācittiya Training Rule

769. Gaṇassāti ābhidhammikādigaṇassa, ūnacatuvaggassa ca.

769. Regarding 'gaṇassa' (of a group): this refers to a group such as the Abhidhammika group, and to a group of less than four.

Aṭṭhamanissaggiyapācittiyasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Eighth Nissaggiya Pācittiya Training Rule is concluded.

9. Navamanissaggiyapācittiyasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

9. Explanation of the Ninth Nissaggiya Pācittiya Training Rule

774. Saññācikenāti [V 0.0334] gaṇayācanāya laddheneva, na aññena.

774. 'Saññācikena' means: only with what is obtained by a group request, not with anything else.

Navamanissaggiyapācittiyasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Ninth Nissaggiya Pācittiya Training Rule is concluded.

10. Dasamanissaggiyapācittiyasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

10. Explanation of the Tenth Nissaggiya Pācittiya Training Rule

779. Dasame [M 0.0366] pana “yā pana bhikkhunī aññadatthikena parikkhārena aññuddisikena puggalikena aññaṃ cetāpeyya, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiya”nti evaṃvidhena bhavitabbaṃ, “puggalikena saṃyācikenā”ti iminā ekādasamena bhavitabbaṃ siyā yathākkamena sambhavato. Kāmameva cetaṃ aṭṭhuppattiyā abhāvato na vuttaṃ, atthato pana gahetabbameva. Ettha pana saṅghagaṇapuggalānaṃ pavāritaṭṭhāne, puggalasseva ñātakaṭṭhāne ca anāpattichāyā dissati, idaṃ sabbaṃ amhākaṃ takkānusāravaseneva vuttanti katvā na sārato daṭṭhabbaṃ. Vicāretvā yathā niccalakāraṇaṃ disvā yaṃ vā vinayakkamakovidā anujānanti, taṃ tadeva gahetabbaṃ. Porāṇagaṇṭhipade pana “āpadāsupi aññaṃ garubhaṇḍameva cetāpetabbaṃ, itaraṃ na vaṭṭati, bhikkhussa pana vaṭṭatī”ti vuttaṃ.

779. In the tenth, however, the Pāḷi should be of this kind: 'Whatever bhikkhunī should have another requisite obtained with a requisite intended for another purpose, designated for another, or belonging to an individual, it is an offense of expiation with forfeiture.' With the words 'with a personally requested [requisite],' this should be the eleventh, as it should occur in due order. Indeed, this training rule was not stated due to the absence of an origin story, but it should certainly be taken in terms of its meaning. Here, however, a shadow of non-offense is seen in a place where one has been invited by the Saṅgha, a group, or an individual, and in the case of an individual's relatives. All this has been stated only according to our line of reasoning, and thus should not be regarded as essential. Having investigated and seen the firm reason, whatever the experts skilled in the Vinaya procedure permit, that very thing should be accepted. But in the ancient glosses, it is said: 'Even in times of danger, only another heavy article should be caused to be purchased; another [type of article] is not allowable. For a bhikkhu, however, it is allowable.'

Dasamanissaggiyapācittiyasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Tenth Nissaggiya Pācittiya Training Rule is concluded.

11. Ekādasamanissaggiyapācittiyasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

11. Explanation of the Eleventh Nissaggiya Pācittiya Training Rule

784. “Dutiyavaggassa paṭhame”ti avatvā “ekādasame”ti idha vuttaṃ. Kasmā? Bhikkhunivibhaṅge tiṃsakakaṇḍaṃ patvā vaggakkamassa avuttattā. Yasmā pavāritaṭṭhāne viññatti nāma na paṭisedhetabbā, tasmā bhagavā aññātikaappavāritaṭṭhāne dhammanimantanavasena vadeyya “yenattho”ti vuttāya “catukkaṃsaparamaṃ viññāpetabba”nti paricchedaṃ dassetīti veditabbaṃ. Aññathā “nidānena sikkhāpadaṃ na sameti, sikkhāpadena ca anāpattivāro”ti ca “akataviññattiyā catukkaṃsaparamaṃ viññāpetabba”nti ca aniṭṭhaṃ āpajjati, tasmā mātikāṭṭhakathāyaṃ cetāpetabbanti ṭhapetvā sahadhammike ca ñātakapavārite ca aññena kismiñcideva guṇena, parituṭṭhena ca vadeyya “yenattho”ti vuttassa “viññāpetabba”nti vuttanayena [V 0.0335] attho daṭṭhabbo. Porāṇagaṇṭhipade pana “idaṃ paricchinnapavāraṇaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Anāpatti ñātakānaṃ pavāritānanti pana sabbappakārena pavattaṃ niccapavāraṇaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Niccapavāraṇā nāma yadā yenattho, tadā taṃ vadeyyāthāti evaṃ pavattā[M 0.0367]. ‘Handa sītapāvuraṇa’nti dentānaṃ pana atirekacatukkaṃsampi gahetuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti vuttaṃ. Ayameva nayo dasamepīti.

784. Instead of saying 'in the first of the second chapter,' it is stated here 'in the eleventh.' Why? Because in the Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga, having reached the section of thirty, the sequence of chapters is not stated. Because a request should not be forbidden at a place of invitation, therefore, it should be understood that the Blessed One, at a place of non-relatives where one is not invited, indicates the limit by way of a doctrinal invitation, saying, 'a maximum of four kaṃsas should be requested' for what is needed. Otherwise, it would lead to the undesirable meaning that 'the training rule does not accord with the origin story, and the chapter on non-offenses does not accord with the training rule,' and that 'for an unmade request, a maximum of four kaṃsas should be requested.' Therefore, in the Mātikā-aṭṭhakathā, regarding 'one may cause to be obtained,' setting aside fellow monastics and invited relatives, if another person, due to some virtue or being pleased, should say, 'whatever is needed,' the meaning for what was said should be understood according to the method stated as 'it should be requested.' In the ancient glosses, however, it is said: 'This is stated in reference to a limited invitation. But the passage "There is no offense for invited relatives" is stated in reference to a perpetual invitation that occurs in all ways. A perpetual invitation is one that proceeds thus: "Whenever there is a need for something, you may state it." For those who give, saying, "Here, take a winter cloak!", it is permissible to accept even more than four kaṃsas.' It should be understood that this same method is found in the tenth rule as well.

Ekādasamanissaggiyapācittiyasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Eleventh Nissaggiya Pācittiya Training Rule is concluded.

Bhikkhunīvibhaṅge tiṃsakavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

In the Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga, the explanation of the section of thirty is concluded.

Nissaggiyakaṇḍavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Nissaggiya section is concluded.

4. Pācittiyakaṇḍavaṇṇanā

4. Explanation of the Pācittiya Section

1. Lasuṇavaggo

1. The Garlic Chapter

1. Paṭhamalasuṇasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

1. Explanation of the First Garlic Training Rule

793-7. Ahaṃ [M 0.0368][V 0.0336] lasuṇenāti ettha “pavāremī”ti pāṭhaseso. Badarasāḷavaṃ kira badaraphalāni sukkhāpetvā cuṇṇetvā kattabbā khādanīyavikati.

793-7. Here, in 'I with garlic,' the remainder of the text, 'I invite,' should be supplied. Badarasāḷava, it is said, is a type of edible food to be made by drying jujube fruits and powdering them.

Paṭhamalasuṇasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the First Garlic Training Rule is concluded.

2. Dutiyasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

2. Explanation of the Second Training Rule

800. Saṃharāpeyyāti “saṃharati vā saṃharāpeti vā”ti padabhājanaṃ veditabbaṃ. Kiñcāpi ettha āpattibhedo na dassito, tathāpi khurasaṇḍāsakattariādipariyesanaghaṃsanādīsu pubbapayogesu dukkaṭaṃ yujjati, yathā cettha, evaṃ talaghātakādimhi ca āpattibhedo pāḷiyaṃ na vutto. Yathāsambhavaṃ pana pubbapayogesu dukkaṭaṃ sambhavati. Evaṃ bhikkhussa ettha ca lasuṇe ca dukkaṭaṃ. Idaṃ kiriyākiriyanti porāṇā. Tattha “kiriyākiriya”nti na vuttaṃ.

800. 'Saṃharāpeyya' (Should cause to be removed): the analysis of the phrase should be understood as 'saṃharati vā saṃharāpeti vā' (one removes or causes to be removed). Although a distinction of offenses is not shown here, nevertheless, in the preliminary acts of searching for, sharpening, etc., a razor, tweezers, scissors, and so on, a dukkaṭa offense is fitting. Just as in this training rule, so too in the case of striking with the palm, etc., a distinction of offenses is not stated in the Pāḷi. However, as is possible, a dukkaṭa offense can arise in the preliminary acts. Similarly, for a bhikkhu, both in this training rule and in the one concerning garlic, a dukkaṭa is fitting. The ancients say, 'This is an action-and-non-action [offense].' In that [training rule on garlic], 'action-and-non-action' is not stated.

Dutiyasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Second Training Rule is concluded.

802-6. Tatiyacatutthasikkhāpadaṃ uttānatthameva.

The Third and Fourth Training Rules are of obvious meaning.

5. Pañcamasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

5. The Explanation of the Fifth Training Rule

812. Pañcame [V 0.0337] udakasuddhipaccaye satipi phassasādiyane yathāvuttaparicchede anāpatti. Tattha dvinnaṃ pabbānanti “dvinnaṃ aṅgulānaṃ sahapavesane ekekaaṅgulassa ekekaṃ pabbaṃ katvā dve pabbā, ekaṅgulappavesane dvinnaṃ pabbānaṃ [M 0.0369] upari na vaṭṭatīti veditabbaṃ. Mahāpaccariyampi ayameva nayo dassito”ti likhitaṃ.

812. In the fifth training rule, even if there is enjoyment of the contact for the purpose of purification with water, there is no offense within the aforementioned limit. Therein, regarding "of two joints," it should be understood thus: "When two fingers are inserted together, by taking one joint from each finger, there are two joints. When one finger is inserted, it is not allowable beyond two joints." In the Mahāpaccarī also, this very method is shown. Thus it is written.

Pañcamasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Fifth Training Rule is concluded.

815. Chaṭṭhasikkhāpadaṃ uttānatthameva.

815. The Sixth Training Rule is of obvious meaning.

7. Sattamasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

7. The Explanation of the Seventh Training Rule

820-822. “Nagaraṃ atiharantī”ti pāṭho. “Nagaradvāre atiharantī”ti katthaci, tattha dvārenāti attho. Ayameva vā pāṭho. Taṃ pubbāparaviruddhanti “punapi vutta”nti vuttaṃ vādaṃ sandhāya, na tato pubbe tattha vuttaṃ vādaṃ. Ettha “mātarampi viññāpetvāti vacanena virujjhatī”ti likhitaṃ, taṃ dullikhitaṃ, na hi tena virodhaṃ sandhāya idaṃ vuttanti. Karaṇe ce pācittiyaṃ, kārāpanepi pācittiyeneva bhavitabbaṃ. Atha kārāpane dukkaṭaṃ, karaṇepi dukkaṭeneva bhavitabbaṃ. Na hi karaṇe vā kārāpane vā viseso atthi āpajjane satīti adhippāyo.

The reading is 'nagaraṃ atiharantī'. In some places, it is 'nagaradvāre atiharantī'; there, the meaning is 'by the gate'. Or this itself is the reading. The statement, "That is contradictory to what precedes and follows," was said with reference to the view stated as "it is said again," not with reference to the view stated there before that. Herein, it is written, "It contradicts the statement 'mātarampi viññāpetvā'", but that is poorly written, for indeed this was not said with reference to that contradiction. If there is a pācittiya offense in doing it, there should be only a pācittiya offense in causing it to be done. Now, if there is a dukkaṭa offense in causing it to be done, there should be only a dukkaṭa offense in doing it. For there is no difference in incurring the offense, whether in doing it or in causing it to be done—this is the intention.

823. Sampaṭicchituṃ vaṭṭatīti appaṭikkhipitvā “sādhū”ti vattuṃ vaṭṭatīti adhippāyo. Na hi paṭiggahetuṃ vaṭṭati. Anāmāsattā “āmakadhaññaṃ pana ñātakapavāritaṭṭhānepi na vaṭṭatī”ti vuttaṃ. Anugaṇṭhipade pana “kappiyena laddhaṃ dhaññaṃ bhajjitvā bhuñjantiyā dukkaṭaṃ. Aparaṇṇepi eseva nayo”ti ca “anāpatti ābādhapaccayāti vacanato satta dhaññānipi anāmāsānīti siddhaṃ, teneva heṭṭhā aṭṭhakathāyaṃ dukkaṭavatthumhi satta dhaññānipi gahitāni anāmāsānī”ti ca vuttāni. Āmāsāni kappiyavatthūni ca yadi bhaveyyuṃ, yathā ñātakapavārite sandhāya “aparaṇṇaṃ viññāpetī”ti avisesena vuttaṃ, evaṃ “anāpatti ñātakānaṃ pavāritānaṃ aññassa atthāya viññāpeti, ummattikāya ādikammikāyā”ti vattabbaṃ. Yasmā dukkaṭavatthuttā ca anāmāsattā ca mātarampi sattavidhaṃ dhaññaṃ viññāpetuṃ na vaṭṭati[V 0.0338], tasmā tadatthadīpanatthaṃ sattavidhaṃ dhaññaṃ sandhāya “anāpatti ābādhapaccayā”ti vuttaṃ, yathā bhikkhuniyā ābādhapaccayā vaṭṭati, tathā bhikkhussāpīti [M 0.0370] ca. Yathā vā pana bhikkhuniyā bhajjanādīni kārāpetuṃ na vaṭṭati, evaṃ bhikkhussāpi. Vuttampi cetaṃ andhakaṭṭhakathāyaṃ “aññataro bālabhikkhu kappiyaṃ ajānanto etadavoca ‘āmakadhaññaṃ sampaṭicchituṃ bhikkhūnaṃ na vaṭṭati. Etaṃ dhaññaṃ bhajjitvā koṭṭetvā pacitvā yāgukhajjakaṃ bhattañca dethā’ti, āṇāpakasseva bhikkhussa āpatti, sabbesaṃ anāpattī”ti. Tasmā “saṅghavārikānaṃ dhaññaṃ koṭṭethā”ti ārāmikānaṃ vattuñca na vaṭṭati. “Divasaṃ paribbayaṃ gaṇhatha, taṇḍule sampādetha, tvaṃ ettake gaṇha, tvaṃ ettake”ti evamādīni pana vattuṃ vaṭṭatīti ca. Yaṃ pana “aviññattiyā labbhamānaṃ pana navakammatthāya sampaṭicchituṃ vaṭṭatī”ti vuttaṃ, tampi heṭṭhā “imaṃ taḷākaṃ khettaṃ vatthuṃ vihārassa demā’ti vutte ‘sampaṭicchituṃ vaṭṭatī”ti vuttaṃ nayaṃ sandhāya vuttattā suvuttameva. “Navakammatthāya dhaññaṃ demā”ti vutte “sādhū”ti vattabbaṃ. Yaṃ pana heṭṭhā “tattha nissaggiyavatthuṃ attano vā saṅghagaṇapuggalacetiyānaṃ vā atthāya sampaṭicchituṃ na vaṭṭati…pe… dukkaṭavatthuṃ sabbesampi atthāya sampaṭicchato dukkaṭamevā”ti vuttaṃ, tampi suvuttameva. Kasmā? “Cetiyassa atthāya dhaññaṃ dātukāmomhi, tumhe bhante tadatthāya sampaṭicchathā”ti vutte paṭiggahetuṃ akappiyattā. “Idaṃ pana tādisaṃ na hotī”ti ca vuttaṃ. Sabbopāyaṃ upatissattheravādo kira. Dhammasiritthero panevamāha “pubbepi navakammatthāya paṭiggaho na vārito, saṅghassatthāya paṭiggahitampi paṭiggāhakasseva akappiya”nti.

823. Herein, 'it is permissible to accept' means it is permissible to say 'good' without rejecting. For it is not proper to receive it for oneself. Because it is an untouchable object, it is said: 'Raw grain, however, is not proper even in a place of invitation from relatives.' But in the Anugaṇṭhipada, it should be known that: 'For a bhikkhunī who roasts and eats grain obtained by a permissible means, there is a dukkaṭa offense. In the case of pulses also, this is the method.' And it is said: 'Because of the statement, "There is no offense on account of illness," it is established that the seven kinds of grain are also untouchable; for that very reason, in the commentary below, in the section on dukkaṭa objects, the seven kinds of grain are also taken as untouchable.' If they were touchable and permissible objects, then just as it is said without distinction, with reference to an invitation from relatives, 'one may request pulses,' so too it should be said: 'There is no offense if one requests on behalf of another from relatives who have made an invitation, nor for a madwoman or a first offender.' Because it is a dukkaṭa object and because it is untouchable, it is not proper to request the seven kinds of grain even from one's mother. Therefore, in order to explain that meaning, with reference to the seven kinds of grain, it was said: 'There is no offense on account of illness.' And just as it is proper for a bhikkhunī on account of illness, so too for a bhikkhu. Or however, just as it is not proper for a bhikkhunī to have roasting, etc., done, so too for a bhikkhu. And this was also said in the Andhakaṭṭhakathā: 'A certain foolish bhikkhu, not knowing what is permissible, said this: "It is not proper for bhikkhus to receive raw grain. Having roasted, pounded, and cooked this grain, give gruel, snacks, and rice." There is an offense for the bhikkhu who is the commander; for all the others, there is no offense.' Therefore, it is not proper to say to the monastery attendants, 'Pound the grain for the bhikkhus on duty from the Saṅgha.' But it is proper to say such things as: 'Take the provisions for the day; prepare the rice grains; you take this much, you take that much.' And this should be known. As for the statement, 'But it is proper to accept that which is being obtained without a request for the purpose of new construction,' that too is indeed well-said, because it was said with reference to the method stated below: 'When it is said, "We give this pond, field, or land to the monastery," it is proper to accept.' When it is said, 'We give grain for the purpose of new construction,' it should be said, 'Good.' As for what was stated below: 'Therein, it is not proper to accept an object to be forfeited for the benefit of oneself, the Saṅgha, a group, an individual, or a cetiya... for one who accepts a dukkaṭa object for the benefit of all, there is only a dukkaṭa offense,' that too is indeed well-said. Why? Because of it being improper to receive by hand when it is said: 'Venerable sirs, I wish to give grain for the benefit of the cetiya; please accept it for that purpose.' And it was said: 'This case, however, is not of such a nature.' This entire decision, it is said, is the view of the Elder Upatissa. But the Elder Dhammasiri says thus: 'Previously also, receiving for the purpose of new construction was not forbidden. That which is received for the benefit of the Saṅgha is improper only for the receiver himself.'

Sattamasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Seventh Training Rule is concluded.

8. Aṭṭhamasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

8. The Explanation of the Eighth Training Rule

824. Porāṇā “nibbiṭṭharājabhaṭo”ti paṭhanti. Tassattho vāritabhattavetano rājabhaṭoti. “Taññeva bhaṭapathanti taṃyeva bhattavetana”nti atthaṃ vadanti. Ummukanti alātaṃ.

824. The ancients recite, 'nibbiṭṭharājabhaṭo.' Its meaning is: a royal soldier whose food-stipend is forbidden. They state the meaning as, 'that very food-stipend.' 'Ummuka' means a firebrand.

826. Ettha chaḍḍitaṃ kiriyā. Anolokanaṃ akiriyā.

826. Here, discarding is an action. Not looking is an inaction.

Aṭṭhamasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Eighth Training Rule is concluded.

9. Navamasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

9. The Explanation of the Ninth Training Rule

832. “Sāmike [M 0.0371][V 0.0339] apaloketvā chaḍḍetī”ti katthaci potthake natthi, katthaci atthi, atthibhāvova seyyo kiriyākiriyattā sikkhāpadassa. Idha khettapālakā, ārāmādigopakā ca sāmikā eva. “Saṅghassa khette, ārāme ca tattha kacavaraṃ na chaḍḍetabbanti katikā ce natthi, bhikkhussa chaḍḍetuṃ vaṭṭati saṅghapariyāpannattā, na bhikkhunīnaṃ. Tāsampi bhikkhunisaṅghasantake vuttanayena vaṭṭati, na tattha bhikkhussa, evaṃ santepi sāruppavaseneva kātabba”nti vuttaṃ.

832. The reading, 'Having informed the owner, one discards it,' is not found in some books but is found in others; its presence is indeed better because the training rule is one of action and inaction. Here, field-keepers and guardians of monasteries and so forth are indeed the owners. It is said: 'If there is no agreement that "rubbish should not be discarded in the Saṅgha's field and in its monastery," it is allowable for a bhikkhu to discard it, because he is included in the Saṅgha, but not for bhikkhunīs. For them too, it is allowable on property belonging to the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha, in the way that has been stated, but not for a bhikkhu there. Even so, it should be done only in a suitable manner.' Thus it was said.

Navamasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the ninth training rule is finished.

10. Dasamasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

10. The Explanation of the Tenth Training Rule

833. Sādhukīḷitagītaṃ vāti ettha pāciṇṇagītampi sotuṃ na vaṭṭati. “Gītupasañhitaṃ pana dhammaṃ sotuṃ vaṭṭatīti dīghanikāyaṭṭhakathāyaṃ vutta”nti vuttaṃ. Porāṇagaṇṭhipade pana “dhammagītampi na vaṭṭatī”ti vatvā “buddhassa gāyāma vādemāti vutte sampaṭicchituṃ na vaṭṭati, dukkaṭaṃ hotī”ti vuttaṃ, “pūjaṃ karoma, jātakaṃ vā vatthuṃ vā desemāti vutte ‘sādhū’ti sampaṭicchituṃ vaṭṭatī”ti ca vuttaṃ.

833. Here, regarding the phrase 'or a well-played song,' it is not allowable to listen even to a noble, well-practiced song about the virtues of the Buddha. It is said: 'However, it is stated in the Dīghanikāya-aṭṭhakathā that it is allowable to listen to the Dhamma connected with song.' But in the ancient Gaṇṭhipada, having said, 'Even a Dhamma song is not allowable,' it is stated: 'When it is said, "Let us sing or play music for the Buddha," it is not allowable to accept; it is a dukkaṭa offense.' And it is also stated: 'When it is said, "Let us make an offering," or "Let us teach a Jātaka or a story," it is allowable to accept by saying, "Sādhu".'

836. Ekapayogo nāma ekadivasāvalokanaṃ. Tesaṃyevāti yesaṃ naccaṃ passati. “Bhikkhunī sayampi naccituṃ vā gāyituṃ vā vādituṃ vā na labhatī”tiādi idha sikkhāpade natthi. Kasmā? Eḷakalomasamuṭṭhānattā. Yadi evaṃ kasmā vuttanti ce? Suttānulomamahāpadesato. Yadi naccādīni passituṃ vā sotuṃ vā na labhati, pageva attanā kātunti nayato labbhamānattā vuttaṃ. Itarathā mahāpadesā niratthakā siyuṃ. Evamaññatthāpi nayo netabbo. “Samuṭṭhānampi idha vuttameva aggahetvā chasamuṭṭhānavasena gahetabba”nti likhitaṃ. Taṃ “aññe nacca, gāya, vādehī”ti vattuṃ na labbhatītiādivacīkammaṃ sandhāya likhitañce, taṃ sulikhitaṃ eḷakalomasamuṭṭhāne vācāya abhāvato. “Sayampi naccitu”ntiādikāyakammañce sandhāya likhitaṃ, dullikhitaṃ. Eḷakalomasamuṭṭhānañhi ekantato kāyakammaṃ [M 0.0372] hoti, tasmā uddhaṭaṃ aggahetvā ādisaddena saṅgahitameva idha gahetabbanti. Etaṃ eḷakalomasamuṭṭhānattāti ettha kāraṇavacane suttānulomamahāpadesatoti ettha pana uddhaṭaṃ gahetabbaṃ, evaṃ yathālābhavasena taṃ likhitanti veditabbaṃ. “Āhaccabhāsitasikkhāpadavasena eḷakalomasamuṭṭhāna”nti vuttanti upatissatthero[V 0.0340]. “Eḷakalomasamuṭṭhānañce idaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ, āṇāpako mucceyya, na ca muccatī”ti vuttaṃ. Taṃ “kasmā”ti vutte “sabbaaṭṭhakathāsu vutta”nti aṭṭhakathācariyo āhāti dhammasiritthero.

836. What is 'single application' (ekapayoga)? It is observing for a single day. 'Of those very ones' (Tesaṃyeva) refers to those whose dancing one sees. The statement, 'A bhikkhunī herself is not allowed to dance, or sing, or play an instrument,' and so on, is not found in this training rule. Why? Because of its origin from goat's wool. If so, why was it said, you might ask? Due to the Great Reference concerning conformity with the Suttas. It was said based on the reasoning that if one is not allowed to watch or listen to dancing and so on, how much less so to do it oneself. Otherwise, the Great References would be meaningless. This method should be applied elsewhere as well. It is written: 'Regarding the origin also, not taking just what is stated here, it should be taken according to the six origins.' If that was written with reference to verbal action such as, 'It is not allowed to say to others, "Dance, sing, play an instrument!"', then it is well-written, because in the origin from goat's wool there is no speech. If it was written with reference to bodily action such as 'to dance oneself', it is poorly written. For the origin from goat's wool is exclusively bodily action. Therefore, not taking what is explicitly stated, only what is included by the word 'etc.' should be taken here. This is in the causal statement 'because of its origin from goat's wool'; but here, in 'due to the Great Reference concerning conformity with the Suttas', what is explicitly stated should be taken. Thus, it should be understood that this was written according to what was available. The Elder Upatissa says: 'It was said, "The origin is from goat's wool by way of a training rule spoken on a specific occasion."' It is said: 'If this training rule has its origin from goat's wool, the one who commands would be released, but he is not released.' The Elder Dhammasiri said: 'When asked, "Why was that said?", the commentary teacher replied, "Because it is said in all the commentaries."

837. Ārāme ṭhatvāti na kevalaṃ ṭhatvā, tato gantvā pana sabbiriyāpathehipi labhati. “Ārāme ṭhitāti pana ārāmapariyāpannāti attho, itarathā nisinnāpi na labheyyā”ti likhitaṃ, taṃ sulikhitameva.

837. As for 'standing in the monastery', it is not only by standing; but having gone from there, one is allowed in all postures. It is written: 'But "standing in the monastery" means "included within the monastery"; otherwise, one would not be allowed even while sitting.' And that is indeed well-written.

Dasamasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the tenth training rule is finished.

Lasuṇavaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Garlic Chapter is finished.

2. Andhakāravaggavaṇṇanā

2. The Explanation of the Chapter on Darkness

1. Paṭhamasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

1. The Explanation of the First Training Rule

839. “Divāpi andhakāraṃ atthi, tappaṭisedhanatthaṃ ‘rattandhakāre’ti vutta”nti vadanti porāṇā. Santiṭṭheyyāti ettha ṭhānāpadesena catubbidhopi iriyāpatho saṅgahito, tasmā purisassa hatthapāse tena saddhiṃ caṅkamanādiṃ karontiyā pācittiyameva. “Sallapeyya vā”ti kevalaṃ nidānavasena vuttaṃ visesābhāvato. “Sallapeyyavāti purisassa hatthapāse ṭhitā sallapati, āpatti pācittiyassā”ti hi vuttaṃ, taṃ na yuttanti eke. Kasmā? Yasmā tassa purisassa hatthapāse ṭhiteneva ekaṃ pācittiyaṃ. Sallapanenapi aparampi ekaṃ āpajjatīti nāpajjati, kathaṃ paññāyatīti? Aṅgavasena. Imassa hi rattandhakāratā, purisassa hatthapāse ṭhānaṃ vā sallapanaṃ vā, sahāyābhāvo, rahopekkhatāti imāni cattāri aṅgāni vuttāni. Tattha yadi ṭhānapaccayā ekā āpatti visuṃ siyā, tassā [M 0.0373] cattāri aṅgāni siyuṃ. Yadi sallapanapaccayā ekā, tassāpi pañca aṅgāni siyuṃ. Tasmā mātikāṭṭhakathāyaṃ “cattāri vā pañca vā aṅgānī”ti vattabbaṃ siyā, na ca vuttaṃ, tasmā sallapanapaccayā visuṃ natthīti. Atthiyeva, mātikāṭṭhakathāvacanañca tadatthamevāti eke. Kathaṃ? Sahuppattito dvinnaṃ āpattīnaṃ. Kiṃ [V 0.0341] vuttaṃ hoti? Sallapane sati ṭhānapaccayā āpajjitabbaṃ caturaṅgikaṃ, sallapanapaccayā āpajjitabbaṃ caturaṅgikanti dve pācittiyāni sahuppannāni ekato āpajjantīti. Idaṃ ayuttaṃ pāḷivirodhato. Pāḷiyañhi “sallapeyya vāti purisassa hatthapāse ṭhitā sallapati, āpatti pācittiyassā”ti vuttaṃ. Yadi dve siyuṃ, “āpatti dvinnaṃ pācittiyāna”nti na vattabbatā siyāti. Ayaṃ nayo dutiyādīsupi yathāyogaṃ veditabbo. Ettha dutiyenāpi saddhiṃ yadi bhikkhuniyā rahopekkhatā atthi, so ce puriso, na dutiyo, purisagaṇanāya āpattiyo. Atha dutiyā bhikkhunī hoti, tassā ca tena purisena saddhiṃ rahopekkhatā atthi, sā ca bhikkhunī na dutiyā hoti. Ubhinnampi āpajjatīti eke, vicāretvā pana gahetabbaṃ. Porāṇagaṇṭhipade pana vuttaṃ “hatthapāse ṭhānena dukkaṭa”nti, taṃ pāḷiyā virujjhati. “Purisassa hatthapāse tiṭṭhati, āpatti pācittiyassā”ti hi pāḷi, kiṃbahunā. Catutthasikkhāpade mātikāṭṭhakathāyaṃ (kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. dutiyikauyyojanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā) “santiṭṭhanādīsu tīṇi pācittiyānī”tiādivacanato vatthugaṇanāya āpatti veditabbā. “Aṅgāni cettha cattāri pañca vā”ti vattabbanti sanniṭṭhānaṃ.

839. The ancients say: 'There is darkness even during the day; to preclude that, 'in the darkness of night' was said.' Here, in the phrase 'should stand together,' by indicating the posture of standing, all four postures are included. Therefore, for a bhikkhunī who performs walking back and forth and so on with a man within his arm's reach, there is a pācittiya offense indeed. The phrase 'or should converse' is stated merely due to the origin story, because there is no distinction. For it is said: 'Or should converse means: standing within a man's arm's reach, she converses; there is an offense of pācittiya.' Some say this is not appropriate. Why? Because by merely standing within that man's arm's reach, one pācittiya is incurred, and by conversing as well, another one is incurred. [To this, some reply that a second offense] is not incurred. How is this known? By way of the factors. For of this training rule, these four factors have been stated: the darkness of night; standing or conversing within a man's arm's reach; the absence of a companion; and the desire for seclusion. Therein, if there were a separate offense on account of standing, it would have four factors. If there were one on account of conversing, it would have five factors. Therefore, in the Mātikāṭṭhakathā, it should have been said, 'four or five factors,' but it was not said. Therefore, there is no separate offense on account of conversing. Some say: 'It does exist, and the statement in the Mātikāṭṭhakathā has that very meaning.' How so? Due to the simultaneous arising of two offenses. What is meant by this? When there is conversation, the offense to be incurred on account of standing has four factors, and the offense to be incurred on account of conversing has four factors; thus two pācittiya offenses, having arisen simultaneously, are incurred together. This is inappropriate because it contradicts the Pāli. For in the Pāli it is said: 'Or should converse means: standing within a man's arm's reach, she converses; there is an offense of pācittiya.' If there were two offenses, it would have been necessary to say, 'an offense of two pācittiyas.' This method should be understood as is appropriate in the second training rule and so on. Here, if a bhikkhunī has a desire for seclusion with a man who is her companion, if he is a man, he is not a companion; the offenses are according to the number of men. Now, if there is a companion bhikkhunī, and she also has a desire for seclusion with that man, then that bhikkhunī is not a companion. Both incur an offense—so some say. This, however, should be accepted only after investigation. But in the ancient glosses it is said, 'By standing within arm's reach, there is a dukkaṭa offense,' which contradicts the Pāli. For the Pāli states: 'She stands within a man's arm's reach; there is an offense of pācittiya.' What more needs to be said? In the fourth training rule, in the Mātikāṭṭhakathā, from the statement beginning, 'In standing together, etc., there are three pācittiya offenses,' the offense should be understood by the count of the instances. The conclusion should be seen as: 'It should be said that the factors here are four or five.'

Paṭhamasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the first training rule is concluded.

2-3-4. Dutiyatatiyacatutthasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

2–3–4. Explanation of the Second, Third, and Fourth Training Rules

842-6. Dutiyatatiyacatutthāni uttānāni. Sabbattha “sallapatīti yaṃ kiñci tiracchānakathaṃ kathetī”ti porāṇagaṇṭhipade vuttaṃ.

842-6. The second, third, and fourth are clear. In all the training rules, it is stated in the ancient glosses that 'sallapati' means: 'one speaks any kind of worldly talk'.

852. Catutthe panāyaṃ viseso – “ekenekā”ti paṭhamaṃ vuttattā dutiyikaṃ vā bhikkhunīnaṃ uyyojeyya, pācittiyaṃ na sambhavatīti ce? Sambhavati. Kasmā? Santiṭṭhanādittayamattāpekkhattā, tassa vacanassāpi vā aññāyapi rahopekkhanassādasambhave sati ubhinnaṃ ekatthasambhavato ca sādhitametaṃ. “Hatthapāsaṃ [M 0.0374] vijahitvā santiṭṭhati vā sallapati vā”ti ettakameva vuttaṃ. Kasmā “nikaṇṇikaṃ vā jappetī”ti na vuttaṃ? Hatthapāsātikkame asambhavato. Tassa tatiyassa padassa pacchinnattā sambhavantampi “dutiyikaṃ vā uyyojetī”ti na vuttaṃ, tasmā atthato hatthapāsaṃ vijahitvā santiṭṭhati vā sallapati vā dutiyikaṃ vā uyyojeti, āpatti dukkaṭassāti vuttaṃ hoti. Esa nayo yakkhena vātiādīsupi. Tattha “hatthapāse”ti vā “hatthapāsaṃ vijahitvā”ti vā na vuttaṃ ubhayattha dukkaṭattā. Anāpattivārepi [V 0.0342] asambhavato “nikaṇṇikaṃ vā jappetī”ti na vuttanti ce? Sambhavati sati karaṇīye nikaṇṇikaṃ vā jappetīti sambhavato. Atha kasmā evaṃ na vuttanti ce? Anavajjakathāyaṃ nikaṇṇikajappane payojanābhāvā, dhammakathāyampi udāyiṃ ārabbha paṭisiddhattā ca.

852. In the fourth, however, there is this distinction: if one were to say that since 'one with one' was stated first, a pācittiya offense does not arise if one dismisses a second nun, (the reply is:) it does arise. Why? Because that word also depends only on the triad of actions beginning with 'standing'; or, because this statement is established from the fact that when there is the arising of delight in looking for privacy on the part of that nun or another, a single purpose is possible for both of them. Only 'stands or speaks having relinquished arm's reach' is stated. Why is 'or whispers in the ear' not stated? Because it is not possible when arm's reach is surpassed. Because that third phrase is separate, even though it is possible, 'or dismisses a second one' is not stated. Therefore, in meaning, it is said that if, having relinquished arm's reach, one stands, or speaks, or dismisses a second one, one incurs an offense of dukkaṭa. This is the same principle in the cases beginning with 'with a yakkha'. There, neither 'within arm's reach' nor 'having relinquished arm's reach' is stated, because in both cases it is a dukkaṭa offense. If one were to ask: 'Is it not stated in the section on no offense either, because it is not possible?' (The reply is:) It is possible. Because it is possible to 'whisper in the ear' when there is a reason to do so. Then if one were to ask: 'Why is it not stated thus?' (The reply is:) Because in blameless talk, there is no purpose in whispering in the ear, and because, even in a Dhamma talk, it was prohibited in connection with Udāyin.

Dutiyatatiyacatutthasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the second, third, and fourth training rules is concluded.

5. Pañcamasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

5. Explanation of the Fifth Training Rule

856. “Kulaṃ nāma cattāri kulānī”ti vuttattā titthiyārāme kappati tassa kulavohārābhāvatoti eke. Titthiyānaṃ khattiyādipariyāpannattā na kappatīti eke. Tassa kappiyabhūmittā na yuttanti ce? Na, yathāvuttakhattiyādīnaṃ sambhavato. Tathāpi gocarakulaṃ idhādhippetaṃ. “Upacāro dvādasahattho”ti likhitaṃ.

856. Some say that, as it is stated, “Household means the four kinds of households,” it is permissible in a sectarian monastery because there is no designation of ‘household’ for it. Others say it is not permissible because sectarians are included among the khattiyas, etc. If one were to argue that this is not appropriate because it is allowable ground, [the reply is:] no, because of the possibility of the aforementioned khattiyas, etc. Nevertheless, a household visited for alms is intended here. It is written: “The boundary is twelve hands’ breadth.”

Pañcamasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the fifth training rule is concluded.

6. Chaṭṭhasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

6. Commentary on the Sixth Training Rule

860. “Nisīdantiyā ekā, nipajjantiyā ekā”ti avatvā “nisīditvā gacchantiyā”tiādi na vattabbaṃ. Na hi gamanapaccayā esā āpattīti? Na, pariyosānādhippāyavasena vuttattā. “Nisīditvā nipajjantiyā dve”ti vacanenapi gamanaṃ idha nādhippetanti dassitaṃ hoti, tathā “nipajjitvā nisīdantiyā dve”tipi vattabbaṃ. Yadi evaṃ “tasmiṃ abhinipajjati, āpatti dvinnaṃ pācittiyāna”nti kasmā na vuttanti ce? Anisīditvāpi nipajjanasambhavato. Nipajjanatthāya [M 0.0375] nisīditvā nipajjantiyā nipajjanakapayogattā ekā āpattīti keci.

860. If one were to say that, instead of stating, 'For one who is sitting down, one offense; for one who is lying down, one offense,' one should not say, 'For one who, having sat down, is going,' and so on, because this offense does not arise from the act of going—the reply is: it is not that this should not be said; it should indeed be said. Why? Because it is stated with the intention of the final act. By the statement, 'For one who, having sat down, lies down, two offenses,' it is shown that going is not intended here. Similarly, it should also be said, 'For one who, having lain down, sits down, two offenses.' If one were to ask, 'If so, why is it not said, “She lies down on it; there is an offense of two pācittiyas”?'—the reply is: because it is possible to lie down even without having sat down. Some say that for a bhikkhunī who, having sat down for the purpose of lying down, then lies down, there is one offense because it is a preparatory act for lying down.

Chaṭṭhasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the sixth training rule is concluded.

7. Sattamasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

7. Commentary on the Seventh Training Rule

867. Anāpattivāre “dhuvapaññatte”ti na vuttaṃ “santharitvā vā santharāpetvā vā”ti vuttattā[V 0.0343]. Idha chaṭṭhe vuttanayena pakatiyā paññatte abhinisīdati vā abhinipajjati vā, pācittiyameva. Aññattha dhuvapaññattaṃ. Idha vuttanayena santharitvā vā santharāpetvā vā abhinisīdati vā abhinipajjati vā, pācittiyameva. Ubhayatthāpi pañcame vuttanayena anāpucchā pakkameyya, pācittiyameva, anāpattivāre mātikāyaṃ vuttakālato aññakālassa aparāmaṭṭhattāti no takkoti ācariyo. Apica atthāpattikāle āpajjati, no vikāletiādittike, atthāpatti rattiṃ āpajjati, no divātiādittike ca aṭṭhakathāyaṃ idha pañcamachaṭṭhasattamasikkhāpadehi saṅgahitāpattīnaṃ aparāmaṭṭhattā yathāsambhavaṃ tividhakāle tividhametaṃ yojetvā dassetuṃ vaṭṭati eva mahāpadesanayānulomato.

867. In the section on non-offenses, 'permanently spread' is not stated, because 'having spread it oneself or having had it spread' is stated. Here, according to the method stated in the sixth rule, if one sits down or lies down on what is naturally spread, it is a pācittiya offense. Elsewhere, it is 'permanently spread'. Here, according to the method stated, if one sits down or lies down after having spread it oneself or having had it spread, it is a pācittiya offense. In both cases, according to the method stated in the fifth rule, if one were to depart without asking, it is a pācittiya offense; our teacher reasons that this is because in the section on non-offenses, a time other than the time stated in the matrix is not considered. Furthermore, regarding such Tīkā passages as, 'An offense is incurred at the proper time, not at the wrong time,' and 'An offense is incurred at night, not during the day,' because the offenses included by the fifth, sixth, and seventh training rules are not considered here in the Aṭṭhakathā, it is indeed proper to apply and present this threefold offense at the three kinds of times, as is possible, in accordance with the method of the Great References.

Sattamasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the seventh training rule is concluded.

8. Aṭṭhamasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

8. Commentary on the Eighth Training Rule

869. Aṭṭhame bhikkhussa dukkaṭaṃ sambhavati.

869. In the eighth, a dukkaṭa offense arises for a monk.

Aṭṭhamasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the eighth training rule is concluded.

9. Navamasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

9. Commentary on the Ninth Training Rule

875-7. Duggāhavasena vā suggāhavasena vā yathāvuttanayena sapathakaraṇe āpattīti veditabbaṃ. Yasmā mātikāyaṃ “attānaṃ vā paraṃ vā”ti vuttaṃ, tasmā yā attānameva ārabbha sapathaṃ kareyya, tassā ekā[M 0.0376]. Paramevārabbha tassā ekā. Ubhopi ārabbha tassā dve āpattiyo sambhavanti. Tikacchedo panettha paramevārabbha sapathakaraṇaṃ sandhāya pavatto.

It should be known that there is an offense in making a curse by the method stated, whether by way of wrong grasping or by way of right grasping. Because it is stated in the matrix, 'oneself or another,' therefore, for whichever bhikkhunī should make a curse concerning only herself, for her there is one offense. Concerning only another, for her there is one. Concerning both, for her two offenses arise. Here, the threefold division is established with reference to making a curse concerning only another.

Navamasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the ninth training rule is concluded.

10. Dasamasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

10. Commentary on the Tenth Training Rule

882. Dasame [V 0.0344] anāpattivāro rodanasseva, na vadhassa, tasmā ñātibyasanādīhi phuṭṭhāpi attānaṃ vadhati eva, na rodati, dukkaṭameva.

882. In the tenth, the section on non-offenses is for weeping only, not for striking. Therefore, even a bhikkhunī afflicted by the loss of relatives and so forth, if she only strikes herself and does not weep, it is only a dukkaṭa.

Dasamasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the tenth training rule is concluded.

Andhakāravaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Andhakāra Vagga is concluded.

3. Naggavaggavaṇṇanā

3. Commentary on the Naggavagga

1-2. Paṭhamadutiyasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

1-2. The Commentary on the First and Second Training Rules

883. Naggavaggassa paṭhamadutiyāni uttānāni. Paṭhame ayaṃ viseso – bhikkhussa tathā nhāyantassa dukkaṭaṃ aññatra jantāgharaudakapaṭicchādīhi. Na ca vigarahi tattha bhagavā attanāva ananuññātattā udakasāṭikāyāti porāṇā. “Ekameva nivāsetvā, pārupitvā ca nahāyituṃ na vaṭṭatī”ti porāṇagaṇṭhipade vuttaṃ.

883. The first and second rules of the Naggavagga are clear. In the first, this is the distinction: for a bhikkhu bathing thus, there is an offense of wrong-doing, except in a steam-bath or with a water-covering. The Blessed One did not rebuke in that case because the bathing-cloth had not been permitted by himself, so say the ancients. 'It is not proper to bathe having worn only one garment or having draped only one garment,' so it is said in the ancient glosses.

Paṭhamadutiyasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the first and second training rules is concluded.

3. Tatiyasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

3. The Commentary on the Third Training Rule

894. Tatiye antocatūhapañcāhaṃ dhuraṃ nikkhipantiyāpi āpatti eva. Liṅgaparivatte dhuraṃ nikkhipantiyā dukkaṭaṃ tikadukkaṭattā. “Sambahulāhi bhikkhunīhi saddhinti ettha catassopi sambahulā”ti porāṇagaṇṭhipade vuttaṃ.

894. In the third rule, for a bhikkhunī who lays down the burden even within four or five days, there is an offense indeed. For a bhikkhunī who lays down the burden upon a change of sex, there is an offense of wrong-doing because it is a triple wrong-doing. 'In the phrase "with many bhikkhunīs", here even four are considered "many",' so it is said in the ancient glosses.

Tatiyasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the third training rule is concluded.

4. Catutthasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

4. The Commentary on the Fourth Training Rule

898. Catutthe [V 0.0345][M 0.0377] saṅghāṭicāranti ettha saṅghāṭiādivasena adhiṭṭhitānaṃyevāyaṃ vidhi, netarāsaṃ kira. Tattha ticīvare eva vippavāsapaccayā nissaggiyaṃ. Antocīvarakālepi pañcāhikaṃ saṅghāṭicāraṃ atikkāmentiyā āpattiyeva. “Vinā etehi cīvarehi upasampadaṃ kātuṃ na vaṭṭatī”ti porāṇagaṇṭhipade vuttaṃ.

898. In the fourth rule, regarding the phrase saṅghāṭicāra, this procedure applies only to robes that have been determined, such as the outer robe and so forth, it is said, not to others. In that case, it is an offense of forfeiture only for the three robes, due to the condition of being separated from them. Even during the robe-period, for a bhikkhunī who exceeds the five-day saṅghāṭicāra, there is an offense indeed. 'It is not proper to perform the higher ordination without these robes,' so it is said in the ancient glosses.

Catutthasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the fourth training rule is concluded.

5. Pañcamasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

5. The Commentary on the Fifth Training Rule

906. Pañcamassa anāpattivāre tāya vā avippavāsāyāti atthato labbhati.

906. In the non-offense section of the fifth rule, the meaning of 'or by not being separated from her' is obtained from the sense of the text.

Pañcamasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the fifth training rule is concluded.

907-911. Chaṭṭhasattamāni uttānāni.

907-911. The sixth and seventh rules are clear.

8. Aṭṭhamasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

8. The Commentary on the Eighth Training Rule

916. Sokajjhāyikā nāma kira māyākārā. Vilumpakā bhaṇḍakāti ca porāṇā.

916. The so-called Sokajjhāyikā, it is said, are magicians. The ancients also say they are plunderers and disputants.

Aṭṭhamasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the eighth training rule is concluded.

9. Navamasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

9. The Commentary on the Ninth Training Rule

920. “Kathañhi nāma atikkāmessatī”ti vuttattā thullanandā cīvarakālasamayaṃ āgamethāti atikkamāpesīti siddhaṃ hoti.

920. Because it was said, 'How indeed will she cause it to be exceeded?', the meaning is established that Thullanandā, having said, 'Wait for the robe-season!', caused it to be exceeded.

Navamasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the ninth training rule is concluded.

10. Dasamasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

10. The Commentary on the Tenth Training Rule

927. Dasame [M 0.0378][V 0.0346] ekakulaṃ etadavocunti ettha kulaṃ nāma tasmiṃ manussā, tasmā bahuvacanaṃ.

927. In the tenth training rule, regarding “one family said this”—here, “family” means the people in that household; therefore, the plural form is used.

Dasamasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the tenth training rule is concluded.

Naggavaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Naggavagga is concluded.

4. Tuvaṭṭavaggavaṇṇanā

4. Commentary on the Tuvaṭṭavagga

1. Paṭhamasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

1. Explanation of the First Training Rule

934-5. Ekāya nipannāya aparā nipajjati, āpatti pācittiyassāti “ubhinnampi paṭhamanipannāya anuṭṭhāpanā”ti vatvā ettha kiriyākiriyanti eke, taṃ aṭṭhakathāya virujjhati. “Kiriya”nti hi aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttaṃ. Atha kassā āpattīti? Ubhinnampi nipajjanakiriyaṃ paṭicca. Imassa anāpattivāre “vavatthānaṃ dassetvā”ti natthi, tasmā vavatthānaṃ katvā nipajjituṃ na vaṭṭatīti eke. Vipulatare vaṭṭatīti eke. “Antaraṃ katvā nipajjituṃ vaṭṭatī”ti porāṇagaṇṭhipade likhitaṃ.

934-5. Regarding "When one has lain down and another lies down, there is an offense of pācittiya," some, having stated, "For both, it is the failure of the one who lay down first to get up," say it is an action-and-non-action. This contradicts the commentary, for in the commentary it is said to be an "action." Then for whom is the offense? For both, on account of the act of lying down. In the non-offense clause for this, "having shown a delimitation" is not found; therefore, some say it is not permissible to lie down having made a delimitation. Others say it is permissible if the space is more ample. "It is permissible to lie down after making a separation"—so it is written in the ancient glosses.

Paṭhamasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the First Training Rule is concluded.

2. Dutiyasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

2. Explanation of the Second Training Rule

940. Vavatthānaṃ dassetvāti ettha upari pārupanampi majjhe obhogaṃ katvā ubhinnaṃ antare otāreti, vaṭṭatīti eke. Vavatthānañca yathā ṭhāne na tiṭṭhati, tathā atikkamitvā tuvaṭṭentiyā āpattiyevāti. “Kiriyākiriya”nti ca porāṇagaṇṭhipade vuttaṃ.

940. Regarding "having shown the delimitation": here, some say it is permissible to make a fold in the middle of the upper robe and lower it between the two. And if the delimitation does not remain in its proper place, there is indeed an offense for the one who rolls over, transgressing it. And "action-and-non-action" is stated in the ancient glosses.

Dutiyasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Second Training Rule is concluded.

3. Tatiyasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

3. Explanation of the Third Training Rule

941. Attano [M 0.0379][V 0.0347] sajjhāyanaṭṭhāne ce vuḍḍhatarā āgacchati, vandanakāle vā, āpucchanakiccaṃ natthi. Ekasmiṃ ovarake āpucchitabbaṃ. “Atha ovarake mahātherī vasati, sammukhe itarā, āpucchitabbā tassā upacārattā”ti porāṇagaṇṭhipade vuttaṃ.

941. If a more senior nun comes while one is in the place of recitation, or at the time of paying respects, there is no need to ask leave. One should ask leave when in the same room. "If the great elder nun resides in the inner room, the other in her presence should ask for leave, because it is her precinct"—so it is stated in the ancient glosses.

Tatiyasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Third Training Rule is concluded.

946-950. Catutthapañcamasikkhāpadaṃ uttānatthameva.

946–950. The fourth and fifth training rules are of clear meaning.

6. Chaṭṭhasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

6. Explanation of the Sixth Training Rule

956. Gahapati nāma ṭhapetvā sahadhammike veditabbo, tasmā bhikkhunā vā sāmaṇerena vā ananulomikena saṃsaggena saṃsaṭṭhāpi na samanubhāsitabbāti sambhavati eva.

956. "Householder" is to be understood as excluding those who share the Dhamma. Therefore, it is indeed possible that even a bhikkhunī who has associated with a bhikkhu or a sāmaṇera through an unsuitable association should not be formally admonished.

Chaṭṭhasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Sixth Training Rule is concluded.

961-5. Sattamaaṭṭhama sikkhāpadaṃ uttānatthameva.

961-5. The seventh and eighth training rules are of clear meaning indeed.

9. Navamasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

9. Explanation of the Ninth Training Rule

969. Ekindriyanti kāyindriyeneva ekindriyaṃ, nigaṇṭhānaṃ acelakānaṃ mataṃ. Kāpilā pana “pañcindriyā”ti maññantā evaṃ vadanti “sacakkhukattā alābumāluvādayo yattha ālambanaṃ, tattha gacchanti. Sasotakattā kadaliyo meghagajjitaṃ sutvā gabbhaṃ gaṇhanti. Saghānakattā panasādayo kuṇapagandhena phalanti. Sajivhakattā udakaṃ pivanti yena, sabbepi ‘pādapā’ti vuccanti. Sakāyapasādattā itthisamphassena asokarukkhā pupphantī”ti. Saṅghātanti vināsaṃ.

969. Regarding "one faculty": that there is only one faculty, the body faculty, is the view of the Nigaṇṭhas, the naked ascetics. The Kāpilas, however, thinking "there are five faculties," say thus: "Because of having the eye faculty, gourd creepers, māluvā creepers, and so on go where there is a support. Because of having the ear faculty, banana trees, having heard the sound of thunder, conceive. Because of having the nose faculty, jackfruit trees and so on bear fruit by the smell of corpses.
