The Elucidation of the Story of the Duties Towards the Preceptor

64. Buddhupajjhāyakānaṃ itaresaṃ ehibhikkhūnaṃ nivāsanapārupanakappato nesaṃ visuṃ visuṃ sadisattā “dunnivatthā duppārutā anākappasampannā”ti vuttā. Na kevalañca itthambhūtā piṇḍāya caranti, apica manussānaṃ bhuñjamānānaṃ uparītiādi. Manussā ujjhāyanti pipāsāsahanato, itaresaṃ ākappasampattiyā pasannattā ca.

64. Although the allowance for wearing the inner and outer robes is respectively the same for them as for the other ehi-bhikkhus whose preceptor is the Buddha, they are described as 'poorly dressed, poorly covered, lacking proper conduct'. And not only do they go for alms in such a state, but also [they do things such as stand] over people while they are eating, and so on. People complain because of [these monks'] inability to endure thirst and also because they are pleased with the proper conduct of the others.

65. Kena ko upajjhāyo gahetabboti? “Tadā so yassa santike pabbājito, etarahi yassa santike upasampadāpekkho hoti. Upajjhāyena [M 0.0417] ca sādhūti sampaṭicchanaṃ sandhāyā”ti kehici likhitaṃ. Taṃ te evaṃ jānanti “upajjhāyena ‘sāhū’tiādinā sampaṭicchite saddhivihārikassa ‘sādhu suṭṭhu sampaṭicchāmī’ti vacanaṃ kevalaṃ bhikkhūhi āciṇṇameva, na katthaci dissati, tasmā vināpi tena upajjhāyo gahitova hotī”ti. Tattha sāhūti sādhūti vuttaṃ hoti. Lahūti lahu, tvaṃ mama na bhāriyosīti vuttaṃ hoti. Opāyikanti upāyapaṭisaṃyuttaṃ, iminā upāyena tvaṃ me ito paṭṭhāya bhāro jātosīti attho. Patirūpanti anurūpaṃ te upajjhāyaggahaṇanti attho.

65. By whom should a preceptor be taken? Some have written: ‘He is the one in whose presence one was given the going forth at that time, and in whose presence one now expects the higher ordination; this is with reference to the preceptor’s acceptance with ‘sādhu’.’ They understand it thus: ‘When the preceptor accepts with ‘sāhu’ and so on, the co-resident’s response, ‘I accept well and properly,’ is merely a customary practice among monks, not found anywhere [in the texts]. Therefore, even without it, the preceptor is indeed taken.’ Therein, ‘sāhu’ means ‘sādhu’ (good) is what is said. ‘Lahu’ means ‘light’; ‘You are not a burden to me’ is what is said. ‘Opāyika’ means ‘connected with a means,’ the meaning of which is: ‘By this means, from now on, you have become a burden to me.’ ‘Patirūpa’ means ‘suitable,’ the meaning of which is: ‘Your taking of a preceptor is fitting.’

66. Tādisameva mukhadhovanodakaṃ utumhi ekasabhāgeti. Ito paṭṭhāyāti “na upajjhāyassa bhaṇamānassā”ti ettha vuttana-kārato paṭṭhāya. Tena “nātidūre gantabbaṃ, nāccāsanne gantabba”nti ettha vuttana-kārena anāpattīti dīpetīti eke. Sacittakā ayaṃ āpatti, udāhu acittakāti? Anādariyapaccayattā sacittakā. Anādariyapaccayatā kathaṃ paññāyatīti [V 0.0382] ce? Anādariyapaccayehi saṅgahitanti. Pātimokkhuddese sekhiyānaṃ gaṇaparicchedākaraṇañhi khandhakapariyāpannāpattiyā saṅgaṇhanatthaṃ. Idaṃ pana lakkhaṇaṃ cāritteyeva veditabbaṃ, na vāritte akappiyamaṃsakhādanādiāpattīnaṃ acittakattā. Khandhakavārittānaṃ tehi saṅgaho, sekhiyavāritteyeva acittakehi sūpodanaviññattipaccayādīhīti ācariyo. Yattha yattha na-kārena paṭisedho karīyati, kiṃ sabbattha dukkaṭāpattīti? Āma. Yattha aṭṭhakathāya nayo na dassito, tattha sabbattha. Parato hi aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “sace pana kāḷavaṇṇakatā vā sudhābaddhā vā hoti nirajamattikā, tathārūpāya bhūmiyā ṭhapetuṃ vaṭṭatī”tiādinā nayena nayo dassito.

66. Similarly, the water for washing the face is of a shared nature in the proper season. ‘From this point onward’ means starting from the negative particle ‘na’ mentioned in ‘not while the preceptor is speaking.’ Therefore, some say that the negative particle ‘na’ used in ‘one should not go too far, one should not go too near’ indicates that there is no offense. Is this offense intentional, or is it unintentional? Because it is conditioned by disrespect, it is intentional. If it is asked, ‘How is it known to be conditioned by disrespect?’ It is known to be included with offenses conditioned by disrespect. Indeed, the non-specification of the number of the Sekhiya rules in the recitation of the Pātimokkha is for the purpose of including offenses that fall under the Khandhakas. However, this characteristic should be understood only in the case of cāritta (rules of conduct), not in the case of vāritta (rules of avoidance), because offenses such as eating unallowable meat are unintentional. The vāritta rules of the Khandhakas are included with those, whereas the vāritta rules of the Sekhiya are included with unintentional offenses conditioned by such things as requesting curry and rice, says the teacher. Wherever a prohibition is made with the negative particle ‘na,’ is it in every case a dukkaṭa offense? Yes. In every case where a method is not shown in the commentary. Indeed, later in the commentary, the method is shown by the guideline beginning: ‘But if the ground is blackened or plastered with white clay and is free from dust, then it is permissible to place something on such ground,’ and so on.

Etthāha – yasmā pāḷiyaṃyeva “sace upajjhāyassa anabhirati uppannā hoti, diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ hotī”ti (mahāva. 66) bhagavato vacanavasena aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttanayo yuttoti dassetuṃ “nātidūre nāccāsanne”ti ettha ko bhagavato vacanalesoti? Vuccate – “paṭhamataraṃ āgantvā āsanaṃ paññāpetabba”ntiādīni vadanti desaniyamanato. Upajjhāyena anumataṃyeva paṭhamagamananti ce? Na, asiddhattā, siddhepi yathāvuttanayasiddhito ca[M 0.0418]. Na hi vārittassa anumati anāpattikarā hoti, evaṃ santepi vicāretvā gahetabbaṃ. Koṭṭhakanti dvārakoṭṭhakaṃ. Na nissajjitabbaṃ, na nidahitabbaṃ vā.

Here it is said: Since the method stated in the commentary is fitting by means of the Blessed One's word in the Pāḷi itself—‘If for the preceptor dissatisfaction has arisen, or a wrong view has arisen’—in order to show this, what is the hint of the Blessed One’s word in ‘not too far, not too near’? It is said: They speak of ‘having arrived earlier, a seat should be prepared,’ and so on, due to the regulation of place. If it is said, ‘Going first is only with the preceptor’s permission,’ the reply is no, because it is not established, and even if it is established, it is also because of its being established according to the method stated. For permission for what is forbidden does not make one free from offense; even so, it should be taken up after consideration. ‘Koṭṭhaka’ means a gateway. It should not be given up, nor should it be laid aside.

Upajjhāyavattakathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Elucidation of the Discourse on the Duties Towards the Preceptor is concluded.

Nasammāvattanādikathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourse on Improper Conduct and So Forth

68. Adhimattaṃ gehassitapemaṃ na hotīti ettha gehassitapemaṃ na akusalamicceva daṭṭhabbaṃ khīṇāsavānampi sādhāraṇattā imassa lakkhaṇassa. Na khīṇāsavānaṃ asammāvattanābhāvatoti ce? Na, tesaṃ na paṇāmetabbaṃ taṃsamannāgamanasiddhito, tasmā “mamesa bhāro”ti mamattakaraṇaṃ tattha pemanti veditabbaṃ. “Eko vattasampanno…pe… tesaṃ anāpattī’ti ettha viya sace eko vattasampanno bhikkhu ‘bhante, tumhe appossukkā hotha, ahaṃ tumhākaṃ saddhivihārikaṃ, antevāsikaṃ vā gilānaṃ vā upaṭṭhahissāmi, ovaditabbaṃ ovadissāmi, iti karaṇīyesu ussukkaṃ āpajjissāmī’ti vadati, te evāsaddhivihārikādayo ‘bhante, tumheva kevalaṃ appossukkā hothā’ti vadanti, vattaṃ vā na sādiyanti, tato paṭṭhāya ācariyupajjhāyānaṃ anāpattī”ti vuttaṃ.

68. Here, in 'there is no excessive household-based affection,' household-based affection should be understood as not unwholesome, because this characteristic is common even to those whose taints are destroyed. If it is said: Is it not that because those whose taints are destroyed have no improper conduct, it is not common to them? No. For them, it is not to be dispelled, because they are established in the possession of that state of being a preceptor. Therefore, in this context, 'affection' should be understood as the act of making something one's own, as in 'This is my burden.' As in the passage: 'One who is accomplished in the duties… etc. … for them there is no offense.' It is said: 'If a monk accomplished in the duties says, “Venerable sirs, be untroubled. I will attend to your co-resident, or pupil, or the sick one; I will advise what should be advised; thus I will undertake diligence in what is to be done,” and those very co-residents and others say, “Venerable sirs, you yourselves should simply be untroubled,” or they do not consent to the duty, from then on, for the teachers and preceptors, there is no offense.'

Nasammāvattanādikathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Discourse on Improper Conduct and So Forth is Concluded.

Rādhabrāhmaṇavatthukathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Story of Rādha the Brahmin

73. “Pūtimuttanti [V 0.0383] muttaṃ pūtikāyo viyā”ti vatvāpi “pūtibhāvena muttaṃ paṭinissaṭṭhaṃ bhesajjaṃ pūtimuttabhesajja”nti likhitaṃ. Sabbattha itthannāmoti ekova na-kāro hoti.

73. Although it is said, 'In the term `pūtimutta`, `mutta` means urine, which is like a putrid body,' it is also written, '`Pūtimuttabhesajja` is medicine (`bhesajjaṃ`) that is abandoned (`muttaṃ`) and discarded (`paṭinissaṭṭhaṃ`) due to its putrid state (`pūtibhāvena`).' Everywhere, in the word `itthannāmo`, there is only one letter 'na'.

Rādhabrāhmaṇavatthukathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Story of Rādha the Brahmin is concluded.

Ācariyavattakathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourse on the Teacher’s Duties

76. “Āyasmato [M 0.0419] nissāya vacchāmī”ti vuttaṃ. “Āyasmato ovādaṃ nissāya vasāmī”ti pāṭhasesavasena veditabbā. Nissāyāti vā nissayā, nissayenāti vuttaṃ hoti. Āyasmatoti vā upayogatthe sāmivacanaṃ.

76. It is said, 'I will live depending on the venerable one.' This should be understood according to the remainder of the text as, 'I live depending on the advice of the venerable one.' Or, `nissāya` is said to mean `nissayena` (by dependence). Or, `āyasmato` is a genitive case used in the sense of the accusative.

Ācariyavattakathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Discourse on the Teacher’s Duties is concluded.

Nissayapaṭippassaddhikathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourse on Relief from Dependence

83. Disaṃ gatoti tattha dhuranikkhittavāso hutvā tirogāmaṃ gato. Yattha nissayo labbhati, tattha gantabbanti etthāpi upajjhāye vuttanayeneva “katipāhena gamissāmī”ti gamane cesa ussāho rakkhati. Mā idha paṭikkamīti mā idha gaccha. Sabhāgā nāma upajjhāyassa sissā. Tattha nissayaṃ gahetvā. Yadi evaṃ ko visesoti ce? Tena idaṃ vuccati “appeva nāma khameyyā”ti. Vasituṃ vaṭṭatīti upajjhāyena pariccattattā upajjhāyasamodhānaṃ niratthakanti attho. Sace upajjhāyo cirena anuggahetukāmo hoti, tato paṭṭhāya upajjhāyova nissayo. Upajjhāyo ce alajjī hoti, saddhivihārikena anekakkhattuṃ vāretvā aviramantaṃ upajjhāyaṃ pahāya vināpi nissayapaṇāmanena aññassa santike nissayaṃ gahetvā vasitabbaṃ. Upajjhāyassa ce liṅgaṃ parivattati, ekadivasampi na rakkhati. Pakkhapaṇḍako ce hoti, nissayajātiko ce “upajjhāyassa sukkapakkhaṃ āgamehī”ti vadati, sayameva vā āgameti, vaṭṭati. Upajjhāyo ce ukkhepaniyakammakato hoti, nānāsaṃvāsakabhūmiyaṃ ṭhitattā nissayo paṭippassambhati. Sammāvattantaṃ pana passitvā kammapaṭippassaddhiṃ āgametuṃ labhati. Mānattācārī ce hoti, abbhānaṃ āgametabbaṃ. Dīghaṃ ce parivāsaṃ carati, aññassa santike nissayo [V 0.0384] gahetabbo, upajjhāyasamodhānaṃ appamāṇaṃ. Parivāsamānattacārinā hi na nissayo dātabbo. Yaṃ pana pārivāsikakkhandhakaṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttaṃ “saddhivihārikānampi sādiyantassa dukkaṭamevā”tiādi (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 75), taṃ yathāvuttamatthaṃ sādheti eva. Yaṃ [M 0.0420] pana vuttaṃ “sace saddhāpabbajitā kulaputtā ‘tumhe, bhante, vinayakammamattaṃ karothā”ti vatvā vattaṃ karontiyeva, gāmappavesanaṃ āpucchantiyeva, taṃ vāritakālato paṭṭhāya anāpattī”ti. Taṃ vattasādiyanapaccayā dukkaṭābhāvamattadīpanatthaṃ, saddhivihārikānaṃ sāpekkhataṃ vā sandhāya vuttanti veditabbaṃ. Tasmā te ce upajjhāyena vāritānurūpameva paṭipajjanti, nissayo tesaṃ paṭippassaddhoti siddhaṃ hoti.

83. “He has gone to another region” means: having laid down the burden of his residence there, he has gone to another village. Regarding “Wherever dependence is obtained, one should go there,” in this case also, by the method stated concerning the preceptor, if there is zeal for going, declaring, “I will go in a few days,” it protects the dependence. “Do not return here” means do not come here. “Those of the same kind” are the preceptor’s disciples. Having taken dependence there. If one asks, “If so, what is the difference?” For that reason, this is said: “Perhaps he might forbear.” “It is allowable to stay” means that because he has been abandoned by the preceptor, reconciliation with the preceptor is meaningless. If the preceptor, after a long time, wishes to show favor, from that point on the preceptor himself is the dependence. If the preceptor is shameless, the co-resident, having repeatedly admonished him, should abandon the preceptor who does not desist and, even without a formal dismissal of dependence, should take dependence from another and stay. If the preceptor’s gender changes, the dependence is not protected even for a single day. If he is a fortnightly eunuch, and if he is of a nature to give dependence and says, “Wait for the preceptor's bright fortnight,” or if he himself waits, it is allowable. If the preceptor has been subjected to an act of suspension, because he stands on a ground of non-communion, the dependence is allayed. However, upon seeing him behaving correctly, one is permitted to wait for the revocation of the act. If he is undergoing the mānatta penance, one should wait for his rehabilitation. If he is undergoing a long probation, dependence should be taken from another; reconciliation with the preceptor is not to be awaited. For dependence should not be given by one undergoing probation and the mānatta penance. However, what is stated in the commentary on the Pārivāsikakkhandhaka, “For one who consents even to the duties of co-residents, there is only a dukkaṭa offense,” etc., that indeed establishes the meaning as stated. And what is said: “If clansmen gone forth through faith say, ‘Venerable Sir, you just perform the Vinaya act,’ and they continue to perform their duties and ask permission before entering the village—from the time they are prevented, there is no offense.” This should be understood as being stated for the purpose of showing merely the absence of a dukkaṭa offense on account of consenting to the duties, or as stated in reference to the co-residents’ consideration. Therefore, if they, having been forbidden by the preceptor, conduct themselves accordingly, it is established that their dependence is allayed.

Dve leḍḍupāte atikkamitvā nivattatīti “ettāvatā disāpakkanto nāma hoti, tasmā antevāsike anikkhittadhurepi nissayo paṭippassambhati. Ācariyupajjhāyā dve leḍḍupāte anatikkamma leḍḍupātadvayabbhantare tirovihārepi parikkhitte, aparikkhitte vā vasituṃ vaṭṭatī”ti likhitaṃ. Aparikkhitteyevāti no takkoti ācariyo, ettha pana aparikkhittassa parikkhepārahaṭṭhānato vimutte aññasmiṃ vihāre vasantīti adhippāyo. Vihāroti cettha “tādisassa vihārassa ante ṭhitā ekā kuṭikā adhippetāti upatissatthero”ti vuttaṃ. Tattha “sace ubhopi ācariyantevāsikā kenaci…pe… nissayo na paṭippassambhatī”ti iminā sāmaññato vuttena aṭṭhakathāvacanena dhammasirittheravādo sameti. Aparikkhitte vāti dvinnaṃ leḍḍupātānaṃ anto parikkhitto vā hoti aparikkhitto vā. “Bahisīma”nti ca vuttattā antovihārasīmāyaṃ dve leḍḍupāte atikkamitvāpi vasituṃ vaṭṭatīti siddhattā pana upatissattheravādo na sameti. Ekāvāse hi parikkhitte vā aparikkhitte vā antamaso antotiyojanepi vasato nissayo na paṭippassambhati. So ca upacārasīmāya paricchinno, sā ca upacārasīmā parikkhittassa vihārassa parikkhepena aparikkhittassa parikkhepārahaṭṭhānena paricchinno ekāvāso.

Regarding 'having passed beyond two clod-throws and turned back': by this much, one is called 'departed to another region.' Therefore, even if a pupil has not laid down the burden, the dependence ceases. It is written: 'It is permissible for the teacher or preceptor, not having gone beyond two clod-throws, to dwell within the space of two clod-throws, in another monastery, whether enclosed or unenclosed.' The teacher says it is not the case that it is 'only in an unenclosed one'; here, however, the intention is that they dwell in another monastery that is free from a place suitable for an enclosure of an unenclosed one. And here, regarding 'monastery,' it is said: 'The Elder Upatissa said that a single hut situated at the edge of such a monastery is intended.' Therein, the view of the Elder Dhammasiri accords with this statement from the commentary, spoken in general terms: 'If both teacher and pupil, by any means… the dependence does not cease.' 'Or in an unenclosed one' means that the space within the two clod-throws may be either enclosed or unenclosed. And because it is said 'outside the boundary,' and since it is established that it is permissible to dwell even having passed beyond two clod-throws within the monastery boundary, the view of the Elder Upatissa does not accord. Indeed, in a single residence, whether enclosed or unenclosed, for one dwelling even within three yojanas at the least, the dependence does not cease. And that single residence is defined by the proximity boundary; and that proximity boundary is the single residence defined by the enclosure of an enclosed monastery or by the place suitable for an enclosure of an unenclosed one.

Uposathakkhandhake ekāvāsavimatiyaṃ sīmāya anuññātattāti ce? Na, cīvarakkhandhakaṭṭhakathāya vicāritattā. Yathāha “sīmaṭṭhakasaṅgho bhājetvā gaṇhātū”ti (mahāva. aṭṭha. 379). Katarasīmāya bhājetabbaṃ? Mahāsivatthero kirāha “avippavāsasīmāyā”ti. Tato naṃ āhaṃsu “avippavāsasīmā nāma tiyojanāpi hoti, evaṃ sante tiyojane ṭhitā lābhaṃ gaṇhissanti, tiyojane ṭhatvā āgantukavattaṃ pūretvā ārāmaṃ pavisitabbaṃ bhavissati, gamiko [M 0.0421] tiyojanaṃ gantvā senāsanaṃ āpucchissati, nissayapaṭippannassa tiyojanātikkame nissayo [V 0.0385] paṭippassambhissati, pārivāsikena tiyojanaṃ atikkamitvā aruṇaṃ uṭṭhāpetabbaṃ bhavissati, bhikkhuniyā tiyojane ṭhatvā ārāmappavesanā āpucchitabbā bhavissati, sabbametaṃ upacārasīmāparicchedavasena kātuṃ vaṭṭatīti. Tasmā antoupacārasīmāya leḍḍupātadvayaṃ atikkamitvāpi vasato nissayo tiyojanātikkame nissayo na paṭippassambhatīti siddhaṃ. Kāmañcettha upacārasīmāya tiyojanappamāṇāya, atirekāya vā yathāvuttadosappasaṅgo siyāti. Sā hi āvāsesu vaḍḍhantesu vaḍḍhati, parihāyantesu parihāyatīti vuttattā, tasmā tādisassa vihārassa ante ṭhitā ekā kuṭi vihāroti idhādhippetā. Sāpi tasseva vihārassa kuṭikāva hotīti katvā so āvāso hoti. Nānāvāso eva ce adhippeto, “ante ṭhitā kuṭikā”ti na vattabbaṃ. Dvinnaṃ leḍḍupātānaṃ abbhantare pana aparikkhitte nānāvāse nissayo na paṭippassambhatīti yvāyaṃ “no takko”ti vutto, so tādise nānāvāse senāsanaggāhassa appaṭippassaddhinayena vutto. Senāsanaggāho hi “gahaṇena gahaṇaṃ ālayo paṭippassambhatī”ti lakkhaṇattā itarattha paṭippassambhati. Tatrāyaṃ pāḷi “tena kho pana samayena āyasmā upanando sakyaputto eko dvīsu āvāsesu vassaṃ vasi…pe… detha, bhikkhave, moghapurisassa ekādhippāya”nti (mahāva. 364). Aṭṭhakathāyañcassa evaṃ vuttaṃ “idañca nānālābhehi nānūpacārehi ekasīmavihārehi kathitaṃ, nānāsīmavihāre pana senāsanaggāho paṭippassambhatī”ti (mahāva. aṭṭha. 364). Aparikkhittā nānāvāsā ekūpacārasaṅkhyaṃ gacchanti. Parikkhittañca ekūpacāraṃ aparikkhittasaṅkhyaṃ gacchati. Ettāvatā leḍḍupātadvayabbhantare aparikkhitte aññasmiṃ vihāre vasato nissayo pana na paṭippassambhati, parikkhitte paṭippassambhati evāti ayamattho sādhitoti. Etthāha – dve leḍḍupāte atikkamitvāva satopi nissayo na paṭippassambhati. Vuttañhi nissaggiyaṭṭhakathāyaṃ “sace gacchantānaṃyeva asampattesu daharesu aruṇaṃ uggacchati, cīvaraṃ nissaggiyaṃ hoti, nissayo pana na paṭippassambhatī”ti (pārā. aṭṭha. 2.495)? Vuccate – taṃ upajjhāyena samāgame saussāhatāya vuttaṃ. Idha dhuvavāsaṃ sandhāya, tasmā aññamaññaṃ na vilomenti[M 0.0422]. Keci pana “dve leḍḍupātaṃ atikkammāti idaṃ devasikaṃ ārocetvā vasanavasena vutta”nti vadanti, taṃ tesaṃ matimattamevāti mama takko. Devasikaṃ ārocetvā vatthabbanti hi neva pāḷiyaṃ na aṭṭhakathāyaṃ dissati, tañca pana apakataññūhi āciṇṇanti veditabbaṃ.

If it is said that this is because in the Uposathakkhandhaka, in the section on doubt regarding a single residence, a boundary was permitted, this should not be said, for it has been examined in the Commentary to the Cīvarakkhandhaka. As it is said: “The Sangha within the boundary should divide and take it.” By which boundary should it be divided? The Elder Mahāsiva, it is said, stated, “By the non-separation boundary.” Then they said to him, “The non-separation boundary can even be three yojanas. If that is so, those standing within three yojanas would receive the gain. One would have to fulfill the duties of a guest monk after standing within three yojanas before entering the monastery. A traveler would have to ask for lodging after walking three yojanas. For one undertaking dependence, dependence would cease if he crosses beyond three yojanas. A probationary monk would have to pass beyond three yojanas before dawn breaks. A nun would have to ask for permission to enter the monastery while standing within three yojanas. All this can be done by defining the proximity boundary.” Therefore, it is established that even for one living beyond two clod-throws within the proximity boundary, dependence does not cease when crossing three yojanas. And yet, if the proximity boundary here is three yojanas or more, the aforementioned faults might arise. For it is said that it expands when residences grow and shrinks when they decline. Therefore, a single hut situated at the edge of such a monastery is here intended as a monastery. And since that is a hut of that very monastery, it becomes that residence. If different residences are intended, one should not say “a hut at the edge.” However, within two clod-throws in unenclosed separate residences, dependence does not cease. This, which is called “our reasoning,” is stated in reference to the non-cessation of the acceptance of lodging in such separate residences. For the acceptance of lodging, being characterized by “dependence ceases when one takes up another lodging,” ceases in other cases. Here is the Pāli: “At that time, the Venerable Upananda the Sakyan spent the rains alone in two residences… Give, monks, to this worthless man a single intention.” And in its commentary it is said thus: “This was spoken regarding single-boundary monasteries with different gains and different proximities. But in separate-boundary monasteries, the acceptance of lodging ceases.” Unenclosed separate residences are reckoned as a single proximity. And an enclosed single proximity is reckoned as unenclosed. By this much, it is established that within two clod-throws, dependence does not cease for one living in another unenclosed monastery, but it does cease in an enclosed one. Here someone says: “Even for one who is beyond two clod-throws, dependence does not cease.” For it is stated in the Nissaggiya-aṭṭhakathā: “If dawn breaks while they are still walking and have not reached the young monks, the robe becomes forfeit, but dependence does not cease.” It is replied: That was said with respect to the diligence in meeting with the preceptor. Here, it refers to permanent residence; therefore, they do not contradict each other. Some, however, say, “Going beyond two clod-throws is stated with respect to residing after announcing daily.” That is merely their opinion, according to my reasoning. For dwelling after announcing daily is seen neither in the Pāli nor in the commentaries, and it should be understood as practiced by those who are unskilled in the Vinaya.

Nissayapaṭippassaddhikathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the discussion on the cessation of dependence is concluded.

Upasampādetabbapañcakakathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discussion on the Pentad of those to be given Higher Ordination

84. Na [V 0.0386] asekkhena sīlakkhandhenātiādi “attānameva paṭhamaṃ, patirūpe nivesaye”ti (dha. pa. 158) vacanavasena vuttaṃ, na āpattiaṅgavasena. Nīlasamāyogato nīlaṃ viya vuttaṃ “asekkhena vimuttiñāṇadassanakkhandhenā”ti. Adhisīle sīlavipanno nāma āpajjitvā avuṭṭhito.

84. “Not by the aggregate of virtue of one beyond training,” and so on—this is stated according to the saying, “First, one should establish oneself in what is proper” (Dhp. 158), not by way of a factor of an offense. Just as something is called blue from its association with blue, so it is said, “by the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation of one beyond training.” One who is corrupt in higher virtue is one who, having fallen into an offense, has not arisen from it.

Upasampādetabbapañcakakathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Discussion on the Pentad of those to be given Higher Ordination is concluded.

Aññatitthiyapubbavatthukathāvaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Discussion of the Story of Former Adherents of Other Sects

86. Yo so aññatitthiyapubboti ettha dve atthavikappā – tassa pasūrassa bhikkhubhāvaṃ sandhāya aññatitthiyapubbo, so bhikkhu taṃyeva titthāyatanaṃ saṅkamīti ayameko attho. Evaṃ titthiyapakkantako puna gihivesena āgato aññatitthiyapubbo, so āgato na upasampādetabboti ayameko attho. Taṃ aññatitthiyapakkantakaṃ ṭhapetvā “yo so, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyapubbo”ti ettha na gihivesadhāraṇova pubbasaddena vutto, kintu tasmiṃ attano yathāsamādinnatitthiyavese ṭhitopi. Diṭṭhivasena atitthiyabhūtattā atitthiyapubbo, so panāgato vibbhanto āgacchati, tassa parivāsadānakiccaṃ natthi. Kiṃ imassa aññatitthiyapubbassa bhikkhuvesaṃ gahetvā saraṇagamanena sāmaṇerapabbajjā jātā, na jātāti? Kiñcettha yadi jātā, “yo so, bhikkhave, aññopi aññatitthiyapubbo imasmiṃ dhammavinaye ākaṅkhati pabbajjaṃ, ākaṅkhati upasampadaṃ, tassa cattāro māse parivāso dātabbo”ti (mahāva. 86) vacanaṃ virujjhati. Atha [M 0.0423] na jātā, parivāsakammavācāya pabbajjāya aparāmasanaṃ virujjhatīti. Tattha mahāvihāravāsino “sāmaṇerasseva sato parivāso dātabbo”ti vadanti. Itare tathā na vadanti. Te hi “evaṃ ārādhako kho bhikkhave aññatitthiyapubbo āgato upasampādetabbo’ti (mahāva. 87) suttapadaṃ pariharitabbaṃ, pure ca pacchā ca ‘aññatitthiyapubbo’ti vacanasāmaññato na sāmaṇero jātoti ce, yadi evaṃ apabbājetvāva upasampādetabboti āpajjati. Tato ca sabbapaṭhamaṃ vuttasuttaṃ virujjhati. ‘Titthāyatanaṃ saṅkanto’ti pāṭhopi na sundaraṃ. Pāṇātipātādīsu aññataraṃ sace bhindati, cattāro māse paripuṇṇepi puna paripūretabbaṃ viya dissati. Vuttampi tassa saṃvaraṃ bhikkhukaraṇatthāya anuññātattā [V 0.0387] sīle vattabbaṃ natthī”ti vadanti, vicāretvā gahetabbaṃ. Saraṇāni sace bhijjanti sāmaṇerasseva.

86. Herein, regarding 'one who was formerly of another sect,' there are two interpretations of the meaning. With reference to the state of being a monk of that Pasūra, he was formerly of another sect; that monk went over to that very sectarian ground. This is one meaning. Thus, a monk who has gone over to the sectarian fold, having returned again in the guise of a layman, is one who was formerly of another sect. Having come, he is not to be given the higher ordination. This is another meaning. Setting aside that one who has gone over to another sect, herein, in the phrase 'O monks, one who was formerly of another sect,' by the word 'formerly' it is not said of only one who wears the guise of a layman, but rather, it is also said of one who abides in the sectarian guise that he has undertaken for himself. By way of view, because he was not truly a sectarian, he is 'formerly a non-sectarian'. But when that one comes, he comes having disrobed; for him, there is no duty of giving probation. For this one who was formerly of another sect, by taking the guise of a monk and by going for refuge, has the novice ordination arisen or not? And here, if it has arisen, the statement, 'O monks, if any other who was formerly of another sect desires the going forth, desires the higher ordination in this Dhamma and Discipline, he should be given probation for four months,' is contradicted. Or if it has not arisen, the non-mention of the going forth in the formal act of probation is contradicted. In this matter, the residents of the Mahāvihāra say, 'Probation should be given only to one who is already a novice.' The others do not say so. For they say, 'The sutta passage, "O monks, an aññatitthiyapubba who has come and is satisfactory should be given the higher ordination," should be set aside. If you say that because of the generality of the expression "aññatitthiyapubba" both before and after, he has not become a novice, then it follows that he should be given the higher ordination without having been given the going forth. And because of that, the sutta spoken at the very beginning is contradicted.' Also, the reading 'has gone over to the sectarian ground' is not good. If he breaks any of the precepts such as killing living beings, it seems as if, even when the four months are complete, it must be fulfilled again. They also say, 'Because his restraint was permitted for the purpose of making him a monk, there is nothing to be said regarding virtue.' This should be understood after investigation. If the refuges are broken, it is only in the case of a novice.

Aññatitthiyapubbavatthukathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Story of the Former Sectarian is concluded.

Pañcābādhavatthukathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Story of the Five Sicknesses

88. Nakhapiṭṭhīti cūḷaṅgulinakhapiṭṭhi adhippetā. “Paṭicchanne nakhapiṭṭhito mahantampi vaṭṭati, evaṃ sesesupī”ti keci vadanti, taṃ aṭṭhakathāya na sameti viya. Padumakaṇṇikāpi āruḷhe rattapadumavaṇṇacitraṃ.

88. Regarding 'nakhapiṭṭhi', the back of the little finger's nail is intended. Some say, 'In a concealed place, even a large mark is allowable on the back of the nail; it is thus in the remaining cases as well.' That seems not to agree with the commentary. 'Padumakaṇṇikā' is a variegated sore that has arisen, having the color of a red lotus.

Pañcābādhavatthukathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Story of the Five Sicknesses is concluded.

Coravatthukathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Story of the Thief

91-2. Dhammasāmīti yasmā sayaṃ dhammasāmī, tasmā bhikkhūhi apabbājetabbakampi coraṃ aṅgulimālaṃ pabbājetvā āyatiṃ evamāhāti attho. Pāḷipotthakesu “kharabhedako”tipi likhitaṃ. Sannisinnāsūti vūpasantāsu.

Regarding 'Dhammasāmī': Because He Himself is the Lord of the Dhamma, therefore, having ordained Aṅgulimāla, a thief who was one not to be ordained by monks, He spoke thus regarding the future—this is the meaning. In the Pāḷi books, it is also written as 'kharabhedako'. 'Sannisinnāsu' means 'when they had subsided' or 'when they were calmed'.

Coravatthukathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Story of the Thief is concluded.

Iṇāyikadāsavatthukathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Story of the Debtor-Slave

96. Passa [M 0.0424] me pattacīvaramattaṃ, ahaṃ idaṃ dassāmīti sāmīci, yato natthi āpatti. Upaḍḍhupaḍḍhanti thokaṃ thokaṃ.

96. ‘See my mere bowl and robes; I will give this.’ This is proper, because there is no offense. 'Upaḍḍhupaḍḍhaṃ' means 'a little at a time, a little at a time'.

97. Desacārittanti sāvanapaṇṇāropanādi taṃ taṃ desacārittaṃ. “Devadāsiputte vaṭṭatī”ti likhitaṃ. “Ārāmikaṃ ce pabbājetukāmo, aññamekaṃ datvā pabbājetabba”nti vuttaṃ. Mahāpaccarivādassa ayamidha adhippāyo. “Bhikkhusaṅghassa ārāmike demā”ti dinnattā na te tesaṃ dāsā. “Ārāmiko ca neva dāso na bhujissoti vattabbato na dāso”ti likhitaṃ. Takkāsiñcanaṃ [V 0.0388] sīhaḷadīpe cārittaṃ. Te ca pabbājetabbā saṅghassārāmikattā. Nissāmikaṃ dāsaṃ attanāpi bhujissaṃ kātuṃ labhati. “Dāsassa pabbajitvā attano sāmike disvā palāyantassa āpatti natthīti vadantī”ti ca likhitaṃ. Attano vā dāso assa bhikkhunoti attho. Nissāmikassa dāsassa rājā sāmi, tasmā rājānaṃ vā tasmiṃ gāme manusse vā āpucchitvā pabbājetabboti eke. “Bhujissaṃ katvā”ti likhitaṃ. Tassa parihāraṃ bhaṇanti “yathā bhujisso hoti, tathā kattabbo”ti. Evaṃ saṅkappena vatvā “payojanaṃ natthī”ti kehici likhitaṃ. Bhujissaṃ kātumeva vaṭṭatīti “sace passanti, anubandhissantī”ti vuttaṃ. Āpatti natthi. “Asuddhā kira metipi taṃ sandhāyeva vutta”nti vadanti.

97. Regarding 'local custom': it refers to various local customs such as making announcements and posting notices. It is written, 'It is permissible for the son of a temple slave.' It is said, 'If one wishes to ordain a monastery worker, he should be ordained after giving another person in exchange.' This, here, is the intention of the Mahāpaccarivāda. Because they are given with the words, 'We give monastery workers to the community of monks,' they are not their slaves. It is written, 'A monastery worker is not their slave.' The pouring of the shuttle is a custom on the island of Sri Lanka. And they should be ordained because they are monastery workers of the Sangha. One may make a masterless slave a freeman even by oneself. And it is written, 'They say, "For a slave who, having been ordained, runs away upon seeing his masters, there is no offense."' Alternatively, the meaning is: he is the monk's own slave. For a masterless slave, the king is the master; therefore, some say he should be ordained after asking permission from the king or the people in that village. It is written, 'Having made him a freeman.' They speak of his treatment: 'He should be treated in the way that a freeman is.' Having spoken with such an intention, it is written by some, 'There is no purpose.' Regarding 'It is indeed proper to make him a freeman,' it is said, 'If they see him, they will pursue him.' There is no offense. They say, 'The statement "My teachings are indeed not for the impure" was said with reference to that very freeman-monk.'

Iṇāyikadāsavatthukathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Story of the Debtor-Slave is concluded.

Kammārabhaṇḍuvatthādikathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Story of the Blacksmith Bhaṇḍu and Others

98. Kammārabhaṇḍūti ettha dārako cūḷāmattaṃ ṭhapetvā āgacchati, tasmā āpucchituṃ labhati. Tañce so vā añño vā avaharati, doso natthi. “Kesamassuorohanaṃ akatvā asatiyā saraṇāni datvā pabbājeti, ruhatevā”ti vadanti.

98. In this passage on Kammārabhaṇḍu: a boy comes, having left only a topknot; therefore, one may ask his leave. If he or another removes it, there is no offense. They say, 'If one, without having the hair and beard shaved off, unmindfully gives the refuges and ordains him, the ordination is surely not valid.'

101-3. Ettha kule. “Ubhayāni kho panassa…pe… anubyañjanasoti sabbopāyaṃ pabhedo mātikāṭṭhakathāyaṃ ñāto hotī”ti ca “āpattiṃ [M 0.0425] jānātīti pāṭhe avattamānepi idaṃ nāma katvā idaṃ āpajjatīti jānāti ce, vaṭṭatī”ti ca likhitaṃ. “Tañca kho tato pubbe pāṭhe paguṇe kateti gahetabbaṃ, ācariyupajjhāyānampi eseva nayo”ti vuttaṃ.

101–3. Here, in this lineage. And it is written: “This entire distinction, ‘…pe… anubyañjanaso,’ is known in the Mātikāṭṭhakathā.” And it is written: “Even if the text ‘āpattiṃ jānāti’ (one knows the offense) is not recited, if one knows thus, ‘Having done such-and-such, one falls into this offense,’ it is allowable.” It is said: “And that should be understood when the text has been made familiar beforehand. This is the same method for teachers and preceptors as well.”

Kammārabhaṇḍuvatthādikathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Exposition of the Story of the Blacksmith Bhaṇḍu and Others is concluded.

Rāhulavatthukathāvaṇṇanā

The Exposition of the Story of Rāhula

105. “Aṅgārino dāni dumā bhadante”tiādīhi (theragā. 527) saṭṭhimattāhi. Dassehi iti maṃ āṇāpesi. Ettha iti-saddo āharitabbo. Pokkharavassanti pokkharapattavaṇṇaṃ udakaṃ, tamhi vassante temitukāmāva tementi. Uṇhīsato paṭṭhāyāti muddhato paṭṭhāya.

105. By about sixty verses beginning with, “Now the trees are like embers, venerable sir.” He commanded me, “Show!” Here, the word ‘iti’ should be supplied. ‘Pokkharavassa’ means water the color of a lotus leaf; when it rains, only those who wish to be wet get wet. ‘Starting from the turban’ means starting from the head.

“Siniddhanīlamudukuñcitakeso[V 0.0389],

Sūriyanimmalatalābhinalāṭo;

Yuttatuṅgamudukāyatanāso,

Raṃsijālavitato narasīho”ti. (apa. aṭṭha. 1.santikenidānakathā; jā. aṭṭha. 1.santikenidānakathā) –

“With hair glossy, dark blue, soft, and curling; with a forehead bright like the surface of the spotless sun; with a nose long, high, and well-proportioned; pervaded by a web of light—the lion among men.”

Ādigāthāhi. Atha vā –

By the opening verses. Or—

“Cakkavaraṅkitarattasupādo,

Lakkhaṇamaṇḍitaāyatapaṇhi;

Cāmarachattavibhūsitapādo,

Esa hi tuyha pitā narasīho.

“With beautiful red feet marked with excellent wheels; with long heels adorned with the marks; with feet honored by the chowry and parasol; this indeed is your father, the lion among men.”

“Sakyakumāravaro sukhumālo,

Lakkhaṇacittikapuṇṇasarīro;

Lokahitāya gato naravīro,

Esa hi tuyha pitā narasīho.

“The best of Sakyan princes, exceedingly delicate; with a full body adorned with the marks; a heroic man who has fared for the welfare of the world; this indeed is your father, the lion among men.”

“Puṇṇasasaṅkanibho mukhavaṇṇo,

Devanarāna piyo naranāgo;

Mattagajindavilāsitagāmī,

Esa hi tuyha pitā narasīho.

“His facial complexion is like the full moon; he is beloved of gods and men, a great man among men; his gait is as graceful as a lordly elephant in rut; this indeed is your father, the lion among men.”

“Khattiyasambhavaaggakulīno[M 0.0426],

Devamanussanamassitapādo;

Sīlasamādhipatiṭṭhitacitto,

Esa hi tuyha pitā narasīho.

“Born of the warrior caste, of the highest lineage; his feet are revered by gods and humans; his mind is established in virtue and concentration; this indeed is your father, the lion among men.”

“Āyatayuttasusaṇṭhitanāso,

Gopakhumo abhinīlasunetto;

Indadhanū [V 0.0390] abhinīlabhamūko,

Esa hi tuyha pitā narasīho.

“With a nose long, well-proportioned, and beautifully formed; with eyelashes like a cow’s and beautiful, very dark blue eyes; with very dark eyebrows arched like Indra’s bow; this indeed is your father, the lion among men.”

“Vaṭṭasuvaṭṭasusaṇṭhitagīvo,

Sīhahanū migarājasarīro;

Kañcanasucchaviuttamavaṇṇo,

Esa hi tuyha pitā narasīho.

“With a neck round, well-rounded, and beautifully formed; with a jaw like a lion and the torso of the king of beasts; with a supreme complexion and beautiful skin the color of gold; this indeed is your father, the lion among men.”

“Suddhasugambhīramañjusaghoso,

Hiṅgulabaddhasurattasujivho;

Vīsati vīsati setasudanto,

Esa hi tuyha pitā narasīho.

“His voice is pure, deep, and melodious; with a beautiful tongue, exceedingly red, as if smeared with vermilion; with twenty teeth above and twenty below, perfectly white—this indeed is your father, the lion among men.”

“Añjanavaṇṇasunīlasukeso,

Kañcanapaṭṭavisuddhanalāṭo;

Osadhipaṇḍarasuddhasuuṇṇo,

Esa hi tuyha pitā narasīho.

“With beautiful hair the color of collyrium, exceedingly dark; with a forehead pure and beautiful like a golden plate; with a pure, shining uṇṇa hair-tuft like the morning star—this indeed is your father, the lion among men.”

“Gacchatinīlapathe viya cando,

Tāragaṇāpariveṭhitarūpo;

Sāvakamajjhagato samaṇindo,

Esa hi tuyha pitā narasīho”ti. (jā. aṭṭha. 1.santikenidānakathā) –

“Just as the moon, its form surrounded by a host of stars, proceeds along the path of the wind; so the Lord of Ascetics, amidst his disciples, proceeds—this indeed is your father, the lion among men.”

Imāhi.

With these verses.

Uddiṭṭheti evaṃ caritabbanti attano, “uttiṭṭhe”ti dhammapadapāṭho. Dhammanti sapadānacārikavattaṃ. Anesanaṃ vajjetvā sucaritaṃ care.

In `Uddiṭṭhe`, the meaning is 'thus one should practice'. By oneself, the Dhammapada reading is `uttiṭṭhe`. In `Dhammaṃ`, the meaning is the duty of going for alms from house to house without interruption. Having avoided improper seeking, one should practice good conduct.

Kesavissajjananti [M 0.0427] pañcasikhākāraṃ vajjetvā ekasikhākāraṃ. Paṭṭabandhoti ettha paṭṭoti tasmiṃ [V 0.0391] kule āciṇṇo alaṅkāraviseso. Gharamaṅgalanti gharamaho. Chattamaṅgalanti yuvarājachattapaṭṭi. Vaṭṭānugatanti kilesavaṭṭānugataṃ. Vighātapaccayattā savighātakaṃ. Thero rādhaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ pubbe pabbajitvā kasmā idāni “kathāhaṃ, bhante, rāhulaṃ pabbājemī”ti āhāti ce? Tattha upasampadāpaṭikkhepo adhippeto, tasmā “bhagavā upasampadameva paṭikkhipi, idāni anāgate saṃsayāpanayanādhippāyo bhagavā”ti ñatvā āha. Cittasamuṭṭhānarūpavasena “aṭṭhimiñjaṃ āhaccā”ti vuttaṃ kira. Buddhānaṃ, cakkavattīnañca byattādivasena nānattaṃ veditabbaṃ, aññathā nandādayopi pabbajitvā buddhā siyuṃ “sace pabbajati, buddho hotī”ti vacanato.

“Kesavissajjana” means avoiding the five-peaked hairstyle and adopting a single-peaked hairstyle. In “Paṭṭabandha,” “paṭṭa” is a special ornament customary in that family. “Gharamaṅgala” means a household festival. “Chattamaṅgala” refers to the raising of the crown prince’s parasol. “Vaṭṭānugata” means following the cycle of defilements. Because it is a cause of affliction, it is afflictive. If one should ask why the Elder, having previously ordained the brahmin Rādha, now says, “How, venerable sir, shall I ordain Rāhula?”—there, the rejection of the higher ordination is intended. Therefore, knowing, “The Blessed One rejected only the higher ordination; now, the Blessed One’s intention is to dispel doubt in the future,” he spoke. It is said that “reaching the bone marrow” was spoken by way of mind-originated form. The distinction between Buddhas and wheel-turning monarchs should be understood by way of their skill, etc. Otherwise, even Nanda and others would become Buddhas after going forth, because of the statement, “If he goes forth, he becomes a Buddha.”

Pesetvā dassetuṃ vaṭṭati, āpucchissāmāti pabbājetuṃ vaṭṭatīti ca idaṃ yasmā videsappatto nāma lokasaṅketenāpi mātāpituvāsato mutto serivihārīti vuccati, tasmāssa te asantapakkhe ṭhitā viya hontīti katvā “na tassa pabbajjācariye vā appasādaṃ karontī”ti evaṃ vuttaṃ naṭṭhameva. Pabbajitā samagatikāti lokavohāro. Teneva cettha dukkhappattādinā desantaragamanañca samagatikaṃ kataṃ. Videsaṃ gantvāti cettha videso nāma mātāpituvāsato añño deso, na uppattidesato. Byañjanattho eva ce pamāṇaṃ, na yutti. Matamātāpitikopi na pabbājetabboti āpajjati, tasmā anuppattabbaṭṭhāne ṭhitehiyeva mātāpitūhi ananuññāto putto na pabbājetabboti evamidhādhippāyo veditabbo, aññathā pāḷiyā virujjheyya, āpattiṭṭhānassa ca sithilakaraṇaṃ aṭṭhakathāya na yujjati. Idaṃ tāva evaṃ hotu, “vihāraṃ vā jhāpemī”tiādinayo kathaṃ na virujjhatīti ce? Attaparūpaddavappasaṅgabhayena avasena pabbajitattā, puttarakkhaṇatthaṃ pabbajitattā ca. Evañhi sati sayameva so attanā pabbajito hoti, na kenaci upalāpetvā pabbajito. “Puttapemaṃ vā puttarakkhe piyo hotī”ti nidānānulomato na virujjhati.

This statement, 'It is proper to send for and show,' and 'It is proper to ordain after asking permission,' is because one who has gone to a foreign country is, even by worldly convention, said to be freed from the parents' residence and to be one who lives at will. Therefore, it is as if his parents are in the position of being absent. For this reason, the statement, 'They do not show displeasure towards his preceptor,' is indeed nullified. 'The ordained have a similar destiny' is a worldly expression. For that very reason, here, going to another country due to encountering suffering and so on is also made to be of a similar destiny. And here, in 'having gone to a foreign country,' a foreign country means a country other than the parents' residence, not other than one's place of birth. If the literal meaning of the words alone is the authority, and not the reasoning, it would follow that even one whose parents are deceased should not be ordained. Therefore, the intention to be understood here is thus: a son not permitted by his parents, who are indeed in a place that can be reached, should not be ordained. Otherwise, it would contradict the Pāli, and the weakening of the basis for an offense is not suitable for the commentary. Let this be so for now. If it is asked, 'How does the method beginning with, “I will burn down the monastery,” not contradict?' It does not contradict because of having been ordained under duress due to fear of the occurrence of harm to oneself and others, and because of having been ordained for the sake of protecting the son. For, this being so, he is ordained by himself of his own accord; he is not ordained after being persuaded by anyone. It does not contradict, being in accordance with the origin story: 'Love for a son is dear to one who protects the son.'

Rāhulavatthukathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Exposition of the Story of Rāhula is concluded.

Sikkhāpadadaṇḍakammavatthukathāvaṇṇanā

Exposition of the Story of the Disciplinary Action for the Training Rule

107. Attano [M 0.0428] pariveṇañcāti puggalikaṃ. Mukhadvārikanti mukhadvārena bhuñjitabbaṃ. Tattha niyojitabbakaṃ, tassa āvaraṇaṃ nivāraṇaṃ karonti. Atha vā “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, āvaraṇaṃ [V 0.0392] kātu”nti yaṃ āvaraṇaṃ anuññātaṃ, taṃ āvaraṇaṃ mukhadvārikaṃ āhāraṃ karontīti adhippāyo.

107. 'One's own dwelling' means personal. 'For the mouth-door' means to be eaten by way of the mouth. There, for him who is to be enjoined, they make a barrier, a prevention. Or alternatively, the intention is this: that barrier which was permitted, 'Bhikkhus, I allow the making of a barrier,' they apply that barrier to the food to be consumed by mouth.

Sikkhāpadadaṇḍakammavatthukathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Exposition of the Story of the Disciplinary Action for the Training Rule is concluded.

Anāpucchāvaraṇavatthuādikathāvaṇṇanā

Exposition of the Stories beginning with the Case of the Barrier without Asking

108. Parassa dussīlabhikkhussapīti attho. Keci “dussīlabhikkhūpī”ti likhanti, taṃ na sundaraṃ. Porāṇā pana “yāvatatiyaṃ vuccamāno ce na oramati, saṅghaṃ apaloketvā nāsetabbo, puna pabbajjaṃ yācamānopi apaloketvā pabbājetabbo”ti vadanti. Bhikkhūnaṃ upasampadakammavācāsadisanti ettha “yathā upasampanno sikkhaṃ paccakkhāya yathānivatthapārutova hutvā pacchā upasampanno pubbe attano navakatarassa samānavassikassa puna vandanādīni karoti, evaṃ sāmaṇeropi puna gahitasaraṇo tato pubbe attano navakatarassa samānavassikassa sāmaṇerassa puna vandanādīni karoti. Liṅgaṃ panettha vuḍḍhatarabhāvaṃ na sādhetīti vuttaṃ hotī”ti vuttaṃ. Vikālabhojanaṃ sāmaṇerānaṃ vītikkamevāti eke. “Accayo maṃ, bhante, accāgamā”tiādinā nayena accayaṃ desāpetabbo. “Diṭṭhiyā anissajjanena ‘tvaṃ, sāmaṇera, gacchā’ti vutteyeva pārājiko hotī”ti vuttaṃ, “yāvatatiyanti vuttattā buddhādīnaṃ avaṇṇabhāsitamattena ca diṭṭhiggahitamattena ca saraṇāni na bhijjantīti vuttaṃ hotī”ti vadanti. Evaṃ sante pāṇātipātādiṃ karontassāpi taṃ sambhotīti mama takko. “Nissīlassa puna nāsanā vuttā”ti ca keci vadanti, taṃ yuttaṃ viya. Na hi bhagavā sīlavantassa liṅganāsanaṃ anujānātīti vicāretabbaṃ, bhikkhunidūsakāpadesena bhabbābhabbe saṅgaṇhātīti porāṇā. “Pabbajjampi na labhatīti yathā cettha ayamattho dassito, tathā ‘paṇḍako, bhikkhave, anupasampanno na upasampādetabbo, upasampanno nāsetabbo’ti (mahāva. 109) ādinā [M 0.0429] nayena vuttānampi pabbajjaṃ natthīti dīpitaṃ hoti. Na hi idaṃ ṭhānaṃ ṭhapetvā tesaṃ pabbajjāya vāritaṭṭhānaṃ atthi. ‘Bhikkhunidūsako, bhikkhave, anupasampanno na upasampādetabbo, upasampanno nāsetabbo’ti (mahāva. 114) vuttenapi samānattā tassa pabbajjā viya tesampi pabbajjā vāritāva hotītipi dassetuṃ puna bhikkhunidūsakoti gahitanti apare”ti vuttaṃ. Kiṃ iminā? Nanu aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttaṃ “yassa cettha pabbajjā vāritā, taṃ sandhāya idaṃ vuttaṃ anupasampanno na upasampādetabbo, upasampanno nāsetabbo”ti.

108. The meaning is also for another immoral monk. Some write 'dussīlabhikkhūpi,' but that is not good. The ancients, however, say: 'If, even when told up to the third time, he does not desist, he should be expelled after informing the Saṅgha. Even if he requests the going-forth again, he should be given the going-forth after informing the Saṅgha.' Here, it is similar to the formal act of higher ordination for monks: it is said that just as one who has received higher ordination, having renounced the training and reverted to being dressed and cloaked as before, upon receiving higher ordination again, then performs acts of respect such as bowing to one of the same seniority who was previously his junior; so too a novice, having taken the refuges again, performs acts of respect such as bowing to a novice of the same seniority who was previously his junior. It is said that the meaning is: the monastic mark here does not establish seniority. Some say that eating at the wrong time is indeed a transgression for novices. He should be made to confess the transgression in the manner of saying, 'Venerable sir, a transgression has overcome me,' and so on. It is said: 'By not relinquishing his wrong view, as soon as he is told, "You, novice, go away!" he becomes one who has committed a pārājika offense.' They say that because it is said 'up to the third time,' the meaning is that the refuges are not broken merely by speaking dispraise of the Buddha and so on, nor merely by holding a wrong view. If that is so, it is my reasoning that this also applies to one who commits the killing of living beings and so on. And some say, 'The expulsion of an immoral one is spoken of again,' which seems correct. Indeed, it should be considered that the Blessed One does not permit the removal of the monastic mark for a virtuous one. The ancients say that under the pretext of a 'corrupter of nuns,' it includes both the suitable and the unsuitable. It is said: 'Just as the meaning "he does not even receive the going-forth" is shown here, so too it is explained that there is no going-forth for those spoken of in the manner beginning with, "A paṇḍaka, O monks, who has not received higher ordination should not be given higher ordination; if he has received higher ordination, he should be expelled" (Mahāvagga 109). For, apart from this passage, there is no other place where the going-forth is forbidden for them. Others say that the term "corrupter of nuns" is taken up again to show that, due to the similarity with what is said in "A corrupter of nuns, O monks, who has not received higher ordination should not be given higher ordination; if he has received higher ordination, he should be expelled" (Mahāvagga 114), just as his going-forth is forbidden, so too is their going-forth forbidden.' What is the use of this? Is it not said in the commentary: 'This statement, "one who has not received higher ordination should not be given higher ordination; if he has received higher ordination, he should be expelled," is said in reference to one for whom the going-forth is forbidden here'?

Anāpucchāvaraṇavatthuādikathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Case of Obstruction without Asking Permission, and so on, is concluded.

Paṇḍakavatthukathāvaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Case of the Paṇḍaka

109. Opakkamikapaṇḍakassa [V 0.0393] hīnaṅgattā apabbajitassa pabbajjā vāritā, pabbajitassa upasampadā na kātabbā. Pubbe upasampannassa ce upacaraṇaṃ atthi, na nāsanā kātabbāti no takkoti ācariyo. Chinnaṅgajāto na paṇḍako. Pañcasu napuṃsakapaṇḍakova abhāvako. Itare cattāro sabhāvakāti veditabbā. Bhāvo pana tesaṃ paṇḍako hoti. Ete cattāropi kira purisāvāti eke. Itthīpi pakkhapaṇḍakī hotīti eke. Upakkame kate paṇḍakabhāvo avassaṃ hoti, tasmā pabbajjaṃ na labhati. “Yadi pana kassaci na hoti, pabbajjā na vāritāti vinicchayaṃ vadantī”ti vuttaṃ.

109. For an opakkamika-paṇḍaka, because of having a deficient organ, the going-forth is forbidden for one who has not yet gone forth; for one who has already gone forth, the higher ordination should not be performed. If there is an investigation concerning one who was previously higher-ordained, expulsion should not be carried out. Thus is our reasoning, says the teacher. One whose sexual organ is severed is not a paṇḍaka. Among the five types, only the napuṃsaka-paṇḍaka lacks a sexual organ. The other four are to be understood as possessing a sexual nature. However, their sexual nature is deficient. Some say that these four are indeed men. Others say that a woman can also be a pakkhapaṇḍakī. When the procedure is performed, the state of being a paṇḍaka certainly occurs; therefore, one does not obtain the going-forth. It is said: 'They state the decision that if, however, for someone this state does not occur, the going-forth is not forbidden.'

“Pabbajjā vāritāti apaṇḍakapakkhe pabbājetvā paṇḍakapakkhe nāsetabboti adhippāyo”ti likhitaṃ. Porāṇagaṇṭhipade pana māsapaṇḍakalekhapaṇḍakehi saha satta paṇḍakā vuttā. Tattha lekhapaṇḍako nāma kira mantavasena upahatabījo. Tattha “opakkamikalekhapaṇḍakā pabbajitā na nāsetabbā. Yo pabbājeti, tassa dukkaṭa”nti ca vuttaṃ.

It is written: 'The meaning of "The going-forth is forbidden" is that one should give the going-forth in the case of a non-paṇḍaka, and one should expel in the case of a paṇḍaka.' But in the ancient Gaṇṭhipada, seven paṇḍakas are mentioned, together with the māsa-paṇḍaka and the lekha-paṇḍaka. There, the one called a lekha-paṇḍaka, it is said, is one whose testicles have been removed by the power of a mantra. And there it is stated: 'Opakkamika-paṇḍakas and lekha-paṇḍakas, if they have gone forth, should not be expelled. For the teacher who gives them the going-forth, there is a dukkaṭa offense.'

Paṇḍakavatthukathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Case of the Paṇḍaka is concluded.

Theyyasaṃvāsakavatthukathāvaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Case of One in Stolen Communion

110. Theyyasaṃvāsakoti [M 0.0430] ettha kiñcāpi byañjanatthavasena saṃvāsatthenakova theyyasaṃvāsakoti paññāyati, atha kho tayo theyyasaṃvāsakā. Saṃvāsoti cettha na ekakammādiko saṃvāso, kintu bhikkhuvassagaṇanādiko kiriyabhedo idha saṃvāso nāma. Imañhi sakkā theyyāya kātuṃ, netaranti aṭṭhakathāya adhippāyo. Videsaṃ gantvā pabbajitehi pucchite “dasavasso”tiādiṃ bhaṇantassa doso. Gihīnaṃ vutte doso natthīti keci. Rājabhayādīhi gahitaliṅgānaṃ “gihī maṃ samaṇoti jānātū”ti vañcanacitte satipi bhikkhūnaṃ vañcetukāmatāya, tehi saṃvasitukāmatāya ca abhāvā doso na jāto. “Sabbapāsaṇḍiyabhattānīti vihāraṃ āgantvā saṅghikaṃ gaṇhantassa saṃvāsaṃ pariharituṃ dukkaraṃ, tasmā vutta”nti ca likhitaṃ. “Sūpasampanno”ti vuttattā gahaṭṭhampi sace upasampādenti, sūpasampannoti āpannaṃ, “anupasampannakāleyevā”ti iminā sace upasampannakāle suṇāti, sūpasampanno eva anārocentopīti dasseti. Andhakaṭṭhakathāyaṃ, porāṇagaṇṭhipadesu ca dussīlabhikkhu [V 0.0394] “theyyasaṃvāsako”ti vutto “theyyāya vo, bhikkhave, raṭṭhapiṇḍo bhutto”ti (pārā. 195) iminā kira pariyāyenāti veditabbaṃ. Tenevāha “taṃ na gahetabba”nti. “Mahāpeḷādīsū”ti etena gihisantakaṃ dassitaṃ.

110. Regarding the term 'theyyasaṃvāsaka': Here, although by the literal meaning of the words it is understood only in the sense of 'communion by theft' (theyyasaṃvāsa), there are, however, three types of theyyasaṃvāsaka. As for 'communion' (saṃvāsa) here, it is not communion beginning with common acts; rather, a distinction of practice beginning with the counting of a bhikkhu's years is here called 'communion'. For it is possible to commit theft in this regard, but not in the other—this is the intention of the commentary. If one goes to another country and, when asked by the ordained, says, 'I have ten years of seniority,' and so on, there is an offense. Some say there is no offense if it is said to laypeople. For those who have assumed the monastic appearance due to fear of the king and so forth, even if there is a deceitful thought, 'Let laypeople know me as an ascetic,' an offense does not arise because of the absence of the desire to deceive bhikkhus and the desire to live in communion with them. And it is written: 'For one who comes to a monastery and takes what belongs to the Sangha, it is difficult to avoid communion; therefore, it was said.' Because it is said 'well-ordained', even if they ordain a householder, it follows that he is 'well-ordained'. By the phrase 'only at the time of not being ordained,' it is shown that if he hears it at the time of being ordained, he is indeed well-ordained even without announcing it. In the Andhaka commentary and in ancient glosses, an immoral bhikkhu is called a 'theyyasaṃvāsaka', and it should be understood that this is said, it seems, by this expression: 'Bhikkhus, the country's alms-food has been eaten by you through theft' (Pārā. 195). For that very reason, it was said, 'That should not be taken.' By 'in Mahāpeḷā and so forth,' what belongs to a householder is shown.

Sayaṃ sāmaṇerova kūṭavassāni gaṇetvā gaṇhanto pārājiko hoti, theyyasaṃvāsako pana na hoti, tathā bhikkhupi, so pana bhaṇḍagghena kāretabboti iminā adhippāyena “sayaṃ sāmaṇerovā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Ayaṃ pana theyyasaṃvāsako nāma yasmā pabbajitova hoti, nāpabbajito, tasmā “theyyasaṃvāsako, bhikkhave, apabbajito na pabbājetabbo, pabbajito nāsetabbo”ti vattuṃ na sakkāti katvā imassa vasena paṇḍakato paṭṭhāya “anupasampanno na upasampādetabbo”tiādinā pāḷi ṭhapitā, na upasampadāmattasseva abhabbattā ekādasannampi nesaṃ pabbajjārahabhāvappasaṅgato. Apica aniṭṭhadosappasaṅgato tathā eva pāḷi ṭhapitā. Yasmā titthiyapakkamanaṃ, saṅghabhedanañca upasampannasseva hoti, nānupasampannassa, so [M 0.0431] duvidhopi pabbajitova hoti, nāpabbajito, tasmā “titthiyapakkantako, bhikkhave, apabbajito na pabbājetabbo”tiādipāḷiyā sati te ubhopi apabbājetabbā hontīti aniṭṭhappasaṅgo āpajjatīti. Tīsu pana theyyasaṃvāsakesu sāmaṇerālayaṃ karonto liṅgatthenako, upasampannālayaṃ karonto saṃvāsatthenako, ubhayatthenako ca. Na hi sāmaṇerasaṃvāso idha saṃvāso nāma, teneva aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “bhikkhuvassagaṇanādiko hi sabbopi kiriyabhedo imasmiṃ atthe saṃvāso”ti vuttanti eke. Yathāvuḍḍhaṃ vandanasādiyanāsanapaṭibāhanānaṃ sāmaṇerasaṃvāsasāmaññato nevāti ācariyo.

A novice himself, having counted deceitful years and taking them, becomes one who has committed a pārājika offense, but he is not a theyyasaṃvāsaka. Likewise for a bhikkhu. With the intention that 'he, however, should be made to pay according to the value of the goods,' the passage beginning 'a novice himself...' was stated. Now, this one called a theyyasaṃvāsaka is so because he is one who has gone forth, not one who has not gone forth. Therefore, because it is not possible to say, 'Bhikkhus, a theyyasaṃvāsaka who has not gone forth should not be given the going forth; one who has gone forth should be expelled,' on account of this, starting from the paṇḍaka, the Pāḷi was established with the words, 'One who is not fully ordained should not be given the higher ordination,' and so on. This is not merely because of their unfitness for just the higher ordination, but because of the consequence that all eleven of those persons would be fit for the going forth. Furthermore, the Pāḷi was established in that very way because of the consequence of an undesirable fault. Because defection to another sect and causing a schism in the Saṅgha occur only for one who is fully ordained, not for one who is not fully ordained, and both of these two types are ones who have gone forth, not ones who have not gone forth, therefore, if there were a Pāḷi text like 'Bhikkhus, one who has defected to another sect who has not gone forth should not be given the going forth,' etc., the undesirable consequence that both of them should not be given the going forth would arise. Now, among the three types of theyyasaṃvāsaka, one who makes a pretext of being a novice is a liṅgatthenaka; one who makes a pretext of being a fully ordained one is a saṃvāsatthenaka and also a ubhayatthenaka. For communion as a novice is not called 'communion' here. Therefore, in the commentary, some say, 'Indeed, every kind of action, such as the counting of a bhikkhu's years, is 'communion' in this sense.' The teacher says: It is not so, because of the commonality with a novice's communion in regard to paying homage, accepting a seat, and preventing another from taking a seat according to seniority.

Theyyasaṃvāsakavatthukathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Discourse on the Case of the Theyyasaṃvāsaka is concluded.

Titthiyapakkantakakathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourse on One Who Has Defected to Another Sect

Titthiyapakkantako, bhikkhavetiādi attano nidānabhūte pasūravatthusmiṃ eva vattabbaṃ samānampi tattha vāritaadhikārābhāvā abhabbā. Idheva theyyasaṃvāsakena vinā sambhavato vutto. Tattha “atha kho na pabbājetabbopī”ti idheva vacanaṃ pasūrassa upasampadāya eva yācanicchāya dassanena, “so āgato na upasampādetabbo”ti bhagavato upasampadāmattapaṭisedhanena ca pabbajjānumatidosappasaṅgabhayāti veditabbaṃ. Tesaṃ liṅge ādinnamatte laddhiyā gahitāyapi aggahitāyapi titthiyapakkantako hoti, avandanīyasseva naggaliṅgassa seṭṭhabhāvaṃ vā upagacchati, na muccati, ettha “padavāre dukkaṭaṃ, ājīvako bhavissanti visamacittavasena gatattā [V 0.0395] naggo hutvā na gamanenā”ti vadanti. Ubhinnampi vasena yuttanti mama takko. Tāva naṃ laddhi rakkhati asampaṭicchitattā. Upasampannabhikkhunā kathitoti kathaṃ paññāyati? Aṭṭhakathāvacanappamāṇatovāti eke. Nidānavasenāti eke. Pasūrassa upasampannattā upasampannānaṃ eva titthiyapakkantatāvacanatoti eke. Yathāha “upajjhāyo pakkantovā hoti, vibbhanto vā, kālaṃkato vā, pakkhasaṅkanto vā”ti ācariyo. Pakkhasaṅkanto vāti sāmaṇeranāsanāvatthūsu abhāvatoti eke. Aññatitthiyapubbassa upasampannassa sato pakkhasaṅkantabhayā anupasampannakāle upasampadatthaṃ parivāsapaññāpanenāti eke[M 0.0432]. Pabbajjatthampīti ce? Na, pubbe vicāritattā, apabbajitassa adhisīlābhāvato ca. Pātimokkhasīlañhi adhisīlaṃ nāma, tañca apabbajitassa natthi. Imassa ca parivāsavatte adhisīlaṃ vuttaṃ. Yathāha “puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyapubbo tibbacchando hoti uddese paripucchāya adhisīle”ti (mahāva. 87). Apica “sace, bhikkhave, jātiyā sākiyo aññatitthiyapubbo āgacchati, so āgato upasampādetabbo”ti (mahāva. 87) ettha upasampadāmattaparidīpanato. Upasampadāmattaparidīpanañhettha tasseva parivāsadānasiddhito. Parivāsadānattanidassanatthe hesā pāḷi.

The section beginning with 'One who has defected to another sect, O bhikkhus'—although this should be spoken only regarding the case of Pasūra, which serves as its origin, it is not suitable there due to the absence of a prohibited matter. Here, it is stated because it is possible without one who has stolen communion. There, the statement 'but he should not even be given the going forth' should be understood as being stated here due to the fear of the fault of implying permission for the going forth, which is shown by Pasūra's desire to request only higher ordination, and by the Blessed One's prohibition of higher ordination alone with the words 'having come, he should not be given the higher ordination.' Merely upon taking on their sign, whether their view has been adopted or not, one becomes a defector to another sect; he attains the superior status of the naked sign, which is not to be venerated, and is not freed. Here, some say: 'At every footstep, there is a dukkaṭa offense. This is because he has gone with an unsteady mind, thinking, "I will become an Ājīvaka," not because of going naked.' My reasoning is that it is suitable in both ways. For the time being, the view protects him, because it has not been accepted. How is it known that this was spoken by a fully ordained bhikkhu? Some say it is known from the authority of the commentary's statement. Others say it is due to the origin story. Others say it is because Pasūra was fully ordained, and because the state of being a defector to another sect is spoken of only for the fully ordained. As the teacher said: 'The preceptor may have gone away, or disrobed, or died, or changed factions.' Some say this is because 'changing factions' is absent among the grounds for the expulsion of a novice. Others say it is known from the fact that probation is prescribed for the purpose of higher ordination while one is not yet ordained, due to the fear that one who was previously a sectarian might change factions after being ordained. If one should say, 'Is it also for the purpose of the going forth?' No, it should not be said, because it has been considered before, and because one who has not gone forth lacks the higher virtue. Indeed, the Pātimokkha virtue is called the higher virtue, and that does not exist for one who has not gone forth. And for this person, during the practice of probation, the higher virtue is mentioned. As it is said: 'Furthermore, O bhikkhus, one who was previously a sectarian is of strong desire in recitation, in questioning, and in the higher virtue.' Moreover, in the passage 'If, O bhikkhus, a Sākiyan by birth who was previously a sectarian comes, having come, he should be given the higher ordination,' it is known from the showing of only the higher ordination. And the showing of only the higher ordination here is established by the granting of probation to him. Indeed, this Pali passage is for the purpose of illustrating the granting of probation.

Titthiyapakkantakakathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Account of One Who Has Defected to Another Sect is concluded.

Tiracchānagatavatthukathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Account of Animal Births

111. Nāgayoniyāti nāgayonito, attano nāgajātihetūti adhippāyo. Kiṃkāraṇā? Abhikkhaṇaṃ sakajātiyā methunapaṭisevane, vissaṭṭhaniddokkamane ca sabbesampi.

111. `Nāgayoniyā` means: because of being of the nāga-species (`nāgayonito`); the implication is 'due to the cause of being of one's own nāga-birth'. What is the reason that one is vexed? Because frequently, for all of them, when engaging in sexual intercourse with their own kind and when descending into relaxed sleep, their nāga body appears.

Tiracchānagatavatthukathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Account of Animal Births is concluded.

Mātughātakādivatthukathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Account of Matricide and So Forth

112-5. Apavāhananti pakkhalanaṃ, kāsāyavatthanivāsanaṃ icchamānanti attho. Duṭṭhacittena. Kīdisena? Vadhakacittenāti adhippāyo. Lohituppādanavasena duṭṭhacittanti keci, taṃ na sundaraṃ.

112-5. `Apavāhanaṃ` means cleansing (`pakkhalanaṃ`); the meaning is desiring to wear the saffron robe. `Duṭṭhacittena` (With a corrupt mind). Of what sort? The implication is: with the mind of a killer. Some say 'corrupt mind' is in the sense of producing blood; but that is not good.

Mātughātakādivatthukathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Account of Matricide and So Forth is concluded.

Ubhatobyañjanakavatthukathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Account of Hermaphrodites

116. “Yadi [V 0.0396] paṭisandhiyaṃ uppannaliṅgena etaṃ nāmaṃ labhantīti adhippāyo”ti likhitaṃ.

116. "The intention is: if they receive this name at rebirth-linking by means of the arisen sexual characteristic," is written.

Ubhatobyañjanakavatthukathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Account of Hermaphrodites is concluded.

Anupajjhāyakādivatthukathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Account of Those Without a Preceptor and So Forth

117. “Keci [M 0.0433] ‘kuppatī’ti vadanti, taṃ ‘na gahetabba”nti yaṃ vuttaṃ, taṃ “pañcavaggakaraṇīyañce, bhikkhave, kammaṃ bhikkhunipañcamo kammaṃ kareyya, akammaṃ na ca karaṇīya”ntiādinā (mahāva. 390) nayena vuttattā paṇḍakādīnaṃ gaṇapūraṇabhāve eva kammaṃ kuppati, na sabbanti katvā suvuttaṃ, itarathā “paṇḍakupajjhāyena kammaṃ kareyya, akammaṃ na ca karaṇīya”ntiādikāya pāḷiyā bhavitabbaṃ siyā. Yathā aparipuṇṇapattacīvarassa upasampādanakāle kammavācāyaṃ “paripuṇṇassa pattacīvara”nti asantaṃ vatthuṃ kittetvā upasampadāya katāya tasmiṃ asantepi upasampadā ruhati, evaṃ “ayaṃ buddharakkhito āyasmato dhammarakkhitassa upasampadāpekkho”ti avatthuṃ paṇḍakupajjhāyādiṃ, asantaṃ vā, vatthuṃ kittetvā katāyapi gaṇapūrakānamatthitāya upasampadā ruhateva. “Na, bhikkhave, paṇḍakupajjhāyena upasampādetabbo, yo upasampādeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa, so ca puggalo anupasampanno”tiādivacanassābhāvā ayamattho siddhova hoti. Na hi buddhā vattabbayuttaṃ na vadanti, tena vuttaṃ “yo pana, bhikkhu, jānaṃ ūnavīsativassaṃ…pe… so ca puggalo anupasampanno”tiādi (pāci. 403). Tathā “byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo’ti (mahāva. 71) vacanato theyyasaṃvāsakādiācariyehi anussāvanāya katāya upasampadā na ruhati tesaṃ abhikkhuttā”ti vacanampi na gahetabbaṃ. Kiñca bhiyyo “imāni cattāri kammāni pañcahākārehi vipajjantī”tiādinā (pari. 482) nayena kammānaṃ sampattivipattiyā kathiyamānāya “sattahi ākārehi kammāni vipajjanti vatthuto vā ñattito vā anussāvanato vā sīmato vā parisato vā upajjhāyato vā ācariyato vā”ti akathitattā na gahetabbaṃ. “Parisato vā”ti vacanena ācariyaupajjhāyānaṃ vā saṅgaho katoti ce? Na, “dvādasahākārehi parisato kammāni vipajjantī”ti etassa vibhaṅge tesamanāmaṭṭhattā. Ayamattho “yasmā tattha tattha sarūpena vuttapāḷivaseneva sakkā jānituṃ, tasmā nayamukhaṃ dassetvā saṃkhittoti ayamassa yuttigavesanā”ti vuttaṃ. Tatridaṃ vicāretabbaṃ – anupajjhāyakaṃ [V 0.0397] upasampādentā te bhikkhū yathāvuttanayena abhūtaṃ taṃ vatthuṃ kittayiṃsu, udāhu musāvādabhayā tāneva padāni na sāvesunti. Kiñcettha yadi tāva upajjhāyābhāvata [M 0.0434] na sāvesuṃ, “puggalaṃ na parāmasatī”ti vuttavipattippasaṅgo hoti, atha sāvesuṃ, musāvādo nesaṃ bhavatīti? Vuccate – sāvesuṃyeva yathāvuttavipattippasaṅgabhayā, “kammaṃ pana na kuppatī”ti aṭṭhakathāya vuttattā ca, na musāvādassa asambhavato, musāvādenāpi kammasambhavato ca. Na hi sakkā musāvādena kammavipattisampattiṃ kātunti. Tasmā “anupajjhāyakaṃ upasampādentī”ti vacanassa ubhayadosavinimutto attho pariyesitabbo.

117. Regarding the statement, 'Some say, "It becomes invalid," but that should not be accepted,' that statement is well-said. This is because it has been stated by the method beginning with, 'Bhikkhus, if a legal act that should be done by a group of five were to be performed with a bhikkhunī as the fifth, it would be an invalid act and one that should not be done.' Therefore, a legal act becomes invalid only in the case where eunuchs and the like are fulfilling the quorum, not every legal act. Otherwise, there would have to be a Pāli text such as, 'If a legal act were performed with a eunuch as preceptor, it would be an invalid act and one that should not be done.' Just as, at the time of ordination for one whose bowl and robes are incomplete, when during the formal act proclamation it is announced, 'His bowl and robes are complete,' declaring a matter that is not true, the ordination nevertheless succeeds even though that is not present; so too, even when an ordination is performed by announcing an untrue matter—such as, 'This Buddharakkhita is the candidate for ordination of the venerable Dhammarakkhita,' when the preceptor is a eunuch, or announcing a matter that is non-existent—the ordination still succeeds due to the presence of those who complete the quorum. Because there is no statement such as, 'Bhikkhus, one should not be ordained by a eunuch preceptor; whoever should so ordain incurs an offense of wrongdoing, and that person is not ordained,' this meaning is indeed established. For the Buddhas do not fail to say what ought to be said. Therefore, it is stated, 'Whatever bhikkhu, knowing... a person under twenty years of age... that person is not ordained,' and so on. Likewise, the statement, 'Based on the text "The Saṅgha should be informed by a competent, capable bhikkhu," an ordination performed with a proclamation by a teacher who is a thief-in-disguise, etc., does not succeed because they are not bhikkhus,' should also not be accepted. Furthermore, when the success and failure of legal acts are being discussed by the method beginning with, 'These four legal acts fail in five ways,' it is not stated that 'Legal acts fail in seven ways: due to the basis, the motion, the proclamation, the boundary, the assembly, the preceptor, or the teacher'; therefore, this should not be accepted. If it is said that the teacher and preceptor are included in the phrase 'due to the assembly,' this is not so, because they are not mentioned in the analysis of 'Legal acts fail in twelve ways due to the assembly.' This meaning is stated: 'Because in each and every case it can be known simply by the Pāli text as it is stated in its own form, therefore, having shown the introduction to the method, it is abbreviated. This is the investigation of its logic.' Herein, this should be investigated: Did those bhikkhus, when ordaining someone without a preceptor, announce that untrue matter according to the aforesaid method, or, out of fear of false speech, did they not recite those very words? And here, if they did not recite them due to the absence of a preceptor, there would be the consequence of the failure stated as 'it does not refer to the person.' But if they did recite them, would it not be false speech for them? It is said: They did indeed recite them, out of fear of the consequence of the aforesaid failure, and because it is said in the commentary, 'But the legal act does not become invalid.' This is not because false speech is impossible, but because a legal act is possible even with false speech. For it is not possible by means of false speech to cause the failure or success of a legal act. Therefore, a meaning for the statement 'they ordain someone without a preceptor' should be sought that is free from both these faults.

Ayañcettha yutti – “yathā pubbe pabbajjupasampadupajjhāyesu vijjamānesupi upajjhāyaggahaṇakkamena aggahitattā ‘tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū anupajjhāyaka’ntiādi vuttaṃ, tathā idhāpi upajjhāyassa vijjamānasseva sato aggahitattā ‘anupajjhāyakaṃ upasampādentī’ti vuttaṃ. Kammavācācariyena pana gahito tena upajjhāyoti saññāya upajjhāyaṃ kittetvā kammavācaṃ sāvetabbaṃ, kenaci vā kāraṇena kāyasāmaggiṃ adentassa upajjhāyassa chandaṃ gahetvā kammavācaṃ sāveti, upajjhāyo vā upasampadāpekkhassa upajjhaṃ datvā pacchā upasampanne tasmiṃ tādise vatthusmiṃ samanuyuñjiyamāno vā asamanuyuñjiyamāno vā upajjhāyadānato pubbe eva sāmaṇero paṭijānāti, sikkhāpaccakkhātako vā antimavatthuajjhāpannako vā paṭijānāti, chandahārakādayo viya upajjhāyo vā aññasīmāgato hoti, ‘kammavācā ruhatī’ti vatvā ‘anujānāmi, bhikkhave, paccantimesu janapadesu vinayadharapañcamena gaṇena upasampada’nti (mahāva. 259) vuttattā keci ‘vinayadharapañcamena upajjhāyena sannihiteneva bhavitabba’nti vadantī”ti porāṇagaṇṭhipade vuttaṃ. So ce pāṭho pamāṇo majjhimesu janapadesu tassa vacanassābhāvato. Asannihitepi upajjhāye kammavācā ruhatīti āpajjatīti ce? Na, kasmā? Kammasampattiyaṃ “puggalaṃ parāmasatī”ti vuttapāṭhova no pamāṇaṃ. Na hi tattha asannihito upajjhāyasaṅkhāto puggalo parāmasanaṃ arahati, tasmā tattha saṅghaparāmasanaṃ viya puggalaparāmasanaṃ veditabbaṃ. Saṅghena gaṇena upajjhāyena upasampādenti tesaṃ atthato puggalattā. Paṇḍakādiupajjhāyena upasampādenti upasampādanakāle aviditattāti porāṇā.

And this is the reasoning here: 'Just as previously, although there were preceptors for the going forth and for the higher ordination, because they were not taken in accordance with the procedure for appointing a preceptor, it was said, "At that time, the monks were without a preceptor," and so on; so also here, although a preceptor is indeed present, because he has not been taken, it is said, "They confer the higher ordination without a preceptor." However, the Kammavācācariya, with the perception that the preceptor has been taken by the candidate, having announced the preceptor, should recite the kammavācā. Alternatively, if the preceptor does not give his physical presence for some reason, he recites the kammavācā after obtaining his consent. Or, a preceptor gives the preceptorship to a candidate for higher ordination, and afterwards, when that one has been ordained, in such a case, whether being questioned or not, the sāmaṇera confesses just before the giving of the preceptor, or confesses to being one who has given up the training or one who has committed a terminal offense; or, like the consent-carriers and others, the preceptor has gone to another boundary. The kammavācā is valid. And, because it was said, "I allow, monks, in the border regions, higher ordination by a chapter with a Vinaya expert as the fifth," some say, "The preceptor must be present with the chapter having a Vinaya expert as the fifth." Thus it is said in the ancient Gaṇṭhipada. If that text is the authority, this is problematic due to the absence of that statement in the middle countries. If it is argued that it follows that the kammavācā is valid even when the preceptor is not present? No. Why? In the completion of the act, the text that says, "it refers to the person," is our authority. For a person designated as a preceptor who is not present there is not worthy of reference. Therefore, the reference to the person should be understood there like the reference to the Saṅgha. They ordain by means of the Saṅgha, by means of a chapter, and by means of a preceptor, because these are, in essence, individuals. The ancients say that they ordain with a preceptor who is a eunuch, etc., because at the time of ordination this was not known.

Apattakādivatthukathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Story of Those Without a Bowl, and so forth

118. Apattacīvaraṃ [M 0.0435] upasampādentīti kammavācācariyo “paripuṇṇassa pattacīvara”nti saññāya[V 0.0398], kevalaṃ atthasampattiṃ anapekkhitvā santapadanihārena vā “paripuṇṇassa pattacīvara”nti kammavācaṃ sāveti. Yathā etarahi matavippavutthamātāpitikopi “anuññātosi mātāpitūhī”ti puṭṭho “āma bhante”ti vadati. Kiṃ bahunā, ayaṃ panettha sāro – “tasmiṃ samaye cattāri kammāni pañcahākārehi vipajjantī”ti lakkhaṇassa na tāva paññattattā anupajjhāyakādiṃ upasampādenti, vajjanīyapuggalānaṃ avuttattā paṇḍakupajjhāyādiṃ upasampādenti. Terasantarāyapucchāya adassanattā apattacīvarakaṃ upasampādenti. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ñatticatutthena kammena upasampādetu”nti (mahāva. 69) evaṃ sabbapaṭhamaṃ anuññātakammavācāya “paripuṇṇassa pattacīvara”nti avacanamettha sādhakanti veditabbaṃ. Tañhi vacanaṃ anukkamenānuññātanti.

118. In the phrase `apattacīvaraṃ upasampādenti` (they ordain one without a bowl and robes), the Kammavācācariya recites the Kammavācā, 'his bowl and robes are complete,' with the perception that this is so, either disregarding the actual accomplishment of the matter or simply by uttering the existing words. It is just as nowadays when even one whose parents are dead or far away, upon being asked, 'Have you been permitted by your mother and father?' says, 'Yes, venerable sir.' What is the use of saying much? This is the essence here: because the characteristic of 'at that time, four formal acts fail in five ways' had not yet been laid down, they ordained those without a preceptor, and so forth. Because the persons to be avoided had not been spoken of, they ordained others with a eunuch, and so forth, as preceptor. Because the questioning about the thirteen obstacles was not seen, they ordained one without a bowl and robes. In the very first Kammavācā that was permitted—'I allow, monks, to ordain by a formal act with the motion as the fourth'—the non-utterance of 'his bowl and robes are complete' should be understood as the proof in this matter. For that statement was indeed permitted in due course.

Hatthacchinnādivatthukathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Story of One with a Severed Hand, and so forth

119. Idaṃ tāva sabbathā hotu, “mūgaṃ pabbājenti, badhiraṃ pabbājentī”ti idaṃ kathaṃ sambhavitumarahati ādito paṭṭhāya “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, imehi tīhi saraṇagamanehi pabbajja”ntiādinā (mahāva. 34) anuññātattāti? Vuccate – “evañca pana, bhikkhave, pabbājetabboti. Evaṃ vadehīti vattabbo…pe… tatiyampi saṅghaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmī”ti ettha “evaṃ vadehīti vattabbo”ti imassa vacanassa micchā atthaṃ gahetvā mūgaṃ pabbājesuṃ. “Evaṃ vadehī”ti taṃ pabbajjāpekkhaṃ āṇāpetvā sayaṃ upajjhāyena vattabbo “tatiyaṃ saṅghaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmī”ti, so pabbajjāpekkho tathā āṇatto upajjhāyavacanassa anu anu vadatu vā, mā vā, tattha tattha bhagavā “kāyena viññāpeti, vācāya viññāpeti, kāyena vācāya viññāpeti, gahito hoti upajjhāyo. Dinno hoti chando. Dinnā hoti pārisuddhi. Dinnā hoti pavāraṇā”ti vadati.
