Tadanumānena vā kāyena tena pabbajjāpekkhena viññattaṃ hoti saraṇagamananti vā lokepi kāyena viññāpento “evaṃ vadatī”ti vuccati, taṃ pariyāyaṃ gahetvā mūgaṃ pabbājentīti veditabbaṃ. Porāṇagaṇṭhipade “mūgaṃ kathaṃ pabbājentī’ti pucchaṃ katvā tassa kāyappasādasambhavato kāyena [M 0.0436] pahāraṃ datvā hatthamuddāya viññāpetvā pabbājesu”nti vuttaṃ. Kiṃ bahunā, ayaṃ panettha sāro – yathā pubbe pabbajjādhikāre vattamāne pabbajjābhilāpaṃ upacchinditvā “paṇḍako, bhikkhave, anupasampanno na upasampādetabbo”tiādinā nayena upasampadavaseneva abhilāpo kato. Theyyasaṃvāsakapade asambhavato kiñcāpi so na kato pabbajjāva tattha katā, sabbattha pana upasampadābhilāpena adhippetā tadanubhāvato. Upasampadāya pabbajjāya vāritāya upasampadā vāritā hotīti katvā. Tathā idha upasampadādhikāre vattamāne [V 0.0399] upasampadābhilāpaṃ upacchinditvā upasampadameva sandhāya pabbajjābhilāpo katoti veditabbo. Kāmaṃ so na kattabbo, mūgapade asambhavato tassa vasena ādito paṭṭhāya upasampadābhilāpova kattabbo viya dissati, tathāpi tasseva mūgapadassa vasena ādito paṭṭhāya pabbajjābhilāpova kato micchāgahaṇanivāraṇatthaṃ. Kathaṃ? “Mūgo, bhikkhave, appatto osāraṇaṃ, tañce saṅgho osāreti, sosārito”ti (mahāva. 396) vacanato mūgo upasampanno hotīti siddhaṃ. So “kevalaṃ upasampannova hoti, na pana pabbajito tassa pabbajjāya asambhavato”ti micchāgāho hoti. Taṃ pariccajāpetvā yo upasampanno, so pabbajitova hoti. Pabbajito pana atthi koci upasampanno, atthi koci anupasampanno. Imaṃ sammāgāhaṃ uppādeti bhagavāti veditabbaṃ.

119. First, let this be in all respects: How is this matter possible, 'They give the going forth to a mute person; they give the going forth to a deaf person,' since from the beginning it was allowed by the text beginning, 'I allow, O monks, the going forth by these three goings for refuge'? It is said: In the passage, 'And thus, O monks, one should be given the going forth. Speak thus... and so on... for the third time, I go to the Sangha for refuge,' they gave the going forth to a mute person by wrongly grasping the meaning of the phrase, 'Speak thus.' Having instructed the candidate for the going forth, 'Speak thus,' the preceptor himself should say, 'For the third time, I go to the Sangha for refuge.' Whether that candidate, thus instructed, repeats the preceptor’s words or not, in such cases the Blessed One says, 'He makes known by body, he makes known by speech, he makes known by body and speech; the preceptor is accepted. Consent is given. Purity is given. The invitation is given.' Or, by inference from that, the going for refuge is made known by that candidate by means of the body. Also in the world, one who makes known by body is said to 'speak thus.' It should be understood that, having taken this method, they give the going forth to a mute person. In the ancient glossaries, having asked the question, 'How do they give the going forth to a mute person?', it is said: 'Because of the possibility of his bodily faculty, having given a touch with the hand and having made it known by a hand gesture, they gave the going forth.' What is the use of saying much? This is the essence here: Just as previously, while the section on the going forth was current, having interrupted the expression for the going forth, the expression was made by way of full ordination itself, by the method beginning with, 'A eunuch, O monks, who is not fully ordained, should not be given full ordination,' and so on. In the section on the thief-in-communion, due to the impossibility [of his going forth], although that expression [prohibiting it] was not made, the going forth itself is what is being addressed there. In all cases, however, the going forth is intended by the expression for full ordination, because of its influence. This is done on the principle that when the going forth is prevented by the [prohibition of] full ordination, the full ordination is [truly] prevented. Similarly here, while the section on full ordination is current, it should be understood that having interrupted the expression for full ordination, the expression for the going forth was made with reference to full ordination itself. Indeed, that should not have been done; because of the impossibility in the case of the mute, it seems that from the beginning the expression for full ordination itself should have been made. Nevertheless, on account of that very case of the mute, from the beginning the expression for the going forth itself was made in order to prevent wrong grasping. How so? According to the text, 'A mute, O monks, has not reached reinstatement; if the Sangha reinstates him, he is well reinstated,' it is established that a mute is fully ordained. Then the wrong grasping arises: 'He is only fully ordained, but not one who has gone forth, because the going forth is impossible for him.' Causing that wrong grasping to be abandoned, the Blessed One teaches that whoever is fully ordained is indeed one who has gone forth. But as for one who has gone forth, there is one who is fully ordained, and there is one who is not fully ordained. It should be understood that the Blessed One causes this right grasping to arise.

Apica tesaṃ hatthacchinnādīnaṃ pabbajitānaṃ supabbajitabhāvadīpanatthaṃ, pabbajjābhāvāsaṅkānivāraṇatthañcettha pabbajjābhilāpo kato. Kathaṃ? “Na, bhikkhave, hatthacchinno pabbājetabbo”tiādinā paṭikkhepena, “pabbajitā supabbajitā”ti vuttaṭṭhānābhāvena ca tesaṃ pabbajjābhāvappasaṅkā bhaveyya. Yathā pasaṅkābhave, tathā pasaṅkaṃ ṭhapeyya. Khandhake upasampadaṃ sandhāya “hatthacchinno, bhikkhave, appatto osāraṇaṃ, tañce saṅgho osāreti, sosārito”tiādinā nayena bhagavā nivāreti. Teneva pana nayena pabbajitā te sabbepi supabbajitā evāti dīpeti, aññathā sabbepete upasampannāva honti, na pabbajitāti ayamaniṭṭhappasaṅgo āpajjati. Kathaṃ? “Hatthacchinno, bhikkhave, na pabbājetabbo, pabbajito nāsetabbo”ti vā “na, bhikkhave, hatthacchinno pabbājetabbo, yo pabbājeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa, so [M 0.0437] ca apabbajito”ti vā tantiyā ṭhapitāya campeyyakkhandhake “sosārito”ti vuttattā kevalaṃ “ime hatthacchinnādayo upasampannāva honti, na pabbajitā”ti vā “upasampannāpi ce pabbajitā, nāsetabbā”ti vā aniṭṭhakoṭṭhāso āpajjatīti adhippāyo.

Moreover, here the expression 'going forth' is used for the purpose of clarifying that those with severed hands and the like who have gone forth are indeed well-gone-forth, and for the purpose of dispelling any doubt that their going forth is invalid. How so? Due to the prohibition, 'Monks, one with a severed hand is not to be given the going forth,' and because there is no passage where it is stated, 'Those who have gone forth are well-gone-forth,' a doubt that their going forth is invalid could arise. In the Khandhaka, with reference to higher ordination, the Blessed One prevents it by the method beginning with, 'Monks, one with a severed hand has not reached reinstatement. If the Sangha reinstates him, he is well-reinstated.' By that very same method, however, it is clarified that all those who have gone forth are indeed well-gone-forth. Otherwise, this undesirable consequence would arise: that all these are only higher-ordained, not gone-forth. How so? If the canonical text were established as, 'Monks, one with a severed hand is not to be given the going forth; one who has gone forth is to be expelled,' or as, 'Monks, one with a severed hand is not to be given the going forth; whoever should give the going forth commits an offense of wrong-doing, and he is not one who has gone forth,' then, because it is said in the Campeyyakkhandhaka, 'he is well-reinstated,' the following undesirable alternative would arise: either 'these with severed hands and so on are only higher-ordained, not gone-forth,' or 'even if higher-ordained, if they have gone forth, they are to be expelled.' This is the intention.

Idaṃ panettha vicāretabbaṃ – “so ca apabbajito”ti vacanābhāvato mūgassa pabbajjasiddhippasaṅgato pabbajjāpi ekatosuddhiyā hotīti ayamaniṭṭhakoṭṭhāso kathaṃ nāpajjatīti? Pabbajjābhilāpena upasampadā idhādhippetāti sammāgāhena nāpajjati, aññathā yathābyañjanaṃ atthe gahite yathāpaññattadukkaṭābhāvasaṅkhāto aparopi aniṭṭhakoṭṭhāso āpajjati. Kathaṃ? “Na, bhikkhave, mūgo pabbājetabbo, yo pabbājeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti vuttadukkaṭaṃ pabbajjapariyosāne hoti, na tassāvippakatāya. Pubbapayogadukkaṭameva hi paṭhamaṃ āpajjati[V 0.0400], tasmā mūgassa pabbajjapariyosānasseva abhāvato imassa dukkaṭassa okāso ca sabbakālaṃ na sambhaveyya. Upasampadāvasena pana atthe gahite sambhavati kammanipphattito. Teneva pāḷiyaṃ “na, bhikkhave, paṇḍako upasampādetabbo, yo upasampādeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti dukkaṭaṃ na paññattaṃ. Apaññattattā pubbapayogadukkaṭameva cettha sambhavati, netaraṃ, ettāvatā siddhametaṃ “pabbajjābhilāpena upasampadā ca tattha adhippetā, na pabbajjā”ti.

Herein, this should be considered: Since there is no statement 'and he is not one who has gone forth,' and because it would follow that the going-forth of a mute person is invalid, how does this undesirable consequence—that the going-forth is also by one-sided purity—not arise? It does not arise due to the correct understanding that here, by the expression 'going forth,' higher ordination is intended. Otherwise, if the meaning is taken literally, another undesirable consequence arises, namely the non-existence of the prescribed dukkaṭa offense. How so? The dukkaṭa offense stated as, 'Monks, a mute person should not be given the going-forth; whoever should give the going-forth incurs an offense of dukkaṭa,' occurs at the conclusion of the going-forth, not before its completion. For indeed, only the dukkaṭa of the preliminary effort is incurred first. Therefore, since for a mute person there is no completion of the going-forth, there would never be any occasion for this dukkaṭa offense. However, when the meaning is taken in the sense of higher ordination, it is possible, because of the completion of the formal act. For that very reason, in the Pāli, a dukkaṭa for the completed act is not prescribed with the words: 'Monks, a eunuch should not be given higher ordination; whoever gives one higher ordination incurs an offense of dukkaṭa.' Because it is not so prescribed, only the dukkaṭa of the preliminary effort is possible here, not the other. By this much, this is established: 'By the expression "going forth," higher ordination is also intended there, not the going-forth itself.'

Etthāha – sāmaṇerapabbajjā na kāyapayogato hotīti kathaṃ paññāyatīti? Vuccate – kāyena viññāpetītiādittikādassanato. Hoti cettha –

Here it is asked: 'How is it known that the going-forth as a novice is not accomplished by bodily effort?' It is said: It is known because the Tika beginning with 'He makes known by the body' is not seen. And there is here:

“Appeva sasako koci, patiṭṭheyya mahaṇṇave;

Na tveva catugambhīre, duggāho vinayaṇṇave”ti.

Perhaps some small hare might find a footing in the great ocean; but never in the fourfold-deep, hard-to-fathom ocean of the Vinaya.

Brahmujugattoti ettha “niddosatthe, seṭṭhatthe ca brahma-saddaṃ gahetvā niddosaṃ hutvā uju gattaṃ yassa so brahmujugatto”ti likhitaṃ. Atha vā kāmabhogittā devindādayo upamāvasena aggahetvā brahmā viya ujugatto brahmujugatto. Mahākucchito ghaṭo mahākucchighaṭo. Tena samāno vuccati “mahākucchighaṭasadiso”ti. Galagaṇḍīti desanāmattamevetanti kathaṃ paññāyatīti? “Na, bhikkhave, pañcahi ābādhehi phuṭṭho pabbājetabbo”ti [M 0.0438] vacanato. Kilāsopi idhādhippetoti na kevalaṃ so eveko, kintu pañcahi ābādhehi phuṭṭho, pāḷiyaṃ āgatā rājabhaṭādayo dāsapariyosānā, rāhulavatthumhi āgatā ananuññātamātāpitaro cāti dasapi janā idhādhippetā. Tadatthadīpanatthameva likhitakakasāhatalakkhaṇāhate pubbe vuttepi ānetvā upālitthero idha hatthacchinnapāḷiyaṃ āha. Teneva campeyyakkhandhake “atthi, bhikkhave, puggalo appatto osāraṇaṃ, tañce saṅgho osāreti, ekacco sosārito, ekacco dosārito”ti (mahāva. 396) imassa vibhaṅge “pañcahi ābādhehi phuṭṭhā, rājabhaṭā, corakārabhedakaiṇāyikadāsā, ananuññātamātāpitaro cā”ti satta janā na gahitā, na ca labbhanti, aññathā imepi tassa vibhaṅge vattabbā siyuṃ. Na vattabbā tattha abhabbattāti ce? Evaṃ sante “saṅgho osāreti, ekacco dosārito”ti imassa vibhaṅge vattabbā paṇḍakādayo viya, na ca vuttā. Ubhayattha avuttattā na cime anubhayā bhavitumarahanti, tasmā avuttānameva dasannaṃ yathāvuttānaṃ saṅgaṇhanatthaṃ puna likhitakādayo vuttāti. Atha kimatthaṃ te idha uppaṭipāṭiyā vuttāti? Iṇāyikadāsānaṃ sosāritabhāvepi iṇāyikadāsā sāmikānaṃ dātabbāti [V 0.0401] tadadhīnabhāvadassanatthaṃ. Teneva tattha vuttaṃ “palātopi ānetvā dātabbo”tiādi. Yo panettha coro katakammo pabbajati, rājabhaṭo vā sace katadoso, iṇāyikaggahaṇeneva gahitoti veditabbo. Atha vā yathāvuttalakkhaṇo sabbopi iṇāyikadāsānaṃ “sosārito”ti vattabbāraho na hotīti katvā tesaṃ parivajjanatthaṃ uppaṭipāṭiyā desanā upari ārohati, na heṭṭhāti dīpanato. Likhitako “sosārito”ti vuttattā desantaraṃ netabbo. Tathākārabhedakādayopīti veditabbaṃ.

Here, regarding 'Brahmujugatta,' it is written: 'Taking the word "brahma" in the sense of faultlessness and excellence, one whose body is faultless and straight is "Brahmujugatta."' Alternatively, not taking the lord of devas and others who enjoy sensual pleasures as a comparison, one whose body is straight like a Brahmā is 'Brahmujugatta.' A pot with a large belly is a 'mahākucchighaṭa.' One who is similar to it is called 'mahākucchighaṭasadisa.' Regarding 'Galagaṇḍī' (goiter) being merely a designation, how is this known? From the statement: 'Monks, one afflicted by the five ailments should not be given the going forth.' Because kilāsa (a skin disease) is also intended here, it is not only that one case, but rather: one afflicted by the five ailments; those mentioned in the Pāḷi, from royal servants down to slaves; and those mentioned in the story of Rāhula, whose parents have not given permission—thus, all ten types of people are intended here. For the very purpose of clarifying that meaning, the Elder Upāli, even though the branded criminal, the one who has been flogged, and the one who has been marked were mentioned before, brought them up again and spoke of them here in the Pāḷi passage concerning one with a severed hand. For that very reason, in the Campeyya Khandhaka, in the analysis of the statement: 'Monks, there is a person who has not reached rehabilitation. If the Saṅgha rehabilitates him, one is well-rehabilitated, another is badly-rehabilitated,' the seven types of persons—those afflicted by the five ailments, royal servants, thieves, prison-breakers, debtors, slaves, and those whose parents have not given permission—are not included, nor are they found there. Otherwise, these too should have been mentioned in its analysis. If it is said, 'They should not be mentioned there because they are incapable,' in that case, they should have been mentioned in the analysis of 'the Saṅgha rehabilitates... one is badly-rehabilitated,' just like the eunuchs and others, but they were not mentioned. Since they are not mentioned in either place, these persons should not be considered as belonging to neither category. Therefore, to include the ten aforementioned persons who were not mentioned, the branded criminals and others are mentioned again. Now, for what reason are they mentioned here out of order? To show that even if debtors and slaves are well-rehabilitated, they must be given to their masters, thus demonstrating their dependent status. For that very reason, it is said there: 'Even if he has run away, he must be brought back and given over,' and so on. Here, whichever thief, having committed a theft, goes forth, or a royal servant, if he has committed an offense, he is to be understood as included simply under the category of 'debtor.' Alternatively, because no debtor or slave with the aforementioned characteristics is worthy of being called 'well-rehabilitated,' the teaching ascends out of order for the purpose of avoiding them, and does not descend—this is what is indicated. Because the branded criminal is said to be 'well-rehabilitated,' he should be taken to another country. Likewise for the prison-breakers and others; thus it should be understood.

Ettāvatā bhagavatā attano desanākusalatāya pubbe gahitaggahaṇena yathāvuttānaṃ dasannampi pabbajjupasampadākammanipphatti, uppaṭipāṭivacanena puggalavemattatañca desanāya kovidānaṃ dīpitaṃ hotīti veditabbaṃ. Hoti cettha –

Thus, it should be known that by this much, the Blessed One, due to his own skill in teaching, has illuminated for those skilled in the teaching—by not stating what has already been stated previously—the completion of the acts of going forth and higher ordination for all ten persons as mentioned, and—by stating them out of order—the diversity of individuals. And here there is this:

“Vattabbayuttaṃ vacanena vatvā, ayuttamiṭṭhaṃ nayadesanāya;

Sandīpayantaṃ sugatassa vākyaṃ, cittaṃ vicittaṃva karotipī”ti.

Having spoken with words what is suitable to be spoken, and illuminating by the method of teaching what is desired though unsuitable to be spoken, the speech of the Well-farer indeed creates great wonder.

Etthāha [M 0.0439] – campeyyakkhandhake ūnavīsativasso ubhayattha avuttattā anubhayo siyāti? Na siyā avuttattā eva. Yadi hi tatiyāya koṭiyā bhavitabbaṃ, sā avassaṃ bhagavatā vattabbāva hoti, na ca vuttā, tasmā na so anubhayo hoti. Atha kataraṃ pakkhaṃ bhajatīti? Dosāritapakkhaṃ bhajati. Atha kasmā na vuttoti? Sikkhāpadena paṭisiddhattā. Upanāhaṃ bandhitvāti puna bandhanaṃ katvā. “Nānāvidhehi osadhehi pādaṃ bandhitvā āvāṭake pavesetvā kattabbavidhānassetaṃ adhivacana”nti likhitaṃ. Kappasīso vā hatthī viya. Gobhattanāḷikā nāma gunnaṃ bhattapānatthaṃ katanāḷikā. Upakkamukho nāma kudhitamukho vuccati, vātaṇḍiko nāma aṇḍakesu vuḍḍhirogena samannāgato. Vikaṭo nāma tiriyaṃ gamanakapādehi samannāgato. “Guṇi kuṇī”ti duvidho kira pāṭho. Yesañca pabbajjā paṭikkhittā, upasampadāpi tesaṃ paṭikkhittāvātiādi yasmā hatthacchinnādayo upasampadāvaseneva vuttā, tasmā te eva hatthacchinnādayo sandhāyāha.

Here, one asks: 'In the Campeyyakkhandhaka, since one who is under twenty years of age is not mentioned in either case, might they belong to neither category?' It could not be, precisely because of not being mentioned. For if there were to be a third category, it would surely have been stated by the Blessed One, but it was not stated. Therefore, that person does not belong to neither category. Then to which side do they belong? They belong to the side of those not to be admitted. Then why were they not mentioned? Because it is prohibited by the training rule. Regarding 'having bound a poultice,' it means having applied a binding again. It is written: 'This is a designation for the procedure to be done by binding the foot with various kinds of medicines and placing it in a pit.' Or one with a flat head (kappasīso), like an elephant. Gobhattanāḷikā is the name for a tube made for the food and drink of cattle. Upakkamukho is said to be one with an inflamed mouth. Vātaṇḍiko is the name for one afflicted with a disease of swelling in the testicles. Vikaṭo is the name for one endowed with feet that go sideways. It is said that there is a twofold reading: 'guṇi' and 'kuṇī'. Regarding the text beginning, 'And for those whose going forth is rejected, their higher ordination is also rejected': since those with severed hands and so on were mentioned only in connection with higher ordination, therefore it was said referring to those very ones with severed hands and so on.

Hatthacchinnādivatthukathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the story concerning those with severed hands and so forth is concluded.

Alajjīnissayavatthukathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Story of Dependence on the Shameless

120. “Na[V 0.0402], bhikkhave, alajjīnaṃ nissayo dātabbo”ti iminā alajjīhi bhikkhūhi, sāmaṇerehi vā saddhiṃ dvepi dhammāmisaparibhogā paṭikkhittā honti nissayabhāve bhāvato tesaṃ. Yathāha “ācariyena, bhikkhave, antevāsiko saṅgahetabbo anuggahetabbo uddesena paripucchāya ovādena anusāsaniyā”tiādi (mahāva. 79) upajjhāyassapi nissayappaṇāmanasambhavato, sopi saddhivihārikassa nissayoti veditabbaṃ, tasmā upajjhāyo ce alajjī hoti, na taṃ nissāya vasitabbanti siddhaṃ hoti. Bhikkhūnaṃ sammāpaṭipattiyā samānabhāgo bhikkhu sabhāgo. Tassabhāvo bhikkhusabhāgatā. Taṃ bhikkhusabhāgataṃ. Yāva jānāmīti adhippāyena vasituṃ vaṭṭati. Bhikkhūhi sabhāgataṃ. Kiṃ taṃ? Lajjibhāvaṃ. “Sattāhaṃ…pe… gahetabbo”ti ettha “sattāhamattaṃ vasissāmi, kiṃ bhikkhusabhāgatājānanenāti [M 0.0440] jānane dhuraṃ nikkhipitvā vasituṃ na labhatīti attho”ti likhitaṃ. “Bhikkhusabhāgataṃ pana jānanto sveva gamissāmi, kiṃ me nissayārocanenā”ti aruṇaṃ uṭṭhapetuṃ na labhati. “Pure aruṇaṃ uṭṭhahitvā gamissāmī”ti ābhogena sayantassa ce aruṇo uggacchati, vaṭṭati.

120. By this statement, 'Monks, dependence should not be given to the shameless,' both kinds of sharing—of the Dhamma and of material requisites—are prohibited with shameless monks or novices, because if they are in a state of dependence, it leads to a shameless state. Just as it is said: 'A teacher, monks, should gather and support a pupil with teaching, questioning, advice, and instruction,' etc. (Mahāvagga 79). Since it is possible to terminate dependence even on a preceptor, he too should be understood as a source of dependence for his co-resident. Therefore, it is established that if the preceptor is shameless, one should not live in dependence on him. A monk who has an equal share in the right practice of monks is a `sabhāga` (one of a similar kind). The state of that is `bhikkhusabhāgatā` (the state of being of a similar kind to monks). It is permissible to dwell with the intention of getting to know that `bhikkhusabhāgatā`. What is that which is shared by monks? The state of having moral shame. In the passage 'For seven days... he should be taken...' it is written: 'The meaning is that one is not allowed to stay having set aside the burden of knowing, thinking, "I will stay for only seven days; what is the use of knowing the `bhikkhusabhāgatā`?"' However, knowing the `bhikkhusabhāgatā`, one is not allowed to let dawn break with the thought, 'I will leave tomorrow; what need is there for me to announce dependence?' If, for one who is sleeping with the intention, 'I will get up before dawn and leave,' the dawn should rise, it is permissible.

Gamikādinissayavatthukathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourse on the Basis for Dependence, Beginning with Travelers

121. “Addhānamaggappaṭipannena bhikkhunā nissayaṃ alabhamānena anissitena vatthunti avassakāleyeva vassakāle addhānagamanassa pāḷiyaṃyeva paṭikkhittattā”ti vuttaṃ, taṃ appamāṇaṃ sattāhaṃ vassacchedādivasena addhānagamanasambhavato, gacchantasseva vassakālagamanasambhavato ca. Antarāmagge…pe… anāpattīti nissayadāyakābhāveyeva. “Tassa nissāyā”ti pāṭhānurūpaṃ vuttaṃ, taṃ nissāyāti attho. “Yadā patirūpo nissayadāyako āgacchissatī”ti vacanena ayaṃ vidhi avassakāle evāti siddhaṃ. “Antovasse pana kassaci āgamanābhāvā”ti vuttaṃ. Sace so jalapaṭṭane vā thalapaṭṭane vā vasanto vassūpanāyikāya āsannāya gantukāmo suṇāti “asuko mahāthero āgamissatī”ti, taṃ ce āgameti, vaṭṭati. Āgamentasseva ce vassūpanāyikadivaso hoti, hotu, gantabbaṃ tattha, yattha nissayadāyakaṃ labhatīti. Pātimokkhuddesakābhāvena ce gantuṃ vaṭṭati, pageva nissayadāyakābhāvena. Sace so gacchanto jīvitantarāyaṃ, brahmacariyantarāyaṃ vā passati, tattheva vasitabbanti eke.

121. It is said: “For a monk traveling on a long road who cannot obtain dependence and is without support, it is allowable only in the non-rains season, because traveling on a long road during the rains season is prohibited in the Pāḷi itself.” That statement is not authoritative, because travel for up to seven days is possible by way of breaking the rains-residence, etc., and because traveling during the rains season is possible for one who is already going. In “Along the way… no offense,” this applies only in the absence of a giver of dependence. The phrase “tassa nissāya” is stated in accordance with the reading; the meaning is “relying on him.” The statement, “When a suitable giver of dependence will arrive,” establishes that this rule applies only in the non-rains season. It is said: “But during the rains-residence, there is no arrival of anyone.” If he, while staying at a river port or a land port, intending to go as the rains-residence approaches, hears, “Such-and-such a great elder will come,” and if he awaits that elder, it is allowable. Even if the day of entering the rains-residence arrives while he is awaiting him, so be it; he should go to that place where he can obtain a giver of dependence. If it is allowable to go due to the absence of a Pātimokkha reciter, how much more so due to the absence of a giver of dependence. If, while going, he sees a danger to his life or a danger to the holy life, some say he should stay right there.

122. “Nāhaṃ [V 0.0403] ussahāmi therassa nāmaṃ gahetu”nti itthannāmo itthannāmassa āyasmatoti lakkhaṇato āha. “Gottenāpī’ti vacanato yena vohārena vohariyanti, tena vaṭṭatīti siddhaṃ, tasmā ‘ko nāmo te upajjhāyo’ti puṭṭhenāpi gottameva nāmaṃ katvā vattabbanti siddhaṃ hoti, tasmā catubbidhesu nāmesu yena kenaci nāmena anussāvanā kātabbā”ti vadanti. Ekassa bahūni nāmāni honti, tattha ekaṃ nāmaṃ ñattiyā, ekaṃ anussāvanāya kātuṃ na vaṭṭati, atthato, byañjanato ca abhinnāhi anussāvanāhi bhavitabbanti. Katthaci “āyasmato buddharakkhitattherassā”ti vatvā katthaci kevalaṃ “buddharakkhitassā”ti [M 0.0441] sāveti, “sāvanaṃ hāpetī”ti na vuccati nāmassa ahāpitattāti eke. Sace katthaci “āyasmato buddharakkhitassā”ti vatvā katthaci “buddharakkhitassāyasmato”ti sāveti, pāṭhānurūpattā khettameva otiṇṇantipi eke. Byañjanabhedappasaṅgato anussāvane taṃ na vaṭṭatīti eke. Sace pana sabbaṭṭhānepi tatheva vadati, vaṭṭati bhagavatā dinnalakkhaṇānurūpattā. Lakkhaṇavirodhato aññathā na vaṭṭatīti ce? Na, payogānurūpattā. Tattha tathā, idha aññathā payogoti ce? Na, vipattilakkhaṇānaṃ virodhato. Na sabbena sabbaṃ, sāvanāhāpanā eva hi pāḷiyaṃ tadatthavibhāvane āgatāti aññapadesu sāvanesu parihāro na sambhavati āciṇṇakappavirodhato. Sopi kiṃpamāṇanti ce? Pamāṇaṃ ācariyuggahassa pamāṇattā.

122. He said, “I do not presume to take the elder’s name,” because of the characteristic “the venerable one of such-and-such a name.” Because of the Pāḷi text “By clan as well,” it is established that it is proper to use whatever designation they are called by. Therefore, it is established that even when asked, “What is the name of your preceptor?” one should answer by using the clan name as the name. Therefore, they say that among the four kinds of names, the announcement should be made using any name whatsoever. One person may have many names; in such a case, it is not proper to use one name for the motion and another for the announcement, for the announcements must be identical in meaning and in wording. In some instances, one might say, “of the venerable elder Buddharakkhita,” while in others simply announcing, “of Buddharakkhita.” Some say this is not called “omitting the announcement,” since the name itself is not omitted. If in one instance one says, “of the venerable Buddharakkhita,” and in another announces, “of Buddharakkhita the venerable,” some hold that this pertains only to the text itself, as it conforms to the reading. Some say that this is not proper in an announcement because of the consequence of a difference in wording. But if one speaks in that same way in all instances, it is proper, as it conforms to the characteristic given by the Blessed One. If one should say that to do otherwise is not proper because it contradicts the characteristic? It is not so; it is proper because it conforms to usage. If one should say, “There the usage is thus, but here it is otherwise”? That should not be said, because it would contradict the characteristics of failure. This is not so in every respect, for indeed, only the omission of the announcement is mentioned in the Pāḷi when clarifying its meaning. Therefore, in other instances of announcements, an omission is not possible, as it would contradict established custom. And if one should ask, “What is the standard for that custom?” It is what is learned from the teacher, for that is the standard.

123. Dve ekānussāvaneti ettha gaṇṭhipade tāva evaṃ likhitaṃ “ekato pavattaanussāvane”. Idaṃ sandhāyāti nānupajjhāyaṃ ekācariyaṃ anussāvanakiriyaṃ sandhāya, tañca anussāvanakiriyaṃ ekenupajjhāyena nānācariyehi anujānāmīti attho. Nānupajjhāyehi ekenācariyena na tveva anujānāmīti atthoti. Porāṇagaṇṭhipadepi tatheva vatvā “tiṇṇaṃ uddhaṃ na kenaci ākārena ekato vaṭṭatī”ti vuttaṃ, taṃ yuttaṃ, na hi saṅgho saṅghassa kammaṃ karotīti ācariyo. Idaṃ panettha cintetabbaṃ. Kathaṃ? Cattāro vā atirekā vā upasampadāpekkhā saṅghavohāraṃ na labhanti bhikkhubhāvaṃ appattattā. Kevalaṃ bhagavatā paricchinditvā “tayo”ti vuttattā tato uddhaṃ na vaṭṭatīti no takkoti ācariyo. Anugaṇṭhipadepi ayamevattho bahudhā vicāretvā vutto. Tathā andhakaṭṭhakathāyampi. Na sabbattha imasmiṃ atthavikappe matibhedo atthi. Yā panesā ubho paripuṇṇavīsativassā, ubhinnamekupajjhāyo, ekācariyo, ekā kammavācā, eko upasampanno, eko anupasampannoti parivārakathā, taṃ dassetvā eko ce ācariyo dvinnaṃ, tiṇṇaṃ vā upasampadāpekkhānaṃ ekaṃ kammavācaṃ ekenupajjhāyena sāveti, vaṭṭatīti eke. Taṃ ayuttaṃ, na hi sakkā sithiladhanitādibyañjanalakkhaṇasampannaṃ tasmiṃ khaṇe kammavācaṃ dassetuṃ vimuttadosādīsu patanato[V 0.0404]. Visuṃ visuṃ karaṇaṃ sandhāya idaṃ vuttanti dīpanatthaṃ “tayo paripuṇṇavīsativassā[M 0.0442], tiṇṇamekupajjhāyo, ekācariyo, ekā kammavācā, dve upasampannā, eko anupasampanno”ti na vutto. Evañhi vutte sakkā tīsu ākāsaṭṭhamapanetvā sīmaṭṭhānaṃ dvinnamanurūpaṃ kammavācaṃ dassetuṃ, tamaniṭṭhappasaṅgaṃ nivāretuṃ “ubho”ti vuttaṃ. “Tattha paripuṇṇavīsativassavacanena vatthusampatti, parisāya padhānattā, ācariyupajjhāyavacanena parisasampatti, kammavācāya anussāvanasampatti dassitā, sīmasampatti evekā na dassitā. Tato vipatti jātā kammavācānaṃ nānākkhaṇikattā. Ekakkhaṇabhāve sati ubhinnaṃ sampatti vā siyā vipatti vā, na ekasseva sampatti ekassa vipattīti sambhavati vimuttādibyañjanadosappasaṅgato”ti vuttaṃ, taṃ vacanaṃ ubhopi cete sīmagatāva honti, ubhinnaṃ ekato kammasampattidīpanato dvinnaṃ ekato anussāvanaṃ ekena upajjhāyena ekenācariyena vaṭṭatīti sādheti. Dvinnaṃ, tiṇṇañca ekato sasamanubhāsanā ca pāḷiyaṃyeva dassitā, tañca anulometi. Aṭṭhakathācariyehi nānuññātaṃ, na paṭikkhittaṃ, vicāretvā gahetabbanti ācariyo, taṃ dhammatāya virujjhati.

123. In the phrase 'two proclamations as one' (dve ekānussāvane), it is written thus in the Gaṇṭhipada: 'in a proclamation that proceeds as one.' This is said in reference to the act of proclamation for those with various preceptors and one teacher; and the meaning is that I allow that act of proclamation by one preceptor and various teachers. The meaning is that I certainly do not allow it by various preceptors with one teacher. Also in the ancient Gaṇṭhipada, having stated in the same way, it is said: 'Beyond three, it is not allowable to do it together in any way.' That is correct, for indeed the Saṅgha does not perform an act for the Saṅgha, says the teacher. Herein, this should be considered. How? Four or more ordination candidates do not obtain the designation 'Saṅgha' because they have not attained the state of a bhikkhu. Merely because the Blessed One, having defined it, said 'three,' it is not allowable beyond that—this is our reasoning, says the teacher. Also in the Anugaṇṭhipada, this very meaning is stated after being examined in many ways. Likewise in the Andhaka-aṭṭhakathā. In all these, there is no difference of opinion in this alternative meaning. But as for that discussion from the Parivāra—'Both are of fully twenty years, for both there is one preceptor, one teacher, one kammavācā; one is ordained, one is not ordained'—having presented that, some say: 'If one teacher, with one preceptor, makes two or three ordination candidates hear one kammavācā, it is allowable.' That is improper, for it is not possible at that moment to recite a kammavācā endowed with the correct consonantal features, such as lax and aspirated sounds, because of falling into faults such as vimutta. To clarify that this was said with reference to performing it separately for each, it was not stated as: 'Three of fully twenty years, for the three one preceptor, one teacher, one kammavācā, two are ordained, one is not ordained.' For if it were stated thus, it would be possible, having removed from the three the one standing in the open space, to present a suitable kammavācā for the two standing in the boundary. To prevent that undesirable consequence, 'both' was said. 'Therein, by the statement 'of fully twenty years', the perfection of the individual is shown; because of the prominence of the assembly, by the statement of 'teacher' and 'preceptor', the perfection of the assembly is shown; by the kammavācā, the perfection of the proclamation is shown. Only the perfection of the boundary is not shown. From that, a failure arises because the kammavācās are at different moments. If they are at the same moment, there would be either perfection or failure for both; it is not possible that there is perfection for one and failure for the other, because of the liability of faults in consonants such as vimutta,' it is said. That statement establishes that if both of these candidates are indeed within the boundary, a proclamation for two together by one preceptor and one teacher is allowable, because it shows the perfection of the act for both together. And the joint admonition for two and three is shown in the Pāḷi itself, and this ruling conforms to that. The teacher says: 'It was not allowed by the commentary teachers, nor was it rejected; it should be accepted after investigation.' That statement contradicts the nature of the Dhamma.

Ayañhi buddhānaṃ dhammatā – yadidaṃ yattha yattha vacananānattamatthi, tattha tattha garukesu ṭhānesu vattabbayuttaṃ vadanti. Dūtena upasampadādayo cettha nidassanaṃ. Yasmā cettha pubbe anuññātakammavācāya nānattaṃ natthi, tasmā “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, dve tayo ekānussāvane kātu”nti vatvā “evañca pana, bhikkhave, kātabbo”ti na vuttaṃ. Nānatte satipi tattha tattha dvinnaṃ, bahūnaṃ vā vasena vuttakammavācānusārena gahetabbato avuttanti ce? Na hi lahukesu ṭhānesu vatvā garukesu avacanaṃ dhammatāti ācariyo. Aññatarasmiṃ pana gaṇṭhipade evaṃ papañcitaṃ dve ekānussāvaneti dve ekato anussāvane. “Ekena” iti pāṭho, ekena ācariyenāti attho. Purimanayenevāti “ekena vā dvīhi vā ācariyehī”ti vuttanayena eva, tasmā ekenācariyena dve vā tayo vā anussāvetabbā. “Dvīhi vā tīhi vā”ti pāṭho. Nānācariyā nānupajjhāyāti ettha “tañca kho ekena upajjhāyena, na tveva nānupajjhāyenā”ti vuttattā na vaṭṭatīti ce? Vaṭṭati. Kathaṃ? Ekena anussāvane ekānussāvaneti viggahassa pākaṭattā līnameva dassetuṃ “ekato anussāvane”ti viggahova vutto, tasmā ujukattameva sandhāya [M 0.0443] tañca kho ekena anussāvanaṃ ekānussāvanaṃ, ekena upajjhāyena anujānāmi, na tveva nānupajjhāyenāti attho. Idaṃ sandhāya hi dvidhā viggaho, tasmā “nānācariyehi nānupajjhāyā na vaṭṭantīti siddhamevā”ti aññathāpi vadanti. Tañca kho ekena upajjhāyena ekassa upajjhāyassa vā vattabbaṃ anussāvanaṃ, na tveva nānupajjhāyena anujānāmīti attho. Kiṃ vuttaṃ hoti? “Eko ācariyo, dve vā tayo vā upasampadāpekkhā [V 0.0405] dvinnaṃ tiṇṇaṃ vā upajjhāyānaṃ na tveva anujānāmī”ti kira vuttanti. Aparasmiṃ pana gaṇṭhipade “ekena anussāvaneti viggahassa pākaṭattā taṃ pakāsetuṃ ‘ekenā’ti vuttaṃ. Evaṃ vutte avassaṃ paṇḍitā jānanti. Taṃpākaṭattā ce jānanti, ekenāti iminā kinti ce? Kiñcāpi jānanti, vivādo pana hoti aladdhalesattā, jānituñca na sakkā, ‘ekenā’ti vutte pana taṃ sabbaṃ na hotīti vutta”nti likhitaṃ. Evaṃ ettha aneke ācariyā ca takkikā ca anekadhā papañcenti, taṃ sabbaṃ suṭṭhu upaparikkhitvā garukulaṃ payirupāsitvā vaṃsānugatova attho gahetabbo. “Na sabbattha imasmiṃ atthavikappe matibhedo atthī”ti vuttameva.

Indeed, this is the nature of the Buddhas: wherever there is a variation in wording, in those very places, they speak what is fit to be said in weighty matters. Higher ordination by a messenger and so forth are an example in this matter. And because in this matter there was previously no variation in the authorized formal act, therefore, having said, 'Monks, I allow a single proclamation to be performed for two or three,' it was not said, 'And thus, monks, it should be done.' If one were to say: 'Even when there is a variation, it was not stated because it should be understood in each case according to the formal act already spoken for two or for many'? For it is not the nature of things to speak on minor matters and not speak on weighty ones, says the teacher. However, in a certain glossary, it is elaborated thus: 'two in a single proclamation' means 'two together in the proclamation.' There is the reading 'by one,' and the meaning is 'by one teacher.' By 'according to the previous method' is meant the method stated as 'by one or by two teachers'; therefore, two or three should be proclaimed by one teacher. There is the reading 'or by two or by three.' If one were to say: 'Regarding different teachers and different preceptors, this is not allowable because it was stated, "And that, indeed, by one preceptor, but not by different preceptors"'? It is allowable. How? Because the analysis of 'a single proclamation' as 'by one proclamation' is clear, the analysis 'together in the proclamation' was stated merely to show the hidden meaning. Therefore, referring only to the straightforward meaning, the meaning is: 'And that proclamation by one is a single proclamation; I allow it by one preceptor, but not by different preceptors.' Indeed, with this meaning in mind, the analysis was stated in two ways. Therefore, others also say, 'Thus it is established that different teachers and different preceptors are not allowable.' And that, by one preceptor, means: 'The proclamation that should be recited is for one preceptor; I do not allow it by different preceptors.' This is the meaning. What is meant by this? It is reportedly said: 'One teacher for two or three candidates for higher ordination of two or three preceptors—this I do not allow.' However, in another glossary, it is written: 'Because the analysis "by one proclamation" is clear, to clarify that meaning, "by one" was stated. When it is stated thus, the wise certainly understand. If they understand because its meaning is clear, what is the use of this "by one"? Although they know, there is still dispute because a basis for argument has not been obtained, and it cannot be known for certain. But when "by one" is stated, all that does not happen. Thus it is said.' Thus, regarding this text, many teachers and logicians elaborate in many ways. Having thoroughly investigated all that, and having attended upon a venerable lineage of teachers, only the meaning that follows the tradition should be accepted. It should not be accepted in every case, for it has indeed been said: 'In this alternative interpretation, there is a difference of opinion.'

Upasampadāvidhikathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Procedure for Higher Ordination

125. Kuṭṭhaṃ gaṇḍoti ettha kuṭṭhādiggahaṇena hatthacchinnādayopi gahitāva hontīti porāṇā, tasmā “manussosi purisosī”ti etehi bhabbābhabbapuggalaparivajjanaṃ karoti. “Bhujissosi aṇaṇosī”tiādīhi pubbe hatthacchinnādhikāre vuttaatthavikappesu dutiyaṃ vikappaṃ upathambheti. Tattha “aṇaṇosi bhujissosī”ti anukkamena avatvā uppaṭipāṭiyā vacanena bhujisso hoti, na ca rañño bhattavetanavasena bhaṭo. Rājādhīnattā pana so rājabhaṭapakkhaṃ bhajatīti tabbipakkhabhāvapucchanatthaṃ “nasi rājabhaṭo”ti vuttaṃ. Aññathā pañcahi ābādhehi phuṭṭhānaṃ gahaṇeneva sabbesaṃ gahaṇe siddhe itare na vattabbā. Atha vattabbā, sabbepi vattabbā siyuṃ.

125. Here, the ancients say that by the inclusion of 'leprosy, boils,' and so forth, those with severed hands and the like are also included. Therefore, with these phrases, 'Are you a human being? Are you a male?,' he excludes fit and unfit persons. With phrases such as 'Are you a freeman? Are you not in debt?,' he supports the second of the alternative interpretations of meaning stated previously in the section on those with severed hands. There, the reason for not saying in sequence, 'Are you not in debt? Are you a freeman?,' but speaking out of order, is this: he is a freeman, and not a servant by way of the king's food and wages. However, because he is subject to the king, he sides with the king's servants; thus, to ask about his not being a king's servant, it is said, 'Are you not a king's servant?'. Otherwise, when the inclusion of all is accomplished just by the inclusion of those afflicted with the five diseases, the others should not be stated. If they are to be stated, then all should be stated.

Cattāronissayādikathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Four Requisites and Related Topics

128-9. “Tāvadeva chāyā metabbā”tiādi “bhikkhūnaṃ pāde vandāpetvā”ti vacanato therātherabhāvajānanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. “Cirena agamāsī”ti kira porāṇapāṭho, ciraṃ akāsīti catthi.

128-9. The phrase 'Only this much shade should be measured,' and so forth, is said for the purpose of knowing the state of being a senior or non-senior monk, because of the text, 'having caused homage to be paid at the feet of the monks.' It is said that 'He arrived after a long time' is an ancient reading; there is also the reading, 'He did for a long time.'

130. Anāpatti [M 0.0444] sambhoge saṃvāseti ukkhittakena saddhiṃ sambhogasaṃvāsapaccayā pācittiyāpatti paññattā, tato anāpattīti attho. Kathaṃ paññāyatīti? Saṃvāsaggahaṇe. Alajjinā saddhiṃ sambhogapaccayā āpajjitabbaṃ dukkaṭaṃ pana āpajjati eva, na saṃvāsapaccayā. Na hi alajjinā saddhiṃ saṃvāso paṭikkhitto. Saṃvāso panettha sahaseyyappahonake āvāse sahavāso, na “pārājiko hoti asaṃvāso”ti ettha vuttasaṃvāso. Ayaṃ saṃvāso ukkhittakena saddhiṃ na vaṭṭati. Alajjinā saddhiṃ ekacco vaṭṭati. Dhammasambhogavinimuttovetaro[V 0.0406]. Idaṃ pana “ukkhittako vibbhamī”tiādisuttaṃ imasmiṃ upasampādetabbānupasampādetabbadīpanasāmaññato vuttaṃ. Kiñca bhiyyo paṭipattikkamatova āpattito suddhi hoti, na vibbhamena, tasmā upasampanno bhikkhu antamaso dubbhāsitampi āpajjitvā aparabhāge vibbhamitvā āgato upasampajjati, taṃ āpattiṃ desetvāva sujjhati, na aññathāti upasampannassa suddhikkamadassanatthaṃ. Asādhāraṇāpattiyā adassanapaccayā ukkhittakassa liṅgaparivattanena āpattito vuṭṭhitassa puna ce pakatiliṅgamevuppajjati, nānāsaṃvāsakatāva, vibbhamitvā āgatepi yathāvuttanayeneva upasampādetvā na vuṭṭhitattāti ce? Na liṅgantarapātubhāvā. Na vibbhamena kammāsujjhanato. Na kammāsujjhane puna upasampadākammavipattippasaṅgato. Na ca kammavipatti, na ca kammapaṭippassaddhi. Vibbhamena ca anupasampanno nānāsaṃvāsakabhāvena kammaṃ kopeti dhammissarena āhacca bhāsitattā. Teneva “passissasī”ti anāgatavacanaṃ kataṃ. Tādiso pana gahaṭṭho nikkhittavattapārivāsiko viya pakatattabhūmiyaṃ vibbhamādinā anupasampannapakatiyaṃyeva tiṭṭhatīti imassa sabbassapi atthavikappassa dassanatthamidaṃ vuttanti veditabbaṃ. Pubbe vuttappakāro pana parivattitaliṅgo hutvā puna pakatiliṅge ṭhitaukkhittako puna pucchitabbo “passasī”ti. “Āma passāmī”ti vadanto osāretabbo. “Desehī”ti na vattabbo liṅgaparivattanena vuṭṭhitattā. Tappaṭikammo ukkhittako pucchitabbo “paṭikammaṃ kiṃ te kata”nti, “āma kata”nti vadanto osāretabbo. “Kattabbaṃ me paṭikammaṃ na hotī”ti vadanto na osāretabboti eke. Asādhāraṇāpattimhi idaṃ vidhānaṃ, na sādhāraṇāya. Tattha ukkhittako [M 0.0445] liṅgaparivattaneneva paṭippassaddhakammoti eke. Vicāretvā yuttataraṃ gahetabbanti ācariyo. Anugaṇṭhipade pana “alajjiparibhogo sahatthadānādivasena paricchinditabbo, ‘sāraṇīyadhammapūrakādayo dassetvā alajjissa sahatthā dātuṃ vaṭṭatī’ti vadantānaṃ vādo paṭisedhetabbo. Kathaṃ? Ukkhittakassa sahatthā dātuṃ na vaṭṭatīti vinicchayānusārena. Dāpetuṃ pana vaṭṭatevāti ca. Kiñcāpi alajjiparibhogavasena dukkaṭaṃ, atha kho ayaṃ alajjī na hoti, tasmā sabbākārena nirāpattitaṃ sandhāya ‘anāpatti sambhoge saṃvāse’ti vuttaṃ. Kathaṃ paññāyatīti? Viññeyyo atthato ucchurasakasaṭānaṃ sattāhakālikayāvajīvikattā ‘vaṭṭati vikāle ucchuṃ khāditu’nti saññaṃ uppādetvā taṃ khāditvā tappaccayā pācittiyaṃ na passati, vaṭṭatīti tathāsaññitāya. Yo vā pana āpattiṃ āpannabhāvaṃ paṭijānitvā ‘na paṭikaromī’ti abhinivisati, ime dve –

130. ‘No offense in communion and co-residence.’ A Pācittiya offense has been laid down on account of communion and co-residence with a suspended monk; the meaning is that from that [co-residence], there is no offense. How is this known? By the inclusion of ‘co-residence.’ However, one does incur a Dukkaṭa offense due to communion with one who is shameless, but not due to co-residence. For co-residence with a shameless person is not prohibited. Here, ‘co-residence’ refers to living together in a residence suitable for sleeping together, not the ‘co-residence’ spoken of in the phrase ‘he is defeated and there is no co-residence.’ This co-residence is not allowable with one who has been suspended. With a shameless person, a certain kind is allowable. The other [co-residence] is indeed exempt from communion in the Dhamma. However, this text beginning with ‘the suspended one disrobed’ is stated due to the commonality of explaining who should and should not be ordained. Furthermore, purification from an offense comes only through the process of practice, not through disrobing. Therefore, an ordained monk, having incurred even a Dubbhāsita offense at the very least, if he later disrobes and returns, he is to be ordained; he is purified only by confessing that offense, not otherwise. This is for the purpose of showing the process of purification for one who is ordained. If it is said: For a monk suspended for not seeing an uncommon offense, who has arisen from that offense by changing his characteristic—if his normal characteristic then arises again, it is simply a state of separate co-residence. And even if he returns after disrobing and is ordained in the aforementioned way, is this because he has not arisen from the suspension? No, because of the manifestation of a different characteristic. He is not purified by disrobing, because the formal act is not purified thereby. This is not so, for if the formal act were not purified, it would lead to the failure of the subsequent ordination act. And there is no failure of the formal act, nor is there pacification of the formal act. And by disrobing, being unordained, he corrupts the formal act through the state of separate co-residence, because it was spoken pointedly by the Lord of the Dhamma. For that very reason, the future tense word ‘you will see’ was used. It should be known that this was stated to show all these alternative meanings: that such a householder, like a monk on probation whose duties have been set aside, stands in his normal state—that is, by disrobing and so forth, he stands only in the natural state of an unordained person. However, a suspended monk of the type mentioned before, who has changed his characteristic and is then re-established in his normal characteristic, should be asked again, ‘Do you see?’ One who says, ‘Yes, I see,’ should be reinstated. He should not be told, ‘Confess,’ because he has arisen from the offense by changing his characteristic. A suspended monk who has made amends should be asked, ‘Have you performed the remedy?’ One who says, ‘Yes, it is done,’ should be reinstated. One who says, ‘The remedy does not need to be done by me,’ should not be reinstated, so say some. This procedure is for an uncommon offense, not for a common one. In that case, some say that the suspended monk's formal act is pacified just by changing his characteristic. The teacher says: ‘Having investigated, the more suitable view should be adopted.’ However, in the Anugaṇṭhipada, ‘communion with a shameless one’ should be defined by way of giving with one's own hand, etc. The view of those who say, ‘It is allowable to give to a shameless monk with one's own hand, having pointed out that he is one who fulfills the states of cordiality, etc.’ should be rejected. Why? In accordance with the ruling that ‘It is not allowable to give to a suspended monk with one's own hand.’ And because ‘It is indeed allowable to cause something to be given.’ Although a Dukkaṭa offense is incurred through communion with a shameless one, nevertheless this monk is not shameless. Therefore, referring to the state of being without offense in every way, it was said, ‘No offense in communion, in co-residence.’ How is this known? It should be understood by way of the meaning: because sugarcane juice and bagasse are seven-day and lifetime allowances, one who, having formed the perception, ‘It is allowable to chew sugarcane at the wrong time,’ chews it, does not see a Pācittiya offense on account of that, because he had such a perception that it was allowable. Or whichever monk, having admitted the fact of having fallen into an offense, resolves, ‘I will not make amends’—these two…

‘Sañcicca āpattiṃ āpajjati, āpattiṃ parigūhati;

Agatigamanañca gacchati, ediso vuccati alajjīpuggalo’ti. (pari. 359) –

‘He intentionally commits an offense, conceals the offense, and pursues wrong courses; such a one is called a shameless person.’

Vuttalakkhaṇe [V 0.0407] apatanato alajjino na honti, tasmā ‘yo āpattidesanapaṭikammāni na karoti, tena saddhiṃ sambhogādikaraṇe anāpattī’ti visesetvā vuttavacanena, itarenapi saddhiṃ kiñcāpi rūpiyasaṃvohāro na hoti, atha kho kayavikkayena āpatti hotiyevāti nayo dinno hoti, pañcahi saddhiṃ sabbathāpi anāpattīti nayo ca. Evaṃ sāpattiṭṭhānesu visesetvā ca vacanato idha tathā avuttattā tena saha alajjiparibhogo natthi. Bhajāpiyamāno pana alajjipakkhaṃ bhajatīti imināpi upāyena sabbattha taṃ taṃ saṃsanditvā attho pariyesitabboti apare. Ācariyā pana evaṃ na vadantī”ti vuttaṃ. “Sacāhaṃ na passissāmīti vadati, na pabbājetabbo”ti vuttattā pubbe āpannāpattiyo uppabbajitassāpi na paṭippassambhantīti siddhaṃ, teneva ācariyā āpattiṃ desāpetvāva sikkhāpaccakkhānaṃ kārāpentīti ca anāpatti sambhoge saṃvāseti idaṃ pubbe āpannaṃ santiṃ eva āpattiṃ na passatīti āsaṅkitabbo. Sā paṭippassaddhāti ñāpanatthaṃ vuttanti [M 0.0446] ca eke. “Passissasī”ti gahaṭṭhattā desetuṃ na vaṭṭatīti anāgatavasena vuttaṃ. “Upasampādetvā passissasī”ti parivāsādinā kattabbassa atthibhāvena “passasī”ti avatvā anāgatavasena vuttaṃ, osāretvāti abbhānavasena. Tattha puna kātabbassa abhāvā “passasī”ti vuttaṃ. Idaṃ sabbaṃ sabbattha paṭijānanaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Ekatrāpi puna na paṭijānāti, etena saha tassā āpattiyā anurūpena saṃvāso na kātabbo, alajjibhāvenāti vuttaṃ hoti. Diṭṭhiyātiādīsu osāraṇaṃ nāma samānakammādinā karaṇanti attho. Anāpatti sambhogeti ukkhittakena sambhoge anāpatti. Kasmā? Ukkhittakakammassa gahaṭṭhabhāvena paṭippassaddhattā, teneva “alabbhamānāya sāmaggiyā”ti vuttaṃ. Idāni bhikkhubhāve kattabbatoti keci. Dvīsupi vāresu kammapaṭippassaddhividhānaṃ teyeva jānanti, tasmā sabbavāresu yuttamayuttañca suṭṭhu sallakkhetvā kathetabbaṃ.

They are not shameless ones for not falling into the stated characteristic. Therefore, because of the statement spoken with distinction, 'There is no offense in performing association, etc., with a monk who does not perform the confession of an offense and its remedy,' and although with another there is no transaction with money, nevertheless, the principle is given that an offense indeed occurs through buying and selling; and the principle is also given that with five others, there is no offense in any way. Thus, because it is stated with distinctions in cases where an offense is incurred, and because it is not stated so here, there is no association with him as with a shameless one. However, others say that when one is made to associate, one joins the shameless faction; and by this method also, in all cases, the meaning should be sought by connecting this and that text. But the teachers do not speak thus,' it is said. Because it is said, 'If he says, "I will not see," he should not be given the going forth,' it is established that offenses incurred previously do not become settled even for one who has disrobed. For that very reason, the teachers have the offense confessed first and only then cause the renunciation of the training. And regarding this statement, 'no offense in association, in communion,' he should be suspected thus: 'He does not see an existing offense incurred previously.' And some say it is said for the purpose of making it known that 'That offense is settled.' 'You will see' is said in the future tense because, being a layman, it is not proper for him to confess. 'Having given the higher ordination, you will see' is said in the future tense, not 'you see,' because of the existence of what must be done, such as probation. 'Having reinstated him' is said by way of rehabilitation. There, because there is nothing further to be done, 'you see' is said. All this is said with reference to acknowledging in every case. If he does not acknowledge again even in one case, communion with him should not be performed in a manner befitting that offense; it is said that this is due to his shamelessness. In cases of wrong view, etc., 'reinstatement' means performing an act of equal status, etc.—this is the meaning. Regarding 'no offense in association,' there is no offense in associating with one who has been suspended. Why? Because the act of suspension has been settled by his becoming a layman; for that very reason, it is said, 'when unanimity is not obtainable.' Some say that now, because it is to be done in the state of a monk, there is no offense. In both cases, they alone know the procedure for settling the formal act. Therefore, in all cases, one should speak after having carefully considered what is proper and improper.

Yo khandhakaṃ pabbajjanāmadheyyaṃ,

Nānānayaṃ sāsanamūlabhūtaṃ;

Ñatvā pakāseti parassa sammā,

Tassādhipaccaṃ munisāsanasminti.

The bhikkhu who, having known the Khandhaka named Pabbajjā, which has various methods and is the root of the Dispensation, explains it well to another—his would be the supremacy in the Dispensation of the Sage.

Mahākhandhakavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Great Section is concluded.

2. Uposathakkhandhakavaṇṇanā

2. The Commentary on the Uposatha Section

Sannipātānujānanādikathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Permission for Assemblies and Other Related Matters

132-3. Tena [M 0.0447][V 0.0408] samayenāti attano ovādapātimokkhuddese dhuraṃ nikkhipitvā bhikkhūnaṃyeva visuṃ uposathakaraṇaṃ anujānitvā ṭhitasamayena. Ko pana soti? Majjhimabodhiyaṃ pātimokkhuddesappahonakasikkhāpadānaṃ pariniṭṭhānakālo. Tenevāha “tāni nesaṃ pātimokkhuddesaṃ anujāneyya”nti. “Evañca pana, bhikkhave, uddisitabba”nti nidānuddesaṃ paññāpetukāmatāya ca sikkhāpadānaṃ uddesaparicchedanidassanatthañca vuttaṃ. Aññathā “evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyathā”ti sabbasikkhāpadānaṃ uddisitabbakkamassa dassitattā idāni “evañca pana, bhikkhave, uddisitabba”nti idaṃ niratthakaṃ āpajjati, idañca sabbasaṅghuposathaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ.

In the text, 'tena samayena' refers to the time when he was established, having laid down the burden of reciting the Ovāda-pātimokkha himself and having permitted the bhikkhus themselves to perform the Uposatha separately. What time is that? It is the time of the completion of the collection of training rules sufficient for the recitation of the Pātimokkha at the Middle Bodhi. For that very reason, he said, 'He should permit them the recitation of the Pātimokkha.' The statement 'And thus, monks, it should be recited' was said because of the desire to lay down the introductory recitation and also to show the division of the recitation of the training rules. Otherwise, because the sequence to be recited of all the training rules was shown by the phrase 'And thus, monks, you should recite this training rule,' this phrase 'And thus, monks, it should be recited' would now become meaningless. And this was said in reference to the Uposatha of the entire Saṅgha.

134. “Yaṃnūna ayyāpi…pe… sannipateyyu”nti bahūnaṃ adhikārappavatti. Tatrāpi vinayaṃ āgamma vutto bhikkhu sāmi, na kevalaṃ saṅghattheroti dassanatthaṃ, saṅghassa gāravayuttavacanārahatādassanatthañca “suṇātu me, bhante”ti āha. Tattha sayaṃ ce thero, bhikkhuṃ sandhāya “āvuso”ti vattuṃ yujjati. Kathaṃ paññāyati? Buddhakāle saṅghatthero abyatto nāma dullabho. Sabbakammavācāya payoganidassane ca “suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho” icceva bhagavā dassetīti ce? Evametaṃ tathā dassanato. Saṅghaṃ upādāya saṅghattherenāpi “suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho”ti vattabbaṃ, bhikkhuṃ upādāya “āvuso”ti mahākassapassa kammavācāya payogadassanato, pārisuddhiuposathe ca therena bhikkhunā “parisuddho ahaṃ, āvuso”ti payogadassanato ca. “Yadi saṅghassa pattakalla”nti parato paññāpetabbe uposathakaraṇantarāye sandhāyāha. Uposathassa bahuvidhattā sarūpato vattuṃ “pātimokkhaṃ uddiseyyā”ti āha. Ettāvatā ñattiṃ niṭṭhapesi. Ñattidutiyakammato eva hi uposathakammaṃ. Na, tatiyānussāvanasambhavatoti [V 0.0409] ce? Na, aññehi ñatticatutthakammehi asadisattā. Na hi ettha catukkhattuṃ “suṇātu me”ti ārabhīyatīti. Aññehi ñattidutiyehi asadisattā ñattidutiyampi māhotūti ce? Na, ñattidutiyakammassa [M 0.0448] aññathāpi kattabbato. Tathā hi ñattidutiyakammaṃ ekaccaṃ apalokanavasenapi kātuṃ vaṭṭati, na aññaṃ aññathā kātuṃ vaṭṭati. Kathaṃ paññāyatīti? Idameva uposathakammaṃ ñāpakaṃ.

134. The phrase 'Perhaps the venerable ones... should assemble' is a statement that occurs according to the wish of many monks. In that context, the monk who speaks, relying on the Vinaya, is the master. He says, 'Venerable sirs, listen to me,' in order to show that it is not merely the Saṅghatthera who is the master, and also to show that the Saṅgha is worthy of being addressed with respectful speech. Therein, if he himself is the elder, it is proper to say 'friend,' addressing a monk. How is this known? In the Buddha's time, an incompetent Saṅghatthera was rare. If it is said: 'And in demonstrating the application of all formal acts, the Blessed One shows only "Venerable sirs, let the Saṅgha listen to me"'? This is so, because of showing the Kammavācā text in that way. With reference to the Saṅgha, even the Saṅghatthera should say, 'Venerable sirs, let the Saṅgha listen to me'; with reference to a monk, one should say 'friend,' because of seeing the application of the formal act by Mahākassapa, and because of seeing the application by the elder monk in the Purity Uposatha: 'I am pure, friend.' He says, 'If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha,' with reference to the obstructions to performing the Uposatha that are to be laid down later. Because the Uposatha has many varieties, to state its essential nature, he says, 'one should recite the Pātimokkha.' With this much, he completes the motion. For the Uposatha act is indeed a motion-and-one-proclamation act. If it is said: 'No, because a third proclamation is possible'? No, because of its dissimilarity to other motion-and-three-proclamation acts. For here 'listen to me' is not begun four times, it should be known. If it is said: 'Because of its dissimilarity to other motion-and-one-proclamation acts, let it also not be a motion-and-one-proclamation act'? No, because a motion-and-one-proclamation act can also be done in another way. Thus, some motion-and-one-proclamation acts are suitable to do by means of informing, but others are not suitable to do otherwise. How is this known? This very Uposatha act is the indicator.

“Kiṃ saṅghassa pubbakicca”nti idaṃ na ñatti niṭṭhapetvā vattabbaṃ, tañhi ñattito puretarameva karīyatīti. Tasmā “suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, kiṃ saṅghassa pubbakiccaṃ, yadi saṅghassā”ti vattabbaṃ siyāti? Tathāpi na vattabbaṃ, na hi taṃ ñattiyā antokarīyatīti. Yadi evaṃ sabbattha na vattabbaṃ payojanābhāvāti ce? Na, yathāgataṭṭhāneyeva vattabbato, parapadāpekkhatāyāti vuttaṃ hoti. Idaṃ pubbakiccaṃ akatvā uposathaṃ karonto saṅgho, puggalo vā ṭhapanakkhettātikkame āpajjati. Na hi tasmiṃ khette atikkante sammajjanāsanodakapadīpakaraṇe āpattimokkho hoti. Uposathakammato pubbe kattabbakiccākaraṇapaccayattā tassā āpattiyā, na sā kammapariyosānāpekkhā etthāgatasampajānamusāvādāpatti viya, tasmā pātimokkhuddesako bhikkhu “pārisuddhiṃ āyasmanto ārocethā”ti vattukāmo paṭhamaṃyeva parisuddhāparisuddhapaccayaṃ pubbakiccaṃ sarāpeti. Tañhi kataṃ parisuddhapaccayo hoti, akataṃ aparisuddhapaccayo, teneva ubhayāpekkhādhippāyena “kataṃ na kata”nti avatvā “kiṃ saṅghassa pubbakicca” miccevāha. Tattha akatapakkhe tāva pārisuddhiārocanakkamanidassanatthaṃ parato “yassa siyā āpatti, so āvi kareyyā”ti ca, katapakkhe “asantiyā āpattiyā tuṇhī bhavitabba”nti ca vakkhati.

The phrase 'What is the preliminary duty of the Sangha?' should not be said after completing the motion, for that is done even before the motion. Therefore, should one say, 'Venerable sirs, let the Sangha listen to me. What is the preliminary duty of the Sangha? If it is timely for the Sangha...'? Even so, it should not be said, for that is not included within the motion. If so, should it not be said in all cases due to lack of purpose? No, for it should be said only in its proper place, because it is dependent on a subsequent phrase, so it is said. The Sangha or an individual who performs the Uposatha without having done this preliminary duty incurs an offense by transgressing the designated area. For when that area is transgressed, there is no release from the offense through the act of sweeping, preparing seats, providing water, or lighting lamps. This is because that offense has, as its condition, the non-performance of a duty that must be done before the Uposatha ceremony; it is not, like the offense of intentional lying mentioned here, dependent on the completion of the formal act. Therefore, the monk reciting the Pātimokkha, wishing to say, 'Venerable sirs, declare your purity,' first reminds them of the preliminary duty, which is a condition for purity and impurity. For when it is done, it is a condition for purity; when not done, a condition for impurity. Precisely with the intention of considering both aspects, without saying 'done or not done,' he says only, 'What is the preliminary duty of the Sangha?'. In this regard, in the case where it has not been done, in order to show the procedure for declaring purity, it will be said subsequently, 'Whoever has an offense, let him reveal it.' And in the case where it has been done, it will be said, 'If there is no offense, one should remain silent.'

Pārisuddhiṃ āyasmanto ārocetha. Kiṃkāraṇā? Yasmā pātimokkhaṃ uddisissāmi. Ettha ca “uddisāmī”ti vattamānakālaṃ aparāmasitvā “uddisissāmī”ti anāgatakālaparāmasanena yvāyaṃ “dāni nesaṃ pātimokkhuddesaṃ anujāneyya”nti (mahāva. 150) ettha vuttapātimokkhuddeso, taṃ sandhāya “pātimokkhaṃ uddisissāmī”ti vuttanti eke. Yasmā “pañcime, bhikkhave, pātimokkhuddesā”ti vuttaṃ, tasmā vattamānassa nidānuddesasaṅkhātassa pātimokkhassa yadetaṃ ante “kaccittha parisuddhā”tiādikaṃ yāvatatiyānussāvanaṃ, tasseva āpattikhettattā, avayavepi avayavīvohārasambhavato ca idha āpattikhettameva sandhāya “pātimokkhaṃ uddisissāmī”ti [M 0.0449] vuttaṃ. Evañhi vutte yasmā parato āpattikhettaṃ āgamissati, tasmā āpattibhīrukā tumhe sabbeva paṭhamameva pārisuddhiṃ ārocethāti ayamattho [V 0.0410] sambhavati. Vattamānakālavasena vutte “pārisuddhiṃ āyasmanto ārocethā”ti vacanameva na sambhavati tadārocanassa paṭhamaṃ icchitabbattā, pageva tassa karaṇābhāvena “pātimokkhaṃ uddisissāmī”ti vacanaṃ. Ayaṃ nayo santiyā āpattiyā ārocane yujjati, na tuṇhībhāve, akammapariyosānā tuṇhībhāvappattito, evaṃ santepi tasmiṃ yujjateva. Pātimokkhuddesako hi aññamaññaṃ āpattiāvikaraṇaṃ akatvā tuṇhībhūte bhikkhū passitvā teneva tuṇhībhāvena ārocitapārisuddhiko hutvā “suṇātu me, bhante”ti pātimokkhuddesaṃ ārabhi.

Venerable sirs, declare your purity. For what reason? Because I will recite the Pātimokkha. And here, some say that 'I will recite the Pātimokkha' is said with reference to the Pātimokkha recitation spoken of in the passage, 'Now he should permit their Pātimokkha recitation,' by not considering the present tense 'uddisāmi' but by considering the future tense 'uddisissāmi'. Because it is said, 'Monks, there are these five Pātimokkha recitations,' therefore, regarding the present Pātimokkha known as the introductory recitation, that which is at the end—from 'Is everyone here pure?' up to the third proclamation—since that very part is the field of offenses, and because it is possible to speak of a part as the whole, here 'I will recite the Pātimokkha' is said with reference to the field of offenses alone. For when it is said thus, the following meaning is possible: since the field of offenses will come later, therefore all of you who are fearful of offenses should declare your purity at the very beginning. If it were said in the present tense, the very statement 'Venerable sirs, declare your purity' would not be suitable, because that declaration is desired first; how much less would the statement 'I will recite the Pātimokkha' be suitable, since that action has not yet been performed. This method is suitable for declaring an existing offense, but not for silence, because silence is maintained until the end of the formal act. Even so, it is indeed suitable in that case. For the Pātimokkha reciter, having seen the monks silent and not having disclosed offenses to one another, takes their purity as declared by that very silence and begins the Pātimokkha recitation with, 'Venerable sirs, let the Sangha listen to me.'

Etthāha – paṭhamaṃ “saṅgho uposathaṃ kareyya, pātimokkhaṃ uddiseyyā”ti vuttattā idhāpi “saṅgho uposathaṃ karissati, pātimokkhaṃ uddisissatī”ti vattabbaṃ, atha “puggalassa uddesā”ti lakkhaṇattā yathārutameva vattabbaṃ, tathāpi “uposathaṃ karissāmi, pātimokkhaṃ uddisissāmī”ti vattabbanti? Na vattabbaṃ lakkhaṇavirodhato, aniṭṭhappasaṅgato ca. Puggalassa uddesā eva hi saṅghassa uposatho kato hoti, na puggalassa uposathakaraṇena. Tañca sova karissati, na saṅghoti aniṭṭhappasaṅgova āpajjati. “Suṇāthā”ti vutte acittasāmaggippasaṅgabhayā “suṇomā”ti vuttaṃ. “Suṇissāmā”ti vattabbaṃ “uddisissāmī”ti vuttattāti ce? Na vattabbaṃ, āpattikhettadassanādhippāyanirapekkhatāya “suṇoma” icceva vattabbaṃ. Ekapadeneva hissa tadadhippāyo atikkantoti. Yadi evaṃ kimatthaṃ taṃ sabbeheva āraddhanti ce? “Uddisissāmī”ti iminā asādhāraṇavacanena āpannassa acittasāmaggippasaṅganivāraṇatthaṃ. Saramānenāti iminā cassa sampajānamusāvādassa sacittakataṃ dasseti. Antarāyiko dhammo vutto bhagavatāti evaṃ akiriyasamuṭṭhānassāpi evaṃ parittakassa imassa musāvādassa mahādīnavataṃ dasseti. Visuddhāpekkhenāti sāvasesaṃ āpattiṃ upādāya anāpattibhāvasaṅkhātaṃ anavasesañca upādāya gihibhāvasaṅkhātaṃ visuddhiṃ icchantena kasmā āvi kātabbā? Antarāyabhāvānupagamanena phāsuvihārapaccayattā. Idha [M 0.0450] “ajjuposatho pannaraso”ti na vuttaṃ parato divasaniyamassa kattukāmatādhippāyena avuttattā. Evaṃ pana te bhikkhū sabbadivasesu uddisiṃsu.

Here, one objects: Since it was first stated, 'The Saṅgha should perform the Uposatha, should recite the Pātimokkha,' here too it should be said, 'The Saṅgha will perform the Uposatha, will recite the Pātimokkha.' Or if, due to the characteristic 'by the recitation of an individual,' it should be stated just as it is written, even so, should it be said, 'I will perform the Uposatha, I will recite the Pātimokkha'? It should not be said, due to contradiction with the characteristic and because it leads to an undesirable consequence. For indeed, the Saṅgha's Uposatha is accomplished only by the individual's recitation, not by the individual's performance of the Uposatha. And that Uposatha, he alone will perform, not the Saṅgha; thus, an undesirable consequence indeed arises. When 'Listen' is said, 'We listen' is said out of fear of the consequence of communion occurring without intention. If it is argued that 'We will listen' should be said because 'I will recite' was stated, the answer is: it should not be said. Because of being without regard for the intention of seeing the field of offenses, it should be said only as 'We listen.' For indeed, by that one word alone, his intention is already conveyed. If so, for what purpose is this response undertaken by all? It is undertaken to prevent, for one who has an offense, the consequence of communion without intention, by this personal statement, 'I will recite.' By this phrase 'while remembering,' it shows that this intentional false speech is done with consciousness. By the phrase 'An obstructive dhamma was spoken by the Blessed One,' it shows the great danger of this minor false speech, even though it arises from non-action. Regarding 'by one who desires purity'—that is, by one desiring the purity designated as the state of no-offense (with reference to an offense with a remainder), and the purity designated as the state of a householder (with reference to an offense without a remainder)—why should it be made manifest? Because by not arriving at the state of being an obstruction, it is a condition for comfortable living. Here, 'Today is the Uposatha, the fifteenth' was not said, because it was not stated with the intention of wanting to make a determination of the day hereafter. Because it was not said thus, however, those monks recited on all days.

135. “Ādimeta”nti sīlapātimokkhameva vuttaṃ, kiñcāpi ganthapātimokkho adhippeto. “Pañcannaṃ vā”ti mātikāyaṃ vuttānaṃ vasena vuttaṃ. Anajjhāpanno vāti puggalādhiṭṭhānadesanā. Porāṇagaṇṭhipade pana “‘uposathaṃ kareyyā’ti ettāvatā ñatti hoti. Yāvatatiyānussāvanā nāma ‘yassa siyā āpattī’tiādivacanattayaṃ, ante ‘dutiyampi tatiyampi [V 0.0411] pucchāmī’ti idañcāti duvidhaṃ. Tattha paṭhamaṃ āpattiṃ saritvā nisinnassa, dutiyaṃ asarantassa sāraṇattha”nti vuttaṃ. “Vacīdvāre”ti pākaṭavasena ujukameva vuttaṃ. Kiñcāpi kāyaviññattiyāpi karīyati, kāyakammābhāvā pana vacīviññattiyāyeva āvi kātabbā. “Saṅghamajjhe vā”tiādi lakkhaṇavacanaṃ kira. Saṅghuposathakaraṇatthaṃ saṅghamajjhe ce nisinno, tasmiṃ saṅghamajjhe. Gaṇuposathakaraṇatthañce gaṇamajjhe nisinno, tasmiṃ gaṇamajjhe. Ekasseva santike ce pārisuddhiuposathaṃ kattukāmo, tasmiṃ ekapuggale āvi kātabbāti, “etena na kevalaṃ saṅghamajjhe evāyaṃ musāvādo sambhavati, atha kho ettha vuttalakkhaṇena asatipi ‘pārisuddhiṃ āyasmanto ārocethā’tiādividhāne gaṇuposathepi sāpattiko hutvā uposathaṃ kattukāmo anārocetvā tuṇhībhūtova karoti ce, sampajānamusāvādāpattiṃ āpajjatīti imassatthassa āvikaraṇato lakkhaṇavacanaṃ kireta”nti vadanti takkikā. Aññathā “gaṇamajjhevā”ti na vuttanti tesaṃ adhippāyo. Ārocanādhippāyavasena vuttanti no takkoti ācariyo. Ārocento hi saṅghassa ārocemīti adhippāyena āvi karonto saṅghamajjhe āvi karoti nāma. Attano ubhatopasse nisinnānaṃ ārocento gaṇamajjhe. Ekassevārocessāmi sabhāgassāti adhippāyena ārocento ekapuggale āroceti nāma. Pubbe vibhattapadassa puna vibhajanaṃ atthavisesābhāvadīpanatthanti veditabbaṃ.

135. In the text 'Ādimetaṃ', although the Ganthapātimokkha is intended, only the Sīlapātimokkha is stated. The text 'Pañcannaṃ vā' is stated by way of the offenses mentioned in the Mātikā. The teaching 'Anajjhāpanno vā' is a teaching based on the individual. However, in the ancient commentary (Porāṇagaṇṭhipada), it is stated: 'By this much, "uposathaṃ kareyyā," the motion (ñatti) occurs. What is called the proclamation up to the third time (yāvatatiyānussāvanā) is twofold: the triad of statements beginning with "yassa siyā āpattī," and this at the end, "dutiyampi tatiyampi pucchāmī." Therein, the first is for one who is seated having remembered an offense; the second is for the purpose of reminding one who does not remember.' The text 'Vacīdvāre' is stated straightforwardly by way of what is manifest. Although it may also be done by bodily intimation, due to the absence of a bodily action, it must be made evident by verbal intimation alone. The text 'Saṅghamajjhe vā,' etc., is, it is said, a defining phrase. If one is seated in the midst of the Saṅgha for the purpose of performing the Saṅgha-uposatha, it must be made evident in the midst of that Saṅgha. If one is seated in the midst of a group for the purpose of performing the group-uposatha, it must be made evident in the midst of that group. If one desires to perform the purity-uposatha in the presence of just one person, it must be made evident to that one person. By this it is shown that 'this false speech does not arise only in the midst of the Saṅgha; but rather, even in a group-uposatha where the procedure beginning with "Venerable sirs, declare your purity" is absent, if one who has an offense and desires to perform the uposatha does so without declaring, just remaining silent, he falls into an offense of intentional false speech. Because it makes this meaning clear, this is, it is said, a defining phrase,' thus say the logicians. Otherwise, 'in the midst of a group' would not have been stated—this is their intention. The teacher says: 'It is our reasoning that it is stated by way of the intention to declare.' For one who is declaring with the intention, 'I will declare to the Saṅgha,' is called making it evident in the midst of the Saṅgha. One who declares to those seated on both sides of oneself is making it evident in the midst of a group. One who declares with the intention, 'I will declare to just one associate,' is called declaring to one person. The re-division of a previously divided term should be understood as being for the purpose of showing the absence of a special meaning.

136-7. “Na, bhikkhave, devasikaṃ…pe… dukkaṭassā”ti vatvā “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, uposathe pātimokkhaṃ uddisitu”nti idaṃ anuposathe eva taṃ dukkaṭaṃ[M 0.0451], uposathe pana devasikampi vaṭṭatīti dīpeti, tasmā te bhikkhū cātuddasiyaṃ uddisitvāpi pannarasiyaṃ uddisiṃsu, tenāha “sakiṃ pakkhassā”ti. Tattha purimena sāmaggīdivaso uposathadivaso evāti dīpeti. Ubhayena aṭṭhamiṃ paṭikkhipitvā devasikaṃ paṭikkhepassa atippasaṅgaṃ nivāreti. Kiṃ vuttaṃ hoti? Bhinno ce saṅgho pāṭipadadivase samaggo hoti, tasmiṃ divase sāmaggīuposathaṃ karonto ubhayampi dukkaṭaṃ āpajjanto ubhayena ekībhūtena nivārito hotīti vuttaṃ hoti. Aññathā sāmaggīuposatho na devasiko. Ce, ahorattaṃ kātabbo. Tasmiñca pakkhe pakatiuposatho na devasiko. Ce, ahorattaṃ kātabbo. Tasmiñca pakkhe pakatiuposatho anuddiṭṭho. Ce hoti, sāmaggīuposatho kātabboti āpajjati. Na apavādanayena gahetabbattāti ce? Na, aniṭṭhappasaṅgato. Kiṃ vuttaṃ hoti? Sāmaggīdivase sāmaggīuposathaṃ katvā puna tasmiṃ pakkhe pakatiuposathadivase sampatte pakatiuposatho na kātabboti. Apavādoti. Apavāditabbaṭṭhānato aññattha ussaggavidhānaṃ nivāreti.

136-7. Having said, “Monks, not daily… it is an offense of wrong-doing,” this statement, “I allow, monks, the recitation of the Pātimokkha on the Uposatha day,” indicates that only on a non-Uposatha day is that an offense of wrong-doing, but on an Uposatha day, even a daily recitation is permissible. Therefore, those monks, having recited on the fourteenth, also recited on the fifteenth. For that reason, it was said, “once a fortnight.” Therein, the former statement indicates that the day of concord is indeed the Uposatha day. By both, having rejected the eighth day, it prevents the over-extension of the rejection of daily observance. What is meant by this? If a divided Saṅgha becomes harmonious on the first day of the fortnight, a monk performing the concord-uposatha on that day, thereby incurring a twofold offense of wrong-doing, is prevented by the two factions having become unified. This is what is meant. Otherwise, the concord-uposatha is not a daily observance; if it were, it would have to be performed day and night. And in that fortnight, the regular uposatha is not a daily observance; if it were, it would have to be performed day and night. And if in that fortnight the regular uposatha is not recited, it follows that the concord-uposatha must be performed. If it is said, “Does this not follow because it should be taken by way of an exception?” No, because of the undesirable consequence. What is meant by this? Having performed the concord-uposatha on the day of concord, when the regular uposatha day arrives again in that fortnight, the regular uposatha should not be performed. This is an exception. It prevents the laying down of a general rule in a place other than where an exception should be made.

Kittāvatā [V 0.0412] nu kho sāmaggīti etthāyamadhippāyo – sāmaggī nāmesā sabhāgānaṃ sannipāto. Sabhāgā ca nāma yattakā sahadhammikā, te sabbepi honti, udāhu āvāsasabhāgatāya sabhāgā nāma hontīti. Tattha yadi sahadhammikānaṃ sāmaggī sāmaggī nāma, sabbesaṃ puthuvibhattānaṃ sāmaggī icchitabbā. Athāvasathavasena, ekāvāsasabhāgānanti vuttaṃ hoti. Aññathā ekāvāse sāmaggīti āpajjati. Mā no agamāsīti agato mā hoti.

To what extent, indeed, is there harmony? Herein, this is the intention: this, called harmony, is the assembly of those who are of a common nature. And are those called 'of a common nature' all who are co-religionists, or are they called 'of a common nature' due to sharing a common residence? Therein, if harmony is called harmony among co-religionists, then harmony should be desired among all who are separately divided. Or, if it is by way of residence, it is meant to be harmony among those who are of a common nature by sharing one residence. Otherwise, it would follow that harmony is only within a single residence. As for the phrase, 'May he not have come to us,' it means, may he not have arrived.

Sīmānujānanakathāvaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Discourse on the Permission for Boundaries

138. Ekāvāsagatānaṃ vasena sāmaggiṃ paṭikkhipitvā ekasīmagatānaṃ vasena anujānitukāmo bhagavā “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sīmaṃ sammannitu”nti āha. Atha āvāsaparicchedaṃ vattukāmo bhaveyya. Ettāvatā ekāvāso yāvatā ekāsīmā. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sīmaṃ sammannitu”nti vadeyya. Tasmā na idha anuññātabaddhasīmāvasena ekāvāsaparicchedo hoti, upacārasīmāvaseneva hotīti veditabbaṃ. Kathaṃ jānitabbanti ce? Pāḷitova, yathāha “tena kho pana samayena āyasmā [M 0.0452] upanando sakyaputto eko dvīsu āvāsesu vassaṃ vasi…pe… ekādhippāya”nti (mahāva. 364). Aññathā vassacchedoti aniṭṭhappasaṅgova, kathaṃ? Ekāvāsavaseneva ce sāmaggī, bahuāvāsaanāvāsesu na sambhaveyya. Tato so taṃ āvāsaṃ gacchanto bahiddhā uposathaṃ karoti. “Na, bhikkhave, tadahuposathe sabhikkhuko anāvāso gantabbo”tiādi (mahāva. 181)-pāḷivirodho satipi saṅghe anāvāse uposathassa akattabbato. Anāvāsepi ce sāmaggī labbhati, “ettāvatā sāmaggī, yāvatā ekāvāso”ti na vattabbaṃ, tasmā sabbathā purimanayo pacchimeneva paṭikkhittoti katvā nānāvāsavasenapi sāmaggīti veditabbaṃ. “Taṃ kammaṃ karomāti vatvā na akaṃsū’tiādīsu viya anāgatampi apekkhati, tasmā ‘karomā’ti vutte na vaṭṭatī”ti vadanti. “Sīmaṃ asodhetvāpi nimittaṃ kittetuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti likhitaṃ. Heṭṭhimakoṭiyā aḍḍhaṭṭhamaratanubbedho hatthippamāṇo. Sace eko baddho hoti, na kātabboti ettha “catūsu disāsu catunnaṃ pabbatakūṭānaṃ heṭṭhā piṭṭhipāsāṇasadise pāsāṇe ṭhitattā ekābaddhabhāve satipi pathavito uddhaṃ tesaṃ sambandhe asati heṭṭhā pathavigatasambandhamatte abbohārikaṃ katvā kittetuṃ vaṭṭati. Teneva ‘piṭṭhipāsāṇo atimahantopi pāsāṇasaṅkhyameva gacchatī’ti vuttaṃ. Pathavito heṭṭhā tassa mahantabhāve gayhamāne pabbatameva hotī”ti anugaṇṭhipade vuttaṃ. “Cinitvā katapaṃsupuñje tiṇagumbarukkhā ce jāyanti, pabbato hotīti dhammasiritthero. Nevāti upatissatthero”ti vuttaṃ.

138. The Blessed One, wishing to reject unity based on a single dwelling and to allow it based on a single boundary, said, “I allow, monks, a boundary to be delimited.” Then, one might wish to define the extent of the dwelling. A single dwelling extends as far as a single boundary. One might say, “I allow, monks, a boundary to be delimited.” Therefore, it should be understood that here the definition of a single dwelling is not based on an authorized bound boundary, but rather on the proximity boundary. How is this to be known? From the Pāḷi itself, as it is said: “At that time, the Venerable Upananda the Sakyan, being one person, spent the rains-residence in two dwellings…with a single intention” (Mahāvagga 364). Otherwise, it would result in the breaking of the rains-residence, an undesirable consequence. How so?
