If unity were based solely on a single dwelling, it would not be possible in multiple dwellings or non-dwellings. Therefore, one going to that dwelling would perform the Uposatha outside. This contradicts the Pāḷi beginning, “Monks, on the Uposatha day, a non-dwelling where there are monks should not be gone to,” etc. (Mahāvagga 181), as the Uposatha cannot be performed in a non-dwelling even if the Saṅgha is present. If unity is achieved even in a non-dwelling, it should not be said, “Unity extends only as far as a single dwelling.” Therefore, having entirely rejected the former method by the latter, it should be understood that unity can also be based on various dwellings. They say: “Just as in cases like ‘Having said, “We will perform that act,” they did not do it,’ it also considers the future; therefore, when ‘We will do it’ is said, it is not valid.” It is written: “Even without purifying the boundary, it is valid to declare the marker.” The lower limit [of a marker] is seven and a half cubits high, of elephantine measure. Regarding the statement, “If one [marker] is bound, it should not be done,” herein: “In the four directions, beneath the four mountain peaks, on stones like backrest stones, because they stand, even if there is a single bound state, when there is no connection for them upwards from the earth, it is valid to declare them, having made the mere connection that has gone into the earth below non-conventional. For that very reason, it is said, ‘Even a very large backrest stone is counted merely as a stone.’ If its great size is considered from below the ground, it becomes a mountain.” This is stated in the Anugaṇṭhipada. It is said: “If grass, shrubs, or trees grow on a heap of earth that has been made by piling it up, it becomes a mountain,” says the Elder Dhammasiri. “It does not,” says the Elder Upatissa.

Pāsāṇoti [V 0.0413] “sudhāmayapāsāṇopi vaṭṭatī”ti vadanti. Vīmaṃsitabbaṃ iṭṭhakāya paṭikkhittattā. Dvattiṃsapalaguḷapiṇḍappamāṇo tulatāya, na tulagaṇanāya. Sopīti khāṇuko viya uṭṭhitapāsāṇo.

Regarding a stone: they say, 'Even a stone made of plaster is allowable.' This should be investigated, since bricks are rejected. A stone the size of a lump of molasses weighing thirty-two palas is to be taken by weighing, not by the count of weights. That too is a stone pillar that has arisen like a tree stump.

Catupañcarukkhanimittamattampīti ekaccesu nimittasaddo natthi. Ettha tayo ce sārarukkhā honti, dve asārarukkhā, sārarukkhānaṃ bahuttaṃ icchitabbaṃ. “Susānampi idha ‘vanamevā’ti saṅkhyaṃ gacchati sayaṃjātattā”ti vuttaṃ. Keci pana “catūsu dve antosārā ce, vaṭṭati. Antosārā adhikā, samā vā, vaṭṭati. Tasmā bahūsupi dve ce antosārā atthi, vaṭṭatī”ti vadanti.

Regarding 'even the mere sign of four or five trees': in some manuscripts, the word 'nimitta' (sign) is not present. Herein, if there are three heartwood trees and two non-heartwood trees, a majority of heartwood trees is to be desired. It is said: 'Even a charnel ground, in this context, is counted as a forest because it is self-grown.' Some, however, say: 'If among four trees, two are heartwood trees, it is allowable. If the heartwood trees are more, or equal, it is allowable. Therefore, even among many trees, if there are two heartwood trees, it is allowable.'

Parabhāgeti [M 0.0453] ettha “etehi baddhaṭṭhānato gatattā vaṭṭati. Tathā dīghamaggepi gahitaṭṭhānato gataṭṭhānassa aññattā”ti vadanti.

Regarding 'in the other part': Herein, they say, 'By these, because they have gone from the bound place, it is allowable. Similarly, even on a long road, it is allowable because the place gone to is different from the place taken from.'

Anvaddhamāsanti ettha “anubaddho addhamāso, addhamāsassa vā anū”ti likhitaṃ. “Antaravāsako temiyatī”ti vuttattā tattakappamāṇaudakeyeva kātuṃ vaṭṭatīti keci. Temiyatīti iminā heṭṭhimakoṭiyā nadilakkhaṇaṃ vuttaṃ. Evarūpāya nadiyā yasmiṃ ṭhāne cattāro māse appaṃ vā bahuṃ vā udakaṃ ajjhottharitvā pavattati, tasmiṃ ṭhāne appodakepi ṭhatvā kātuṃ vaṭṭatīti eke. “Pavattanaṭṭhāne nadinimitta’nti vuttattā setuto parato tattakaṃ udakaṃ yadi pavattati, nadī evā”ti vadanti.

Regarding 'fortnightly': Herein, it is written, 'A connected half-month, or the sequence of a half-month.' Some say that because it is said, 'The under-robe is dampened,' it is allowable to perform the act only in water of that much quantity. By this word 'temiyati' (is dampened), the characteristic of a river at its lower limit is stated. Some say: 'In a river of such a nature, in whatever place water flows, having inundated it, for four months, whether a little or a lot, in that place it is allowable to perform the act, having stood even where the water is little.' They also say: 'Because it is said, “The sign of a river is in the place of flowing,” if that much water flows beyond a dyke, it is indeed a river.'

Jātassarādīsu ṭhitodakaṃ jātassarādipadesena anantarikampi nimittaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭati nadipārasīmāya nimittaṃ viya. Sace so padeso kālantarena gāmakhettabhāvaṃ pāpuṇāti, tattha aññaṃ sīmaṃ sammannituṃ vaṭṭati. Ukkhepimanti uddharitvā gahetabbakaṃ.

In natural lakes and so on, it is allowable to make the standing water a sign, even if it is contiguous with the area of the natural lake, etc., just like the sign for a river-bank sīmā. If that area, after a time, becomes a village-field, it is allowable to establish another sīmā there. 'Ukkhepimaṃ' means that which is to be taken by scooping or drawing out.

Abaddhasīmavihārānaṃ sīmāya upacāraṃ ṭhapetvāti “āyatiṃ sammannitabbāya okāsaṃ ṭhapetvā”ti likhitaṃ. Antonimittagatehi panāti “ekassa upaḍḍhaṃ antokattukāmatāya sati sabbesaṃ āgamane payojanaṃ natthīti katvā ‘antonimittagatehī’ti vuttaṃ, tañca sāmīcivasenā”ti vadanti. Anāgamanampi vaṭṭatīti “sīmāya abaddhattā vaggaṃ nāma na hotī”ti likhitaṃ. “Aññasmiṃ gāmakhette ṭhatvā nimittakittanakāle, samānasaṃvāsakasīmāya sammannanakāle ca āgamanapayojanaṃ natthī”ti vuttaṃ. Bherisaññaṃ vāti “sammannanapariyosānaṃ karomāti [V 0.0414] vatvā”ti likhitaṃ, tena tādise kāle taṃ kappatīti siddhaṃ hoti. Kiṃ iminā? Sukhakaraṇatthanti mahājanasannipātanaparissamaṃ akatvā appatarehi sukhakaraṇatthaṃ. Yadi mahāsīmābandhanakāle antarāyo hoti, tattakenapi sukhavihāroti dassanatthaṃ “paṭhama”nti vuttanti eke. Tato oraṃ na vaṭṭatīti kathaṃ paññāyatīti? Vīsativaggakaraṇīyaparamattā saṅghakammassa. Kammārahena saddhiṃ ekavīsati bhikkhū ce gaṇhāti, vaṭṭati. Tattakappamāṇaṃ sukhanisajjavasena veditabbaṃ. Tameva nimittaṃ aññepi kittetvā sace bandhanti, vaṭṭatīti eke.

Regarding 'having set aside the vicinity of the boundary for monasteries with an unestablished boundary,' it is written: 'having set aside an opportunity for one to be designated in the future.' But as for 'by those who have gone inside the marker,' some say: 'Since there is no purpose in everyone coming, it is said, “by those who have gone inside the marker,” and that is said by way of propriety.' Regarding 'Even non-arrival is allowable,' it is written: 'Because the boundary is not established, it is not called a group.' It is said: 'When standing in another village-field at the time of announcing the markers, and at the time of designating the boundary for common residence, there is no purpose in coming.' Regarding 'or a drum signal,' it is written: 'Having said, “Let us make the conclusion of the designation.”' Therefore, at such a time, that is allowable; thus it is established. What is the purpose of this? For the sake of ease: for the sake of making it easy with fewer bhikkhus, without the exertion of gathering a large assembly. Some say it is said 'first' in order to show that if an obstacle arises during the establishment of a great boundary, there is a comfortable abiding even with just that much of a partial boundary. 'Less than that is not allowable'—how is this known? Because the supreme limit of a formal act of the Sangha is that which is to be performed by a group of twenty. If one takes twenty-one bhikkhus together with one who is worthy of the act, it is allowable. That much of a measure should be known by way of comfortable sitting. Some say that if other bhikkhus also, having announced that very marker, should establish the boundary, it is allowable.

“Evaṃ [M 0.0454] baddhāsu pana…pe… sīmantarikā hi gāmakhettaṃ bhajatī”ti na āvāsavasena sāmaggīparicchedo, kintu sīmāvasenevāti dassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. “Nimittupagapāsāṇe ṭhapetvā”ti sañcārimanimittassa tapparato vuttaṃ. Ito paṭṭhāya gaṇṭhipadakkamo hoti – na sakkhissantīti te avippavāsaṃ asallakkhetvā “samānasaṃvāsakameva samūhanissāmā”ti vāyāmantā samūhanituṃ na sakkhissanti. “Ekaratanappamāṇā”ti suviññeyyantarā hotīti katvā vuttaṃ. Ekaṅgulamattampi vaṭṭateva. Khaṇḍasīmato paṭṭhāya bandhanaṃ āciṇṇaṃ. Āciṇṇakaraṇena vigatasammoho hotīti. Kuṭigeheti kuṭighare bhūmighare. Udukkhalaṃvāti bhūmiudukkhalaṃ viya khuddakāvāṭaṃ. “Pamukhe”ti bhūmikuṭiṃ sandhāya vuttanti eke. Heṭṭhā na otaratīti bhittito oraṃ nimittāni ṭhapetvā kittitattā heṭṭhā ākāse na otarati, upari kate pāsādeti attho. Bhittilaggeti bhittinissitake. Ime kira bhittilaggāpi “ekābaddhā”ti na vuccanti. Sabbo pāsādo sīmaṭṭho hotīti ekābaddho vā hotu, mā vā. Tālamūlakapabbato nāma anupubbena tanuko. Ākāsapabbhāranti aparikkhepapabbhāraṃ. Susirapāsāṇo nāma leṇaṃ hoti. Antoleṇanti pabbatassa antoleṇaṃ. Dvāraṃ pana sandhāya parato “orato”ti vuttaṃ, sabbathāpi sīmato bahileṇena otaratīti adhippāyo.

“Thus bound... the intermediate space between boundaries indeed belongs to the village-field”—this is stated to show that the definition of unity is not by means of the residence, but only by means of the boundary. “Having placed stones that have gone to the marker…” This was said with reference to the measure of a movable marker. From here onwards, the sequence of glosses begins. They, without perceiving non-separation, though striving by saying, “We will remove only those of shared residence,” will not be able to remove it. “Of the measure of one cubit” is stated because the interval is easily distinguishable. Even a finger's breadth is sufficient. Binding from a fragmented boundary onwards is the traditional practice. By following the traditional practice, one becomes free from confusion. “Kuṭigeha” means a hut-house or an earthen house. “Like a mortar” refers to a small opening like an earthen mortar in the ground. “At the front” is said by some with reference to an earthen hut. “It does not descend below”: because the markers are placed and proclaimed inside from the wall, it does not descend into the space below; the meaning refers to a building made above. “Attached to the wall” means those relying on the wall. These, it is said, even if attached to the wall, are not called “single-bound.” The entire building is situated within the boundary, whether it is single-bound or not. A “Tālamūlakapabbata” is one that is gradually tapering. An “Ākāsapabbhāra” is a slope without an enclosure. A “Susirapāsāṇa” is a cave. “Antoleṇa” means a cave inside the mountain. With reference to the door, however, “inside” is said of what is beyond it; the intention is that in any case, it descends by way of the cave that is outside the boundary.

Mahāsīmaṃ sodhetvāti sīmaṭṭhaṃ dūragatampi sīmagataṃ sīmasambandhaṃva, tasmā taṃ anāmasitvā ṭhātabbanti adhippāyo. Yadi evaṃ “tannissitakaṃ apanetvā kammaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti vattabbaṃ. Mahāaṭṭhakathāyampi “sīmaṃ sodhetvā kātabba”nti ettakameva vuttaṃ. Mahātherāpi “sodhetabba”micceva vadantīti eke. “Mahāsīmaṃ sodhetvā vā kammaṃ kātabba”nti ca pāṭho atthi. “Vuttanayenevā”ti ca parato vakkhati, tasmā sādhāraṇapāṭhova sundaroti eke. Purimanayepīti khaṇḍasīmāya uṭṭhahitvā mahāsīmāya onatepīti attho. Ukkhipāpetvā kātuṃ na vaṭṭati. Kasmā? Anto ṭhitattā. Rukkhassa heṭṭhā pathavigataṃ mūlaṃ khaṇḍasīmāva hoti, abbohārikaṃ [V 0.0415] vāti apare. “Majjhe pana chinne mahāsīmāya ṭhitamūlaṃ mahāsīmameva bhajati, khaṇḍasīmāya ṭhitaṃ khaṇḍasīmameva bhajati tadāyattapathavirasādīhi anuggahitattā”ti vuttaṃ. “Sīmāya pacchā uṭṭhitarukkhe nisīditvā kammaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭati [M 0.0455] pacchāsīmāyaṃ katagehe viyā”ti vatvā “bandhanakāle ṭhitarukkhe nisīditvā kātuṃ na vaṭṭati uparisīmāya agamanato”ti kāraṇaṃ vadanti. Evaṃ sati bandhanakāle puna ārohaṇaṃ nāma natthi, bandhitakāle eva āruhatīti āpajjati. Pacchā uṭṭhitarukkho pana tappaṭibaddhattā sīmasaṅkhyameva gato, evaṃ pubbe uṭṭhitarukkhopīti gahetabbaṃ. “Yaṃ kiñcipī”ti vacanato tiṇādipi saṅgahitaṃ. Mahātherāpi tiṇaṃ sodhetvāva karontīti.

Regarding 'Having cleared the great sīmā': that which stands in the sīmā, even if it has gone far, is considered as being within the sīmā, as it is indeed connected with the sīmā. Therefore, one should stand without touching it—this is the intended meaning. If so, it should be said, “After removing what depends on it, the act may be performed.” In the Great Commentary, only this much is said: “The boundary should be cleaned before performing the act.” Some say that the great elders also simply say, “It should be cleaned.” There is also a reading: “Or the act should be performed after cleaning the great boundary.” And later it will be said, “In the manner already stated,” so some hold that the common reading is preferable. “In the previous way as well” means even after rising up from a fragmented boundary and entering into the great boundary. It is not permissible to perform the act after having caused it to be lifted up. Why? Because it stands inside. The roots of a tree that have gone into the earth beneath belong to the fragmented boundary, or they are not formally designated, according to others. “But if the middle is cut, the roots standing within the great boundary belong to the great boundary, and those standing within the fragmented boundary belong to the fragmented boundary, because they are supported by the earth’s nutrients and so forth dependent on that,” it is said. “One may perform the act while sitting on a tree that has grown up after the boundary, like in a dwelling made in the sīmā afterwards,” they say, and give the reason: “But one may not perform the act while sitting on a tree that was standing at the time of establishing the boundary, because it does not go to the upper boundary.” If this is so, then at the time of establishing the boundary there is no such thing as “growing up again”; it would follow that it only grows up at the time of being established. A tree that grows up afterward, however, is counted as part of the boundary because it is connected to it. Similarly, it should be understood that a tree that grew up beforehand is also counted as part of the boundary. Because of the statement “Whatever it may be,” even grass and the like are included. The great elders also perform the act only after clearing away the grass.

140. Yasmā majjhato koṇaṃ hoti, tasmā “koṇato koṇa”nti vuttaṃ. “Āpattiñca āpajjati acittakattā”ti vadanti. Pārayatīti ajjhottharati. Kā sā? Sīmā. “Yā sabbantimena…pe… vahatī”ti tato heṭṭhimā nāvāsaṅkhyaṃ na gacchatīti katvā vuttanti eke, taṃ na yuttaṃ dutiyapārājike nāvaṭṭhabhaṇḍādhikāre tassāpi adhippetattā. Majjhimapurisassa bhārappamāṇena vuttanti eke. Bhikkhunīnampi nadīpārasīmāsambhavato tāsaṃ “ekā vā nadīpāraṃ gaccheyyā”ti vuttadosapariharaṇatthanti ācariyassa takko. Ubhayatthāpi dhuva-saddo gahito. Tena uposathantarāya pariharaṇatthaṃ uposathadivaso niyamatova vutto. Ettha ca nāvā nāma pamāṇayuttā sabbasādhāraṇā thambhanāvā adhippetā, na kullanāvāti no takkoti ācariyo. Rukkhaṃ chinditvā katoti attho. Sace ekaṃ gāmakhettaṃ, sabbanimittānaṃ anto ṭhite bhikkhū hatthapāsagate katvā sammannitabbā. Nānāgāmakhettaṃ ce, anāgamanampi vaṭṭati. Ubhayatīre nimittakittanamattena dīpako saṅgahito na hoti, tasmā dīpake nimittāni kittetabbāneva. “Nadiyā heṭṭhā nisinnabhikkhu kammaṃ kopeti. Upariyeva hi nadī hotī”ti vadanti.

140. Because it is a corner from the middle, it is said, 'from corner to corner.' They say, 'He incurs an offense due to it being unintentional.' 'Pārayati' means to cover over. What is that? Some say that it was said because a boat smaller than that which 'carries... etc.' does not count as a boat, but that is not correct, because in the section concerning goods left on a boat in the second Pārājika, that too is intended. Some say it is stated according to the burden-carrying capacity of an average man. Regarding nuns, since a river-crossing boundary is possible for them, the teacher's reasoning is that the statement 'one may go to the far side of the river' is made to avoid that fault. In both cases, the word 'dhuva' (permanent) is taken. Therefore, to prevent an obstacle to the Uposatha, the Uposatha day is stated as a fixed rule. Here, a 'boat' is intended to be a properly sized, common, anchored boat—not a raft; this is the teacher's reasoning. The meaning is that it is made by cutting down a tree. If it is a single village-field, the agreement should be made by having the monks standing within all the landmarks come within arm’s reach. If there are multiple village-fields, not coming is also permissible. An island is not included merely by announcing landmarks on both banks, so landmarks must be announced on the island itself. They say, 'A monk sitting downstream invalidates the formal act, for the river is indeed upstream'.

Sīmānujānanakathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the discourse on the permission of boundaries is concluded.

Uposathāgārādikathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourse on the Uposatha Hall and So Forth

141. “Yaṃ saṅgho ākaṅkhati vihāraṃ vā…pe… guhaṃ vā”ti vacanato na kevalaṃ pathaviyaṃyeva, vihārādīnaṃ uparipi sīmā anuññātā hoti uposathakammapadhānattāti siddhaṃ. Tappadhānā sīmāti kathaṃ paññāyatīti ce? Tadadhikārānuññātattā, sammutiyaṃ “samānasaṃvāsā”ti [V 0.0416] ettāvatā [M 0.0456] siddhe visuṃ “ekūposathā”ti vacanato ca. “Uposathaṃ ṭhapetvā sesakammāni samānasaṃvāsā nāmā”ti likhitaṃ. “Ekaṃ samūhanitvā”ti pāḷipāṭho.

141. From the statement, “Whatever the Saṅgha desires, whether a monastery… or a cave,” it is established that a boundary is permitted not only on the ground but also above monasteries and so forth, because the Uposatha ceremony is primary. If it is asked how it is known that the boundary has that as its primary purpose, it is because it was permitted in that context, and because—while it is established by just this much in the agreement: “of common communion”—there is the separate statement, “of one Uposatha.” It is written: “Setting aside the Uposatha, the remaining ceremonies are called ‘of common communion’.” There is the Pāḷi reading: “ekaṃ samūhanitvā.”

142. Katovassāti ekasīmāya samagge sandhāya vuttaṃ. Aññathā nānāsīmāyaṃ ṭhitānaṃ savanaṃ pamāṇaṃ, ekasīmāyapi hatthapāsaṃ muñcitvā ṭhitānaṃ vā savanameva pamāṇanti aniṭṭhaṃ āpajjati. Tattha sammatāya vā asammatāya vāti uposathāgārasammutiyā, na sīmāsammutiyā. Kathaṃ paññāyatīti? Adhikārato, parato chandadānapaññattito, pārisuddhidānapaññattito ca. Tattha purimaṃ kāraṇaṃ purimaṃ aniṭṭhaṃ nivāreti, pacchimaṃ pacchimanti veditabbaṃ. Uposathamukhanti uposathaṭṭhānaṃ. “Uposathamukhassāti uposathāgāraṭṭhānassā”ti likhitaṃ. Yāni kānici nimittāni kittetuṃ vaṭṭetīti idaṃ kathaṃ paññāyatīti? “Paṭhamaṃ nimittā kittetabbā nimitte kittetvā”ti ettakameva vuttattā. Paṭhamaṃ vuttattā na vuccantīti ce? Taṃ pana akāraṇaṃ, na hi buddhānaṃ desanāya ālasiyaṃ atthi. Sīmāsamūhananakāle uposathāgāraṃ samūhanitvāva sīmāsamūhananaṃ ijjhatīti eke. Taṃ ayuttaṃ abaddhāya sīmāya uposathāgārasammutisiddhitoti no takkoti ācariyo. Uposathamukhanti uposathāgārassa mukhanti ācariyā. Uposathamukhassa nimittakittanā sīmāya vuttanayena kātabbā. Ekenāpi kittetuṃ vaṭṭatīti eke. “Pāsādo vā hotu, maṇḍapādīsu vā aññataro. Kammavācāya pana ‘uposathamukha’micceva vattabba”nti vadanti. “Porāṇako āvāso nāma mūlāvāso”ti likhitaṃ. Vadati ghaṭamattā iti hi lakkhaṇaṃ.

142. ‘Katovassā’ was said with reference to the united Saṅgha within a single boundary. Otherwise, for those standing in separate boundaries, the measure is hearing; even within a single boundary, if they stand beyond arm’s reach, the measure is still hearing—this leads to an undesirable consequence. Here, ‘sammatāya vā asammatāya vā’ pertains to the agreement on the Uposatha hall, not the boundary agreement. How is this understood? From the context, from the subsequent ruling on giving consent, and from the ruling on giving purity. In this regard, it should be understood that the first reason prevents the first undesirable outcome, and the latter prevents the latter. ‘Uposathamukha’ means the place of the Uposatha. It is written, ‘“Uposathamukhassa” means the location of the Uposatha hall.’ How is it understood that ‘it is proper to declare whatever landmarks’? Because only this much is stated: ‘First, the landmarks should be declared; after declaring the landmarks.’ If it is said, ‘Because it was stated first, they are not mentioned,’ that is not a valid reason, for there is no laziness in the teachings of the Buddhas. Some say that at the time of dissolving a boundary, the boundary dissolution is accomplished only after dissolving the Uposatha hall. That is incorrect, for the agreement on the Uposatha hall is established even for an unconsecrated boundary; this is the teacher's reasoning. ‘Uposathamukha’ means the entrance of the Uposatha hall—so the teachers say. The declaration of landmarks for the Uposatha entrance should be done in the manner stated for the boundary. Some say it is proper for even one person to declare it. They say, “Whether it is a mansion or any other structure like a pavilion, in the formal act, the term ‘uposathamukha’ must be used.” It is written, “The ancient dwelling is called the root dwelling.” The characteristic is that it speaks of a mere pot.

Avippavāsasīmānujānanakathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourse on Permitting the Non-Separation Boundary

143-4. “Manamhi vūḷho”ti vā pāṭho. Tattha manamhi vūḷhoti manaṃ vūḷho amhīti attho. Ṭhapetvā gāmañca gāmūpacārañcāti antaragharasaṅkhātaṃ gāmañca gāmūpacārañca ṭhapetvā. Keci “parikkhittaṃ gāmaṃ sandhāya ‘gāma’nti vuttaṃ, aparikkhittaṃ sandhāya ‘gāmūpacāra”nti vadanti, taṃ pana aṭṭhakathāya virujjhati. Tasmā nivesanaracchādayo sandhāya gāmaṃ, parikkhepārahaṭṭhānāni sandhāya “gāmūpacāra”nti ca vuttaṃ. Ettha pana anekadhā paṭhanti. Kiṃ tena, pāḷiñca [M 0.0457] aṭṭhakathañca suṭṭhu upaparikkhitvā yathā samenti, tathā gahetabbaṃ. Bhikkhūnaṃ purimakammavācā na vaṭṭatīti gāmagāmūpacāre antokatvā samānasaṃvāsakasīmāya sammatāya upari avippavāsasīmāsammutiyaṃ yujjati. Yattha pana kevalaṃ araññaṃyeva sammataṃ, tattha kathaṃ na vaṭṭatīti. Tattha “ṭhapetvā gāmañca gāmūpacārañcā”ti vacanaṃ na sātthakanti ce? Vuccate [V 0.0417] – evametaṃ, kintu anussāvanahānippasaṅgato taṃ vacanaṃ vattabbamevāti imināva adhippāyena “purimakammavācā na vaṭṭatī”ti vuttaṃ siyā. Ekasmiṃ vā atthe kammavācādvayaābhāvatoti vuttaṃ. “Na hi te aññamaññassa kamme gaṇapūrakā hontī”ti vuttattā ubhinnaṃ nānāsaṃvāsakasaṅghānampi ayameva vidhi āpajjeyyāti ce? Nāpajjati paṭiggahasannidhīnaṃ anuññātattā, omasanādipaccayā avisesato, kammapaṭippassaddhimattāpekkhatāya ca. Tassāti bhikkhunisaṅghassa. Na kammavācaṃ vaggaṃ karontīti kammaṃ na kopentīti attho. Etthāti ṭhapetvā gāmanti ettha. “Yadi bhikkhūnaṃ avippavāsasīmā gāmañca gāmūpacārañca na otarati, atha kasmā gāme sīmābandhanakāle avippavāsaṃ sammannantīti ce? Āciṇṇakappena, na tato aññaṃ kañci atthaṃ apekkhitvā”ti likhitaṃ. “Atthato hi sā bahiddhāpi abaddhā eva hotī”ti vuttaṃ. Antaragāme baddhā samānasaṃvāsasīmā yasmā gāmasaṅkhyaṃ na gacchati, tasmāti eke. Sopi sīmāsaṅkhyameva gacchatīti avippavāsasīmāsaṅkhyaṃ gacchatīti attho. Idaṃ panettha vicāretabbaṃ – gāmaṃ antokatvā baddhāya sīmāya puna avippavāsasammutiyaṃ araññapadese ṭhatvā avippavāsakammavācā kātabbā, udāhu gāme ṭhatvāti? Gāme ṭhatvā katāyapi kappiyabhūmiyā pharatīti. Bahisīme ṭhitasammatadosānulomattā akappiyabhūmiyaṃ ṭhatvā na kātabbāti no takko, esa nayo samūhananepīti ācariyo. Khaṇḍasīmāyaṃ ṭhatvā avippavāsasīmātiādīsu mahāsīmā kira “avippavāsasīmā”ti vuttā.

143-4. Or, the reading is: 'with mind carried away.' There, 'with mind carried away' means 'I am one whose mind is carried away.' 'Excluding the village and the village precincts' means excluding the village, which is designated as the inner house, and the village precincts. Some say that 'village' is said with reference to an enclosed village, and 'village precincts' with reference to an unenclosed one, but that contradicts the commentary. Therefore, 'village' is said with reference to dwellings, roads, and so on, and 'village precincts' is said with reference to places suitable for enclosure. Here, however, they recite in many ways. What of that? Having carefully examined the Pāḷi and the commentary, it should be accepted in such a way that they are in agreement. 'The monks' prior formal act is not valid' is applicable in the case of the agreement of a non-separation boundary on top of a common-residence boundary that has been agreed upon including the village and village precincts. But where only the forest is agreed upon, how is it not valid? If one should say: There, the statement 'excluding the village and the village precincts' is not meaningful? It is said: This is so, but because of the possibility of a defect in the announcement, that statement must indeed be said. It may be that 'the prior formal act is not valid' was said with just this intention. Or, it was said because of the absence of two formal acts in one matter. If one should say: Since it is said, 'For they do not complete the quorum for each other's act,' would this very same method apply also to two Saṅghas of different communion? It does not apply, because of the allowance of acceptance and presence, because of the non-difference of conditions such as touching, and because of the dependence only on the pacification of the act. 'Of her' means of the Saṅgha of nuns. 'They do not make the formal act incomplete' means they do not corrupt the act. 'Here' means here in 'excluding the village.' It is written: 'If the non-separation boundary of the monks does not extend over the village and the village precincts, then why do they agree upon a non-separation boundary at the time of binding the boundary in the village? By established custom, not with regard to any other purpose than that.' It is said: 'For in meaning, it is indeed unbound even outside.' Some say that because a common-residence boundary bound within a village does not attain the designation of 'village,' it therefore attains only the designation of a boundary. This means it goes into the category of a non-separation boundary. This should be investigated here: In the case of a boundary bound including a village, during the subsequent agreement of non-separation, should the formal act of non-separation be performed standing in a forest region, or standing in the village? Even when done standing in the village, it pervades the suitable ground. It is our reasoning that it should not be done standing on unsuitable ground, because of its conformity with the fault of an agreement made while standing outside the boundary. This is the method also in removal, says the teacher. In cases such as 'a non-separation boundary standing in a partial boundary,' the great boundary, it is said, is called the 'non-separation boundary.'

146. “Yassāyasmato khamati etissā sīmāya samānasaṃvāsāya ekūposathāya samugghāto, so tuṇhassā”ti andhakapotthake, sīhaḷapotthakesu ca kesuci pāṭho atthi. Kesuci “samugghāto etissā sīmāyā”ti paṭhamaṃ likhanti, kesuci “etissā sīmāya samugghāto”ti ca.

146. ‘If it is agreeable to the venerable one that there be an abolition of this boundary for common dwelling and a single Uposatha, let him remain silent.’ There is a reading in the Andhakapotthaka and in some Sīhaḷapotthakas. Some write first, “the abolition of this boundary,” and some also write, “of this boundary, the abolition.”

Gāmasīmādikathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discussion on Village Boundaries and So Forth

147. Sā [M 0.0458] cāti sā paricchinditvā dinnagāmasīmā ca itarā ca. Sā katamāti ce? “Pakatigāmā”tiādimāha. Baddhasīmāsadisāyeva hontīti sā ca hoti itarā ca hotīti adhippāyo, tasmāyeva “ticīvaravippavāsaparihāraṃ labhatī”ti ekavacanaṃ kataṃ, taṃ na yuttaṃ ubhinnampi gāmattāti eke. “Honti, na labhantī”ti ca bahuvacanampi karontīti. “Sā ca itarā cā”ti vuttā “majjhe bhinditvā dinnagāmasīmā pakatigāmādayo abhinnā”ti ca vadanti. “Bhikkhuvasatī”ti pāṭho, “vasantī”ti ca likhitaṃ. “Athassa ṭhitokāsato”ti [V 0.0418] vuttattā ekavacanameva yuttaṃ. Sabbā, bhikkhave, nadī asīmāti kataraṃ sīmaṃ paṭikkhipati? Baddhasīmaṃ, ekādasavipattisīmaññatarappasaṅgatoti ācariyā. Sace paṭhamaṃ sīmāya baddhāya pacchā nadiādayo honti, paṭikkhepoti pasaṅgo āpajjati, tasmā abaddhasīmameva paṭikkhipati. Yathā sabbo gāmo gāmasīmā, tathā sabbā nadī asīmā. Kintu tassa tassa bhikkhuno udakukkhepasīmāti sīmānānattaṃ dassetīti no takkoti ācariyo. Yaṃ majjhimassa purisassa samantā udakukkhepāti pana ekissā nadiyā catuvaggādīnaṃ saṅghānaṃ visuṃ catuvaggakaraṇīyādikammakaraṇakāle sīmāparicchedadassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Ticīvarena vippavāsāvippavāsaparicchedadassanatthampi sattabbhantarasīmāya paricchedadassanaṃ viyāti ācariyā, tasmā udakukkhepaparicchedābhāvepi antonadiyaṃ kammaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭatīti siddhaṃ.

147. “And that” refers to the village-sīmā given by demarcation and the other. If it is asked, “Which is that?”, he says, “The natural village,” and so on. They are indeed like a consecrated sīmā; this is the meaning: both that one and the other are. Therefore, the singular form “obtains the exemption from separation from the three robes” was used. Some say that this is not suitable, because both are villages. They also use the plural form: “they are, they do not obtain.” Regarding the statement, “that one and the other,” some also say, “The village-sīmā given by dividing in the middle, and the natural villages and so on, are undivided.” The reading is “a bhikkhu resides,” and it is also written as “they reside.” Because it is said, “Then, from his standing place,” only the singular form is suitable. “All rivers, O bhikkhus, are not a sīmā”—which sīmā does this reject? The teachers say it rejects a consecrated sīmā, because of the consequence of it being one among the eleven defective sīmās. If, after a sīmā has first been consecrated, rivers and so on later come to be, the consequence of rejection would arise. Therefore, it rejects only an unconsecrated sīmā. Just as every village is a village-sīmā, so every river is not a sīmā. However, it is our reasoning, says the teacher, that it shows a diversity of sīmās, such that for each individual bhikkhu there is a water-splash sīmā. The statement, “the water-splash all around of a man of medium build,” is said concerning a single river to show the demarcation of the sīmā at the time when separate groups of four bhikkhus, etc., are performing acts to be done by a quorum of four, and so on. The teachers say that this is also for the purpose of showing the demarcation of separation and non-separation from the three robes, just like the showing of the demarcation of a seven-abbhantara sīmā. Therefore, it is established that even in the absence of a demarcation by water-splash, it is allowable to perform a formal act within a river.

Ayaṃ pana viseso – tattha nāvāgato ce, nāvāyaṃ vuttanayena. Satthagato ce, satthe vuttanayena. So ce atirekacātumāsaniviṭṭho, gāme vuttanayena ticīvarāvippavāso veditabbo. Tatthāpi ayaṃ viseso – sace sattho udakukkhepassa anto hoti, udakukkhepasīmāpamāṇanti eke. Satthova pamāṇanti ācariyā. Sace panettha bahū bhikkhūtiādimhi keci adhiṭṭhānuposathaṃ, keci gaṇuposathaṃ, keci saṅghuposathanti vattukāmatāya “bahū saṅghā”ti avatvā “bhikkhū”ti vuttaṃ. Ūnakaṃ pana na vaṭṭatīti ettha sīmāsambhedasambhavatoti upatissatthero. Ṭhapente hi ūnakaṃ na ṭhapetabbaṃ. “Aṭhapetumpi vaṭṭati evā”ti vuttaṃ. Gacchantiyā panāti ettha “udakukkhepamanatikkamitvā parivattamānāya kātuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti likhitaṃ. Aññissā sīmāya ñattītiādi kiṃ sīmato kammavipattibhayā vuttaṃ[M 0.0459], udāhu parisatoti? Ekakammassa nānāsīmāya asambhavato sīmatoti. Ekakammassa nānāsīmaṭṭhasaṅghena asambhavato parisatotipi eke. “Savanaṃ hāpetī”ti vuttadosappasaṅgatoti no takko. Ekissā hi sīmāya ekaṃ kammaṃ aniṭṭhapento hāpetīti ācariyo.

This, however, is the distinction: if one has gone by boat, the non-separation from the three robes is to be understood in the manner spoken of for a boat. If one has gone with a caravan, it is to be understood in the manner spoken of for a caravan. If that caravan has been established for more than four months, the non-separation from the three robes is to be understood in the manner spoken of for a village. Therein also, this is the distinction: if the caravan is within a water-throw, some say the water-throw boundary is the measure. The teachers say the caravan itself is the measure. In the phrase beginning with "If there are many monks here," because of the desire to speak of some performing the Uposatha by determination, some by a group, and some by the Saṅgha, it is said "monks" without saying "many Saṅghas." Here, regarding "However, a lesser distance is not permissible," the Elder Upatissa says this is "because of the possibility of the overlapping of boundaries." Indeed, those establishing it should not establish a lesser one. It is said, "It is not permissible even not to establish it." Here, regarding "But while it is going," it is written: "It is permissible to perform the act while turning around, without having crossed the water-throw." Regarding the passage beginning with "The motion in another boundary," was this said out of fear of a procedural failure due to the boundary, or was it due to the assembly? It was said "due to the boundary" because of the impossibility of a single formal act in different boundaries. Some say it was said "also due to the assembly" because of the impossibility of a single formal act with a Saṅgha situated in different boundaries. The reasoning that it is because of the consequence of the fault spoken of as "he omits the recitation" is not correct. For the teacher says: One who does not bring a single formal act to completion within a single boundary omits it.

Bahinaditīre jātarukkhassa antonadiyaṃ paviṭṭhasākhāya vāti ettha ca naditīre khāṇukaṃ koṭṭetvāti ettha ca sace pana setu vā setupādā vā bahitīre patiṭṭhitāti ettha ca sīmāsodhanaṃ nāma gāmasīmaṭṭhe hatthapāsānayanaṃ. Khaṇḍasīmāya uṭṭhitarukkhato viyojetvā kātuṃ vaṭṭati. Kasmā? Tīraṭṭhe rukkhe baddhanāvāya gāmo ādhāroti. “Ubhatobhāgena gāmasīmaṃ phusitvā ṭhitasetu khaṇḍasīmāmahāsīmāyo phusitvā ṭhitarukkhena upametabbo”ti ca likhitaṃ. Tattha purimanaye tāva idaṃ vicāretabbaṃ – tādise ṭhāne katakammaṃ kiṃ nadiyaṃ katasaṅkhyaṃ gacchati, udāhu gāmasīmāyaṃ, atha ubhayatthāti? Kiñcettha taṃ ce nadiyaṃ katasaṅkhyaṃ gacchati, udakukkhepasīmāva [V 0.0419] sodhetabbā, na itarā. Atha gāmasīmāyaṃ katasaṅkhyaṃ gacchati, udakukkhepasīmā na sodhetabbā. Yadi ubhayattha katasaṅkhyaṃ gacchati, dvīsu sīmāsu ekakammaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭatīti aniṭṭhappasaṅgo āpajjati. Tato “aññissā sīmāya ñatti, aññissā anussāvanā hotī”ti idañca “khaṇḍasīmāmahāsīmaṭṭhānaṃ kāyasāmaggiyā kammaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti idañcāniṭṭhaṃ āpajjatīti? Ettha vuccate – yathāvuttaṃ kammaṃ ubhayattha katasaṅkhyaṃ gacchati, na ca yathāvuttaṃ aniṭṭhaṃ āpajjati. Kasmā? “Ñattianussāvanānaṃ ekekasīmāyaṃ pavattattā, kārakabhikkhūnaṃ vā ekekasīmāyaṃ ṭhitattā”ti vadanti. Ubhayatthāpi ṭhātuṃ sakkuṇeyyatāya pana taṃ akāraṇaṃ. Ekībhāvaṃ upagatasīmaṭṭhāne katattāti idaṃ acalakāraṇaṃ. Ekībhāvaṃ upagatāsu hi dvīsu nadīgāmasīmāsu kammaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭatīti ca. Sattabbhantarasīmāyaṃ ce nadī hoti, samuddo vā, jātassaro vā. Tesu ṭhitabhikkhu sattabbhantarasīmāyaṃ ṭhitasaṅkhyaṃ na gacchati. Tattha ce nadiādilakkhaṇaṃ appatto dīpako, pāsāṇo, rukkho vā hoti, sattabbhantarasaṅkhyaṃ gacchati. Manussehi vaḷañjanaṭṭhānaṃ ce taṃ hoti, gāmakhettasaṅkhyaṃ gacchati. Kataragāmakhettaṃ? Yato manussā sañcaranti, sabbe ce sañcaranti, visuṃ gāmakhettasaṅkhyaṃ gacchatīti ca ācariyā.

In cases such as a branch of a tree grown on the outer riverbank that has entered into the river, or a post driven on the riverbank, or a bridge or bridge-posts established on the outer bank, what is called 'purification of the boundary' is the bringing of the monks standing in the village boundary into hand's reach. In the case of a separate boundary, it is proper to perform the act after disjoining it from a tree that has grown there. Why? Because the village is the support for a boat tied to a tree standing on the bank. And it is written: 'A bridge standing touching the village boundary on both sides should be compared with a tree standing touching the separate and great boundaries.' There, in the former method, this should first be investigated: In such a place, does an act performed count as done in the river, or in the village boundary, or else in both? And what is the consequence here? If that act counts as done in the river, only the water-throw boundary should be purified, not the other. If it counts as done in the village boundary, the water-throw boundary should not be purified. If it counts as done in both, an undesirable consequence arises, namely that it would be proper to perform one act in two boundaries. From that, does this undesirable consequence arise, namely, 'the motion is in one boundary, and the proclamation is in another'; and does this undesirable consequence arise, namely, 'for those in the separate and great boundaries, it is proper to perform an act with bodily unity'? Here, the reply is given: The aforesaid act counts as done in both, and the aforesaid undesirable consequence does not arise. Why? They say it is 'because the motion and proclamations occur in each respective boundary, or because the officiating monks stand in each respective boundary.' But because it is possible to stand in both places, that is not a reason. 'Because it is performed in a boundary-place that has reached a state of unity'—this is the unshakeable reason. For it is proper to perform an act in the two boundaries, the river-boundary and the village-boundary, that have reached a state of unity. If there is a river, or an ocean, or a natural lake within a seven-abbhantara boundary, a monk standing in them does not count as standing within the seven-abbhantara boundary. If there, there is an island, a rock, or a tree that does not have the characteristics of a river, etc., it counts as within the seven-abbhantara. If that is a place used by people, it counts as a village-field. Which village-field? The one from which people travel. If all travel from there, it counts as a separate village-field, thus say the teachers.

Pacchimanaye [M 0.0460] sace setu nadīlakkhaṇaṭṭhānaṃ aphusitvā ṭhito, gāmasīmāsaṅkhyaṃ gacchati. Tattha eko ce gāmo, taṃ sodhetvā, dvīsu tīresu sace dve, dvepi gāme sodhetvā kammaṃ kātabbaṃ. Evañhi kataṃ ubhayatra kataṃ hoti. Iminā nayena dvīsu nadīsu, jātassaresu ca ekakammapasiddhi veditabbā. Ayaṃ pana nayo khaṇḍasīmāmahāsīmānampi labbhateva. Sace setu nadīlakkhaṇaṭṭhānaṃ phusitvā ṭhito, udakukkhepasīmāpi sodhetabbā.

In the latter method, if a bridge stands without touching the place with the characteristics of a river, it is counted as a village boundary. There, if there is one village, after purifying it, and if there are two villages on the two banks, after purifying both villages, the act should be performed. For an act thus performed is performed in both places. By this method, the validity of a single act in two rivers and in natural lakes should be known. This method, moreover, is indeed applicable to separate and great boundaries. If the bridge stands touching the place with the characteristics of a river, the water-throw boundary must also be purified.

Sīmānameva cekattaṃ, vehāsaṭṭhaṃ vinā gato;

Viditvā ekakammassa, sīmato idamādise.

Indeed, there is a oneness of the boundaries, excluding the one established in the sky. Having understood this for a single act, one should declare this from the boundary.

Ekasīmaṃ dvisīmaṃ vā, tisīmaṃ catusīmakaṃ;

Ekakammaṃ siyā tassa, kopo parisato siyāti.

Whether it concerns one boundary, two boundaries, three, or four boundaries, it would be a single act. There might be agitation from the assembly on account of it.

Ayaṃ panettha viseso – nadiyaṃ karontānaṃ udakukkhepato bahi rukkhādisambandho appamāṇaṃ. Gāme karontānaṃ nadiyaṃ sambandharukkhassa udakukkhepato bahi ṭhitabhikkhu appamāṇaṃ, tato oraṃ pamāṇaṃ. Baddhasīmāya sambandharukkhassa baddhasīmāya ṭhitabhikkhu pamāṇanti [V 0.0420] veditabbaṃ, teneva vuttaṃ “sīmaṃ sodhetvā kammaṃ kātabba”nti. “Sace pana setu vā setupādā vā bahitīre patiṭṭhitā kammaṃ kātuṃ na vaṭṭatī”ti vacanampi pārohādīsu viya sakalasīmāsodhanameva kātabbanti sādheti, vīmaṃsitabbaṃ. Ativuṭṭhikāle panāti ettha ativuṭṭhi nāma yathā cātumāsikāyāti veditabbā, tasmā catumāsaṃ ativuṭṭhiyeva sace hoti, sabbopi oghena otthaṭokāso nadī eva. Atha ekissāpi ativuṭṭhiyā ogho catumāsaṃ tiṭṭhati, sandati vā, bahitīre patiṭṭhitaoghena otthaṭokāso sabbopi nadī eva. Nadiṃ ottharitvā sandanaṭṭhānato paṭṭhāyāti tameva vā nadiṃ aññaṃ vā apubbaṃ vā padesaṃ attano pavattavasena nadilakkhaṇappattaṃ ottharitvā sandanaṭṭhānato paṭṭhāya vaṭṭati. Gāmanigamasīmaṃ ottharitvāti catumāsappavattiṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. “Agamanapatheti tadahu gatapaccāgataṃ kātuṃ asakkuṇeyyake”ti likhitaṃ. Yaṃ pana andhakaṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttaṃ, taṃ na gahetabbaṃ. Kasmā? Nadiyampi taṃdosappasaṅgato. Tipusakādīti ettha ādi-saddena kamaluppalādīnipi saṅgahaṃ gacchanti[M 0.0461]. Sabbopi ajātassaro hoti, gāmasīmāsaṅkhyameva gacchatīti yehi kataṃ, tesaṃ gāmasīmāsaṅkhyaṃ vā, samantato tīraṭṭhagāmehi ce kataṃ, sabbagāmasaṅkhyaṃ vā, aññehi gāmakhettehi asambandhaṭṭhānaṃ ce, visuṃgāmasīmāsaṅkhyaṃ vā gacchatīti attho.

Herein is the distinction: For those performing the act in a river, a connection to trees and so forth outside the water-casting boundary is not a factor. For those performing the act in a village, a monk standing outside the water-casting boundary of a tree connected to the river is not a factor; within that, he is a factor. It should be understood that for a tree connected to a fixed boundary, a monk standing within the fixed boundary is a factor. Therefore, it is said, “The act should be performed after purifying the boundary.” The statement, “If, however, a bridge or bridge foundations are established on the far bank, it is not permissible to perform the act,” also establishes that, as in the case of river-bank growths and so forth, the entire boundary must be purified; this should be investigated. Regarding 'at the time of excessive rain': here, 'excessive rain' should be understood as that which causes water to stand for four months. Therefore, if there is indeed excessive rain for four months, the entire area covered by the flood is the river itself. Furthermore, if a flood from even a single excessive rain stands for four months, or flows, the entire area on the far bank covered by the established flood is the river itself. Regarding 'having overflowed the river, from the place of flowing': it is permissible from the place where it overflows and flows, whether it be that same river, or another, or an unprecedented area that, by its own flowing, has attained the characteristics of a river. 'Having overflowed the village or town boundary' is said with reference to a four-month flow. Regarding 'an impassable path': it is written, '[this means] a place where one is unable to go and return on that same day.' However, what is stated in the Andhakaṭṭhakathā should not be accepted. Why? Because the same fault would apply to a river as well. Regarding 'Tipusaka, etc.': here, by the word 'etc.', lotuses, water lilies, and so forth are also included. All of this is a natural lake. It is counted only as a village boundary. For those by whom it was established, it is counted as their village boundary; or, if it was established by the villages situated on the bank all around, it is counted as the boundary of all villages; or, if it is a place unconnected with other village-fields, it is counted as a separate village boundary. This is the meaning.

148. Saṃsaṭṭhaviṭapāti iminā āsannattaṃ dīpeti, tena padesasambhindanā idha sambhedoti dīpeti. So pana vaḍḍhanto sīmāsaṅkaraṃ karotīti baddhasīmaṭṭhānappavesanavasena “ekadesabaddhasīmā”ti vattabbato saṅkaradoso hoti. Na, bhikkhave, sīmāya sīmā sambhinditabbāti ettha “paṭhamaṃ baddhasīmāya pacchā attanā bandhitabbasīmā na sambhinditabbā”ti eke adhippāyaṃ saṃvaṇṇayanti. Paṭhamaṃ sammatasīmāyaṃ sambhedābhāvato svādhippāyo ajjhottharaṇena yujjati, tasmā pacchā bandhitabbasīmāya paṭhamaṃ baddhasīmā na sambhinditabbā. Sakalaṃ vā ekadesato vā nimittānaṃ antokaraṇena paṭhamaṃ baddhasīmāya sīmantarike akittetvā sammannanato hi sambhindati nāma, paresaṃ baddhasīmaṃ sakalaṃ vā ekadesato vā nimittānaṃ antokaraṇena ajjhottharati nāma, tenevāha “sīmaṃ sammannantena sīmantarikaṃ ṭhapetvā”tiādi. Tassattho – paṭhamaṃ baddhasīmāya sīmantarikaṃ pacchā bandhitabbasīmāya nimittabhūtaṃ ṭhapetvā pacchā sīmaṃ sammannitunti. Imā dvepi vipattiyo bhikkhubhikkhunīsīmānaṃ aññamaññaṃ na sambhavanti. So pana vaḍḍhanto sīmāsaṅkaraṃ karotīti ettha kevalaṃ sīmāsaṅkarameva karoti. Tasmiṃ katakammāni na kuppantīti keci, taṃ nayuttaṃ sākhāpārohachedanasīmāsodhanānaṃ vuttattā. Idaṃ sabbaṃ suṭṭhu vicāretvā garukule payirupāsitvā gahetabbayuttakaṃ gahetabbaṃ, itaraṃ chaḍḍetabbaṃ.

148. “Saṃsaṭṭhaviṭapā” (intermingled branches) indicates proximity; by this, it indicates that the intermingling of a region is here called “sambheda” (overlap). However, if it expands and causes boundary confusion, then because it is called “ekadesabaddhasīmā” (partially fixed boundary) by way of entering a fixed boundary area, the fault of confusion arises. In “Monks, a boundary should not overlap another boundary,” some explain the meaning as: “A boundary that is to be fixed later by oneself should not overlap a boundary fixed earlier.” Since there is no overlap in a boundary agreed upon first, that interpretation is consistent with encroachment. Therefore, a boundary fixed earlier should not be overlapped by a boundary to be fixed later. For it is called “overlapping” when, by including the markers of a boundary fixed earlier, either entirely or partially, one establishes a boundary without designating a boundary interval. It is called “encroaching” when one includes the markers of another’s fixed boundary, either entirely or partially. Therefore, he said, “When establishing a boundary, one should leave a boundary interval,” and so forth. Its meaning is: one should establish the later boundary after having set aside the boundary interval of the boundary fixed first, which serves as a marker for the boundary to be fixed later. These two faults do not occur mutually between the boundaries of monks and nuns. However, regarding 'if it expands and causes boundary confusion': it only creates boundary confusion. Some say that acts performed within it are not invalidated, but that is not proper, because the cutting of branches and offshoots and the purification of the boundary have been stated. All this should be carefully considered, and after attending upon one's teachers, what is proper to be accepted should be accepted, and the rest should be discarded.

Uposathabhedādikathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Discourse on the Division of the Uposatha and so forth

149. “Dveme[V 0.0421], bhikkhave, uposathā”ti tadā sāmaggīuposathassa ananuññātattā vuttaṃ. Sāmaggīuposathassa pubbakicce “ajjuposatho sāmaggī”ti vattabbaṃ, na ca kammavācāya bhagavatā payogo dassito, pāḷinayato aṭṭhakathācariyehi uddisitabbakkamo dassito. Tathā pañcannaṃ pātimokkhuddesānaṃ uddesakkamo siddhoti veditabbaṃ. Tayo vā dve vā pātimokkhaṃ uddisanti, adhammena samaggaṃ nāma hotīti ettha kāmaṃ [M 0.0462] saṅghassa sāmaggī nāma hoti vaggakathāya yathākammaṃ sāmaggīvavatthānato. Tathāpi vaggapaṭipakkhabhāvena samaggaṃ, samaggapaṭipakkhabhāvena ca vaggaṃ nāma kataṃ. Āveṇikato vā gaṇakammādisambhavato, tassa ca samaggavaggabhāvasambhavato vuttanti veditabbaṃ. Dhammena vagganti ettha pārisuddhikaraṇaṃ dhammikaṃ, saṅghasseva chandāgamanaṃ, na gaṇassāti katvā vaggaṃ nāma hoti. “Ekavāraṃ kataṃ sukataṃ, āpattiṃ pana āpajjati, puna kātuṃ na labhantī”ti vadanti. “Pañcasu ekassa chandaṃ āharitvā catūhi pātimokkhaṃ uddisituṃ vaṭṭatī”ti vadanti, taṃ yuttaṃ, chandahārake bhikkhūnaṃ santikaṃ patte tena saṅgho pahoti, tasmā chando saṅghappatto hotīti katvā vuttaṃ.

149. “These two, bhikkhus, are Uposathas”—this was said at a time when the communal Uposatha had not been permitted. For the preliminary duty of the communal Uposatha, it should be announced, “Today is the communal Uposatha,” but the procedure for the formal motion was not shown by the Blessed One; the order to be recited was indicated by the commentary teachers according to the Pāli method. Similarly, it should be understood that the order for the five Pātimokkha recitations is established. In the case of 'Whether three or two recite the Pātimokkha, it is called “united by unrighteousness”': indeed, it is called unity of the Sangha, since in the matter of a faction, unity is established according to the formal act. Nevertheless, by being the opposite of division, it is called united, and by being the opposite of unity, it is called divided. Or, it should be understood that this was said because of the separate possibility of group-acts and so on, and because of the possibility of that act being one of unity or division. In the case of 'divided by Dhamma': the act of purification is righteous; the giving of consent belongs only to the Sangha, not to a group, and for this reason, it is called divided. Some say: “Done once, it is well done. But one incurs an offense; they are not able to do it again.” Others say: “Among five, having brought the consent of one, it is permissible for four to recite the Pātimokkha.” That is proper, for when the consent-bringer has arrived in the presence of the bhikkhus, with him the Sangha is sufficient. Therefore, it is said that the consent has reached the Sangha.

Pātimokkhuddesakathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Discourse on the Recitation of the Pātimokkha

150. Mātikāṭṭhakathāyaṃ (kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. nidānavaṇṇanā) “suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho…pe… āvikatā hissa phāsu hoti, tatthāyasmante pucchāmi…pe… tasmā tuṇhī. Evametaṃ dhārayāmī’ti vatvā ‘uddiṭṭhaṃ kho āyasmanto nidāna’ntiādinā nayena avasese sutena sāvite uddiṭṭho hotī”ti vuttattā “evametaṃ dhārayāmīti sutā kho panāyasmantehī”ti ettha “dhārayāmī”ti vatvā “uddiṭṭhaṃ kho āyasmanto nidāna”nti vacanaṃ saṃkhittanti gahetabbaṃ, teneva khuddakapeyyālavasena likhitaṃ. Evaṃ mātikāṭṭhakathāyampi “āvikatā hissa phāsu hoti, tatthāyasmante”ti etthāpi “uddiṭṭhaṃ kho āyasmanto nidāna”nti vacanaṃ saṃkhittanti gahetabbanti eke. Keci “avivadamānehi sikkhitabba’nti vutte nidānuddeso niṭṭhito nāma hoti, tasmā anāvikaronto āpattiṃ āpajjatī”ti vadanti, taṃ na yuttaṃ. Kasmā? “Nidānaṃ uddisitvā”ti niṭṭhānavacanena hi nidānassa niṭṭhitabhāvo vutto, nidānāvasāne ca āpatti vuttāti. “Sarabhaññaṃ nāma sarena bhaṇana”nti likhitaṃ. Sajjhāyaṃ adhiṭṭhahitvāti “sajjhāyaṃ karomī”ti cittaṃ uppādetvā. “Āpucchāmīti vuttamattena kathetuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti [V 0.0422] vadanti. Taṃ tuṇhībhāve yujjati. “Athāpi lābhādinā abhibhūto vāreti, taṃ na pamāṇa”nti vadanti. Eseva nayoti kathento yadi vicchindati, puna āpucchitabbanti.

150. In the Mātikāṭṭhakathā, because it is said: 'Having stated, «Let the Saṅgha, venerable sirs, listen to me… for it is comfortable for him to declare it openly. Therefore, I ask the venerable ones… therefore, be silent. I remember it thus,» it is considered recited when the remainder has been announced by hearing, in the manner beginning with, «Venerable sirs, the introduction has been recited.»' Therefore, in the phrase, «I remember it thus. Venerable sirs, you have indeed heard...,» it should be understood that after saying «I remember it,» the statement «Venerable sirs, the introduction has been recited» is abbreviated; for that reason, it is written in the form of a minor abbreviation. Thus, some hold that also in the Mātikāṭṭhakathā, in the phrase «for it is comfortable for him to declare it openly. Therefore, I ask the venerable ones,» the statement «Venerable sirs, the introduction has been recited» is abbreviated. Some say: 'When it is said, «One should train without disputing,» the recitation of the introduction is considered finished. Therefore, a monk who does not make it manifest commits an offense.' That is not correct. Why? Because by the concluding words, «Having recited the introduction,» the completion of the introduction is stated, and an offense is mentioned at the end of the introduction. It is written: 'Sarabhañña is reciting with intonation.' 'Having determined on recitation' means having aroused the thought, 'I will do the recitation.' They say: 'It is allowable to speak merely by having said, «I ask leave.»' That is appropriate in the case of silence. They say: 'If, being overcome by gain and so forth, he should prevent it, that is not a valid measure.' This is the method: if one interrupts while speaking, one should ask leave again.

Adhammakammapaṭikkosanādikathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Discourse on the Rejection of Unrighteous Actions and So Forth

154. “Tesaṃ [M 0.0463] anupaddavatthāyā”ti saṅgho saṅghassa kammaṃ na karoti, aññopi upaddavo bahūnaṃ hoti, tasmā vuttaṃ.

154. 'For their non-affliction': the Saṅgha does not perform an act of the Saṅgha, and another affliction also arises for many; therefore, it is said.

Pātimokkhuddesakaajjhesanādikathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Discourse on the Request for the Pātimokkha Reciter and So Forth

155. “Therādhikaṃ pātimokkha”nti vatvāpi pacchā avisesena “yo tattha byatto paṭibalo, tassādheyya”nti vuttattā “bhante”ti vacanaṃ therassāpi atthīti siddhaṃ hoti. “Gacchāvuso saṃkhittena vā vitthārena vā”ti vacanato asatipi antarāye thāmaṃ pamāṇanti siddhaṃ hoti.

155. Even though it was said, 'The Pātimokkha is under the authority of the senior monk,' because it was later stated without distinction, 'Whoever there is who is skilled and able, to him it should be entrusted,' it is established that the saying 'Venerable sir' is also for a senior monk. Because of the statement, 'Go, friend, either in brief or in detail,' it is established that even when there is no obstacle, strength is the measure.

Disaṃgamikādivatthukathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Story of Those Going to Other Regions and so forth

163. “Sacassa saddhiṃcarā bhikkhuupaṭṭhākā atthī”ti pāṭho. “Utuvasseti utusaṃvacchare hemantagimhesū”ti likhitaṃ.

163. There is the reading: 'If he has companion monks and monk-attendants.' It is written: 'Regarding the word utuvassa, it means in the seasonal year, in winter and summer.'

Pārisuddhidānakathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Discourse on the Giving of Purity

164. Pārisuddhiṃ dammīti “sāpattiko therānaṃ deti, sampajānamusāvāde dukkaṭaṃ sambhavatī”ti ācariyena likhitaṃ. Kiṃ nu kho kāraṇaṃ? Sampajānamusāvādena dukkaṭāpatti nāma kevalaṃ bhagavatā vuttattā akiriyasamuṭṭhānā hotīti. “Pārisuddhiṃ dammī”ti ettha pana kiriyā paññāyati, tasmā sampajānamusāvāde pācittiyaṃ viya dissati, suṭṭhu upaparikkhitabbaṃ. Mahantā hi te ācariyā nāma. Tattha “dammī”ti attano uposathakammanibbattinimittaṃ vuttaṃ. “Harā”ti ca “ārocehī”ti ca hārakassa anārocanapaccayā dukkaṭamocanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Eseva nayo chandadānepi. Tattha “dammī”ti attano cittasāmaggidīpanavacanaṃ, sesaṃ vuttanayameva, evaṃ upatissatthero vaṇṇeti. Atha vā paṭhamaṃ samaggabhāvaṃ [V 0.0423] sandhāya, dutiyaṃ pacchā vidhātabbabhāvaṃ, tatiyaṃ chandahārakassa dukkaṭamocanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Ubhayatthāpi “saṅghappatto pakkamatī”tiādivacanato saṅghe samagge eva chandapārisuddhidānaṃ ruhati, nāsamaggeti siddhaṃ. “Saṅghappatto ukkhittako paṭijānāti, āhaṭā hoti pārisuddhī”tiādivacanato ukkhittakādīnampi chandapārisuddhidānaṃ ruhatīti siddhaṃ, tañca kho [M 0.0464] pakatattasaññāya, no aññathāti takko. Jānitvā sāmaṇerassa dinne na yāti, āpatti ca, ajānitvā dinne yāti ca, anāpattīti eke. Biḷālasaṅkhalikā nāma pārisuddhīti ettha saṅkhalikā nāma anantarena sambajjhati, aññena ca saṅkhalikenāti kevalaṃ saṅkhalikā pārisuddhi nāma hotīti upatissatthero. Evaṃ sante visesanaṃ niratthakaṃ hoti. Biḷālasaṅkhalikā baddhāva hoti antogehe eva sampayojanattā. Yathā sā na katthaci gacchati, tathā sāpi na katthaci gacchatīti kira adhippāyo.

164. Regarding 'I give purity,' it is written by the teacher: 'A monk who has an offense gives it to the elders; due to intentional false speech, a `dukkaṭa` offense should arise.' What, then, is the reason? It is because the `dukkaṭa` offense for intentional false speech arises from non-action, solely because it was stated by the Blessed One. But here, in the phrase 'I give purity,' action is apparent; therefore, in the case of intentional false speech, it appears like a `pācittiya` offense and should be thoroughly examined. For those teachers are indeed great. There, 'I give' is spoken for the purpose of completing one's own Uposatha ceremony. And 'Take' and 'Announce' are said for the purpose of releasing the bearer from a `dukkaṭa` offense due to not announcing. This same method applies also in the giving of consent. There, 'I give' is a statement indicating one's own unity of mind; the rest is by the method already stated. Thus the Elder Upatissa explains. Alternatively, the first part refers to the state of harmony, the second to what is to be arranged afterwards, and the third is said for the purpose of releasing the consent-bearer from a `dukkaṭa` offense. In both cases, from the statement 'having reached the Sangha, he departs,' etc., it is established that the giving of consent and purity is valid only when the Sangha is in harmony, not when it is not. From the statement, 'Having reached the Sangha, a suspended monk acknowledges, "the purity has been brought,"' etc., it is established that the giving of consent and purity is valid even for suspended monks and others. And that is so only with the perception of being a monk in good standing, not otherwise—this is the reasoning. Some say that if it is knowingly given to a novice, it is not conveyed and there is an offense; if unknowingly given, it is conveyed and there is no offense. Regarding 'cat's-chain purity,' the Elder Upatissa says that a 'chain' is connected to the adjacent one and to another chain, and so it is simply called a 'chain-purity.' If this is so, the qualifier becomes meaningless. A cat's chain is always bound only within the house because of its being attached there. The intended meaning, it seems, is that just as that chain does not go anywhere, so too this purity does not go anywhere.

Chandadānādikathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Discourse on the Giving of Consent and so forth

165-7. “Chandaṃ datvā khaṇḍasīmaṃ vā sīmantarikaṃ vā bahisīmaṃ vā gantvā āgato bhikkhu kammaṃ na kopeti, tasmā gamikabhikkhūnaṃ chandaṃ gaṇhitvā khaṇḍasīmaṃ bandhitvā puna vihārasīmaṃ bandhituṃ tesaṃ chandaṃ na gaṇhantī”ti vadanti. “Muhuttaṃ ekamantaṃ hothā”tiādivacanato yaṃ kiñci bhikkhukammaṃ gahaṭṭhādīsu hatthapāsagatesu na vaṭṭatīti siddhaṃ. Nissīmanti bahisīmaṃ. Tassa sammutidānakiccaṃ natthīti tasmiṃ satipi vaṭṭatīti attho. Āsanena saha udakanti attho. Pannarasopīti api-saddo cātuddasiṃ sampiṇḍeti, tena vuttaṃ mahāaṭṭhakathāyaṃ “yadi no eta”nti. “Ajja me uposatho pannaraso”ti adhiṭṭhānaṃ sadā na kiñci, na aññathāti eke.

165-7. 'A monk who, having given consent, goes to a split boundary, or an intermediate boundary, or an outer boundary and returns does not invalidate the formal act. Therefore,' they say, 'after taking the consent of the monks residing in the village and establishing a split boundary, they do not take their consent again to establish the monastery boundary.' From the Pāḷi text beginning with, 'Be aside for a moment,' it is established that any formal act of the monks is not allowable when householders and so on are within arm's reach. `Nissīmaṃ` means an outer boundary. Regarding the statement, 'There is no duty of giving formal consent for it,' the meaning is that it is allowable even if that mad monk is present. The meaning is: water together with the seat. In the word `pannarasopi`, the particle `api` includes the fourteenth; therefore, it is said in the Mahā-aṭṭhakathā, 'If it is not this...' Some say that the determination, 'Today is my Uposatha, the fifteenth,' is always so, not sometimes, and not otherwise.

Āpattipaṭikammavidhikathādivaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourse on the Procedure for Making Amends for Offenses, and so on.

169-170. Paṭidesemīti yāya kāyaci bhāsāya vutte desanā ca paṭiggaho ca hotiyeva diṭṭhāvikammena visuddhiyā vuttattāti keci. Vematikena “ahaṃ, bhante, ekissā thullaccayāpattiyā vematiko, yadā nibbematiko bhavissāmi, tadā taṃ āpattiṃ paṭikarissāmī”ti vattabbaṃ. Evaṃ kate yāva nibbematiko na hoti, tāva sabhāgāpattiṃ paṭiggahetuṃ na labhati, aññesañca kammānaṃ parisuddho nāma hoti. Puna nibbematiko hutvā desetabbaṃ. Na cāti neva pāḷiyaṃ na aṭṭhakathāyaṃ atthi, desite pana doso natthīti. Tathā ito [V 0.0424] vuṭṭhahitvā taṃ āpattiṃ paṭikarissāmīti ettha ca sakalasaṅghe sabhāgāpattiṃ [M 0.0465] āpanne, vematike ca. Tathā ca “sabbo saṅgho sabhāgāpattiṃ āpajjitvā yadā suddhaṃ passissatī”ti, “tadā tassa santike taṃ āpattiṃ paṭikarissatī’ti vatvā ‘uposathaṃ kātuṃ labhatī”ti ca likhitaṃ.

169-170. Some say that regarding the phrase, 'I confess' (Paṭidesemi), when it is spoken in any language whatsoever, both the confession and the acceptance certainly occur, because purification through a formal act done in one's presence has been stated. By a monk who is in doubt, it should be said: 'Venerable sir, I am in doubt about a certain thullaccaya offense. When I become free from doubt, I will then make amends for that offense.' When this is done, as long as he is not free from doubt, he is not permitted to accept a confession of a similar offense, and he is called 'purified' for other formal acts. Again, having become free from doubt, it should be confessed. The phrase 'na ca' is not found in the Pāḷi nor in the Aṭṭhakathā, but there is no fault when it is confessed. Similarly, this applies in the case of the resolution, 'Having risen from this, I will make amends for that offense,' when the entire Saṅgha has incurred a similar offense, and when one is in doubt. And so it is written that, having said, 'When the entire Saṅgha, having incurred a similar offense, sees a pure monk, then in his presence he will make amends for that offense,' he is permitted to perform the Uposatha.

Anāpattipannarasakādikathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourse on the Fifteen Points of Non-Offense, and so on.

172-3. “Atthaññe”ti pubbavāre, “athaññe”ti pacchāvāre pāṭho. Sīmaṃ okkante vā okkamante vā passanti. Dhammasaññino pana aññāṇena honti. “Vematikapannarasakaṃ uttānamevā”ti pāṭho.

172-3. In the earlier section, the reading is 'atthaññe'; in the later section, the reading is 'athaññe'. They see them either having entered or while entering the boundary. But those who perceive it as a valid formal act are so through ignorance. 'The fifteen points concerning doubt are indeed obvious'—this is the reading.

Sīmokkantikapeyyālakathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourse on the Sīmokkantika Abbreviated Passage.

178. “Na akāmā dātabbā”tivacanato icchāya sati dātabbāti siddhaṃ.

178. From the statement, “It should not be given unwillingly,” it is established that it should be given when there is willingness.

Liṅgādidassanakathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourse on Seeing the Marks, and so on.

180. Nābhivitarantīti ettha laddhinānāsaṃvāsakā kira te. Kammanānāsaṃvāsakañhi diṭṭhiṃ paṭinissajjāpetvā tassa osāraṇakammaṃ kātabbaṃ. Evañhi kate tena saddhiṃ uposathaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭati. Itarena laddhinissajjanamattena kātunti vuttaṃ. Āpattiyā adassane appaṭikamme ukkhittakañca diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge ukkhittakañca jānitvā tena saddhiṃ karontassa pācittiyaṃ, tasmā ime ukkhittānuvattakāti veditabbāti eke.

180. Herein (in the phrase 'nābhivitaranti'), they are indeed those of different communion based on doctrine (laddhinānāsaṃvāsakā). Indeed, for one of different communion based on formal acts (kammanānāsaṃvāsaka), after having made him renounce his view, the act of rehabilitation (osāraṇakamma) should be performed. For only when this is done is it allowable to perform the Uposatha with him. With the other one (i.e., the one of different communion based on doctrine), it is said that it is allowable to perform it merely by the renunciation of the view. For one who, knowing a monk has been suspended for not seeing an offense and for not making amends, or a monk has been suspended for not relinquishing a wrong view, performs (the Uposatha) together with him, there is a Pācittiya offense. Therefore, these should be known as followers of the suspended—thus say some.

Nagantabbagantabbavārakathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourse on the Section of What Should Not Be Gone To and What Should Be Gone To.

181. Na gantabboti kiṃ sandhāya? “Aññatra saṅghenā”ti vacanato yasmiṃ vihāre sataṃ bhikkhū viharanti, te sabbe kenacideva karaṇīyena dasa dasa hutvā visuṃ visuṃ nānāudakukkhepasīmādīsu ṭhatvā uposathaṃ kātuṃ labhanti. Navakammasālādikā nānāsīmākoṭi uposathādhiṭṭhānatthaṃ sīmāpi nadīpi na gantabbā. Garukaṃ pātimokkhuddesaṃ vissajjitvā lahukassa akattabbattā “aññatra saṅghenā”ti vacanaṃ sādheti. Tattha “yasmiṃ āvāse [M 0.0466] uposathakārakā [V 0.0425] …pe… akatvā na gantabbo”ti vacanato vissaṭṭhauposathāpi āvāsā gantuṃ vaṭṭatīti siddhaṃ. “Tato pārisuddhiuposathakaraṇatthaṃ vissaṭṭhauposathā gantuṃ vaṭṭati, khaṇḍasīmaṃ vā pavisitunti apare vadantī”ti vuttaṃ. Iminā neva uposathantarāyoti “attano uposathantarāyo”ti likhitaṃ.

181. With reference to what was 'One should not go' said? Because of the statement 'Except for the Sangha,' in whatever monastery a hundred monks reside, if all of them, due to some duty, form groups of ten and, staying in various separate water-throwing boundaries and so on, they may perform the Uposatha. For the purpose of determining the Uposatha, one should not go to a new work hall, etc., nor to various boundary limits, nor to a boundary, nor to a river. Because, having abandoned the weighty recitation of the Pātimokkha, a lesser act should not be performed, this establishes the statement 'Except for the Sangha.' Therein, because of the statement 'In whatever residence the Uposatha-performers... without having performed it, one should not go,' it is established that even a monk whose Uposatha is excused is permitted to go from the residence. It is stated: 'Therefore, for the purpose of performing the Uposatha of purity, it is permissible for a monk whose Uposatha is excused to go, or to enter a broken boundary—thus say other teachers.' Regarding the phrase 'By this, there is no obstacle to the Uposatha,' it is written: 'For oneself, there is no obstacle to the Uposatha.'

Vajjanīyapuggalasandassanakathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourse on Pointing Out Persons to Be Avoided.

183. “Antimavatthuṃ ajjhāpannassa nisinnaparisāya kalahādibhayena nāhaṃ karissāmī”ti cittaṃ uppādetvā nisīdituṃ vaṭṭati. Aññakamme tassa nisinnaparisāya āpatti natthīti eke. “Na ca, bhikkhave, anuposathe uposatho kātabbo aññatra saṅghasāmaggiyā”ti (mahāva. 183) vacanato sāmaggīdivaso anuposathadivasoti atthato vuttaṃ viya dissati. “Dveme, bhikkhave, uposathā”ti vuttavacanavasenetaṃ vuttaṃ, aññathā parivārapāḷiyā virujjhatīti ācariyā. Cātuddasiyaṃ, pannarasiyaṃ vā ce saṅgho samaggo hoti, “ajjuposatho sāmaggī”ti avatvā pakatinīhāreneva kattabbanti dassanatthaṃ yathādesanā katāti no takko. Aññathā yathāvuttadvaye ce sāmaggī hoti, tattha uposathaṃ akatvā anuposathadivase eva sāmaggīuposatho kātabboti āpajjati. Aññathā pubbe paṭisiddhattā idāni paṭisedhanakiccaṃ natthi. “Na, bhikkhave, devasikaṃ pātimokkhaṃ uddisitabba”nti (mahāva. 136) pubbe hi vuttaṃ. Atha vā “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, uposathe pātimokkhaṃ uddisitu”nti pubbe vuttattā “sakiṃ pakkhassa cātuddase vā pannarase vā”ti ca “dveme, bhikkhave, uposathā”ti (mahāva. 149) ca pacchā vuttattā tato aññasmiṃ divase uposatho na kātabboti atthato āpannaṃ aniṭṭhaṃ, sati saṅghasāmaggiyā añño divaso pakativasena anuposathopi uposathadivaso nāma hotīti dassanavasena nivāretumpi evaṃdesanā katāti veditabbā.

183. It is proper for one who has transgressed a final offense to sit down after arousing the thought, 'I will not act due to fear of quarrels and so on in the seated assembly.' Some say there is no offense for him in a seated assembly during another formal act. Because of the Pāḷi which states, 'Monks, the Uposatha should not be performed on a non-Uposatha day, except for the harmony of the Saṅgha' (Mahāvagga 183), it appears as if it is said, in terms of meaning, that the day of harmony is a non-Uposatha day. This is stated by the power of the words, 'Monks, there are these two Uposathas.' Otherwise, it contradicts the Parivāra Pāḷi, say the teachers. If the Saṅgha is in harmony on the fourteenth or fifteenth day, it should be performed in the normal manner without saying, 'Today is the harmony Uposatha.' That the teaching was given to show this is our reasoning. Otherwise, if there is harmony on the two aforementioned days, the meaning would follow that the harmony Uposatha should be performed only on a non-Uposatha day, without performing the Uposatha on those days. Alternatively, since it was prohibited before, there is now no need for prohibition. For it was indeed said before, 'Monks, the Pātimokkha should not be recited daily' (Mahāvagga 136). Or, because it was said before, 'Monks, I allow the recitation of the Pātimokkha on the Uposatha day,' and because it was said later, 'once a fortnight, on the fourteenth or the fifteenth,' and 'Monks, there are these two Uposathas' (Mahāvagga 149), the meaning that follows is that the Uposatha should not be performed on another day, which is an undesirable conclusion. It should be understood that this teaching was given also to prevent this by way of showing that when there is harmony in the Saṅgha, another day, even one that is by nature a non-Uposatha day, becomes what is called an Uposatha day.

Uposathakkhandhakavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Uposatha Chapter is Completed.

3. Vassūpanāyikakkhandhakavaṇṇanā

3. The Commentary on the Chapter on Entering the Rains-residence.

Vassūpanāyikānujānanakathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Account of Allowing the Entering of the Rains-residence.

184. Mahāaṭṭhakathāyampi [V 0.0426][M 0.0467] “saṅkāsayissantī”ti pāṭho, dīpavāsino “saṅkāpayissantī”ti paṭhanti kira. “Kati nu kho vassūpanāyikā”ti cintāyaṃ “kiṃ nimitta”nti vutte “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, vassaṃ upagantu”nti yaṃ vassūpagamanaṃ vuttaṃ, taṃ “imaṃ temāsaṃ vassaṃ upemī”ti vatvā upagantabbaṃ. Vassānamāsā ca cattāro. Tattha paṭhamaṃ temāsaṃ, pacchimaṃ temāsanti duvidhaṃ temāsaṃ. Tenāyaṃ tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ cintā ahosi.

184. In the Mahāaṭṭhakathā also, the reading is 'saṅkāsayissantī'; the residents of the Island, it is said, recite it as 'saṅkāpayissantī'. Regarding the thought, 'How many enterings upon the Rains are there?', when it was asked, 'What is the reason?', the entering upon the Rains which was spoken of as, 'Bhikkhus, I allow you to enter upon the Rains,' is to be undertaken by saying, 'I enter upon the Rains for this three-month period.' And the months of the Rains are four. Among them, the three-month period is of two kinds: the first three-month period and the last three-month period. For that reason, this thought arose in those bhikkhus.

Vassānecārikāpaṭikkhepādikathāvaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Discourse Concerning the Prohibition of Wandering During the Rains, etc.

185. Anapekkhagamanena vā aññattha aruṇaṃ uṭṭhāpanena vā āpatti veditabbāti ettha paṭhamaṃ tāva so sattāhaṃ anāgatāya pavāraṇāya sakaraṇīyo pakkamati. “Āgaccheyya vā so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu taṃ āvāsaṃ na vā āgaccheyya, tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno purimikā ca paññāyati, paṭissave ca anāpattī”ti vacanato oraṃ sandhāya vuttanti veditabbaṃ. Tathā hi “so tadaheva akaraṇīyo pakkamati, sakaraṇīyo pakkamati, tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno purimikā ca na paññāyati, paṭissave ca āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti (mahāva. 207) vuttaṃ.

185. Herein, regarding the statement that 'an offense is to be understood through departing without taking leave or by causing the dawn to arise elsewhere,' firstly, a bhikkhu departs on business when the Pavāraṇā has not yet arrived within seven days. Because it is said, 'Whether that bhikkhu, O bhikkhus, returns to that residence or not, for that bhikkhu, O bhikkhus, the first period of the Rains is established, and in regard to his promise, there is no offense,' it should be understood that this was said in reference to a period of less than seven days. For indeed, it is said: 'He departs on that very day without business... for that bhikkhu, O bhikkhus, the first period is not established, and in regard to his promise, there is an offense of dukkaṭa.'

Sattāhakaraṇīyānujānanakathāvaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Discourse Concerning the Permission for a Seven-Day Task

187-8. Dutiyaṃ pana “so taṃ sattāhaṃ bahiddhā vītināmeti, tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno purimikā ca na paññāyati, paṭissave ca āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti vacanato sattāhato [V 0.0427] paraṃ veditabbaṃ. Tathā hi “so taṃ sattāhaṃ anto sannivattaṃ karoti, tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno purimikā ca paññāyati, paṭissave ca anāpattī”ti (mahāva. 207) vuttaṃ. Satipi kāraṇadvaye vassacchedakāraṇābhāve āpatti veditabbā, tasmā tīṇipi etāni vacanāni yathāsambhavaṃ yojitāni viggahāni honti. Tīṇi parihīnānīti tāsaṃ natthitāya.

Secondly, because of the statement, 'He spends that seven-day period outside; for that bhikkhu, O bhikkhus, the first period is not established, and in regard to his promise, there is an offense of dukkaṭa,' it should be understood as referring to a time beyond seven days. For indeed, it is said: 'He returns within that seven-day period; for that bhikkhu, O bhikkhus, the first period is established, and in regard to his promise, there is no offense.' Even when there are two reasons, if there is no reason for breaking the Rains-residence, an offense is to be understood. Therefore, these three statements, applied as is suitable, become analyses. The statement 'The three are deficient' is said because of their (the bhikkhunīs') non-existence.

Pahiteyevaanujānanakathāvaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Discourse on Allowing Only When Sent

199. “Anujānāmi [M 0.0468] bhikkhave, saṅghakaraṇīyena gantuṃ, sattāhaṃ sannivatto kātabbo”ti vacanato antovasse saṃhārikabhāvena gantuṃ vaṭṭati. Tattha dhammachandavasenapi āgate saṅghassa āyamukhaṃ vinassati. Tato “senāsanāni katvā”ti ca vuttaṃ. Āgatanti āgamanaṃ. Bhāvettha tapaccayoyaṃ. Saṅghakaraṇīyena gantunti ettha “senāsanapaṭisaṃyuttesu eva saṅghakaraṇīyesu, na aññesū”ti dhammasiritthero vadati kira. Aṭṭhakathāyampi taṃ padaṃ uddharitvā “yaṃ kiñci uposathāgārādīsu senāsanesū”tiādinā senāsanameva dassitaṃ, tasmā upaparikkhitabbaṃ.

199. Because of the statement, 'Bhikkhus, I allow you to go for Sangha business; a return within seven days must be made,' it is permissible to go during the Rains-residence by reason of having a duty to be undertaken. In that case, even when they come out of zeal for the Dhamma, the Sangha's source of income is destroyed. Therefore, it is also said, 'having prepared the lodgings.' `Āgataṃ` means 'coming'; this is a `ta`-suffix in the sense of an abstract state. Regarding the phrase 'to go for Sangha business,' it is said that the Elder Dhammasiri states, 'It is permissible to go only for Sangha business connected with lodgings, not for others.' In the Commentary also, having extracted that phrase, only lodging is shown by the text beginning with 'whatever lodgings in the Uposatha hall, etc.' Therefore, this should be investigated.

Animantitena gantuṃ na vaṭṭatīti tassa ratticchedo ca dukkaṭāpatti ca hoti, taṃ “vassacchedo”ti ca vadanti. Nimantitoyeva nāma hotīti ettha upāsakehi “imasmiṃ nāma divase dānādīni karoma, sabbe sannipatantū”ti katāyapi katikāya gantuṃ vaṭṭati. Pavāraṇāya navamito paṭṭhāya paṃsukūlikacīvaraṃ pariyesituṃ kāvīrapaṭṭane viya sabbesaṃ gantuṃ vaṭṭati anusaṃvaccharaṃ niyamato upāsakehi sajjitvā ṭhapanato. Vuttampi cetaṃ andhakaṭṭhakathāyaṃ “bhikkhusaṅghena vā katikā katā ‘samantā bhikkhū gacchantū’ti, ghosanaṃ vā kataṃ upāsakehi, tattha gacchantassa ratticchedo natthīti tathā ‘anusaṃvaccharaṃ āgacchantū’ti sakiṃ nimantitepi vaṭṭatī”ti ca “cīvarakālato paṭṭhāya niyamaṃ katvā samantato āgatānaṃ sajjetvā dānato kāvīrapaṭṭane ghosetvā karaṇākāro paññāyatīti apare”ti ca. Ācariyā pana evaṃ na vadanti.

Regarding the statement that it is not permissible to go uninvited, for such a person there is both an interruption of the residence-period and an offense of wrong-doing; this they also call 'the breaking of the Rains-residence.' Regarding the statement that one is indeed to be considered invited: even when an agreement has been made by lay supporters, saying, 'On such-and-such a day we will make offerings and so on; let all assemble,' it is permissible to go. From the ninth day after the Pavāraṇā, it is permissible for all to go to seek a rag-robe, as in Kāvīrapaṭṭana, because it is annually prepared and set aside by the lay supporters as a regular practice. And this is also stated in the Andhakaṭṭhakathā: 'Or the community of bhikkhus has made an agreement, saying, "Let bhikkhus come from all around," or an announcement has been made by the lay supporters that for one who goes there, there is no interruption of the residence-period. Likewise, it is permissible even if invited only once with the words, "Let them come annually."' And others say: 'From the robe-season onwards, having made it a rule, the manner of doing so is known by announcement in Kāvīrapaṭṭana, because of the giving after preparing for those who have come from all around.' The teachers, however, do not say thus.

Antarāyeanāpattivassacchedakathāvaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Discourse of No Offense in Breaking the Rains-Residence Due to an Obstacle

201. “Sace dūraṃ gato hoti, sattāhavārena aruṇo uṭṭhāpetabbo”ti vacanato ‘yasmiṃ antarāye sati vassacchedaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭati, tasmiṃ antarāyeva vassacchedamakatvā sattāhakaraṇīyena [V 0.0428] vītināmetuṃ vaṭṭatīti dīpitanti apare”ti vuttaṃ. Vinayadharā pana na icchanti, tasmā “sattāhavārena aruṇo uṭṭhāpetabbo”ti idaṃ tatruppādādinimittaṃ vuttanti veditabbaṃ. Taṃ sandhāya “ācariyā pana evaṃ na vadantī”ti vuttaṃ. Gāvuṃ [M 0.0469] vāti balibaddhaṃ vā. Bahisīmāya ṭhitānanti tehi khaṇḍasīmāya ṭhitehipīti upatissatthero. Vassacchede assa vassacchedassa. Vihārā aññattha vuṭṭhāpentehi tattheva sannipatitvā “iminā ca iminā ca kāraṇena imasmiṃ nāma padese imaṃ vihāraṃ netvā vuṭṭhāpemā”ti anussāvetvāva kātabbanti.

201. Because of the statement, 'If one has gone far, the dawn must be made to arise within the seven-day allowance,' it is said that others explain it thus: 'When there is an obstacle for which it is allowable to break the Rains-residence, it is allowable to pass the time by means of the seven-day leave without breaking the Rains-residence on account of that very obstacle.' The Vinaya experts, however, do not approve of this. Therefore, it should be known that this statement, 'the dawn must be made to arise within the seven-day allowance,' is said concerning a reason such as the arising of requisites there. In reference to that, it is said, 'But the teachers do not speak thus.' `Gāvuṃ vā` means `balibaddaṃ vā` (or an ox). Regarding 'those standing outside the boundary,' the Elder Upatissa says this means 'by those standing even in a broken boundary.' `Vassacchede` refers to `assa vassacchedassa` (of this breaking of the Rains-residence).
