Asamādānacāro anadhiṭṭhitaticīvarassa natthi atecīvarikassa yāvadatthacīvaracatutthādicīvaraggahaṇasambhavato. Itarassāpi anadhiṭṭhānamukhena labbhati. Cīvaruppādo apaṃsukūlikasseva. “Kathinatthatasīmāya”nti upacārasīmaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Upacārasīmaṭṭhassa matakacīvarādibhāgiyatāya baddhasīmāya tatruppādābhāvato viññeyyametaṃ upacārasīmāvettha adhippetāti. Kathinatthāraṃ ke labhantīti ke sādhentīti attho. Pañca janā sādhenti. Kathinadussassa hi dāyakā pacchimakoṭiyā cattāro honti. Eko paṭiggāhakoti. “Tatra ce, bhikkhave, yvāyaṃ catuvaggo bhikkhusaṅgho ṭhapetvā tīṇi kammāni upasampadaṃ pavāraṇaṃ abbhāna”nti (mahāva. 388) campeyyakkhandhake vuttattā “na pañcavaggakaraṇīya”nti gahetabbaṃ. “Yassa saṅgho kathinadussaṃ deti, taṃ hatthapāse akatvāpi bahisīmāya ṭhitassapi dātuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti vadanti, taṃ hatthapāse katvā eva dātabbaṃ. Kasmā? “Tassa kammappattattā”ti vuttaṃ. “Tatruppādena taṇḍulādinā vatthesu cetāpitesu atthatakathinānameva tāni vatthāni pāpuṇanti. Vatthehi pana taṇḍulādīsu cetāpitesu sabbesaṃ tāni pāpuṇantī”ti vuttaṃ. Paṭhamapavāraṇāya pavāritā labhantīti idaṃ ukkaṭṭhakoṭiyā vuttaṃ. Antarāyena appavāritānampi vutthavassānaṃ kathinatthārasambhavato itare gaṇapūrake katvā kathinaṃ attharitabbanti kathaṃ paññāyatīti ce? “Dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ atthārakassa ca anumodakassa cā”ti (pari. 403) [V 0.0446] parivāre ekavacanakaraṇato, tattheva “saṅghassa atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, gaṇassa puggalassa atthataṃ hoti kathina”nti (pari. 414) vacanato ca.

306. “Regarding ‘Kathina,’ it is written that the meaning is ‘firm’ because of its ability to include the five benefits. Without saying ‘five are allowable,’ the future tense ‘they will be allowable’ is appropriate in consideration of the genitive case of ‘vo’ (for you), since at that moment, the Kathina was not yet spread for them. Among these two interpretations of the meaning, the latter is correct, as all those Pāveyyaka monks were observers of all the ascetic practices. Indeed, the practice of going uninvited is laid down only for one who accepts an invitation; similarly, group-eating. The privilege of going without the determined set of robes does not exist for one who has not determined his three robes. The privilege of keeping extra robes is not for one who is not a strict three-robe-wearer, given the possibility of receiving a fourth robe and so on. For another monk also, it is obtained by means of non-determination. The privilege concerning the arising of robes is only for one who is not a refuse-rag wearer. ‘Within the Kathina-spreading boundary’ is said with reference to the vicinity-boundary. It should be understood that the vicinity-boundary alone is intended here, because for one who is within the vicinity-boundary, there is the state of having a share in funeral robes, etc., and because in a fixed boundary there is no arising of things that arise there. ‘Who obtains the Kathina-spreading?’ means ‘Who accomplishes it?’ Five individuals accomplish it. Indeed, for the Kathina cloth, the donors are, at the minimum, four, and one is the recipient. Because it is said in the Campeyyakkhandhaka, ‘There, O monks, this group of four monks, excepting three acts: higher ordination, pavāraṇā, and rehabilitation…’ (Mahāva. 388), it should be understood that it is not an act requiring a fivefold group. Some say, ‘To whichever monk the Saṅgha gives the Kathina cloth, it is allowable to give it even without bringing him into hand’s reach, even if he is standing outside the boundary.’ But it should be given only after bringing him into hand’s reach. Why? Because it is said, ‘Because of his being present for the formal act.’ It is said: ‘If, with what has arisen there, such as rice, cloths are caused to be bought, then those cloths accrue only to those for whom the Kathina has been spread. But if, with cloths, rice, etc., are caused to be bought, then they accrue to all.’ That those who have performed the first pavāraṇā receive it—this is stated as the highest standard. If it is asked: ‘Since it is possible for even those who have completed the rains-residence but have not performed pavāraṇā due to an obstacle to spread the Kathina, how is it known that the Kathina should be spread by making others complete the quorum?’ (It is known because) in the Parivāra, the singular is used: ‘For two individuals, the Kathina is spread: for the one who spreads it and for the one who rejoices in it’ (Pari. 403); and because it is stated in that same text: ‘The Kathina is spread for the Saṅgha; the Kathina is spread for a group, for an individual’ (Pari. 414).

Aññasmiṃ [M 0.0489] vihāre vutthavassāpi na labhantīti idaṃ kiṃ ekasīmasmiṃ, udāhu nānāsīmasminti? Kiñcettha – yadi tāva ekasīmasmiṃ, parato “sace pana ekasīmāya bahū vihārā honti, sabbe bhikkhū sannipātetvā ekattha kathinaṃ attharitabbaṃ, visuṃ visuṃ attharituṃ na vaṭṭatī”ti iminā aṭṭhakathāvacanena virujjhati. Idañhi vacanaṃ sabbesaṃyeva eko kathinatthāroti dīpeti. Atha nānāsīmasmiṃ, upanandassa ekādhippāyadānānumatiyā virujjhati. Vuttañhetaṃ “detha, bhikkhave, moghapurisassa ekādhippāya”nti (mahāva. 364). Idañhi vacanaṃ dvīsupi āvāsesu tassa kathinatthārasiddhiṃ dīpetīti. Avirodhova icchitabbo appaṭisiddhattā, tasmā ekasīmasmiṃ vā nānāsīmasmiṃ vā nānūpacāre aññasmiṃ vihāre vutthavassāpi na labhantīti adhippāyo veditabbo. “Pacchimikāya upasampanno paṭhamapavāraṇāya pavāretumpi labhati, vassiko ca hoti ānisaṃsañca labhatīti sāmaṇerānaṃ vassūpagamanaṃ anuññātaṃ hoti, sāmaṇerā kathinānisaṃsaṃ labhantī”ti vadanti.

Regarding the statement, 'Even those who have completed the rains-residence in another monastery do not receive the privilege,' does this refer to a single boundary or to different boundaries? Herein, if it refers to a single boundary, it contradicts the subsequent commentary statement: 'If, however, there are many monasteries within a single boundary, all the bhikkhus should assemble and spread the Kaṭhina in one place; it is not permissible to spread it separately.' For this statement indicates that there is only one spreading of the Kaṭhina for all. If, on the other hand, it refers to different boundaries, it contradicts the permission given to Upananda for a gift with a single intention. For it was said: 'Give, bhikkhus, to this foolish man according to his single intention' (Mahāvagga 364). This statement shows that the spreading of the Kaṭhina is effective for him in both dwellings. Non-contradiction is to be desired, as it is not prohibited. Therefore, the meaning should be understood as: whether in a single boundary or in different boundaries, those who have completed the rains-residence in another monastery in a different vicinity do not receive the privilege. Some say: 'One ordained on the last day can also perform the first Pavāraṇā, is considered one who has kept the rains, and receives the benefits. Thus, the undertaking of the rains-residence is permitted for novices, and novices receive the benefits of the Kaṭhina.'

Tiṇṇaṃ cīvarānaṃ aññatarappahonakanti idaṃ “na aññatra saṅghāṭiyā uttarāsaṅgena antaravāsakena atthataṃ hoti kathina”nti imāya pāḷiyā virujjhanaṃ viya dissati. Ayañhi pāḷi tiṇṇaṃ cīvarānaṃ aññataravirahenāpi na atthataṃ hoti kathinanti dīpetīti ce? Na, tadatthajānanato, na tiṇṇaṃ cīvarānaṃ aññataravirahena na atthataṃ hoti kathinanti hi dīpetukāmo bhagavā taṃ pāḷimāha. Yadi evaṃ “aññatra saṅghāṭiyā uttarāsaṅgena antaravāsakenā”ti na vattabbā siyāti ce? Na, adhippāyajānanatova. Yo saṅghāṭiyā attharitukāmo, tassa aññatra saṅghāṭiyā na atthataṃ hoti. Esa nayo itaratthāpīti ayamettha adhippāyo. Teneva sukkapakkhe “saṅghāṭiyā atthataṃ hotī”tiādinā nayena ekameva cīvaraṃ vuttaṃ, evaṃ sante “catuvīsatiyā ākārehi anatthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, sattarasahi ākārehi atthataṃ hoti kathina”nti yathārahaṃ ukkaṭṭhakoṭiyā vuttanti veditabbaṃ, tasmā kaṇhapakkhe ullikhita…pe… nissīmaṭṭhānumodanānaṃ catuvīsatiyā ākārānaṃ sambhavantānaṃ sabbena sabbaṃ abhāvenapi nimittakatādīnaṃ asambhavantānaṃ aññatarabhāvenapi na atthataṃ hoti kathinanti evamadhippāyo [M 0.0490] veditabbo. Sukkapakkhepi ahatāhatakappa…pe… sīmaṭṭhānumodanānaṃ sattarasannaṃ ākārānaṃ sambhavantānaṃ aññatarabhāvenapi itaresaṃ sabbena sabbaṃ abhāvenapi atthataṃ hoti kathinanti evamadhippāyo veditabbo. Aññathā aññamaññavirodho, yathāsambhavaṃ yojetvā veditabbo.

The statement, “It is sufficient with any one of the three robes,” seems to contradict this Pāḷi text: “The kathina is not spread except with the double-layered robe, the upper robe, and the lower garment.” If one were to say: “Does this Pāḷi text indeed show that the kathina is not spread even with the absence of any one of the three robes?” That should not be said. Why? Because of knowing its meaning. Indeed, it is not the case that the Blessed One spoke that Pāḷi text wishing to show that ‘the kathina is not spread with the absence of any one of the three robes.’ If one were to say: “If this were so, the phrase ‘except with the double-layered robe, the upper robe, and the lower garment’ should not have been spoken.” That should not be said. Why? Precisely because of knowing the intention. For whichever monk wishes to spread the kathina with the double-layered robe, for him it is not spread except with the double-layered robe. This is the method in the other cases as well. This is the intention here. For that very reason, in the ‘white section’ (sukkapakkha), by the method beginning with ‘it is spread with the double-layered robe,’ only one robe was spoken of. This being so, it should be known that the statement, ‘the kathina is not spread in twenty-four modes, and is spread in seventeen modes,’ was spoken, as is suitable, as the highest limit. Therefore, in the ‘black section’ (kaṇhapakkha), the intention should be understood thus: the kathina is not spread even with the complete absence of the twenty-four possible modes—from ullikhita… to… nissīmaṭṭhānumodana—or even with the presence of any one of the impossible modes, beginning with making a sign. In the ‘white section’ (sukkapakkha) also, the intention should be understood thus: the kathina is spread even with the presence of any one of the seventeen possible modes—from ahatāhatakappa… to… sīmaṭṭhānumodana—and with the complete absence of the others. Otherwise, there would be mutual contradiction; it should be understood by applying it as is suitable.

Tatridaṃ [V 0.0447] mukhamattanidassanaṃ – kaṇhapakkhe “uttarāsaṅgena atthate kathine na aññatra saṅghāṭiyā na aññatra antaravāsakena atthataṃ hoti kathina”nti vacanappamāṇato taṃ kathinaṃ anatthataṃ siyā. Sukkapakkhe ca “animittakatena atthataṃ hoti kathina”nti vacanappamāṇato animittakatena kathine atthate tañce parikathā kataṃ, tathāpi atthatameva kathinaṃ hotīti ayaṃ duvidhopi virodho. Yathāvuttanayena adhippāye gahite parihāro hotīti veditabbaṃ.

Herein, this is a mere introductory example: In the negative section, according to the authority of the statement, 'When the kathina is spread with the upper robe, it is not spread without the double-layered robe, nor is it spread without the lower robe,' that kathina would be considered unspread. And in the positive section, according to the authority of the statement, 'The kathina is spread by that which is undesignated,' when the kathina is spread with an undesignated robe, and that robe has been made the subject of preliminary talk, even so, the kathina is indeed spread. Thus, this is a twofold contradiction. It should be understood that the resolution is found when the intention is grasped according to the method already stated.

Yo ānisaṃsaṃ bahuṃ detīti iminā paccayalolabhāvaṃ viya dīpeti, tathāpi bhagavatā yāvadatthacīvarapariyesanapaññāpanamukhena dvāraṃ dinnanti katvā saṅghānuggahatthaṃ hoti. “Akātuṃ na hotīti anādariyena akarontassa dukkaṭa”nti likhitaṃ. Anumodāmāti ettha sabbasaṅgāhikavasena evaṃ vuttaṃ. “Anumodāmī”ti ekakena vattabbaṃ, itarathā “na vaṭṭatī”ti mahāaṭṭhakathāyaṃ kira vuttaṃ. Kathinacīvaraṃ adhiṭṭhahitvā “imāya saṅghāṭiyā kathinaṃ attharāmī”ti vācāya bhinnamattāya puggalassa atthataṃ hoti. “Kammavācā pana ekāyeva vaṭṭatīti kathinadussassa eva kammavācā, sesacīvaradāne apalokanamevāti attho”ti likhitaṃ. Ekasīmāyāti ekaupacārasīmāyāti attho yujjati. Keci pana “baddhasīmā adhippetā ekasīmāya ekaṭṭhāne attharite sabbattha attharitaṃ hoti ‘sabbe bhikkhū sannipatitvā’ti vuttattā, tehipi anumodantehi attharitameva hoti, upacāraparicchinne tattha tattha laddhaṃ tehi tehi laddhabbaṃ hoti. Tattha paviṭṭhehipi labhitabbaṃ sabbehipi attharitattā, ayaṃ viseso. Mahāaṭṭhakathāyampi evameva vutta”nti vadanti, vīmaṃsitabbaṃ.

By this statement, 'Which gives many benefits,' it seems to indicate a state of greed for requisites. Nevertheless, considering that the Blessed One has given an allowance by means of laying down the rule concerning the seeking of robes only as needed, it is for the support of the Saṅgha. It is written: 'Regarding “It is not right not to do,” for one who does not do it out of disrespect, a dukkaṭa offense is incurred.' Herein, 'Anumodāma' (We rejoice) is said by way of including all. 'Anumodāmi' (I rejoice) should be said by an individual; otherwise, 'it is not proper,' so it is said in the Mahā-aṭṭhakathā. Having determined the kathina robe, merely by the utterance of the words, 'With this double-layered robe, I spread the kathina,' the spreading is accomplished for the individual. It is written: 'Regarding “But the formal act is proper only once,” the meaning is that the formal act is only for the kathina cloth; in the giving of the remaining robes, there is only an announcement.' Regarding 'in one boundary,' the meaning 'in one vicinity-boundary' is suitable. But some say: 'A consecrated boundary is intended. When it is spread in one place within one boundary, it is spread everywhere, because it is said, “all the bhikkhus having assembled.” By them also, who are rejoicing, it is indeed spread. When the vicinity is defined, what is received in various places should be received by those various bhikkhus. It should also be received by those who have entered there, because it has been spread by all. This is the distinction. Also in the Mahā-aṭṭhakathā it is said just so.' This should be investigated.

308. Catuvīsati ākāravantatāya mahābhūmikaṃ. “Dīghasibbitanti pacchākatasibbanaṃ, ovaṭṭitvā sibbanaṃ vā”ti likhitaṃ. Kaṇḍusaṃ nāma pubbabandhanaṃ. Paṭhamacimilikā ghaṭetvā ṭhapitā hotīti kathinadussaṃ dubbalaṃ disvā [M 0.0491] taṃ balavatā attano pakatidussena saddhiṃ ghaṭetvā dupaṭṭaṃ katvā sibbitukāmehi kathinadussato pakatidussassa mahantatāya paṭhamaṃ tappamāṇānurūpaṃ bandhakaṇḍuse ghaṭetvā rajjukehi bandhitvā kataṃ hotīti adhippāyo. Kathinacīvarassa appatāya paṭhamaṃ baddhadussaṃ kucchicimilikā hoti, mahāpaccariyaṃ, kurundiyañca vuttavacananidassanaṃ, byañjane eva bhedo, atthe natthīti dassanatthaṃ katanti veditabbaṃ. “Iminā kiṃ dīpetīti ce? Tathākataṃ dupaṭṭacīvaraṃ pakaticīvarassa mahantatāya pakaticīvarasaṅkhyameva gacchati, na kathinacīvarasaṅkhyanti kassaci siyā, nevaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Evaṃ kucchicimilikabhāvena ṭhitampi kathinacīvaraṃ. Mahantampi taṃ pakaticīvaraṃ attano kathinacīvaramevāti. Heṭṭhimakoṭiyā pañcakassa icchitabbattā kathinadussaṃ khaṇḍākhaṇḍaṃ bahudhā chinditvā sibbitukāmo kathinacīvarato [V 0.0448] paṭṭaṃ gahetvā aññasmiṃ akathinacīvare paṭṭamāropetī”ti likhitaṃ. Atha vā bahūni kathinadussāni paṃsukūlāni khuddakakhuddakāni ekacīvaratthāya, mahantāni ca ūnatthāya dinnāni honti. Kathinacīvaratoti bhikkhu ekaccato kathinacīvarato paṭṭaṃ gahetvā aññasmiṃ āropeti. Etthāha – kiṃ paṃsukūlāni kathinadussāni vikappanupagapacchimāni dātabbāni, udāhu khuddakānipīti? Ettha acīvarasaṅkhyattā khuddakāni dātuṃ na vaṭṭati. Kammavācā tattha na ruhatīti eke. “Paṃsukūlena atthataṃ hotī”ti pāḷiyaṃ nayadānato kucchicimilikabhāvena ṭhitassa kathinadussassa attano sabhāvena anadhiṭṭhānupagassa purāṇacīvarabhāveneva adhiṭṭhānārahassapi kathinacīvarabhāvānumatimukhena aṭṭhakathāyaṃ padānato ca khuddakānipi dātuṃ vaṭṭati. Tañhi kathinatthārako ghaṭetvā kathinacīvaraṃ karissatīti katvā kappatīti eke, yuttataraṃ gahetabbaṃ.

308. Because it possesses twenty-four characteristics, it is called Mahābhūmika. It is written: 'Long stitching means stitching done afterwards, or stitching done by rolling it up.' 'Kaṇḍusaṃ' means the initial binding. The phrase 'the first cimilikā is prepared and set aside' has this intended meaning: seeing that the kathina cloth is weak, those who wish to stitch it, having joined it with their own strong ordinary cloth and made it double-layered—because the ordinary cloth is larger than the kathina cloth—first prepare a binding 'kaṇḍusa' of appropriate size, and having joined it and tied it with strings, complete it. Due to the weakness of the kathina robe, the first bound cloth is the 'kucchicimilikā'. The statement mentioned in the Mahāpaccarī and the Kurundī is an example of this. It should be understood that this is done to show that the distinction is only in the wording, not in the meaning. If asked, 'What does this indicate?'—someone might think that such a double-layered robe, due to the largeness of the ordinary cloth, is counted only as an ordinary robe, not as a kathina robe. This should not be seen as such. Even when existing as a 'kucchicimilikā,' it is a kathina robe. And even if that ordinary cloth is large, it is indeed one's own kathina robe. It is written: 'Because a five-panel robe is desired as the minimum, a monk who wishes to cut the kathina cloth into many pieces and stitch it may take a strip from the kathina robe and apply it to another, non-kathina robe.' Alternatively, many very small kathina cloths, being rag-robes, are given for the purpose of a single robe, and large ones are given for the purpose of making up a deficiency. A monk takes a strip from a certain kathina robe and applies it to another. Here, a questioner asks: 'Should the rag-robes that are kathina cloths be given only if they are at the minimum size for `vikappana`, or can even smaller pieces be given?' Here, because they are not counted as a robe, it is not allowable to give small pieces. The `kammavācā` does not apply to them, so say some. Because of the guideline given in the Pāḷi, 'It is spread with a rag-robe,' and because it is stated in the commentary—by way of allowing its status as a kathina robe—that even a kathina cloth which exists as a `kucchicimilikā`, which by its own nature is not fit for formal determination, and which is fit for formal determination only in the manner of an old robe, it is allowable to give even small pieces. Some say it is permissible because the monk who spreads the kathina will assemble it and make a kathina robe. The more reasonable view should be adopted.

Nicayasannidhi saṅghāyattā saṅghena katattā. Rattātikkantaṃ nissajjitabbattā “nissaggiya”nti vuccati. Pañca khaṇḍāni paṭṭāni pamāṇaṃ assāti pañcakaṃ. Tena vā atirittena vāti attho. Tadaheva sañchinnenāti saṅghena kathinatthārakassa kammavācaṃ vatvā dinneneva tadaheva sañchinnena samaṇḍalikatena bhavitabbaṃ. Evaṃ dinnaṃyeva hi parivāre “pubbakaraṇaṃ sattahi dhammehi saṅgahita”nti vuttaṃ, na dāyakena diyyamānaṃ, tasmā pariniṭṭhitapubbakaraṇameva ce [M 0.0492] dāyako saṅghassa deti, sampaṭicchitvā kammavācāya dātabbaṃ. Tena ca tasmiṃyeva sīmāmaṇḍale adhiṭṭhahitvā attharitvā saṅgho anumodāpetabbo katapubbakaraṇassa puna kattabbābhāvato. Atthārakassa hatthagatameva hi sandhāya “na ullikhitamattenā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Pariniṭṭhitapubbakaraṇampi puna dhovitvā visibbitvā kātabbameva vacanapamāṇatoti ce? Na, chinnassa puna chedāsambhavato. Aññasmiṃ ṭhāne chinditabbamevāti ce? Na, pabbajjādhikāre “kesamassuṃ ohārāpetvā”ti vacanappamāṇato muṇḍikassa chinnepi kese pariyesitvā sirasmiṃ ṭhapetvā puna ohārāpetvā pabbājetabbappasaṅgato, na idha na-kārena paṭisiddhattāti ce? Na, “na aññatra saṅghāṭiyā”ti na-kārena paṭisiddhattā uttarāsaṅgena atthate anatthataṃ hotīti aniṭṭhappasaṅgato, tasmā abhiniveso na kātabbo. “Bahiupacārasīmāya ṭhito”ti vuttattāpi pubbe vuttavinicchayova gahetabbo.

The accumulation and storage is dependent on the Saṅgha because it is done by the Saṅgha. Because it has passed one night and must be forfeited, it is called 'nissaggiya'. A robe of five sections (pañcaka) is so called because its measure is five sections or strips. The meaning is: either by that or by what is in excess of it. Regarding 'cut on that very day': it must be a robe that, having been given by the Saṅgha to the monk who is to spread the kathina after reciting the formal act, is cut and made with a border on that very day. Indeed, regarding only what is given in this way, it is said in the Parivāra, 'The preliminary work is comprised of seven factors,' not regarding what is being given by a donor. Therefore, if a donor gives to the Saṅgha a robe for which the preliminary work is already completed, it should be accepted and then bestowed by means of a formal act. And that monk, having determined it and spread it out within that very boundary area, should have the Saṅgha rejoice, because for that for which the preliminary work has been done, there is nothing further to be done. Indeed, with reference to what has come into the hands of the spreader, it is said, 'Not by mere marking,' and so forth. If it is said: 'Even for a robe for which the preliminary work is completed, must it be washed and unstitched again, taking the text as the authority?' No, because for what has been cut, a re-cutting is impossible. If it is said: 'It must be cut in another place'? No, because in the section on ordination, if one takes the text 'having had the hair and beard removed' as the authority, it would lead to the absurd consequence that one would have to ordain a bald person by searching for his already-cut hair, placing it on his head, and having it removed again. If it is said: 'Here, that absurd consequence would not arise, because it is prohibited by the negative particle 'na'?' No, because it would lead to the undesirable consequence that, due to the prohibition by the negative particle 'na' in the phrase 'not other than the double-layered robe,' if one were to spread the kathina with an upper robe, it would be considered 'not spread'. Therefore, adherence should not be practiced. Also because it is said, 'standing outside the precinct boundary,' the decision stated previously should be accepted.

309. Asannidhikatena atthataṃ hoti kathinanti ettha kiṃ kathinatthāramāseyeva duvidhopi sannidhi adhippeto, udāhu tato pubbepi, dāyakena vā kadā dātabbaṃ, kiṃ kathinatthāramāseyeva, udāhu [V 0.0449] tato pubbepi, kathinatthāramāsepi asukasmiṃ divaseyeva atthāratthāya dammīti dātuṃ vaṭṭati na vaṭṭatīti idaṃ vicāretabbaṃ. Kathinatthāramāse eva duvidhopi sannidhi. Dāyakenāpi vassāvāsikaṃ viya kathinacīvaraṃ uddissa dinnaṃ na vaṭṭati. Kasmā? “Kathinadāyakassa vattaṃ atthī”tiādinā (mahāva. aṭṭha. 306) nayena aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttattā. Ukkaṭṭhamattametanti ce? Na, “kathinaṃ nāma atiukkaṭṭhaṃ vaṭṭatī”ti (mahāva. aṭṭha. 308) vuttattā. Na āgamanaṃ sandhāya vuttanti ce? Na, idampi āgamanameva sandhāya vuttaṃ, pubbe dinnaṃ na vaṭṭatīti.

309. Herein, regarding the statement 'the kathina is spread by one who has not stored it up,' is both kinds of storage intended only during the month of the spreading of the kathina, or even before that? And by the donor, when should it be given? Only during the month of the spreading of the kathina, or even before? And even during the month of the spreading of the kathina, is it permissible or not permissible to give on a specific day, stating, 'I give for the purpose of spreading'? This matter should be investigated. Both kinds of storage are intended only in the month of the spreading of the kathina. Also by the donor, it is not permissible to give a kathina robe having designated it beforehand, like a rains-residence robe. Why? Because it is stated in the commentary by the method beginning, 'There is a duty for the kathina donor.' If one were to say, 'This is merely the highest standard,' it should not be said. Why? Because it is stated, 'The kathina, indeed, is permissible only at the highest standard.' If one were to say, 'This was not said with reference to the scriptural tradition,' the answer is no. This too was said with reference to the scriptural tradition itself; it should be understood that what is given beforehand is not permissible.

310. Kathinassāti kathinatthārassa. Ubbhārāyāti vūpasamāya, appavattiyāti attho. Kimatthiyaṃ ubbhāranidassananti ce? Pañcahi anāpattikālapariyantadassanena tesu saṃvaruppādanatthaṃ. Aññathā “cīvarakālasamayo nāma anatthate kathine vassānassa pacchimo māso, atthate kathine pañca māsā”ti (pārā. 649) vibhaṅge vuttattā antarāpakkamanantikādiubbhārābhāvepi pañcahi pañcasu māsesu anāpattiyevāti micchāgāho siyā[M 0.0493]. Tato āpattikhette anāpattikhettasaññāya taṃ taṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati, itaresañca bhikkhūnaṃ lābhantarāyaṃ karotīti veditabbaṃ.

310. ‘Of the kathina’ means ‘of the spreading of the kathina.’ ‘For the withdrawal’ means ‘for the cessation,’ that is, ‘for the non-occurrence.’ If it is asked for what purpose the indication of the withdrawal is shown, it is for the purpose of producing restraint in those cases by showing the limit of the period of no-offence regarding the five grounds. Otherwise, because it is stated in the Vibhaṅga, ‘The robe-time, indeed, is the last month of the rains-residence when the kathina is not spread, and five months when the kathina is spread,’ even in the absence of a withdrawal due to the departure-limit and so on in the interim, a wrong view might arise that for the five grounds during the five months there is only no-offence. Therefore, in a field of offence, with the perception of a field of no-offence, one falls into that very offence and creates an obstacle to the gains of other bhikkhus. This should be understood.

Ādāyasattakakathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourse on the Heptad of Taking

311. Sanniṭṭhānantike dvepi palibodhā ekato chijjantīti idha, parivāraṭṭhakathāyañca vuttaṃ imissā khandhakapāḷiyā sameti ekato ubhinnampi dhuranikkhepassa katattā. “Idaṃ bahisīmāyameva vuttaṃ sanniṭṭhānantikaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Yaṃ pana vuttaṃ parivāre ‘cattāro kathinuddhārā siyā antosīmāya uddhariyyanti, siyā bahisīmāya uddhariyyanti, niṭṭhānantiko sanniṭṭhānantiko nāsanantiko āsāvacchediko’ti (pari. 416). Tattha bahisīmāya sanniṭṭhānantiko uddhariyyatīti idha dassitanayova. Kathaṃ antosīmāya sanniṭṭhānantiko? Akatacīvaramādāya ‘na paccessa’nti gato, gatagataṭṭhāne phāsuvihāraṃ alabhanto tameva vihāraṃ āgacchati, tassa cīvarapalibodho ṭhito. So ca ‘nevimaṃ cīvaraṃ kāressa’nti citte uppannamatte chijjati, tasmā antosīmāya uddhariyyati, tasmā duvidho sanniṭṭhānantiko”ti porāṇagaṇṭhipade likhitaṃ, taṃ yuttaṃ, aññathā antosīmāya “nevimaṃ cīvaraṃ kāressa”nti pavattaubbhāro itaresu samodhānaṃ na gacchatīti atiritto siyā. Sīmātikkantikoti cīvarakālasīmātikkantiko. Saubbhāre cīvarapalibodho paṭhamaṃ chijjanto viya khāyati, atha kho [V 0.0450] sāpekkhatāya cīvarakaraṇe saussāhova hotīti lesaṃ sandhāya parivāravasena “dve palibodhā apubbaṃ acarimaṃ chijjantī”ti (mahāva. aṭṭha. 311) vuttaṃ. “Katacīvaro”ti vuttattā idha na sambhavati.

311. Regarding the withdrawal by determination-ending, the statement that ‘both hindrances are cut off simultaneously,’ which is mentioned both here and in the Parivāra commentary, agrees with this Khandhaka Pāḷi, because the laying down of the burden for both is done simultaneously. This is stated with reference to the determination-ending that occurs only outside the boundary. However, in the Parivāra, it is said: ‘There are four withdrawals of the Kathina: some are withdrawn within the boundary, and some are withdrawn outside the boundary; they are the withdrawal by completion-ending, by determination-ending, by destruction-ending, and by cutting off of hope.’ Among those, that the withdrawal by determination-ending is done outside the boundary is the very method shown here. How is there a withdrawal by determination-ending within the boundary? A monk, having taken an unmade robe, goes away thinking, ‘I will not return.’ Not finding a comfortable dwelling in whatever place he goes, he returns to that very monastery; his robe-hindrance remains. And as for him, as soon as the thought ‘I will certainly not make this robe’ arises in his mind, it is cut off. Therefore, it is withdrawn within the boundary. Thus, the withdrawal by determination-ending is of two kinds.” This is written in the ancient glossaries, and it is correct. Otherwise, the withdrawal that occurs within the boundary with the thought ‘I will certainly not make this robe’ would not find inclusion among the others and would thus be superfluous. ‘Crossing the boundary’ means crossing the boundary of the robe-period. In the case of withdrawal with the robe-cloth, the robe-hindrance appears as if it is cut off first. However, due to remaining expectation, one is still eager in the making of the robe. With reference to this subtle point, it is stated according to the Parivāra: ‘The two hindrances are cut off neither one before nor one after.’ Because it is said, ‘one whose robe is made,’ it is not applicable here.

316. Sabbaṃ attano parikkhāraṃ anavasesetvā pakkamanto “samādāya pakkamatī”ti vuccati. “Kathinuddhāre viseso natthi. Puggalādhippāyavisesena kevalaṃ vāradassanatthaṃ samādāyavārā vuttā”ti sabbesu gaṇṭhipadesu likhitaṃ. Idha pana puggalādhippāyena payojanaṃ vīmaṃsitabbaṃ. Pakkamanantikassa abhāvā “yathāsambhava”nti vuttaṃ. Vippakatepi dhuranikkhepavasena pakkamanantikatā sambhavati, tasmā pakkamanantikavāropi vattabboti ce? Na, sanniṭṭhānantikalakkhaṇappasaṅgato. Akatacīvarassa na savanantikatā ca.

316. One who departs without leaving behind any of his requisites is called ‘one who departs taking them along.’ It is written in all the Ganthipadas: “There is no distinction in the removal of the Kathina. The ‘taking-along’ sections are stated solely for the purpose of showing the allowance, based on the particular intention of the individual.” Here, however, the purpose should be examined based on the intention of the individuals. Due to the absence of a departure-ending, it is said ‘as is possible.’ If one were to say that even when the robe is unmade, the state of being a departure-ending is possible by way of relinquishing the burden, and therefore the departure-ending section should also be stated? No, because it would involve the characteristic of the determination-ending. And for an unmade robe, there is no state of being a hearing-ending.

Tatrāyaṃ [M 0.0494] ādito paṭṭhāya vāravibhāvanā – ādāyavārā satta, tathā samādāyavārāti dve sattakavārā. Tato pakkamanantikaṃ vajjetvā vippakatacīvarassa ādāyavārā, samādāyavārā cāti dve chakkavārā. Tato paraṃ niṭṭhānasanniṭṭhānanāsanantikānaṃ vasena tīṇi tikāni dassitāni, tattha paṭhamattikaṃ antosīmāya “na paccessa”nti imaṃ vidhiṃ anāmasitvā bahisīmāyaṃ eva “na paccessa”nti pavattaṃ, tasmā pakkamanantikasīmātikkantikasaubbhārā tattha na yujjanti. “Āsāvacchediko sambhavantopi yathāvuttakāraṇena na vutto. Dutiyattikaṃ antosīmāya ‘na paccessa’nti pavattaṃ, ettha kiñcāpi pakkamanantiko sambhavati, tathāpi yehi cīvarapalibodho chijjati, tesaṃyevādhippetattā na vutto”ti porāṇagaṇṭhipade vuttaṃ. Sabbasmimpi pannarasake vippakatacīvarassevādhippetattāti takko. Adhiṭṭhānupage ca vippakate sati na niṭṭhānantiko. Niṭṭhānāvasese sati na nāsanantikoti porāṇā. Tatiyattikaṃ anadhiṭṭhita-padena visesetvā pavattaṃ, atthato paṭhamattikena sameti. Tassa atthadassanapayojanaṃ kira taṃ. Yasmā ime tayo atthavikappā imehi eva tīhi kathinuddhārehi sakkā dassetuṃ, tasmā imeva yojitā ekasambandhavasena, aññathā paṭhamattikaṃ chakkaṃ bhaveyya imassa pannarasakassa ante chakkaṃ viya. Tatiyattikānantaraṃ catutthattikaṃ sambhavantaṃ “antosīmāyaṃ ‘paccessa”nti vacanavisesena sambhavati. Tathā ca yojiyamānaṃ itarehi savanantikādīhi aviruddhakkamaṃ hoti, tasmā catutthattikaṃ ahutvā chakkaṃ jātanti veditabbaṃ. Evaṃ tīṇi tikāni ekaṃ chakkañcāti paṭhamaṃ pannarasakaṃ veditabbaṃ. Idāni idameva pannarasakaṃ upasaggavisesena dutiyaṃ samādāyapannarasakaṃ nāma kataṃ. Puna vippakatacīvaraṃ ādāyāti tatiyaṃ pannarasakaṃ, samādāyāti catutthaṃ pannarasakaṃ dassitaṃ. Evaṃ cattāri pannarasakāni veditabbāni[V 0.0451]. Tattha paṭhamadutiyesu pannarasakesu sabbena sabbaṃ akatacīvaraṃ adhippetaṃ, itaresu dvīsu vippakatanti yojetabbaṃ. “Pubbe nibaddhaṭṭhāne cīvarāsāya gahetabbaṃ, aññattha na vaṭṭati. Upacchinnāya ce cīvarāsāya cīvaraṃ uppannaṃ, na taṃ cīvarapalibodhaṃ karotī”ti porāṇagaṇṭhipade vuttaṃ. Nissaggiyesu tatiyakathine āgatacīvarapaccāsā idha cīvarāsāti takko. Yattha cīvarāsā, taṃ ṭhānaṃ adhikaraṇūpacārena “cīvarāsā”tveva vuccatīti katvā “taṃ cīvarāsaṃ payirupāsatī”tiādi vuttaṃ, tasmā anāsāya labhatīti anāsāyitaṭṭhāne labhatītiādinā attho [M 0.0495] gahetabbo. Ettha niṭṭhānasanniṭṭhānanāsanaāsāvacchedikavasena eko vāroti idamekaṃ catukkaṃ jātaṃ, tasmā pubbe vuttāni tīṇi tikāni āsāvacchedikādhikāni tīṇi catukkānīti ekaṃ anāsāyadvādasakanti veditabbaṃ. Tadanantare āsāyadvādasake kiñcāpi paṭhamadvādasakkamo labbhati, tathāpi taṃ nibbisesanti tamekaṃ dvādasakaṃ avuttasiddhaṃ katvā visesato dassetuṃ ādito paṭṭhāya “antosīmāya paccessa”nti vuttaṃ, taṃ dutiyacatukke “so bahisīmagato suṇātī”tiādivacanassa tatiyacatukke savanantikādīnañca okāsakaraṇatthanti veditabbaṃ. Idaṃ pana dvādasakaṃ anāsāya vasena labbhamānampi iminā avuttasiddhaṃ katvā na dassitanti veditabbaṃ. Evamettha dve dvādasakāni uddharitāni. Karaṇīyadvādasakepi yathādassitaanāsāyadvādasakaṃ, avuttasiddhaṃ āsāyadvādasakañcāti dve dvādasakāni uddharitabbāni. Idāni disaṃgamikanavakaṃ hoti. Tattha yasmā “disaṃgamiko pakkamatī”ti vacaneneva “na paccessa”nti idaṃ avuttasiddhameva, tasmā taṃ na vuttaṃ. Ettāvatā āvāsapalibodhābhāvo dassito.

Herein, this is the clarification of the sections, starting from the beginning: the ‘taking’ sections are seven; similarly, the ‘undertaking’ sections are seven. Thus, there are two sevenfold sections. From that, excluding the departure-ending, for a bhikkhu with an unfinished robe, there are the ‘taking’ sections and the ‘undertaking’ sections; thus, there are two sixfold sections. After that, three triads are shown by way of the completion-ending, determination-ending, and loss-ending. Among them, the first triad proceeds only outside the boundary with “I will not return,” without considering this procedure within the boundary. Therefore, the departure-ending, the boundary-crossing-ending, and the with-removal-ending are not applicable there. “Although the cutting-off-of-hope-ending is possible, it is not mentioned for the reason already stated. The second triad proceeds within the boundary with ‘I will not return.’ Here, although the departure-ending is possible, nevertheless, because only those removals by which the robe-impediment is cut off are intended, it is not mentioned.” Thus it is said in the ancient gloss. The reasoning is that in the entire fifteenfold section, only the unfinished robe is intended. And when a robe suitable for determination is unfinished, there is no completion-ending. When there is a remainder after completion, there is no loss-ending. Thus say the ancients. The third triad proceeds, being distinguished by the term ‘undetermined’; in meaning, it agrees with the first triad. It has the purpose of showing the meaning of that first triad. Because these three variations of meaning can be shown by these very three Kathina removals, therefore these very ones are connected by way of a single connection. Otherwise, the first triad would become a sixfold section, like the sixfold section at the end of this fifteenfold section. After the third triad, a fourth triad, while being possible, is possible with the specific statement, “I will return within the boundary.” And being connected in such a way, it has a non-conflicting sequence with the others, such as the hearing-ending. Therefore, it should be understood that a fourth triad did not come to be, but a sixfold section has arisen. Thus, three triads and one sixfold section should be understood as the first fifteenfold section. Now, this very fifteenfold section, with a specific prefix, is made into what is named the second, the ‘undertaking’ fifteenfold section. Again, with ‘taking an unfinished robe,’ the third fifteenfold section is shown; with ‘undertaking,’ the fourth fifteenfold section is shown. Thus, four fifteenfold sections should be understood. Among them, in the first and second fifteenfold sections, a completely unmade robe is intended; in the other two, ‘unfinished’ should be applied. “With hope for robe-material, it should be taken at the previously designated place; elsewhere, it is not allowable. If, when the hope for robe-material is cut off, a robe arises, it does not create a robe-impediment.” Thus it is said in the ancient gloss. The reasoning is that the ‘expectation for robe-material that has arrived’ in the third Kathina rule of the Nissaggiyas is here called ‘hope for a robe.’ Where there is hope for robe-material, that place, by metaphorical extension of the basis, is called ‘hope for a robe.’ Because of this, “he attends to that hope for a robe,” etc., is said. Therefore, from ‘he obtains without hope,’ the meaning should be taken as ‘he obtains in a place where there is no hope,’ etc. Here, by way of completion, determination, loss, and cutting off of hope, there is one section; thus this one tetrad has arisen. Therefore, the three triads previously mentioned, with the addition of the cutting-off-of-hope-ending, become three tetrads, and this should be understood as one twelvefold section without hope. After that, in the twelvefold section with hope, although the sequence of the first twelvefold section is obtained, nevertheless, making that one twelvefold section implicitly understood in order to show it specifically, from the beginning “I will return within the boundary” is stated. It should be understood that this is for the purpose of making an opportunity for the statement “he, having gone outside the boundary, hears,” etc., in the second tetrad, and for the hearing-ending, etc., in the third tetrad. It should be understood that this twelvefold section, although also obtainable by way of being without hope, is not shown, having been made implicitly understood by this other one. Thus, two twelvefold sections have been extracted here. Also in the twelvefold section of what is to be done, two twelvefold sections should be extracted: the twelvefold section without hope as shown, and the implicitly understood twelvefold section with hope. Now there is the ninefold section on one going to another region. There, because by the very statement “one going to another region departs,” this “I will not return” is indeed implicitly understood, therefore it is not stated. By this much, the absence of the residence-impediment is shown.

321. “Cīvarapaṭivīsaṃ apavilāyamāno”ti iminā cīvarapalibodhasamaṅgitamassa dasseti. Paṭivīsoti attano pattabbo cīvarabhāgo. Apavilāyamānoti ākaṅkhamāno. Tassa cīvaralābhe sati vassaṃvutthāvāse niṭṭhānasanniṭṭhānanāsanantikānaṃ vasena ekaṃ tikaṃ, tesaṃyeva vasena antarāmagge ekaṃ, gataṭṭhāne ekanti tiṇṇaṃ tikānaṃ vasena ekaṃ navakaṃ veditabbaṃ. Tato paraṃ niṭṭhānasanniṭṭhānanāsananti kasīmātikkantikasaubbhārānaṃ vasena phāsuvihārapañcakaṃ vuttaṃ. Ubhayattha sesakathinuddhārāsambhavo pākaṭova. Ayaṃ panettha pañcake viseso – samādāyavāro na sambhavati “paccessa”nti paccāgamanādhippāyato.

321. By “not letting go of the robe-share,” it shows his being endowed with the robe-impediment. “Share” means the portion of the robe due to him. “Not letting go” means desiring. When he obtains a robe, after having spent the rains residence, one triad is to be understood by way of the completion-ending, determination-ending, and loss-ending; and by way of these same, one on the journey in between, and one at the place reached—thus, one ninefold section is to be understood by way of three triads. After that, the fivefold section concerning comfortable abiding is stated by way of the completion-ending, determination-ending, loss-ending, boundary-crossing-ending, and with-removal-ending. In both cases, the impossibility of the remaining Kathina removals is evident. The particular difference in this fivefold section is this: the “undertaking” section is not possible because of the intention to return, as in “I will return.”

325. Dveme bhikkhave kathinassa palibodhāti kathinatthārassa anupabandhanapaccayāti.

325. In the phrase, “These two, bhikkhus, are hindrances to the Kathina,” the meaning should be understood as: the conditions for not continuing the Kathina spreading.

Kathinakkhandhakavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Kathina chapter is concluded.

8. Cīvarakkhandhakavaṇṇanā

8. Commentary on the Robe Chapter

Jīvakavatthukathāvaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Story of Jīvaka

326. Rājagahakoti [M 0.0496][V 0.0452] rājagahavāsī.

326. “Rājagahako” means a resident of Rājagaha.

328. Amohajātikattā na cirasseva viññutaṃ pāpuṇi. Ahaṃ te pitā, kenaṭṭhena? Yasmā tvaṃ mayā posāpito.

328. Because he was of an undeluded nature, he quickly attained understanding. It is said, “I am your father.” In what sense? Because you were raised by me.

329. “Sakke vissaṭṭhamatte”ti pāṭho, aṭṭhamasikkhāpade vissaṭṭhamattova.

329. The reading is “Sakke vissaṭṭhamatte”; in the eighth training rule, it is simply “vissaṭṭhamatta.”

Pajjotarājavatthukathāvaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Story of King Pajjota

334. Bhuñjituṃ nisinnassāti ettha “dhammapade ‘bahinagare disvā’ti vuttaṃ, tasmā dvīsu divasesu dinnaṃ tena tesu ekekaṃ gahetvā dvīsu aṭṭhakathāsu vuttanti yujjatī”ti vadanti.

334. Regarding “while sitting to eat,” here they say: “It is said in the Dhammapada, ‘having seen outside the city.’ Therefore, it is fitting that what was given on two days—taking one from each—is mentioned in the two commentaries.”

Samattiṃsavirecanakathāvaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Story of the Thirty Purges

336. Kabaḷe kabaḷeti ettha kiñcāpi guḷādīsu pakkhittaṃ, taṃ pana bhagavāva paribhuñji, tasmā natthi doso.

336. Regarding “in every mouthful,” here, although it was put into molasses and so forth, only the Blessed One partook of it; therefore, there is no fault.

Varayācanakathāvaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Story of the Request for a Boon

337. Mahāpiṭṭhiyakojavaṃ nāma atirekacaturaṅgulapupphaṃ kira.

337. What is called Mahāpiṭṭhiyakojava, it is said, is a flower exceeding four finger-widths.

Kambalānujānanādikathāvaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Story of the Allowance for Blankets and So Forth

340. Upacāreti [V 0.0453] susānassa upacāre. Bahipi vaṭṭatīti eke. Katikakaraṇaṃ dassetvā “mayhaṃ santakaṃ tava ca mama ca hotūti vatvā itarena ca tathāvutte vaṭṭatī”ti samānaparikkhāravidhiṃ vadanti.

340. In the phrase `upacāre`: in the vicinity of the charnel ground. Some say it is permissible even outside. Having shown the reason for making an agreement, and having said, 'Let what is mine be yours and mine,' and when the other has spoken likewise, it is permissible. Thus they speak of the procedure for shared requisites.

342. “Khaṇḍasīmāyapi sammannituṃ vaṭṭatīti vuttattā sesakammānipi tattha nisīditvā kātuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti vuttaṃ. “Evaṃ sante corikāya katasadisaṃ hoti[M 0.0497], tasmā na vaṭṭatī”ti dīpavāsino vadanti kira. “Corikāya gahitattā na pāpuṇātīti senāsanakkhandhake āgatasuttañca sādhaka”nti vadanti, tasmā tesaṃ matena idaṃ āveṇikalakkhaṇanti veditabbaṃ.

342. Because it is said, 'It is permissible to agree upon even a fragmentary boundary,' it is said that it is permissible to perform the remaining acts, having sat down there. 'If this is so, it becomes like something done by stealth; therefore, it is not permissible,' the island-dwellers are said to say. 'Because it was taken by stealth, one does not attain it,' and the Sutta that comes in the Section on Lodgings is proof, they say. Therefore, according to their view, it should be understood that this is a distinctive characteristic.

Bhaṇḍāgārasammutiādikathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discussion Beginning with the Designation of a Storehouse

343. “Idaṃ pana bhaṇḍāgāranti āveṇikalakkhaṇa”nti vuttaṃ.

343. It is said: 'This, however, is a distinctive characteristic' in the passage concerning the storehouse.

Cīvararajanakathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discussion on Robe-Dyeing

344. Gomaye āpatti natthi, virūpattāvāritaṃ. “Kuṅkumapupphaṃ na vaṭṭatī”ti vadanti. “Allikāyā”tipi pāṭho atthi.

344. In the case of cow dung, there is no offense; it is forbidden because of its unseemliness. They say, 'The saffron flower is not permissible.' There is also the reading `allikāya`.

Nisīdanādianujānanakathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discussion on the Allowance for Sitting Cloths and So Forth

353. Aṭṭhānametanti ettha rūpakaṇḍe “catusamuṭṭhānika”nti vuttattā kammasamuṭṭhānaṃ rāgacittābhāvā na muccatīti vā rāgapaccaye sati kammasamuṭṭhānaṃ hotīti vā vicāretvā gahetabbaṃ kathāvatthunā ca.

353. In the phrase `aṭṭhānametaṃ` ('this is impossible'): here, because it is stated in the section on form to be 'of four origins,' it should be understood by investigating with the Kathāvatthu as well whether (1) that which is originated from kamma is not released due to the absence of a mind-state with lust, or (2) when the condition of lust is present, that which is originated from kamma occurs.

362. Aggaḷaguttiyeva pamāṇanti imehi catūhi nikkhepakāraṇehi ṭhapentena aggaḷaguttivihāreyeva ṭhapetuṃ vaṭṭatīti adhippāyo.

362. In the phrase `aggaḷaguttiyeva pamāṇaṃ` ('security by a bolt itself is the standard'): the meaning is that it is permissible for one who is depositing something for these four reasons for depositing to deposit it only in a monastery with a secure bolt.

Saṅghikacīvaruppādakathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discussion on the Arising of Robes for the Sangha

363. No [V 0.0454] ce atthataṃ hoti “ekaṃ cīvaramāsa”nti na vattabbaṃ. Kasmā? “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tasseva tāni cīvarāni yāva cīvaramāsā”ti vacanassa abhāvato, tasmā anatthatakathinassa ananuññātanti ce? Na, heṭṭhā anuññātattā, tato līnatthadīpanatthamidha tathā vuttattā ca. Heṭṭhā hi “akālacīvaraṃ nāma anatthate kathine ekādasamāse uppannaṃ, atthate kathine sattamāse uppannaṃ, kālepi ādissa dinnaṃ, etaṃ akālacīvaraṃ nāmā”ti (pārā. 500) vacanato anatthatakathinānaṃ ekacīvaramāse uppannaṃ, tesaṃyeva hotīti siddhaṃ, tasmā idha taṃ avatvā ekopi tayo gaṇapūrake labhitvā kathinaṃ attharituṃ labhatīti imaṃ līnatthaṃ pakāsetuṃ “yāva kathinassa ubbhārāyā”ti vuttaṃ. Itarathā ayamattho na ñāyati. “Jānitabbo [M 0.0498] ca vinayadharehīti tathā vuttoti apare”ti vuttaṃ. Atthataṃ hoti, pañca māse sabbaṃ tasseva bhikkhuno hotīti sambandho. Accantasaṃyogavasena upayogavacanaṃ. “Idha vassaṃvutthasaṅghassā”ti niyamitattā “vassāvāsikaṃ demā”ti ettha ca “idhā”ti adhikārattā tasmiṃ vutte labhati. “Piṭṭhisamaye uppannattāti cīvarakālassāsannattā ca anatthatakathinānampi vutthavassānañca anuññātaṭṭhānattā eva vutta”nti aññatarasmiṃ gaṇṭhipade likhitaṃ. Keci pana “yaṃ pana idaṃ ‘idha vassaṃvutthasaṅghassā’tiādiṃ katvā yāva ‘anāgatavasse’ti padaṃ, tāva pucchitvā ‘kasmā? Piṭṭhisamaye uppannattā’ti idaṃ parato ‘tatra sammukhībhūtānaṃ sabbesaṃ pāpuṇātī’ti imassa pariyosāne ‘kasmā? Piṭṭhisamaye uppannattā’ti likhitabbaṃ. Kasmāti ce? Parato ‘cīvaramāsato paṭṭhāya yāva hemantassā’ti vuttena nibbisesattā, tasmā eva ekaccesu paṇḍitanti vadantī”ti vadanti. Idha pana idha-saddena visesitaṃ, tattha natthi, tasmā aññamaññavirodho natthīti gahetabbaṃ. “Mayhimāni cīvarāni pāpuṇantī”ti vacanamevādhiṭṭhānaṃ, idamettha ukkaṭṭhavasena vuttaṃ. “Mayhimāni cīvarānī’ti vuttepi adhiṭṭhitameva hotī”ti vuttaṃ. “Mayhimānī’ti vutte tassa cīvarāni nāma natthi, tasmā ‘cīvarāni pāpuṇantī’ti vattabbamevā”ti vadanti. Duggahitānīti saṅghikāneva honti. “Gahitameva nāmā’ti imassa idaṃ pattanti kiñcāpi na viditaṃ, te pana bhāgā tesaṃ atthato pattāyevāti adhippāyo”ti likhitaṃ. “Ekasmiṃ apatite puna āgatā labhantī”ti vuttaṃ.

363. If the Kathina is not spread, one should not say, 'one robe-month.' Why? Because there is no statement such as, 'I allow, bhikkhus, those very robes for the duration of the robe-month.' Therefore, if one were to say that it is not permitted for one for whom the Kathina is not spread? No, because it was permitted below, and because it is stated thus here in order to clarify the hidden meaning from that. For below it was said: 'An untimely robe is one that arises during the eleven months when the Kathina is not spread, or during the seven months when it is spread, or even if given during the season but designated as such—this is called an untimely robe.' By this statement, it is established that what arises in the single robe-month for those for whom the Kathina is not spread, belongs to them alone. Therefore, here, without stating that, it is said, 'until the lifting of the Kathina,' in order to reveal this hidden meaning: that even one bhikkhu, having obtained three bhikkhus who complete the quorum, is able to spread the Kathina. Otherwise, this meaning would not be known. It is said by others, 'It should be understood by those versed in the Vinaya, and so it was stated thus.' The connection is as follows: if the Kathina is spread, for five months everything belongs to that very bhikkhu. The word for 'use' is employed in the sense of complete association. 'Here, for the Sangha that has spent the Rains'—because it is specified—and in 'we give to the Rains-resident,' because 'here' has governing force, it is obtained when stated thus. 'Because it arises at the back time (piṭṭhisamaya), and because it is close to the robe season, and because it is a case where permission is given both to those for whom the Kathina is not spread and to those who have spent the Rains'—thus it is written in a certain commentary note. Some, however, say: 'As for this passage, beginning with "here, for the Sangha that has spent the Rains" and so forth up to the word "in the coming Rains," having set it aside as a question, this phrase, "Why? Because it arises at the back time," should be written later at the conclusion of "there, it reaches all those present." If it is asked "Why?", it is because there is no distinction with what is stated later: "from the robe-month onwards up to the winter"; therefore, some say of them, "They are wise."' Here, however, it is specified by the word 'here,' while there it is not; therefore, it should be understood that there is no contradiction between them. 'These robes reach me'—this statement itself is the determination; this is stated here in the pre-eminent sense. It is said that even if 'these robes are mine' is said, it is still determined. If 'these are mine' is said, that statement contains no word 'robes'; therefore, it must indeed be said, 'the robes reach me'—so they say. 'Misapprehended'—they are indeed Sangha property. It is written: 'Regarding the statement, "It is indeed taken by name," although it is not known that "this has been obtained," nevertheless, those portions have in substance been obtained by them—this is the intention.' 'If one has not arrived, those who come later receive a share'—thus it is said.

Upanandasakyaputtavatthukathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Story of Upananda the Sakyan

364. “Na, bhikkhave, aññatra vassaṃvutthenā”ti cīvarasamayaṃ upādāya paṭikkhepo kato[V 0.0455].Ekasmiṃ vihāre “rājavihāre viya nānāpariveṇesu vā idha vā vutthā labhatū”ti vatvā dinnaṃ. “Sattāhavārena aruṇameva uṭṭhāpetīti etaṃ vacanamattameva ekavihāre sattāhakiccābhāvā”ti ca likhitaṃ.

364. “Monks, not unless one has completed the rains-residence,” thus a refusal was made with reference to the robe-season. In one monastery, it was given after saying, “Let those who have completed the rains-residence here receive it, just as in a royal monastery or in various separate dwellings.” And it was written, “This statement, ‘He causes the dawn to be announced on a weekly turn,’ is merely a saying, because in a single monastery there is no seven-day duty.”

Matasantakakathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Account of the Property of the Deceased

369. Bhikkhussāti bhikkhusmiṃ kālaṃkate. Tattha “pattacīvare”ti padhānaparikkhāradassanamukhena sabbaparikkhāranidassananti veditabbaṃ. Adhammena uppannañcetaṃ [M 0.0499] hoti, saṅghassa kappiyameva matattāti eke. Noti takko pattacatukke sabbathā akappiyapattanayavirodhato. Adhammena uppannasenāsane ca vasato anāpatti. Aññatarasmiṃ āvāse dve bhikkhū vasanti, tattha ceko kālaṃkato, itaro tassa parikkhāraṃ apāpetvā taṃ theyyacittena gaṇhāti, saṅghasantakaṃ gahitaṃ hoti, bhaṇḍagghena kāretabbo. Anāvāse gaṇhāti, na kāretabbo assāmikassa gahitattā. Maraṇasamaye vattuṃ asahanto ce citteneva deti, puññaṃ pasavati, saṅghova tassa sāmī. Paro vā avissāsiko sayameva gaṇhāti, gahaṇaṃ na ruhati, theyyacittena ce, bhaṇḍagghena kāretabbo. Tassa ca āvāsagatassa ko sāmī. “Saṅgho sāmī”ti vacanato saṅghena balakkārena so vāretabboti eke. Jīvamānakāle gahitattā na saṅgho sāmīti eke. Sāmiko ce sayaṃ passitvā acchindituṃ labhati, saṅghopi labhati sāmiṭhāne ṭhitattāti itare, vicāretvā gahetabbaṃ.

369. “Bhikkhussa”: this concerns a bhikkhu who has passed away. Therein, “pattacīvare” (bowl and robe) should be understood as an indication of all requisites by way of showing the principal requisites. Some say that even if it has arisen unlawfully, it is permissible for the Sangha because its owner is dead. The reasoning against this is that it is not permissible, because it completely contradicts the principle concerning impermissible bowls in the section on the four bowls. And there is no offense for one dwelling in a lodging that has arisen unlawfully. In a certain dwelling, two bhikkhus reside; if one of them dies there, and the other, without delivering his (the deceased's) requisites, takes them with a thieving mind, what is taken is the Sangha's property; he should be made to pay its value. If he takes it in a non-dwelling, he should not be made to pay, because what was taken was ownerless. If at the time of death, being unable to speak, he gives with the mind alone, merit arises; the Sangha alone is its owner. Or if another, an untrusted person, takes it by himself, the taking is not valid; if with a thieving mind, he should be made to pay its value. And of his property that is in the dwelling, who is the owner? Because of the statement “The Sangha is the owner,” some say that he should be forcibly restrained by the Sangha. Some say that the Sangha is not the owner because it was taken while he was alive. If there is an owner, he, having seen it, is able to seize it back; the Sangha is also able to, because it stands in the position of the owner, thus say others. It should be taken after investigation.

Matakassa hiraññādiakappiyabhaṇḍaṃ hoti. Uggahitañcetaṃ hoti, uggahite vuttanayena paṭipajjitabbaṃ. Dhammena uppannaṃ ce, kappiyakārako ācikkhitabbo. Dāso ce gahito hoti, na saṅgho sāmī, ārāmiko ce, saṅgho sāmī. Gāvīmahiṃsīādayo honti, āvāsagatānaṃ saṅgho sāmī, anāvāsagatānaṃ na saṅgho sāmī. Saṅgho ce āvāsaṃ ānetvā attano santakaṃ katvā pacchā samīpe bahisīmāya ṭhapeti, kārakasaṅgho sāmī, tathā ārāmike. Matakassa parikkhāro nikkhepavasena ṭhapito hoti, esova sāmī. Mahaggho ce hoti, sesassa saṅgho sāmī. “Kenaci gilānupaṭṭhākenā”ti vattabbakkamo etena dassito. Puna upaṭṭhākānaṃ bahubhāve sati sabbesaṃ dātabbakammaṃ dassentena bhagavatā kammavācāyaṃ “gilānupaṭṭhākāna”nti vuttaṃ. Sāmaṇeravāre “cīvara”nti pāṭho. “Imaṃ tuyhaṃ demi dadāmi dajjāmi oṇojemi pariccajāmi vissajjāmi nissajjāmī’ti vā ‘itthannāmassa demi…pe… nissajjāmī’ti vā vadati, ‘sammukhā vā parammukhā vā vutte dinnaṃyeva hotī’ti [V 0.0456] dānalakkhaṇassa ca ‘tuyhaṃ gaṇhāhī’ti vutte ‘mayhaṃ gaṇhāmī’ti vadati, ‘sudinnaṃ suggahitañcā’ti (pārā. aṭṭha. 2.469) gahaṇalakkhaṇassa ca vuttattā ‘mama [M 0.0500] santakaṃ tava ca mama ca hotū’ti evamādivacanena samānaparikkhāraṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭatīti ācariyā”ti likhitaṃ.

If a deceased monk has gold and other unallowable items, and if these have been accepted, one should proceed according to the method stated in the Uggahita training rule. If they have arisen lawfully, the one who makes things allowable should be informed. If a slave has been accepted, the Sangha is not the owner; if it is a monastery attendant, the Sangha is the owner. If there are cows, buffaloes, and the like, for those that are on the monastery grounds, the Sangha is the owner; for those not on the monastery grounds, the Sangha is not the owner. If the Sangha brings an item to the monastery, makes it its own property, and later places it nearby outside the boundary, the Sangha that performed the act is the owner; the same applies in the case of a monastery attendant. If a deceased monk's requisites have been placed by way of a deposit, that very person with whom they are deposited is the owner. If they are of great value, the Sangha is the owner of the remainder. The procedure to be followed is indicated by the phrase, 'by some attendant of the sick.' Furthermore, when there are many attendants, the Blessed One, showing the act of giving to all of them, said in the formal act (kammavācā), 'to the attendants of the sick.' In the section on novices, the reading is 'robe.' One says, 'I give this to you, I grant, I would give, I dedicate, I relinquish, I release, I give up,' or 'To one named so-and-so I give... I give up.' And because of the characteristic of giving—that 'when it is said whether in one's presence or in one's absence, it is indeed given'—and because of the characteristic of receiving—that when told, 'Take this for yourself,' one says, 'I take what is for me,' and it is said, 'it is well-given and well-received'—it is written: 'The teachers state that it is allowable to make requisites common property with such words as, "Let my property be yours and mine."

Anugaṇṭhipade pana atīva papañcaṃ katvā puna “idamettha ācariyānaṃ sanniṭṭhānaṃ – sacesambahulā, dve vā samānaparikkhāraṃ kattukāmā honti, te sabbe attano santakaṃ vattamānaṃ uppajjanakena saddhiṃ pesalassa ekassa pariccajanti, so puna tesameva pariccajati, ettāvatā te samānaparikkhārikā hontīti. Idaṃ samānaparikkhāralakkhaṇaṃ pāḷiādīsu vuttalakkhaṇeyeva patanato acalappattaṃ hoti, tathāpi porāṇavidhiṃ ajjhottharitvā vattanato paṭisedhetabbo, ācariyānaṃ matānusārena kātabbaṃ kātukāmenāti apare”ti vuttaṃ, “vassaṃvutthasāmaṇero pañcasu sikkhāpadesu ekaṃ atikkamitvā puna gahito lābhaṃ na labhati, antimavatthuṃ ajjhāpanno nāma hotī”ti vadanti.

However, in the Anugaṇṭhipada, having greatly elaborated, it is further said: 'This is the conclusion of the teachers herein: if many monks, or two, wish to have shared requisites, they all relinquish their own present belongings, together with future belongings, to one virtuous monk; he, in turn, relinquishes it to those same monks. By this much, they become sharers of requisites. This characteristic of shared requisites, because it falls within the very characteristic stated in the Pāḷi and other texts, becomes unshakeable. Nevertheless, because it proceeds by overwhelming the ancient procedure, it should be rejected. It should be done by one who wishes to act in accordance with the opinion of the teachers, thus others say.' It is said: 'They say that a novice who has completed the rains-residence, having transgressed one of the five training precepts and having been reinstated, does not receive the gain; he is called one who has committed a final offense.'

Vassaṃvutthānaṃanuppannacīvarakathāvaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Discussion of the Robe-cloth Not Yet Arisen for Those Who Have Completed the Rains-residence

375. Uppanne cīvare abhājite pakkamatīti ettha “saṅghena tatruppādato ekekassa bhikkhuno ettakaṃ vassāvāsikaṃ dātuṃ saṅghassa ruccatī”ti sāvitepi vibbhamati, tato na labhati, puna pabbajitvā upasampajjitvā cīvarabhājanaṃ sambhāventopi na labhatiyeva pubbapakatito bhaṭṭhattā. Atha pāpite vibbhamati, labhatī”ti ca vuttaṃ.

375. Herein, regarding 'he departs when the robe-cloth has arisen but is undivided': Even when it has been announced, 'The Saṅgha approves of giving this much rains-residence cloth to each monk from what has arisen there,' if he disrobes, because of that he does not receive it. Even having gone forth again, received higher ordination, and being present for the robe-distribution, he certainly does not receive it, because of having fallen from his former state. And it is said: 'Now, if he disrobes after it has been brought, he receives it.'

Saṅghebhinnecīvaruppādakathāvaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Discussion of the Arising of Robe-cloth When the Saṅgha is Split

376. Parasamuddeti jambudīpe.

376. Regarding `parasamudde`: it means in Jambudīpa.

Aṭṭhacīvaramātikākathāvaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Discussion of the Mātikā of the Eight Robe-cloths

379. Yasmā aparikkhittassa parikkhepārahaṭṭhānaṃ dubbijānaṃ, tasmā “apicā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha dhuvasannipātaṭṭhānampi pariyantagatameva gahetabbaṃ. “Mahāpaccariyaṃ pana bhikkhūsupi…pe… pāpuṇātīti ‘upacārasīmāya demā’ti evaṃ dinnameva sandhāyā”ti likhitaṃ[V 0.0457]. “Samānasaṃvāsakasīmāyā”ti vutte khaṇḍasīmādīsu ṭhitānaṃ na pāpuṇāti tāsaṃ visuṃ samānasaṃvāsakasīmattā. Samānasaṃvāsakaavippavāsasīmānaṃ idaṃ nānattaṃ – “avippavāsasīmāya dammī”ti dinnaṃ gāmaṭṭhānaṃ na pāpuṇāti. Kasmā? “Ṭhapetvā gāmañca [M 0.0501] gāmūpacārañcā”ti vuttattā. “Samānasaṃvāsakasīmāyā”ti dinnaṃ pana yasmiṃ ṭhāne avippavāsasīmā atthi, tattha ṭhitānaṃ, itaratra ṭhitānañca pāpuṇāti. “Khaṇḍasīmāyaṃ ṭhatvā ‘sīmaṭṭhakasaṅghassa dammī’ti vutte upacārasīmāya eva paricchinditvā dātabba”nti vuttaṃ. “Avippavāsasīmāya demā”ti khaṇḍasīmāyaṃ ṭhatvā dinne tattheva pāpuṇātīti keci. Yojanasatampi pūretvā nisīdantīti ettha vihārūpacāre hatthapāsena, bahigāmādīsu dvādasahatthena upacāroti eke. “Imasmiṃ vihāre saṅghassā”ti vutte ekābaddhā hutvāpi parikkhepaparikkhepārahaṭṭhānaṃ atikkamitvā ṭhitānaṃ na pāpuṇātīti eke. “Bhikkhunivihārato bahi yattha katthaci ṭhatvā ‘saṅghassā’ti vutte bhikkhusaṅghova sāmī”ti vadanti. Ekopi gantvāti ettha sabbesaṃ vā pāpetvā gantabbaṃ, ānetvā vā pāpetabbaṃ, itarathā gatassa na pāpuṇāti. Samānalābhakatikā mūlāvāse sati siyā, mūlāvāsavināsena katikāpi vinassati. Samānalābhavacanaṃ sati dvīsu, bahūsu vā yujjati. Teneva ekasmiṃ avasiṭṭhe yujjatīti no mati.

379. Because, for a monastery that is not enclosed, the area suitable for an enclosure is difficult to know, therefore, 'apicā,' etc., was said. Therein, even a place of constant assembly should be taken as only that which is situated at the boundary. In the Mahāpaccarī, however, it is written: '...it reaches even the bhikkhus...etc.'—this refers only to that which is given thus: 'We give within the proximity boundary.' When 'within the common residence boundary' is said, it does not reach those standing in fragmented boundaries, etc., because they have separate common residence boundaries. This is the difference between the common residence boundary and the non-separation boundary: what is given with the words, 'I give within the non-separation boundary,' does not reach those situated in the village. Why? Because it was said, 'excluding the village and the village vicinity.' But what is given with the words, 'within the common residence boundary,' reaches those standing in a place where a non-separation boundary exists, and also those standing in another place. It was said: 'When, having stood in a fragmented boundary, one says, "I give to the Sangha of the boundary," it should be given having demarcated it only by the proximity boundary.' Some say that when, having stood in a fragmented boundary, one gives, saying, 'We give within the non-separation boundary,' it reaches only that very non-separation boundary. Regarding 'they sit filling even a hundred yojanas,' some say that the proximity is by a hand's reach in the monastery's vicinity, and by twelve cubits outside the village, etc. Some say that when it is said, 'To the Sangha in this monastery,' even if it is a single connected area, it does not reach those who are standing having gone beyond the enclosure and the area suitable for an enclosure. They say that when, having stood anywhere outside a bhikkhunī's monastery, one says, 'To the Sangha,' only the Bhikkhu Sangha is the owner. Regarding 'even one may go,' one should go having made it reach all, or one should have it brought and made to reach them; otherwise, it does not reach the one who has gone. An agreement for shared gains may exist when the original residence exists; with the destruction of the original residence, the agreement is also destroyed. The term 'shared gains' is applicable when there are two or many. That it is applicable for that very reason when one remains—this is our opinion.

“Tāvakālikakālena, mūlacchedavasena vā;

Aññesaṃ kammaṃ aññassa, siyā nāvāsasaṅgamo”ti. –

For a temporary period, or by way of cutting off the root, the formal act of some concerning others may result in non-association in the residence.

Ācariyo.

The teacher.

Sabbattha dinnamevāti “samānabhāgova hotī”ti vadanti. “Ekamekaṃ amhākaṃ pāpuṇātīti ce vadati, vaṭṭatī”ti vadanti vibhāgassa katattā. “Bhikkhusaṅghassa cīvare dinne paṃsukūlikānaṃ na vaṭṭatī”ti vadanti. “Ubhatosaṅghassā”ti vutte “bhikkhusaṅghassā”ti avuttattā bhikkhunisaṅghena missitattā, tattha apariyāpannattā ca puggalo visuṃ labhati. Evaṃ sante “bhikkhusaṅghassa ca bhikkhunisaṅghassa ca dammī”ti vuttepi “ubhatosaṅghassa dinnameva hotī”ti iminā virujjhatīti ce? Na virujjhati, taṃ dvinnaṃ saṅghānaṃ dinnabhāvameva dīpeti, na ubhatosaṅghapaññattiṃ, tasmā eva “bhikkhusaṅghassa ca bhikkhunisaṅghassa ca tuyhañcā”ti vāro na vutto. Atha vā aṭṭhakathāvacanameva pamāṇaṃ, na vicāraṇāti eke. Yasmā eko addhānādiyako viya duvidho na hoti, tasmā ubhatosaṅghaggahaṇena eko bhikkhu na gahitoti[V 0.0458]. “Sabbāvāsassa ca cetiyassa ca dhammassa [M 0.0502] cā’ti vutte sabbavihāresu cetiyadhammānaṃ ekekassa bhikkhuno bhāgo dātabbo”ti vadanti. “Bhikkhusaṅghassa ca cetiyassa cā”ti vutte na virujjhatīti ce? Na, tattha “bhikkhusaṅghassā”ti vuttattā, idha vihārena ghaṭitattā ca tamhi tamhi vihāre ekabhāgaṃ labhitabbamevāti pariharanti. Attano pāpetvāti vikāle aparibhogattā sakalopi vaṭṭeyyāti ce? “Bhikkhusaṅghassa harā”ti vuttattā, tena “harāmī”ti gahitattā ca na vaṭṭati. Pacchimavassaṃvutthānampīti ettha api-saddo avadhāraṇattho, pacchimavassaṃvutthānamevāti attho, itarathā samuccayatthe gahite “lakkhaṇaññū vadantī”ti vacanaṃ niratthakaṃ siyā. Kasmāti ārabhitvā papañcaṃ karonti. Kiṃ tena, parato “cīvaramāsato paṭṭhāya…pe… atītavassaṃvutthānameva pāpuṇātī”ti iminā siddhattā na vicāritaṃ, tena vuttaṃ “lakkhaṇaññū”ti acalavasena. Sace pana bahiupacārasīmāya ṭhito…pe… sampattānaṃ sabbesaṃ pāpuṇātīti yattha katthaci vutthavassānanti adhippāyo “yattha katthaci vutthavassānaṃ sabbesaṃ sampattānaṃ pāpuṇātī”ti (kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. akālacīvarasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā) kaṅkhāvitaraṇiyaṃ vuttattā. Gimhānaṃ paṭhamadivasato paṭṭhāya vutte pana yasmā anantarātītaṃ hemantaṃ eva vutthā nāma honti, na vassaṃ, tasmā “mātikā āropetabbā”ti vuttaṃ. Ye vā therehi pesitā, tesaṃ pāpuṇātīti kira attho.

Because it is given to all, they say, 'There is an equal share.' They say, 'If one says, "It reaches each one of us," it is allowable,' because the division has been made. They say, 'When a robe is given to the Bhikkhu Saṅgha, it is not allowable for the rag-robe wearers.' When 'to the dual Saṅgha' is said, because 'to the Bhikkhu Saṅgha' is not said, and because it is mixed with the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha, and because an individual is not included therein, a person receives separately. This being so, if one were to say: does it contradict the statement, 'It is indeed given to the dual Saṅgha,' even when it is said, 'I give to the Bhikkhu Saṅgha and to the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha'? It does not contradict. That indicates only the fact of having been given to the two Saṅghas; it does not indicate the designation 'dual Saṅgha'. For that very reason, the case 'to the Bhikkhu Saṅgha and to the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha and to you' is not stated. Alternatively, some say the word of the commentary itself is the authority, not investigation. Because one person, like a traveler, is not twofold, therefore by the term 'dual Saṅgha' a single bhikkhu is not included. When it is said, 'To all residences, and to the cetiya, and to the Dhamma,' they say that in all monasteries, a share for the cetiya and the Dhamma should be given to each bhikkhu. If one were to say: does this contradict the ruling given when it is said 'to the Bhikkhu Saṅgha and to the cetiya'? No. Because there it was stated 'to the Bhikkhu Saṅgha,' and here, because it is connected with the monastery, they resolve it thus: 'In each respective monastery, one share must indeed be received.' Regarding 'having brought it for oneself': if one were to say, 'Since it is not for consumption at the wrong time, would the whole thing be allowable?' Because it was said, 'Take it for the Bhikkhu Saṅgha,' and because it was taken by him with the thought, 'I am taking it,' it is not allowable. Here, in 'also for those who have completed the later rains-retreat,' the word 'also' (api) has the sense of emphasis. The meaning is 'only for those who have completed the later rains-retreat.' Otherwise, if it were taken in the sense of conjunction, the statement 'those who know the characteristics say' would be meaningless. If one asks, 'Why?', they begin to elaborate. What is the use of that? Since it is established by the later statement, 'From the robe-month onwards... it reaches only those who have completed the past rains-retreat,' it is not investigated. Therefore, 'those who know the characteristics' is said in the sense of being unshakeable. In the passage, 'But if, standing outside the surrounding boundary... it reaches all who have arrived,' the intended meaning is 'for those who have completed the rains-retreat anywhere whatsoever,' because it is stated in the Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī: 'It reaches all who have arrived who have completed the rains-retreat anywhere whatsoever.' But when it is said 'from the first day of the hot season onwards,' because only the immediately preceding cool season is what is called 'completed,' not the rains-retreat, therefore it is said, 'The matrix should be applied.' Or, for those who were sent by the elders, the meaning is that it is said to reach them.

Cīvarakkhandhakavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Chapter on Robes is Concluded.

9. Campeyyakkhandhakavaṇṇanā

9. The Commentary on the Campeyya Section

Dvenissāraṇādikathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Account Beginning with the Two Kinds of Expulsion.

395. Appatto [V 0.0459][M 0.0503] nissāraṇanti ettha nissāraṇaṃ nāma kuladūsakānaṃyeva anuññātaṃ, ayaṃ pana kuladūsako na hoti, tasmā “appatto”ti vutto. Yadi evaṃ kathaṃ sunissārito hotīti? Cūḷavagge “ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho pabbājanīyakammaṃ kareyyā”ti (cūḷava. 27) vuttattā. “Tassapāpiyasikakammārahassa tassapāpiyasikakammaṃ karontī”ti vacanato cakkaṃ bandhanti ñātabbaṃ.

395. Herein, regarding the phrase ‘Not liable for expulsion’: the act called expulsion is permitted only for those who corrupt families, but this monk is not a corrupter of families; therefore, he is said to be ‘not liable’. If so, how is he well-expelled? Because in the Cūḷavagga it is said, ‘If the Saṅgha wishes, it may perform the act of banishment,’ he is well-expelled. In accordance with the statement, ‘They perform the tassapāpiyasikakamma for one who is deserving of the tassapāpiyasikakamma,’ it should be understood that they bind the wheel.

Upālipucchākathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Account of Upāli’s Questions.

400. “Paratoti upālipucchato para”nti likhitaṃ. Dosāritapāḷiyaṃ “ūnavīsativasso na āgato vippannavatthukattā”ti vuttaṃ. Imasmiṃ campeyyakkhandhake adhammakammāniyeva dvidhā katvā pañcāgatānīti veditabbaṃ. Teneva parivāre imasmiṃ khandhake “pañca adhammikānī”ti vuttaṃ. “Andhamūgabadhiro sosārito”ti iminā apabbajitassapi upasampadā ruhatīti siddhaṃ.

400. ‘Parato’ is written as ‘after the questions of Upāli.’ In the Dosārita-pāḷi, it is stated, ‘A person of less than twenty years has not come (to ordination) because of having a faulty basis.’ In this Campeyya Section, it should be understood that the unlawful acts themselves, having been divided into two, have come to five. For that very reason, both in the Parivāra and in this section, it is said, ‘five are unlawful.’ By this text, ‘A blind, mute, and deaf person is well-admitted,’ it is established that the higher ordination of one who has not gone forth also succeeds.

Campeyyakkhandhakavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Campeyya Section is concluded.

10. Kosambakakkhandhakavaṇṇanā

10. The Commentary on the Kosambaka Section.

Kosambakavivādakathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Account of the Kosambaka Dispute.

451. Suttantikoti [V 0.0460][M 0.0504] ettha kiñcāpi “vinayadharo mātikādharo”ti vuttaṃ, ubhatovibhaṅgaṃ pana sandhāya vuttaṃ, na khandhakabhāṇako hoti. Āvuso ettha āpattīti vacanaṃ upādāya “so tassā āpattiyā āpattidiṭṭhi hotī”ti vuccati. Pacchā vinayadharo “vatthumhi sati pamāṇaṃ, na paññattiya”nti satiṃ paṭilabhitvā tassā āpattiyā āpattidiṭṭhi ahosi, tena vuttaṃ ante “aññe bhikkhū tassā āpattiyā āpattidiṭṭhino hontī”ti.

451. Herein, regarding 'Suttantika': although it is said, 'a Vinaya-holder, a Mātikā-holder,' this is said in reference to both Vibhaṅgas; he is not a reciter of the Khandhakas. Based on the statement, 'Friend, herein is an offense,' it is said, 'he has the view of an offense regarding that offense.' Later, the Vinaya-holder, having regained mindfulness that 'when there is a basis, it is the standard, not the regulation,' had the view of an offense regarding that offense. Therefore, it is said at the end, 'other bhikkhus have the view of an offense regarding that offense.'

455. “Yathā mayā ñattī”ti likhanti “paññattā”ti ekavacanattā.

455. They write, 'As the motion by me,' because 'paññattā' is in the singular.

Dīghāvuvatthukathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Account of the Story of Dīghāvu.

458. “Bhūtapubbaṃ, bhikkhave, bārāṇasiyaṃ brahmadatto”ti likhanti. Purāṇapotthakesu “bārāṇasiya”nti natthi, “natthibhāvova sundaro”ti vadanti.

458. They write: ‘Formerly, bhikkhus, in Bārāṇasī, Brahmadatta...’ In ancient palm-leaf manuscripts, the reading ‘bārāṇasiya’ is not present; they say, ‘Its very absence is good.’

Pālileyyakagamanakathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Account of the Going to Pālileyyaka.

467. Rakkhitavanasaṇḍeti saṅgītittherehi suviññeyyaṃ katvā vuttaṃ. “Pālileyyoti gāmo, tassa vasenā”tipi vadanti, taṃ dhammapadaṭṭhakathāya na virujjhati.

467. ‘In the Rakkhita Forest Grove’ was stated by the Elders of the Council, having made it easily understandable. They also say, ‘Pālileyya is a village; it is on account of that.’ This does not contradict the Dhammapada Commentary.

Aṭṭhārasavatthukathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Account of the Eighteen Matters.

473. Na [V 0.0461] tveva…pe… paṭibāhitabbanti vadāmīti ettha senāsanārahassa yo senāsanaṃ paṭibāhati, tasseva āpatti dukkaṭassa. “Kalahakārakādīnamettha okāso natthītiādikaṃ saṅghassa katikaṃ vatvā taṃ na paññāpentassa vā ‘ahaṃ buddho’ti pasayha attanā attano paññāpetvā gaṇhantaṃ ‘yuttiyā gaṇhathā’ti vatvā vārentassa vā doso natthi. Idha kalahavūpasamanatthaṃ āgatānaṃ kosambikānampi ‘yathāvuḍḍha’nti avatvā ‘vivitte asati vivittaṃ katvāpi dātabba’nti vuttattā vivittaṃ katvā dentaṃ [M 0.0505] paṭibāhentasseva āpattīti kira ayamattho pārivāsikādīnaṃ vihārapariyantadāpanena sādhitabbo”ti likhitaṃ.

473. Herein, regarding the passage, ‘I do not say… it should be obstructed’: For one who obstructs a lodging for a monk deserving of a lodging, for that very one there is an offense of wrong-doing. Having stated the Saṅgha's formal act, such as, ‘There is no opportunity here for quarrel-makers and the like,’ there is no fault for the one (the Buddha) who did not lay down that rule, nor for one who prevents another—who, having forcibly declared, ‘I am the Buddha,’ makes this known to his own disciples and takes them—by saying, ‘Take them by right.’ Here, for the purpose of quelling the quarrel, even for the Kosambī monks who have come, since it was said, without saying ‘according to seniority,’ that ‘If there is no secluded place, it should be given even after making one secluded,’ there is an offense only for the one who obstructs another who is giving a lodging after making it secluded. It is written that it seems this meaning should be established by having the very last monastery given to those on probation and the like.

Saṅghasāmaggīkathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Account of Saṅgha Harmony.

475. “Atha kho te ukkhittānuvattakā bhikkhū taṃ ukkhittakaṃ bhikkhuṃ osāretvā yena ukkhepakā bhikkhū…pe… tassa vatthussa vūpasamāya saṅghasāmaggiṃ karomā”ti vacanaṃ duviññeyyavinicchayaṃ vinayalakkhaṇakusalassa. Vijjamāne hi kārakasaṅghe itaro saṅgho osārituṃ na labhati. Osārento ce, te bhikkhū kārakasaṅghena samānaladdhikabhāvaṃ pattattā tena samānasaṃvāsakā honti, tato ukkhepakānaṃ chandaṃ aggahetvā osārentānaṃ kammaṃ kuppati, tasmā “tena hi, bhikkhave, taṃ bhikkhuṃ osārethā”ti (mahāva. 474) bhagavato vacanena ukkhittānuvattakā osāresuṃ, udāhu nissīmaṃ gantvā, udāhu itaresaṃ chandaṃ gahetvā osāresuṃ, nanu etesamaññatarenettha bhavitabbaṃ, na ca panetaṃ sabbagaṇṭhipadesu vicāritaṃ. Ayaṃ panettha takko –

475. The statement, ‘Then those bhikkhus who followed the expelled one, having reinstated that expelled bhikkhu, went to the expelling bhikkhus… for the resolution of that matter, let us perform Saṅgha harmony,’ is a decision difficult to discern even for one skilled in the characteristics of the Vinaya. For when the acting Saṅgha exists, the other Saṅgha cannot reinstate him. If they do reinstate him, those bhikkhus, having attained the state of holding the same view as the acting Saṅgha, become of the same communion with them. Then, for those who reinstate without obtaining the consent of the expelling bhikkhus, the act is invalid. Therefore, by the Blessed One’s statement, ‘Well then, bhikkhus, reinstate that bhikkhu,’ did the followers of the expelled one reinstate him? Or did they go beyond the boundary and reinstate him? Or did they obtain the consent of the others and reinstate him? Surely, one of these must have happened here. However, this has not been examined in all the knotty points. Here is our reasoning:

“Yasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ saṅghena, katakammassa bhikkhuno;

Sati tasmiṃ na aññassa, paṭippassambhanaṃ khamaṃ.

‘In a matter where an act has been performed by the Saṅgha concerning a bhikkhu, while that matter exists, its revocation by another is not allowable.

“Viramante tato doso, api saṅgho akārako;

Osāretuṃ alaṃ yasmā, kārako anulomiko”ti.

‘There would be a fault in refraining from that; since the acting Saṅgha is in conformity, even a non-acting Saṅgha is not fit to reinstate.’

477. “Aṭṭha dūtaṅgāni nāma sotā ca hoti, sāvetā ca uggahetā ca dhāretā ca viññātā [V 0.0462] ca viññāpetā ca kusalo ca sahitāsahitadassano ca akalahakārako cāti etānī”ti vuttaṃ.

477. ‘Eight qualities of a messenger are named: he is a listener, one who makes others listen, a learner, a retainer, one who understands, one who makes others understand, skilled, one who discerns what is beneficial and not beneficial, and not a quarrel-maker.’ Thus it is said.

Kosambakakkhandhakavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Kosambaka Section is concluded.

Mahāvaggassa līnatthapakāsanā niṭṭhitā.

The Elucidation of the Obscure Meanings of the Mahāvagga is concluded.

Namo tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa

Homage to the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One.

Cūḷavaggavaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Cūḷavagga

1. Kammakkhandhakavaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Kammakkhandhaka.

Adhammakammadvādasakakathāvaṇṇanā

1. The Commentary on the Discourse of the Twelve Unrighteous Acts.

4. Asammukhā [M 0.0507][V 0.0463] kataṃ hotītiādayo tikā kevalaṃ desanāmattameva.
