Na hi tīhi eva aṅgehi samodhānehi adhammakammaṃ hoti, ekenapi hoti eva, ayamattho “tiṇṇaṃ, bhikkhave”tiādipāḷiyā (cūḷava. 6) sādhetabbo. “Appaṭiññāya kataṃ hotī”ti lajjiṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Kaṇhapakkhe “adesanāgāminiyā āpattiyā kataṃ hotī”ti sukkapakkhe “desanāgāminiyā āpattiyā kataṃ hotī”ti idaṃ dvayaṃ parato “tīhi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho tajjanīyakammaṃ kareyya. Adhisīle sīlavipanno hotī”ti iminā virujjhati, adesanāgāminiṃ āpanno hi “adhisīle sīlavipanno”ti vuccatīti. Yuttametaṃ, kattu adhippāyo ettha cintetabbo. Etthāha upatissatthero “tajjanīyakammassa hi visesena bhaṇḍanakārakattaṃ aṅga’nti aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttaṃ, taṃ pāḷiyā āgatanidānena yujjati, tasmā sabbattikesupi bhaṇḍanaṃ āropetvā bhaṇḍanapaccayā āpannāpattivasena idaṃ kammaṃ kātabbaṃ, tasmā ‘adhisīle sīlavipanno’ti etthāpi pubbabhāge vā [V 0.0464] aparabhāge vā codanāsāraṇādikāle bhaṇḍanapaccayā āpannāpattivaseneva kāretabbaṃ, na kevalaṃ saṅghādisesapaccayā kātabba”nti. “Adesanāgāminiyā āpattiyāti pārājikāpattiyā’ti ettakamattaṃ vatvā parato ‘adhisīle pārājikasaṅghādisese ajjhācārā’ti porāṇagaṇṭhipade vutta”nti likhitaṃ. “Adhisīle sīlavipanno’ti saṅghādisesaṃ sandhāyā”ti gaṇṭhipade likhitaṃ. Idaṃ porāṇagaṇṭhipade purimavacanena sameti, tasmā tattha pacchimaṃ pārājikapadaṃ atthuddhāravasena vuttaṃ siyā[M 0.0508], aṭṭhakathāyañca “adesanāgāminiyāti pārājikāpattiyā vā saṅghādisesāpattiyā vā”ti vuttaṃ, tattha pārājikāpatti atthuddhāravasena vuttā siyā. Yato gaṇṭhipade “adhisīle sīlavipanno’ti saṅghādisesaṃ sandhāyā”ti ettakameva likhitaṃ, tasmā sabbattha gaṇṭhipade sakalena nayena pārājikāpattipaccayā uppannabhaṇḍanahetu na tajjanīyakammaṃ kātabbaṃ payojanābhāvā, saṅghādisesapaccayā kātabbanti ayamattho siddho hoti. Na, sukkapakkhe “desanāgāminiyā āpattiyā kataṃ hotī”ti (cūḷava. 5) vacanatoti ce? Na, ekena pariyāyena saṅghādisesassapi desanāgāminivohārasambhavato,

4. The triads beginning with 'It is done not in the presence' are merely a matter of teaching. Indeed, an unlawful formal act does not occur only by the combination of three factors; it occurs even by one. This meaning should be established by the Pāḷi text beginning with 'Monks, of three...'. The statement 'It is done without acknowledgement' was said in reference to a scrupulous person. In the black section, 'It is done for an offense not leading to confession,' and in the white section, 'It is done for an offense leading to confession'—these two statements are contradicted by the following: 'Monks, the Saṅgha, if it wishes, may carry out the formal act of censure on a monk endowed with three factors. He is corrupt in higher virtue.' For one who has fallen into an offense not leading to confession is called 'corrupt in higher virtue'. This objection is fitting. The intention of the author should be considered here. Here, the Elder Upatissa said: 'Indeed, it is said in the commentary: "For the formal act of censure, being a maker of quarrels is a specific factor." That is consistent with the origin story that has come down in the Pāḷi. Therefore, in all triads as well, having imputed quarreling, this formal act should be done on account of an offense one has fallen into due to quarreling. Therefore, in the case of "corrupt in higher virtue" as well, it should be carried out only on account of an offense one has fallen into due to quarreling, either in the earlier part or in the later part, at the time of accusation, reminding, etc.; it should not be done merely on account of a Saṅghādisesa offense.' It is written: 'Having said just this much, "‘An offense not leading to confession’ means a Pārājika offense," it is said later in the ancient glossary, "‘In higher virtue’ means transgression in Pārājika or Saṅghādisesa.”' It is written in the glossary: 'The phrase "corrupt in higher virtue" is said in reference to a Saṅghādisesa offense.' This agrees with the previous statement in the ancient glossary. Therefore, there, the latter term 'Pārājika' may have been said for the purpose of extracting the meaning. And in the commentary it is said: 'An offense not leading to confession means either a Pārājika offense or a Saṅghādisesa offense.' There, 'Pārājika offense' may have been said for the purpose of extracting the meaning. Since in the glossary only this much is written, 'The phrase "corrupt in higher virtue" is said in reference to a Saṅghādisesa offense,' therefore, everywhere in the glossary, by the entire method, the formal act of censure should not be done on account of a quarrel that has arisen due to a Pārājika offense, because there is no purpose. It should be done on account of a Saṅghādisesa offense. Thus this meaning is established. If it is said, 'This is not so, because of the statement in the white section, "It is done for an offense leading to confession,"' that should not be said. Why? Because in one way, it is possible to speak of a Saṅghādisesa offense also as 'leading to confession'.

Yena kammena santajjanaṃ karīyati, taṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ nāma. Yena kammena nissāya te vatthabbanti nissiyati bhajāpiyati niyasso, taṃ niyasakammaṃ nāma. Yena tato āvāsato, gāmato ca pabbājenti kuladūsakaṃ, taṃ pabbājanīyakammaṃ nāma. Yena kammena akkuṭṭhagahaṭṭhasamaīpameva paṭisāriyati so akkosako pacchā pesiyati, taṃ paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ nāma. Yena samānasaṃvāsakabhūmito ukkhipiyati. Chaḍḍīyati sātisāro bhikkhusaṅghena, taṃ kammaṃ ukkhepanīyakammaṃ nāmāti veditabbaṃ.

The act by which intimidation is done is called the act of censure (tajjanīyakamma). The act by which one is made to depend, saying, 'You should dwell in dependence,' and is made to associate with a teacher, that is called the act of dependence (niyasakamma). The act by which they expel a corrupter of families from that monastery and from that village is called the act of expulsion (pabbājanīyakamma). The act by which that abuser is sent only to the presence of a householder who is not angry and is sent back afterwards is called the act of reconciliation (paṭisāraṇīyakamma). The act by which a monk with an offense is removed from the ground of communal living and is discarded by the Saṅgha of monks, that should be known as the act of suspension (ukkhepanīyakamma).

11. “Nissāya te vatthabba”nti garunissayaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ, na itaranti.

11. The statement, 'You should dwell in dependence,' was said with reference to dependence on a respected teacher; it was not said with reference to another.

21. Assajipunabbasukavatthusmiṃ “tesu vibbhantesupi kammaṃ paṭippassambhetuṃ anuññātampi sammāvattantānaṃyevā”ti likhitaṃ. Sammukhā vuttameva gihipaṭisaṃyuttaṃ nāma. Parammukhā vuttaṃ desanaṃ gacchati.

21. In the story of Assaji and Punabbasu, it is written: 'Although it was permitted to revoke the formal act even for those monks who had disrobed, it was permitted only for those who were practicing well.' Only what is said in one's presence is called 'connected with a householder.' What is said in one's absence amounts to a report.

41. Khamāpentena “khamāhī”ti vattabbamattameva, na ukkuṭikādisāmīcinā payojananti. Anudūtanti sahāyanti attho.

41. By one asking for forgiveness, only 'Forgive' should be said; there is no need for proper conduct such as squatting. The meaning of 'anudūta' is a companion.

50. Adassaneyeva ukkhepanīyaṃ kātabbaṃ, na aññathā. “Tajjanīyādikaraṇakāle āpattiṃ [V 0.0465] ropetvā tassā adassane, appaṭikamme vā bhaṇḍanakārakādiaṅgehi kātabba”nti likhitaṃ.

50. The act of suspension should be done only for not seeing an offense, not for any other reason. It is written: 'At the time of performing an act of censure and so on, having charged him with an offense, the act should be done on account of his not seeing that offense, or not making amends for it, or on account of factors such as being quarrelsome.'

Tajjanīyakammādīsu ayaṃ pakiṇṇakavinicchayoti veditabbo. Kiṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ, tajjanīyakammassa kiṃ mūlaṃ, kiṃ vatthu, kiṃ pariyosānaṃ, kasmā [M 0.0509] “tajjanīyakamma”nti vuccatīti? Kiṃ tajjanīyakammanti vatthusmiṃ sati karaṇasampatti. Tajjanīyakammassa kiṃ mūlanti saṅgho mūlaṃ. Tajjanīyakammassa kiṃ vatthūti kalahajātāpattivatthu. Kiṃ pariyosānanti bhāvanāpariyosānaṃ. Kasmā tajjanīyakammanti vuccatīti saṅgho kalahakārakapuggalaṃ kalahe ca bhede ca bhayaṃ dassetvā khantiyā janeti, upasame janeti, tasmā “tajjanīyakamma”nti vuccati. Kathaṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ kataṃ hoti, kathaṃ akataṃ. Kinti ca tajjanīyakammaṃ kataṃ hoti, kinti ca akataṃ. Kena ca tajjanīyakammaṃ kataṃ hoti, kena ca akataṃ. Kattha ca tajjanīyakammaṃ kataṃ hoti, kattha ca akataṃ. Kāya velāya tajjanīyakammaṃ kataṃ hoti, kāya velāya akataṃ hoti? Kathaṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ kataṃ hotīti samaggena saṅghena ñatticatutthena kammena. Kathaṃ akataṃ hotīti vaggena saṅghena ñatticatutthena kammena. Kinti ca kataṃ hotīti karaṇasampattiyā. Kinti ca akataṃ hotīti karaṇavipattiyā. Kena ca kataṃ hotīti saṅghena. Kena ca akataṃ hotīti gaṇena puggalena. Kattha ca kataṃ hotīti yassa puggalassa saṅgho tajjanīyakammaṃ karoti, tassa puggalassa sammukhībhūte. Kattha ca akataṃ hotīti yassa puggalassa saṅgho tajjanīyakammaṃ karoti, tassa puggalassa asammukhībhūte. Kāya velāya kataṃ hotīti yadā kalahajātāpatti saṃvijjati. Kāya velāya akataṃ hotīti yadā kalahajātāpatti na saṃvijjati. Katihākārehi tajjanīyakammassa pattakallaṃ hoti, katihākārehi apattakallaṃ? Sattahākārehi tajjanīyakammassa pattakallaṃ hoti, sattahākārehi apattakallaṃ. Katamehi sattahākārehi pattakallaṃ, katamehi sattahākārehi apattakallaṃ hoti? Kalahajātāpatti na saṃvijjati, so vā puggalo asammukhībhūto hoti, saṅgho vā vaggo hoti, asaṃvāsiko vā puggalo tassaṃ parisāyaṃ saṃvijjati, acodito vā hoti asārito vā, āpattiṃ vā anāropito. Imehi sattahākārehi tajjanīyakammassa apattakallaṃ hoti, itarehi sattahākārehi pattakallaṃ hoti. Evaṃ sesakammesūti.

In regard to the act of censure (tajjanīyakamma) and other such matters, this miscellaneous judgment should be understood. What is the act of censure? What is the root of the act of censure? What is its basis? What is its conclusion? Why is it called ‘the act of censure’? Regarding the question, 'What is the act of censure?': it is the accomplishment of the procedure when a basis exists. Regarding the question, 'What is the root of the act of censure?': the Saṅgha is the root. Regarding the question, 'What is the basis of the act of censure?': an offense arising from a quarrel is the basis. Regarding the question, 'What is its conclusion?': the announcement (kammavācā) is the conclusion. Regarding the question, 'Why is it called ‘the act of censure’?': because the Saṅgha, showing the quarrelsome person fear regarding quarrels and divisions, generates patience and generates calm; therefore it is called ‘the act of censure’. How is the act of censure carried out, and how is it not carried out? In what way is the act of censure carried out, and in what way is it not carried out? By whom is the act of censure carried out, and by whom is it not carried out? Where is the act of censure carried out, and where is it not carried out? At what time is the act of censure carried out, and at what time is it not carried out? How is the act of censure carried out? By a harmonious Saṅgha with a formal act preceded by a motion. How is it not carried out? By a factional Saṅgha with a formal act preceded by a motion. In what way is it carried out? By the accomplishment of the procedure. In what way is it not carried out? By the failure of the procedure. By whom is it carried out? By the Saṅgha. By whom is it not carried out? By a group or an individual. Where is it carried out? In the presence of the person against whom the Saṅgha is carrying out the act of censure. Where is it not carried out? In the absence of the person against whom the Saṅgha is carrying out the act of censure. At what time is it carried out? When an offense arising from a quarrel exists. At what time is it not carried out? When an offense arising from a quarrel does not exist. In how many ways is the act of censure fit to be carried out, and in how many ways is it unfit to be carried out? In seven ways, the act of censure is fit to be carried out; in seven ways, it is unfit to be carried out. Which seven ways make it fit to be carried out, and which seven ways make it unfit to be carried out? An offense arising from a quarrel does not exist; or that person is not present; or the Saṅgha is divided; or a person who is not in communion is present in that assembly; or he has not been accused or reminded; or the offense has not been charged. In these seven ways, the act of censure is unfit to be carried out; in the other seven ways, it is fit to be carried out. Thus it should be understood for the remaining acts.

Kammakkhandhakavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Chapter on Formal Acts is finished.

2. Pārivāsikakkhandhakavaṇṇanā

2. The Commentary on the Chapter concerning Probationers

Pārivāsikavattakathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourse on the Probationer's Observances

75. Pārivāsikakkhandhake [V 0.0466][M 0.0510] “mā maṃ gāmappavesanaṃ āpucchathāti vutte anāpucchāpi gāmaṃ pavisituṃ vaṭṭatī”ti vadanti. Saṅgho attano pattaṭṭhāne gahetuṃ vaṭṭati. Oṇojanaṃ nāma vissajjanaṃ. “Taṃ pana pārivāsikena pāpitassa attanā sampaṭicchitasseva punadivasādiatthāya vissajjanaṃ kātabbaṃ, asampaṭicchitvāyeva ce vissajjeti, na labhatī”ti vuttaṃ.

75. In the chapter concerning probationers, they say: 'When it is said, "Do not ask me about entering the village," it is permissible to enter the village even without asking.' It is permissible for the Saṅgha to take at its place of arrival. Relinquishment (oṇojana) is giving up. It is said: 'But that relinquishment should be done by the probationer for the purpose of the next day, etc., only of that which has been brought to him and accepted by himself; and if he relinquishes it without having accepted it, he does not obtain it.'

76. Pakatiyāva nissayoti ettha “antevāsikānaṃ ālayasabbhāve yāva vassūpanāyikadivaso, tāva kappati, tassa ālayassa sabbhāve nissayo na paṭippassambhatīti ce? Na vaṭṭati. Tattha idāni khamāpeyyāmītiādinā vaṭṭatī”ti vuttaṃ. Tattha ekantena vissaṭṭhattā, idha pana ekanteneva dvinnampi samabhāvo icchitabbo evāti eke. Paṭibalassa vā bhikkhussāti ettha “laddhasammutikena āṇattopi garudhammehi, aññehi vā ovadituṃ na labhatī”ti likhitaṃ. Tato vā pāpiṭṭhatarāti ettha “asañcicca āpannasañcarittato sukkavissaṭṭhi pāpiṭṭhatarāti ayampi nayo yojetabbo”ti vuttaṃ. Paccayanti vassāvāsikaṃ. Senāsanaṃ na labhati seyyapariyantabhāgitāya. “Uddesādīni dātumpi na labhatī”ti vadanti. “Sace dve pārivāsikā gataṭṭhāne aññamaññaṃ passanti, ubhohipi aññamaññassa ārocetabbaṃ avisesena ‘āgantukena ārocetabbaṃ, āgantukassa ārocetabba’nti vuttattā”ti vuttaṃ. Aññavihāragatenāpi tattha pubbe ārocitassa punārocanakiccaṃ natthi. “Anikkhittavattassa bahi ārocitassa yathā puna vihāre ārocanakiccaṃ natthi, evaṃ ‘āgantukasodhanatthaṃ uposathadivase ārocetabba’nti vacanañhettha sādhaka”nti vadanti.

76. Herein, regarding 'natural dependence,' it is said: 'For disciples, if there is attachment, it is allowable until the day of entering the rains-residence. If one were to say that in the presence of that attachment the dependence does not cease, that is not proper. Therein, it is said that it is proper by stating, "Now I will ask for forgiveness," etc.' Therein, it ceases because it is entirely relinquished. But here, some say that an equal status for both should indeed be desired. Herein, regarding 'or of a capable monk,' it is written: 'A monk who has received authorization, even if instructed, is not able to advise concerning grave matters or other things.' Herein, regarding 'or more evil than that,' it is said: 'The offense of emission of semen is more evil than a sañcaritta offense incurred without intention; this method should also be applied.' Regarding 'requisite,' it refers to the rains-residence lodging. One does not obtain it because one's share is limited to a sleeping place. They say: 'One is not able to give recitations, etc., either.' It is said: 'If two probationers see each other in the place they have gone to, both should inform each other, because it is said without distinction, "The newcomer should inform; the newcomer should be informed."' Even for one who has gone to another monastery, there is no duty to inform again one who has been previously informed there. Some say: 'Just as for one who has not laid aside the observance and has informed outside, there is no duty to inform again in the monastery, so also the statement, "One should inform on the Uposatha day for the purpose of purifying newcomers," is the proof in this matter.'

81. Ekacchanne nisinnassāpi ratticchedadukkaṭāpattiyo hontīti eke. Avisesenāti pārivāsikassa ukkhittakassāti imaṃ bhedaṃ akatvā. “Tadahupasampannepi pakatatte”ti vacanato anupasampannehi vasituṃ vaṭṭati. “Samavassāti etena apacchā apurimaṃ nipajjane dvinnampi vattabhedāpattibhāvaṃ dīpetī”ti likhitaṃ.

81. Some say that even for one sitting under a common roof, offenses of wrong conduct for interrupting the night occur. 'Without distinction' means without making the distinction between a probationer and one who has been suspended. Because it is said, 'Even one ordained on that day is a monk in good standing,' it is proper to live with those not fully ordained. It is written: 'By this, "of equal seniority," it indicates that for both, in lying down not in order of seniority, there is an offense of breaking the observance.'

Pārivāsikavattakathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Discourse on the Probationer's Observances is concluded.

Mūlāyapaṭikassanārahavattakathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourse on the Observances for One Deserving Return to the Root

86. Attano [V 0.0467][M 0.0511] attano navakataranti pārivāsikādinavakataraṃ. Paṭhamaṃ saṅghamajjhe parivāsaṃ gahetvā nikkhittavattena puna ekassapi santike samādiyituṃ, nikkhipituñca vaṭṭati. Mānatte pana nikkhipituṃ vaṭṭati. Ūne gaṇe caraṇadosattā na gahetunti eke. Paṭhamaṃ ādinnavattaṃ ekassa santike yathā nikkhipituṃ vaṭṭati, tathā samādiyitumpi vaṭṭatīti porāṇagaṇṭhipade.

86. Herein, 'newer for each one' refers to a younger monk on probation. First, having taken probation in the midst of the Sangha, for one whose practice has been set aside, it is permissible to undertake it again in the presence of even one monk, and also to set it aside. In the case of penance, however, it is permissible to set it aside. Some say that it is not proper to undertake it in an incomplete group because of the fault of conduct. In the Ancient Commentary it is said: 'Just as it is permissible to set aside the initially undertaken practice in the presence of one monk, so too is it permissible to undertake it.'

Pārivāsikakkhandhakavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Chapter on Probation is concluded.

3. Samuccayakkhandhakavaṇṇanā

3. The Explanation of the Chapter on Compilation

Sukkavissaṭṭhikathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourse on Seminal Emission

97. “Vedayāmīti [M 0.0512] jānāmi, cittena sampaṭicchitvā sukhaṃ anubhavāmi, na tappaccayā ahaṃ dukkhitoti adhippāyo”ti likhitaṃ. Yassa māḷake nārocitaṃ, tassa ārocetvā nikkhipitabbaṃ. Yassa ārocitaṃ, tassa puna ārocanakiccaṃ natthi, kevalaṃ nikkhipitabbameva. Vattaṃ nikkhipitvā vasantassa upacārasīmāgatānaṃ sabbesaṃ ārocanakiccaṃ natthi. Diṭṭharūpānaṃ sutasaddānaṃ ārocetabbaṃ, adiṭṭhaassutānampi antodvādasahatthagatānaṃ ārocetabbaṃ. “Idaṃ vattaṃ nikkhipitvā vasantassa lakkhaṇa”nti vuttaṃ. “Parikkhittassa vihārassa parikkhepato’tiādi kiñcāpi pāḷiyaṃ natthi, atha kho aṭṭhakathācariyānaṃ vacanena tathā eva paṭipajjitabba”nti ca vuttaṃ. “Atthibhāvaṃ sallakkhetvāti dvādasahatthe upacāre sallakkhetvā, anikkhittavattānaṃ upacārasīmāya āgatabhāvaṃ sallakkhetvā sahavāsādikaṃ veditabba”nti ca vuttaṃ. “Nikkhipantena ārocetvā nikkhipitabbaṃ, payojanaṃ atthī”ti ca vuttaṃ, na pana taṃ payojanaṃ dassitaṃ. Ciṇṇamānatto bhikkhu abbhetabboti ciṇṇamānattassa ca abbhānārahassa ca ninnānākāraṇattā aññathā “abbhānāraho abbhetabbo”ti vattabbaṃ siyā. Ukkhepanīyakammakatopi attano laddhiggahaṇavasena sabhāgabhikkhumhi sati tassa anārocāpetuṃ na labhati.

97. It is written: '“I feel” means “I know”; having accepted it with the mind, I experience pleasure. Because of that reason, I am not suffering'—this is the intended meaning. For a monk for whom it has not been announced outside the chapter hall, it should be laid aside after having been announced to him. For one to whom it has been announced, there is no further duty of announcing; it should simply be laid aside. For one who is dwelling having laid aside the observance, there is no duty of announcing to all who have come to the proximity boundary. It should be announced to those whose forms are seen and whose sounds are heard; it should also be announced to those whose forms are not seen and whose sounds are not heard but who have come within twelve cubits. It is said: 'This is the characteristic of one who is dwelling having laid aside the observance.' And it is also said: 'Although the passage beginning “of an enclosed monastery, from its enclosure…” is not in the Pāḷi (Canon), it should nevertheless be practiced exactly according to the word of the commentary teachers.' And it is also said: 'Regarding the phrase “having discerned their presence”: having discerned within the twelve-cubit proximity, and having discerned the fact of the arrival of those who have not laid aside the observance into the proximity boundary, co-residence and so forth should be understood.' And it is also said: 'By one who is laying aside the observance, it should be laid aside after having been announced; there is a purpose,' but that purpose is not shown. Regarding the phrase 'a monk who has completed the mānatta should be reinstated': because there is no difference between one who has completed the mānatta and one who is worthy of reinstatement; otherwise, it should have been said, 'one worthy of reinstatement should be reinstated.' Even one who has been subjected to an act of suspension, by way of his own taking up of a view, cannot, when a monk of the same group is present, refrain from having it announced to him.

Parivāsakathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourse on Probation

102. “Anantarāyikassa [V 0.0468] pana antarāyikasaññāya chādayato acchannāvā”ti pāṭho. Averibhāvena sabhāgo averisabhāgo. “Sabhāgasaṅghādisesaṃ āpannassa pana santike āvi kātuṃ na vaṭṭatī”ti pasaṅgato idheva pakāsitaṃ. Lahukesu paṭikkhepo natthi. Tattha ñattiyā āvi katvā uposathaṃ kātuṃ anuññātattā lahukasabhāgaṃ āvi kātuṃ vaṭṭatīti. Sabhāgasaṅghādisesaṃ pana ñattiyā ārocanaṃ na vaṭṭatīti kira. “Tassa santike taṃ āpattiṃ paṭikarissatī’ti (mahāva. 171) vuttattā lahukassevāyamanuññātā[M 0.0513]. Na hi sakkā suddhassa ekassa santike saṅghādisesassa paṭikaraṇaṃ kātu”nti likhitaṃ. Lahukesupi sabhāgaṃ āvi kātuṃ na vaṭṭatīti, tasmā eva hi ñattiyā āvikaraṇaṃ anuññātaṃ, itarathā taṃ niratthakaṃ siyā. Aññamaññārocanassa vaṭṭati, tato na vaṭṭatīti dīpanatthameva ñattiyā āvikaraṇamanuññātaṃ, teneva idha “sabhāgasaṅghādisesaṃ āpannassā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Ayamattho “ettāvatā te dve nirāpattikā honti, tesaṃ santike sesehi sabhāgāpattiyo desetabbā”ti (kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. nidānavaṇṇanā) vacanena kaṅkhāvitaraṇiyaṃ pakāsitova. Saṅghādisesaṃ pana ñattiyā ārocetvā uposathaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭati. Tassā ñattiyā ayamattho yadā suddhaṃ bhikkhuṃ passissati, tassa santike ārocanavasena paṭikarissati. Evaṃ paṭikate “na ca, bhikkhave, sāpattikena pātimokkhaṃ sotabbaṃ, yo suṇeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti (cūḷava. 386) vuttāpattito mokkho hotīti, tasmā “garukaṃ vā hotu lahukaṃ vā, ñattiyā āvi kātuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti vuttaṃ, ubhosu nayesu yuttataraṃ gahetabbaṃ.

102. “However, there is a reading: ‘For one without an obstruction who conceals with the perception of an obstruction, it is indeed not concealed.’” An associate through non-enmity is a non-enemy associate. “But for one who has incurred a shared Saṅghādisesa offense, it is not proper to disclose it in his presence”; this is explained here in context. There is no prohibition regarding minor offenses. Because it is permitted there to make known a minor shared offense through a formal announcement (ñatti) and then perform the Uposatha, it is proper to disclose a minor shared offense. But it seems that announcing a shared Saṅghādisesa offense through a formal announcement is not proper. “Because it was said, ‘He will deal with that offense in his presence,’ this permission is only for minor offenses. For it is not possible to carry out the rehabilitation for a Saṅghādisesa offense in the presence of a single pure monk,” thus it is written. Even with respect to minor offenses, it is not proper to disclose a shared offense; therefore, indeed, disclosure by formal announcement is permitted, otherwise it would be pointless. Mutual disclosure is proper; the permission to disclose by formal announcement is solely for the purpose of clarifying that it is not proper otherwise, and thus here “For one who has incurred a shared Saṅghādisesa offense,” etc., is stated. This meaning is indeed disclosed in the Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī with the statement, “With just this much, these two become free from offenses, and the remaining shared offenses should be confessed in their presence.” However, having announced a Saṅghādisesa offense through a formal announcement, it is proper to perform the Uposatha. The meaning of that announcement is this: when he sees a pure bhikkhu, he will deal with it by means of disclosure in his presence. Once dealt with in this way, there is release from the offense stated, “Monks, a person with an offense should not listen to the Pātimokkha. Whoever listens, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).” Therefore, it is said, “Whether grave or minor, it is proper to disclose by formal announcement.” In both methods, the more reasonable should be adopted.

Nāmañceva āpatti cāti “tena tena vītikkamenāpannāpatti āpatti. Nāmanti tassā āpattiyā nāma”nti likhitaṃ. Ārocetvā nikkhipitabbanti ettha ārocanaṃ vattabhedadukkaṭapaaharaṇappayojananti veditabbaṃ. Akāraṇametanti “sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajji”nti vutte vuṭṭhānato.

Regarding 'name and offense,' it is written: 'The offense incurred by that transgression is an offense. "Name" is the name of that offense.' Regarding 'having declared, it should be put aside,' it should be understood that the declaration has the purpose of removing the dukkaṭa offense for breaking the observance. Regarding 'This is without reason,' it is because of emerging from the offense when it is said, 'He has committed many Saṅghādisesa offenses.'

Dasasataṃ rattisatanti dasasataṃ āpattiyo rattisataṃ chādetvāti yojetabbaṃ. Agghasamodhāno nāma sabhāgavatthukāyo sambahulā āpattiyo āpannassa bahurattiṃ paṭicchāditāpattiyaṃ nikkhipitvā dātabbo, itaro nānāvatthukānaṃ vasenāti ayametesaṃ visesoti.

Regarding 'a thousand, a hundred nights,' it should be construed as: 'having concealed a thousand offenses for a hundred nights.' Agghasamodhāna is to be given to one who has committed many offenses of a similar basis, having grouped them into the offense concealed for many nights. The other is to be given by way of offenses with different bases. This is the distinction between them.

Parivāsakathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Discourse on Probation is concluded.

“Gāmassāti [V 0.0469] na vutta”nti vacanato kira gāmūpacārepi vaṭṭatīti adhippāyoti likhitaṃ. Vuttañca “ayaṃ pana viseso”ti. “Ettha aṭṭhakathācariyāva pamāṇaṃ. Yuttaṃ na dissatī”ti likhitaṃ. Anugaṇṭhipade pana “ayaṃ pana viseso, āgantukassa…pe… okkamitvā gacchati, ratticchedo hotiyevā”ti vacane heṭṭhā “antoaruṇe eva nikkhamitvā gāmūpacārato dve [M 0.0514] leḍḍupāte atikkamitvā”tiādinā nayena garuṃ katvā vacanato, bhikkhunīnaṃ garukavaseneva tattha tattha sikkhāpadānaṃ paññattattā ca tadanurūpavaseneva aṭṭhakathācariyena bhikkhunīnaṃ garuṃ katvā mānattacaraṇavidhidassanatthaṃ “yattakā purebhattaṃ vā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Kurundiādīsu vuttavacanena karontassapi doso natthīti dassetuṃ kevalaṃ lakkhaṇamattameva vuttaṃ, tadubhayampi tena tena pariyāyena yujjati, vinicchaye patte lakkhaṇe eva ṭhātabbato kurundiādīsu vuttavacanaṃ pacchā vuttaṃ. Payogo pana purimova. Yathā cettha, tathā sace kāci bhikkhunī dve leḍḍupāte anatikkamitvā aruṇaṃ uṭṭhapeti, doso natthi, tathāpi sabbaṭṭhakathāsu vuttattā “purimameva āciṇṇa”nti vuttaṃ. Parivāsavattādīnanti “parivāsanissayapaṭippassaddhiādīnaṃ upacārasīmāya paricchinnattā bhikkhunupassayassa upacārasīmāva gahetabbā, na gāmo”ti likhitaṃ. “Tasmiṃ gāme bhikkhācāro sampajjatī’tiādi pavāritavasena vuttaṃ. Na hi tattha antogāme vihāro atthī”ti ca likhitaṃ, “tampi tena pariyāyena yujjati, na atthato”ti ca.

It is written: “Because it is not stated as ‘of the village,’ the intention is that it is permissible even in the vicinity of a village.” And it is said: “But this is the distinction.” It is written: “Here, the commentary teachers are the authority. What is suitable is not apparent.” In the sub-commentary, however, regarding the statement, “But this is the distinction: for a visitor… having entered, he goes—there is indeed an interruption of the night,” it is said below, “having left just before dawn, passing beyond two stone-throws from the vicinity of the village,” and so on, by way of treating the matter with gravity. Because the training rules for bhikkhunīs were laid down with gravity in various places, the commentary teachers, in accordance with that gravity, stated, “as much as before the meal,” and so on, to demonstrate the method of observing mānatta for bhikkhunīs by treating it with gravity. In the Kurundī and other commentaries, it is said that to show there is no fault even for one who acts according to the statement, only the characteristic is mentioned. Both are justified in their respective ways. When a decision is reached, one should stand only on the characteristic; therefore, the statement in the Kurundī and other commentaries was stated later. The application, however, is as before. Just as here, if any bhikkhunī causes the dawn to arise without having passed beyond two stone-throws, there is no fault. Nevertheless, because it is stated in all the commentaries, it is said: “only the earlier practice is followed.” Regarding the observances of probation and so on, it is written: “Because probation, dependence, cessation, and so on are defined by the vicinity-boundary, the vicinity-boundary of the bhikkhunīs’ residence should be taken, not the village.” It is also written: “The statement, ‘In that village, the alms-round is successful,’ and so on, is said by way of invitation. For there is no monastery within that village,” and also, “that too is justified in that way, but not in terms of its direct meaning.”

Paṭicchannaparivāsādikathāvaṇṇanā

The Exposition of the Discourse on Concealed Probation and so on

108. “Visuṃ mānatthaṃ caritabbanti mūlāya paṭikassanaṃ akatvā visuṃ kammavācāyā”ti ca likhitaṃ. “Saṅghādisesāpattī”ti vuttattā ekova, ekavatthumhi āpannā saṅghādisesā thullaccayadukkaṭamissakā nāma. Makkhadhammo nāma chādetukāmatā.

108. And it is also written: “To undergo mānatta separately means it should be undergone by a separate formal act without having been sent back to the root.” Because it is said “a Saṅghādisesa offense,” there is only one. Saṅghādisesa offenses incurred on a single occasion are called those mixed with thullaccaya and dukkaṭa offenses. The characteristic of hypocrisy (makkha) is the desire to conceal.

143. Dhammatāti dhammatāya, tathātāyāti attho “alajjitā”ti ettha viya.

143. Regarding `dhammatā`: the meaning is 'by its nature,' 'by its true state,' as in the case of `alajjitā`.

148. Purimaṃ upādāya dve māsā parivasitabbāti ettha “parivasitadivasāpi gaṇanūpagā hontī”ti likhitaṃ.

148. Regarding the statement, “Taking into account the previous, probation should be undergone for two months,” it is written: “Even the days on which probation was undergone are included in the count.”

184. Tasmiṃ bhūmiyanti tassaṃ bhūmiyaṃ. Sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjati parimāṇampītiādi jātivasenekavacanaṃ.

184. `Tasmiṃ bhūmiyaṃ` means 'in that place' or 'in that ground.' The phrase beginning with 'he incurs numerous Saṅghādisesa offenses, and also of a certain measure' is in the singular by way of class. The Exposition of the Discourse on Concealed Probation and so on is concluded.

Samuccayakkhandhakavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Chapter on Accumulation is concluded.

4. Samathakkhandhakavaṇṇanā

4. The Commentary on the Chapter on Settlement

Sammukhāvinayakathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Discourse on Face-to-Face Adjudication

186-187. Yattha [V 0.0470][M 0.0515] yattha kammavācāya “aya”nti vā “ime”ti vā sammukhāniddesaniyamo atthi, sabbaṃ taṃ kammaṃ sammukhākaraṇīyameva, na kevalaṃ tajjanīyādipañcavidhameva. Pañcavidhasseva pana uddharitvā dassanaṃ kammakkhandhake tāva tasseva pāḷiāruḷhattā, catuvīsatiyā pārājikesu vijjamānesu pārājikakaṇḍe āgatānaṃyeva catunnaṃ uddharitvā dassanaṃ viyāti veditabbaṃ. Tattha “puggalassa sammukhatā hatthapāsūpagamanamevā”ti vuttaṃ, taṃ kāraṇaṃ sammukhākaraṇīyassapi sammukhāniddesaniyamābhāvato. Kāmaṃ ayamattho kammakkhandhakeyeva “tīhi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgataṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ adhammakammañca hoti…pe… asammukhākataṃ hotī”ti (cūḷava. 4) vacaneneva siddho, tattha pana āpatti na dassitā. Idha “yo kareyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti tattha bhavitabbāpattidassanatthaṃ idaṃ āraddhanti veditabbaṃ. “Sammukhāvinayapatirūpakena vūpasantampi sammukhāvinayeneva vūpasantagaṇanaṃ gacchatīti dassetuṃ ‘adhammavādī puggalo’tiādi āraddha”nti vuttaṃ, likhitañca. Evaṃ vūpasantaṃ sammukhāvinayapatirūpakena vūpasantaṃ nāma hoti, na sammukhāvinayena ca aññena kenacīti dassetuṃ idamāraddhanti ācariyo.

In whichever formal act there is a rule of designation in the presence, saying ‘this’ or ‘these,’ all such acts must be performed in the presence, not merely the five kinds beginning with the act of censure. However, the presentation of only the five kinds by singling them out in the Chapter on Formal Acts is because they alone are included in the Pāḷi text. This should be understood to be like the presentation of only the four Pārājikas that are mentioned in the Section on Pārājikas by singling them out, even though twenty-four Pārājikas exist. Therein, it is said, “The presence of a person is only the coming within arm’s reach.” That is because, even for an act that must be performed in the presence, there is no rule of designation in the presence. Indeed, this meaning is already established in the Chapter on Formal Acts itself by the statement: “Monks, an act of censure endowed with three factors is an unlawful act… it is not performed in the presence…” However, the offense is not shown there. Here, it should be understood that this was introduced to show the offense that should be incurred therein, by the words, “Whoever should do so, commits an offense of wrong conduct.” It is said, and also written: “The passage beginning with ‘a person who speaks contrary to the Dhamma’ was introduced to show that even what is settled by a semblance of the face-to-face procedure is counted as settled by the face-to-face procedure itself.” The teacher says that this was introduced to show that what is thus settled is called ‘settled by a semblance of the face-to-face procedure,’ and it is not settled by the face-to-face procedure itself, nor by any other means. The Commentary on the Discourse on Face-to-Face Adjudication is concluded.

Sativinayakathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Discourse on the Procedure for Mindfulness

195. Dabbassa kammavācāya “saṅgho imaṃ āyasmantaṃ dabba”nti sammukhāniddeso natthi, tathāpi “paṭhamaṃ dabbo yācitabbo”ti vacanena sammukhākaraṇīyatā tassa siddhā. Tathā aññatthāpi yathāsambhavaṃ leso veditabbo. Sativepullappattassa dātabbo vinayo sativinayo.

195. In the formal act concerning Dabba, there is no designation in the presence, such as “The Saṅgha… this Venerable Dabba.” Nevertheless, the fact that it must be performed in his presence is established by the statement, “First, Dabba should be requested.” Similarly, in other cases as well, a hint should be understood as is possible. The procedure to be given to one who has attained the full expansion of mindfulness is the procedure for mindfulness. The Commentary on the Discourse on the Procedure for Mindfulness is concluded.

Amūḷhavinayakathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Discourse on the Procedure for One Not Deluded

196-7. “Yassa ummattakassa taṃtaṃvītikkamato anāpatti, tādisasseva amūḷhavinayaṃ dātuṃ vaṭṭatīti amūḷhassa kattabbavinayo amūḷhavinayo”ti likhitaṃ, taṃ yuttaṃ “saṅgho [V 0.0471] gaggassa bhikkhuno amūḷhassa amūḷhavinayaṃ [M 0.0516] detī”ti vacanato. “Tīṇimāni, bhikkhave, adhammikāni amūḷhavinayassa dānānī”ti imassa vibhaṅge “na sarāmī”ti vacanaṃ vītikkamakālaṃ sandhāya tassa vibhaṅgassa pavattattā. Amūḷhavinayadānakāle panassa amūḷhatā vinicchitabbā.

It is written: “For whichever insane person there is no offense for transgressing this or that, it is proper to grant the procedure for one not deluded only to such a one; thus, the procedure to be performed for one who is not deluded is the procedure for one not deluded.” This is appropriate because of the statement, “The Saṅgha grants the procedure for one not deluded to the bhikkhu Gagga, who is not deluded,” and because in the analysis of “Monks, these three are unrighteous ways of granting the procedure for one not deluded,” the statement “I do not remember” proceeds in reference to the time of the transgression. However, at the time of granting the procedure for one not deluded, his state of not being deluded must be ascertained. The Commentary on the Discourse on the Procedure for One Not Deluded is concluded.

Paṭiññātakaraṇakathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Discourse on Acting upon Acknowledgement

200. “Appaṭiññāya bhikkhūnaṃ kammāni karontī”ti ārabhantassa kāraṇaṃ vuttameva. Paṭiññātena karaṇaṃ paṭiññātakaraṇaṃ.

200. The reason for beginning with, “They perform formal acts for the bhikkhus by way of acknowledgement,” has already been stated. Acting upon acknowledgement is `paṭiññātakaraṇa`. The Commentary on the Discourse on Acting upon Acknowledgement is concluded.

Tassapāpiyasikākathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Discourse on the Procedure for Further Misconduct

207. “Tīhi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgataṃ tassapāpiyasikākamma”nti ārabhitvā pañca aṅgāni dassetvā pāḷi gatā, “sā peyyālena saṅkhipitvā gatāti ñātabba”nti likhitaṃ. Tathā sukkapakkhepi.

207. Having begun with, 'Monks, the Tassapāpiyasikā act is endowed with three factors,' and having shown five factors, the Pāḷi text proceeds. It is written: 'It should be known that it proceeds, having been abbreviated by means of peyyāla.' It is likewise in the bright section.

Tiṇavatthārakādikathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourse on Tiṇavatthāraka and so forth

214. “Sabbeheva ekajjhaṃ sannipatitabba”nti chandadānassa paṭikkhittattā pavāraṇakkhandhakaṭṭhakathāyañca “bhinnassa hi saṅghassa samaggakaraṇakāle, tiṇavatthārakasamathe, imasmiñca pavāraṇasaṅgaheti imesu tīsu ṭhānesu chandaṃ dātuṃ na vaṭṭatī”ti (mahāva. aṭṭha. 241) vuttattā idha āgantvā vā chandaṃ datvā pariveṇādīsu nisinnāti idaṃ virujjhati viya khāyatīti ce? Na khāyati adhippāyaññūnaṃ. Ayañhettha adhippāyo – visujjhitukāmehi sabbeheva sannipatitabbaṃ, asannipatitassa natthi suddhi chandadāyakassa. Kevalaṃ taṃ kammaṃ sannipatitānaṃ sampajjati. Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ visujjhitukāmānaṃ chandaṃ dātuṃ na vaṭṭatīti adhippāyo. Itarathā pāḷiyā ca virujjhati. “Ṭhapetvā ye na tattha hotī”ti hi ayaṃ pāḷi sannipātaṃ āgantvā chandaṃ datvā ṭhitānaṃ atthitaṃ dīpeti. Nissīmagate sandhāya vuttaṃ siyāti ce? Nissīmagate ṭhapetvā idha kiṃ, tasmā yo sāmaggīuposathe chandaṃ datvā tiṭṭhati ce, nānāsaṃvāsakabhūmiyaṃyeva tiṭṭhati, tassa chandadāyakassa pavāraṇasaṅgahopi natthi. Yo ca tiṇavatthārakakamme nāgacchati, so tāhi āpattīhi na sujjhatīti veditabbaṃ. Yassa etaṃ na ruccati[V 0.0472], tassa parivāre vuttaparisato kammavipattilakkhaṇaṃ [M 0.0517] virujjhati, tattha hi kevalaṃ chandārahānaṃ chando anāhaṭo hoti sace, akataṃ tabbiparītena sampattidīpanatoti vuttaṃ hoti. Tathā pattakallalakkhaṇampi virujjhati. Tesu tīsu ṭhānesu kammappattāyeva sabbe, na tattha chandāraho atthīti ce? Na, catuvaggādikaraṇavibhājane avisesetvā chandārahassa āgatattā, taṃ sāmaññato vuttaṃ. Idañca āveṇikalakkhaṇaṃ, teneva satipi diṭṭhāvikamme idaṃ paṭikuṭṭhakataṃ na hotīti ce? Na, nānattasabhāvato. Idha hi ye pana “na metaṃ khamatī’ti aññamaññaṃ diṭṭhāvikammaṃ karontī”ti (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 214) vacanato na saṅghassa diṭṭhāvikammaṃ kataṃ. Tasmiṃ sati paṭikuṭṭhakatameva hoti. Aññathā pubbabhāgā tā ñattiyo niratthikā siyuṃ, na ca parivāraṭṭhakathāyaṃ chandārahādhikāre nayo dinno. Pavāraṇakkhandhakaṭṭhakathāyaṃ “tīsu ṭhānesu chandaṃ dātuṃ na vaṭṭatī”ti (mahāva. aṭṭha. 241) vuttattā virujjhatīti ce? Na, aṭṭhakathāya pamāṇabhāve sati “idha chandaṃ datvā pariveṇādīsu nisinnā”tiādi vacane suddhikāmato eva gahite sabbaṃ na virujjhatīti eke. “Āgantvā vā chandaṃ datvā pariveṇādīsu nisinnā, te āpattīhi na vuṭṭhahantī”ti idaṃ na vattabbaṃ. Kasmā? Heṭṭhā “sabbeheva ekajjhaṃ sannipatitabba”nti chandadānassa paṭikkhepavacanato aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “tīsu ṭhānesu chandaṃ dātuṃ na vaṭṭatī”ti vuttattā, andhakaṭṭhakathāyampi tatheva vuttattā cāti? Na, ekajjhameva kamme karīyamāne yo idha “suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, amhākaṃ…pe… gihipaṭisaṃyutta”nti sādhāraṇañattiṃ ṭhapetvā puna “suṇantu me, āyasmantā”tiādinā asādhāraṇañattiyo ṭhapetvā “suṇātu me, bhante saṅgho, amhākaṃ…pe… evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti ekatopakkhikānaṃ sandhiyā katāya tadanantare kenaci karaṇīyena chandaṃ datvā gacchati, tassa āpattīhi vuṭṭhānaṃ natthi. Aparesampi ekatopakkhikānaṃ abbhantare ṭhitattā vibhūtattā karaṇassa ayamatthova vutto. Sādhāraṇavasena dutiyāya ñattiyā ṭhapitāya ye tasmiṃ khaṇe ñattidutiyakammavācāsu anāraddhāsu, apariyositāsu vā chandaṃ datvā gacchanti, tesampi na vuṭṭhāti eva. Ye na tattha hontīti padassa ca ye vuttappakārena nayena tattha na hontīti attho gahetabbo. Vuttappakāratthadīpanatthañca aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “chandaṃ datvā pariveṇādīsu nisinnā”ti idameva [M 0.0518] avatvā “ye pana tehi vā saddhiṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitvāpi tattha anāgatā, āgantvā vā chandaṃ datvā pariveṇādīsu nisinnā”ti vuttaṃ, evaṃ pubbenāparaṃ sandhīyati. “Pāḷiyā ca tattha diṭṭhāvikammena kammassa akuppatā veditabbā”ti vuttaṃ.

214. “All should gather together in one place”—because the giving of consent is rejected, and because it is stated in the commentary on the Pavāraṇakkhandhaka: “At the time of performing the harmony Uposatha for a divided Sangha, during the tiṇavatthāraka settlement, and during this Pavāraṇā saṅgaha, it is not proper to give consent in these three situations.” If one were to say: “Here, does the statement ‘[some monks] having come and given consent are sitting in their own quarters, etc.’ seem contradictory?” It does not appear so to those who understand the intention. For the intention here is this: those who desire purification must all gather together. There is no purification for the one who, being a giver of consent, does not assemble. Only, that act is accomplished for those who have gathered. The intention in the commentary is that it is not proper for those desiring purification to give consent. Otherwise, it contradicts the Pāḷi. This Pāḷi passage, “except those who are not present there,” indeed indicates the existence of those who come to the gathering, give consent, and remain. If one were to say: “Might it refer to those outside the boundary?” [The reply is:] Setting aside those outside the boundary, what relevance is that here? Therefore, if someone gives consent for the Uposatha of unity but remains [away], he remains in a place of different affiliation, and for that consent-giver, there is no inclusion in the Pavāraṇā saṅgaha. And one who does not attend the tiṇavatthāraka act should be understood as not purified from those offenses. For one who does not accept this, the characteristic of a failed act, as stated in the Parivāra, is contradicted. For there, it is said that if merely the consent of those entitled to give consent is not brought, the act is considered not done, and by its opposite, accomplishment is indicated. Likewise, the characteristic of fitness for the act is also contradicted. If one were to say: “In those three situations, are all fit for the act, with no one there entitled to give consent?” No, because in the analysis of acts performed by groups of four or more, one entitled to give consent is mentioned without distinction. That [statement about the three places] is a general statement. If one were to say: “And is this a special characteristic, so that even in the case of diṭṭhāvikamma, this is not considered paṭikuṭṭhaka?” No, due to the difference in nature. Here, according to the statement, “those who say, ‘This is not agreeable to me,’ and perform diṭṭhāvikamma against each other,” diṭṭhāvikamma has not been performed by the Sangha. In such a case, it is indeed paṭikuṭṭhaka. Otherwise, those preliminary motions would be meaningless, and the commentary on the Parivāra does not provide a method in the section on those entitled to give consent. If one were to say: “Does it contradict because the commentary on the Pavāraṇakkhandhaka states, ‘It is not proper to give consent in these three situations’?” No. According to some, since the commentary is authoritative, if the statement, “Here, having given consent, they sit in their own quarters,” etc., is understood in the context of desiring purification, then nothing is contradictory. Should it not be said, “Having come and given consent, they sit in their own quarters, and they are not freed from those offenses”? Why? Is it because previously, the statement, “All should gather together in one place,” rejects the giving of consent, and the commentary states, “It is not proper to give consent in these three situations,” and the Andhakaṭṭhakathā says the same? No. When the act is being performed together in one place, if someone—after establishing the common motion, ‘Venerable sirs, let the Sangha hear me… connected with householders,’ and then establishing the specific motions with ‘Venerable sirs, hear me…,’ and then after the unification of one faction is made with, ‘Venerable Sangha, hear me… thus do I hold it’—immediately after this, gives consent and leaves for some reason, they are not freed from those offenses. For others too, this very meaning is stated, because they remain within the one faction and the matter is clear. When the second motion has been established as common, those who at that moment give consent and leave while the ñatti-dutiyakamma-vācās have not begun or are incomplete, they too are indeed not freed. The phrase, “those who are not present there,” should be understood as meaning those who are not there in the manner described. And to clarify the meaning as described, the commentary, instead of just saying, “having given consent, they sit in their own quarters,” states, “those who, having committed an offense together with them, have not come there, or having come, give consent and sit in their own quarters.” Thus, the latter connects with the preceding. “And in the Pāḷi, the act’s unshakeability should be understood as due to diṭṭhāvikamma there,” it is said.

Adhikaraṇakathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Discourse on Disputes

220. Cittuppādo [V 0.0473] vivādo. Vivādasaddopi kāraṇūpacārena kusalādisaṅkhyaṃ gacchati. Taṃ sandhāya “samathehi ca adhikaraṇīyatāya adhikaraṇa”nti vuttaṃ. Atha vā vivādahetubhūtassa cittuppādassa vūpasamena sambhavassa saddassapi vūpasamo hotīti cittuppādassapi samathehi adhikaraṇīyatā pariyāyo sambhavati. “Kusalacittā vivadantī”ti vuttavivādepi “vipaccatāya vohāro”ti vuttaṃ, na vuttavacanahetuvasenāti veditabbaṃ.

220. A thought-arising is a dispute. Also, the term 'dispute,' through metaphorical usage for the cause, attains the designation of 'wholesome, etc.' Referring to that, it was said: 'And because it is to be settled by the means of settlement, it is an issue (adhikaraṇa).' Alternatively, since by the calming of the thought-arising that has become the cause of the dispute, there is also the calming of the word that has arisen, it is therefore possible that for the thought-arising also, the figurative expression 'being something to be settled by the means of settlement' applies. Regarding the dispute spoken of in 'Wholesome thoughts dispute,' it is said to be 'a conventional expression of opposition,' not by way of the spoken word being the cause—thus it should be understood.

222. “Āpattiñhi āpajjanto kusalacitto vā”ti vacanato kusalampi siyāti ce? Na taṃ āpattādhikaraṇaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ, yo āpattiṃ āpajjati, so tīsu cittesu aññataracittasamaṅgī hutvā āpajjatīti dassanatthaṃ “yaṃ kusalacitto āpajjatī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Yo “paññattimattaṃ āpattādhikaraṇa”nti vadeyya, tassa akusalādibhāvopi āpattādhikaraṇassa na yujjateva vivādādhikaraṇādīnaṃ viyāti ce? Na, “natthāpattādhikaraṇaṃ kusala”nti iminā virodhasambhavato. Anugaṇṭhipade pana “āpattādhikaraṇaṃ nāma tathāpavattamānaakausalacittuppādarūpakkhandhānametaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Avasiṭṭhesu kusalābyākatapaññattīsu ‘āpattādhikaraṇaṃ siyā akusalaṃ siyā abyākata’nti vacanato paññattitāva paṭisiddhā kusalattike apariyāpannattā. Kusalapaṭisedheneva tena samānagatikattā kiriyābyākatānampi paṭisedho veditabbo, kiriyābyākatānaṃ viya anugamanato vipākābyākatānampi paṭisedho katova hoti, tathāpi abyākatasāmaññato rūpakkhandhena saddhiṃ vipākakiriyābyākatānampi adhivacananti veditabba”nti vuttaṃ. Tattha “kusalacittaṃ aṅgaṃ hotī”ti vinaye apakataññuno sandhāya vuttaṃ appaharitakaraṇādike sati. Tasmāti yasmā [M 0.0519] “natthi āpattādhikaraṇaṃ kusala”nti vattuṃ na sakkā, tasmā kusalacittaṃ aṅgaṃ na hotīti attho. Yadi evaṃ kasmā “ticittaṃ tivedana”nti vuccatīti ce? Taṃ dassetuṃ “nayida”ntiādi āraddhanti eke. Āpattisamuṭṭhāpakacittaṃ aṅgappahonakacittaṃ nāma. “Ekantatoti yebhuyyenāti attho, itarathā virujjhati. Kasmā? ‘Yassā sacittakapakkhe cittaṃ akusalameva hotī’ti (kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. paṭhamapārājikavaṇṇanā) vuttattā”ti vadanti. Tena kiṃ? Vipāko natthi, kasmā? Ekantākusalattā, tasmā kathāva tattha natthi. Yattha pana atthi, taṃ dassento “yaṃ pana paṇṇattivajja”ntiādimāha. Asañcicca pana kiñci ajānantassa…pe… abyākataṃ hotīti bhikkhumhi kammaṭṭhānagatacittena nipanne, niddāyante vā mātugāmo ce seyyaṃ kappeti, tassa bhikkhuno vijjamānampi kusalacittaṃ āpattiyā aṅgaṃ na hoti, tasmā tasmiṃ khaṇe seyyākārena [V 0.0474] vattamānarūpameva āpattādhikaraṇaṃ nāma. Bhavaṅgacitte vijjamānepi eseva nayo. Tasmiñhi khaṇe uṭṭhātabbe jāte anuṭṭhānato rūpakkhandhova āpatti nāma, na vipākena saddhiṃ. Sace pana vadeyya, tassa evaṃvādino acittakānaṃ kusalacittaṃ āpajjeyya. Kiṃ vuttaṃ hoti? Eḷakalomaṃ gahetvā kammaṭṭhānamanasikārena tiyojanaṃ atikkamantassa, paṇṇattiṃ ajānitvā padaso dhammaṃ vācentassa ca āpajjitabbāpattiyā kusalacittaṃ āpajjeyyāti. Āpajjatiyevāti ce? Nāpajjati. Kasmā? “Natthi āpattādhikaraṇaṃ kusala”nti vacanato.

222. If one were to say, 'Because of the statement, "one who commits an offense with a wholesome mind," could the offense-basis also be wholesome?' This was not said with reference to the offense-basis. Rather, it was said to show that whoever commits an offense does so being endowed with one of three minds; thus, the statement beginning with 'one who commits an offense with a wholesome mind' was said. If someone were to say, 'The offense-basis is merely a designation,' would it not follow that in their view, the state of the offense-basis as unwholesome, etc., is indeed untenable, just as for dispute-issues and so on? No, because of the possibility of a contradiction with this statement: 'There is no wholesome offense-basis.' However, in the Anugaṇṭhipada, it is said: 'The term "offense-basis" is a designation for the unwholesome mind-moments and the aggregate of form that occur in such a way. Among the remaining wholesome, indeterminate, and designations, because of the statement, "an offense-basis could be unwholesome or indeterminate," its being a designation is precluded, as it is not included in the wholesome triad. By the very preclusion of the wholesome, because they have a similar nature, the preclusion of functional-indeterminate states should also be understood. Just as with functional-indeterminate states, because they follow suit, the preclusion of resultant-indeterminate states is also indeed made. Nevertheless, due to their general indeterminacy, it should be known that this is also a designation for resultant- and functional-indeterminate states along with the aggregate of form.' Therein, the statement 'a wholesome mind is a factor' was said in the Vinaya with reference to those who are unskilled, when there are cases such as the clearing of green grass. Therefore, since it is not possible to say, 'There is no wholesome offense-basis,' the meaning is that a wholesome mind is not a factor. If so, why is it said, 'three minds, three feelings'? To explain this, some begin with 'this is not...' and so on. The mind that originates an offense is called a mind sufficient to be a factor. Some say: 'The meaning of "exclusively" is "for the most part"; otherwise, it is contradicted. Why? Because it is said, "For whom, in the case involving mind, the mind is exclusively unwholesome".' What of that? There is no result. Why? Because it is exclusively unwholesome. Therefore, there is no discussion of it there. But showing where there is, he said, 'But as for what is a fault by designation...' and so on. For one who unintentionally and unknowingly... it is indeterminate. For instance, if a monk is lying down with a mind gone to a meditation subject, or is drowsing, and a woman prepares a bed, for that monk, even though a wholesome mind is present, it is not a factor for the offense. Therefore, at that moment, only the form that is occurring in the manner of lying down is called the offense-basis. Even when a life-continuum mind is present, this is the method. For at that moment, when the need to get up has arisen, from not getting up, only the aggregate of form is called an offense, not together with a result. But if one were to say this, for such a speaker, an offense would be incurred with a wholesome mind in the mindless cases. What is meant? For one who, having taken sheep's wool, transgresses three yojanas with attention on a meditation subject, and for one who, not knowing the designation, teaches the Dhamma word by word, the offense that should be incurred would be incurred with a wholesome mind. If one says, 'One does indeed commit it'? One does not commit it. Why? Because of the text, 'There is no wholesome offense-basis'.

Calito kāyo, pavattā vācā, aññatarameva aṅganti aññatarameva āpattīti attho. Kevalaṃ paññattiyā akusalādibhāvāsambhavato āpattitā na yujjati. Āpattiṃ āpajjanto tīsu aññatarasamaṅgī hutvā āpajjatīti dassanatthaṃ “yaṃ kusalacitto”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tassattho – pathavīkhaṇanādīsu kusalacittakkhaṇe vītikkamavasena pavattarūpasambhavato kusalacitto vā abyākatāpattiṃ āpajjati. Tathā abyākatacitto vā abyākatarūpasaṅkhātaṃ abyākatāpattiṃ āpajjati, pāṇātipātādīsu akusalacitto vā akusalāpattiṃ āpajjati, rūpaṃ panettha abbohārikaṃ. Supinapassanakālādīsu pāṇātipātādiṃ karonto sahaseyyādivasena āpajjitabbāpattiṃ āpajjanto akusalacitto [M 0.0520] abyākatāpattiṃ āpajjatīti veditabbo. Idaṃ vuccati āpattādhikaraṇaṃ akusalanti akusalacittuppādo. Porāṇagaṇṭhipadesu pana “puthujjano kalyāṇaputhujjano sekkho arahāti cattāro puggale dassetvā tesu arahato āpattādhikaraṇaṃ abyākatameva, tathā sekkhānaṃ, tathā kalyāṇaputhujjanassa asañcicca vītikkamakāle abyākatameva. Itarassa akusalampi hoti abyākatampi. Yasmā cassa sañcicca vītikkamakāle akusalameva hoti, tasmā vuttaṃ ‘natthi āpattādhikaraṇaṃ kusala’nti. Sabbattha abyākataṃ nāma tassa vipākābhāvamattaṃ sandhāya evaṃnāmakaṃ jāta”nti likhitaṃ, vicāretvā gahetabbaṃ.

The body is moved, speech is uttered, and one of these is a factor; this means that one of these is an offense. Since unwholesome states and so on cannot arise by mere designation, the status of being an offense is not justified. To show that one who incurs an offense does so while endowed with one of three states of mind, it is said, 'When one has a wholesome mind,' and so on. The meaning is this: during moments of wholesome consciousness in acts such as digging the earth, one with a wholesome mind incurs an indeterminate offense due to the arising of the corresponding physical action by way of transgression. Similarly, one with an indeterminate mind incurs an indeterminate offense, which is reckoned as indeterminate form. In cases like killing living beings, one with an unwholesome mind incurs an unwholesome offense. Here, however, form is not a matter for discussion. When one kills or commits similar acts in dreams or the like, incurring an offense that should be incurred in the manner of co-sleeping and so on, one with an unwholesome mind incurs an indeterminate offense—this should be understood. This is called the offense-issue as unwholesome—that is, the arising of an unwholesome state of mind. In the ancient glosses, however, it is written: after presenting the four types of individuals—the ordinary person, the virtuous ordinary person, the trainee, and the Arahant—it is stated that for the Arahant, the offense-issue is solely indeterminate; likewise for trainees; and likewise for the virtuous ordinary person when unintentionally transgressing, it is indeterminate. For the other person, it can be unwholesome or indeterminate. Because for this person, when transgressing intentionally, it is solely unwholesome, it is said, 'There is no wholesome offense-issue.' In all cases, what is called 'indeterminate' is so named in reference to the mere absence of its result. This should be considered and understood.

224. Vivādo vivādādhikaraṇanti yo koci vivādo, so sabbo kiṃ vivādādhikaraṇaṃ nāma hotīti ekapucchā. “Vivādo adhikaraṇanti vivādādhikaraṇameva vivādo ca adhikaraṇañcāti pucchati. Tadubhayaṃ vivādādhikaraṇamevāti pucchatīti vuttaṃ hotī”ti porāṇagaṇṭhipade vuttaṃ. Kesuci potthakesu ayaṃ pucchā natthi. Yadi evaṃ imāya na bhavitabbaṃ vivādo vivādādhikaraṇaṃ, vivādādhikaraṇaṃ vivādo, vivādādhikaraṇaṃ vivādo ceva adhikaraṇañcāti pañcapañhāhi bhavitabbaṃ siyā. Kesuci potthakesu tisso, kesuci catasso, pañca natthi. Tattha dve vibhattā. Itarāsu adhikaraṇaṃ vivādoti yaṃ kiñci adhikaraṇaṃ, vivādasaṅkhyameva [V 0.0475] gacchati, vivādo adhikaraṇanti yo koci vivādo, so sabbo adhikaraṇasaṅkhyaṃ gacchatīti pucchati. Esa nayo sabbattha.

224. Regarding 'A dispute is a dispute-issue': Is any given dispute called a dispute-issue? This is one question. In the ancient gloss, it is said: 'Regarding 'A dispute is an issue,' it asks if a dispute-issue is both a dispute and an issue. It is said that it asks if both together are simply a dispute-issue.' In some books, this question is not found. If so, this question should not be; rather, there should be five questions: Is a dispute a dispute-issue? Is a dispute-issue a dispute? Is a dispute-issue both a dispute and an issue? Is an issue a dispute? Is a dispute an issue? In some books, there are three questions; in some, four; there are not five. Therein, two are analyzed. Among the other questions, regarding 'An issue is a dispute,' it asks: Does any given issue come to be designated as a dispute? Regarding 'A dispute is an issue,' it asks: Does any given dispute come to be designated as an issue? This is the method in all cases.

228. Sammukhāvinayasminti sammukhāvinayabhāve.

228. In the presence-procedure, meaning in the state of being a presence-procedure.

230. “Antarenāti kāraṇenā”ti likhitaṃ.

230. It is written: '`Antarena` means by reason.'

233. Ubbāhikāya khiyyanake pācitti na vuttā tattha chandadānassa natthitāya.

233. A `pācitti` offense is not stated for disparagement by means of a formal act of the Sangha, because in that case there is no giving of consent.

236. Tassa kho etanti esoti attho “etadagga”nti ettha viya.

236. The meaning of the phrase `tassa kho etaṃ` should be understood as `eso`, as in the case of `etadagga`.

238. “Kā [M 0.0521] ca tassa pāpiyasikā”ti kira pāṭho.

238. The reading is said to be: 'And what is his procedure for the more serious offense?'

242. “Kiccameva kiccādhikaraṇa”nti vacanato apalokanakammādīnametaṃ adhivacanaṃ, taṃ vivādādhikaraṇādīni viya samathehi sametabbaṃ na hoti, kintu sammukhāvinayena sampajjatīti attho.

242. Because 'A duty itself is a duty-issue,' this is a designation for formal acts such as proclamation and so on. Unlike dispute-issues and the like, it is not to be settled by settlements, but rather is accomplished by the presence-procedure. This is the meaning.

Samathakkhandhakavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Chapter on Settlements is finished.

5. Khuddakavatthukkhandhakavaṇṇanā

5. The Commentary on the Chapter on Minor Matters

Khuddakavatthukathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Discourse on Minor Matters

244. Puthupāṇinā [M 0.0522] kattabbaṃ kammaṃ puthupāṇikaṃ.

244. An act to be done with the back of the hand is called `puthupāṇika`.

245. “Kaṇṇato nikkhantamuttolambakādīnaṃ kuṇḍalādīna”nti likhitaṃ. “Kāyūra”nti pāḷipāṭho. “Keyūrādīnī”ti ācariyenuddhaṭaṃ.

245. It is written: '...of earrings and the like, such as pearl pendants, that have come out from the ear.' The Pāḷi reading is `kāyūra`. `Keyūrādīni` is what is cited by the teacher.

248. “Sādhugītaṃ [V 0.0476] nāma parinibbutaṭṭhāne gīta”nti likhitaṃ. Dantagītaṃ gāyitukāmānaṃ vākkakaraṇīyaṃ. Dantagītassa vibhāvanatthaṃ “yaṃ gāyissāmā”tiādimāha.

248. It is written: 'What is called a song of praise is a song sung in the place where Parinibbāna was attained or in a matter connected with it.' A tooth-song is the preparation of the voice for those who wish to sing. In order to clarify 'tooth-song,' he said, 'What we shall sing,' and so on.

249. Caturassavattaṃ nāma catuppādagāthāvattaṃ. “Taraṅgavattādīni uccāraṇavidhānāni naṭṭhapayogānī”ti likhitaṃ. Bāhiralominti bhāvanapuṃsakaṃ, yathā tassa uṇṇapāvārassa bahiddhā lomāni dissanti, tathā dhārentassa dukkaṭanti vuttaṃ hoti.

249. What is called the square style is the style for reciting a four-line verse. It is written: 'The methods of recitation such as the wave style have fallen out of use.' The word 'bāhiralomi' is a neuter noun denoting a state. Just as the hairs on the outside of that woolen cloak are visible, so for the monk who wears it, there is an offense of wrong conduct; thus it is said.

251. Virūpakkhehītiādi sahayogakaraṇavacanaṃ. Sarabūti gehagoḷikā. Sā kira setā savisā hoti. Sohanti yassa me etehi mettaṃ, sohaṃ namo karomi bhagavatoti sambandho. Aññamhi…pe… chetabbamhīti rāgānusaye.

251. 'With the Virūpakkhas,' etc., is an instrumental case used in the sense of accompaniment. 'Sarabū' is a house lizard. It is said that if it is white, it is poisonous. In 'so'haṃ,' the connection is: 'I, who have loving-kindness for these Virūpakkhas, pay homage to the Blessed One.' In 'when another... should be cut,' it refers to the latent tendency of lust.

252. Uṭṭitvāti pakkhipitvā. Otaratūti iddhiyā otāretvā gaṇhātu. Anupariyāyīti anuparibbhami.

252. 'Having arisen' means 'having put in.' 'Let him descend' means 'having brought it down by psychic power, let him take it.' 'He went around' means 'he wandered about.'

253. Na acchupiyantīti na lagganti. Rūpakākiṇṇānīti itthirūpādīhi vokiṇṇāni.

253. 'They are not defiled' means 'they do not cling.' 'Filled with forms' means 'replete with forms of women and so on.'

254. Ālindakamiḍḍhikādīnanti pamukhamiḍḍhikādīnaṃ. Parivattetvā tatthevāti ettha “parivattetvā tatiyavāre tattheva miḍḍhiyā patiṭṭhātī”ti likhitaṃ. Paribhaṇḍaṃ nāma gehassa bahi kuṭṭapādassa thirabhāvatthaṃ katā tanukamiḍḍhikā [M 0.0523] vuccati. Ettha “parivaṭṭitvā patto bhijjatīti adhikaraṇabhedāsaṅkāya abhāve ṭhāne ṭhapetuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti likhitaṃ. Pattamāḷako vaṭṭitvā pattānaṃ apatanatthaṃ vaṭṭaṃ vā caturassaṃ vā iṭṭhakādīhi parikkhipitvā māḷakacchannena kato. “Pattamaṇḍalikā pattapacchikā tālapattādīhi katā”ti ca likhitaṃ. Miḍḍhante ādhārake ṭhapetuṃ vaṭṭati pattasandhāraṇatthaṃ vuttattā. Mañce ādhārakepi na vaṭṭati nisīdanapaccayā vāritattā. Āsannabhūmikattā olambetuṃ vaṭṭati.

254. Ālindakamiḍḍhikādīnaṃ means 'of principal ledges and so on.' In 'parivattetvā tattheva,' it is written: 'Having turned, on the third time, it stands on that very ledge.' What is called 'paribhaṇḍa' is said to be a small ledge made outside the monastery at the base of the wall for the sake of stability. Here, it is written: 'Lest the bowl break by being turned over, it is permissible to place it in a place where there is no fear of the support breaking.' A 'pattamāḷaka' is made by enclosing a round or square area with bricks and so on, with a roofed stand, to prevent the bowls from falling by rolling. And it is also written: 'A bowl-ring and a bowl-basket are made from palm leaves and so on.' It is permissible to place it on a support at the edge of the ledge, because it was said for the purpose of holding a bowl. It is not permissible to place it even with a support on a bed, because it is forbidden on account of being a requisite for sitting. Because it is a place for sitting, it is permissible to hang it down.

255. “Aṃsakūṭe laggetvāti vacanato aggahatthe laggetvā aṅke ṭhapetuṃ na vaṭṭatī”ti keci vadanti, na sundaraṃ, “na kevalaṃ yassa patto”tiādi yadi hatthena gahitapatte bhedasaññā, pageva aññena sarīrāvayavenāti katvā vuttaṃ. Pāḷiyaṃ pana pacuravohāravasena vuttaṃ. Ghaṭikapālamayaṃ ghaṭikaṭāhaṃ. Chavasīsassa pattanti “silāputtakassa sarīraṃ, khīrassa dhārātiādivohāravasena [V 0.0477] vuttaṃ. Mañce nisīdituṃ āgatoti attho. “Pisācillikāti pisācadārakā”tipi vadanti. Dinnakameva paṭiggahitameva. Cabbetvāti khāditvā. Aṭṭhikāni ca kaṇṭakāni ca aṭṭhikakaṇṭakāni. “Etesu sabbesu paṇṇattiṃ jānātu vā, mā vā, āpattiyevā”ti likhitaṃ.

255. Some say that because of the phrase 'having hung it on the shoulder-top', it is not permissible to hang it from the fingertips or to place it on the lap. This is not sound. Regarding 'not only whose bowl,' etc., it is said having considered that if there is a perception that a bowl held by the hand will break, what need is there to speak of holding it with another part of the body? In the Pāḷi, however, it is stated according to common usage. A ghaṭikaṭāha is a bowl made by a potter. The phrase 'the bowl of a corpse's head' is stated by way of conventional expressions such as 'the body of a stone doll' or 'a stream of milk.' The meaning is: 'He has come to sit on the bed.' Some also say: 'Pisācillikā means young pisācas.' What is given is indeed what is accepted. 'Cabbetvā' means 'having chewed.' Bones and fish bones are 'aṭṭhikakaṇṭakāni'. It is written: 'In all these cases, whether one knows the regulation or not, there is indeed an offense.'

256. Vipphāḷetvāti phāḷetvā. Kiṇṇena pūretunti surākiṇṇena pūretuṃ. Bidalakaṃ nāma diguṇakaraṇasaṅkhātassa kiriyāvisesassa adhivacanaṃ. Kassa diguṇakaraṇaṃ? Yena kilañjādinā mahantaṃ kathinamatthataṃ, tassa. Tañhi daṇḍakathinappamāṇena pariyante saṃharitvā diguṇaṃ kātabbaṃ. Aññathā khuddakacīvarassa anuvātaparibhaṇḍādividhānakaraṇe hatthassa okāso na hoti. Salākāya sati dvinnaṃ cīvarānaṃ aññataraṃ ñatvā sibbitāsibbitaṃ sukhaṃ paññāyati. Daṇḍakathine kate na bahūhi sahāyehi payojanaṃ. “Asaṃkuṭitvā cīvaraṃ samaṃ hoti. Koṇāpi samā hontī”ti likhitaṃ, “haliddisuttena saññākaraṇa”nti vuttattā haliddisuttena cīvaraṃ sibbetumpi vaṭṭatīti siddhaṃ. Tattha hi keci akappiyasaññino. Paṭiggaho nāma aṅgulikoso.

256. 'Vipphāḷetvā' means 'having split open.' 'Kiṇṇena pūretuṃ' means 'to fill with yeast.' 'Bidalaka' is a term for the specific action known as 'doubling.' Doubling of what? Of the large kaṭhina cloth that is spread out on a kilañja mat or the like. Indeed, that should be folded at the edge to the size of a daṇḍakathina and made double. Otherwise, there is no space for the hand when making arrangements such as the border strip and hem for a small robe. When there is a pin, having pierced one of the two robes, it is easily discerned whether it is sewn or unsewn. When the daṇḍakathina is made, there is no need for many companions. It is written: 'Without wrinkling, the robe becomes even, and the corners are also even.' Because it is said, 'making a mark with turmeric-dyed thread,' it is established that it is also proper to sew the robe with turmeric-dyed thread. Therein, some have the perception that it is improper. 'Paṭiggaha' is a finger-stall.

257-8. Pātīti [M 0.0524] paṭiggahasaṇṭhānaṃ. Paṭiggahatthavikanti aṅgulikosatthavikaṃ. Sūcisatthakānaṃ pubbe āvesanatthavikāya anuññātattā “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bhesajjatthavika”nti vuttaṃ. Ettha sūcisatthakādīnipi ṭhapetabbānīti nidānaṃ sūceti. Sacepi upanando bhikkhu alajjī, tathāpi santakametaṃ amūlacchedakatabhikkhuno lajjinopi samānassa kappatīti yujjati. Na sammatīti na pahoti.

Pāti means a bowl shaped like a thimble. Paṭiggahatthavikā means a bag for a thimble. Since a bowl-shaped basket for needles and knives was previously allowed, it is said: ‘Monks, I allow a medicine bag.’ The introduction indicates that needles, knives, and the like should also be kept in this. Even if the monk Upananda is shameless, nevertheless this possession is allowable even for a conscientious monk who has not committed a root-cutting offense; thus it is suitable. Na sammati means it is not sufficient.

260-1. Bahi kuṭṭassa samantato nīcavatthukaṃ katvā ṭhitaṃ “maṇḍalika”nti vuccati. Jantāgharappaṭicchādinā channassa naggiyaṃ yassa na paññāyati, tasseva parikammaṃ kātabbaṃ. Esa nayo udakavatthapaṭicchādīsupi.

A thing established with a low base all around the outside of a wall is called a ‘maṇḍalika’. For one who is covered by a covering for a steam-bath house, whose nakedness is not apparent, for him only should the rubbing of the body be done. This is the same method in cases of being covered by water, by a cloth, and so on.

262-3. Paṇiyā nāma paṇiyakārakā. Ākaḍḍhanayantaṃ ākaḍḍhiyamānaṃ kūpassa uparibhāge paribbhamati. Arahaṭaghaṭiyantaṃ sakaṭacakkasaṇṭhānayantaṃ. Tassa are are ghaṭikāni bandhitvā ekena, dvīhi vā paribbhamiyamānassa udakanibbāhanaṃ veditabbaṃ. Āviddhapakkhapāsaṃ nāma yattha maṇḍalākārena pakkhapāsā bajjhanti āviddhavatthatā viya āviddhapakkhapāsakā. Pubbe pattasaṅgopanatthaṃ, idāni ṭhapetabbaṃ bhuñjituṃ ādhārako anuññāto.

Paṇiyā means vendors of vegetables. A pulling-machine revolves in the upper part of a well when it is being pulled. An arahaṭaghaṭiyanta is a machine shaped like a cart-wheel; the drawing out of water should be understood as it is made to revolve by one or two, having tied pots to its spokes. Āviddhapakkhapāsa is where side-fastenings are tied in a circular manner, like an unpierced object; these are called āviddhapakkhapāsakā. Previously, this was for protecting the bowl; now a stand is allowed for placing the bowl on in order to eat.

273. Paragalaṃ [V 0.0478] gacchatīti imassa payogābhāvā vaṭṭati. Kammasatenāti mahatā ussāhena.

273. Paragalaṃ gacchati: This is allowable because of his absence of effort. Kammasatena means with great effort.

277-8. Lohabhaṇḍaṃ nāma kaṃsato sesalohabhaṇḍaṃ. Muddikakāyabandhanaṃ nāma caturassaṃ akatvā sajjitaṃ. Pāmaṅgadasā caturassā. Mudiṅgasaṇṭhānenāti saṅghāṭiyā mudiṅgasibbanākārena varakasīsākārena. Pavanantoti pāsanto. “Dasāmūla”nti ca likhitaṃ. Akāyabandhanena sañcicca vā asañcicca vā gāmappavesane āpatti. “Saritaṭṭhānato bandhitvā pavisitabbaṃ, nivattitabbaṃ vā”ti likhitaṃ.

Lohabhaṇḍa means metalware other than bronze. Muddikakāyabandhana means a waistband that is prepared without being made square. A pāmaṅgadasā is square. Mudiṅgasaṇṭhānena, on the outer robe, means in the manner of sewing a mudiṅga drum, or in the shape of a millet head. Pavananto means the end of the loop. And it is written: ‘dasāmūla’. Upon entering a village without a waistband, whether intentionally or unintentionally, there is an offense. It is written: ‘From the place where one remembers, one should tie it and enter, or one should turn back.’

279. Sattaṅgulaṃ vā aṭṭhaṅgulaṃ vāti ettha “sugataṅgulenā”ti avuttattā pakatiaṅgulena sāruppatthāya vaḍḍhetvāpi karonti ce, na doso.

279. Seven or eight finger-breadths—here, since 'Sugata finger-breadth' is not mentioned, if they make it by increasing it with a normal finger-breadth for the sake of suitability, there is no fault.

280. Tālavaṇṭākārena sīhaḷitthīnaṃ viya.

280. In the shape of a palm-leaf fan, like the manner of dress of Sinhalese women.

Khuddakavatthukkhandhakavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Chapter on Minor Matters is concluded.

6. Senāsanakkhandhakavaṇṇanā

6. The Explanation of the Chapter on Lodgings

Vihārānujānanakathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourse on the Permission for Dwellings

294. Nilīyanti [M 0.0525] bhikkhū etthāti vihārādayo leṇāni nāma. Āgata-vacanena tassāgatasaṅghova sāmī, na anāgatoti keci, taṃ na yujjati samānalābhakatikāya siddhattā.

294. Because bhikkhus hide (nilīyanti) or dwell here (ettha), dwellings and so on are called ‘shelters’ (leṇāni). Some say that by the word ‘arrived’ (āgata), only the Sangha that has arrived is the owner, not the one that has not arrived. That is not appropriate, because it is established by the agreement of equal gain.

296-7. Dīpinaṅguṭṭhenāti ettha “dīpinā akappiyacammaṃ dassetī”ti likhitaṃ. Thambhakavātapānaṃ nāma tiriyaṃ dārūni adatvā ujukaṃ ṭhiteheva dārūhi kattabbaṃ. Bhisīnaṃ anuññātaṃ vaṭṭatīti bimbohane vaṭṭatīti attho. Tūlapūritaṃ bhisiṃ apassayituṃ na vaṭṭati uṇṇādīnaṃyeva [V 0.0479] anuññātattā. Nisīdananipajjanaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ, tasmā apassayituṃ vaṭṭatīti ce? Akappiyanti na vaṭṭatīti keci. Yadi evaṃ akappiyamañcañca apassayituṃ na vaṭṭeyya. Yasmā vaṭṭati, tasmā doso natthi. Apica gilānassa bimbohanaṃ nipajjitumpi anuññātaṃ, tasmā bhisipi vaṭṭati apassayituṃ. Ācariyā ca anujānanti, vaḷañjenti cāti eke. Simbalitūlasuttena sibbitaṃ cīvaraṃ vaṭṭati. Kasmā? Kappāsassa anulomato. “Akkaphalasuttamayampi akkavākamayameva paṭikkhitta”nti te eva vadanti.

296-7. Regarding `dīpināṅguṭṭhena`, it is written: 'By `dīpinā`, an unallowable hide is indicated.' A 'pillar-window' (`thambhakavātapāna`) is one that should be made with upright wooden beams, without placing wooden beams horizontally. The meaning of `bhisīnaṃ anuññātaṃ vaṭṭati` (it is allowed for bolsters) is that it is allowed for a pillow (`bimbohana`). It is not allowed to lean on a bolster (`bhisi`) stuffed with cotton, because only wool and the like are permitted. This was said with reference to sitting and lying down. Therefore, if one were to say, 'It is allowed to lean on it'? Some say it is not allowed, as it is an unallowable item. If so, it would not be allowed to lean on an unallowable bed either. Since that is allowed, there is no fault. Moreover, for a sick person, a pillow is permitted even for lying down; therefore, it is also allowed to lean on a bolster. Some say that the teachers permit it and also use it. A robe sewn with thread from the silk-cotton tree is allowed. Why? Because it is in accordance with cotton. Those same ones say: 'That made of thread from the Akka fruit is also allowed; only that made from Akka bark is rejected.'

298. Anibandhanīyo alaggo. Paṭibāhetvāti maṭṭhaṃ katvā. “Setavaṇṇādīnaṃ yathāsaṅkhyaṃ ikkāsādayo bandhanatthaṃ vuttā”ti likhitaṃ.

298. `Anibandhanīyo` means unfettered; `alaggo` means unattached. `Paṭibāhetvā` means having made smooth. It is written: 'For white colors and the like, lac and so on are mentioned for the purpose of binding, in corresponding order.'

300. Pakuṭṭaṃ samantato āviddhapamukhaṃ.

300. `Pakuṭṭaṃ` means having an opening pierced from all around.

303. Sudhālepoti sudhāmattikālepo.

303. `Sudhālepo` means a plaster of lime and clay.

305. Āsatti taṇhā. Santiṃ adaraṃ.

305. `Āsatti` means `taṇhā` (craving). `Santiṃ` means `adaraṃ` (respect).

307. Ketunti kayena gahetuṃ.

307. `Ketuṃ` means to take by buying.

308. Citāti iṭṭhakāyo kabaḷena niddhamanavasena chinditvā katāti attho.

308. `Citā` means that bricks are made by cutting and removing them in lumps.

310. Chabbaggiyānaṃ [M 0.0526] bhikkhūnaṃ antevāsikāti ettha vīsativassaṃ atikkamitvā chabbaggiyā uppannā. “Ārādhayiṃsu me bhikkhū citta”nti (ma. ni. 1.225) vuttattā aññasmiṃ kāle sāvatthigamane uppannaṃ vatthuṃ idha āpattidassanatthaṃ āharitvā vuttanti yuttaṃ viya, vicāretvā gahetabbaṃ. Vuddhanti vuddhataraṃ.

310. Regarding 'the disciples of the group-of-six bhikkhus,' herein the group-of-six arose after twenty years had passed. Because it is said, 'The bhikkhus pleased my mind' (MN 1.225), it seems appropriate that an incident that occurred at another time during a journey to Sāvatthī has been brought here and stated for the purpose of showing the offense; this should be investigated and understood. Regarding `vuddha`, it means a more senior elder.

313. Santhareti tiṇasantharādayo.

313. `Santharati`: [This refers to] spreading grass mats and so forth.

Senāsanaggāhakathāvaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Discourse on the Taker of Lodgings

318. “Seyyaggenāti mañcaṭṭhānaparicchedena. Vihāraggenāti ovarakaggenā”ti likhitaṃ. Thāvarāti [V 0.0480] niyatā. Paccayeneva hi tanti tasmiṃ senāsane mahātherā tassa paccayassa kāraṇā aññattha agantvā vasantāyeva naṃ paṭijaggissantīti attho. Aghaṭṭanakammaṃ dassetuṃ “na tattha manussā”tiādimāha. “Vitakkaṃ chinditvā suddhacittena gamanavatteneva gantabba”nti pāṭho. Muddavedikā nāma cetiyassa hammiyavedikā. Paṭikkammāti apasakkitvā. Samānalābhakatikā mūlāvāse sati siyā, mūlāvāsavināsena katikāpi vinassati. Samānalābha-vacanaṃ sati dvīsu, bahūsu vā yujjati, teneva ekasmiṃ avasiṭṭheti no mati. Tāvakālikaṃ kālena mūlacchedanavasena vā aññesaṃ vā kammaṃ aññassa siyā nāvāyaṃ saṅgamoti ācariyo. Puggalavaseneva kātabbanti apalokanakāle saṅgho vassaṃvutthabhikkhūnaṃ pāṭekkaṃ “ettakaṃ vassāvāsikaṃ vatthaṃ deti, ruccati saṅghassā”ti puggalameva parāmasitvā dātabbaṃ, na saṅghavasena kātabbaṃ. Na saṅgho saṅghassa ettakaṃ detīti. “Ekasmiṃ āvāse saṅghassa kammaṃ karotī’ti vacanato saṅghavasena kātabba”nti likhitaṃ. Na hi tathā vutte saṅghassa kiñci kammaṃ kataṃ nāma hoti. “Sammatasenāsanaggāhāpakato aññena gāhitepi gāho ruhati aggahitupajjhāyassa upasampadā viyā”ti likhitaṃ. “Kammavācāyapi sammuti vaṭṭatī”ti likhitaṃ.

318. It is written: 'By `seyyagga` is meant by the demarcation of the bed's location. By `vihāragga` is meant by the order of the inner chamber.' `Thāvarā` means fixed. Indeed, the meaning is that the great elder monks, because of that very requisite, will attend to that lodging, dwelling there without going elsewhere. To show an undisturbed act, he said, 'No people are there,' and so on. There is a reading: 'Having cut off thought, one should go with a pure mind by the very practice of going.' What is called `muddavedikā` is the railing of the stupa's platform. `Paṭikkamma` means having withdrawn. The agreement of equal gain would exist if the original residence remains; with the destruction of the original residence, the agreement also perishes. The statement of equal gain is fitting when there are two or many; for that very reason, it is our opinion that it does not apply when only one remains. The teacher says: What is temporary may, in time, either by way of uprooting or through the work of others, become another's, like a meeting on a boat. It should be done on the basis of the individual: at the time of the announcement, having considered only the individual, it should be given to each monk who has completed the rains-residence, stating: 'This much rains-residence cloth is given; it is agreeable to the Sangha.' It should not be done on the basis of the Sangha. The Sangha does not give this much to the Sangha. It is written: 'Because of the statement, "He performs an act of the Sangha in one residence," it should be done on the basis of the Sangha.' For indeed, if it were so stated, no act would be called an act of the Sangha.
