It is written: 'Due to the absence of an appointed lodging-assigner, even when taken by another, the taking is valid, like the ordination of one whose preceptor has not been accepted.' It is written: 'Even by a formal act, an appointment is valid.'

Aṭṭhapi soḷasapi janeti ettha kiṃ visuṃ visuṃ, udāhu ekatoti? Ekatopi vaṭṭati. Na hi te tathā sammatā saṅghena kammakatā nāma honti[M 0.0527], teneva sattasatikakkhandhake ekato aṭṭha janā sammatāti. Tesaṃ sammuti kammavācāyapīti ñattidutiyakammavācāyapi. Apalokanakammassa vatthūhi sā eva kammavācā labbhamānā labbhati, tassā ca vatthūhi apalokanakammameva labbhamānaṃ labbhati, na aññanti veditabbaṃ. Imaṃ nayaṃ micchā gaṇhanto “apalokanakammaṃ ñattidutiyakammaṃ kātuṃ, ñattidutiyakammañca apalokanakammaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti gaṇhāti, evañca sati kammasaṅkaradoso āpajjati. Maggo pokkharaṇīti ettha maggo nāma magge katadīghasālā, pokkharaṇīti nahāyituṃ katapokkharaṇī. Etāni hi asenāsanānīti ettha bhattasālā na āgatā, tasmā taṃ senāsananti ce? Sāpi ettheva paviṭṭhā vāsatthāya akatattā. Bhojanasālā pana ubhayattha nāgatā. Kiñcāpi nāgatā, upari “bhojanasālā pana senāsanamevā”ti (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 318) vuttattā senāsanaṃ. “Kappiyakuṭi ca ettha kātabbā”ti vadanti, taṃ neti eke. Rukkhamūlaveḷugumbā channā kavāṭabaddhāva senāsanaṃ. “Alābhakesu āvāsesūti alābhakesu senāsanesū”ti likhitaṃ, taṃ yuttaṃ. Na hi pāṭekkaṃ senāsanaṃ hoti. Taṃ saññāpetvāti ettha paññattiṃ agacchante balakkārenapi vaṭṭati. Ayampīti paccayopi.

Here, regarding 'it generates eight or sixteen,' is it separately or together? It is permissible even together. For indeed, they, having been authorized in that way, are not called 'those for whom an act has been done by the Sangha'; for that very reason, in the Sattasatikakkhandhaka it is said, 'eight persons are authorized together.' 'Their authorization is also by a formal act' means it is also by a formal act consisting of a motion and one announcement. It should be understood that for an act of seeking approval, that very formal act is obtained by its subject matters; and for that formal act, only an act of seeking approval is obtained by its subject matters, not another. One who wrongly grasps this principle thinks, 'It is permissible to perform an act of seeking approval as a formal act consisting of a motion and one announcement, and to perform a formal act consisting of a motion and one announcement as an act of seeking approval.' This being so, the fault of confusion of acts arises. Here, in 'path, lotus pond,' 'path' means a long hall built on the path, and 'lotus pond' means a pond made for bathing. Here, in 'These are indeed not resting places,' the kitchen hall is not included. If one were to ask, 'Therefore, is it a resting place?'—it too is included right here, because it was not made for the purpose of dwelling. The dining hall, however, is not included in either. Although it is not included, it is a resting place because it is stated above, 'But the dining hall is indeed a resting place.' Some say, 'And a suitable hut should be made here,' but others say this is not so. The foot of a tree or a bamboo thicket, when covered and fitted with a door, is a resting place. It is written, '“In residences where there are no gains” means “in resting places where there are no gains”'; that is correct. For an individual component is not a resting place. Here, in 'having informed them,' it is permissible to compel, even by force, those who do not go to the designated place. 'This also' means also the forfeited requisites.

Upanibandhitvāti [V 0.0481] tassa samīpe rukkhamūlādīsu vasitvā tattha vattaṃ katvāti adhippāyo. Pariyattipaṭipattipaṭivedhavasena tividhampi. “Dasakathāvatthukaṃ dasaasubhaṃ dasaanussati”nti pāṭho. “Paṭhamabhāgaṃ muñcitvāti idaṃ ce paṭhamagāhitavatthuto mahagghaṃ hotī”ti likhitaṃ. Chinnavassānaṃ vassāvāsikaṃ nāma pubbe gahitavassāvāsikānaṃ pacchā chinnavassānaṃ. Bhatiniviṭṭhanti bhatiṃ katvā viya niviṭṭhaṃ pariyiṭṭhaṃ. “Saṅghikaṃ pana…pe… vibbhantopi labhatevā”ti idaṃ tatruppādaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Iminā apalokanameva pamāṇaṃ, na gāhāpananti keci. Vinayadharā pana “amhākaṃ vihāre vassaṃ upagatānaṃ ekekassa ticīvaraṃ saṅgho dassatī’tiādinā apalokitepi abhājitaṃ vibbhantako na labhati. ‘Apalokanakammaṃ katvā gāhita’nti vuttattā, ‘abhājite vibbhamatī’ti evaṃ pubbe vuttattā cā”ti vadanti. “Paccayavasenāti gahapatikaṃ vā aññaṃ vā vassāvāsikaṃ paccayavasena gāhita”nti likhitaṃ. “Ekameva vatthaṃ dātabbanti tattha nisinnānaṃ ekamekaṃ [M 0.0528] vatthaṃ pāpuṇātī”ti likhitaṃ. Dutiyo therāsaneti anubhāgo. Paṭhamabhāgo aññathā therena gahitoti jānitabbaṃ.

Upanibandhitvāti means: having stayed near that monastery at the foot of a tree or such places, and having performed duties there—this is the meaning. It is threefold by way of learning (pariyatti), practice (paṭipatti), and realization (paṭivedha). The reading is: 'The ten topics of discussion, the ten meditations on foulness, the ten recollections.' It is written: 'Regarding "having abandoned the first portion," if this is more valuable than the object first taken.' For those who have broken the Rains-residence, the vassāvāsika (rains-residence robe) is for those who, having previously received a rains-residence robe, later broke their Rains-residence. Bhatiniviṭṭhaṃ means: as if having made a payment, it was sought for, thoroughly searched for. This, 'However, what belongs to the Saṅgha… even one who has disrobed still obtains it,' is said with reference to its arising there. By this, some say that announcement alone is the measure, not the causing to be taken. But the Vinaya experts say: 'Even if an announcement is made with phrases like, "In our monastery, the Saṅgha will give the three robes to each of those who have entered the Rains-residence," one who has disrobed does not receive it while it is still undivided. This is because it is said, "Having performed the act of announcement, it is caused to be taken," and because it was previously stated, "One disrobes while it is undivided."' It is written: 'Paccayavasena (by means of a requisite)' means 'a robe from a householder or another rains-residence robe is received by means of a requisite.' It is written: 'Ekameva vatthaṃ dātabbaṃ (only one cloth should be given)' means 'there, to each one seated, one cloth is obtained.' Dutiyo therāsane (the second in the elder's seat) is a portion. It should be understood that the first portion was taken differently by the elder.

Upanandavatthukathāvaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Story of Upananda

320. Tivassantarenāti tiṇṇaṃ vassānaṃ anto ṭhitena. Hatthimhi nakho assāti hatthinakho. Pāsādassa nakho nāma heṭṭhimaparicchedo. Gihivikaṭanīhārenāti gihīhi katanīhāreneva. “Tehi attharitvā dinnāneva nisīdituṃ labbhanti, na bhikkhunā sayaṃ attharitvā vissajjitabbaṃ saṅghena attharāpetvā vā”ti likhitaṃ.

320. Tivassantarena (within three years) means: by one who has stayed within three years. Hatthinakho (elephant-nail) is so called because it has a nakha (projection) like an elephant's. The nakha of a mansion is the lower boundary. Gihivikaṭanīhārena (in the manner of what is fashioned by householders) means: precisely in the manner of what is made by householders. It is written: "They are allowed for sitting on only when they have been spread and given by them (householders); if it is spread by a bhikkhu himself, or caused to be spread by the Saṅgha, it must be relinquished."

Avissajjiyavatthukathāvaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Story of Non-Relinquishable Items

321. “Na vissajjetabbaṃ saṅghena vā gaṇena vā puggalena vā”ti vacanaṃ “yaṃ agarubhaṇḍaṃ vissajjiyaṃ vebhaṅgiyaṃ saṅghikaṃ, taṃ gaṇo ce tasmiṃ āvāse vasati puggalopi vā, gaṇena vā puggalena vā vissajjitaṃ saṅghena vissajjitasadisameva hotī”ti aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttavacanaṃ sādheti, aññathā ettha gaṇapuggalaggahaṇaṃ niratthakaṃ. Arañjaro udakacāṭi, alañjalo, bahuudakagaṇhanakoti attho. “Vaṭṭacāṭi viya hutvā thokaṃ dīghamukho majjhe paricchedaṃ dassetvā kato”ti likhitaṃ. Maṃsadibbadhammabuddhasamantacakkhuvasena pañca.

321. The statement, 'It should not be relinquished by the Saṅgha, or by a group, or by an individual,' establishes the statement spoken in the commentary: 'Whatever property is light, relinquishable, divisible, and communal—if a group or an individual resides in that monastery, then what is relinquished by the group or by the individual is just like being relinquished by the Saṅgha.' Otherwise, the inclusion of 'group' and 'individual' here would be meaningless. Arañjaro is a water pot; alañjalo means capable of holding much water. It is written: 'It is made like a round pot, with a slightly long mouth, showing a division in the middle.' By way of the fleshly eye, the divine eye, the Dhamma-eye, the Buddha-eye, and the all-seeing eye, there are five.

Garubhaṇḍena ca garubhaṇḍanti saṃhārimaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Pattacīvaraṃ nikkhipitunti aṭṭakacchannena [V 0.0482] kate mañce. Vaṭṭalohaṃ nāma pītavaṇṇaṃ. Pārihāriyaṃ na vaṭṭatīti āgantukassa adatvā paricārikahatthato attano nāmaṃ likhāpetvā gahetvā yathāsukhaṃ pariharituṃ na vaṭṭati. “Gihivikaṭanīhārenevāti yāva attano kammanibbatti, tāva gahetvā detī”ti likhitaṃ. Sikharaṃ nāma yena paribbhamantā chindanti. Pattabandhako nāma pattassa gaṇṭhiādikārako. “Paṭimānaṃ suvaṇṇādipattakārako”tipi vadanti. “Aḍḍhabāhūti kapparato paṭṭhāya yāva aṃsakūṭa”nti likhitaṃ. Ito paṭṭhāyāti imaṃ pāḷiṃ ādiṃ katvā. Daṇḍamuggaro nāma yena rajitacīvaraṃ pothenti. ‘Paccattharaṇagatika’nti vuttattā, “tampi garubhaṇḍamevāti vuttattā ca api-saddena pāvārādipaccattharaṇaṃ sabbaṃ garubhaṇḍamevā”ti vadanti. Eteneva [M 0.0529] suttena aññathā atthaṃ vatvā “pāvārādipaccattharaṇaṃ na garubhaṇḍaṃ, bhājanīyameva, senāsanatthāya dinnapaccattharaṇameva garubhaṇḍa”nti vadanti, upaparikkhitabbaṃ. Gaṇṭhikāti cīvaragaṇṭhikā. Bhañcako nāma sarako.

By 'heavy goods' is meant movable property. 'Placing the bowl and robe' means on a bed made with a canopy. Vaṭṭaloha is a yellow-colored metal. The phrase 'It is not permissible to use' means: it is not permissible, without giving it to an incoming bhikkhu, to take it from the hand of an attendant, have one's own name inscribed on it, and use it as one pleases. It is written: 'As with a mat made by householders, it can be taken until one’s own work is completed, then given back.' A sikhara is that with which one pierces while rotating. A pattabandhaka is one who makes the knots, etc., for a bowl. They also say: 'One who makes bowls of fine color and so on by shaping them well.' It is written: 'Aḍḍhabāhu means from the elbow up to the tip of the shoulder.' 'Starting from here' means beginning with this Pāḷi text. A daṇḍamuggara is that with which one beats a dyed robe. Because it is said to be 'included among coverings,' and because it is said, 'that too is a heavy item,' they say that by the word api, all coverings, such as cloaks, are included as heavy items. However, interpreting this very text differently, others say: 'Coverings such as cloaks are not heavy items but are only distributable; only a covering given for the sake of a lodging is a heavy item.' This should be investigated. Gaṇṭhikā is a stick for beating robes. Bhañcaka is a cup.

Navakammadānakathāvaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Discourse on Giving for New Construction

323-4. Aggaḷabandhasūcidvārakaraṇamattenapi. “Kapotabhaṇḍikā nāma vaḷabhiyā upari ṭhapetabbavalayaṃ vā tiṇacchadanagehassa piṭṭhivaṃsassa heṭṭhā ṭhapetabbaṃ vā ubhayamassa gatā dārū”ti likhitaṃ. Kārantarāti tadā puna pavisaṭṭhaṃ pubbapayojitānānaṃ vacanapātasenāsanavāso. Na pana patisaṭṭhatoti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Sabbattha vinaṭṭhavāso na ca paṭisedhako hotīti daṭṭhabbo. Dvāravātapānādīni apaharitvā dātuṃ asakkuṇeyyato “paṭidātabbāniyevā”ti vuttaṃ. Gopānasiādayo dentassa vihāro palujjatīti “mūlaṃ vā dātabba”ntiādi vuttanti eke. “Nevāsikā pakatiyā anatthatāya bhūmiyā ṭhapenti ce, tesampi anāpattiyevā”ti likhitaṃ. “Dvāravātapānādayo aparikammakatāpi apaṭicchādetvā na apassayitabbā”ti likhitaṃ.

Even by the mere act of fastening a bolt and inserting the pin. It is written: 'Kapotabhaṇḍikā is the name for either a ring to be placed above a door-frame, or a ring to be placed below the ridge-pole of a grass-thatched monastery; it is wood that pertains to both of these for that monastery.' Regarding 'kārantara': at that time, it is a re-entering, a dwelling in a lodging subject to various designations not previously applied. It should be understood, however, that this is not a dwelling by way of being completely abandoned. It should be understood that everywhere, a ruined dwelling is not prohibited. Because one would be unable to give away the lodging without removing the doors, windows, and so on, it is said, 'They must indeed be returned.' Some say that because the monastery is ruined when a bhikkhu gives away the rafters and so on, it is said, 'the foundation should be given,' etc. It is written: 'If resident bhikkhus place things on ground that is naturally without a covering, for them too there is indeed no offense.' And it is written: 'Doors, windows, and so on, even if they are unfinished, should not be leaned against without being covered.'

Saṅghabhattādianujānanakathāvaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Discourse Concerning the Allowance of Meals for the Saṅgha and Other Such Topics

Uddesabhattakathāvaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Discourse on the Designated Meal

325. Yā bhattuddesaṭṭhānabhūtāya bhojanasālāya pakatiṭhitikā. Dinnaṃ panāti yathā so dāyako deti, taṃ dassento “saṅghato bhante”tiādimāha. Ekavaḷañjanti ekadvārena vaḷañjitabbaṃ[V 0.0483]. Ticīvaraparivāranti ettha “udakamattalābhī viya aññopi uddesabhattaṃ alabhitvā vatthādimanekappakāraṃ labhati ce, tasseva ta”nti likhitaṃ. “Uddesapatte dethā’ti vatvā gahetvā āgatabhāvena saṅghassa pariccattaṃ na hotiyeva tasseva hatthe gatattā, tasmā tehi vuttakkamena sabbehi bhājetvā bhuñjitabba”nti vuttaṃ. Paṭipāṭipattaṃ vā ṭhitikāya ṭhitapattaṃ vā. “Kūṭaṭṭhitikā nāma aggahetabbānampi gāhitattā”ti likhitaṃ, “paṇītabhattaṭṭhitikañca ajānitvā missetvā gāhitepi evameva paṭipajjitabba”nti [M 0.0530] ca likhitaṃ. Tañce theyyāya haranti pattahārakā, āṇāpakassa gīvā hoti. Atikkantampi ṭhitikaṃ ṭhapetvāti ettha “taṃdivasameva ce bhikkhā labbhati, aparadivasato paṭṭhāya na labbhati kirā”ti likhitaṃ. Pacchā “sabbo saṅgho paribhuñjatū”ti avuttepi bhājetvā paribhuñjitabbaṃ. “Ettake bhikkhū saṅghato uddisitvā dethā’ti avatvā ‘ettakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ bhattaṃ gaṇhathā’ti dinnaṃ saṅghikanimantanaṃ nāmā”ti likhitaṃ.

325. In the dining hall, which is the place for the designation of meals, there are the normal arrangements. Regarding `dinnaṃ pana` (given, however): showing the manner in which that donor gives, He said, `‘saṅghato bhante’` (from the Sangha, venerable sir), and so on. `Ekavaḷañjaṃ` means it is to be used through one door. Regarding `ticīvaraparivāraṃ` (accompanied by the three robes), here it is written: 'Just as one who receives only water, if another monk, not receiving the designated meal, receives various items such as cloth, it belongs to that very monk.' It is said: 'Having said, "Give the designated shares," and having taken them and come, it is not relinquished to the Sangha because it has gone into that very monk's hand. Therefore, it should be distributed by all of them according to the stated procedure and then consumed.' A bowl in order, or a bowl placed according to the arrangement. It is written: 'A deceitful arrangement is so-called because even what should not be taken is taken,' and it is also written: 'Even when, not knowing the arrangement for superior food, it is taken mixed, one should proceed in this very same way.' If the bowl-carriers take it with intent to steal, the one who gives the order is liable for a penalty. Regarding `atikkantampi ṭhitikaṃ ṭhapetvā` (even having set aside the arrangement that has passed), here it is written: 'If alms are received on that very day, it is said that from the next day onwards they are not received.' Afterwards, even if it is not said, 'Let the entire Sangha partake,' it should be distributed and partaken of. It is written: 'Without saying, "Having designated so many monks from the Sangha, give," a gift given by saying, "Take the meal for so many monks," is called an invitation to the Sangha.'

Nimantanabhattakathāvaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Discussion of the Invitation Meal

Paṭipāṭiyāti yathāladdhapaṭipāṭiyā. Vicchinditvāti bhattaṃ gaṇhathāti padaṃ avatvā. Ālopasaṅkhepenāti ayaṃ nayo nimantanāyameva, uddesabhatte pana ekassa pahonakappamāṇe eva ṭhitikā tiṭṭhati. “Ekavāranti yāva tasmiṃ āvāse vasanti bhikkhū, sabbeva labhantī”ti likhitaṃ.

Regarding `paṭipāṭiyā` (in order): in the order it was received. Regarding `vicchinditvā` (having divided): without saying the phrase, 'Take the meal,' having divided it into portions. This method applies only to an invitation; in a designated meal, however, the arrangement stands only for an amount sufficient for one person. Regarding `ekavāraṃ` (one turn), it is written: 'For as long as monks reside in that monastery, all of them receive.'

Salākabhattakathāvaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Discussion of the Ticket Meal

Na hi bahisīmāya saṅghalābhoti ettha “uddesabhattādīsu bahisīmāya ṭhitassapi ce upāsakā denti, gahetuṃ labhanti, attanopi pāpetvā gahaṇaṃ anuññātaṃ, tathā idha na vaṭṭatī”ti vuttaṃ. Na pāpuṇantīti uddisitvāpi. Vāragāmanti dūrattā vārena niggahena gantabbagāme. Phātikammamevāti atirekalābhā ca bhavanti. Sammukhībhūtassāti yebhuyyena ce bhikkhū bahisīmaṃ gatā, sammukhībhūtassa pāpetabbaṃ. Sabhāgattā hi ekena laddhaṃ sabbesaṃ pahoti, tasmimpi asati attano pāpetvā dātabbaṃ. “Laddhā vā aladdhā vā”ti vacanasiliṭṭhavasena vuttaṃ. Vihāre apāpitaṃ pana…pe… na vaṭṭatīti salākabhattaṃ vihāre uddisiyati. Tena pana dinnasalākena. Tassāti gahetvā gatassa. Salākā gahetabbāti yuttaṃ viya. Sabbapotthakesu “gāhetabbā”ti pāṭho, tasmā tenāti salākaggāhāpakenāti attho. “Corikāya [V 0.0484] gahitattā na pāpuṇātī”ti vacanato “kuṭisodhanaṃ vaṭṭatī”ti ca dīpavāsino vadanti kira. Ekaṃ mahātherassāti mahāthero vihārato yebhuyyena na gacchati, itare kadāci gacchati, tasmā sabhāgā ce, attano pāpetvā puna itaresaṃ diyyati. Vihāre therassa pattasalākabhattanti mahāthero ekakova vihāre ohīno, “avassaṃ sabbasalākā attano pāpetvā ṭhito”ti [M 0.0531] paṭissayaṃ gantvā āgantukabhikkhūnampi adassanato kukkuccaṃ akatvā bhuñjanti.

Herein, regarding 'For a gain for the Saṅgha does not occur outside the boundary': it is said, 'In the case of designated meals and so on, even for a monk standing outside the boundary, if lay devotees give, it is allowable to take. It is permitted to have it brought to oneself and receive it; in such a way, it is not allowable here.' 'They do not receive it' means even if it is designated. 'Vāragāma' refers to a village that must be gone to by turn or by compulsion due to its distance. 'Phātikamma only' means there are also excess gains. 'To one who is present' means if, for the most part, the monks have gone outside the boundary, it should be brought to the one who is present. Because of common ownership, what is received by one is sufficient for all. If that one is also not present, it should be brought to oneself and given. 'Whether received or not received' is said for the sake of a smooth expression. Regarding 'But if it is not brought to the monastery... it is not allowable': the ticket-meal is designated in the monastery. But by that monk who has been given the ticket. 'His' refers to the one who, having taken it, has gone. The statement 'The tickets should be taken' appears as if it were correct. In all the manuscripts, the reading is 'should be caused to be taken'; therefore, 'by him' means by the one who causes the ticket to be taken. Because of the statement 'Because it was taken by stealth, it does not reach him,' the residents of the island say, it is said, 'The announcing of a hut is allowable.' 'One for the great elder' means the great elder, for the most part, does not go from the monastery, while the others go sometimes. Therefore, if the fellow monks go, having had it brought to oneself, it is given again to the others. Regarding 'The ticket-meal that has come to the elder in the monastery': the great elder alone is left behind in the monastery. Thinking, 'He has surely remained, having had all the tickets brought to himself,' they go to the lodging and, not seeing any incoming monks either, they eat without remorse.

Pakkhikabhattakathāvaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Discussion of the Fortnightly Meal

Uposathadivase āpattidesanaṃ sandhāya “parisuddhasīlāna”nti āha. Lekhaṃ katvā nibaddhāpitaṃ. “Āgantukabhattampi gamikabhattampī”ti āgantukova hutvā gacchantaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Anāthagilānupaṭṭhākopi tena dinnaṃ bhuñjati ce, tassapi pāpetabbameva. Guḷapiṇḍaṃ tālapakkamattaṃ.

On the Uposatha day, with reference to the confession of an offense, He said, “of those with purified virtue.” Having been written, it was established. The phrase, “both the meal for a newcomer and the meal for one who is departing,” was said in reference to one who, having been a newcomer, is departing. If one who attends to the unprotected sick eats what is given by that person, it must be brought to him as well. A lump of molasses is the size of a ripe palm fruit.

Senāsanakkhandhakavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Chapter on Lodgings is concluded.

7. Saṅghabhedakakkhandhakavaṇṇanā

7. The Commentary on the Chapter on Schism in the Sangha

Chasakyapabbajjākathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Story of the Going Forth of the Six Sakyans

330. “Anupiyaṃ [M 0.0532] nāmā”ti ekavacanena dissati, sattamiyaṃ pana “anupiyāya”nti. “Kāḷudāyippabhutayo dasa dūtā”ti pāṭho. “Na heṭṭhāpāsādā na heṭṭhāpāsādaṃ vā”ti likhitaṃ.

330. “Anupiyaṃ nāma” appears in the singular, but in the locative case, “anupiyāya” appears. There is the reading: “Kāḷudāyi and others, ten messengers.” It is written: “He does not descend downwards from the palace, or he does not descend to the lower palace.”

332. Pubbe pubbakāle. “Rañño sato”ti ca “raññovasato”ti ca pāṭho.

332. `Pubbe` means in a former time. There is the reading “rañño sato” and also “raññova sato”.

333. Na [V 0.0485] lābhataṇhā idha kāmataṇhā, jhānassa nesā parihāni hetu. Buddhattasīlaṃ pana patthayanto jhānāpi naṭṭhoti. Nanu pattabhāvanā. Manomayanti jhānamanomayaṃ.

333. Here, it is not craving for gain, but craving for sensual pleasures. This is not the cause for the decline of jhāna. But it should be understood that because he desired the false practice of claiming Buddhahood, he was lost even from jhāna. When the question is asked, “Is the attained development not mind-made?” The answer is that jhāna is mind-made.

334. Satthāroti gaṇasatthāro.

334. `Satthāro` means teachers of a group.

339. Potthanikanti churikaṃ.

339. `Potthanikaṃ` means a dagger.

340. Manusseti purise.

340. `Manusse` means persons.

341. Ekarattādhikārena rakkhaṃ paccāsīsantā īdisāti dassanatthaṃ “pañcime”tiādi vuttaṃ. “Pubbe rakkhasseta”nti vuttattā mayhaṃ pana rakkhaṇe kiccaṃ natthīti dassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Parūpakkamena tathāgataṃ jīvitā voropeyyāti idaṃ āṇattiyā āgatattā evaṃ vuttaṃ.

341. In order to show that those who hope for protection by the authority of more than one night are of such a nature, the phrase “these five,” etc., was said. Because it was said previously, “You shall protect,” it was said in order to show, “But for me, there is no duty of protecting.” This phrase, “One might deprive the Tathāgata of life through the undertaking of another,” was said thus because it came by way of a command.

342. Mā āsadoti mā vadhakacittena upagaccha. Itoti imamhā jīvitamhā. “Yatoti yasmā, yatoti vā gatassā”ti likhitaṃ. “Paṭikuṭitoti apasakkitvā saṅkucito hutvā vā paṭisakkatī”ti likhitaṃ.

342. `Mā āsado` means do not approach with a murderous mind. `Ito` means from this life. It is written: “`Yato` means `yasmā` (because); or, `yato` means ‘for you who have gone from this very existence.’” It is written: “`Paṭikuṭito` means: having drawn back, or having become contracted, he retreats.”

343. Tikabhojananti tīhi bhuñjitabbabhojanaṃ. “Tikabhojanīya”ntipi pāṭho. Parikappato hi tiṇṇaṃ bhuñjituṃ anujānāmi, tato uddhaṃ gaṇabhojanameva hoti, tassāpi idameva vuttaṃ. Idha apubbaṃ natthi. “Akataviññattiladdhaṃ [M 0.0533] tiṇṇaṃ bhuñjantānaṃ kiñcāpi taṃ gaṇabhojanaṃ nāma na hoti, viññattivasena pana na vaṭṭatī”ti likhitaṃ. Tayo atthavase paṭiccāti etthāpi “mā pāpicchāpakkhaṃ nissāya saṅghaṃ bhindeyyu”nti pesalānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ phāsuvihārāyāti yojetabbaṃ. Kulānuddayatāya cāti kulānaṃ pasādarakkhaṇatthaṃ. Vajjanti vajjameva. “Vajjamimaṃ phuseyyā”ti likhitaṃ. “Vajjanīyaṃ puggalaṃ phuseyyā”ti vuttaṃ. “Imassa mano na phuseyyā”ti vattabbampi siyā. Cakkabhedanti sāsanabhedaṃ. Āyukappanti ettha kiñcāpi avīcimhi āyuparimāṇaṃ natthi, yena pana kammena yattakaṃ anubhavitabbaṃ, tassa āyukappanti veditabbaṃ.

343. A meal for three (tikabhojana) is food to be eaten by three. There is also the reading 'allowable for three' (tikabhojanīya). For, by arrangement, I allow three to eat; beyond that, it becomes a group meal, and for that also this very rule is stated. Here, there is nothing new. It is written: 'Although for three eating what is obtained without a formal request, it is not called a group meal, it is, however, not allowable by means of a formal request.' In regard to 'depending on three reasons' (tayo atthavase paṭicca)—here too, it should be connected thus: for the comfortable dwelling of virtuous bhikkhus, 'lest they, relying on the faction of evil desire, should split the Saṅgha.' And 'out of compassion for families' (kulānuddayatāya ca) means for the protection of the families' faith. 'Fault' (vajja) means a fault indeed. It is written: 'He might incur this fault.' It is said: 'He might come into contact with a person who should be avoided.' It could also be said: 'May it not affect his mind.' 'Breaking the wheel' (cakkabheda) means the schism of the Dispensation. 'Life-eon' (āyukappa)—here, although in Avīci there is no fixed life-span, whatever duration must be experienced for a certain kamma, that should be understood as the 'life-eon'.

345. “Aññataraṃ āsanaṃ gahetvā nisīdī”ti vacanato visabhāgaṭṭhānaṃ gatassa pesalassapi bhikkhuno tesaṃ āsane nisīdituṃ vaṭṭatīti siddhaṃ. Āgilāyatīti rujjati. Ādesanāpāṭihāriyānusāsaniyāti [V 0.0486] tassa tassa cittācāraṃ ādissa ādissa desanā, ādesanāpāṭihāriyānusāsanī. Iddhi eva pāṭihāriyaṃ iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ, iddhipāṭihāriyasaṃyuttāya anusāsaniyā ovadatīti attho. Nanu taṃ āvusoti ettha taṃ vacanaṃ nanu mayā vuttosīti attho.

345. From the statement 'Having taken a certain seat, he sat down,' it is established that it is allowable for even a virtuous bhikkhu who has gone to a place of those with a different disposition to sit on their seats. `Āgilāyati` means it aches. `Ādesanāpāṭihāriyānusāsanī` is the teaching given by repeatedly pointing out the mental conduct of each and every being. Psychic power (iddhi) itself is the miracle, the miracle of psychic power (iddhipāṭihāriya); the meaning is that he advises with the instruction connected with the miracle of psychic power. Regarding 'Friend, were you not told that?' (nanu taṃ āvuso), the meaning is: 'Friend, were you not told that word by me?'

346-9. Suvikkhālitanti sudhotaṃ. Saṃkhāditvāti suṭṭhu khāditvā. “Mahiṃ vikubbatoti mahāvisālo”ti likhitaṃ. Tassa bhisaṃ ghasamānassa. Tattha nadīsu jaggatoti pālentassa. “Kiṃ? Hatthiyūthaṃ gantu”nti vadanti. “Asaṃpāto’ti pāṭho, apatto hutvāti attho”ti likhitaṃ. “Apāyabahuttā puna dassito”ti vuttaṃ. “Evaṃsateti evaṃ assa te āsavā”ti likhitaṃ.

`Suvikkhālita` means well-washed. `Saṃkhāditvā` means having eaten well. It is written: '`Mahiṃ vikubbato` means very large.' Of him eating the lotus root. Regarding `tattha nadīsu jaggato`, it means 'of him guarding.' They say, 'What is the use of going to the elephant herd?' It is written: 'The reading is `asaṃpāto`, and the meaning is "not having attained".' It is said: 'It is shown again because of the abundance of the lower realms.' Regarding `evaṃsate`, it is written: `evaṃ assa te āsavā`, meaning 'thus for him are those taints'.

350. “Vosānaṃ pariniṭṭhānaṃ vā”ti ca likhitaṃ. Jātūti daḷhatthe nipāto. Mā udapajjathāti mā uppajjeyya. “So pamādamanuyuñjanto”ti pāṭho. Anādaraṃ kusalesu. Udadhi mahāti kittako mahā? Bhesmā yāva bhayānako, tāva mahāti vuttaṃ hoti.

350. It is also written: '`Vosāna` means the end or completion.' `Jātu` is a particle in the sense of strengthening. `Mā udapajjathā` means 'may it not arise.' The reading is '`So pamādamanuyuñjanto`.' `Anādara` means disrespect towards wholesome qualities. Regarding `udadhi mahā` (the great ocean): How great is it? It is said to be as great as it is frightening.

351. Na kho, upāli, bhikkhunī saṅghaṃ bhindatīti ettha bhikkhu saṅghaṃ na bhindati, bhikkhunī saṅghaṃ bhindatīti keci, netaṃ gahetabbaṃ. Kevalaṃ “saṅgho”ti [M 0.0534] vutte bhikkhusaṅghova adhippeto. “Saṅghassa deti, ubhatosaṅghassa deti cā”ti (mahāva. 379) mātikāvacanampi sādheti. Tasmiṃ adhammadiṭṭhibhede dhammadiṭṭhi siyā. “Sīlasatibhedesupi samāno dhammaṃ kātunti saṅghabhede vematikopi tādiso vā”ti likhitaṃ. Vinidhāyāti attano vañcanādhippāyataṃ chādetvā.

351. Regarding 'Indeed, Upāli, a bhikkhunī does not split the Saṅgha': here some say that a bhikkhu does not split the Saṅgha, but a bhikkhunī does split the Saṅgha. This should not be accepted. Simply, when 'Saṅgha' is said, only the Bhikkhu Saṅgha is intended. The wording of the matrix, 'He gives to the Saṅgha, and he gives to both Saṅghas,' also proves this. In that division by wrong view, there might be a right view. It is written: 'Also in divisions of virtue and mindfulness, one should act in accordance with the Dhamma; in a schism of the Saṅgha, one who is doubtful is also of such a nature.' `Vinidhāya` means having concealed one's own intention to deceive.

Saṅghabhedakakkhandhakavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Chapter on Schism is concluded.

8. Vattakkhandhakavaṇṇanā

8. Commentary on the Chapter on Observances

Āgantukavattakathāvaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Discussion of the Observance for Visitors

357. Ekasmiṃ [M 0.0535][V 0.0487] gāme aññavihārato āgatopi āgantukova. Tattha keci evaṃ vadanti “āvāsiko katthaci gantvā sace āgato, ‘tenāpi āgantukabhattaṃ bhuñjitabba’nti vuttattā dūrāgamanaṃ vuttaṃ hoti, na gāme, tasmā na yutta”nti. Te vattabbā “āgantukabhattaṃ nāma gahaṭṭhehi ṭhapitaṃ. Yasmiṃ nibaddhaṃ, tato aññagāmatoti āpannaṃ. Tathā vihārādhikārattā aññavihārato āgatopi āgantuko vā”ti ācariyānaṃ sanniṭṭhānaṃ. Pānīyaṃ pucchitabbaṃ, paribhojanīyaṃ pucchitabbanti uddharitvā ghaṭasarāvādigataṃ sandhāya paṭhamaṃ, dutiyaṃ kūpataḷākādigatanti ācariyo. Dutiyavāre attano vasanaṭṭhānattā visuṃ pucchitabbameva, tasmā vuttaṃ etaṃ “paricchinnabhikkho vā gāmo”ti. Bahūsu potthakesu duvidhāpi yujjati.

357. In the same village, even one who comes from another monastery is a visitor. On this point, some say: 'If a resident bhikkhu, having gone somewhere, returns, since it is said, "He too should eat the visitor's meal," coming from afar is meant, not coming within the village; therefore, it is not proper.' They should be told: 'The visitor's meal is that which is established by householders. Where it is regularly established, from another village is what is meant. Likewise, because it is a matter concerning the monastery, even one who comes from another monastery is a visitor.' This is the teachers' conclusion. The phrases 'Drinking water should be asked for' and 'Water for use should be asked for' should be extracted. The first refers to water in drinking pots, bowls, and so on; the second, says the teacher, refers to water in wells, ponds, and so on. On the second occasion, because it is one's own dwelling place, it should indeed be asked for separately; therefore, this was said: 'a village with a designated bhikkhu.' In many manuscripts, both ways are suitable.

Anumodanavattakathāvaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Discussion of the Observance of Thanksgiving

362-4. Pañcame anumodanatthāya nisinne. “Manussānaṃ parivisanaṭṭhānanti yattha manussā saputtadārā āvasitvā dentī”ti likhitaṃ. Imasmiṃ khandhake āgantukāvāsikagamikānumodanabhattaggapiṇḍacārikāraññakasenāsanajantāgharavaccakuṭiupajjhācariyasaddhivihārikantevāsikavattāni cuddasa mahāvattāni nāma. Aggahitaggahaṇena gaṇiyamānāni asīti khandhakavattāni nāma honti.

When the fifth bhikkhu is seated for the purpose of giving thanks. It is written: 'The place of serving for humans' means 'where people, together with their children and wives, dwell and give.' In this Chapter, the fourteen observances—for visitors, residents, travelers, giving thanks, the refectory, the alms-round, forest-dwelling, lodgings, the steam-bath house, the latrine, the preceptor, the teacher, the co-resident, and the pupil—are called the Great Observances. When counted without taking up what has already been taken up, they are eighty Chapter Observances.

Vattakkhandhakavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Chapter on Observances is concluded.

9. Pātimokkhaṭṭhapanakkhandhakavaṇṇanā

9. Commentary on the Chapter on the Suspension of the Pātimokkha

Pātimokkhuddesayācanakathāvaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Discussion of Requesting the Pātimokkha Recitation

383-4. “Nandimukhī”ti [V 0.0488][M 0.0536] likhitaṃ. Āyatakenevāti ādimhi eva. Yanti yasmā. Savantiyo mahānadiyo. “Mahantabhūtāna”nti pāṭho. Pattāti patvā. “Samūlikāya ṭhapeti akatāyā”ti ṭhapanakassa saññāmūlavasena vuttaṃ. Taṃ vatthuṃ avinicchinitvāva parisā vuṭṭhāti.

'Nandimukhī' is written. `Āyatakeneva` means 'just in the beginning.' For `yanti`, the meaning is `yasmā`. `Savantiyo mahānadiyo` means 'flowing great rivers.' There is the reading 'mahantabhūtāna.' For `pattā`, the meaning is `patvā` (having reached). The phrase `samūlikāya ṭhapeti akatāya` ('he suspends for a rooted transgression that is not done') is said with reference to the one who suspends, by way of it being rooted in his perception. Without having decided that matter, the assembly rises.

Attādānaaṅgakathāvaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Discussion of the Factor of Taking Oneself as an Authority

398-9. “Attādānanti sayaṃ parehi codito attānaṃ sodhetuṃ anādiyitvā paresaṃ vippaṭipattiṃ disvā sāsanaṃ sodhetuṃ attanā āditabba”nti likhitaṃ. Vassārattoti vassakālo. Sappaṭimāsoti ākaḍḍhanayuttoti adhippāyo.

398-9. It is written: 'Attādāna' means that when reproached by others, without undertaking to purify oneself, but seeing the misconduct of others, one should undertake to purify the Dispensation. 'Vassāratto' is the rainy season. 'Sappaṭimāso' means suitable for prolongation—this is the intended meaning.

401. Upadahātabboti uppādetabbo, vippaṭisāramukhena dhāretabboti adhippāyo.

401. 'Upadahātabbo' means it should be produced; the intended meaning is that it should be maintained with an expression of remorse.

Pātimokkhaṭṭhapanakkhandhakavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Chapter on the Suspension of the Pātimokkha is concluded.

10. Bhikkhunikkhandhakavaṇṇanā

10. 10. The Explanation of the Chapter on Bhikkhunīs

Mahāpajāpatigotamīvatthukathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Story of Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī

402-3. Sūnehīti [M 0.0537] sutehi. “Setaṭṭikā nāma rogajātī”ti pāḷi. “Setaṭṭhikā”ti aṭṭhakathā[V 0.0489]. “Paṭisambhidāpattakhīṇāsavaggahaṇena jhānānipi gahitāneva honti. Na hi nijjhānikānaṃ sabbappakārā sampatti ijjhatī”ti likhitaṃ.

402-3. 'Sūnehīti' means 'sutehi': with oozing blood. The Pāli is: 'A type of disease called Setaṭṭikā.' The commentary has: 'Setaṭṭhikā.' It is written: 'By the inclusion of the group of those who have attained the analytical knowledges and are taint-destroyed, the jhānas are also included. Indeed, for those who are without jhāna, no attainment of any kind is accomplished.'

Bhikkhunīupasampadānujānanakathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Account of Granting Permission for Bhikkhunī Ordination

404. Yadaggena yaṃ divasaṃ ādiṃ katvā. Tadevāti tasmiṃ eva divase. “Anuñattiyā”ti pāṭho. “Anupaññattiyā”ti na sundaraṃ.

404. 'Yadaggena' means: from which day, having made it the beginning. 'Tadevāti' means: on that very day. The reading is 'anuñattiyā'. The reading 'anupaññattiyā' is not good.

405. “Paṭiggaṇhāmi yāvajīvaṃ anatikkamanīyo”ti vatvā idāni kiṃ kāraṇā varaṃ yācatīti ce? Parūpavādavivajjanatthaṃ. Dubbuddhino hi keci vadeyyuṃ “mahāpajāpatiyā paṭhamaṃ sampaṭicchitattā ubhatosaṅghassa yathāvuḍḍhaabhivādanaṃ na jātaṃ. Gotamī ce varaṃ yāceyya, bhagavā anujāneyyā”ti.

405. If one should ask, 'Having said, "I accept for life that which is not to be transgressed," for what reason does she now request a boon?' It is for the purpose of avoiding the criticism of others. For some of weak understanding might say, 'Because Mahāpajāpatī was the first to accept, the salutation according to seniority between the two Saṅghas did not come to be. If Gotamī were to request a boon, the Blessed One would grant it.'

408. Vimānetvāti aparajjhitvā.

408. 'Vimānetvāti' means 'aparajjhitvā': having offended.

410-3. Kammappattāyopīti kammārahāpi. Āpattigāminiyopīti āpattiṃ āpannāyopi. Dve tisso bhikkhuniyoti dvīhi tīhi bhikkhunīhi. “Manosilikāyā”ti pāṭho.

410-3. 'Kammappattāyopīti' means 'kammārahāpi': even those deserving of a formal act. 'Āpattigāminiyopīti' means 'āpattiṃ āpannāyopi': even those who have committed an offense. 'Dve tisso bhikkhuniyo' means 'dvīhi tīhi bhikkhunīhi': with two or three bhikkhunīs. The reading is 'Manosilikāyā'.

420. “Tena ca bhikkhu nimantetabbo”ti sāmīcivasena vuttaṃ.

420. The statement, 'And a bhikkhu should be invited by her,' was said as a matter of propriety.

422-3. “Anujānāmi…pe… tāvakālika”nti puggalikaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ, na saṅghikanti ācariyo. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, utuniyā kaṭisuttaka”nti vacanato bhikkhussa vinibandhaṃ kaṭisuttakaṃ na vaṭṭati. Paggharantī visaviṇā. Vepurisikā massudāṭhī.

422-3. The statement, 'I allow... for a temporary period,' was said in reference to what is personal, not what is communal, says the Teacher. Because of the statement, 'I allow, monks, a waistband for a menstruating woman,' a tied waistband is not allowable for a bhikkhu. 'Paggharantī' means a woman with flowing blood. 'Vepurisikā' means a woman with a beard and canine teeth.

425. Tayo nissayeti rukkhamūlañhi sā na labhati.

425. Regarding 'the three dependencies,' she indeed does not obtain the root of a tree as a dwelling.

426. Bhattagge [M 0.0538] sace dāyakā bhikkhunisaṅghassa bhuttavato catupaccaye dātukāmā honti, yathāvuḍḍhameva.

426. In the refectory, if donors wish to give the four requisites to the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs after they have eaten, it should be done only according to seniority.

427. Vikāleti [V 0.0490] yāva vikāle honti, tāva pavāresunti attho. Ajjattanāti ajjatanā.

427. Regarding 'vikāle', the meaning is: for as long as it was the wrong time, for that long they invited. Regarding 'ajjattanā', it means 'ajjatanā' (until today).

428. Anuvādanti issariyaṭṭhānaṃ. Idaṃ sabbaṃ “ajjatagge ovaṭo bhikkhunīnaṃ bhikkhūsu vacanapatho”ti paññattassa garudhammassa vītikkamaāpattipaññāpanatthaṃ vuttanti veditabbaṃ, aññathā yesaṃ garudhammānaṃ paṭiggahaṇena bhikkhunīnaṃ upasampadā anuññātā, tesaṃ vītikkame anupasampannāva siyāti āsaṅkā bhaveyya.

428. Regarding 'anuvādanti', it refers to a position of authority. It should be understood that all this was said for the purpose of laying down the offense for transgressing the weighty rule that was established as: 'From today onward, the path of speech from bhikkhunīs to bhikkhus is closed.' Otherwise, the doubt could arise that, by transgressing those weighty rules through the acceptance of which ordination was allowed for bhikkhunīs, she would become unordained.

429. Itthiyuttenāti itthīhi gāvīādīhi dhuraṭṭhāne yuttena. Purisantarenāti purisena antarikena. “Purisadutiyenā”ti likhitaṃ, purisasārathināti adhippāyo. “Bāḷhataraṃ aphāsū”ti vacanato gilānāya vaṭṭaticceva siddhaṃ, bhagavantaṃ āpucchitvā anuññātaṭṭhāne upasampajjissāmīti adhippāyo.

429. Regarding 'itthiyuttena', it means yoked in the place of the yoke with women, cows, and so on. Regarding 'purisantarena', it means by a vehicle driven by a man. It is written 'purisadutiyena' (with a man as a companion); the intention is 'with a male charioteer.' Because of the statement, 'more severe discomfort,' it is thus established that it is allowable for one who is sick. The intention is: 'Having asked the Blessed One, I will receive ordination in a permitted case.'

430. Sā kenacideva antarāyenāti sabbantarāyasaṅgahanavacanaṃ, tasmā taṃ na antarāyaṃ kittetvā, vuttantarāyena “rājantarāyenā”ti sādhetabbanti ācariyo.

430. The statement, 'she, by some obstacle,' is a statement that comprehends all obstacles. Therefore, without enumerating that obstacle, the meaning should be established by the stated obstacle, 'an obstacle from the king,' says the Teacher.

431-2. “Navakammanti katvā ‘ettakāni vassāni vasatū’ti apaloketvā saṅghikabhūmidāna”nti likhitaṃ. “Sāgāra”nti vuttattā agārapaṭisaṃyuttarahonisajjasikkhādivajjitāti keci, yuttametaṃ. Kasmā? “Sahāgāraseyyamattaṃ ṭhapetvā”ti aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttattā. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, posetu”nti vacanato posanayuttakammaṃ sabbaṃ vaṭṭati mātuyā, na aññesaṃ. Vasituṃ ce na sakkoti dutiyaṃ vinā, sammannitvāva dātabbā tāya iti no mati. Kittakaṃ kālaṃ? Vasitvā ce dutiyā gantumicchati, aññaṃ sammannituṃ yuttāva. Sā vijātā labheti ācariyo.

431-2. It is written: 'Having done new work, and having requested, "May she dwell for this many years," it is a giving of Saṅgha land.' Because it is said 'with a dwelling,' some say that what is connected with a dwelling, such as the training rule on sitting in seclusion, is to be excluded; this is correct. Why? Because in the commentary it is said, 'having set aside the mere sharing of a dwelling.' Because of the statement, 'I allow, O bhikkhus, to support,' all actions connected with supporting are allowable for the mother bhikkhunī, not for others. If she is not able to dwell without a companion, a companion should be given to her only after having been appointed; this is our opinion. For how long? If the companion, after having dwelt, wishes to go, it is proper to appoint another. The teacher says: 'She who has given birth should receive one.'

434. “Idaṃ odissa anuññātaṃ vaṭṭatīti ekato vā ubhato vā avassave satipi vaṭṭatī”ti likhitaṃ. “Kesacchedādikaṃ kammaṃ anujānāmi sādituṃ [M 0.0539]”icceva vuttattā vuttaṃ “tadaññe sāditu”nti. “Kesacchedādikaṃ kammaṃ anujānāmi, bhikkhave”ti avatvā ettakaṃ yasmā “sāditu”nti bhāsitaṃ, tasmā sā vicikicchāya ubhatopi avassave api pārājikakhettena sā pārājikaṃ phusati. Iti aṭṭhakathāsvetaṃ sabbāsupi vinicchitaṃ. Odissakābhilāpo [V 0.0491] hi aññathā nibbisesato taṃ pamāṇaṃ. Yadi tathā bhikkhussa kappati vicikicchā.

434. It is written: 'Regarding the statement, "It is allowable, having been permitted with reference to this," it is allowable even if there is an outflow from one side or from both sides.' Because it was said only thus, 'I allow the act of cutting hair, etc., to be consented to,' it is said, 'to consent to other than that.' Because, without saying, 'I allow the act of cutting hair, etc., O bhikkhus,' only this much was spoken—'to consent'—therefore, that bhikkhunī, with doubt, even if there is an outflow from both sides, touches upon a Pārājika offense by way of the Pārājika-realm. Thus, this has been decided in all the commentaries. Indeed, a statement of specific designation is the standard; otherwise, it is without distinction. If it were so, doubt would be allowable for a bhikkhu.

Kālamodissa naṃ padaṃ, na sattodissakañhi taṃ;

Atha bhikkhuniyā eva, kālamodissa bhāsitaṃ.

That statement refers to a time, for it does not refer to a being. Then, for the bhikkhunī alone, it was spoken with reference to a time.

Evaṃ pārājikāpatti, sithilāva katā siyā;

Sabbaso pihitaṃ dvāraṃ, sabbapārājikasminti.

Thus, the Pārājika offense would be made lax. In every Pārājika, the door is completely closed.

Niratthakabhāvato, ubbhajāṇumaṇḍale;

Tasmā na sādiyantīti, nidānavacanakkamaṃ.

Because of its becoming meaningless in the case of what is above the knees, therefore, one should follow the sequence of the introductory words, 'they do not consent.'

Nissāya satthunā vuttaṃ, sāditunti na aññathā;

Attano paṇhisamphassaṃ, sādituṃ yena vāritaṃ.

It was said by the Teacher with reference to a specific case, 'to consent,' and not otherwise; by whom consenting to the touch of one's own heel was forbidden.

Api pārājikakkhette, kathaṃ dvāraṃ dadeyya so;

Tathāpi buddhaputtānaṃ, buddhabhāsitabhāsitaṃ.

In the realm of Pārājika, how indeed would he grant an opening? Nevertheless, for the sons of the Buddha, there is the teaching as it was spoken by the Buddha.

Vacanañca samānento, no cettha yuttikathā dhīrā;

Kesacchedādikammassa, avassaṃ karaṇīyato.

The wise, having well adduced the word, our statement in this matter should be a suitable one, also because the act of cutting hair and so forth must necessarily be done.

Cittassa cātilolattā, gaṇassa ca aṅgasampadā-

Bhāvā bhikkhunīnaṃ mahesinā, rakkhituñca asaṅkattā;

Nanu modissakaṃ katanti.

And because of the extreme fickleness of the mind, and because of the group's lack of completeness of factors, and because the Great Sage was without hesitation to protect the bhikkhunīs, was not a specific regulation made? Thus it should be known. The Explanation of the Discourse on Permitting the Higher Ordination for Bhikkhunīs is finished.

Bhikkhunikkhandhakavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Khandhaka on Bhikkhunīs is finished.

11. Pañcasatikakkhandhakavaṇṇanā

11. The Explanation of the Chapter on the Five Hundred

Saṅgītinidānakathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourse on the Origin of the Council

437. Chinnapātanti [V 0.0492][M 0.0540] bhāvanapuṃsakaṃ, tenākārena patantīti attho. Upaddutā ca mayaṃ homāti atītatthe vattamānavacanaṃ, ahumhāti attho. Atha vā tasmiṃ sati homa. “Pañca bhikkhusatānī”ti gaṇanavasena vatvā “vassaṃ vasantā”ti puggalaniddeso kato.

437. The term 'chinnapāta' is a neuter noun of state, meaning 'they fall in that broken manner'. The phrase 'upaddutā ca mayaṃ homa' is a present tense form used in a past sense, meaning 'we were oppressed'. Or alternatively, 'when he is present, we are oppressed'. Having stated 'five hundred bhikkhus' by way of enumeration, the designation of the individual is made with 'dwelling for the rains-retreat'. The Explanation of the Discourse on the Origin of the Council is finished.

Khuddānukhuddakakathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourse on the Minor and Lesser Matters

443. “Vassikasāṭikaṃ akkamitvā”ti vacanato bhagavato catutthacīvarampi atthīti siddhaṃ. Tenevāha cīvarakkhandhake “catutthaṃ cīvaraṃ pārupī”ti.

443. From the statement, 'having stepped on the rains-retreat cloth,' it is established that the Blessed One also had a fourth robe. For that very reason, it is said in the Chapter on Robes: 'he donned the fourth robe.'

444. “Apica yatheva mayā”tiādi saṅgītiyā aggahaṇādhippāyavasena vuttaṃ, kintu susaṅgītā āvuso therehi dhammo ca vinayo ca. Apicāhaṃ nāma tathevāhaṃ dhāressāmīti yatheva mayā bhagavato sammukhā sutaṃ sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ, tatheva therehi bhagavatā sayameva etadaggaṃ āropitehi, tasmā susaṅgahitā saṅgītīti vuttaṃ hoti.

444. The phrase beginning 'Moreover, just as by me...' was spoken with the intention of not accepting it at the council. However, friends, the Dhamma and the Vinaya were well-recited by the elders. Furthermore, in the passage '...I will remember it just as it was heard by me in the presence of the Blessed One, received in his presence,' if it was so for me, what need is there to say so for the elders who were appointed to this foremost position by the Blessed One himself? Therefore, it is said that the council was well-compiled. The Explanation of the Discourse on the Minor and Lesser Matters is finished.

Brahmadaṇḍakathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourse on the Brahma-penalty

445. “Tvaṃyeva āṇāpehī”ti ettakameva vuttaṃ, therā pana brahmadaṇḍaṃ katvā vuttaṃyeva “channassā”tiādimāhaṃsūti veditabbaṃ. Ettha ca ānandatthero viya aññopi saṅghena āṇatto bhikkhu brahmadaṇḍakatena bhikkhunā ālapituṃ labhati, na añño. Ujjavanikāyāti paṭisotagāminiyā. Āgamā nu kho idha āgamā nu khvidha. Āgamā kho idha, te orodhā idha āgamā kho. “Bhisicchavīti bhisitthavikā”ti likhitaṃ. Sabbevimeti sabbameva. Kulavaṃ gamentīti niratthakavināsaṃ gamenti. Kucchito lavo kulavo, anayavināsoti vuttaṃ hoti. Imāya kho pana “dhammavinayasaṅgītiyā”ti vattabbe visesena vinayassa sāsanamūlabhāvadassanatthaṃ, tasmiṃ ṭhite sakalasāsanaṭhitisiddhidīpanatthañca “idaṃ vo kappati, idaṃ vo na kappatī”ti [V 0.0493] vatthusmiṃ āraddhattā, imissā ca pariyattiyā vinayapiṭakattā “vinayasaṅgītiyā”ti idha vuttaṃ.

445. “You alone should command”—only this much was said. But it should be understood that the elders, having imposed the brahma-penalty, spoke what had been said, namely, “for Channa,” and so on. Here, like the Venerable Ānanda, any other bhikkhu commanded by the Saṅgha may address a bhikkhu who has been subjected to the brahma-penalty, but no other. Ujjavanikāya means in a boat going upstream. “Did you come here? Is there a reason for coming here? Indeed, you have arrived here. Indeed, having come here, let there be your confession.” “Bhisicchavī means bhisitthavikā”—so it is written. Sabbevimeti means all indeed. Kulavaṃ gamenti means they bring about meaningless destruction. Kucchito lavo is kulavo; it is said to mean unprofitable destruction. Although it should have been said “this Dhamma-Vinaya recitation,” it is specifically called “Vinaya recitation” here for the purpose of showing that the Vinaya is the root of the Sāsana; and to demonstrate that when it is established, the establishment of the entire Sāsana is accomplished; and because it was undertaken concerning the matter of “this is allowable for you, this is not allowable for you;” and because this scripture is the Vinaya Piṭaka.

Pañcasatikakkhandhakavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Khandhaka of the Five Hundred is finished.

12. Sattasatikakkhandhakavaṇṇanā

12. The Commentary on the Khandhaka of the Seven Hundred

Dasavatthukathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Discourse of the Ten Topics

446. Nikkhittamaṇisuvaṇṇāti [M 0.0541] sikkhāpadeneva paṭikkhittamaṇisuvaṇṇā. Tattha maṇiggahaṇena sabbaṃ dukkaṭavatthu, suvaṇṇaggahaṇena sabbaṃ pācittiyavatthu gahitaṃ hoti. Bhikkhaggena bhikkhugaṇanāyāti vuttaṃ hoti.

446. Nikkhittamaṇisuvaṇṇā means jewels and gold rejected by the training rule itself. Therein, by the term “jewels,” all matters of wrong conduct (dukkaṭa) are included; by the term “gold,” all matters of expiation (pācittiya) are included. Bhikkhaggena means by the number of bhikkhus.

447. Mahikāti himaṃ. Posāti sattā. Sarajāti sakilesarajā. Magāti magasadisā. Tasmiṃ tasmiṃ visaye, bhave vā netīti netti, taṇhāyetaṃ adhivacanaṃ, tāya saha vattantīti sanettikā.

447. Mahikā means snow or frost. Posā means beings. Sarajā means having the dust of defilements. Magā means similar to a deer. In this or that sphere, or in this or that existence, it leads (neti)—thus it is called netti (that which leads). This is a designation for craving. Because they exist together with it, they are called sanettikā (those with that which leads).

450-2. Ahogaṅgoti pabbatassa nāmaṃ. Anumānessāmāti paññāpessāma. Āsutāti sajjitā, “asuttā”ti vā pāṭho, anāvilā apakkā taruṇā.

Ahogaṅga is the name of the mountain. Anumānessāma means we shall make known. Āsutā means prepared; or there is the reading asuttā, meaning untroubled, with unripe wisdom, and young.

453. Ujjaviṃsu paṭisotena gacchiṃsu.

453. They went upstream; they went against the current.

455. Appeva nāmāti sādhu nāma. Mūlā dāyakā pesalakā. “Kullakavihārenāti khuddakavihārenā”ti likhitaṃ. Rūpāvatārattā kullakavihāro nāma. Kathaṃ panetaṃ paññāyati, yena sannidhikataṃ yāvajīvikaṃ yāvakālikena tadahupaṭiggahitena sambhinnarasaṃ tadahupaṭiggahitasaṅkhayaṃ āgantvā sannidhikatāmisasaṅkhyameva gacchatīti? Vuccate – “yāvakālikena, bhikkhave, yāvajīvikaṃ tadahupaṭiggahita”nti vacanato purepaṭiggahitaṃ yāvajīvikaṃ tadahupaṭiggahitenāmisena [V 0.0494] ce sambhinnaṃ, purepaṭiggahitasaṅkhyameva gacchatīti siddhaṃ. Aññathā “sattāhakālikena, bhikkhave, yāvajīvikaṃ paṭiggahitaṃ sattāhaṃ kappatī”ti (mahāva. 305) vuttaṭṭhāne viya idhāpi “yāvakālikena, bhikkhave, yāvajīvikaṃ paṭiggahitaṃ kāle kappatī”ti vadeyya, tañcāvuttaṃ. Tasmā purepaṭiggahitaṃ taṃ āmisasambhinnaṃ āmisagatikamevāti veditabbaṃ. Gaṇṭhipade pana “sannidhikārakaṃ khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā”ti (pāci. 253) vuttaṃ. Byañjanamattaṃ na gahetabbaṃ.

455. In `Appeva nāma`, it means 'it is indeed good.' The root donors are those who love virtue. In `Kullakavihārena`, it is written as `khuddakavihārena` (by a small dwelling). Because it is from the Rūpāvatāra, it is called Kullakavihāra. But how is this known, that a stored lifelong item, having a mixed taste with a temporary item received on that day, having arrived at the designation of 'received on that day,' goes only to the designation of 'mixed with a stored edible'? It is said: Because of the statement, 'O bhikkhus, a lifelong item received on that day with a temporary item...,' it is established that if a lifelong item previously received is mixed with an edible received on that day, it goes only to the designation of 'previously received.' Otherwise, just as in the place where it is said, 'O bhikkhus, a lifelong item received with a seven-day item is allowable for seven days,' here also one should say, 'O bhikkhus, a lifelong item received with a temporary item is allowable for the proper time.' But that was not said. Therefore, it should be understood that the previously received item, when mixed with an edible, has the same nature as the edible. But in the Gaṇṭhipada, it is said: 'storable hard food or soft food.' The mere word should not be taken.

457. Idhāti [M 0.0542] imasmiṃ pāṭhe. “‘Kāle kappati, vikāle na kappatī’ti (mahāva. 305) vuttavacanamattena ‘vikāle kappatī’ti vikālabhojanapācittiyaṃ āvahaṃ hotīti attho, ‘na kappatī’ti sannidhibhojanapācittiyaṃ āvahaṃ hotīti attho, yadi sambhinnarasaṃ ajjapaṭiggahitampi yāvajīvikanti attho”ti likhitaṃ. Suttavibhaṅgeti mātikāsaṅkhāte sutte ca tassa padabhājanīyasaṅkhāte vibhaṅge cāti attho. Idaṃ āgatameva. Kataranti? “Atikkāmayato chedanaka”nti idaṃ.

457. `Idha` means 'in this text.' It is written: "By the mere words spoken, 'It is allowable at the proper time, not allowable at the improper time,' the meaning is that 'it is allowable at the improper time' brings about the pācittiya offense of eating at the wrong time; and the meaning is that 'it is not allowable' brings about the pācittiya offense of eating stored food; the meaning is: if a lifelong item, even if received today, has a mixed taste." `Suttavibhaṅge` means in the Sutta called the Mātikā and in its analysis, the Vibhaṅga called the Padabhājanīya. This has indeed been stated. Which? This: "For one who causes it to be passed over, it is a cutting offense."

Tividatthipamāṇañce, adasaṃ taṃ nisīdanaṃ;

Nisīdanaṃ kathaṃ hoti, sadasaṃ tañhi lakkhaṇaṃ.

If that sitting-cloth is of the measure of three spans, but is without a border, how can it be a sitting-cloth? Indeed, its characteristic is to have a border.

Tividatthipamāṇaṃ taṃ, dasā tattha vidatthi ce;

Taṃnisīdananāmattā, tasmiṃ chedanakaṃ siyā.

That sitting-cloth is three spans in measure. If there is a border of one span on it, then because it has the name 'sitting-cloth,' cutting should be done on it.

Anisīdananāmamhi, kathaṃ chedanakaṃ bhave;

Iti ce neva vattabbaṃ, nisīdanavidatthito.

If one were to say: 'In a cloth that does not have the name "sitting-cloth," how could there be cutting?'—this should not be said, because of the three-span measure of the sitting-cloth.

Kappate sadasāmattaṃ, nisīdanamiti kāraṇaṃ;

Kathaṃ yujjati no cetaṃ, nisīdanassa nāmakaṃ.

How could this reason be suitable: 'A sitting-cloth with a border of just one span is allowable'? For this, which is only a border, does not have the name 'sitting-cloth'.

Nisīdananti vuttattā, pamāṇasamatikkamā;

Tassānumatihetuttā, tattha chedanakaṃ bhave.

Because it is called a 'sitting-cloth,' because it exceeds the measure, and because it is a cause for consent, cutting occurs in that case.

Jātarūpakappe –

In the section on accepting gold and silver—

Jātarūpaṃ [V 0.0495] paṭikkhittaṃ, puggalasseva pāḷiyaṃ;

Na saṅghassāti saṅghassa, tañce kappati sabbaso.

In the Pāḷi, gold and silver are rejected only for an individual, not for the Saṅgha. Therefore, if it is allowable for the Saṅgha in every way...

Vikālabhojanañcāpi, puggalasseva vāritaṃ;

Na saṅghassāti saṅghassa, kappatīti kathaṃ samaṃ.

Eating at the wrong time is also forbidden only for an individual, not for the Saṅgha. How then could the two cases be consistent in concluding, 'It is allowable for the Saṅgha'?

Sattasatikakkhandhakavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Khandhaka of the Seven Hundred is finished.

Cūḷavaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Cūḷavagga is finished.

Namo tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa

Homage to the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One.

Parivāravaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Parivāra

Soḷasamahāvāravaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Sixteen Great Sections

Paññattivāravaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Section on Designations

1-2. Sīlasamādhipaññāvimuttivimuttiñāṇadassanasaṅkhātassa [V 0.0496][M 0.0543] dhammakkhandhasarīrassa sāsaneti attho. Parivāroti saṅgahaṃ yo samāruḷho, tassa parivārassa. Vinayabhūtā paññatti vinayapaññatti. “Paññattikālaṃ jānatā”ti dukanayavasena vatvā puna suttantanayena vattuṃ “apica pubbenivāsādīhī”ti vuttaṃ. Tattha passanaṃ nāma dassanattā dibbacakkhunā yojitaṃ paṭivedhañāṇadassanaṃ. Desanāpaññāya passatāti āsayānusayādike. Pucchāyāti sattamī. Punapi etthāti pucchāvissajjane. Micchādiṭṭhīti natthikadiṭṭhi antaggāhikadiṭṭhi. “Ājīvahetu paññattānī”ti vacanato imāni cha sikkhāpadāni ṭhapetvā sesā ācāravipatti nāmāti veditabbaṃ. Kāyena pana āpattiṃ āpajjatīti ettha “pubbabhāge sevanacittamaṅgaṃ katvā kāyadvārasaṅkhātaṃ viññattiṃ janayitvā pavattacittuppādasaṅkhātaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati, kiñcāpi cittena samuṭṭhāpitā viññatti, tathāpi cittena adhippetassa atthassa viññattiyā sādhitattā ‘kāyadvārena āpajjatī’ti vutta”nti imamatthaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ, na bhaṇḍanādittayavūpasamaṃ. Āpāṇakoṭikanti jīvitapariyantaṃ katvā. Porāṇakehi mahātherehīti sīhaḷadīpe mahātherehi potthakaṃ [V 0.0497] āropitakāle ṭhapitāti attho. “Catutthasaṅgītisadisā potthakāruḷhasaṅgīti ahosī”ti vuttaṃ.

1-2. The meaning is: in the teaching of the Blessed One, whose body is the aggregates of Dhamma known as virtue, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation. The Parivāra is that which has been included in the compilation. The regulations that constitute the Vinaya are called Vinayapaññatti. Having stated the dual method by saying, “by one knowing the time of designation,” it is then explained again according to the sutta method with the words, “moreover, through past lives, etc.” Here, “seeing” refers to the knowledge and vision of penetration, connected with the divine eye because of its nature of seeing. In the phrase 'one sees with the wisdom of teaching', it refers to inclinations, latent tendencies, and so on. “Pucchāya” is in the locative case. “Again, here” refers to the question and answer. “Wrong view” means nihilistic view and view of extremes. From the statement, “due to livelihood, regulations are established,” it should be understood that apart from these six training rules, the rest are called misconduct in behavior. Regarding “one commits an offense with the body,” this is said with reference to the meaning that in the preliminary stage, having formed the intention to engage as an element, one generates intimation, which is called the bodily door, and thereby incurs an offense, which is called the arising of consciousness that proceeds. Although the intimation is produced by the mind, nevertheless, because the intended purpose of the mind is accomplished through the intimation, it is said, “one commits an offense through the bodily door.” This is not said with reference to the pacification of the triad beginning with quarreling. “Up to the limit of life” means having made the limit of life. “By the ancient elders” refers to the elders in Sri Lanka who established it when the book was compiled. It is said, “The compilation of the book was like the Fourth Council.”

Mahāvibhaṅge paññattivāravaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Section on Designations in the Mahāvibhaṅga is concluded.

Katāpattivārādivaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Section on Offenses, etc.

166. Katāpattivāre [M 0.0544] “saṅghikaṃ mañcaṃ vā”tiādi ajjhokāsattā vihārabbhantarepi āpajjanato leḍḍupātātikkamavasena vuttaṃ. Dutiye seyyaṃ santharitvāti abbhantare santharitabhāvato vihārato bahigamanepi taṃdivasānāgame āpajjanato “parikkhepaṃ atikkāmetī”ti vuttaṃ.

166. In the section on offenses, regarding “a monastic bed or” etc., due to being in the open air, the offense can be incurred even within the monastery precincts; hence it is stated in terms of exceeding the throwing of a clod. In the second case, having spread out a sleeping place, because it has been spread out inside, the offense is incurred even when going outside the monastery if that day has not ended; hence it is stated as “crossing the boundary.”

171. Sañcicca pāṇaṃ jīvitā voropento catasso āpattiyoti ettha kiñcāpi tasmiṃ sikkhāpade tiracchānagatapāṇova adhippeto, atha kho pāṇoti vohārasāmaññato atthuddhāravasena “catasso”ti vuttaṃ. Esa nayo aññesupi evarūpesu ṭhānesu.

171. Herein, regarding “intentionally depriving a living being of life incurs four offenses,” although in that training rule only an animal is intended, nevertheless, due to the common usage of the term “living being,” “four” is stated by way of extracting the meaning. This is the principle in other such instances as well.

173. Vikāle gāmappavesane “paṭhamaṃ pādaṃ parikkhepaṃ atikkāmeti, āpatti dukkaṭassā’ti vuttattā upacāre nāpajjati, parikkhepaṃ atikkamitvāva āpajjatīti siddhamevā”ti vadanti.

173. Regarding entering a village at an unseasonable time, some say: “Because it is said, ‘When one makes the first foot cross the boundary, there is an offense of wrong-doing,’ one does not incur an offense in the vicinity; one incurs it only after having crossed the boundary. This is indeed established.”

193. Paccayavāre purimavārato viseso atthiyeva, “methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevanto kati āpattiyo āpajjatī”ti vutte jatumaṭṭhakassokāso na jāto, idha pana “methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevanapaccayā”ti vutte puggalaniddesābhāvā jatumaṭṭhakañca paviṭṭhaṃ, evaṃ viseso atthi. Tathā evarūpesu ṭhānesu.

193. In the section on conditions, there is indeed a distinction from the previous section. When it is said, “Engaging in sexual intercourse, how many offenses does one incur?” the occasion for the Jatumaṭṭhaka training rule does not arise. Here, however, when it is said, “on account of engaging in sexual intercourse,” due to the absence of specifying a person, the Jatumaṭṭhaka training rule is also included. Thus, there is a distinction. It is the same in other such instances.

Mahāvibhaṅge ca bhikkhunivibhaṅge soḷasamahāvāravaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

In the Mahāvibhaṅga and in the Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga, the explanation of the sixteen great sections is concluded.

Samuṭṭhānasīsavaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Chapter on Origins

257. Anattāti [V 0.0498][M 0.0545] attavirahitā “alavaṇabhojana”ntiādīsu viya. Karuṇāsītalabhāvena candasadiso. Kilesatimirappahānato ādicco. Yasmā te desayanti, tasmā aṅgīrasopi. Piṭake tīṇi desayi tesaṃ aññatarattāti attho. Vinayo yadi tiṭṭhati, evaṃ paṭipattisaddhammādi nīyati pavattatīti attho. Ayaṃ pana kathaṃ tiṭṭhatīti? Āha “ubhato cā”tiādi. Parivārena ganthitā tiṭṭhantīti attho. Tasseva parivārassa sutte. Niyatasamuṭṭhānaṃ kataṃ, vuttanti adhippāyo. Asambhinnasamuṭṭhānāni asaṅkarasamuṭṭhānāni, aññehi asadisasamuṭṭhānānīti attho. Yasmā parivāre sati vinayo tiṭṭhati, vinaye sati saddhammo tiṭṭhati, yasmā samuṭṭhānāni ca sutte dissanti, tasmā sikkheti attho. “Dhammakāmo supesalo”ti parivāre gāravajananatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Tatthāti “dissantī”ti tattha. “Ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhātīti paṭhamapārājikaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhātī”ti vuttaṃ. Pāḷiyañhi niddiṭṭhasamuṭṭhānañca dissati. “Tasseva parivārassa, samuṭṭhānaṃ niyato kata”nti vuttaṃ purimanayeti attho. Yathāñāyanti yathābhūtaṃ. “Sañcarittābhāsanañcā”ti pāṭho. “Sañcarittānubhāsanañcā”tipi atthi. Nayavajjehi vinayavajjehīti attho.

257. “Non-self” means devoid of self, as in “food without salt,” and so on. He is like the moon by virtue of his compassionate coolness. He is like the sun by virtue of having dispelled the darkness of defilements. Because they teach, therefore Aṅgīrasa also taught the three Piṭakas; the meaning is that this is one of them. If the Vinaya stands, in that case the good Dhamma of practice, and so on, is led on and proceeds—this is the meaning. But how does this stand? He said, “on both sides,” and so on. The meaning is that they stand, being strung together by the Parivāra. In the Sutta of that very Parivāra, the fixed origin is made; the intention is that it is stated. Undivided origins are unmixed origins, meaning origins dissimilar to others. Because when the Parivāra exists, the Vinaya stands; when the Vinaya stands, the good Dhamma stands; and because the origins are also seen in the Sutta, therefore one should train in the Parivāra—this is the meaning. “Dhamma-loving, very amiable” is said in the Parivāra to generate respect. The word “there” refers to “are seen” in that context. It is said, “The first Pārājika arises from one origin; it arises from one origin.” For in the Pāḷi, the designated origin is also seen. It is said, “Of that very Parivāra, the origin is made fixed,” meaning according to the previous method. “As is appropriate” means as it truly is. There is the reading, “And speaking as a go-between.” There is also, “And repeating as a go-between.” The meaning of `nayavajjehi` is 'by faults of the Vinaya'.

Paṭhamapārājikasamuṭṭhānavaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Origins of the First Pārājika

258. Nānubandhe pavattininti “yā pana bhikkhunī vutthāpitaṃ pavattiniṃ dve vassāni nānubandheyyā”ti vuttasikkhāpadañca. Ayaṃ pāṭho ekaccesu potthakesu na dissati. Chasattati paṭhamapārājikasamuṭṭhānā.

258. Regarding 'not following the pavattinī,' this refers to the training rule that was stated: 'Whatever bhikkhunī should not follow for two years a pavattinī who has been rehabilitated...' This reading is not found in some manuscripts. There are seventy-six origins of the first Pārājika.

Dutiyapārājikasamuṭṭhānavaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Origins of the Second Pārājika

259. “Kukkuccaṃ cīvaraṃ datvāti kukkuccuppādanañca dhammikānaṃ kammānaṃ chandaṃ datvā khīyanañca cīvaraṃ datvā khīyanañcā”ti pāṭho. “Datvā”ti uppaṭipāṭiyā vuttaṃ, tasmā “kukkuccaṃ dhammikaṃ datvāti pāṭho sundaro”ti vadanti, vicāretvā gahetabbaṃ.

259. Regarding 'Kukkuccaṃ cīvaraṃ datvā,' the reading is: '...the causing of regret, and disparaging after having given consent for righteous deeds, and disparaging after having given a robe.' The word 'datvā' is said to be out of order; therefore, they say, 'The reading "kukkuccaṃ dhammikaṃ datvā" is good.' This should be accepted after investigation.

269. Akatanti [V 0.0499] abhinavaṃ.

269. 'Akataṃ' means new.

Antarapeyyālaṃ

Intermediate Repetition Section

Katipucchāvāravaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Chapter on Questions

271. Paṭiniddesanti [M 0.0546] punappunaṃ niddisanaṃ. Āpattikkhandhehi vinītāni saṃvarānīti attho. Etehi āpattikkhandhehi. “Ārakā”ti nivattiatthena vuttattā taṃ puna sarūpena vattukāmo “bhusā vā”ti āha. “Gehaṃ dhūmena puṇṇaṃ ādhūmita”ntiādīsu viya rāgādiveraṃ maṇati vināseti. Etāyāti viratiyā. Vela calane. Niyyānaṃ maggaṃ sinoti bandhatīti setu. “Setughātoti vītikkamapaṭipakkhabhūtā virati, tadatthanibbattikaracittuppādo vā”ti vuttaṃ. “Dhammassavanagganti dhammaṃ suṇantānaṃ samūha”nti likhitaṃ. Sace na gacchati, vikkhitto vā nisīdati. Kāyappāgabbhiyaṃ kāyaduccaritaṃ. “Pamāde”ti vatvā tadatthaṃ dassetuṃ “sativippavāse”ti vuttaṃ.

271. 'Paṭiniddesa' means repeated instruction. The meaning is: restraints are things disciplined by the aggregates of offenses. By these aggregates of offenses. Because 'ārakā' is said with the meaning of avoidance, wishing to state that again in its own form, he said 'bhusā vā'. It crushes, it destroys the enmity of lust and so on. 'By this' means by abstinence. The word 'vela' is used in the sense of movement. Because it binds the path of deliverance, it is a 'setu' (dam). It is said: 'Setughāta (destroying the dam) is abstinence which is the opposite of transgression, or it is the arising of a thought that accomplishes that purpose.' It is written: 'Dhammassavanaggaṃ means an assembly of those who listen to the Dhamma.' If one does not go, or sits distracted. 'Kāyappāgabbhiyaṃ' (bodily impudence) is bodily misconduct. Having said 'pamāde' (negligence), to show its meaning, 'sativippavāse' (absence of mindfulness) is stated.

272-3. Saparasantāne vāti sasantāne vā parasantāne vā. Tathā vivadantā panāti bhedakaravatthūni nissāya vivadantā. Ubhayehipīti theranavehi. Nanti mettaṃ kāyakammaṃ. Yesaṃ puggalānaṃ piyaṃ karoti, tesaṃ mettākāyakammasaṅkhāto dhammo. Ettakanti āmisavibhattidassanaṃ. Asukassa cāti puggalavibhattidassanaṃ. “Dussīlassa adātumpi vaṭṭatī”ti vuttattā eva alajjiparibhogo vārito. Sabbesaṃ dātabbamevāti sanniṭṭhānena ajānantena vibhāgaṃ akatvā dātabbabhāvaṃ dīpetīti eke. “Sabbesaṃ dātabbamevā”ti vuttaṃ aṭṭhakathāsu. Tattha “alajjiukkhittakānaṃ paribhogasīsena sahatthā na dātabbaṃ, dāpetabbanti apare”ti vuttaṃ. Vicinitvā dānaṃ viceyya dānaṃ. Yasmā ayaṃ viseso kātabboyevāti ayaṃ karoti, tasmā puggalavibhāgo na katoti sambandho. Pakativaṇṇena visabhāgavaṇṇena. “Idaṃ nāma āpanno”ti parehi aparāmasitabbato aparāmaṭṭhāni. Anulomehi gahitasaṅkhārārammaṇehi nibbānārammaṇaṃ katvā niyyāti.

272-273. 'Saparasantāne vā' means in one's own continuum or in another's continuum. 'Tathā vivadantā pana' refers to those who dispute, having relied on divisive subjects. 'Ubhayehi pi' means by both the elders and the new monks. The word 'naṃ' means loving-kindness in bodily action. The quality called loving-kindness in bodily action belongs to those persons to whom one shows affection. 'Ettakaṃ' shows the distribution of material things. 'Asukassa ca' shows the distribution among individuals. Because it is said, 'It is allowable even not to give to the immoral,' the consumption by the shameless is prohibited. Some say that the phrase 'It should be given to all' indicates that it should be given by one who does not know with certainty, without making a distinction. 'It should be given to all' is stated in the commentaries. Therein, it is said: 'Others say that to the shameless and the suspended monk, it should not be given with one's own hand for the purpose of consumption; it should be caused to be given by another.' Giving after investigating, giving after discerning. The connection is as follows: Because this one acts thinking, 'This distinction must indeed be made,' therefore the distinction among individuals is not made. With natural color, with dissimilar color. Because they are not to be touched by others with the thought, 'Such and such has been attained,' they are called 'untouched'. By means of conformable states of mind that have taken formations as their object, having made Nibbāna the object, one is liberated.

Chaāpattisamuṭṭhānavārādivaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Sections on the Six Origins of Offenses, etc.

276. “Paṭhamena [V 0.0500] āpattisamuṭṭhānena dubbhāsitaṃ āpajjeyyāti na hīti vattabba”nti vuttaṃ vācācittavasenevāpajjitabbato.

276. It is said, 'It should not be said that one would incur an offense of wrong speech through the first origin of an offense,' because it is to be incurred only by the power of speech and mind.

277. Kuṭiṃ [M 0.0547] karotīti ettha sañcarittamavatvā dukkaṭathullaccayasaṅghādisesānaṃ ekasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ paṭipāṭiyā uppattidassanatthamidaṃ vuttaṃ. Na hi sañcaritte eva āpajjati. “Iminā pana nayena sabbattha paṭipāṭiyā aggahaṇe kāraṇaṃ veditabba”nti vuttaṃ.

277. Herein, regarding 'He makes a hut,' without mentioning sañcaritta, this is said in order to show the sequential arising of dukkaṭa, thullaccaya, and saṅghādisesa offenses in a single case. For one does not incur an offense only in the case of sañcaritta. It is said, 'But by this method, the reason for not taking the sequence in all cases should be known.'

283. Vivekadassināti tadaṅgavivekādipañcavidhavivekadassinā.

283. 'One who sees seclusion' means one who sees the five kinds of seclusion, beginning with momentary seclusion.

284. Attano duṭṭhullanti saṅghādisesaṃ.

284. 'One's own gross offense' means a saṅghādisesa offense.

288. Vivādādhikaraṇapaccayāti aññehi, attanā vā pubbabhāge āpannapaccayāti attho. Omasatīti “ayaṃ dhammo, ayaṃ vinayo”ti vivadanto “tvaṃ kiṃ jānāsī”tiādinā omasati. Tīhi samathehi sammukhāvinayapaṭiññātakaraṇatiṇavatthārakehi. “Sammukhāvinayañcettha sabbattha icchitabbato ‘sammukhāvinayena ceva paṭiññātakaraṇena cā’tiādinā dvīhipi yojitaṃ. Esa nayo sabbatthā”ti vuttaṃ.

288. The phrase 'due to a cause for a legal issue involving dispute' means due to the cause of having previously fallen into an offense, either by others or by oneself. 'He disparages' means that while disputing, 'This is the Dhamma, this is the Vinaya,' one disparages with words such as, 'What do you know?'. By the three settlements: settlement in the presence, settlement by acknowledgement, and settlement by covering with grass. Because settlement in the presence is desired in all cases, it is connected with both by means of the phrase 'by settlement in the presence and by acknowledgement,' and so on.

291. Ṭhapetvā satta āpattiyoti ettha “kiñcāpi avasesā natthi, tathāpi paṭipāṭiyā pāṭavajananatthaṃ pucchā katā”ti vuttaṃ.

291. Regarding 'except for the seven offenses,' here it is said: 'Although there are no remaining ones, the question is nevertheless asked in order to generate proficiency in the sequence.'

Antarapeyyālaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Intermediate Repetition Section is concluded.

Samathabhedavaṇṇanā

291. Explanation of the Classification of Settlements

Adhikaraṇapariyāyavārādivaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Section on Categories of Legal Issues, etc.

293-4. Lobhakāraṇā [M 0.0548][V 0.0501] vivādanato “lobho pubbaṅgamo”ti vuttaṃ. Evaṃ sesesu. Ṭhānānītiādīni kāraṇavevacanāni. Kāraṇañhi tiṭṭhanti etthāti ṭhānaṃ, vasanti etthāti vatthu, bhavanti etthāti bhūmīti vuccati. Ke tiṭṭhanti vasanti bhavanti cāti? Vivādādhikaraṇādayo. Kusalākusalābyākatacitto hutvā vivadanato “nava hetū”ti vuttaṃ. Kodhano hoti upanāhītiādīni dvādasa mūlāni. Akkosantena hi catūsu vipattīsu ekena anuvadanato “catasso vipattiyo ṭhānānī”ti vuttaṃ. Cuddasa mūlānīti vivādādhikaraṇe vuttā dvādasa, kāyo, vācā ca.

293-294. Because one disputes due to the cause of greed, it is said, 'greed is the forerunner.' It should be understood similarly in the remaining cases. 'Grounds,' and so on, are synonyms for 'cause'. For a cause is called a 'ground' (ṭhāna) because things stand (tiṭṭhanti) there; it is called a 'basis' (vatthu) because they dwell (vasanti) there; it is called a 'plane' (bhūmi) because they arise (bhavanti) there. What things stand, dwell, and arise? Legal issues involving dispute, and so on. Because one disputes after having a wholesome, unwholesome, or indeterminate mind, it is said, 'nine causes.' 'One is angry, one is resentful,' and so on, are the twelve roots. For, because one who reviles accuses by means of one of the four failures, it is said, 'the four failures are grounds.' The fourteen roots are the twelve mentioned in the context of a legal issue involving dispute, plus body and speech.

295-6. Satta āpattikkhandhā ṭhānānīti ettha “āpattiṃ āpajjitvā paṭicchādentassa yā āpatti hoti, tassā āpattiyā pubbe āpannā āpatti ṭhānaṃ hotī”ti vuttaṃ. “Natthi āpattādhikaraṇaṃ kusalanti vacanato natthi āpattādhikaraṇassa kusalahetu, kusalacittaṃ pana aṅgaṃ hotī”ti likhitaṃ. Cattāri kammāni ṭhānānīti ettha “evaṃ kattabbanti ṭhitapāḷi kammaṃ nāma. ‘Yathāṭhitapāḷivasena karontānaṃ kiriyā kiccādhikaraṇaṃ nāmā’”ti vuttaṃ, “pāḷianusārena paṭikātabbalakkhaṇaṃ vā kammaṃ. Tatheva karaṇaṃ kiccādhikaraṇa”nti ca. Ñattiñattidutiyañatticatutthakammāni ñattito jāyanti, apalokanakammaṃ apalokanato, “kiccādhikaraṇaṃ ekena samathena sammati sampajjatīti attho”ti likhitaṃ. Siyunti honti. Kathañca siyāti kathaṃ hoti. Vivādādhikaraṇassa dveti te dve ṭhapetvā aññehi na sammati.

In 'The seven groups of offenses are grounds,' it is said: 'For a monk who, having committed an offense, conceals it, the previously committed offense is the ground of that offense.' It is written: 'Because of the statement “An offense-issue is not wholesome,” there is no wholesome cause for an offense-issue, but a wholesome mind is a factor.' In 'The four formal acts are grounds,' it is said: 'The established Pāḷi text stating “Thus it should be done” is called a formal act. The action of those performing it according to the established Pāḷi text is called a duty-issue.' And also: 'Alternatively, a formal act has the characteristic of what should be performed in accordance with the Pāḷi. The performance in that very way is a duty-issue.' The formal acts of a motion, a motion with one announcement, and a motion with three announcements arise from a motion; the formal act of seeking leave arises from seeking leave. It is written: 'The meaning is that a duty-issue is settled and accomplished by a single settlement.' 'They might be' (`siyunti`) means 'they are' (`honti`). 'And how might they be?' (`kathañca siyā`) means 'how is it?' (`kathaṃ hoti`). For a dispute-issue, there are two; excluding those two, it is not settled by other settlements.

297. Sādhāraṇāti taṃ sametabbā.

297. `Sādhāraṇā` (common) means that it (the dispute-issue) should be settled.

298. Tabbhāgiyāti taṃkoṭṭhāsā.

298. `Tabbhāgiyā` means having that as its portion.

299. Ekādhikaraṇaṃ sabbe samathā samaggā hutvā sametuṃ bhabbāti pucchanto “samathā samathassa sādhāraṇā”ti āha. Samathā samathassā siyā sādhāraṇā siyā asādhāraṇā.

299. Asking, 'Are all settlements, having become harmonious, able to settle a single issue?', he said, 'Settlements are common to a settlement.' Settlements may be common to a settlement, or they may be uncommon.

300. Samathā [M 0.0549][V 0.0502] samathassa tabbhāgiyavārepi eseva nayo.

300. This same method applies also in the section on `tabbhāgiya` (belonging to that portion) of settlements to a settlement.

301. Ime samathā samathā, na sammukhāvinayoti attho.

301. The meaning is: these settlements are just settlements, not the 'procedure in the presence'.

302. “Samathā vinayo”tipi vuccati, tasmā vinayo sammukhāvinayoti vinayavāro uddhaṭo siyā. Na sammukhāvinayoti sammukhāvinayaṃ ṭhapetvā sativinayādayo sesasamathā.

302. 'Settlements are discipline' is also said; therefore, a section on discipline might be extracted, stating, 'discipline is the procedure in the presence.' 'Not the procedure in the presence' means that, having set aside the procedure in the presence, the remaining settlements are the procedure of mindfulness and so on.

303. Saṅghassa sammukhā paṭiññāte taṃ paṭijānanaṃ saṅghassa sammukhatā nāma hotīti “tassa paṭijānanacittaṃ sandhāya ‘sammukhāvinayo kusalo’tiādi vutta”nti vadanti. Natthi sammukhāvinayo akusaloti “dhammavinayapuggalasammukhatāhi tivaṅgiko sammukhāvinayo etehi vinā natthi.
