336. Regarding 'Thirty-one are grave offenses': there are eight pārājikas for both communities, thirteen saṅghādisesas for bhikkhus, and ten saṅghādisesas for bhikkhunīs. By way of being common and uncommon, the eight pārājikas are called offenses 'without remainder'. Regarding 'that very thing', it refers only to the transgression of virtue. To explain in detail, by means of 'pārājika', etc., he answered the very question that was asked. Therein, there is the reading: 'yo cāyaṃ, akkosati hasādhippāyo'. Setting aside the failure that has come by way of explaining the grave offenses, he began to answer the 'as far as the third time' questions in the order of questioning. The bhikkhunī who follows an expelled one and the eight 'as far as the third time' saṅghādisesas, because they are asked about here, have become what are called the 'immediately following questions'.

Chedanakādivaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Rules Requiring Cutting, etc.

337. Pamāṇātikkantamañcanisīdanakaṇḍupaṭicchādivassikasāṭikāsugatacīvarappamāṇaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ udakasāṭikāti cha chedanakāni. Cīvaravippavāsasammutiādayo catasso sammutiyo. “Ayaṃ tattha sāmīcī”ti evaṃ āgatā satta sāmīciyo.

337. The six rules that are chedanaka (requiring cutting) are: those concerning a couch, a sitting-cloth, an itch-covering, a rains-cloth, and the measure of the Sugata's robe, all of which are in excess of the proper measurement; and the water-cloth for bhikkhunīs. The four rules involving permissions are those beginning with the permission to be separated from one's robes. The seven rules concerning proper conduct are those that have come down thus: 'This is proper conduct there'.

Asādhāraṇādivaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Uncommon, etc.

338. Pubbe vuttacuddasaparamāneva antarapañhe niṭṭhapetvā purimapañhaṃ vissajjento. Dhovanañca paṭiggahoti gāthā aṭṭhakathācariyānaṃ. Dve lomāni eḷakalomatiyojanaparamāni.

338. Having concluded in the intermediate question the fourteen paramas previously mentioned, he, answering the former question, said: The verse 'Dhovanañca paṭiggaho' is a verse of the commentary teachers. The two rules concerning wool are the training rules called 'Sheep's Wool' and 'The Three-Yojana Limit'.

Dvevīsati khuddakāti –

The twenty-two minor rules are:

“Sakalo bhikkhunivaggo, paramparañca bhojanaṃ;

Anatirittaṃ abhihaṭaṃ, paṇītañca acelakaṃ;

Jānaṃ duṭṭhullachādanaṃ.

“The entire Bhikkhunīvagga; successive eating; bringing forward food not designated as a leftover; exquisite food; and a naked ascetic; knowingly concealing a grave offense.

“Ūnaṃ [V 0.0519] mātugāmena saddhiṃ, yā ca anikkhantarājake;

Santaṃ bhikkhuṃ anāpucchā, vikāle gāmappavesanaṃ.

Making an arrangement together with a woman; and whichever training rule concerns a district where the king has not departed; entering a village at the wrong time without asking a bhikkhu who is present.

“Nisīdane ca yā sikkhā, vassikāya ca sāṭikā;

Dvāvīsati imā sikkhā, khuddakesu pakāsitā”ti. –

And the training rule concerning the sitting-cloth, and the rains-cloth; these twenty-two training rules are declared among the minor ones.”

Pāṭho[M 0.0568]. “Kulesu cārittāpattī”ti pāṭho na gahetabbo sādhāraṇattā tassa sikkhāpadassa. Chacattārīsā cimeti chacattārīsa ime. “Pārājikāni saṅghādiseso”ti evaṃ vuttasikkhāpade eva vibhajitvā vuttattā vibhattiyo nāma. Sādhāraṇanti aṭṭhannampi sādhāraṇaṃ. Pārājikabhūtā vibhattiyo pārājikavibhattiyo. Sādhāraṇe sattavajjo saṅghādiseso. Aññatarasmiṃ gaṇṭhipade “atha vā ‘dve uposathā dve pavāraṇā cattāri kammāni pañceva uddesā caturo bhavanti, naññathā’ti pāḷiṃ uddharanti. Tattha ‘cattāri kammānī’ti visesābhāvā uddharitapotthakameva sundaraṃ, pubbepi vibhattimattadassanavaseneva cetaṃ vuttaṃ. ‘Na samathehi vūpasamanavasenā’ti vatvā cattāri kammavibhajane ‘samathehi vūpasammatī’ti na visesitaṃ uposathappavāraṇānaṃyeva vibhāgattā. Kasmā? Etthāpi ‘uposathappavāraṇānaṃyeva visesetvā nayaṃ dethā’ti vuttattā, adhammena vaggādikammena āpattiyopi vūpasammantīti āpajjanatoti veditabba”nti vuttaṃ, vicāretabbaṃ. Dvīhi catūhi tīhi kiccaṃ ekenāti dvīhi vivādādhikaraṇaṃ, catūhi anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ, tīhi āpattādhikaraṇaṃ, ekena kiccādhikaraṇaṃ sammatīti attho.

The reading. The reading “Kulesu cārittāpattī” is not to be taken, as that training rule is common. The phrase `chacattārīsā cime` is to be divided as `chacattārīsa ime` (these forty-six). “Pārājikas, saṅghādisesas”—because they are stated having divided only the aforementioned training rules, they are called classifications. `Sādhāraṇa` means common to all eight. The classifications that have become Pārājika are Pārājika-classifications. In the common section, the Saṅghādisesa group is with seven excluded. In a certain knotty passage, they cite the Pāḷi: “Or else, ‘two uposathas, two pavāraṇās, four formal acts, and five recitations become four, not otherwise.’” There, regarding “four formal acts,” because there is no distinction, the cited text itself is good; and previously, this was stated merely by way of showing the classification. Having said, “Not by way of pacification through settlements,” in the analysis of the four formal acts, it is not specified that “it is pacified by settlements,” because only the Uposatha and Pavāraṇā are analyzed. Why? Because here too it is said, “Give the method, specifying only for Uposatha and Pavāraṇā,” and because it would follow that offenses are also pacified unlawfully. It is stated, “This should be understood,” and it should be investigated. Regarding the phrase 'by two, by four, by three, a duty by one,' the meaning is: a legal issue of dispute is settled by two settlements; a legal issue of accusation, by four; a legal issue of an offense, by three; and a legal issue of duties, by one.

Pārājikādiāpattivaṇṇanā

The Explanation of Offenses Beginning with Pārājika

339. Nibbacanamattanti vevacanamattaṃ. Seseti ādito sesā majjhantā. Padanti sikkhāpadaṃ. Saddhācittaṃ pasannacittanti attho, “santācitta”nti vā pāṭho. Anāḷiyanti daliddaṃ. Kiñcāpi idaṃ nibbacanaṃ “garukaṃ lahukañcā”tiādipañhe natthi, “handa vākyaṃ suṇoma te”ti iminā pana vacanena saṅgahitassatthassa dīpanatthaṃ vuttanti veditabbaṃ. “Ākāso pakkhinaṃ gatī”ti ca pāṭho atthi, so jātivasena yujjati. Pakkhīnanti ujukameva.

339. `Nibbacanamattaṃ` is just a synonym. In `sesa`, from the beginning, the remaining are the middle and the end. `Pada` is the training rule. `Saddhācittaṃ` means a mind with faith, a serene mind; or there is the reading `santācitta`. `Anāḷiya` means a poor person. Although this explanation is not found in the question beginning with 'grave and light,' it should be understood that it is stated to explain the meaning included by this statement, 'Come, let us hear your words.' There is also the reading, 'The sky is the path of birds,' and that reading is suitable by way of species. The word `pakkhīnaṃ` is straightforward.

Paṭhamagāthāsaṅgaṇikavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the First Verse-Compilation is concluded.

Adhikaraṇabhedavaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Divisions of Legal Issues

Ukkoṭanabhedādivaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Divisions of Reopening and so forth

340. Adhikaraṇaukkoṭena [V 0.0520][M 0.0569] samathānaṃ ukkoṭaṃ dassetunti adhikaraṇāni sattahi samathehi sammanti, tāni ukkoṭento satta samathe ukkoṭeti nāmāti adhippāyo. Pasavatīti sambhavati. “Anuvādādhikaraṇe labbhantī’tiādīni ‘dhammo adhammo’tiādīnaṃ samānattā tesu visesato labbhantī”ti vuttaṃ. Anihatanti suttādinā. Avinicchitanti “āpattianāpattī”tiādinā. “Tattha jātakaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ ukkoṭeti…pe… tiṇavatthārakaṃ ukkoṭetī”ti daseva vuttā. “Sammukhāvinayapaṭiññātakaraṇayebhuyyasikā avuttattā ukkoṭetuṃ na sakkā, kammavācāpi tesaṃ natthi. Tasmā te ukkoṭetuṃ na sakkāti vadantī”ti likhitaṃ. Pāḷimuttakavinicchayenevāti vinayalakkhaṇaṃ vinā kevalaṃ dhammadesanāmattavasenevāti attho. Khandhakato vā parivārato vā ānītasuttena. Nijjhāpenti dassenti. Pubbe dhammavinayena vinicchitaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ upajjhāyādīnaṃ atthāya “adhammaṃ dhammo”tiādīni dīpetvāti attho. Visamāni kāyakammādīni nissitattā visamanissito. Evaṃ sesesu.

340. Regarding 'to show the reopening of the settlements by the reopening of legal issues': the intention is that legal issues are settled by the seven settlements, and one who reopens them is called one who reopens the seven settlements. `Pasavati` means it is possible. It is said: 'Because things such as "they are found in a legal issue of accusation" are similar to things such as "Dhamma, not-Dhamma," they are found specifically in those cases.' `Anihaṭa` means by the Sutta, etc. `Avinicchita` means by 'offense, no-offense,' etc. 'There, one reopens a legal issue that has arisen... one reopens a case settled by covering with grass'—thus only ten are stated. It is written: 'Because it is not stated, it is not possible to reopen cases settled by procedure-in-the-presence, acceptance of the claim, and decision by majority; for them there is also no formal act. Therefore, they say, it is not possible to reopen them.' Regarding 'by a decision apart from the Pāḷi alone': the meaning is, without the characteristic of the Vinaya, merely by the power of a Dhamma teaching alone. Or by a sutta brought from the Khandhaka or from the Parivāra. `Nijjhāpenti` means they explain, they show. The meaning is: having explained things such as 'not-Dhamma as Dhamma' for the sake of preceptors, etc., regarding a legal issue previously decided by the Dhamma and Vinaya. Because of relying on unbalanced bodily actions, etc., it is called `visamanissito` (relying on the unbalanced). It should be understood thus in the remaining cases.

Adhikaraṇanidānādivaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Origin of Legal Issues and so forth

342-3. Kiṃsambhāranti kiṃparikkhāraṃ, ettha kinti liṅgasāmaññamabyayaṃ. Pubbe uppannavivādaṃ nissāya pacchā uppajjanakavivādo vivādanidānaṃ nāma. Āpattādhikaraṇapaccayā catasso āpattiyo āpajjatīti bhikkhunī jānaṃ pārājikaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicchādeti pārājikaṃ, vematikā paṭicchādeti thullaccayaṃ, bhikkhu saṅghādisesaṃ paṭicchādeti pācittiyaṃ, ācāravipattiṃ paṭicchādeti dukkaṭaṃ. Pubbe kataukkhepaniyādikiccaṃ nissāya uppajjanakakiccānaṃ. Kīdisānaṃ? Samanubhāsanādīnaṃ vasena. Taṃ hīti adhikaraṇaṃ.

342-3. 'Kiṃsambhāraṃ' means 'what are the requisites' (kiṃparikkhāraṃ). Herein, the word 'kiṃ' is an indeclinable of general gender. A dispute that arises later, based on a dispute that has arisen previously, is called the origin of disputes. Due to the condition of a legal issue concerning an offense, one falls into four offenses: if a bhikkhunī, knowing, conceals a pārājika matter, she incurs a pārājika offense; if, being doubtful, she conceals it, she incurs a thullaccaya offense; if a bhikkhu conceals a saṅghādisesa offense, he incurs a pācittiya offense; if one conceals a corruption of conduct, one incurs a dukkaṭa offense. This concerns duties that are to arise based on previously performed acts such as suspension. Of what kind? By way of duties such as formal admonition, etc. Herein, `taṃ hi` refers to the legal issue.

344. Adhikaraṇesu yena adhikaraṇena sammanti, taṃ dassetunti yadā adhikaraṇehi sammanti, tadā kiccādhikaraṇeneva sammanti, na aññehīti [M 0.0570] dassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ, na ekantato adhikaraṇeneva sammantīti dassanatthaṃ.

344. To show by which legal issue among legal issues they are settled: when they are settled from legal issues, they are settled by the legal issue concerning procedure alone, not by others—this was stated to show this, not to show that they are settled absolutely by a legal issue alone.

348. Āpattādhikaraṇe [V 0.0521] saṅgho vivadatīti āpattānāpattīti evaṃ.

348. When the Saṅgha disputes about a legal issue concerning an offense, it disputes thus: 'Is it an offense or not an offense?'

353. Samuṭṭhānābhāvato sammukhāvinaye kammassa kiriyākaraṇamiccādinā avibhajitvāva sativinayādīnaṃ channaṃyeva cha samuṭṭhānāni vibhattāni. Taṃ kasmā? Kammasaṅgahābhāvena, sativinayādīnaṃ viya saṅghasammukhatādīnaṃ kiccayatā nāma natthīti adhippāyo.

353. Due to the absence of an origin, and without analyzing the `sammukhāvinaya` by way of 'the performance of an act,' and so forth, the six origins of only the six settlements beginning with `sativinaya` have been analyzed. Why is that? The meaning is this: due to the absence of the inclusion of a formal act, there is no such thing as a functional requirement for matters such as the presence of the Saṅgha, unlike for the settlements beginning with `sativinaya`.

Adhikaraṇabhedavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Kinds of Legal Issues is Concluded.

Dutiyagāthāsaṅgaṇikavaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Second Verse Collection

Codanādipucchāvissajjanāvaṇṇanā

Explanation of Questions and Answers Beginning with Accusation

359. Viggāhikakathanti attho. Nisāmayāti sallakkhehi. “Kāraya” iti pāṭho. Pubbāparaṃ na jānāti, tasmā akovido hotīti eke. Ayaṃ pana duvidhepi kicce kenaci iriyāpathena.

359. 'Viggāhikakathā' means 'contentious speech'. 'Nisāmaya' means 'mark well'. There is also the reading 'kāraya'. Some say: "Because he does not know the antecedent and consequent, therefore he is unskilled." But this monk, in both kinds of duties, by some posture.

Codanākaṇḍavaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Chapter on Accusation

Anuvijjakakiccavaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Examiner's Duty

360. Anuvijjakapucchane ājīvavipatti na pucchitā. Pañcāpattikkhandhavasena ācāravipatti pucchitā. “Ājīvavipattiyāpi tatheva, saṅgahagamanato”ti vadanti. “Ajjhāpajjanto”ti pāṭho.

360. In questioning the examiner, corruption of livelihood is not asked about. Corruption of conduct is asked about in terms of the five aggregates of offenses. They say: “Corruption of livelihood is also included right there [in corruption of conduct], due to its inclusion.” There is also the reading 'ajjhāpajjanto'.

363. Tasmā na ca āmisaṃ nissāyāti sambandhitabbaṃ.

363. Therefore, it should be connected with 'na ca āmisaṃ nissāya'.

Cūḷasaṅgāmavaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Minor Conflict

365. Ṭhānanisajjavatthādinissitāti [V 0.0522][M 0.0571] “evaṃ ṭhātabbaṃ evaṃ nisīditabba”nti evamādikā. Saññājananatthanti “evaṃ vattabba”nti evaṃ sañjānanatthaṃ. Anuvidhiyantenāti citte ṭhapentenāti attho. Lajjā sā nu khoti kiṃ sā lajjā ayaṃ parisāti adhippāyo. Anuyogavattaṃ kathāpetvāti “kimanuyogavattaṃ jānāsī”ti pucchitvā teneva kathāpetvā. Ajānanappasaṅgā nāma aññāṇaṃ.

365. `Ṭhānanisajjavatthādinissitā` means: 'One should stand thus, one should sit thus,' and so on. `Saññājananatthaṃ` means: for the purpose of knowing, 'Thus it should be said.' `Anuvidhiyantena` means: by placing it in the mind. Regarding `Lajjā sā nu kho`, the intention is: 'Why does this assembly have such shame?' Regarding `Anuyogavattaṃ kathāpetvā`: Having asked, 'Do you know the duty of interrogation?' and having made him speak on that very topic. `Ajānanappasaṅgā` means ignorance.

367. “Bhayena bhayā gacchatī”ti bhayena bhayahetu bhayā gacchatīti hetuvasena vuttaṃ. Yathā “rattattā pana duṭṭhattā ca chandā dosā ca gacchatī”ti hi vuttaṃ, evaṃ.

367. Regarding 'Bhayena bhayā gacchati': `bhayena` means because of the cause that is fear; `bhayā gacchati` means one goes out of fear. This is stated in a causal sense. Just as it is said, 'One goes out of desire and out of aversion, because of being lustful and because of being malevolent,' so it is stated here.

403-4. Kinti [V 0.0523][M 0.0572] kathaṃ. Anādiyadānaṃ tāvakālikavatthu. “Anāgatavasena anantarā hutvā”ti udakāharaṇādipayogassa dhovanādipubbakaraṇassa pacchā uppajjanato, dhovanādikiriyañca sandhāya payogakaraṇato vuttaṃ. Purejātapaccaye panesa payogoti attho. Ekaṃ dhammampi na labhati attano purejātassa natthitāya.

`Kinti` should be understood to mean `kathaṃ` (how). `Anādiyadānaṃ` (a gift not taken first) is a temporary matter. Regarding 'being immediate in terms of the future': this is said because it arises after the preliminary act of washing, etc., which is associated with the application of fetching water, etc., and it is said with reference to the action of washing, etc., because of the performance of the application. But in the case of the pre-nascence condition, this is the application; this is the meaning. One does not obtain even one thing because of the non-existence of one's own pre-nascent basis.

Palibodhapañhābyākaraṇakathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Discourse on Answering Questions about Obstructions

415-6. Sanniṭṭhānantiko kathaṃ bahisīmāya uddharīyati? Bhikkhu akatacīvaraṃ samādāya pakkamati “na paccessa”nti, tassa bahisīmāgatassa evaṃ hoti “nevimaṃ cīvaraṃ kāressa”nti, evametassa bahisīmāgatassa uddharīyati. Kathaṃ antosīmāya? Akatacīvaraṃ samādāya pakkamati “na paccessa”nti, tato tattha phāsuvihāraṃ alabhanto tameva vihāraṃ āgacchati, tassa cīvarapalibodhoyeva ṭhito, so ca “nevimaṃ cīvaraṃ kāressa”nti citte uppanne chijjati, tasmā “antosīmāya uddharīyatī”ti vuttaṃ. Sanniṭṭhānantikaṃ duvidhaṃ “na paccessa”nti āvāsapalibodhaṃ chinditvā tato punapi tameva vihāraṃ āgantvā “nevimaṃ cīvaraṃ kāressa”nti sanniṭṭhānaṃ karoti, bahisīmāya ṭhatvā “nevimaṃ cīvaraṃ kāressaṃ na paccessa”nti cittuppādena sanniṭṭhānantikaṃ hoti. Gāthāyampi “dve palibodhā apubbaṃ acarima”nti [V 0.0524] idaṃ imameva sandhāya. “Āsāvacchediko kathaṃ antosīmāya[M 0.0573]? Āsīsitena ‘tumhe vihārameva patthetha, ahaṃ pahiṇissāmī’ti vutto pubbe ‘na paccessa’nti āvāsapalibodhaṃ chinditvā gato puna taṃ vihāraṃ gantvā tena ‘nāhaṃ sakkomi dātu’nti pahito hotī”ti likhitaṃ. “Atthāre hi sati uddhāro nāmā”ti atthāraṃ vinā uddhāraṃ na labhanti, tasmā vuttaṃ. Purimā dveti “dve kathinuddhārā ekuppādā ekanirodhā”ti vuttādhikāre paṭhamaṃ vuttā antarabbhārasahubbhārā. Na pakkamanantikādayo dve. Ekato nirujjhantīti uddhārabhāvaṃ pāpuṇantīti attho.

How is the sanniṭṭhānantika (determination-ending withdrawal) revoked outside the boundary? A bhikkhu, taking an unmade robe, departs thinking, 'I will not return.' For that bhikkhu who has gone outside the boundary, the thought arises thus: 'I will not make this robe.' Thus, for that one who has gone outside the boundary, it is revoked. How is it revoked inside the boundary? Taking an unmade robe, he departs thinking, 'I will not return.' Then, not obtaining a comfortable dwelling there, he returns to that same monastery. For him, the robe-impediment still stands. And that impediment is severed when the thought, 'I will not make this robe,' arises. Therefore, it is said, 'It is revoked inside the boundary.' The sanniṭṭhānantika is twofold: (1) having severed the residence-impediment by thinking, 'I will not return,' and then having returned to that same monastery, he makes the determination, 'I will not make this robe.' (2) While standing outside the boundary, the sanniṭṭhānantika occurs with the arising of the thought, 'I will not make this robe; I will not return.' In the verse too, this saying, 'The two impediments, neither preceding nor succeeding,' is said with reference to just this. How is the āsāvacchedika (hope-severing withdrawal) revoked inside the boundary? It is written: 'A bhikkhu, who was previously told by one who had expressed a wish, "You should desire the monastery itself; I will send it," having severed the residence-impediment by thinking, "I will not return," departed. Later, having gone to that monastery again, he is sent a message by that person, saying, "I am unable to give it."' 'For when there is the spreading, there is the withdrawal' means that without the spreading, they do not obtain the withdrawal; therefore, it is said. 'The first two' means: in the section where it is said, 'Two kathina withdrawals, of single arising, of single cessation,' the antarubbhāra (withdrawal during the interval) and sahubbhāra (simultaneous withdrawal), which were mentioned first, are meant. The two beginning with pakkamanantika (departure-ending) are not meant. 'They cease together' means they reach the state of withdrawal; this is the meaning.

The Explanation of the Chapter on Conventional Usage.

424. Bhedakaravatthūni nissāya vivādādhikaraṇaṃ samuṭṭhāti, evaṃ yathāsaṅkhyaṃ gacchati. Kodhopanāhādidvādasamūlapayogaṃ vivādādhikaraṇaṃ, tathā sesesu. Osāraṇādīsu navasu ṭhānesu kammañattiyā karaṇaṃ. Dvīsu ṭhānesu ñattidutiyañatticatutthakammesu. Yasmā mahāaṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttanayeneva ubhatovibhaṅgā asaṅgahitā, tasmā yaṃ kurundiyaṃ vuttaṃ, taṃ gahetabbanti sambandho.

424. A legal issue of dispute arises based on grounds for schism; thus it proceeds according to the number. The application of the twelve roots beginning with anger and hostility is a legal issue of dispute; similarly for the remaining cases. In the nine instances beginning with rehabilitation, the procedure is done by the motion for a formal act. In two instances, it is done in acts with a motion and one announcement, and acts with a motion and three announcements. Because, by the method stated in the Great Commentary, both Vibhaṅgas are not included, therefore what is stated in the Kurundī commentary should be taken; this is how the connection should be made.

467. “Ekāvatto”tipi [V 0.0526] paṭhanti, tassa kuddho kodhābhibhūtoti kirattho. Ekavatthotipi keci, uttarāsaṅgaṃ apanetvā ṭhitoti kirattho, taṃ sabbaṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ uddhaṭapāḷiyā virujjhatīti. 467. Some also read it as `ekāvatto`; its meaning, it is said, is 'angry, overcome by anger.' Some also read it as `ekavattho`; its meaning, it is said, is 'standing having removed the upper robe.' All of that contradicts the Pāli text cited in the commentary. For `ekāvaṭo` is indeed what is cited; therefore, this should not be accepted. Herein, regarding the phrase 'due to the reason stated in between': it refers to the reason stated, beginning with, 'Because of being preoccupied with some duty, while not paying attention to paying homage, one might strike one's forehead.'

474-5. Nidānuddesaṃ [M 0.0576] vinā sesuddesābhāvā “sabbapātimokkhuddesānañca saṅgaho hotī”ti vuttaṃ. Vinaye garukā vinayagarukā. Idaṃ pana dvīsu gāthāsu kiñcāpi āgataṃ, aññehi pana missetvā vuttabhāvā nānākaraṇaṃ paccetabbaṃ. Navasu ṭhānesu kammaṃ hotīti kammañatti hoti. Vācāti vacīsambhavā. Addhānahīno ūnavīsativasso. “Apicetthāti kurundivādo”ti vuttaṃ. Vanappatinti evaṃ adinnādāne āgataṃ vanappatiṃ. Vissaṭṭhichaḍḍaneti sukkavissaṭṭhiyaṃ. Dukkaṭā katāti dukkaṭaṃ vuttaṃ. Āmakadhaññaṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjantiyā pubbapayoge dukkaṭaṃ, ajjhohāre pācittiyaṃ.

474–475. Because there is no other exposition apart from the fundamental exposition, it is said, “It is a collection of all the Pātimokkha expositions.” `Vinayagarukā` means reverence for the Vinaya. Although this has come up in two verses, because it is stated mixed with other terms, a distinction should be understood. The phrase “an act occurs in nine instances” means it is a formal act of the Sangha. `Vācā` means arising from speech. `Addhānahīno` means one who is less than twenty years of age. It is said, “As for `apicettha`, it is the Kurundi view.” As for `vanappati`, it is the `vanappati` that comes in the section on taking what is not given. As for `vissaṭṭhichaḍḍana`, it means in the case of emission of semen. As for `dukkaṭā katā`, it means a `dukkaṭa` offense is stated. For a bhikkhunī who eats raw grain after having requested it, there is a `dukkaṭa` offense in the preliminary effort, and a `pācittiya` offense upon swallowing.

Pācittiyavaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Pācittiya Offenses

476. Mahāsaṅghikā [V 0.0527] sāmaṇerepi āpattiṃ desāpenti kira, tena vuttaṃ “na desāpetabbā”ti, daṇḍakammaṃ pana tesaṃ kātabbaṃ tathārūpe oḷārikavītikkame.

476. The Mahāsaṅghikas, it is said, make even novices confess offenses; for that reason it is stated, “They should not be made to confess.” However, a punitive act should be carried out for them in the case of such a gross transgression.

Avandanīyapuggalādivaṇṇanā

477. Dasasataṃ āpattiyoti sahassaṃ āpattiyo. Campāyaṃ vinayavatthusminti campeyyakkhandhake. Adhammena vaggantiādīni cattāri kammāniyeva bhagavatā vuttānīti attho. Na kevalaṃ āpattiyeva, atha kho cha samathā…pe… sammukhāvinayena sammanti, samāyogaṃ gacchanti sammukhāvinayena sampayogaṃ gacchantīti attho. Vinā samathehi sammati, samathabhāvaṃ gacchati. Paṭisedhatthe sati vinā samathehīti samathehi vināti attho.

477. `Dasasataṃ āpattiyo` means a thousand offenses. `Campāyaṃ vinayavatthusmiṃ` means in the Campeyya-khandhaka. The meaning is that only the four formal acts beginning with `adhammena vagga` were stated by the Blessed One. Not only an offense, but rather the six settlements... are settled by the procedure of being face-to-face; the meaning is that they reach association and connection by the procedure of being face-to-face. It is settled without the settlements; it reaches a state of settlement. When `vinā` has the meaning of prohibition, `vinā samathehi` means 'apart from the settlements.'

Soḷasakammādivaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Sixteen Formal Acts, and so on

478. Asuttakanti suttavirahitaṃ, usuttaṃ tatra natthīti adhippāyo.

478. The term `asuttakaṃ` means devoid of a sutta; the intended meaning is that there is nothing therein that is not from the suttas.

Sedamocanagāthāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Sweat-Inducing Verses

Avippavāsapañhāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Questions on Non-Separation

479. Tahinti [M 0.0577] tasmiṃ puggale. Akappiyasambhogo nāma methunadhammādi. “Varasenāsanarakkhaṇatthāya vissajjetvā paribhuñjituṃ vaṭṭatī”ti garubhaṇḍavinicchaye vutto. Ekādasāvandiye paṇḍakādayo ekādasa. Upeti saparisaṃ. Na jīvati nimmitarūpattā. “Ubbhakkhakena vadāmī”ti iminā mukhe methunadhammābhāvaṃ dīpeti. Adhonābhivivajjanena vaccamaggappassāvamaggesu[V 0.0528]. Gāmantarapariyāpannaṃ nadipāraṃ okkantabhikkhuniṃ sandhāyāti bhikkhuniyā gāmāpariyāpannaparatīre nadisamīpameva sandhāya vuttā. Tattha paratīre gāmūpacāro ekaleḍḍupāto nadipariyantena paricchinno, tasmā paratīre ratanamattampi araññaṃ na atthi, tañca tiṇādīhi paṭicchannattā dassanūpacāravirahitaṃ karoti. Tattha attano gāme āpatti natthi. Paratīre pana ekaleḍḍupātasaṅkhāte gāmūpacāreyeva padaṃ ṭhapeti. Antare abhidhammavasena araññabhūtaṃ sakagāmaṃ atikkamati nāma, tasmā gaṇamhā ohīyanā ca hotīti ñātabbaṃ. Ettāvatāpi santosamakatvā vicāretvā gahetabbaṃ. Bhikkhūnaṃ santike upasampannā pañcasatā mahāpajāpatippamukhā. Mahāpajāpatipi hi ānandattherena dinnaovādassa paṭiggahitattā bhikkhūnaṃ santike upasampannā nāma.

479. `Tahiṃ` refers to that person. `Akappiyasambhogo` means improper association, such as sexual intercourse and so forth. The statement 'For the sake of protecting the excellent lodging, having relinquished it, it is allowable to use it' is stated in the Garubhaṇḍavinicchaya. The eleven unworthy of veneration are the eleven beginning with the paṇḍaka. `Upeti saparisaṃ` means one approaches with one's retinue. `Na jīvati` means it does not live, because it is a created form. By the phrase `Ubbhakkhakena vadāmi`, it indicates the absence of sexual intercourse in the mouth. `Adhonābhivivajjanena` means by avoiding what is below the navel, in the paths for excrement and urine. The phrase 'referring to a bhikkhunī who has crossed to the far bank of a river that is included in another village' is said with reference to a bhikkhunī in the vicinity of the river on the far bank that is included in the village. There, on the far bank, the village precinct is a single clod's throw, defined by the riverbank. Therefore, on the far bank, there is not even a cubit's measure of wilderness, and that, being covered by grass and so forth, is rendered outside the range of sight. In one's own village, there is no offense. On the far bank, however, one places one's foot only in the village precinct, which is designated as a single clod's throw. In between, according to the higher teaching, this is called transgressing one's own village which has become wilderness. Therefore, it should be known that one is also left behind by the group. Even with this much, one should not be content but should grasp it after investigation. The five hundred bhikkhunīs headed by Mahāpajāpatī were ordained in the presence of the bhikkhus. Indeed, Mahāpajāpatī, because of having accepted the exhortation given by the Elder Ānanda, is called 'ordained in the presence of the bhikkhus'.

Pārājikādipañhāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Questions on the Pārājika and So Forth

480. “Dussakuṭiṃ sandhāyā”ti saha dussena vītikkamanassa sakkuṇeyyatāya vuttaṃ. Liṅgaparivatte paṭiggahaṇassa vijahanato sāmaṃ gahetvā bhuñjituṃ na vaṭṭati. Kākaūhadanaṃ vāti kākena ūhadanaṃ vā. “Tayo purisepi upagantvā”ti pāṭhaseso.

480. The phrase 'referring to the cloth dwelling' is said because of the possibility of transgressing together with the cloth. In the case of a change of gender, because of the abandoning of formal acceptance, it is not proper to take and eat it oneself. 'Or what is left by a crow' means what is left over by a crow. The remainder of the text is 'having approached even three men'.

Pācittiyādipañhāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Questions on the Pācittiya and So Forth

481. Methunadhammapaccayā nāma kāyasaṃsaggo. Taṃhetu methunadhammassa pubbabhāgabhūtaṃ kāyasaṃsaggaṃ vāyāmantiyāti aṭṭhavatthupūraṇaṃ sandhāya. Paribhogappaccayāti [M 0.0578] paribhogakāraṇā. Tasmāti yasmā paribhogappaccayā āpajjati, tasmā bhojanapariyosāne hotīti attho. Porāṇapotthakesu “tassā”ti pāṭho. “Kāraṇavacanaṃ sundaraṃ bhojanaparicchedadassanato”ti vadanti.

481. What is called 'due to the condition of sexual intercourse' is bodily contact. On account of that reason, it is said with reference to the completion of the eight bases of one who strives for bodily contact, which is the preliminary part of sexual intercourse. 'Due to the condition of use' means because of the reason of using. Therefore, since one incurs an offense due to the condition of use, it happens at the end of the meal—this is the meaning. In the ancient books, there is the reading 'tassā'. They say: 'The word stating the reason is fitting, because it indicates the limit of the meal.'

Sedamocanagāthāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Sedamocanagāthā is concluded.

Pañcavaggo

The Fifth Section

Kammavaggavaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Chapter on Kamma

483. “Ummattakasammutiṃ [V 0.0529][M 0.0579] ummattake yācitvā gate asammukhāpi dātuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti vuttaṃ. Tattha nisinnepi na kuppati niyamābhāvā. Asammukhā kate dosābhāvaṃ dassetuṃ “asammukhākataṃ sukataṃ hotī”ti vuttaṃ. Dūtena upasampadā panettha sammukhā kātuṃ na sakkā. Kammavācānānattasabhāvā pattanikkujjanādayo hatthapāsato apanetvā kātabbā, tena vuttaṃ “asammukhā kataṃ sukataṃ hotī”ti. “Pucchitvā codetvā sāretvā kātabbaṃ apucchitvā acodetvā asāretvā karotī”ti ayaṃ vacanattho. Ṭhapetvā kattikamāsanti so pavāraṇāmāso, dve ca puṇṇamāsiyoti paṭhamadutiyavassūpagatānaṃ pavāraṇā puṇṇamāsā dve.

483. It is said: 'Regarding the formal designation of insanity, when the insane monk has requested it and departed, it is allowable to grant it even in his absence.' In that case, even if he is seated, it is not invalidated, because of the absence of a fixed rule. To show there is no fault when it is done in his absence, it is said: 'What is done in absence is well done.' Herein, however, ordination by a messenger cannot be done in person. Because of the diverse nature of the formal acts, procedures such as overturning the bowl must be performed after removing him from within arm's reach; therefore it is said: 'What is done in absence is well done.' The meaning of the statement is: 'It should be done after questioning, admonishing, and reminding; but he does it without questioning, without admonishing, and without reminding.' 'Except for the month of Kattika'—that is the Pavāraṇā month. 'And the two full moons'—for those who have entered upon the first and second rains-retreats, the Pavāraṇā full moons are two.

485. Padaṃ vā chaḍḍetīti attho. Ka-vaggādīsu pañcasu. Garukanti dīghaṃ, saṃyogaparañca. “Buddharakkhitattherassa yassa nakkhamatī”ti ettha ta-kāraka-kārā saṃyogaparā. Dīghe vattabbe rassanti “so tuṇhī assā”ti vattabbe so tuṇhi assāti vacanaṃ.

485. 'Or he omits a word'—this is the meaning. In the five classes, beginning with the Ka-class. A 'heavy' syllable is a long one or one followed by a conjunct consonant. In the phrase 'For the Elder Buddharakkhita, who does not approve,' the letters 'ta' and 'ka' are followed by a conjunct consonant. When a long vowel should be said, a short one is said. When 'so tuṇhī assā' (he should be silent) should be said, the statement is 'so tuṇhi assā'.

486. Sesaṭṭhakathāsu vuttavacanaṃ kurundiyaṃ pākaṭaṃ katvā “nisīdituṃ na sakkontī”ti vuttaṃ.

486. Having made clear in the Kurundī commentary a statement made in the remaining commentaries, it is said: 'They are not able to sit down.'

487-8. Parisuddhasīlā cattāro bhikkhūti pārājikaṃ anāpannā. Na tesaṃ chando vā pārisuddhi vā etīti tīsu, dvīsu vā nisinnesu ekassa, dvinnaṃ vā chandapārisuddhi āhaṭāpi anāhaṭāva.

'Four monks of pure virtue' means monks who have not incurred a pārājika offense. As for 'Neither their consent nor their purity is present': when three or two monks are seated, the consent and purity of one or of two, even if brought, are as if not brought.

Apalokanakammakathāvaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Discourse on the Act of Announcement

495-6. Kāyasambhogasāmaggidānasahaseyyapaṭiggahaṇādi imassa apalokanakammassa ṭhānaṃ hotīti evampi apalokanakammaṃ pavattatīti attho. Kammaññeva lakkhaṇanti kammalakkhaṇaṃ. Osāraṇanissāraṇabhaṇḍukammādayo viya kammañca hutvā aññañca nāmaṃ na labhati[V 0.0530], kammameva hutvā upalakkhīyatīti [M 0.0580] kammalakkhaṇaṃ upanissayo viya. Hetupaccayādilakkhaṇavimutto hi sabbo paccayaviseso tattha saṅgayhati, evampi “kammalakkhaṇamevā”ti vuttaṃ. Kammalakkhaṇaṃ dassetuṃ “acchinnacīvarajiṇṇacīvaranaṭṭhacīvarāna”ntiādi vuttaṃ. “Tato atirekaṃ dentena apaloketvā dātabba”nti vuttaṃ apalokanaṃ kammalakkhaṇameva. Evaṃ sabbattha lakkhaṇaṃ veditabbaṃ. Iṇapalibodhampīti sace tādisaṃ bhikkhuṃ iṇāyikā palibujjhanti. Tatruppādato dātuṃ vaṭṭati. Antarasannipātoti uposathappavāraṇādimahāsannipāte ṭhapetvā antarā maṅgaluccāraṇādi. Upanikkhepatoti cetiyassa āpadatthāya nikkhittato. “Aññā katikā kātabbā”ti ye rukkhe uddissa pubbe katikā katā, tehi imesaṃ aññattāti vuttaṃ. “Sace tattha mūle”ti pubbe “ito paṭṭhāya bhājetvā khādantū”ti vacanena puggalikaparibhogo paṭikkhitto hoti. Anuvicaritvāti pacchato pacchato gantvā. Tesaṃ santikā paccayaṃ paccāsīsantenāti attho. Mūlabhāganti dasamabhāgaṃ katvā. Pubbakāle dasamabhāgaṃ katvā adaṃsu, tasmā “mūlabhāgo”ti vuttaṃ. Akatāvāsaṃ vā katvāti uppannaāyena. Jaggitakāleyeva na vāretabbāti jaggitā hutvā pupphaphalabharitakāleti attho. Jagganakāleti jaggituṃ āraddhakāle. Ñattikammaṭṭhānabhede panāti ñattikammassa ṭhānabhede.

The sharing of bodily requisites, the giving of communal items, the sharing of a lodging, the acceptance of things, and so on, is the basis for this act of announcement; thus, the act of announcement also proceeds in this way—this is the meaning. The act itself is the characteristic; therefore, it is called 'the characteristic of an act'. Like the acts of rehabilitation, expulsion, the act concerning a pederast, and so on, being an act, it does not receive another name; being just an act, it is designated as such, and therefore it is called 'the characteristic of an act', like a decisive support condition. For indeed, every specific condition that is free from the characteristics of a root-condition and so on is included therein; in the same way, it is said, “It is just the characteristic of an act.” To show the characteristic of an act, it is said, “for those with stolen robes, worn-out robes, or lost robes,” and so on. The announcement stated as, “What is in excess of that should be given after making an announcement,” is itself the characteristic of an act. In this way, the characteristic should be understood in all cases. As for “debt and obstruction”: if creditors trouble such a monk, it is allowable to give from what has been produced there. As for “an interim assembly”: setting aside the great assemblies for Uposatha, Pavāraṇā, and so on, it is an assembly in between for the recitation of auspicious verses, etc. As for “a deposit”: it means because of being placed near a cetiya for use in a calamity. As for “Another agreement should be made”: it is said because these trees are different from those trees concerning which an agreement was previously made. As for “If at the root there”: by the earlier statement, “From this point on, let them divide and eat,” personal use is prohibited. As for “having followed”: it means going behind, behind; the meaning is, by one who is expecting requisites from them. As for “the root portion”: it means having made it a tenth part. In former times, they gave after making it a tenth part; therefore, it is called “the root portion.” As for 'or having made a dwelling where none existed': this means with the income that has arisen. As for “should not be prevented during the time of tending”: the meaning is, at the time when, having been tended, the trees are laden with flowers and fruit. As for “at the time of tending”: it means at the time of beginning to tend. As for “in the distinction of the basis for an act with a motion”: it means in the distinction of the basis of the act with a motion.

Idaṃ panettha pakiṇṇakaṃ – atthi saṅghakammaṃ saṅgho eva karoti, na gaṇo, na puggalo, taṃ apalokanakammassa kammalakkhaṇekadesaṃ ṭhapetvā itaraṃ catubbidhampi kammaṃ veditabbaṃ. Atthi saṅghakammaṃ saṅgho ca karoti, gaṇo ca karoti, puggalo ca karoti, taṃ pubbe ṭhapitaṃ. Vuttañhetaṃ “yasmiṃ vihāre dve tayo janā vasanti, tehi nisīditvā katampi saṅghena katasadisameva. Yasmiṃ pana vihāre eko bhikkhu hoti, tena bhikkhunā”tiādi (pari. aṭṭha. 495-496). Atthi gaṇakammaṃ saṅgho ca karoti, gaṇo ca karoti, puggalo ca karoti, taṃ yo pārisuddhiuposatho aññesaṃ santike karīyati, tassa vasena veditabbaṃ. Atthi gaṇakammaṃ gaṇova karoti, na saṅgho, na puggalo, taṃ yo pārisuddhiuposatho aññamaññaṃ ārocanavasena karīyati, tassa vasena veditabbaṃ. Atthi puggalakammaṃ puggalova karoti, na saṅgho, na gaṇo, taṃ adhiṭṭhānuposathavasena [M 0.0581] veditabbaṃ. Atthi gaṇakammaṃ ekaccova gaṇo karoti, ekacco na karoti, tattha añattikaṃ dveyeva karonti, na tayo. Sañattikaṃ tayova karonti, na tato ūnā vā adhikā vāti.

Herein, this is the miscellaneous section: There is an act of the Saṅgha that only the Saṅgha performs, not a group, not an individual; that, setting aside a part of the characteristic of an act of announcement, should be understood as the other four kinds of acts. There is an act of the Saṅgha that the Saṅgha performs, a group performs, and an individual performs; that has been established previously. For it has been said: “In whatever monastery two or three persons reside, an act done by them sitting together is just like one done by the Saṅgha. But in whatever monastery there is one monk, by that monk…” and so on. There is an act of a group that the Saṅgha performs, a group performs, and an individual performs; that should be understood by way of the purity-Uposatha performed in the presence of others. There is an act of a group that only a group performs, not the Saṅgha, not an individual; that should be understood by way of the purity-Uposatha performed through mutual declaration. There is an act of an individual that only an individual performs, not the Saṅgha, not a group; that should be understood by way of the determination-Uposatha. There is an act of a group that a certain group performs, and a certain group does not. Therein, an act without a motion is performed by only two, not three. An act with a motion is performed by only three, not fewer or more than that.

Apaññattepaññattavaggavaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Chapter of the Unprescribed and the Prescribed

500. Kakusandhakoṇāgamanakassapā [V 0.0531] eva hi satta āpattikkhandhe paññapesuṃ. Vipassīādayo pana ovādapātimokkhaṃ uddisiṃsu, na sikkhāpadaṃ paññapesuṃ.

500. For only Kakusandha, Koṇāgamana, and Kassapa laid down the seven groups of offenses. But Vipassī and the others recited the Ovāda-pātimokkha; they did not lay down the training rules.

Nigamanakathāvaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Concluding Discourse

Ubhatovibhaṅgakhandhakaparivārehi vibhattaṃ desanaṃ atthi tassa vinayapiṭakassa, nāmena samantapāsādikā nāma saṃvaṇṇanā “samantapāsādikā nāmā”ti vuttavacanasaṃvaṇṇanā samattāti āha. Tattha padhānaghare. Iddhā atthavinicchayādīhi.

Of that Vinaya Piṭaka, there is the teaching divided by the two Vibhaṅgas, the Khandhakas, and the Parivāra. He says that the commentary named Samantapāsādikā, which is the explanation of the spoken phrase 'named Samantapāsādikā', is complete. There, in the Padhānaghara monastery, it was accomplished by means of the determination of meanings and so forth.

Sammā udito samudito, te guṇe akicchena adhigato adhikappamāṇaguṇehi vā samudito, tena samuditena “gatānaṃ dhammānaṃ gatiyo samannesatī”ti vuttāya satiyā uppāditā saddhādayo paramavisuddhā nāma samannārakkhattā. Iti satipi saddhādīhi vuttā hoti. Evaṃ sante ettha vutte catubbidhe sīle pātimokkhasaṃvarasīlaṃ saddhā maṇḍeti. Saddhāsādhanañhi taṃ. Indriyasaṃvarājīvapārisuddhipaccayaparibhogasīlāni paṭimaṇḍenti sativīriyapaññāyoti yathāyogaṃ veditabbaṃ. Apica saddhā ca buddhirahitā avisuddhā hoti buddhiyā pasādahetuttā. Buddhiyo pana tassānubhāvena paramavisuddhā nāma honti. Paññā saddhārahitā kerāṭikapakkhaṃ bhajati, saddhāyuttā eva visuddhā hoti. Vīriyañca samādhirahitaṃ uddhaccāya saṃvattati, na samādhiyuttanti vīriyassa suddhavacanato samādhipi vutto hoti, evaṃ paramavisuddhā saddhādayopi pātimokkhaṃ paṭimaṇḍentīti ñātabbaṃ. Kathaṃ? Paṭipattidesake satthari ca paṭipattiyañca paṭipattiphale ca saddhāya vinā sīlasamādānaṃ, samādinnavisodhanañca kātuṃ na sakkāti saddhā pātimokkhaṃ paṭimaṇḍeti. Tattha “itipi so [M 0.0582] bhagavā”tiādinā (dī. ni. 1.255; ma. ni. 1.74; saṃ. ni. 1.249) satthari ca pūjetuṃ sakkoti. Paṭipattiyaṃ sīlavipattisampattimūlake sandiṭṭhikasamparāyikaphale ca saddhāpavatti vitthārato ñātabbā, sīlavipattisampattinimittaṃ ādīnavamānisaṃsañca ādīnavapariccāge, ānisaṃsasampādane ca upāyaṃ disvā tathā pavattamānā paññā pātimokkhasaṃvaraṃ paṭimaṇḍeti. “Atisīta”ntiādinā appavattanārahaṃ kosajjaṃ “yo ca sītañca uṇhañcā”ti vuttānusārena pajahitvā anuppannuppannānaṃ asaṃvarasaṃvarānaṃ anuppādanapajahanauppādanavaḍḍhanavasena pavattamānavīriyaṃ pātimokkhaṃ paṭimaṇḍeti, iminā nayena indriyasaṃvarādīsupi yojetabbaṃ. Catunnampi [V 0.0532] saṅgahavatthūnaṃ anukūlasamudācāro idha ācāroti veditabbo. Ajjava-vacanena lābhasakkārahetu kāyaduccaritādikuṭilakaramāyāsāṭheyyapaṭipakkhaajjavadhammasamāyogadīpanena alobhajjhāsayatā dīpitā. Maddava-vacanena kakkhaḷabhāvakarapaṭighādipaṭipakkhabhūtamettādimaddavadhammasamāyogadīpanena hitajjhāsayādīni dīpitāni honti. Ādi-saddena “khanti ca soraccañca sākhalyañca paṭisanthāro cā”tiādinā (dha. sa. dukamātikā 125-126) vuttadhammehi samāyogo dīpito hoti. Idha vuttā ajjavamaddavādayo guṇā sīlasampattiyā hetū ca honti sīlasampattiphalañca taṃsampādanato. Sakasamayoti catuparisā. Etena sabhāgadukkhabhāvābhāvo sūcito. Atha vā sakasamayoti sogataṃ piṭakattayaṃ sakasamayo eva gahanaṃ duddīpanattā, sakasamayassa sanniṭṭhānaṃ sakasamayagahanaṃ –

Well arisen, fully arisen; those qualities are attained without difficulty, or are fully arisen through qualities of exceeding measure. By that arisen state, faith and so forth—produced by mindfulness which is said to 'seek the courses of phenomena that have occurred'—are called supremely pure because they are completely guarded. Thus, mindfulness is also spoken of along with faith and so forth. This being so, in the fourfold virtue mentioned here, faith adorns the virtue of Pātimokkha restraint, for it is indeed accomplished by faith. The virtues of sense restraint, purification of livelihood, and use of requisites are adorned by mindfulness, energy, and wisdom; this should be understood as is appropriate. Furthermore, faith without wisdom is impure, because wisdom is the cause of clarity. Wisdoms, however, through the power of that faith, are called supremely pure. Wisdom devoid of faith enters the faction of the deceitful; only wisdom conjoined with faith is pure. Energy devoid of concentration leads to restlessness; that which is conjoined with concentration does not. Thus, from the statement about the purity of energy, concentration is also spoken of. In this way, it should be known that even faith and so forth, being supremely pure, adorn the Pātimokkha. How? Without faith in the Teacher who teaches the practice, in the practice, and in the fruit of the practice, it is not possible to undertake virtue or to purify the virtue that has been undertaken. Therefore, faith adorns the Pātimokkha. Therein, by means of 'Thus is that Blessed One...' and so on, one is able to honor the Teacher. Regarding the practice, the occurrence of faith in the visible and future fruits, which are rooted in the failure and success of virtue, should be known in detail. Wisdom, seeing the danger and the benefit which are the signs of the failure and success of virtue, and seeing the means for abandoning the danger and for accomplishing the benefit, and thus proceeding, adorns the Pātimokkha restraint. Having abandoned laziness—which is unworthy of being engaged in—with such thoughts as 'it is too cold,' in accordance with what was said, 'He who regards cold and heat...'; energy that proceeds by way of not producing unarisen non-restraint, abandoning arisen non-restraint, producing unarisen restraint, and developing arisen restraint, adorns the Pātimokkha. By this method, it should also be applied to sense restraint and so forth. Suitable good conduct regarding the four bases of sympathy should be known here as 'conduct' (ācāra). By the word 'straightforwardness,' through showing the association with the quality of straightforwardness—which is the opposite of crooked actions, deceit, and fraud such as bodily misconduct for the sake of gain and honor—the state of having a non-greedy intention is shown. By the word 'gentleness,' through showing the association with the quality of gentleness, such as loving-kindness—which is the opposite of things like aversion that cause a state of harshness—intentions for welfare and so forth are shown. By the word 'etc.,' association with the qualities spoken of as 'patience, gentleness, courtesy, and hospitality,' and so on, is shown. The qualities of straightforwardness, gentleness, and so forth spoken of here are both causes for the accomplishment of virtue and its fruit, because they bring about that accomplishment. 'One's own doctrine' means the fourfold assembly. By this, the absence of the state of suffering for those of a similar nature is indicated. Or alternatively, 'one's own doctrine' means the three Piṭakas of the Sugata. One's own doctrine itself is difficult to grasp because it is difficult to explain. The ascertainment of one's own doctrine is the grasping of one's own doctrine.

“Saccaṃ satto paṭisandhi, paccayākārameva ca;

Duddasā caturo dhammā, desetuñca sudukkarā”ti. (vibha. aṭṭha. 225) –

“Truth, a being, rebirth-linking, and the mode of conditions; these four things are hard to see, and very hard to teach.”

Vuttattā yathā sakasamayassa gahanapadena yojanā vuttā, tathā parasamayassapi. Paññāveyyattiyenāti anena tikhiṇena ñāṇena katasilānisitasatthasadisasabhāvapaññā vuttā. Tipiṭakasaṅkhātāya pariyattiyā pabhedo tipiṭakapariyattippabhedo. Tasmiṃ pabhede. Tanti ca tantiattho ca sāsanaṃ nāma. Idha “tanti evā”ti vadanti. Yasmiṃ ayaṃ saṃvaṇṇanā niṭṭhāpitā, tasmiṃ kāle paṭivedhañāṇābhāvato sutamayaṃ sandhāya “appaṭihatañāṇappabhāvenā”ti vuttaṃ. Karaṇasampattiyā janitattā [M 0.0583] sukhaviniggataṃ. Sukhaviniggatattā madhurodātavacanalāvaṇṇayuttenāpi yojetabbaṃ, īdisaṃ vacanaṃ sotasukhañca sannivesasampattisukhañca hoti. “Veyyākaraṇenā”ti avatvā “mahāveyyākaraṇenā”ti vuttattā sikkhāniruttichandovicityādipaṭimaṇḍitapāṇiniyanyāsādhāraṇadhāraṇasabhāvo sūcito bhavati. Yuttavādinātiādīsu yuttamuttavādinā ṭhānuppattiyapaññāya samannāgatenāti attho. Ojābhedepi āyusattikaraṇatādisāmatthayogānaṃ mahākavinā racitaganthassa mahantattā vā “tipiṭakapariyattippabhede”tiādīhi sāsane, hetuvisaye, sadde cāti imesu tīsu ṭhānesu pāṭavabhāvaṃ dīpento venayikabuddhisampattisabbhāvamassa sūceti. Yesaṃ puggalānaṃ pabhinnā paṭisambhidādi, te pabhinnapaṭisambhidādayo dhammā. Tehi parivārito ukkhittasantatiupacchedamakatvā attano santāne uppādanavaḍḍhanavasena vārito so pabhinnapaṭisambhidāparivāro. Tasmiṃ pabhinnapaṭisambhidāparivāre uttarimanussadhammeti attho. Chaḷabhiññacatupaṭisambhidādippabhedaguṇapaṭimaṇḍite pana chaḷabhiññā uttarimanussadhammā eva. Catūsu paṭisambhidāsu atthapaṭisambhidāya ekadesova. Tadubhayaṃ [V 0.0533] sayaṃ uttarimanussadhammapariyāpannaṃ kathaṃ uttarimanussadhammaṃ paṭimaṇḍetīti ce? Rukkhaṃ rukkhassa avayavabhūtapupphādayo viya sayañca yesaṃ uttarimanussadhammānaṃ avayavattāti. Kāmāvacaradhammapariyāpannapaṭisambhidāñāṇaṃ uttarimanussadhammānaṃ anavayavabhūtaṃ uttarimanussadhammaṃ paṭimaṇḍeti, purisassa anavayavabhūto alaṅkāro viya purisaṃ. Atha vā kāmāvacarapaasambhidāparivāro chaḷabhiññāpaṭisambhidādippabhedaguṇe paṭimaṇḍeti. Lokuttarapaṭisambhidaṃ sandhāya puna paṭisambhidāvacanañca. Sāsane uppajjitvā sāsanassa alaṅkārabhūtena, yasmiṃ vaṃse uppanno, tasseva vā alaṅkārabhūtena. Saṅkhepavitthāresu itarītarakaraṇaṃ, appasannapasannānaṃ pasāduppādanābhivuḍḍhikaraṇaṃ, vuttānaṃ gambhīrānaṃ gambhīruttānabhāvakaraṇanti evaṃ chabbidhācariyaguṇayogato vipulabuddhi nāma. Ye dhammacintanaṃ atidhāvantā keci ucchedādinānappakāraṃ antaṃ vā gaṇhanti, “sabbaṃ ñeyyaṃ paññatti evā”ti vā “paramattho evā”ti vā gaṇhanti, tesaṃ buddhi micchādiṭṭhipaccayattā samalā nāma hoti, imassa pana buddhi dhammacintātidhāvanarahitattā visuddhā nāma hoti. Tena vuttaṃ “vipulavisuddhabuddhinā”ti[M 0.0584]. Garūhi “piyo garu bhāvanīyo”tiādinā (a. ni. 7.37; netti. 113) vuttaguṇehi yuttagarūhi. Guṇehi thirabhāvaṃ gatattā therena.

Because it has been said, just as the application by way of difficult passages for one's own doctrine has been stated, so too for other doctrines. In the phrase `paññāveyyattiyena`, by this sharp wisdom is meant wisdom that has a nature similar to a sword sharpened on a prepared whetstone. The division of the scriptural collection called the Tipiṭaka is `tipiṭakapariyattippabhedo`. In that division. Both the text and the meaning of the text are called the Teaching. Here, some say, 'only the text.' At the time when this commentary was completed, due to the absence of penetration-knowledge, the phrase `appaṭihatañāṇappabhāvena` was said in reference to knowledge based on learning. Because it is produced by the perfection of the vocal organs, it is called `sukhaviniggataṃ` (well-uttered). Because it is well-uttered, it should also be connected with sweet, pure speech and graceful composition; such speech is pleasant to the ear and pleasant for the perfection of comprehension. Because `mahāveyyākaraṇena` was said instead of `veyyākaraṇena`, the nature of mastering uncommon treatises such as Pāṇini's grammar, adorned by phonetics, etymology, metrics, and so on, is indicated. In `yuttavādinā`, etc., the meaning is: by one who speaks what is appropriate and freely spoken, endowed with ready wit. Also in the distinction of potency, or because of the greatness of the treatise composed by the great poet who is among those endowed with abilities such as creating life-force, by the phrases `tipiṭakapariyattippabhede`, etc., while showing proficiency in these three places—in the Teaching, in the domain of causes, and in grammar—it indicates for him the actual existence of the accomplishment of wisdom skilled in the Vinaya. The analytical knowledges, etc., which are distinguished for certain persons, are the states called `pabhinnapaṭisambhidādayo dhammā`. He is surrounded by them. Without cutting off the uplifted continuity, he is surrounded by way of producing and developing them in his own mind-stream; such a person is called `pabhinnapaṭisambhidāparivāro` (one surrounded by the analytical knowledges). In that `pabhinnapaṭisambhidāparivāre`, the meaning is 'in the superhuman state.' However, in being adorned with the qualities distinguished as the six supernormal knowledges, the four analytical knowledges, etc., the six supernormal knowledges are indeed superhuman states. Among the four analytical knowledges, only a part of the analytical knowledge of meaning is a superhuman state. If one should say: 'How does that pair, which is itself included in superhuman states, adorn a superhuman state?' [The answer is:] Just as flowers, etc., which are parts of a tree, adorn the tree, so too it adorns because it is itself a part of those superhuman states. The knowledge of analytical knowledge included in sense-sphere phenomena, not being a part of superhuman states, adorns a superhuman state, just as an ornament, not being a part of a person, adorns a person. Alternatively, the retinue of sense-sphere analytical knowledge adorns the qualities distinguished as the six supernormal knowledges, analytical knowledges, etc. And again, the word `paṭisambhidā` was said in reference to the supramundane analytical knowledge. By one who, having arisen in the Teaching, has become an ornament of the Teaching; or, by one who has become an ornament of the very lineage in which he was born. The ability to teach concisely or in detail; the ability to inspire confidence in the unconvinced and increase it in the convinced; the ability to make profound teachings that have been spoken clear—thus, through connection with these six qualities of a teacher, wisdom is called `vipulabuddhi` (extensive wisdom). The wisdom of those who, over-extending their thought on the Dhamma, grasp various kinds of extreme views such as annihilationism, or grasp that 'all knowable things are mere concepts,' or that they 'are only ultimate reality,' is called defiled because it is conditioned by wrong view. But the wisdom of this one is called pure because it is free from over-extending thought on the Dhamma. Therefore, it was said, `vipulavisuddhabuddhinā` (by one with extensive and pure wisdom). By teachers means by noble teachers endowed with the qualities mentioned in the phrase `piyo garu bhāvanīyo`, etc. By the Elder, because he has reached a state of stability through qualities.

Sīlena sīlassa vā visuddhiyā sīlavisuddhiyā. Avijjaṇḍakosaṃ padāletvā paṭhamaṃ abhinibbattattā lokajeṭṭhassa. Lokassa vā gambhīre mahante sīlādikkhandhe esi gavesīti mahesīti.

The compound `sīlavisuddhiyā` means: by virtue, or for the purification of virtue. Because of being the first to arise, having split the eggshell of ignorance, He is the foremost in the world. Or, because He sought and searched for the great aggregates of qualities such as virtue in the world, which is like a deep abyss, He is called a Great Seer.

Ettāvatā samadhikasattavīsatisahassaparimāṇāya samantapāsādikasaññitāya vinayaṭṭhakathāya sabbapadesu vinicchayajātaṃ saṅkhipitvā gaṇṭhiṭṭhānavikāsanā katā hoti, tathāpi yaṃ ettha likhitaṃ, taṃ suṭṭhu vicāretvā pāḷiñca aṭṭhakathañca sallakkhetvā ye ācariyā buddhassa bhagavato mahānubhāvaṃ, vinayapiṭakassa ca vicitranayagambhīratthataṃ sallakkhetvā porāṇānaṃ kathāmaggaṃ avināsetvā attano matiṃ pahāya kevalaṃ saddhammaṭṭhitiyā, parānuggahakāmatāya ca vinayapiṭakaṃ pakāsentā ṭhitā, tesaṃ pādamūle vanditvā khantisoraccādiguṇasamannāgatena hutvā vattasampattiyā tesaṃ cittaṃ ārādhetvā paveṇiyā āgataṃ vinicchayaṃ kathāpetvā upadhāretvā yaṃ tena saṃsandati, taṃ gahetabbaṃ, itaraṃ chaḍḍetabbaṃ. Itarathā tuṇhībhūtena bhavitabbaṃ. Vinicchayasaṅkarakarena pana na bhavitabbameva. Kasmā? Sāsanassa nāsahetuttā. Hoti cettha –

By this much, having condensed the collection of decisions in all parts of the Vinaya commentary known as the Samantapāsādikā, which has a measure of over twenty-seven thousand, the explanation of the knotty points has been made. Nevertheless, whatever is written herein, that should be accepted only after carefully considering it and noting the Pāḷi and the Aṭṭhakathā. As for those teachers who, recognizing the great power of the Blessed Buddha and the varied and profound meaning of the Vinaya Piṭaka, expound the Vinaya Piṭaka without destroying the path of speech of the ancients, having abandoned their own views, solely for the stability of the good Dhamma and from the wish to benefit others—having paid homage at their feet, having become endowed with qualities such as patience and gentleness, having pleased their minds through the accomplishment of duties, and having caused them to speak of the decision that has come down through tradition and having investigated it, whatever of that traditional decision agrees with this text, that should be accepted; the other should be rejected. Otherwise, one should remain silent. One should certainly not be a person who confuses decisions. Why? Because it is a cause for the destruction of the Dispensation. And there is a summary verse on this matter:

“Asambudhaṃ [V 0.0534] buddhamahānubhāvaṃ,

Dhammassa gambhīranayatthatañca;

Yo vaṇṇaye taṃ vinayaṃ aviññū,

So duddaso sāsananāsahetu.

“Whatever unwise monk, not understanding the great power of the Buddha and the profound method and meaning of the Dhamma, explains that Vinaya—he is a cause for the destruction of the Dispensation, a fact that is hard to see.”

Pāḷiṃ tadatthañca asambudhañhi,

Nāseti yo aṭṭhakathānayañca;

Anicchayaṃ nicchayato parehi,

Gāheti teheva purakkhato so.

“Indeed, whoever, not understanding the Pāḷi, its meaning, and the method of the Aṭṭhakathā, causes others to accept what is undecided as decided—he, being esteemed by those very ones, destroys the Pāḷi, its meaning, and the method of the Aṭṭhakathā.”

Anukkameneva [M 0.0585] mahājanena,

Purakkhato paṇḍitamānibhikkhu;

Apaṇḍitānaṃ vimatiṃ akatvā,

Ācariyalīḷaṃ purato karotī”ti.

“Gradually honored by the great multitude, one who fancies himself wise, without dispelling the doubts of the unwise, puts on the airs of a teacher before them.”

Samantapāsādikāya gaṇṭhipadādhippāyappakāsanā samattā.

The Elucidation of the Intended Meaning of the Knotty Terms of the Samantapāsādikā is complete.

Vajirabuddhiṭīkā niṭṭhitā.

The Vajirabuddhiṭīkā is finished.
